[2001 Translation of the Holy Bible (2001)] [2001] [T2001]
[Genesis] [1]:[1] In the beginning, The God created the sky and the land.
[Genesis] [1]:[2] But the land was hidden and unfinished, Darkness covered its depth, And God’s breath moved over its waters.
[Genesis] [1]:[3] Then The God spoke, and He said: ‘May the light come to be.’ So, the light came to be,
[Genesis] [1]:[4] And God saw that the light was beautiful. Then The God brought a division Between the light and the darkness.
[Genesis] [1]:[5] He called the light the daytime And the darkness, the night. So came the evening and the morning Of the very first day.
[Genesis] [1]:[6] And then The God spoke, and He said: ‘Let there be a firmament between all the waters... A division of the waters and the waters.’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[7] For God ordered a firmament between the waters That were under the firmament, From those that were over the firmament.
[Genesis] [1]:[8] Then God called the firmament the sky, And He saw that this too was beautiful. So came the evening and the morning Of [His] day number two.
[Genesis] [1]:[9] Then The God said: ‘Let the waters that are under the skies Be brought together so the land can be seen.’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[10] God called the dry space the land And the collected waters the seas… And God saw that this too was beautiful.
[Genesis] [1]:[11] Then The God spoke, and He said: ‘Let the land sprout with pastures of grasses Which [each] bear seeds of its kind and appearance. And let there be fruit trees that bear fruit with seeds, [Each] of its kind [and appearance].’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[12] The ground sprouted with pastures of grasses That [each] bore seeds of its kind and appearance, And the fruit trees bore fruit with their seeds, [Each] of its kind [and appearance]. And God saw that this too was beautiful.
[Genesis] [1]:[13] So came the evening and the morning Of [His] day number three.
[Genesis] [1]:[14] Then The God spoke, and He said: ‘Let there be lights in the firmament of the skies To serve as light for the land, To make a division between day and night, And as signs for the days, years, and seasons.
[Genesis] [1]:[15] Let them serve as sources of lights in the firmament, So as to shine on the ground.’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[16] For God made the two huge [sources of] light; The greater light to rule over the days, And the lesser light and the stars To be rulers over the nights.
[Genesis] [1]:[17] Then God assigned them spaces [high] in the skies So as to shine on the earth…
[Genesis] [1]:[18] To dominate the days and the nights, And to make the division between light and darkness. Then God saw that it too was beautiful.
[Genesis] [1]:[19] So came the evening and the morning Of [His] day number four.
[Genesis] [1]:[20] Then The God spoke, and He said: ‘Now, let the waters give birth, To living animals that slither, And [let there be] winged creatures to fly, Above the earth in the firmament of the skies.’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[21] Then God created the great creatures That would live in the seas... Creatures that slither and live in the waters, Each according to their own kinds, And all the feathered flying creatures Each according to their own kinds. And God saw that this too was beautiful.
[Genesis] [1]:[22] So God blest them all, and He said: ‘Reproduce and multiply in the waters Until you fill up the seas, And let the winged creatures multiply on the earth.’
[Genesis] [1]:[23] So came the evening and the morning Of [His] day number five.
[Genesis] [1]:[24] Then The God spoke, and He said: ‘Let the land give birth to living creatures, Each according to their own kinds… Those that travel on their four feet, Those that slither [and crawl] on the ground, And those that are wild on the earth, Each according to their own kinds.’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[25] So God made the wild creatures [that walk on] the ground, Each according to their own kinds… Along with those [that travel] in herds, Each according to their own kinds… And all that slither [and crawl] on the ground. Each according to their own kinds. And God saw that this too was beautiful.
[Genesis] [1]:[26] Then The God spoke, and He said: ‘Let us make a man in our image and like us, To rule over the creatures [that live] in the seas, The winged creatures [that fly] in the skies, The animals that travel in herds, And those that slither and crawl on the ground.’
[Genesis] [1]:[27] So then, God created mankind. He created mankind in the image of the Gods, As a male and female [He made them].
[Genesis] [1]:[28] Then The God blest them and said: ‘Reproduce and now become many… Fill the whole earth and control it. Rule over those that [live in] the seas, The winged creatures that [live in] skies, The animals that [travel in] herds, The animals that slither and crawl on the ground, And [in fact], the whole earth.’
[Genesis] [1]:[29] Then The God said: ‘Look! I’ve given you all the seed-bearing crops, That [you can plant] in the ground, As well as all the seed-bearing trees, [That you] can plant for your food.
[Genesis] [1]:[30] ‘[I have given] the green-yellow plants As food for the wild ones [walking] on the ground, For all the winged creatures [flying in] the skies, And for all that slither and crawl on the ground… For all have the breath of life.’ And that’s what thereafter happened.
[Genesis] [1]:[31] Then The God viewed all that He’d made, And {Look!} it was all beautiful. So came the evening and the morning Of [His] day number six.
[Genesis] [2]:[1] [At that], the skies and the lands were completed, As was the arranging of them.
[Genesis] [2]:[2] For on the sixth day, God finished His work, And on the seventh day, He rested From all the things He’d done.
[Genesis] [2]:[3] Then God blest the seventh day and declared it as holy, For He had completed [all of] the work That He’d set out to do.
[Genesis] [2]:[4] This was the scroll of the origins of the skies and the lands, and of when they came to be in the day that The God spoke the sky and the land [into existence],
[Genesis] [2]:[5] as well as when all the greenish-yellow plants for it began on the ground, and all the grasses of the fields started growing from it. However, because [Jehovah] God had not yet provided rain on the earth and there were no men to cultivate it,
[Genesis] [2]:[6] springs poured from the ground and watered the entire surface of the land.
[Genesis] [2]:[7] Then The God formed the man from the dust of the ground. He breathed the breath of life against his face, and he became a living creature.
[Genesis] [2]:[8] Thereafter, God planted a Paradise east of Edem where He put the man whom he had formed...
[Genesis] [2]:[9] And it was there that God caused every tree that was attractive to look at and worthy as food to spring from the ground. [He also] put the Tree of Life in the middle of the Paradise, as well as the tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil.
[Genesis] [2]:[10] There was also a river that flowed out of Edem to water the Paradise, and from there separated into the sources of four [rivers].
[Genesis] [2]:[11] The name of the [first river] is Phison. It flows around the land of Evilat, where there’s gold,
[Genesis] [2]:[12] and the gold from that land is good. There’s also red gemstone and ornamental stone there.
[Genesis] [2]:[13] The name of the second river is Geon. It runs around the land of Kush.
[Genesis] [2]:[14] The third river is the Tigris. It flows over towards the Assyrians. And the fourth river is the Euphrates.
[Genesis] [2]:[15] Then [Jehovah] God took the man whom He’d formed and put him in the Paradise of Delights so that He could cultivate it and take care of it.
[Genesis] [2]:[16] And [Jehovah] God gave these instructions to Adam: ‘You may eat from all the trees of Paradise,
[Genesis] [2]:[17] but you must not eat from the tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil. For on whatever day you eat from it, your life will end and you’ll die.’
[Genesis] [2]:[18] Then [Jehovah] God said: ‘It isn’t good for the man to be alone, so let’s make a helper for him.’
[Genesis] [2]:[19] Well, after God had made all the wild animals of the plains and all the winged creatures of the skies from the [dirt], He brought them to Adam to see what he would call them. And whatever Adam called each living animal was what its name became.
[Genesis] [2]:[20] So Adam named all the cattle, all the winged creatures of the skies, and all the wild animals of the plains. Yet, a suitable helper that was like Adam couldn’t be found.
[Genesis] [2]:[21] God then put Adam into a trance, and while he was sleeping, He took one of his ribs and filled the place where it was with flesh.
[Genesis] [2]:[22] Then The God built the rib that He took from Adam into a woman... And brought her to Adam.
[Genesis] [2]:[23] And Adam said: ‘This is now bone from my bones, And flesh from my flesh. ‘She will be called a woman, Because she was taken from a man.
[Genesis] [2]:[24] ‘Because of this, a man will leave his father and mother And bond with his woman, And the two will become one flesh.’
[Genesis] [3]:[1] [Well at the time], both of them (the man and the woman) were naked and unashamed.
[Genesis] [3]:[2] Then the snake (which was the wiliest of the animals that [Jehovah] had made on the earth) asked the woman: ‘Why did God tell you that you shouldn’t eat from all of the trees in the Paradise?’
[Genesis] [3]:[3] And the woman replied to the snake: ‘We can eat the fruit from the trees of Paradise, but God said that we shouldn’t eat the fruit from the tree in the middle of Paradise – that we shouldn’t even touch it – or we’ll die.’
[Genesis] [3]:[4] Then the snake said to the woman: ‘You won’t stop living and die,
[Genesis] [3]:[5] for God knows that on whatever day you eat from it your eyes will be opened wide and you’ll be like the gods knowing good and evil.’
[Genesis] [3]:[6] Well, the woman saw that the tree was worthy as food, it was a pleasant sight to her eyes, and it was a beautiful thing to think about. So after picking its fruit, she ate it. Then she gave some to her man (who was with her), and they ate it [together]...
[Genesis] [3]:[7] And thereafter, the eyes of both of them were opened wide and they realized that they were naked. So they sewed fig leaves together and made skirts to go around themselves.
[Genesis] [3]:[8] But then, when they heard the voice of [Jehovah] God as He walked around in Paradise at dusk, Adam and his woman hid from the face of [Jehovah] God among the trees in the Paradise.
[Genesis] [3]:[9] So [Jehovah] God called out to Adam, asking: ‘Where are you Adam?’
[Genesis] [3]:[10] And [Adam] replied to God: ‘I heard Your voice as You were walking through the Paradise, but I was afraid because of my nakedness, so I hid myself.’
[Genesis] [3]:[11] Then The God asked him: ‘If you haven’t eaten from the only tree about which I commanded you not to eat; then, who told you that you were naked?’
[Genesis] [3]:[12] And Adam replied: ‘It was this woman whom You gave to me as a companion… She gave me some [fruit] from the tree, and I ate it.’
[Genesis] [3]:[13] Then [Jehovah] God asked the woman: ‘Why did you do this?’ And the woman replied: ‘The snake seduced me, so I ate it.’
[Genesis] [3]:[14] So [Jehovah] God said to the snake: ‘Because you did this; among all the cattle and wild animals of the earth, you [alone] are doomed to be punished. Therefore, you’ll now travel on your chest and belly and you’ll have to eat from the ground all the days of your life.
[Genesis] [3]:[15] ‘I’m also going to create hatred between you and the woman, and between your descendant and her descendant. He will then watch for your head, and you will watch for his heel.’
[Genesis] [3]:[16] And after that, He said to the woman: ‘I’ll now make your sorrow and groaning [much] worse; for when you give birth to children, you’ll do so with groaning. You will also have to submit to your man and he will dominate you.’
[Genesis] [3]:[17] Then He said to Adam: ‘Because you listened to your woman’s voice and ate from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat (and from which you went ahead and ate); all the work that you will do on the ground will be cursed, and you’ll groan as you eat from it all the days of your life!
[Genesis] [3]:[18] ‘Briars and thistles will grow for you, and your food will be the grasses in the fields.
[Genesis] [3]:[19] ‘You will then eat your bread through the sweat on your face until you return to the ground from which you were taken… Yes, you were taken from the ground and that’s where you’ll return!’
[Genesis] [3]:[20] Well, thereafter, Adam called his woman’s name Life, because she was to be the mother of all [human] life.
[Genesis] [3]:[21] Then [Jehovah] God made leather clothing for Adam and his woman, and He dressed them in it.
[Genesis] [3]:[22] And after that, The God said: ‘Look, Adam has now become one of us in knowing good and evil!’ Therefore, to keep him from reaching out to pick and eat from the Tree of Life so as to gain age-long life,
[Genesis] [3]:[23] [Jehovah] God then put Adam outside of the Paradise of Delights, where he had to work the ground from which he was taken.
[Genesis] [3]:[24] Yes, He drove Adam out and made him live next to the Paradise of Delights. Then He stationed the [heavenly] cherubs with their flaming, spinning swords to guard the way to the Tree of Life.
[Genesis] [4]:[1] Well thereafter, Adam had [sexual relations] with Eue, his woman, so she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. And she said: ‘I have gained a man through God.’
[Genesis] [4]:[2] Then she again gave birth to his brother, Abel. Abel [grew up to be] a herder of sheep, while Cain worked the ground.
[Genesis] [4]:[3] Then after many days, Cain brought some of the fruit of the ground as an offering to [Jehovah],
[Genesis] [4]:[4] while Abel brought the first-born of his sheep and his belongings. Well, God looked favorably upon Abel and his gifts,
[Genesis] [4]:[5] but He paid no attention to Cain and his sacrifices, which made Cain very sad, and his face [reflected] this.
[Genesis] [4]:[6] So [Jehovah] God asked Cain: ‘Why are you so sad and why is your face so long?
[Genesis] [4]:[7] For even if you didn’t bring [your gifts] righteously, you didn’t sin by sharing. Overlook this, because [Abel] will submit to you and you’ll [rule] over him!’
[Genesis] [4]:[8] But thereafter, Cain said to his brother Abel: ‘Let’s go out into the fields.’ Then, while they were in their fields, Cain attacked his brother Abel and killed him.
[Genesis] [4]:[9] And when [Jehovah] God asked Cain: ‘Where is your brother?’ He replied: ‘I don’t know… I’m not my brother’s keeper!’
[Genesis] [4]:[10] Then [Jehovah] God asked: ‘What have you done? ‘I hear the blood of your brother calling out to Me from the ground!
[Genesis] [4]:[11] Therefore, you’ll now be cursed by the ground, which has opened her mouth wide to [drink] the blood of your brother from your hand.
[Genesis] [4]:[12] ‘So from here on, whenever you work the ground, it will [no longer] give you its strength, and you’ll groan and tremble on the earth.’
[Genesis] [4]:[13] Then Cain said to [Jehovah] God: ‘My crime is too great to be forgiven.
[Genesis] [4]:[14] So if you [drive me] away from Your face and the face of this land today, I’ll have to hide, groaning and trembling on the land… For anyone who finds me will kill me!’
[Genesis] [4]:[15] And [Jehovah] God replied: ‘That isn’t so! For whoever kills Cain will pay seven penalties.’ Then [Jehovah] God put a mark on Cain so that nobody that found him would kill him.
[Genesis] [4]:[16] And thereafter, Cain left the presence of God and lived in Nod, which also borders Edem.
[Genesis] [4]:[17] There, Cain [had sex] with his woman and she became pregnant, giving birth to Enoch. [Then Cain] built a city, which he named after his son, Enoch.
[Genesis] [4]:[18] Enoch fathered GaiDad, GaiDad fathered MalaleEl, MalaleEl fathered MethuSelah, and MethuSelah fathered Lamech.
[Genesis] [4]:[19] Then Lamech took two women; the first was Ada and the second was SelLa.
[Genesis] [4]:[20] Ada gave birth to JoBel, who was the ancestor of those who lived in tents and herded cattle.
[Genesis] [4]:[21] He had a brother named JuBal, who invented the lute and the harp.
[Genesis] [4]:[22] SelLa also gave birth to ThoBel, who worked iron and brass. And he had a sister named NoEma.
[Genesis] [4]:[23] Then Lamech said this to his women (Ada and SelLa): ‘Listen to me, [my] women and remember; I’ve killed a man who wounded me… A young man who whipped me.
[Genesis] [4]:[24] So if the vengeance [for killing] Cain was seven punishments; Mine will be seven times that.’
[Genesis] [4]:[25] Well, Adam [again had sex with] his woman Eue and she became pregnant, giving birth to a son whom she named Seth. For she said: ‘God has [provided me with] another son to replace Abel, who was murdered by Cain.’
[Genesis] [4]:[26] Then Seth had a son whom he named Enos, who hoped to call upon the Name of The God, [Jehovah].
[Genesis] [5]:[1] This was the scroll of the early [days] of mankind, when God fathered Adam, forming him in [His] image.
[Genesis] [5]:[2] He created the male and the female and He blest them. Then in the day that He created [the first man], He named him Adam.
[Genesis] [5]:[3] Adam was 230 years old when he fathered a son who was just like him and looked like him, that he named Seth.
[Genesis] [5]:[4] Then after fathering Seth, Adam lived on for 700 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[5] So Adam was 930 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[6] Now, Seth was 205 years old when he fathered Enos.
[Genesis] [5]:[7] And after fathering Enos, he lived on for 707 more years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[8] So Seth was 912 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[9] Enos was 190 years old when he fathered Kainan.
[Genesis] [5]:[10] Then after fathering Kainan, he lived on for another 715 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[11] So Enos was 905 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[12] Kainan was 170 years old when he fathered MaleLeal.
[Genesis] [5]:[13] Then after fathering MaleLeal, he lived on for some 740 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[14] So Kainan was 910 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[15] MaleLeal was 165 years old when he fathered JaRed.
[Genesis] [5]:[16] And after fathering JaRed, he lived on for 730 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[17] So MaleLeal was 895 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[18] JaRed was 162 years old when he fathered Enoch.
[Genesis] [5]:[19] Then after fathering Enoch, he lived on for another 800 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[20] So JaRed was 962 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[21] Enoch was 165 years old when he fathered MethuSelah.
[Genesis] [5]:[22] And it was after he fathered MethuSelah that God found Enoch to be righteous. So after he lived for 200 more years, and after he’d fathered other sons and daughters,
[Genesis] [5]:[23] when he was 365 years old
[Genesis] [5]:[24] (and because he had pleased God), God transported him and he disappeared.
[Genesis] [5]:[25] Well, MethuSelah was 187 years old when he fathered Lamech.
[Genesis] [5]:[26] Then after fathering Lamech, he lived on for another 782 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[27] So MethuSelah was 969 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[28] Lamech was 188 years old when he fathered a son
[Genesis] [5]:[29] whom he named Noah. And he said: ‘He will stop us from doing all the [bad] things that we’re doing, as well as from working with our hands and from [living on] the ground that [Jehovah] has cursed.’
[Genesis] [5]:[30] Then, after he fathered Noah, [Lamech] lived on for some 565 years, as he fathered other sons and daughters.
[Genesis] [5]:[31] So Lamech was 753 years old when he died.
[Genesis] [5]:[32] Well, it was after Noah was 500 years old that he fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and JaPheth.
[Genesis] [6]:[1] Now, as the population of men grew on the earth and they fathered daughters,
[Genesis] [6]:[2] the sons of The God noticed that the daughters of men were beautiful; so, they took all whom they chose as their women.
[Genesis] [6]:[3] Then [Jehovah] God said: ‘There’s no way that my breath will stay with these men. They’re [just] flesh, so their [lives] will last just 120 [more] years.’
[Genesis] [6]:[4] Well, there were giants on the earth back in those days; for after that, the sons of The God continued to [had sex] with the daughters of mankind and fathered [children] for themselves who became the giants and the famous men of that age.
[Genesis] [6]:[5] Well, [Jehovah] God saw that the badness of the people on the earth was getting much worse… For the things that they conceived in their hearts every day was all twisted towards evil.
[Genesis] [6]:[6] So God became disturbed that He had created humans on the earth… He shook His head
[Genesis] [6]:[7] and declared: ‘I will wipe the humans that I made off the face of the earth… Yes, the people, the cattle, and the winged creatures of the skies, for I’m sorry that I made them.’
[Genesis] [6]:[8] However, Noah found mercy in the eyes of The God, [Jehovah].
[Genesis] [6]:[9] This is the account of Noah’s origin: Noah was a righteous man… Perfect [when compared to] that generation, for Noah pleased God well.
[Genesis] [6]:[10] Then he fathered three sons: Shem, Ham, and JaPheth.
[Genesis] [6]:[11] As God saw it, the land had become unclean and the earth was filled with unrighteousness.
[Genesis] [6]:[12] So when [Jehovah] God looked at the earth, all He saw was corruption, because all flesh had become corrupt in its ways.
[Genesis] [6]:[13] Then [Jehovah] God told Noah: ‘A season is now before me [that will lead to the end of] all mankind, because the earth is filled with their unrighteousness. Look! I’m going to lay waste to them and to the whole earth!
[Genesis] [6]:[14] ‘So [you must] make a chest of squared timbers for yourself and [divide the] chest into stalls, then cover both the inside and outside of it with tar.
[Genesis] [6]:[15] ‘This is how you should build the chest; [make it:] 300 cubits [500 feet / 152m] long, 50 cubits [80 feet / 24.4m] wide, and 30 cubits [50 feet / 15.25m] tall.
[Genesis] [6]:[16] ‘You must also make a roof that’s about 1 cubit [~20in / ~50cm] thick, and put a door in the side of the chest… Make a bottom floor, a second floor, and a third floor.
[Genesis] [6]:[17] ‘[For after it’s completed], {Look!} I’m going to bring a downpour of water upon the ground to destroy all flesh under the skies that has the breath of life… So, all that’s on the ground will then come to an end.
[Genesis] [6]:[18] And after that, I’ll establish an agreement between you and Me.’
[Genesis] [6]:[19] ‘Therefore, [I want you to] bring all [types of] cattle, slithering creatures, and wild animals – all [types of] flesh – into the chest by pairs of males and females. ‘Then, bring in enough food for them and for yourselves.
[Genesis] [6]:[20] For they’ll all be eating there with you… All the winged creatures, all types of cattle, and all varieties of slithering animals that crawl on the ground (both the males and the females).
[Genesis] [6]:[21] ‘Yes, you must gather all types of food for yourselves so that you’ll each have something to eat.’
[Genesis] [6]:[22] And thereafter, Noah did everything that [Jehovah] God told him to do.
[Genesis] [7]:[1] Then [Jehovah] God said to Noah: ‘Now you and your family must enter the chest, because I’ve [only] found you to be righteous among this generation.
[Genesis] [7]:[2] Take 7 pairs (males and females) of [all the] clean cattle in with you, and take in [single] pairs (males and females) of [all the] unclean animals.
[Genesis] [7]:[3] ‘[Do the same with all] the winged creatures of the sky… Bring in 7 pairs (males and females) of the clean ones, and [just] pairs of all the unclean winged creatures, so that their descendants will remain on the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[4] ‘For in just 7 days, I’ll bring rain to the ground [that will last for] 40 days and 40 nights, and I’ll blot every creature that I’ve made off of the face of the entire earth!’
[Genesis] [7]:[5] And thereafter, Noah did everything that [Jehovah] God had commanded him to do.
[Genesis] [7]:[6] Noah was 600 years old when the Downpour of waters started on the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[7] Then Noah, his wife, his sons, and their wives went into the chest with him (because of the downpour of water).
[Genesis] [7]:[8] And the clean winged creatures, the unclean winged creatures, the clean cattle, the unclean cattle, and all the wild animals as well as all the things that crawled on the ground
[Genesis] [7]:[9] came to Noah and entered the chest in pairs of males and females, just as God had commanded Noah.
[Genesis] [7]:[10] Then after 7 days, the waters of the Downpour started falling on the earth.
[Genesis] [7]:[11] It was in the 600th year of Noah’s life, on the 27th day of the 2nd month, that all the springs under the ground broke open, and the floodgates of the skies were opened.
[Genesis] [7]:[12] Then it rained on the earth for 40 days and 40 nights.
[Genesis] [7]:[13] It started on the very day that Noah, his wife, as well as Shem, Ham, JaPheth (the sons of Noah and his wife) and their three wives went into the chest with him.
[Genesis] [7]:[14] Also, all the wild animals (each of its kind), all the cattle (each of its kind), all the slithering animals that move on the earth (each of its kind),
[Genesis] [7]:[15] and all the winged creatures (each of its kind) went inside the chest to Noah in pairs of males and females… Everything that had the breath of life.
[Genesis] [7]:[16] Males and females of all flesh went inside, just as God had commanded Noah... Then [Jehovah] God closed the chest from the outside.
[Genesis] [7]:[17] Thereafter, the Downpour continued on the earth for 40 days and 40 nights, and the water got so deep that it lifted the chest high above the ground.
[Genesis] [7]:[18] The water dominated and totally covered the land, and the chest was carried along on top of the water.
[Genesis] [7]:[19] For the water dominated and covered even the tallest mountains under the whole sky…
[Genesis] [7]:[20] It covered the highest mountains by at least 15 cubits [25 feet / 7.6m].
[Genesis] [7]:[21] So everything that moved on the earth died… All the men, winged creatures, cattle, wild animals, and all the animals that slithered across the ground.
[Genesis] [7]:[22] Everything that lived on the ground and had the breath of life, died.
[Genesis] [7]:[23] God blotted out all His creatures on the face of the earth… The men, the animals, the winged creatures, and the slithering animals. He blotted them all from the earth. The only ones who remained were Noah and those who were with him inside the chest.
[Genesis] [7]:[24] Altogether, the water covered the land for 150 days.
[Genesis] [8]:[1] But God didn’t forget Noah or any of the wild animals, cattle, winged creatures, or crawling, slithering animals that were inside the chest. So God sent a wind to the earth that stopped the water…
[Genesis] [8]:[2] For the springs that were under the ground closed and the floodgates of the skies and the rain from the skies were held back.
[Genesis] [8]:[3] Then the water level started to drop, flowing off the ground. And after 150 days, the water lowered, and the chest came to rest on Mount Ararat on the 27th day of the 7th month.
[Genesis] [8]:[4] Well, the water levels kept dropping through the 10th month,
[Genesis] [8]:[5] and on the 1st day of the 10th month, they could see the mountaintops.
[Genesis] [8]:[6] Then, after 40 days, Noah opened the window that he had made in the chest, and he sent out a crow, which left and didn’t return until the water had abated.
[Genesis] [8]:[7] So it left and it didn’t return (until [later, when] the water had dried off the ground).
[Genesis] [8]:[8] And after that, he sent out a dove to see if the earth was still flooded.
[Genesis] [8]:[9] But the dove couldn’t find a place to rest its feet, because the water was still covering all the ground, and it returned to the chest. So [Noah] stuck out his hand to take [the dove], and brought it to himself inside the chest.
[Genesis] [8]:[10] Well, a week later, he sent the dove out from the chest once again.
[Genesis] [8]:[11] And that evening, the dove returned to him with a stem and leaf from an olive tree in its beak. That’s when Noah knew [for sure] that the water had left the ground.
[Genesis] [8]:[12] However, he continued to wait another week before he released the dove once more. And this time, it didn’t return at all.
[Genesis] [8]:[13] So by the 601st year of Noah’s life, on the 1st day of the 1st month, the water had poured off the ground. Then Noah opened the roof that he had made for the chest, and he could finally see that the water had drained from the ground…
[Genesis] [8]:[14] And by the 22nd day of the 2nd month, the ground was dry.
[Genesis] [8]:[15] Then [Jehovah] God spoke to Noah and said:
[Genesis] [8]:[16] ‘Come out of the chest… You, your wife, your sons, their wives who are with you,
[Genesis] [8]:[17] and all the wild animals that are with you. ‘Bring out all the flesh that’s with you – the winged creatures, the cattle, and the slithering animals that move on the ground – [so that they can] reproduce and multiply on the earth.’
[Genesis] [8]:[18] So Noah, his wife, his sons, and his son’s wives that were with him, came out.
[Genesis] [8]:[19] And all the wild animals, all the cattle, all the winged creatures, and all the slithering animals that crawl on the ground (according to their kinds) came out of the chest.
[Genesis] [8]:[20] Then Noah built an altar to [Jehovah], and he took some of the clean animals, as well as some from among all the clean winged creatures, and offered them whole… Burning them on the altar.
[Genesis] [8]:[21] And as [Jehovah] noticed the sweet smell, He thought about it and said: ‘Never again will I curse the ground for the bad things that men do, because the imagination of men is totally bent towards doing bad things from the time they’re young. Also, will I never again [destroy] all living flesh as I have just done.
[Genesis] [8]:[22] Then, during all the days of the earth, the seed [planting] time and harvesting, the heat and the cold, the spring and the summer, and the days and nights won’t ever be brought to an end.’
[Genesis] [9]:[1] Thereafter, God blest Noah and his sons and told them: ‘Now, reproduce and multiply… Fill the earth and rule over it.
[Genesis] [9]:[2] For all the wild animals of the earth, all the winged creatures in the skies, and everything that moves on the ground (including all the creatures in the seas) will have a dread and fear of you. So I have put you in charge over all of them!
[Genesis] [9]:[3] ‘Also, all the living and slithering animals can serve as meat for you… I’ve given them all to you as though they were green vegetation.
[Genesis] [9]:[4] But you must not eat their flesh with its blood of life,
[Genesis] [9]:[5] or I’ll require your blood at the hand of all those wild animals. ‘I’ll also require a man’s life at the hands of his brothers…
[Genesis] [9]:[6] For, whoever spills the blood of mankind will also have his blood spilled, since I made mankind in the image of God.
[Genesis] [9]:[7] ‘Now, reproduce and multiply… Fill the earth and rule over it!’
[Genesis] [9]:[8] Then The God spoke to Noah and his sons that were with him and said:
[Genesis] [9]:[9] ‘Look; I’m making an agreement between you and Me, [as well as] with your descendant [that will come] after you
[Genesis] [9]:[10] and with every living thing (the winged creatures, the [domesticated] animals, and all the wild animals of the earth)… With all who are with you and came out of the chest.
[Genesis] [9]:[11] ‘This is My promise to you and to all flesh: ‘I’ll never again send a downpour of water to kill all flesh, and I’ll never again send a downpour to destroy the whole earth.’
[Genesis] [9]:[12] Then The God said to Noah: ‘This is the sign of the Agreement that I have established between you and Me throughout ages of generations, as well as with every living creature that’s with you:
[Genesis] [9]:[13] ‘I have put My bow in the clouds, which will serve as the sign of the Agreement between the earth and Me,
[Genesis] [9]:[14] so that whenever I gather clouds over the earth, My bow will be seen in those clouds,
[Genesis] [9]:[15] and this will remind Me of My agreement between you and Me, and with every living creature and all flesh, that never again will I send a downpour of water that will blot out all flesh.
[Genesis] [9]:[16] ‘My bow will be there in the clouds, and when I see it, I’ll remember the age-long agreement between Me and the earth, as well as with every living creature among all the flesh that’s on the earth.’
[Genesis] [9]:[17] And God said to Noah: ‘Yes, this is the sign of the Agreement that I made with all flesh that is on the earth and Myself.’
[Genesis] [9]:[18] Now, the sons of Noah who came out of the chest were [named] Shem, Ham, and JaPheth (Ham was the father of CanaAn).
[Genesis] [9]:[19] And it was from these three sons of Noah that all men came to be scattered over the whole earth.
[Genesis] [9]:[20] Thereafter, Noah took up farming and he planted some grapes.
[Genesis] [9]:[21] [Then, one day], Noah was drinking some wine while he was naked in his house, and he got drunk.
[Genesis] [9]:[22] But then, Ham (CanaAn’s father) saw his father’s nakedness, and he went outside and told his brothers about it.
[Genesis] [9]:[23] So Shem and JaPheth grabbed a robe, put it over their backs, and walked backward to cover their father’s naked body. And because they were looking away, they didn’t see their father’s nakedness.
[Genesis] [9]:[24] Well, after Noah recovered from the wine, he realized what his youngest son [or grandson] had done to him.
[Genesis] [9]:[25] So he said: ‘The servant CanaAn is cursed, and he will be a slave to his brothers.’
[Genesis] [9]:[26] Then he added: ‘May [Jehovah], Shem’s God, bless him… But let CanaAn be his houseboy.
[Genesis] [9]:[27] ‘Also, may God make room for JaPheth and allow him to live in the tents of Shem… And may CanaAn then become his also.’
[Genesis] [9]:[28] Well, after the Downpour, Noah lived on for another 350 years.
[Genesis] [9]:[29] So he lived for 950 years, and then he died.
[Genesis] [10]:[1] Now, these are the generations of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and JaPheth. And these are the sons who were born to them after the Downpour.
[Genesis] [10]:[2] JaPheth’s sons were: Gamer, Magog [the Scythians], Madoi [the Medes], Jovan, EliSa, ThoBel [of Tubal], Mosoch [possibly Moscow of Russia], and Thiras [Islands of the Aegean Sea].
[Genesis] [10]:[3] Gamer’s sons were: AshKenaz [Germans, Slavs], RiPhath [of Northwestern Asia Minor], and Thorgama [the Armenians].
[Genesis] [10]:[4] Jovan’s sons were: EliShah [of Tyre], TarShish [of Spain], Cetian [of Cypress], and Rhodes [of Rhodes].
[Genesis] [10]:[5] [They settled the] islands, which lands were divided by tribe and nation among the ethnics, each according to his own language.
[Genesis] [10]:[6] Ham’s sons were: Kush, Mesrain [Egyptian tribes], Phud [Libyans], and CanaAn [Palestinians].
[Genesis] [10]:[7] The sons of Kush were: Saba [peoples of southern Africa], Evilat, SaBatha, Rhegma, and Sabathaca [East Africans]. The sons of Rhegma were: Saba [of 13 Arabian tribes], and Dadan [part of Arabia].
[Genesis] [10]:[8] Kush fathered NimRod, who became a giant on the earth.
[Genesis] [10]:[9] He was a gigantic hunter before [Jehovah] God, and that’s why people speak of NimRod as ‘the gigantic hunter before [Jehovah].’
[Genesis] [10]:[10] His kingdom started with Babylon and stretched to Orech, Archad, and ChalanNe, which were all in the land of Shinar.
[Genesis] [10]:[11] Then outside of that land, [he went to] Assyria and built Nineveh, the cities of RehobOth, Chalach,
[Genesis] [10]:[12] and Dase (between Nineveh, and Chalach), which is the great city.
[Genesis] [10]:[13] Mesrain fathered: The Lydim [Lydians], the MaphTuhim [people of Memphis, Egypt], the AnaMim [Libyans], the Lehabim [people of Lower Egypt],
[Genesis] [10]:[14] the Pathrusim [people of Upper Egypt], the Casluhim [Cretans] (from whom the Philistines descended), and the GaphThoriim [also from the area of Crete].
[Genesis] [10]:[15] CanaAn’s first-born son was Sidon. Then there were: The Hittites,
[Genesis] [10]:[16] the Jebusites, the Amorites, the Girgashites,
[Genesis] [10]:[17] the Hevites, the Arukites, the Sinites [Chinese?], the Asenites,
[Genesis] [10]:[18] the Aradians, the Samarians [Northern Lebanon], and the Hamathites. But the CanaAnites were scattered,
[Genesis] [10]:[19] so their territory stretched from Sidon to Gerar (near Gaza), to Sodom and GomorRah, to Adama, and to Seboim, as far as Dasa.
[Genesis] [10]:[20] So these were the descendants of Ham by tribe, country, language, and nation.
[Genesis] [10]:[21] Shem, who was the elder brother of JaPheth and the ancestor of all the sons of Heber [the ancestor of the Israelites], also had children born to him.
[Genesis] [10]:[22] His sons were: ElAm, AsSur, ArphaxAd, Lud, Aram, and Kainan.
[Genesis] [10]:[23] Aram’s sons were: Uz, Ul, Gater, and Mosoch.
[Genesis] [10]:[24] ArphaxAd fathered [a son whom he named] Kainan, who fathered Sala, who fathered [a son whom he named] Heber.
[Genesis] [10]:[25] This Heber had two sons. He named the first PhalEd (Division), because the land became divided in his day, and his brother’s name was JekTan.
[Genesis] [10]:[26] JekTan fathered: ElModad, Saleth, SarMoth, Jarach,
[Genesis] [10]:[27] OdorRha, AiBel, Decla,
[Genesis] [10]:[28] Eval, AbiMaEl, Saba,
[Genesis] [10]:[29] Uphir, Evila, and Jobab. These were all the sons of JekTan.

[Genesis] [10]:[32] and these were the tribes of the sons of Noah by generations and nations. From them came the people of all the islands and nations that were scattered around the earth after the Downpour.
[Genesis] [11]:[1] [At the time], the whole earth shared the same lips, because they all spoke the same language.
[Genesis] [11]:[2] And as they migrated from the east, they found a flat area of land in Shinar, and started living there.
[Genesis] [11]:[3] Then one man said to his neighbor: ‘Come on; let’s make some bricks and bake them in an oven.’ So bricks became their ‘stone’ and tar served as their ‘mortar.’
[Genesis] [11]:[4] And they said: ‘Come on; let’s build ourselves a city with a tower that reaches into the sky. And let’s create a name for ourselves, before we end up being scattered all over the face of the earth.’
[Genesis] [11]:[5] Then [Jehovah] came down to see this city and its tower that the sons of men had built.
[Genesis] [11]:[6] And [Jehovah] said: ‘Look; they’re all the same race and they share the same lips… And now they’ve started doing this. [Before long], they’ll be able to accomplish anything that they set out to do.
[Genesis] [11]:[7] ‘Therefore, let’s go down there and change their language so that no one will be able to understand the voice of his neighbor.’
[Genesis] [11]:[8] So, [Jehovah] scattered them from there over the entire face of the earth, and they stopped building the city and its tower.
[Genesis] [11]:[9] That is why [the city] is named ‘Confusion,’ because, that’s where [Jehovah] confused all the languages of the earth and scattered them from there over all the face of the earth.

[Genesis] [11]:[12] ArphaxAd was 135 years old when he became father to Kainan.
[Genesis] [11]:[13] And after ArphaxAd became the father to Kainan, he lived 330 years more (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died. Kainan was 130 years old when he became father to Sala. And after he became father to Sala, he lived 330 years (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died.
[Genesis] [11]:[14] Sala was 130 years old when he became father to Heber.
[Genesis] [11]:[15] And after he became father to Heber, he lived 330 years more (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died.
[Genesis] [11]:[16] Heber was 134 years old when he became father to Phaleg.
[Genesis] [11]:[17] And after he became father to Phaleg, he lived 270 years (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died.
[Genesis] [11]:[18] Phaleg was 130 years old when he became father to Ragau.
[Genesis] [11]:[19] After he became father to Ragau, he lived 209 years (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died.
[Genesis] [11]:[20] Ragau was 132 years old when he became father to Seruch.
[Genesis] [11]:[21] After he became father to Seruch, he lived 207 years (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died.
[Genesis] [11]:[22] Seruch was 130 years old when he became father to NaHor.

[Genesis] [11]:[24] NaHor was 79 years old when he became father to Terah.
[Genesis] [11]:[25] And after he became father to Terah, he lived 129 years (as he fathered other sons and daughters), and then he died.
[Genesis] [11]:[26] [After] Terah was 70 years old, he became father to: Abram, NaHor, and Haran.
[Genesis] [11]:[27] These are the generations of Terah: Terah became father to Abram, NaHor, and Haran; and Haran became father to Lot.
[Genesis] [11]:[28] Haran died in the presence of Terah his father in the land where he was born, the country of the Chaldeans.
[Genesis] [11]:[29] Both Abram and NaHor then took women for themselves. Abram’s wife was named Sara, and NaHor’s wife was named Malcha. She was the daughter of Haran (the father of Malcha and Jescha).
[Genesis] [11]:[30] However, Sara was sterile, so she didn’t have any children.
[Genesis] [11]:[31] Then Terah took his son Abram, Abram’s wife Sara (his daughter-in-law), and his grandson Lot (son of Haran), and led them from the land of the Chaldeans towards the land of CanaAn. However, when they got to Haran, they started living there.
[Genesis] [11]:[32] And thereafter, Terah continued living in the land of Haran. Terah died in Haran at the age of 205.
[Genesis] [12]:[1] Then [Jehovah] said to Abram: ‘Leave this land, as well as your family and your father’s home, and go to a land that I’ll show you,

[Genesis] [12]:[4] So Abram did just as [Jehovah] told him… And Lot went with him. Abram was 75 years old when he left Haran,

[Genesis] [12]:[6] Abram traveled down through the land to a place called SheChem, where there was a tall tree. And at the time, the CanaAnites were living in the land.

[Genesis] [12]:[9] Thereafter, Abram left that place and camped in the desert.
[Genesis] [12]:[10] Well, there came a famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to stay, because the famine had devastated the land.
[Genesis] [12]:[11] And as Abram was about to enter Egypt, he said to his wife Sara: ‘You’re a beautiful woman,
[Genesis] [12]:[12] [and I’m afraid] that when the Egyptians see you they’ll say, ‘[Look at] his wife!’, and they’ll kill me… But they’ll let you live.
[Genesis] [12]:[13] ‘So tell people that you’re my sister. That way, things will go well for me because of you, and my life will be safe because of you.’
[Genesis] [12]:[14] And that’s what happened. When Abram entered Egypt and the Egyptians saw how beautiful his woman was,
[Genesis] [12]:[15] one of PharaOh’s princes praised her to PharaOh [possibly Pepi II] and brought her into PharaOh’s [Palace].
[Genesis] [12]:[16] And because of her, PharaOh treated Abram very well. So he accumulated [many] sheep, calves, burros, male and female servants, mules, and camels.
[Genesis] [12]:[17] However, God cursed PharaOh and his house with some very serious and difficult problems because of Sara (Abram’s wife).
[Genesis] [12]:[18] So PharaOh called Abram and asked: ‘What have you done to me? You didn’t tell me that she’s your wife.
[Genesis] [12]:[19] Why did you tell us that she’s your sister? Look, I’ve already taken her as mine! ‘Now, there’s your wife standing before you… She’s yours, so take her and leave quickly!’
[Genesis] [12]:[20] Then PharaOh gave his men instructions about Abram, telling them to accompany him and his wife on their way, along with all the things that they owned.
