[Genesis] [15]:[1] Well after that, [Jehovah] sent word to Abram in a vision, saying: ‘Don’t be afraid, Abram... For I am your shield, and you’ll receive a huge reward.’
[Genesis] [15]:[2] Then Abram said: ‘O Almighty [Jehovah]! What can You give me, since I’m about to die without a son? EliEzer of Damascus, the home-born son of my [slave girl] Masek of Damascus, is my heir.’
[Genesis] [15]:[3] And Abram continued: ‘I’m so very sad, because You haven’t given me a descendant, and the home-born [of my slave girl] will be my heir.’
[Genesis] [15]:[4] Well, the Lord immediately replied, saying: ‘He won’t be your heir… Another that comes from you will be your heir.’
[Genesis] [15]:[5] Then He took him outside and said: ‘Look up into the sky and count all the stars… That is, if you can come up with an accurate count.’ And He said: ‘This is how your offspring will be.’
[Genesis] [15]:[6] So Abram believed The God, and his [faith] was counted to him as righteousness.
[Genesis] [15]:[7] Then [God] said to him: ‘I’m the God who brought you out of the land of the Chaldeans to give you this land as an inheritance.’
[Genesis] [15]:[8] And [Abram] said: ‘My Lord and Master, how can I know [for sure] that I’ll inherit it?’
[Genesis] [15]:[9] And He replied: ‘Collect for Me a 3-year-old heifer, a 3-year-old nanny goat, a 3-year-old billy goat, a dove, and a pigeon.’
[Genesis] [15]:[10] So Abram brought all three of [the animals] to Him, cut them each into halves, and set [the halves] opposite each other… But he didn’t cut the winged creatures into halves.
[Genesis] [15]:[11] Well, birds then started landing on the bodies (the cut-up parts), as Abram sat there next to them.
[Genesis] [15]:[12] Then, about sunset, Abram fell into a trance and {Look!} he had an ominous premonition.
[Genesis] [15]:[13] For Abram was told [by God]: ‘You must know this for a fact; your offspring will have to live as aliens in a foreign land where they’ll be slaves who are treated badly and humbled for 400 years.
[Genesis] [15]:[14] ‘Then I’ll judge the nation that they are to serve; and following that, [your offspring] will return here with many possessions.
[Genesis] [15]:[15] However, you’ll go to your fathers [in the grave] well fed and in peace at a ripe old age.
[Genesis] [15]:[16] ‘Then the 4th generation will return here... Because, even up to this point, the sins of the Amorites haven’t reached their climax yet.’
[Genesis] [15]:[17] Well, as the sun was setting, {look!} there was a flame that looked like a smoking furnace and like lamp fires that moved between the divided pieces [of the animals]!
[Genesis] [15]:[18] This was the day that [Jehovah] made a Sacred Agreement with Abram. He said: ‘I will give this land – from the [Nile] River of Egypt to the great Euphrates River – to your offspring,
[Genesis] [15]:[19] along with: The Kainites, the Kenezites, the KedMoneans,
[Genesis] [15]:[20] the Hittites, the Pherezites, the Raphaim,
[Genesis] [15]:[21] the Amorites, the CanaAnites, the Hevites, the Gergesites, and the Jebusites.’
[Genesis] [16]:[1] Well, Sara (Abram’s wife) hadn’t given him any children. However, she had an Egyptian handmaid whose name was Hagar.
[Genesis] [16]:[2] And so, Sara said to Abram: ‘Look; [Jehovah] has kept me from getting pregnant; so, [sleep with] my maid that I might have my children through her.’ Well, Abram accepted this offer from Sara,
[Genesis] [16]:[3] so Sara (Abram’s wife) took Hagar her Egyptian handmaid (this was after Abram had lived in the land of CanaAn for 10 years) and gave her to her man Abram as his woman.
[Genesis] [16]:[4] Then [Abram] went in to [bed with] Hagar, and she became pregnant. However, after she realized that she was going to have a child, she started being disrespectful to her mistress.
[Genesis] [16]:[5] So Sara said to Abram: ‘I’ve really been hurt by you, for I gave you my handmaid [to sleep with], and when I saw that she was pregnant, she started treating me disrespectfully! ‘So may [Jehovah] judge between you and me!’
[Genesis] [16]:[6] Then Abram told Sara: ‘Look, your handmaid is yours! Treat her any way that seems right to you!’ So Sara started treating [Hagar] badly, and she ran away.
[Genesis] [16]:[7] Then a [spirit] messenger from [Jehovah] found [Hagar] by a spring of water in the desert (the spring on the way to Sur).
[Genesis] [16]:[8] And [Jehovah’s] messenger said to her: ‘Hagar, Sara’s maid! Where are you coming from and where are you going?’ And she replied: ‘I’m running away from my mistress, Sara.’
[Genesis] [16]:[9] Then [Jehovah’s] messenger said: ‘Return to your mistress and obey her.’
[Genesis] [16]:[10] And the messenger of [Jehovah] told her: ‘I will make your offspring grow, and they’ll become so many that they can’t be counted.’
[Genesis] [16]:[11] The messenger of [Jehovah] then went on to say: ‘Look; you are pregnant with a child. You’ll give birth to a son, and you should name him IshMaEl (‘God has Noticed’), because [Jehovah] has noticed how you’ve been humiliated.
[Genesis] [16]:[12] ‘He will be a wild man, for his fists [will be lifted] against everyone, and everyone [will lift] their fists against him. However, he will live in the midst of all his brothers.’
[Genesis] [16]:[13] Then she called upon the Name of the Lord God who was speaking to her, saying: ‘You are the God who watches over me...’ And she added: '...because I openly saw the One who appeared to me.’
[Genesis] [16]:[14] [So from that point on], she called that well, ‘The Well of The One Whom I Openly Saw.’ Look; it [still can be found] between Cades and BarAd.
[Genesis] [16]:[15] Well after that, Hagar bore a son to Abram; and Abram named the son whom Hagar bore to him, IshMaEl.
[Genesis] [16]:[16] Abram was 86 years old when Hagar bore IshMaEl.
[Genesis] [17]:[1] Then, when Abram was 99 years old, the Lord appeared to him [again] and said: ‘I am your God. So, if you’ll be pleasing before Me and not do anything for which you can be blamed,
[Genesis] [17]:[2] I’ll establish a Sacred Agreement between you and Me, and I will make you prosper greatly!’
[Genesis] [17]:[3] Well at that, Abram fell with his face [to the ground]. Then The God spoke to him [again], saying:
[Genesis] [17]:[4] ‘Look! ‘I am making My Sacred Agreement with you. Since you’ll become the father of many nations, your name will no longer be called Abram, but AbraHam...
[Genesis] [17]:[5] For I’ve made you the father of many nations.
[Genesis] [17]:[6] ‘I will make you grow tremendously, I’ll make nations come from you, and kings will descend from you.
[Genesis] [17]:[7] ‘I’ll also extend my Sacred Agreement between you and Me to the offspring that comes from you through its generations. It’s a Sacred Agreement throughout the ages that [I] will be your God and the God of the offspring that comes from you.
[Genesis] [17]:[8] ‘Also, I’ll give the land where you’re [now] living as an alien, to you and to your offspring. This includes the entire land of CanaAn… It’ll become yours throughout the ages, and I’ll be their God.’
[Genesis] [17]:[9] Then The God told AbraHam: ‘You must absolutely keep my Sacred Agreement… Both you and your offspring that descends from you through all their generations.
[Genesis] [17]:[10] ‘This is the Sacred Agreement between you and your offspring and Me through all its generations: ‘All of your males must be circumcised…
[Genesis] [17]:[11] The foreskin of their flesh must be circumcised, for this will be the sign of the Sacred Agreement between you and Me.
[Genesis] [17]:[12] ‘All of your male children must be circumcised by you when they’re 8-days old, throughout all your generations. [This includes all your] home-born servants and those who are bought with money (the sons of aliens that are not your offspring).
[Genesis] [17]:[13] ‘Those who are born in your house and those who are bought with money must surely be circumcised. So My Sacred Agreement will be in their flesh as [a sign of the] Sacred Agreement throughout the ages.
[Genesis] [17]:[14] ‘As for the uncircumcised males who aren’t circumcised in the flesh of their foreskin on the 8th day... Such individuals must be totally destroyed from among their families for breaking My Sacred Agreement!’
[Genesis] [17]:[15] Then The God told AbraHam: ‘Your wife Sara will no longer be called Sara… SarAh will be her name.
[Genesis] [17]:[16] For I’ll bless her and give you a son from her, whom I will also bless… nations and kings of nations will come from him!’
[Genesis] [17]:[17] Well with that, AbraHam fell to his face and laughed, asking in his heart: ‘Will a 100-year-old [man] father a child? And will SarAh –who is 90 years old– give birth to it?’
[Genesis] [17]:[18] Then AbraHam said to God: ‘Please accept IshMaEl to [stand] before You.’
[Genesis] [17]:[19] But God told AbraHam: ‘Look; your wife SarAh will give birth to your son, and you should name him IsaAc [which means ‘Laughter’]. ‘I’ll make my Sacred Agreement [with you] firm through him… It’ll be an age-long Sacred Agreement that I’ll be his God and [the God] of his offspring that descends from him.
[Genesis] [17]:[20] ‘As for IshMaEl; {Look!} I’ve heard you and I’ve blest him. I’ll make him grow and multiply tremendously, so he will become the father of 12 nations that I’ll make a great people.
[Genesis] [17]:[21] ‘However, My Sacred Agreement will be established with IsaAc, whom SarAh will bear to you at this time next year.’
[Genesis] [17]:[22] Then The God stopped talking to him, and He left AbraHam.
[Genesis] [17]:[23] Well thereafter, AbraHam took his son IshMaEl, all of his home-born servants, all of those whom he’d bought with money… All the males in AbraHam’s house, and circumcised their foreskins on that very day, just as God had told him.
[Genesis] [17]:[24] AbraHam was 99 years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin,
[Genesis] [17]:[25] and his son IshMaEl was 13 years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin.
[Genesis] [17]:[26] Both AbraHam and his son IshMaEl were circumcised that very day,
[Genesis] [17]:[27] along with all the men of his house… Those who were born there and the foreigners who were bought with money.
[Genesis] [18]:[1] God [next] appeared to [AbraHam] around noon, as he was sitting at the entrance to his tent by the big tree close to MamRe.
[Genesis] [18]:[2] For when he looked up, he saw three men standing in front of him. And when he noticed them, he ran from the entrance of his tent to meet them, bowing all the way to the ground.
[Genesis] [18]:[3] Then he said: ‘Lords, ‘If I have indeed found favor in your sight, don’t pass your servant by.
[Genesis] [18]:[4] [I’ll have] water brought and [my servants] will wash your feet! You just rest here under this tree.
[Genesis] [18]:[5] I’ll also bring some bread for you to eat, and then you can continue your journey… Allow your servant to offer you some refreshment.’ And they replied: ‘You may do as you’ve said.’
[Genesis] [18]:[6] So AbraHam ran back to SarAh (who was in the tent) and said to her: ‘Hurry… Knead three scoops of fine flour and make [some bread].’
[Genesis] [18]:[7] Then AbraHam ran to the pens, where he took a young calf (a nice, tender one) and gave it to his servant, who quickly prepared it.
[Genesis] [18]:[8] Next, he got some butter, some milk, and the calf that he’d prepared, and set it all out before them… And they ate as he stood near them under the tree.
[Genesis] [18]:[9] Then the Lord asked: ‘Where is your woman SarAh?’ And [AbraHam] replied: ‘Look, she’s there in the tent!’
[Genesis] [18]:[10] So the Lord said: ‘I’ll return this way and come to see you during this season [next year], and your woman SarAh will have a son.’ Well, SarAh overheard this as she stood behind him at the entrance of the tent.
[Genesis] [18]:[11] And because AbraHam and SarAh were old, and SarAh was [well beyond the age of child bearing], she laughed inside herself, saying:
[Genesis] [18]:[12] ‘This hasn’t happened to me [in the past]… And now my lord is [too] old!’
[Genesis] [18]:[13] And at that, the Lord asked AbraHam: ‘Why is SarAh laughing inside herself and asking, ‘Will I give birth? I’m already old’?
[Genesis] [18]:[14] ‘Is there anything that’s impossible for [Jehovah]? ‘I’ll return to you [next year] in this season, and SarAh will have a son!’
[Genesis] [18]:[15] However, SarAh denied it, saying, ‘I didn’t laugh’ (she said this because she was afraid). And the Lord replied: ‘Oh, but you did laugh.’
[Genesis] [18]:[16] Then the men got up and headed towards Sodom and GomorRah, and AbraHam traveled along with them to assist in their journey.
[Genesis] [18]:[17] So the Lord then asked: ‘Shall I hide the things that I’m about to do from my servant AbraHam?
[Genesis] [18]:[18] ‘For AbraHam will become a great and highly populated nation through whom all the nations of the earth will be blest,
[Genesis] [18]:[19] because I know that he will order his sons and the house that is to come from him to keep the ways of [Jehovah]… To be righteous and just, so that [Jehovah] can bring all the things to AbraHam that He’s promised.’
[Genesis] [18]:[20] Then the Lord told him this: ‘The cries that I’m hearing about Sodom and GomorRah keep growing, and their sins are very bad.
[Genesis] [18]:[21] So I’m going down to see if they’re as bad as the cries that I’m hearing have said. ‘And if not, at least I’ll know [for sure].’
[Genesis] [18]:[22] And at that, the men headed towards Sodom. Meanwhile, AbraHam was still there in the Lord’s presence.
[Genesis] [18]:[23] So AbraHam went up to him and asked: ‘Are you going to destroy the righteous along with the wicked, treating the righteous as though they were wicked?
[Genesis] [18]:[24] If there are 50 righteous [people] in the city, will you destroy them? Wouldn’t you spare the whole place if there were 50 righteous [people] there?
[Genesis] [18]:[25] ‘You would never do such a thing as to destroy the righteous along with the wicked and treat the righteous as though they were wicked… No way! Won’t you, the judge of the whole earth, do what’s right?’
[Genesis] [18]:[26] And the Lord said: ‘If there are 50 righteous [people] in the city of Sodom, I’ll spare the whole city and the whole place for their sakes.’
[Genesis] [18]:[27] Then AbraHam continued: ‘My Lord, ‘Here I’m speaking to you, and all I am is dirt and ashes.
[Genesis] [18]:[28] However, what if there weren’t 50 righteous [people] and there were only 45. Would you destroy the whole city because of the lack of 5?’ And the Lord said: ‘I won’t destroy it if I can find 45 there.’
[Genesis] [18]:[29] However, [AbraHam] just kept talking to him and said: ‘What if there are only 40?
[Genesis] [18]:[30] Would you not destroy it for the sake of the 40?’ And he went on: ‘Lord, please don’t hold it against me if I continue to speak; but, what if there are 30?’ And the Lord replied: ‘I won’t destroy it for the sake of 30.’
[Genesis] [18]:[31] So he said: ‘Since I’m allowed to speak to [my] Lord; what if you can only find 20?’ And he said: ‘I won’t destroy it if I can only find 20.’
[Genesis] [18]:[32] Finally, he said: ‘Lord, ‘Would you hold it against me if I were to say just one more thing? What if you were to find just 10 [righteous people]?’ And he replied: ‘I won’t destroy it for the sake of the 10.’
[Genesis] [18]:[33] Then the Lord stopped speaking to AbraHam and left, and AbraHam returned to his [tent].
[Genesis] [19]:[1] Well, that evening, the two messengers [of God] finally arrived at Sodom, where they found Lot sitting by the [city] gate. And when Lot saw them, he got up [and went] to meet them, bowing low with his face to the ground. He said:
[Genesis] [19]:[2] ‘Look here, my lords; come to the house of your servant and rest from your journey. [Then you can] wash your feet and get up early in the morning to continue on your way.’ However, they said: ‘No, we’ll just sleep here in the street.’
[Genesis] [19]:[3] But [Lot] kept insisting, so they went with him to his house. Then he baked flatbread and made a feast for them, which they ate.
[Genesis] [19]:[4] [Well, that evening], before they went to bed, the men of the city of Sodom gathered around the house… All of them, from the young to the old,
[Genesis] [19]:[5] and they shouted for Lot, saying: ‘Where are the men who came to your home this evening? ‘Send them out to us, so we can [have sex] with them!’
[Genesis] [19]:[6] Well, Lot went out on his porch, shut the door behind him,
[Genesis] [19]:[7] and said: ‘Absolutely not, my brothers! Don’t do this wicked thing!
[Genesis] [19]:[8] ‘I have two daughters that have never [had sex] with a man. I’ll bring them out to you and you can do whatever you want with them. However, don’t harm these men! It was to avoid such a thing that [I brought them] under the shelter of my roof!’
[Genesis] [19]:[9] But they replied: ‘Get out of the way! You came here to live among us, and [now, do you think] have become our judge? ‘We’re going to do more harm to you than we’ll do to them!’
[Genesis] [19]:[10] So they started pushing Lot and were ready to break down his door. But the [messengers] reached out and grabbed Lot, dragged him back inside the house, and shut the door.
[Genesis] [19]:[11] Then they struck the men who were at the door of the house with blindness, both the great and the small… Until they finally got tired of trying to find the door.
[Genesis] [19]:[12] And the [messengers] said to Lot: ‘If you have any sons, daughters, sons in law, or any friends in the city, you must take them away from this place,
[Genesis] [19]:[13] because we’re going to destroy it! ‘A great cry has been raised against [this city] to [Jehovah], and [He] has sent us to destroy it.’
[Genesis] [19]:[14] So Lot went and spoke to his [future] sons-in-law that [were engaged to] his daughters, and said: ‘Get up and leave this place, because [Jehovah] is going to destroy the city!’ However, to his [future] sons-in-law, it seemed as though he was joking.
[Genesis] [19]:[15] Then the next morning, the messengers started to hurry Lot along, saying: ‘Get up! Take your wife and your two daughters and go, so you won’t be destroyed with the sins of this city!’
[Genesis] [19]:[16] However, they were unsure. So the messengers grabbed the hands of Lot, his wife, and his two daughters… And that’s how [Jehovah] saved them.
[Genesis] [19]:[17] Then, once they were outside [of the city], the [messengers] told them: ‘Now, do whatever you must to save your own lives. You must not turn around and look back at the things that are behind you… And don’t stay anywhere in the countryside around here. Run to the mountains, so you won’t be [destroyed along] with the rest!’
[Genesis] [19]:[18] But Lot said: ‘I beg you, Lord, ‘Your servant has been shown such mercy and you have shown such righteousness in the things that you’ve done for me to save my life.
[Genesis] [19]:[19] However, I won’t be able to make it to the mountains, because the [destruction] will likely catch up with me and kill me.
[Genesis] [19]:[20] ‘Look, there’s a town nearby… A small one that I can escape to and be spared. Isn’t this just a small thing? ‘If you [allow] this, you’ll save my life!’
[Genesis] [19]:[21] And [the messenger] told him: ‘Look; I’ll respect your wishes in this matter and I won’t destroy the town that you’re talking about.
[Genesis] [19]:[22] But hurry and get out of here, because I won’t be able to do anything until you get there.’ And from that point on, [Lot] referred to that town as Segor [meaning, ‘small’].
[Genesis] [19]:[23] Well, the sun was already up by the time that Lot arrived in Segor, and that’s when
[Genesis] [19]:[24] [Jehovah] poured fire and sulfur from the sky upon Sodom and GomorRah,
[Genesis] [19]:[25] which destroyed those cities, all the countryside around them and everyone who lived in the cities… Including even the plants that grew on the ground.
[Genesis] [19]:[26] However, [Lot’s] wife had turned and looked back, and she then became an upright block of salt.
[Genesis] [19]:[27] Well, that morning (as AbraHam arose early to go to the place where he’d stood before the Lord)
[Genesis] [19]:[28] when he looked towards Sodom, GomorRah, and the surrounding countryside, he saw what looked like the flames and smoke of a furnace arising from that land!
[Genesis] [19]:[29] And this is how it all happened. However, when God destroyed all the cities around there, He remembered AbraHam and He brought Lot out of the midst of that destruction, when the Lord overthrew those cities where Lot had been living.
[Genesis] [19]:[30] Well after that, Lot and his daughters left Segor and they went to live in the mountains, because he was afraid to live in Segor. So he and his daughters went and lived in a cave.
[Genesis] [19]:[31] [It was there that] the eldest [daughter] said to the younger: ‘Our father is old, and no one on earth will come to us here where we’re living...
[Genesis] [19]:[32] So let’s get our father drunk with wine and then we’ll sleep with him, so we can raise our father’s offspring.’
[Genesis] [19]:[33] Well, that night, they brought their father some wine to drink, and the eldest went in and laid down with him. However, he wasn’t aware of when he went to sleep or when he got up.
[Genesis] [19]:[34] Then the next day, the eldest said to the younger: ‘Look; I slept with our father last night. Therefore, let’s get him some wine to drink again tonight, and then you go in and sleep with him, so we can raise offspring from our father.’
[Genesis] [19]:[35] Well, they got their father to drink wine again, and the younger went in and slept with her father that night… And he didn’t know when he went to sleep or when he got up.
[Genesis] [19]:[36] As a result, the two daughters of Lot became pregnant by their father.
[Genesis] [19]:[37] Then the eldest bore a son whom she called MoAb, saying: ‘He’s of my father.’ ([MoAb] is the father of the MoAbites to this day).
[Genesis] [19]:[38] And the younger also bore a son whom she named AmMon, saying: ‘He’s the son of my family.’ ([AmMon] is the father of the AmMonites to this day).
[Genesis] [20]:[1] Well, sometime after that, AbraHam moved to the southern part of the country and took up living between Cades and Sur, staying for a while in GeraRa.
[Genesis] [20]:[2] And [there], AbraHam [again told the people] that his wife SarAh was his sister. He didn’t want to say, ‘She’s my wife,’ for fear that the men of that city would kill him because of her. So AbiMelech (the king of GeraRa) sent for SarAh and took her [to be his woman].
[Genesis] [20]:[3] But God came to AbiMelech at night in a dream and told him: ‘Look; you’re all going to die because of this woman you’ve taken, since she [already has] a husband!’
[Genesis] [20]:[4] Well, AbiMelech hadn’t touched her [yet], so he replied: ‘Lord, would you destroy a righteous nation that has sinned in ignorance?
[Genesis] [20]:[5] ‘Didn’t he tell me, She’s my sister? ‘And didn’t she tell me, He’s my brother? ‘I’ve done this with righteous hands and with a pure heart!’
[Genesis] [20]:[6] Then The God replied to him in his [dream], saying: ‘Yes, I know that you did this with a pure heart... That’s why I’ve spared you and [kept you from] sinning against Me, and that’s why I also kept you from touching her.
[Genesis] [20]:[7] ‘So return this man’s wife now, because he’s a Prophet. Then he will pray for you and you’ll continue to live. ‘However, if you don’t return her, you and all that are yours will die.’
[Genesis] [20]:[8] So early the next morning, AbiMelech got up and called all his servants in; then he told them everything that was said, which frightened them.
[Genesis] [20]:[9] And thereafter, AbiMelech called AbraHam in and asked: ‘What have you done to us? [What type of bad] have you seen in me that you should do such a thing? Have we sinned against you in some way so that you’d draw my whole kingdom and me into such a great sin? ‘Why, you’ve done something to me that no one should ever do!’
[Genesis] [20]:[10] And AbiMelech continued: ‘What [bad] have you seen in me that you would do such a thing?’
[Genesis] [20]:[11] Then AbraHam replied: ‘[I thought] that this surely couldn’t be a place of godly people, so they’ll kill me for my wife.
[Genesis] [20]:[12] [And in fact], she really is my sister by my father (but not by my mother), whom I took as my wife.
[Genesis] [20]:[13] ‘So when God took me from my father’s house, I told her: ‘I have a righteous thing that I want you to do for me: Wherever we go, tell [people] that I’m your brother.’
[Genesis] [20]:[14] Then AbiMelech returned his wife SarAh, along with 1,000 silver coins, as well as sheep, cattle, and male and female servants.
[Genesis] [20]:[15] And AbiMelech said to AbraHam: ‘Look, my whole land lies before you. So now, go wherever you wish.’
[Genesis] [20]:[16] Then he told SarAh: ‘Look, I’ve given your brother 1,000 silver coins. These are yours as the price of your face and for all the women who are with you… But [in the future, you must] always tell the whole truth!’
[Genesis] [20]:[17] So AbraHam prayed to God, and God healed AbiMelech. [He also healed AbiMelech’s] wife and his concubines, and they thereafter gave birth to children
[Genesis] [20]:[18] (since [Jehovah] had closed all the wombs in AbiMelech’s house due to AbraHam’s wife, SarAh).
[Genesis] [21]:[1] Then the Lord visited SarAh and did as [He had promised] to her.
[Genesis] [21]:[2] She became pregnant and bore a son to AbraHam in his old age, at the exact time that the Lord had specified.
[Genesis] [21]:[3] And AbraHam named the son who was born to him through SarAh, IsaAc [meaning ‘Laughter’].
[Genesis] [21]:[4] Then on the 8th day, AbraHam circumcised IsaAc, just as God had instructed him.
[Genesis] [21]:[5] AbraHam was 100 years old when his son IsaAc was born.
[Genesis] [21]:[6] And SarAh said: ‘[Jehovah] has created laughter for me, because everyone who hears [about this] will rejoice with me.’
[Genesis] [21]:[7] Then she added: ‘Who could tell AbraHam that I’m nursing a child, because I’ve given birth in my old age?’
[Genesis] [21]:[8] Thereafter, the child grew; and on the day that he was weaned, AbraHam prepared a great feast.
[Genesis] [21]:[9] However, SarAh noticed Hagar’s son (the one who was born to AbraHam through the Egyptian [woman]) playfully making fun of their son IsaAc.
[Genesis] [21]:[10] So she told AbraHam: ‘Throw this slave woman and her son out, because I won’t have this slave’s son receive an inheritance with my son IsaAc!’
[Genesis] [21]:[11] Now, those words about his son were very difficult for AbraHam.
[Genesis] [21]:[12] But God said to AbraHam: ‘Don’t allow this thing about your son and the slave woman to become too difficult for you. Listen to whatever SarAh tells you, because IsaAc will be the one who is called your offspring.
[Genesis] [21]:[13] However, I’ll make a great nation of this slave woman’s son, because he’s also your offspring.’
[Genesis] [21]:[14] So the next morning, AbraHam got up, gave Hagar some loaves [of bread] and a skin [bottle] of water, put her son on her shoulders, and sent her away. Then she left there and wandered in the desert near the Well of the Promise.
[Genesis] [21]:[15] However, [before long], the skin [bottle] of water was empty. So she threw her child under a fir tree,
[Genesis] [21]:[16] where she left him, and then she sat some distance across from him (a bow-shot away). And she said: ‘I can’t just watch my child die.’ So she sat there across from him as her child bawled and cried.
[Genesis] [21]:[17] Well, God heard the voice of the child from the place where He was, and a [spirit] messenger from God called to Hagar out of the sky, and asked: ‘Why are you so concerned, Hagar? ‘Don’t worry; for God has heard the child’s voice from where He is.
[Genesis] [21]:[18] So now, get up and take the child by his hand, because I’m going to make a great nation of him!’
[Genesis] [21]:[19] Then The God opened her eyes and she saw a life [sustaining] well of water; so she went and filled the skin with water and gave the child a drink.
[Genesis] [21]:[20] God was with that child, so he grew up living in the desert and he became an archer.
[Genesis] [21]:[21] And while he was living there in the desert, his mother found a woman for him in Pharan, Egypt.
[Genesis] [21]:[22] Now, the time came when AbiMelech, OchoZath (his trusted friend), and Pichol (the head of his army) [came to] AbraHam and said: ‘God is with you [and has blest] everything that you do.
[Genesis] [21]:[23] So swear to me by God that you won’t harm me, my offspring, or my name; rather, you should deal with me in the same righteous way that I’ve dealt with you in this land in which you’re living.’
[Genesis] [21]:[24] And AbraHam said: ‘I swear.’
[Genesis] [21]:[25] Then AbraHam complained to AbiMelech about some water wells that his servants had taken from him.
[Genesis] [21]:[26] And AbiMelech replied: ‘I don’t know who did this thing to you, nor did you tell me about it. Today is the first time I’ve heard of this.’
[Genesis] [21]:[27] And thereafter, AbraHam took some cattle and sheep and gave them to AbiMelech, and they made a treaty.
[Genesis] [21]:[28] Then AbraHam set aside 7 female lambs.
[Genesis] [21]:[29] And AbiMelech asked him: ‘Why have you set those 7 female lambs aside?’
[Genesis] [21]:[30] And AbraHam replied: ‘I’m giving my 7 female lambs to you as testimony to the fact that I dug this well.’
[Genesis] [21]:[31] So thereafter, he named that place, ‘The Well of the Promise,’ because that’s where they swore their oath
[Genesis] [21]:[32] and made their treaty. Then AbiMelech, his trusted friend OchoZath, and Pichol (the head of his army) got up and returned [home] to the land of the Philistines.
[Genesis] [21]:[33] Well, after that, AbraHam planted a field near The Well of the Promise and started calling on the Name of the God of the ages, [Jehovah].
[Genesis] [21]:[34] And he stayed there in the land of the Philistines for many days.
[Genesis] [22]:[1] It was then that God put AbraHam to the test. He called to him, saying: ‘AbraHam… ‘AbraHam!’ And [AbraHam] replied: ‘Look! It’s me!’
[Genesis] [22]:[2] Then [God] said: ‘Take your beloved son (this one whom you so love, IsaAc) then go to the highlands and offer him there on one of the mountains that I’ll tell you about – as a burnt offering.’
[Genesis] [22]:[3] So AbraHam got up in the morning, saddled his burro, and [prepared to] take two servants and his son IsaAc with him. Then, after splitting some wood for the offering, he got up and traveled towards the place that God had spoken to him about.
[Genesis] [22]:[4] Well, it was on the 3rd day that AbraHam looked up and saw the place in the distance.
[Genesis] [22]:[5] Then AbraHam said to his servants: ‘Stay here with the burros; for my son and I will go over there… And after we bow low [before God], we’ll return to you.’
[Genesis] [22]:[6] So AbraHam took the wood for the offering and laid it on his son IsaAc’s [shoulders], and the two went off together, with him carrying both the fire and the knife in his own hands.
[Genesis] [22]:[7] Then IsaAc called out to his father (AbraHam) and said: ‘Father!’ And he replied: ‘What is it, son?’ And [IsaAc] continued: ‘Look! [We have the] the fire and the wood, but where is the sheep for the offering?’
[Genesis] [22]:[8] Then AbraHam said: ‘God will provide His own sheep for the offering, son.’ So they both traveled on, and they
[Genesis] [22]:[9] finally arrived at the place that God had spoken to him about... Then AbraHam built the altar there and laid the wood on it, and he tied his son IsaAc’s feet together and laid him on the wood on top of the altar!
[Genesis] [22]:[10] And just as AbraHam was reaching for the knife to slaughter his son,
[Genesis] [22]:[11] a [spirit] messenger of [Jehovah] called out to him from the sky, and said: ‘AbraHam… ‘AbraHam!’ And he said: ‘Look, it’s me!’
[Genesis] [22]:[12] Then [the messenger] said: ‘Don’t lay a hand on the child and don’t do anything to him! ‘For now I know that you fear God, since you haven’t spared even your loved son for My sake!’
[Genesis] [22]:[13] And when AbraHam looked up, he saw {Look!} a male goat that was caught by its horns on a bush in the thicket. So AbraHam went over and grabbed the male goat; [then he] offered it as a whole burnt offering instead of his son IsaAc.
[Genesis] [22]:[14] Well, AbraHam thereafter named that place, ‘The Lord Was Seen.’ [He did that] so people today would say, ‘This is the mountain where the Lord was seen.’
[Genesis] [22]:[15] Then a messenger of [Jehovah] called AbraHam a second time from the sky, saying:
[Genesis] [22]:[16] ‘This is what [Jehovah] has said: ‘I’ve sworn [an oath] by Myself that, because you’ve done this thing (because you haven’t spared your loved son for Me);
[Genesis] [22]:[17] when it comes to blessings, I’ll bless you, and when it comes to multiplying, I’ll multiply your offspring like the stars in the skies and as the sands on the sea shores! ‘Your offspring will inherit the cities of their enemies,
[Genesis] [22]:[18] and all the nations of the earth will be blest by your offspring, because you’ve listened to My voice!’
[Genesis] [22]:[19] Well thereafter, AbraHam returned to his servants, and they all got up and traveled together to the Well of the Promise. Then AbraHam took up living there at the Well of the Promise.
[Genesis] [22]:[20] Then later on, AbraHam received this report: ‘Look! Melcha has given birth to sons by your brother, NaHor!’
[Genesis] [22]:[21] [They were:] Uz (the first-born), Baux his brother, CamuEl ([who later became] the father of the Syrians), Chazad,
[Genesis] [22]:[22] Azav, Phaldes, JelDaph, and BathuEl (BathuEl [later] fathered RebecKa).
[Genesis] [22]:[23] Melcha bore these 8 sons to AbraHam’s brother NaHor.
[Genesis] [22]:[24] In addition, his concubine (named RheUma) also gave birth to: TaBec, TaAm, Tochos, and Mocha.
[Genesis] [23]:[1] Well, SarAh lived to be 127 years old,
[Genesis] [23]:[2] and then [she] died in the city of ArBoc (HebRon in the land of CanaAn), which is located in a valley. So AbraHam went to SarAh to mourn for her.
[Genesis] [23]:[3] And as AbraHam stood before his dead [wife], he spoke to the sons of Ket, saying:
[Genesis] [23]:[4] ‘I’m just a visitor and a stranger among you; but [please] allow me to buy a burying-place among [your people], so I can bury my dead away from [my place].’
[Genesis] [23]:[5] And the sons of Ket replied to AbraHam, saying: ‘No Sir!
[Genesis] [23]:[6] ‘Listen; you may live among us, but you’re [really] a king from God! So bury your dead in our best tombs! None of us will ever withhold our tombs to keep you from burying your dead here!’
[Genesis] [23]:[7] Then AbraHam arose and bowed low before the people of the land (the sons of Ket).
[Genesis] [23]:[8] And AbraHam said to them: ‘If you approve of me burying my dead out of my sight; then, listen to what I have to say and [please] speak on my behalf to EphRon, son of SaAr...
[Genesis] [23]:[9] ‘[I want] him to give me the double cave that he owns, which is located in his field. I’ll [be happy to] pay whatever it’s worth for a burial-place among you.’
[Genesis] [23]:[10] Now, EphRon happened to be sitting there in the midst of the children of Ket, and [he] answered AbraHam (speaking where he could be heard by all the sons of Ket and by all that were entering the city) saying:
[Genesis] [23]:[11] ‘Pay attention to me, my lord; here before all my countrymen [I say]: Bury your dead!’
[Genesis] [23]:[12] And at that, AbraHam bowed low before the people of the land,
[Genesis] [23]:[13] and he told EphRon (before the people of the land): ‘Since you’re on my side, listen to me; accept the price of the field from me and I’ll bury my dead there.’
[Genesis] [23]:[14] However, EphRon answered AbraHam, saying:
[Genesis] [23]:[15] ‘No, my lord! I’ve heard that the land [is worth] 400 silver coins, but what value is that between me and you? No, just bury your dead.’
[Genesis] [23]:[16] And although AbraHam heard what EphRon had said, he still paid [him] the money, just as he had vowed before the sons of Ket – 400 silver coins that had been approved by the merchants.
[Genesis] [23]:[17] So at that, the double cave that was in the field of EphRon opposite MamRe (the field, the cave that was in it, every tree in the field, and everything that was within its borders) was sold
[Genesis] [23]:[18] to AbraHam as his possession, there in front of the sons of Ket and everyone [who’ll be] entering the city.
[Genesis] [23]:[19] There, AbraHam buried his woman SarAh inside the field’s double cave, which is opposite MamRe (HebRon in the land of CanaAn).
[Genesis] [23]:[20] Yes, the field and its cave were sold to AbraHam as his burying place by the sons of Ket.
[Genesis] [24]:[1] Well by then, AbraHam was very old, and [Jehovah] had blest AbraHam in everything.
[Genesis] [24]:[2] So AbraHam said to his servant (the elder of his house that was in charge of all his possessions): ‘Put your hand under my thigh,
[Genesis] [24]:[3] because I want you to swear by [Jehovah] the God of heaven and the God of the earth, that you won’t take a woman for my son IsaAc from the daughters of the CanaAnites… These [people] among whom I’m living.
[Genesis] [24]:[4] ‘Instead, I want you to go to my country – to the place I was born and to my people – to find a woman for my son IsaAc.’
[Genesis] [24]:[5] And his servant replied: ‘But if the woman isn’t happy and willing to return with me to this land, should I take your son back to that land from which you came?’
[Genesis] [24]:[6] And AbraHam said to him: ‘Make sure that you don’t take my son back there.
[Genesis] [24]:[7] For it was [Jehovah] (the God of heaven and the God of earth) who took me out of my father’s house and out of the land where I was born. He spoke to me and swore to me, saying: ‘I’ll give this land to you and to your offspring.’ ‘[So I know that He] will send His messenger ahead of you… And you must take a woman for my son from there.
[Genesis] [24]:[8] However, if the woman isn’t willing to come with you into this land, you’ll be free from this oath. Just don’t take my son back there.’
[Genesis] [24]:[9] At at that, the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master AbraHam and swore to him.
[Genesis] [24]:[10] Then the servant took 10 camels from his master’s herd and [some of] his master’s valuables, and he traveled through MesoPotamia to the city of NaHor.
[Genesis] [24]:[11] Well, it was towards evening that he [stopped and] rested his camels outside of the city, by the well where the young women went to draw water.
[Genesis] [24]:[12] And he [prayed]: ‘O [Jehovah], the God of my master AbraHam! ‘Bless what I’m doing today, and be merciful to my master AbraHam.
[Genesis] [24]:[13] '{Look!} Here I’m standing by the well where the daughters of those who live in this city come to draw water.
[Genesis] [24]:[14] And may it be that whichever virgin to whom I say: ‘Bring down the water jar so that I may have a drink...’ ‘And she replies: ‘Take a drink, and I’ll also [pour water] for your camels to drink until they’re satisfied...’ ‘I’ll know that this is the one You’ve prepared for Your servant IsaAc, and that You’ve been merciful to my master, AbraHam.’
[Genesis] [24]:[15] Well, before he was even done speaking in his mind, {Look!} RebecKa, the daughter of BathuEl (son of Melcha, the woman of NaHor, AbraHam’s brother) came there carrying a water jug on her shoulders...
[Genesis] [24]:[16] This virgin was very beautiful, and she was in fact a virgin… No man ever had sexual relations with her. She went down to the well, filled her water jug, and [walked back] up.
[Genesis] [24]:[17] Then [AbraHam’s] servant ran to meet her, and said: ‘Give me a little water to drink from your pitcher.’
[Genesis] [24]:[18] And she said: ‘Have a drink, sir.’ So she quickly removed the pitcher [from her head] and allowed him to drink until he was finished.
[Genesis] [24]:[19] Then she said: ‘I’ll also draw water for your camels, until they’ve all had enough to drink.’
[Genesis] [24]:[20] And she quickly emptied the water jug into the trough, and then she kept running to the well to draw, until she’d drawn enough water for all the camels.
[Genesis] [24]:[21] Well, the man paid attention to this, but he didn’t say anything, because he wanted to know whether this was [Jehovah’s] blessing.
[Genesis] [24]:[22] Then, after all the camels were finished drinking, he gave her [two] gold earrings (each weighing about a drachma [1/8th of an ounce / 3.5g]), and he [put] two bracelets on her hands (they weighed about the same as 10 gold coins),
[Genesis] [24]:[23] and he asked her: ‘Whose daughter are you? Tell me! ‘And is there room for us to lodge with your father?’
[Genesis] [24]:[24] Then she replied: ‘I’m the daughter of BathuEl, who is the son of Melcha and whose father was NaHor.’
[Genesis] [24]:[25] And she added: ‘We have straw, a lot of fodder, and a place for [you to] rest.’
[Genesis] [24]:[26] Well at that, the man (who was very happy) bowed low to [Jehovah]
[Genesis] [24]:[27] and said: ‘May [Jehovah] the God of my master AbraHam be praised, [because He] hasn’t allowed His righteousness or His truth to fail my master, since the Lord has led me right to the house of my lord’s brother!’
[Genesis] [24]:[28] Then the young maiden ran and reported what he said to the household of her mother.
[Genesis] [24]:[29] Now, RebecKa had a brother whose name was Laban; and Laban ran all the way to the well to meet the man.
[Genesis] [24]:[30] For when he saw the earrings and the bracelets on his sister’s hands, and when he heard what his sister RebecKa said about what the man had told her, he went to the man as he was standing by the well with his camels
[Genesis] [24]:[31] and said to him: ‘Come on in, you who are blest by [Jehovah]! ‘Why are you standing outside? I’ve prepared the house and I’ve also made a place for your camels!’
[Genesis] [24]:[32] So the man went into the house, and [Laban] unloaded the camels, gave them straw and fodder, and he drew water to wash the feet [of AbraHam’s servant] as well as the feet of the men who were with him;
[Genesis] [24]:[33] then he set loaves of bread before them to eat. However, [AbraHam’s servant] said: ‘I’m not going to eat until I’ve told you the reason why I came here.’ And [Laban] said: ‘Then go ahead and speak.’
[Genesis] [24]:[34] So he said: ‘I’m a servant of AbraHam,
[Genesis] [24]:[35] and [Jehovah] has greatly blest my master. ‘He’s highly respected and has been given sheep, cattle, silver, gold, male and female servants, camels, and burros...
[Genesis] [24]:[36] And SarAh, my master’s wife, bore one son to my master after he’d grown old, to whom he’s given everything that he owns.
[Genesis] [24]:[37] ‘Now, my master made me swear [an oath], saying: ‘You must not take a woman for my son from among the daughters of the CanaAnites… These [people] I’m living among.
[Genesis] [24]:[38] But you should go to the house of my father and to my tribe, and take a woman for my son from there!’
[Genesis] [24]:[39] ‘Then I asked my master: ‘What if the woman is unhappy about coming along?’
[Genesis] [24]:[40] ‘And he replied: ‘[Jehovah] God, who has found me to be acceptable in His presence, will send His messenger along with you, and your journey will be blest. ‘You should take a woman for my son from among my tribe and from the house of my father.
[Genesis] [24]:[41] Then you’ll be free from the curse [of your oath]... And if they won’t give her to you when you get to my tribe, you’ll be freed from your oath.
[Genesis] [24]:[42] ‘So today I came to this well, and I [prayed]: ‘O [Jehovah], the God of my master AbraHam; If you’ll bless this journey that I’m now on,
[Genesis] [24]:[43] {Look!} I’ll stand by this well where the daughters of the people of this city come to draw water. And whichever young woman to whom I’ll say: ‘Give me a little water to drink out of your pitcher...’
[Genesis] [24]:[44] ’...and she replies: ‘Take a drink, and I’ll also [pour water] for your camels to drink until they’re satisfied...’ ‘...this is the woman whom [Jehovah] has prepared for His servant IsaAc, and that’s how I’ll know that You’ve been merciful to my master, AbraHam.
[Genesis] [24]:[45] ‘Well, before I had even finished speaking in my mind, RebecKa arrived with her pitcher on her shoulders. And [after] she went down to the well and drew water, I said to her: ‘Give me a drink.’
[Genesis] [24]:[46] ‘Then she quickly took the pitcher from her head, and said: ‘Take a drink, and I’ll also give your camels [something to] drink.’ ‘So I drank, and then she watered the camels!
[Genesis] [24]:[47] ‘Then I asked her: ‘Whose daughter are you… Tell me!’ ‘And she replied: ‘I’m the daughter of BathuEl, son of Melcha, and whose father was NaHor.’ ‘And that’s when I gave her the earrings and put the bracelets on her hands.
[Genesis] [24]:[48] ‘Well, all of this made me so happy that I bowed low and praised [Jehovah], the God of my master AbraHam, who has truly blest me in such a way that I might take the daughter of my master’s own brother for his son.
[Genesis] [24]:[49] ‘Now, tell me whether you’ll be merciful and just with my lord, so I can know which way to turn.’
[Genesis] [24]:[50] And at this, Laban and BathuEl answered, saying: ‘Since this thing has come from [Jehovah], we can’t answer you in either a bad way or a good way!
[Genesis] [24]:[51] ‘Look! There is RebecKa standing before you… Take her and go! Let her be the wife of your master’s son, just as [Jehovah] has said.’
[Genesis] [24]:[52] And when AbraHam’s servant heard these words, he bowed to the ground to [Jehovah].
[Genesis] [24]:[53] Then he brought out silver and gold jewelry, as well as clothing, and gave it to RebecKa. He also gave gifts to her brother and to her mother.
[Genesis] [24]:[54] And afterward, both he and the men who were with him ate and drank; then they went to sleep. Well, when he got up in the morning, he said to them: ‘Now allow me to leave, so I can return to my master.’
[Genesis] [24]:[55] And her brothers and mother said: ‘Let the virgin stay here with us for 10 more days, and then she can go.’
[Genesis] [24]:[56] But he replied to them: ‘Don’t hold me back, because [Jehovah] has blest my journey. Send me away now, so I can return to my master!’
[Genesis] [24]:[57] And they said: ‘Let’s call the girl and ask [her what she wants to do].’
[Genesis] [24]:[58] So they called RebecKa and asked: ‘Will you go with this man?’ And she replied: ‘I’ll go.’
[Genesis] [24]:[59] So they [agreed to] send their sister RebecKa and all her possessions along with AbraHam’s servant and his attendants.
[Genesis] [24]:[60] Then they [gave] RebecKa a blessing, saying to her: ‘You are our sister; now become ten thousands of thousands, and may your offspring own the cities of their enemies.’
[Genesis] [24]:[61] Thereafter, RebecKa and her female attendants mounted the camels and went along with the man. And the servant, once having received RebecKa, departed.
[Genesis] [24]:[62] Meanwhile, IsaAc had traveled through the desert towards the Well of the Vision, and he took up living in the southern portion of that land.
[Genesis] [24]:[63] It was towards evening that IsaAc had gone out into the plains to think (because he was discouraged). And when he looked up, he saw camels coming.
[Genesis] [24]:[64] It was then that RebecKa looked up and saw IsaAc. So she quickly dismounted the camel
[Genesis] [24]:[65] and asked the servant: ‘Who is the man who is walking across the plains to meet us?’ And the servant said: ‘This is my master.’ So she took her veil and covered herself.
[Genesis] [24]:[66] Thereafter, the servant told IsaAc everything that he’d done.
[Genesis] [24]:[67] And IsaAc went to the house of his mother and took RebecKa, so she became his wife… And he loved her… And IsaAc was given comfort for [the death of] his mother, SarAh.
[Genesis] [25]:[1] Well, after that, AbraHam took a wife again, whose name was KetTura.
[Genesis] [25]:[2] She bore to him: ZomBran, JeZan, Madal, MidiAn, JesBoc, and SoYe.
[Genesis] [25]:[3] JeZan fathered: Saba, and DeDan. The sons of DeDan were the AsShurites, the Latusians, and the Laomim.
[Genesis] [25]:[4] The sons of MidiAn were: Gephar, Aphir, Enoch, Abida, and ElDaAh. These were all the sons of KetTura.
[Genesis] [25]:[5] However, AbraHam had given all of his possessions to his son IsaAc.
[Genesis] [25]:[6] He just gave gifts to the sons of his concubines, then he sent them away from his son IsaAc, to a country in the east.
[Genesis] [25]:[7] AbraHam lived to be 175 years old.
[Genesis] [25]:[8] But AbraHam [eventually found himself in] failing health and he died at a ripe old age… An old man who’d lived a full life; and he was [buried] with his family.
[Genesis] [25]:[9] His sons, IsaAc and IshMaEl buried him in the double cave that was in the field of EphRon (son of SaAr the Kettite), which is across from MamRe.
[Genesis] [25]:[10] So AbraHam and his wife SarAh [were both buried] in that field, inside the cave that AbraHam bought from the sons of Ket.
[Genesis] [25]:[11] Well, after AbraHam died, God blest his son IsaAc. And IsaAc went to live by the Well of the Vision.
[Genesis] [25]:[12] These are the generations of IshMaEl, son of AbraHam, whom Hagar (SarAh’s Egyptian handmaid) had born to AbraHam,
[Genesis] [25]:[13] and these are the names of IshMaEl’s sons by each of their generations: NabaiOth (the firstborn of IshMaEl), then Kedar, NabDeEl, MasSam,
[Genesis] [25]:[14] MasMa, Duma, MasSe,
[Genesis] [25]:[15] ChodDan, ThaEman, Jetur, Naphes, and Kedma.
[Genesis] [25]:[16] Those are all IshMaEl’s sons, whose names are on their tents and dwellings… 12 princes of their nations.
[Genesis] [25]:[17] And this is how long IshMaEl lived: 137 years. Thereafter, [his health started to] fail and he died and was [buried with] his family.
[Genesis] [25]:[18] [IshMaEl] and all his descendants lived [in the area] from Evilat [in the northeast] to Sur [in the southwest], and from Assyria to just across from Egypt.
[Genesis] [25]:[19] And these are the generations of IsaAc, son of AbraHam:
[Genesis] [25]:[20] AbraHam fathered IsaAc. And when IsaAc was 40 years old, he took RebecKa (the daughter of BathuEl, the Syrian of Syrian MesoPotamia, the sister of Laban the Syrian) as his wife.
[Genesis] [25]:[21] Then IsaAc prayed to [Jehovah] about his wife RebecKa, because she was sterile, and [Jehovah] heard him... So his wife (RebecKa) got pregnant.
[Genesis] [25]:[22] And [one day], the babies that were inside her jumped. And she asked: ‘Why did this happen to me?’ So she went to ask [Jehovah],
[Genesis] [25]:[23] and He told her: ‘There are two nations in your womb, and two races will be separated from your belly. One race will become greater than the other, and the older one will serve the younger.’
[Genesis] [25]:[24] Well, when it came time for her to deliver, she [found that] she indeed had twins in her womb!
[Genesis] [25]:[25] The first came out red and covered with hair all over his skin; and she named him Esau.
[Genesis] [25]:[26] Then his brother was born while holding onto the heel of Esau with his hand, so she named him Jacob [meaning, ‘Snatcher of the Heel’]. IsaAc was 60 years old when RebecKa bore them.
[Genesis] [25]:[27] Well, after the boys grew up, Esau became a skilled hunter who lived in the country, while Jacob was a simple man who lived in a house.
[Genesis] [25]:[28] And although IsaAc loved Esau (because he enjoyed venison), RebecKa loved Jacob.
[Genesis] [25]:[29] Then [one day], while Jacob was cooking up some stew, Esau came in from the plains tired and weak,
[Genesis] [25]:[30] he said to Jacob: ‘Let me have a taste of that red stew, because I’m weak.’ (That’s when he started to be called Edom [or Red]).
[Genesis] [25]:[31] And Jacob replied to Esau: ‘Then, sell me your right [as firstborn]… Right now!’
[Genesis] [25]:[32] So Esau said: ‘Look, I’m about to die! What good does this right [of the firstborn] mean to me?’
[Genesis] [25]:[33] And Jacob said to him: ‘Swear to me right now!’ So then he swore to him, and that’s when Esau sold his birthright to Jacob.
[Genesis] [25]:[34] Thereafter, Jacob gave Esau some bread and some lentil stew, which he ate and then he drank, and he got up and left. This is how [little regard] Esau [had] his birthright.
[Genesis] [26]:[1] Thereafter, a famine came upon the land that was greater than past famines that had happened in the time of AbraHam. So IsaAc went to GeraRa to see AbiMelech, the king of the Philistines.
[Genesis] [26]:[2] And there the Lord appeared to him and said: ‘Don’t go to Egypt! Rather, live in the land that I’m going to tell you about.
[Genesis] [26]:[3] Stay in this land and I’ll be with you and bless you! ‘I’m going to give all of this land to you and to your offspring, for now I’ll fulfill the oath that I swore to your father AbraHam.
[Genesis] [26]:[4] ‘I will increase your offspring as the stars in the skies, I’ll give all of this land to your offspring, and all the nations of the earth will be blest by your offspring,
[Genesis] [26]:[5] because AbraHam (your father) listened to My voice and did as I said… He obeyed My commandments, rules, and laws.’
[Genesis] [26]:[6] So thereafter, IsaAc started living there in GeraRa.
[Genesis] [26]:[7] Well, when the men in GeraRa asked him about RebecKa (his wife), he told them that she was his sister, because he was afraid to tell them that she was his wife, as she was very pretty and [he feared that] the men there would kill him for RebecKa.
[Genesis] [26]:[8] Then, after he’d lived there a long time, AbiMelech (the king of GeraRa) happened to lean over to look out his window, and he saw IsaAc playing with RebecKa, his wife.
[Genesis] [26]:[9] So AbiMelech called IsaAc and asked him: ‘Is she your wife? [And if so, then] why did you say she’s your sister?’ And IsaAc replied: ‘Well, I said this so that I wouldn’t be killed for her.’
[Genesis] [26]:[10] And AbiMelech said: ‘Why would you do such a thing to us? ‘Before long, one of my relatives would have had [sex] with your wife, and you would have brought a sin upon us in our ignorance!’
[Genesis] [26]:[11] So, AbiMelech gave a command to all his people, that said: ‘Any man who touches this man or his wife will die!’
[Genesis] [26]:[12] Then IsaAc planted grain in the land; and that year, the barley produced 100 times [more than what he’d planted], for [Jehovah] was blessing him.
[Genesis] [26]:[13] So he became highly regarded and very wealthy, as he continued to prosper.
[Genesis] [26]:[14] For he owned many sheep, cattle, and tillable lands. But as a result, the Philistines [started to] envy him,
[Genesis] [26]:[15] and [they] stopped up all the wells that his father’s servants had dug back in his time, filling them in with dirt.
[Genesis] [26]:[16] Then AbiMelech told IsaAc: ‘[I want you to] leave us, because you’ve become much greater than us.’
[Genesis] [26]:[17] So IsaAc left there, stopping to rest in the valley of GeraRa, where [he decided to] live.
[Genesis] [26]:[18] And once more, IsaAc dug the [same type of] wells that his father’s servants had dug (which the Philistines had stopped up after AbraHam’s death). And he gave them each names, using the same names as his father had used.
[Genesis] [26]:[19] Then when IsaAc’s servants dug in the valley of GeraRa, they found a live well of water.
[Genesis] [26]:[20] However, the shepherds of GeraRa argued with IsaAc’s shepherds, claiming that the water was theirs. So they named the well Injury, because [they claimed] injury over this matter.
[Genesis] [26]:[21] As a result, he left that place and dug another well. [But then the people] started claiming [that it was theirs also]. So he named it Hatred.
[Genesis] [26]:[22] And he left that place and dug another well, which no one else claimed to be theirs; so he named it Expanse, saying: ‘[Jehovah] has made space for us and He’s prospered us in the land.’
[Genesis] [26]:[23] Then he traveled to the Well of the Promise,
[Genesis] [26]:[24] where the Lord appeared to him that evening and said: ‘I am the God of your father AbraHam! ‘Don’t be afraid, for I am with you! Because of your father AbraHam, I’ll bless you and your offspring will increase.’
[Genesis] [26]:[25] So he built an altar there, and he named it [Jehovah]. Then he set up camp, and IsaAc’s servants dug another well there in the valley of GeraRa.
[Genesis] [26]:[26] However, later, AbiMelech came to him from [the City of] GeraRa with his trusted friend OchoZath and with Phichol, the commander of his army.
[Genesis] [26]:[27] And IsaAc asked them: ‘Why have you come to me here, now that you’ve shown your hatred for me and driven me away?’
[Genesis] [26]:[28] And they replied: ‘We’ve seen that the Lord is surely with you. So we said: ‘Let us swear an oath between him and us.’ ‘Yes, we want to make an agreement with you,
[Genesis] [26]:[29] that you won’t do any wrong to us, and we won’t show any more hatred towards you. After all, isn’t it because we treated you well by sending you away peacefully that you’re now being blest by [Jehovah]?’
[Genesis] [26]:[30] So, [IsaAc] prepared a feast for them, and they all ate and drank.
[Genesis] [26]:[31] And when they got up the next morning, they each swore [an oath] to their neighbors. Then IsaAc sent them away, and they left him in safety.
[Genesis] [26]:[32] However, that very same day, IsaAc’s servants came and [gave him news about] the well that they were digging. They said: ‘We’ve found water!’
[Genesis] [26]:[33] So he named it and the city, ‘The Oath.’ This is why that city is called ‘The Well of the Promise’ [BeerSheba] to this day.

[Genesis] [27]:[1] Well, after IsaAc grew old, his eyes became so dim that he couldn’t see. Then he called Esau, his eldest son, and said to him: ‘Son!’ And [Esau] replied: ‘Look, here I am!’

[Genesis] [27]:[4] Then prepare the meat for me just the way I like it and bring it to me, so I can eat it. ‘Thereafter, I’ll pass my blessing upon your life before I die.’

[Genesis] [27]:[17] Thereafter, she put the meat and the bread that she’d prepared into the hands of Jacob,

[Genesis] [27]:[24] Well after that, [IsaAc] again asked: ‘Are you my son Esau?’ And [Jacob] replied: ‘It’s me.’

[Genesis] [27]:[29] ‘May the gentiles serve you, and may their princes bow low before you. May you be the lord of your brother, and may your father’s [other] sons show you respect. ‘May anyone who curses you be cursed, and may all that praise you be blest.’
[Genesis] [27]:[30] Well, right after IsaAc had blest his son Jacob (immediately after Jacob had left the presence of IsaAc his father), his brother Esau returned from his hunt.

[Genesis] [41]:[5] Then he had another dream. {Look!} There were 7 large and good-looking [heads] of grain that grew on a single stalk.

[Genesis] [41]:[7] Then the [stalk] with the 7 thin and windblown [heads] ate the ones with the 7 large, good-looking [heads]… And that’s when PharaOh woke up… And it was just a dream.
[Genesis] [41]:[8] Well the next morning, he was deeply disturbed [by the dreams], so he sent for all the [dream] interpreters of Egypt and all the wise men. PharaOh told them of his dreams, but no one could tell him what they meant.
[Genesis] [41]:[9] And that’s when PharaOh’s chief cupbearer told him: ‘I just remembered something that I’m responsible for...
[Genesis] [41]:[10] [You were once] quite angry with your servants and you had us imprisoned in the house of the captain of the guard… Both the chief baker and me.
[Genesis] [41]:[11] Each of us had a dream in that same night (both him and me)… But we each had our own dream.
[Genesis] [41]:[12] ‘And there was a young man with us, a Hebrew servant of the captain of the guard, to whom we told [our dreams], and he interpreted [them] to us.
[Genesis] [41]:[13] ‘Well, everything that he said would happen, came true… I was restored to my office and [the baker] was hanged!’
[Genesis] [41]:[14] So, PharaOh sent for JoSeph… They took him from the prison, shaved him and changed his clothes; then he went in to PharaOh.
[Genesis] [41]:[15] And PharaOh said to JoSeph: ‘I had a vision that no one can interpret, and I’ve heard that you’ve listened to dreams and interpreted them.’
[Genesis] [41]:[16] But JoSeph answered PharaOh, saying: ‘Without God, [I couldn’t] give a safe answer to PharaOh.’
[Genesis] [41]:[17] Then PharaOh told JoSeph: ‘In my dream, I was standing by the bank of the river.
[Genesis] [41]:[18] Then out of the river came 7 fat and good-looking cows that fed along the river’s edge.
[Genesis] [41]:[19] And after that, {Look!} 7 more cows came up out of the river that were evil, skinny, and ugly… I’ve never seen worse in the entire land of Egypt!
[Genesis] [41]:[20] ‘Then the 7 skinny, ugly cows ate the 7 fat and good-looking cows…
[Genesis] [41]:[21] They swallowed them down whole; yet, I couldn’t see that they had gone into their stomachs, because they still looked as ugly as they did before. ‘And after I woke up, I went to sleep again.
[Genesis] [41]:[22] Then I saw what looked like 7 large, good-looking [heads] of grain growing from a single stalk.
[Genesis] [41]:[23] And [after that, I saw] 7 more [heads] that were thin and windblown, coming up next to them.
[Genesis] [41]:[24] Then the 7 thin and wind-blown [heads] ate the 7 large, good-looking [heads]. ‘Now, I told all this to the [dream] interpreters, but none of them could explain it to me.’
[Genesis] [41]:[25] So JoSeph told PharaOh: ‘Both of your dreams are the same, for The God has shown PharaOh what He’s going to do!
[Genesis] [41]:[26] ‘The 7 good-looking cows mean 7 years, and the 7 good-looking [grain heads] mean 7 years… So PharaOh’s dreams are both the same!
[Genesis] [41]:[27] ‘Also, the 7 skinny cattle that came up after them mean 7 years, and the 7 thin and windblown [heads] mean 7 years… Therefore, there’ll be 7 years of famine.
[Genesis] [41]:[28] ‘Now, what I’m telling PharaOh is that it’s God’s purpose to show you what He’s going to do...
[Genesis] [41]:[29] And look! 7 years are coming when there’ll be a great abundance throughout the land of Egypt;
[Genesis] [41]:[30] but these will be followed by 7 years of famine, which will be so bad that the abundance Egypt had will be forgotten, and famine will consume the land.
[Genesis] [41]:[31] ‘Yes, the abundance in the land will be gone because of the famine that will follow, since it’s going to be an extremely bad time...
[Genesis] [41]:[32] And the fact that PharaOh saw the dream twice, proves that the things I’m telling you (which will come from The God) are true; for, God will cause it to happen very soon!
[Genesis] [41]:[33] ‘Therefore, search for a wise and discerning man, and put him in charge over the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[34] Also, PharaOh should appoint local governors over the land that must collect 1/5 of all the produce in the land of Egypt during the 7 abundant years.
[Genesis] [41]:[35] ‘They must gather all the food that will come in during the 7 good years, and have all the grain gathered into the hands of PharaOh… And you must store the food in each city.
[Genesis] [41]:[36] ‘This stored food will then [protect] the land during the 7 years of famine that are coming upon Egypt, so [the country] won’t be totally destroyed by the famine.’
[Genesis] [41]:[37] Well, what [JoSeph] said appeared good to PharaOh and to all of his servants.
[Genesis] [41]:[38] So [he] asked his servants: ‘Where can we find such a man as this… Someone who has the breath of God in him?’
[Genesis] [41]:[39] Then PharaOh said to JoSeph: ‘Since God has shown all of these things to you; is there a man who is wiser or more discerning than you?
[Genesis] [41]:[40] ‘I’ll appoint you to be over my house, and then all of my people must do whatever you say… Only I will be greater than you on the throne.’

[Genesis] [41]:[46] Well, JoSeph was 30 years old when he stood before PharaOh, the king of Egypt. So thereafter, JoSeph left the presence of PharaOh and he traveled throughout the land of Egypt.
[Genesis] [41]:[47] And After that, the land did in fact produce well during the 7 years of abundance… By the heaping handfuls!
[Genesis] [41]:[48] So, during those 7 years he gathered much food, because there was such abundance in the land, and he stored it away in each of the cities. He took the food that grew in the fields around each city and stored it in them.

[Genesis] [41]:[53] Well, the 7 years of abundance in the land of Egypt soon passed,

[Genesis] [42]:[8] Well, although JoSeph recognized his brothers, they didn’t recognize him...

[Genesis] [50]:[22] Well, JoSeph continued to live in Egypt along with his brothers and his father’s family for 110 years.
