[Genesis] [50]:[24] Then JoSeph told his [family]: ‘I’m dying. But, God will surely come to you and take you from this land into the land that God swore to give to our ancestors, AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob.’
[Genesis] [50]:[25] Then JoSeph made the Sons of IsraEl swear, saying: ‘When God comes for you, you must carry my bones back with you.’
[Genesis] [50]:[26] So JoSeph died at the age of 110 [c. 1879 BC], and they prepared his body, then they placed it in a [tomb] in Egypt.
[Exodus] [1]:[1] These are the names of the Sons of IsraEl that came to Egypt with their father Jacob and their families:
[Exodus] [1]:[2] ReuBen, SimeOn, Levi, Judah,
[Exodus] [1]:[3] IshSachar, ZebuLun, BenJamin,
[Exodus] [1]:[4] Dan, NaphTali, Gad, and Asher.
[Exodus] [1]:[5] Then [there was] JoSeph [who lived] in Egypt; so altogether, there were 75 of these people who [descended] from Jacob.
[Exodus] [1]:[6] [In time], JoSeph, his brothers, and that entire generation died.
[Exodus] [1]:[7] But the children of IsraEl grew and multiplied into a large and strong [nation], and the land helped them to grow.
[Exodus] [1]:[8] Then a new king became the ruler over Egypt who didn’t know JoSeph [possibly SobeKemsaf I].
[Exodus] [1]:[9] And he said to his nation: '{Look!} The children of IsraEl have [grown tremendously] and they’re now more powerful than we are!
[Exodus] [1]:[10] ‘So, let’s be crafty in the ways that we deal with them, because if they continue to grow, and then we find ourselves at war, they could side with our enemies! ‘And after they beat us in war, they will leave our land!’
[Exodus] [1]:[11] So he appointed [governors] over them, whose [job] was to make them do hard labor; and they built fortified cities for PharaOh, including Pithom, RaMesse, and On (the City of the Sun).
[Exodus] [1]:[12] But the more they held [the IsraElites] down, the faster they grew. Well, they multiplied so much and grew so strong that the Egyptians hated the children of IsraEl!
[Exodus] [1]:[13] So the Egyptians became tyrants over IsraEl
[Exodus] [1]:[14] and made their lives unbearable by forcing them to work hard by making bricks from clay and working in the fields… Whatever needed to be done. And they were also dealt with violently.
[Exodus] [1]:[15] Then the king of Egypt told the midwives that [served] the Hebrews (one was SepPhora and the other was Poua):
[Exodus] [1]:[16] ‘When you serve as midwives to the Hebrew women and they’re about to give birth, kill [the baby] if it’s a boy, but leave it alone if it’s a girl.’
[Exodus] [1]:[17] However, the midwives feared God and wouldn’t do what the king of Egypt told them… They allowed the male [babies] to live.
[Exodus] [1]:[18] So, the king of Egypt called for the midwives and asked them: ‘Why haven’t you [killed] the male [babies]?’
[Exodus] [1]:[19] And the midwives answered PharaOh, saying: ‘Hebrew women aren’t like the women of Egypt, because they give birth before the midwives arrive, so they [already] have their children!’
[Exodus] [1]:[20] As a result, God dealt kindly with the midwives, while the [IsraElites] continued to multiply and grow very strong.
[Exodus] [1]:[21] Also, these midwives that feared God were able to start families.
[Exodus] [1]:[22] Then PharaOh told all his people: ‘Whenever a male is born to the Hebrews, you must throw it into the river… But let the females live.’
[Exodus] [2]:[1] Now, there was a certain man of the tribe of Levi who married one of the daughters of [his tribe].
[Exodus] [2]:[2] Then she got pregnant and gave birth to a male child. And after she saw how beautiful the child was, they hid him for three months.
[Exodus] [2]:[3] But when they could no longer hide him, his mother got a box for him and coated it with tar, put the child inside, then she set it in the mud by the river,
[Exodus] [2]:[4] and she had his sister keep watch in the distance to see what would happen to him.
[Exodus] [2]:[5] Well, PharaOh’s daughter thereafter came down to the river to bathe. And as her handmaids were walking along by the river, they saw the box lying in the mud, so she sent a handmaid out to pick it up...
[Exodus] [2]:[6] And when she opened it, she found the baby inside the box, crying! Well, PharaOh’s daughter felt sorry for it and said: ‘This is a Hebrew child!’
[Exodus] [2]:[7] Then [the baby’s] sister went up and asked PharaOh’s daughter: ‘Would you like me to call a Hebrew [woman] to nurse the child for you?’
[Exodus] [2]:[8] And PharaOh’s daughter replied: ‘Go!’ So the young woman went and called [her] mother.
[Exodus] [2]:[9] Then PharaOh’s daughter said to [the mother]: ‘Take care of this child and nurse it for me, and I’ll pay you.’ So the woman took the child and nursed it.
[Exodus] [2]:[10] And after the boy had grown, she brought him to PharaOh’s daughter and he became her son. [PharaOh’s daughter] named him Moses [Egyptian: Mo-sheh, meaning, to draw], because she said: ‘I drew him from the water.’
[Exodus] [2]:[11] In time, after Moses had grown, he went to see his brothers, the sons of IsraEl. And as he was observing how bad things were, he noticed an Egyptian beating one of his Hebrew brothers of the children of IsraEl.
[Exodus] [2]:[12] Then he looked around and he didn’t see anyone, so he bludgeoned the Egyptian and buried [his body] in the sand.
[Exodus] [2]:[13] Well, on the next day, he noticed two Hebrew men fighting, and he asked the bully: ‘Why are you beating your neighbor?’
[Exodus] [2]:[14] And he replied: ‘Who appointed you to be our ruler and judge? Are you going to kill me like you killed that Egyptian yesterday?’ This stunned Moses, and he thought: ‘If [he knows], then others will know!’
[Exodus] [2]:[15] And when PharaOh found out about it, he tried to have Moses put to death. So Moses withdrew from the face of PharaOh and went to live in the land of MidiAn. Then, upon arriving in the land of MidiAn, he sat down next to a well.
[Exodus] [2]:[16] And nearby, the 7 daughters of the Priest of MidiAn happened to be grazing their father’s sheep. Then, when they came [to the well] to fill their buckets to water the flock,
[Exodus] [2]:[17] some shepherds arrived and [tried to] chase them away. However, Moses stood up and protected them. And thereafter, he drew water for them and watered their sheep.
[Exodus] [2]:[18] Well, after they returned to their home, their father (RagouEl) asked them: ‘Why have you returned so quickly today?’
[Exodus] [2]:[19] And they replied: ‘An Egyptian protected us from the shepherds; and then he drew water for us and watered our sheep.’
[Exodus] [2]:[20] So [RaguEl] asked his daughters: ‘Where is he… Why did you leave the man? Invite him over [for a meal].’
[Exodus] [2]:[21] Well [after that], Moses developed a good relationship with the man, and [RaguEl] gave his daughter SepPhoran to be Moses’ wife.
[Exodus] [2]:[22] Then she got pregnant and gave birth to a son, whom Moses named GerSam [meaning, Visitor], for he said: ‘I’m a visitor in a strange land.’
[Exodus] [2]:[23] After a while, the king of Egypt died. But the children of IsraEl kept groaning and crying because of their hard work. And the cries over their labor ascended to God!
[Exodus] [2]:[24] [He] heard their groaning and God remembered the Sacred Agreement He had made with AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob...
[Exodus] [2]:[25] So He [started paying attention] to the children of IsraEl, and He made Himself known to them.
[Exodus] [3]:[1] It was while Moses was out tending the flock of his father-in-law (His Excellence, the Priest of MidiAn) that he’d led the sheep into the desert to the dry mountain.
[Exodus] [3]:[2] And there, [Jehovah’s] messenger appeared to him in a flame that was burning in a bush. He saw the flames in the bush, but [the bush] wasn’t really burning.
[Exodus] [3]:[3] And Moses said: ‘I’ll get closer, so I can see this great sight… To find out why the bush isn’t being burned!’
[Exodus] [3]:[4] And when [God] saw him drawing closer to look, the Lord called to him from the bush. He said: ‘Moses! ‘Moses!’ And [Moses] asked: ‘What is it?’
[Exodus] [3]:[5] And He said: ‘Don’t come any closer. Take your sandals off, because you’re standing on holy ground.’
[Exodus] [3]:[6] Then He said: ‘I am the God of your ancestors… The God of AbraHam, the God of IsaAc, and the God of Jacob.’ Well at that, Moses turned his face away, because he was afraid to look at God.
[Exodus] [3]:[7] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘I’ve seen the hardships that My people are enduring in Egypt, and I’ve heard their cries about their task-masters, so I know what they’re going through.
[Exodus] [3]:[8] ‘Now, I’ve come down here to free them from the Egyptians and to take them away from that land, to a land that’s good and has plenty of room… A land that’s flowing with milk and honey. It’s the place where the CanaAnites, Chettites, Amorites, Pherezites, Gergeshites, Evites, and Jebusites [live].
[Exodus] [3]:[9] ‘For, {Look!} the shouting of the children of IsraEl has now reached to Me, and I’ve seen the suffering that the Egyptians are bringing upon them.
[Exodus] [3]:[10] ‘So now, come; because, I’m going to send you to PharaOh, the king of Egypt, and you’re going to bring My people (the children of IsraEl) out of the land of Egypt.’
[Exodus] [3]:[11] But Moses asked God: ‘Just who am I that I should go to PharaOh the king of Egypt and bring the children of IsraEl out of that land?’
[Exodus] [3]:[12] And God replied: ‘I will be with you! This [place] will serve as the sign that I’m sending you. ‘Then when you bring My people out of Egypt, you must serve God on this mountain.’
[Exodus] [3]:[13] But Moses said to God: ‘Look, I’ll go to the children of IsraEl and tell them: ‘The God of our ancestors has sent me to you.’ ‘But they’re going to ask: ‘What is His Name?’ ‘So, what should I tell them?’
[Exodus] [3]:[14] And God told Moses: ‘I am The Being! Just tell the children of IsraEl that The Being has sent you.’
[Exodus] [3]:[15] Then God said to Moses: ‘Tell the Sons of IsraEl that [Jehovah] the God of your ancestors – the God of AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob – has sent you to them. ‘That has been My Name throughout the ages, and it’s how I shall be remembered from generation to generation.
[Exodus] [3]:[16] ‘So, go and gather the elders of the children of IsraEl, then tell them that [Jehovah], the God of your ancestors, has appeared to you. He’s the God of AbraHam, the God of IsaAc, and the God of Jacob. ‘[And report that] He said: ‘I have looked [down] and [seen] all the bad things that are happening to you in Egypt.’
[Exodus] [3]:[17] ‘And tell them that I will take them away from their oppression in Egypt into the land of the CanaAnites, Chettites, Amorites, Pherezites, Gergeshites, Evites, and Jebusites… A land that is flowing with milk and honey.
[Exodus] [3]:[18] ‘And then they’ll listen to what you have to say. ‘After that, you and the elders of IsraEl must go to PharaOh the king of Egypt and tell him this: ‘The God of the Hebrews has called us, so we’re going on a 3-day journey into the desert to offer a sacrifice to our God.’
[Exodus] [3]:[19] ‘However, I know that PharaOh (the king of Egypt) won’t let you go [unless he sees] a mighty hand [of power].
[Exodus] [3]:[20] So I’ll raise My hand and strike the Egyptians with all the wonders that I [wish to show] to them… And then he will allow you to leave.
[Exodus] [3]:[21] ‘I will also make [My] people look good in the eyes of the Egyptians, so that when you escape, you won’t leave empty handed.
[Exodus] [3]:[22] ‘Women will ask their neighbors and landlords for clothing, and for gold and silver [jewelry], which you’ll then put on your sons and your daughters… So you’ll plunder the Egyptians!’
[Exodus] [4]:[1] Then Moses asked: ‘But, what if they don’t listen to me and do what I tell them to do? Or, what if they say, God hasn’t appeared to you… What should I tell them then?’
[Exodus] [4]:[2] So the Lord asked him: ‘What do you have in your hand?’ And he replied: ‘My walking stick.’
[Exodus] [4]:[3] Then [the Lord] said: ‘Throw it on the ground.’ Well, when he threw it on the ground it became a snake, and Moses ran from it.
[Exodus] [4]:[4] And after that, the Lord told Moses: ‘Now, reach out and grab it by the tail.’ So [Moses] reached out and grabbed it by the tail,
[Exodus] [4]:[5] and it became a walking stick in his hand once again. [And God continued]: ‘That’s why they’ll believe you when you say that the God of your ancestors has appeared to you… The God of AbraHam, and of IsaAc, and of Jacob.’
[Exodus] [4]:[6] Then the Lord told him: ‘Now, put your hand inside [your robe and touch] your chest.’ So, he reached inside and touched his chest; and when he brought his hand out, it was [as white] as snow!
[Exodus] [4]:[7] Then [the Lord] said: ‘Now, put your hand back in and touch your chest once more.’ So, he reached in and touched his chest, and when he brought it out, its color had returned to the regular shade of his flesh!
[Exodus] [4]:[8] [Then the Lord said]: ‘So, if the first sign doesn’t make them listen to you and believe, the second sign will.
[Exodus] [4]:[9] But if they still won’t listen to you or believe after these two signs, then draw some water from the river and pour it out on the dry ground… And the river water will turn into blood.’
[Exodus] [4]:[10] Then Moses said to the Lord: ‘I beg you Lord; I’ve not been good at this in the past, and I’ve not become any better at it since You’ve started talking to your servant… I’m a poor speaker and I talk slowly!’
[Exodus] [4]:[11] And the Lord asked Moses: ‘Who gave man his mouth? Who made both those who can hear and the deaf, as well as those who can see and the blind? Wasn’t it Me… God?
[Exodus] [4]:[12] ‘Now, go on, and I’ll open your mouth and tell you what to say!’
[Exodus] [4]:[13] But Moses continued: ‘I beg you Lord, send someone who is more capable!’
[Exodus] [4]:[14] Well, this made the Lord very angry with Moses, so He said: ‘Look; isn’t Aaron the Levite your brother? I know that he’ll speak for you… Look, he’s coming to meet you, and when he sees you, he’ll be jumping for joy.
[Exodus] [4]:[15] ‘Then you must talk to him and put My words into his mouth, and I’ll open both of your mouths and tell you what to say.
[Exodus] [4]:[16] Let him speak to the people for you… He will serve as your mouth and you will be the things of God to him.
[Exodus] [4]:[17] ‘So now, take this walking stick that turned into a snake in your hands and work miracles with it!’
[Exodus] [4]:[18] Well thereafter, Moses returned to His Excellence (his father-in-law), and said: ‘I’m going to visit my brother in Egypt to see if he’s still living.’ And His Excellence said to Moses: ‘Go in health.’ Well, after some time, the king of Egypt [possibly Kamose] died.
[Exodus] [4]:[19] And the Lord said to Moses (while he was still in MidiAn): ‘Now go… Leave for Egypt, because those who wanted to kill you, are dead.’
[Exodus] [4]:[20] So Moses took his wife and children, mounted them on his animals, and returned to Egypt. Moses also carried along the walking stick [through which he’d received power] from God.
[Exodus] [4]:[21] And the Lord said to Moses: ‘When you return to Egypt, consider all the miracles that I’ve given to you, then you must perform these things before PharaOh. ‘However, I’ll make him hard-hearted and he will still refuse to send the people away.
[Exodus] [4]:[22] So you must tell PharaOh: ‘This is what [Jehovah] has said: ‘IsraEl is My firstborn,
[Exodus] [4]:[23] and I’ve told you to send My people away so they can serve Me; however, if you won’t send them away, {Look!} I’ll destroy all your firstborn!’
[Exodus] [4]:[24] Well, [during their journey], a messenger of [Jehovah] met them along the way at an inn, and he wanted to kill [Moses’ son].
[Exodus] [4]:[25] But SepPhoran grabbed a [sharp] stone and cut off her son’s foreskin. Then she fell at his feet and said: ‘See… The blood of my son’s circumcision is flowing!’
[Exodus] [4]:[26] So because she said, ‘The blood of my son’s circumcision is flowing,’ he left.
[Exodus] [4]:[27] Then the Lord told Aaron: ‘Now, go into the desert to meet Moses.’ So, he went and met him at the Mountain of God, and they kissed each other.
[Exodus] [4]:[28] And thereafter, Moses told Aaron everything that the Lord had said, why he was being sent, and about all the things that he’d been instructed to do.
[Exodus] [4]:[29] So Moses and Aaron went and gathered the elders of the children of IsraEl,
[Exodus] [4]:[30] and Aaron told them everything that God had said to Moses; then he performed the miracles before the people…
[Exodus] [4]:[31] And the people believed and were happy, because God was visiting the children of IsraEl and He had seen how they were being oppressed. So, the people all bowed to their faces before him.
[Exodus] [5]:[1] Well after that, Moses and Aaron went to PharaOh and said to him: ‘This is what [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl, said: ‘Send My people away, so they can hold a feast to Me in the desert.’
[Exodus] [5]:[2] And PharaOh asked: ‘Just who is this [Jehovah], that I must pay attention to anything He has to say and send the children of IsraEl away? I don’t know [Jehovah], and I’m not letting IsraEl go!’
[Exodus] [5]:[3] So [Moses and Aaron] said: ‘The God of the Hebrews has called us to Him, and we’re going on a 3-day journey into the desert to [offer] sacrifices to our God [Jehovah]; otherwise, we’re afraid that He might strike us and we’ll die!’
[Exodus] [5]:[4] But the king of Egypt replied: ‘Why are you, Moses and Aaron, trying to keep people from doing their work? Now, go back and just do your jobs!’
[Exodus] [5]:[5] Then PharaOh said [to his people]: '{Look!} There are huge numbers of them and we can’t allow them to slack off from doing their work!’
[Exodus] [5]:[6] And as a result, PharaOh gave orders to those who were in charge to tell their supervisors
[Exodus] [5]:[7] not to give the people any straw for brick-making as they did the day before and three days before that. He said: ‘Let them gather and carry the straw for themselves!
[Exodus] [5]:[8] However, they must maintain the quota for the daily brick making… Don’t let up on them, because they’re lazy! ‘Why, they came here demanding that we must allow them to [go out and] offer a sacrifice to their God.
[Exodus] [5]:[9] Therefore, make the men’s work much harder, so they’ll pay attention to that instead of to idle chatter!’
[Exodus] [5]:[10] Well, the taskmasters and the supervisors acted quickly, and they told the people: ‘This is what PharaOh says: ‘I’m not going to give you straw anymore.
[Exodus] [5]:[11] Go get it yourselves! Take it from wherever you can find it… But you must still make the same number of [bricks]!’
[Exodus] [5]:[12] So the people were scattered all over the land of Egypt as they gathered stubble for straw.
[Exodus] [5]:[13] And the taskmasters kept pushing them, saying: ‘You aren’t meeting the quotas you had when [we were providing] the straw.’
[Exodus] [5]:[14] But then the supervisors who were assigned over the children of IsraEl by PharaOh’s governors were whipped… And they were asked: ‘Why aren’t you meeting your brick-making quotas as you did yesterday and three days ago?’
[Exodus] [5]:[15] Well as a result, the children of IsraEl’s supervisors went to see PharaOh, and asked him: ‘Why are you treating your servants this way?
[Exodus] [5]:[16] You don’t give us any straw, but you tell us to make bricks anyhow... And now {Look!} your servants have been whipped! Are you going to allow your people to be injured?’
[Exodus] [5]:[17] And he said to them: ‘You’re lazy and you’re slackers! For you said, ‘Let us go and offer sacrifices to our God.’
[Exodus] [5]:[18] ‘Now, go to work instead, because you won’t be given any straw… But you must meet the same quota of bricks.’
[Exodus] [5]:[19] Well, the children of IsraEl’s supervisors realized that they were in a tight situation, since they’d been told that they still had to deliver the same daily quota of bricks.
[Exodus] [5]:[20] So when they saw Moses and Aaron coming to meet them (just after they’d left PharaOh),
[Exodus] [5]:[21] they said: ‘May God look down on you and judge you, because you’ve made us so hated by PharaOh and his servants that you’ve put the sword into their hands to kill us!’
[Exodus] [5]:[22] Then Moses turned to [Jehovah], and said: ‘I beg You, O Lord, ‘Why have You caused trouble for these people, and why did You send me?
[Exodus] [5]:[23] ‘For from the time that I went to PharaOh to speak in Your Name, he’s made things harder for these people… And You still haven’t taken Your people away.’
[Exodus] [6]:[1] And [Jehovah] replied to Moses: ‘Now you’re going to see what I will do to PharaOh; for he will indeed send them away… With a strong hand and a hard pitch he’ll throw them out of his land!’
[Exodus] [6]:[2] And God said to Moses: ‘I am [Jehovah].
[Exodus] [6]:[3] ‘I appeared to AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob as their God – and wasn’t my name [Jehovah] declared to them?
[Exodus] [6]:[4] I established My sacred agreement with them [and promised] to give them the land of the CanaAnites… The land where they were visitors and living as strangers.
[Exodus] [6]:[5] ‘Now, I’ve heard the groaning of the children of IsraEl over the oppressive ways that the Egyptians are keeping them in slavery, and I’ve remembered the sacred agreement [that I made] with them.
[Exodus] [6]:[6] ‘So, go and tell the children of IsraEl that I am [Jehovah] and that I will lead them out of the tyranny of the Egyptians and free them from slavery. ‘I’ll pay their ransom with a hard pitch and a great judgment,
[Exodus] [6]:[7] then I’ll take them to be My people and I’ll be their God… And they’ll know that I am [Jehovah] their God who freed them from the tyranny of the Egyptians.
[Exodus] [6]:[8] ‘Then I’ll bring them into the land that I reached out to give to AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob… I’ll give it to them as their inheritance, for I am [Jehovah]!’
[Exodus] [6]:[9] So, that’s what Moses then went and told the Sons of IsraEl. However, they wouldn’t listen to Moses, because of their fear and their hard work.
[Exodus] [6]:[10] So the Lord told Moses:
[Exodus] [6]:[11] ‘Go and tell PharaOh the king of Egypt to send the children of IsraEl out of his land!’
[Exodus] [6]:[12] And Moses replied to the Lord, saying: ‘Look, the children of IsraEl didn’t listen to me, so how will I get PharaOh to listen to me? Besides, I’m not a good speaker.’
[Exodus] [6]:[13] So the Lord spoke to [both] Moses and Aaron and told them to order PharaOh (the king of Egypt) to send the children of IsraEl out of the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [6]:[14] Now, these were the family heads of each of the houses of [IsraEl at the time]... The sons of ReuBen (IsraEl’s firstborn) were: Enoch, PhalLus, AsRon, and Charmi. They were ReuBen’s children.
[Exodus] [6]:[15] The sons of SimeOn were: JemuEl, JaMin, Aod, JaChin, SaAr, and Saul (a Phoenician woman’s son). These were SimeOn’s children.
[Exodus] [6]:[16] The sons of Levi (and the family heads) were: GedSon, CaAth, and MeraRi. And Levi lived to be 137 years old.
[Exodus] [6]:[17] The sons of GedSon (and the family heads) were: LoBeni, and Semei. CaAth’s sons were:
[Exodus] [6]:[18] AmBram, IshSaAr, ChebRon, and Ozie. And CaAth lived to be 133 years old.
[Exodus] [6]:[19] The sons of MeraRi (and the family heads) were: MoOli, and Omusi.
[Exodus] [6]:[20] Now, AmBram married his cousin JochaBed (the daughter of his father’s brother), and she gave birth to: Aaron, Moses, and MiriAm (their sister). AmBram [died] when he was 132 years old.
[Exodus] [6]:[21] The sons of IshSaAr were: KorAh, Naphec, and ZechRi.
[Exodus] [6]:[22] And the sons of OziEl were: MisaEl, EliShaphan, and Segri.
[Exodus] [6]:[23] Then Aaron married EliShaBeth, the daughter of AminAdab and the sister of NaAsson, and she gave birth to: NaDab, AbiUd, EliEzer, and IthaMar.
[Exodus] [6]:[24] KorAh’s sons were: Asir, ElKana, and AbiAsar. These were KorAh’s children.
[Exodus] [6]:[25] Aaron’s son EliEzer married one of the daughters of PhutiEl, and she gave birth to PhineAs. These are the heads of the family of the Levites, by their generations.

[Exodus] [6]:[27] So, this is what they went and said to PharaOh the king of Egypt (before Aaron and Moses brought the children of IsraEl out of the land of Egypt)
[Exodus] [6]:[28] on the very day that the Lord spoke to Moses.
[Exodus] [6]:[29] For the Lord told Moses: ‘I am [Jehovah]! So, speak to PharaOh the king of Egypt and tell him whatever I say to you.’
[Exodus] [6]:[30] But Moses replied to the Lord: ‘Look, I’m not a good speaker; so how will I get PharaOh to listen to me?’
[Exodus] [7]:[1] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Look! I’ve made you a god to PharaOh, and your brother Aaron is your Prophet.
[Exodus] [7]:[2] ‘So, tell PharaOh everything that I’ve told you to say through your brother Aaron… Tell him that he must send the children of IsraEl out of his land!
[Exodus] [7]:[3] ‘However, I will make PharaOh hardhearted, then I will bring many signs and wonders to the land of Egypt;
[Exodus] [7]:[4] but, PharaOh will still refuse to listen to you. ‘Then I will lay My hand upon Egypt and bring My people the children of IsraEl out of their land by My power and with a great vengeance.
[Exodus] [7]:[5] And all the Egyptians will know that I am [Jehovah], and that I stretched out My hand towards Egypt and brought the children of IsraEl out of their midst.’
[Exodus] [7]:[6] So Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord had commanded them.
[Exodus] [7]:[7] Now, Moses was 80 years old, and his brother Aaron was 83 years old when they spoke to PharaOh.
[Exodus] [7]:[8] Then the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
[Exodus] [7]:[9] ‘If PharaOh says that you must give him a sign or perform a miracle; tell your brother Aaron to throw his walking stick on the ground in front of PharaOh and his servants, and it will become a snake.’
[Exodus] [7]:[10] So when Moses and Aaron went in [and stood] before PharaOh and his servants, they did just as the Lord had instructed them. Aaron threw his walking stick before PharaOh and his servants, and it became a snake.
[Exodus] [7]:[11] However, PharaOh brought in all the Egyptian wise men, warlocks, and soothsayers, and they used their magic to do the same thing…
[Exodus] [7]:[12] They each threw down their walking sticks and they became snakes... But then, Aaron’s walking stick swallowed down their walking sticks!
[Exodus] [7]:[13] Nevertheless, PharaOh’s heart became hard and he refused to listen to what [Jehovah] had instructed them to say. [Plague #1 – Water into blood]
[Exodus] [7]:[14] So, the Lord told Moses: ‘Now, PharaOh’s heart has become hard and he won’t let the people go.
[Exodus] [7]:[15] So, approach PharaOh when he goes down to the river tomorrow morning and meet with him there on its bank... Then take [Aaron’s] walking stick that turned into a snake,
[Exodus] [7]:[16] and tell [PharaOh] that [Jehovah] the God of the Hebrews has sent you to him, and that He says: ‘Send My people away so they can serve Me in the desert! Look, you haven’t listened to Me so far,
[Exodus] [7]:[17] but this is how I’m going to let you know that I am the Lord!’ ‘[Then tell him]: ‘Look; I’m going to slap the water with this walking stick in my hand, and the river water will change into blood.
[Exodus] [7]:[18] And at that, all the fish in the river will die and it’ll stink, so the Egyptians won’t be able to drink water from the river.’
[Exodus] [7]:[19] And the Lord continued: ‘Then tell your brother Aaron to take his walking stick and hold his arms out over all the water in Egypt (over its rivers, canals, ponds, and any standing water) and they’ll turn into blood... This blood will be throughout the entire land of Egypt… Even in their pottery and wooden jars!’
[Exodus] [7]:[20] So Moses and Aaron did just as the Lord commanded them. [Aaron] held out the walking stick and slapped the river right there in front of PharaOh and his servants, and all the river water changed into blood!
[Exodus] [7]:[21] Then all the fish in the river died and the river had a foul odor, so the Egyptians couldn’t drink water from it... And there was blood throughout the entire land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [7]:[22] However, the Egyptian soothsayers used their magic to do the same thing. So the heart of PharaOh became hard and he wouldn’t listen to them… Which is just what the Lord said [would happen].
[Exodus] [7]:[23] Then PharaOh turned around and went back into his palace without looking at anything.
[Exodus] [7]:[24] Well, the Egyptians had to dig [wells] around the river to find drinking water, because they couldn’t drink the water from the river.
[Exodus] [7]:[25] And [Jehovah’s] conquest of the river lasted for 7 days.
[Exodus] [8]:[1] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Now go to PharaOh [again] and tell him that this is what [Jehovah] has said: ‘Send My people away, so they can serve Me.
[Exodus] [8]:[2] And if you don’t send them away, {Look!} I’ll fill your land with frogs…
[Exodus] [8]:[3] the river will teem with frogs, and they’ll get into your houses, into your bedrooms, and onto your beds... ‘[They’ll be] in the homes of your citizens, in the homes of your servants, on your dough, and on your ovens.
[Exodus] [8]:[4] They will also climb on you, your servants, and your people.’
[Exodus] [8]:[5] And the Lord said to Moses: ‘Then, tell your brother Aaron to raise his arms with his walking stick in his hand over the rivers, canals, and pools, to bring up the frogs.’
[Exodus] [8]:[6] So when Aaron held his arms out over the waters of Egypt, it did bring up the frogs; and the frogs that he brought up covered the whole land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [8]:[7] Well, the Egyptian soothsayers used their magic and they too brought frogs upon the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [8]:[8] But then PharaOh called for Moses and Aaron, and said: ‘Pray to [Jehovah] for me and ask Him to take the frogs away from my people and from me! ‘Then I will send [the children of IsraEl] away to offer their sacrifices to [Jehovah].’
[Exodus] [8]:[9] And Moses said to PharaOh: ‘Tell me exactly when I should pray for the frogs to disappear from you, your servants, and your people, [for that’s when they’ll leave] you, your people, and your houses. ‘However, they’ll remain in the river.’
[Exodus] [8]:[10] And [PharaOh] replied: ‘Tomorrow morning.’ Then [Moses] said: ‘It’ll be just as you’ve said… And then you’ll know that there’s no [God] other than [Jehovah].
[Exodus] [8]:[11] For the frogs will be removed from you, your houses, your villages, your servants, and your people. However, they’ll remain in the river.’
[Exodus] [8]:[12] And at that, Moses and Aaron left PharaOh. Then [the next morning] Moses called to [Jehovah] and asked Him to remove the frogs, as PharaOh had requested.
[Exodus] [8]:[13] And [Jehovah] did just as Moses had asked… The frogs died in the houses, villages, and fields.
[Exodus] [8]:[14] Then they gathered them in piles, which caused the whole land to stink.
[Exodus] [8]:[15] Well, when PharaOh saw that there was some relief, his heart became hard again, and he didn’t listen to the things that they told him that [Jehovah] had said. [Plague #3 – Fleas]
[Exodus] [8]:[16] So the Lord told Moses: ‘Now, tell Aaron to take his walking stick in his hand and to hit the dirt on the ground; then fleas will cover the men and animals throughout the entire land of Egypt.’
[Exodus] [8]:[17] So Aaron stuck out his walking stick and hit the dirt on the ground, and fleas covered the men and the animals… There were fleas on the ground everywhere!
[Exodus] [8]:[18] Well, the soothsayers tried to use their magic to do the same thing and bring out the fleas, but they were unable to do so. However, the fleas covered both the men and the animals.
[Exodus] [8]:[19] So the soothsayers said to PharaOh: ‘This is the finger of God!’ But PharaOh’s heart was again hardened and he wouldn’t listen to them and do as [Jehovah] had said. [Plague #4 – Stable Flies]
[Exodus] [8]:[20] So the Lord said to Moses: ‘Get up early in the morning and stand before PharaOh as he’s going down to the water. Then you must tell him that this is what [Jehovah] has said: ‘Send My people away so they can serve Me in the desert.
[Exodus] [8]:[21] _For if you won’t let My people go, {Look!} I’m going to send stable flies to you, your servants, your citizens, and into your homes. The houses of the Egyptians will be filled with stable flies wherever they live in the land. _
[Exodus] [8]:[22] ‘[But this time], I’ll create a marvelous difference in the land of Gesem, where My people are living… There’ll be no stable flies there. Then you’ll know that I am [Jehovah], the God of the whole earth,
[Exodus] [8]:[23] when I create a difference between My people and yours! ‘This is going to happen in your land tomorrow!’
[Exodus] [8]:[24] Well, the stable flies came in huge numbers and they got into the houses of PharaOh, his servants, and everyone in the land of Egypt… The land was virtually destroyed by stable flies!
[Exodus] [8]:[25] So PharaOh called Moses and Aaron [again] and said: ‘Now, go and offer a sacrifice to [Jehovah] your God… [but do it] here in this land.’
[Exodus] [8]:[26] However, Moses said: ‘We can’t do that, because the things we’ll sacrifice to [Jehovah] our God are considered disgusting by the Egyptians. So if we sacrifice such things in front of the Egyptians, they’ll stone us.
[Exodus] [8]:[27] ‘Instead, let us travel three days into the desert, and we’ll offer our sacrifices to [Jehovah] our God there, just as our Lord told us.’
[Exodus] [8]:[28] Then PharaOh said: ‘Well, you can go and sacrifice to your God in the desert; but, don’t go too far… And pray to [Jehovah] for me!’
[Exodus] [8]:[29] And Moses said: ‘Now I’ll leave you and pray to God, so that the stable flies will leave your servants and your citizens tomorrow. But PharaOh… Don’t deceive me again and then refuse to send the people away to sacrifice to [Jehovah]!’
[Exodus] [8]:[30] So Moses left PharaOh and he prayed to God;
[Exodus] [8]:[31] and [Jehovah] did just as Moses said… He removed all the stable flies from PharaOh, his servants, and his citizens.
[Exodus] [8]:[32] However, PharaOh’s heart became hard once again and he wouldn’t send the people away.
[Exodus] [9]:[1] So the Lord told Moses: ‘Go to PharaOh and tell him that this is what [Jehovah] the God of the Hebrews has said: ‘Send My people away so they can serve Me!
[Exodus] [9]:[2] If you don’t send My people away and if you prevent them from going,
[Exodus] [9]:[3] {Look!} the Lord will touch the cattle in your fields – the horses, burros, camels, bulls, and sheep – and many will die!
[Exodus] [9]:[4] ‘I’ll also show a marvelous difference between [the way I’ll treat] the cattle of the Egyptians and the cattle of the children of IsraEl. None of those who belong to the children of IsraEl will die.’
[Exodus] [9]:[5] Then God told him when this would happen. He said: ‘I’ll bring it on the land tomorrow.’
[Exodus] [9]:[6] And the next day, cattle that belonged to all the Egyptians died, but none of the children of IsraEl’s cattle died.
[Exodus] [9]:[7] And when PharaOh saw that none of the cattle that belonged to the children of IsraEl died (not one), his heart became even harder; so he refused to let the people go. [Plague #6 – Blisters]
[Exodus] [9]:[8] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying: ‘Moses should take handfuls of furnace ashes and throw them into the sky before PharaOh and his servants,
[Exodus] [9]:[9] so it can blow like dust over the entire land of Egypt. ‘Then the men and animals throughout all of Egypt will break out with blisters.’
[Exodus] [9]:[10] So Moses carried furnace ashes before PharaOh and threw them into the sky… And they caused blisters to break out on both the men and their animals.
[Exodus] [9]:[11] Well, the soothsayers were no longer able to stand before Moses, because they were also covered with blisters like everyone else in the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [9]:[12] But [Jehovah] made PharaOh’s heart even harder, so he wouldn’t listen to them and do what the Lord told him to do. [Plague #7 – Hailstorm]
[Exodus] [9]:[13] And the Lord said to Moses: ‘Get up early in the morning and stand before PharaOh, then tell him that this is what [Jehovah] the God of the Hebrews has said: ‘Send My people away so they can serve Me.
[Exodus] [9]:[14] For I’ve been sending all My plagues into your heart and into the hearts of your servants and your people, so you’ll know that there isn’t anyone else like Me in the entire earth.
[Exodus] [9]:[15] ‘And now I’m going to raise My hand to strike you and kill your people, wiping them off of the earth.
[Exodus] [9]:[16] For, the very reason that you’ve been allowed to live is so that I might display My strength through you, and so that My Name might be advertised throughout the whole world!
[Exodus] [9]:[17] ‘You’ve taken great pains to keep My people and to not let them go, haven’t you?
[Exodus] [9]:[18] So look! At this same time tomorrow I’ll bring a hailstorm that will be the worst that Egypt has seen since the time it was founded!
[Exodus] [9]:[19] ‘Hurry and gather your cattle, as well as everything else that you have in the fields… All the men and cattle that you can find in the fields... For if they don’t go inside a building, the hail will hit them and kill them!’
[Exodus] [9]:[20] So, those servants of PharaOh that were afraid of what the Lord said brought their cattle into their homes.
[Exodus] [9]:[21] And those who didn’t pay any attention to what the Lord said left their cattle in the fields.
[Exodus] [9]:[22] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Raise your hands to the sky, and there’ll be a hailstorm throughout the entire land of Egypt… On the men, the cattle, and all the plants that are growing on the ground.’
[Exodus] [9]:[23] So Moses raised his hands to the sky, and [Jehovah] sent hail, thunder, and lightning that rolled around on the ground. And this hail from [Jehovah] rained throughout the entire land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [9]:[24] There was hail and there was lightning mixed with hail… It was the greatest hailstorm to hit Egypt in the [history of] that nation!
[Exodus] [9]:[25] The hail landed all over the land of Egypt – on the men, the animals, and the grass in the fields – and it broke all the trees in the fields.
[Exodus] [9]:[26] But in the land of Gesem where the children of IsraEl were, there was no hail.
[Exodus] [9]:[27] So PharaOh sent for Moses and Aaron, and said: ‘I’ve sinned this time. [Jehovah] is righteous, and my people and I are wicked.
[Exodus] [9]:[28] ‘Pray to [Jehovah] for me and have Him stop the thunder, lightning, and the hail; then, I’ll send you away and you won’t have to [live here] anymore.’
[Exodus] [9]:[29] And Moses said to him: ‘After I leave the city, I’ll raise my hands to [Jehovah], and the thunder, lightning, hail, and rain will stop… Then you’ll know that the earth belongs to [Jehovah].
[Exodus] [9]:[30] ‘However, I know that you and your servants still don’t fear [Jehovah].’
[Exodus] [9]:[31] Well, [Egypt’s] flax and barley was all destroyed, because the barley was fully-grown and the flax had seeds.
[Exodus] [9]:[32] However, the wheat and rye hadn’t been damaged, because they came up later.
[Exodus] [9]:[33] Then Moses left PharaOh and [walked] out of the city. And when he raised his hands to [Jehovah], the thundering ended, and the rain and hail stopped falling.
[Exodus] [9]:[34] But when PharaOh saw that the rain, hail, and thundering had stopped, he continued to sin. He hardened his heart and the hearts of his servants.
[Exodus] [9]:[35] And it was because of this hardened heart that PharaOh refused to send the children of IsraEl away, as [Jehovah] had instructed him through Moses.
[Exodus] [10]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said: ‘Go to PharaOh [again], because I’ve hardened the hearts of him and his servants so I could bring these signs upon them.
[Exodus] [10]:[2] ‘[I did this] so you could tell your children and your children’s children of the many ways that I’ve mocked the Egyptians through the wonders I’ve brought upon them, and so that they’ll know that I am the Lord.’
[Exodus] [10]:[3] Then Moses and Aaron went before PharaOh and said to him: ‘This is what [Jehovah], the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How much longer will you refuse to respect Me? ‘Send My people away, so they can serve Me!
[Exodus] [10]:[4] ‘But if you won’t send My people away... {Look!} at this same time tomorrow, I’ll bring huge amounts of locusts to all your borders.
[Exodus] [10]:[5] They’ll cover the entire land, so that you won’t be able to see the ground. They’ll eat everything that the hail has left for you, and chew up every tree that you still have growing in the land.
[Exodus] [10]:[6] ‘Your houses, the houses of your servants, and all the houses throughout the land of Egypt will be filled with them. It’ll be something that neither your fathers nor their ancestors have seen from their time until this day.’ Then Moses turned and left PharaOh.
[Exodus] [10]:[7] And PharaOh’s servants said to him: ‘How much longer are you going to allow them to be a snare to us? ‘Send those people away so they can serve their God! ‘Don’t you realize that Egypt is [being] destroyed?’
[Exodus] [10]:[8] So they went and brought Moses and Aaron back to PharaOh, and he said to them: ‘You may go and serve [Jehovah] your God… But, who will be going with you?’
[Exodus] [10]:[9] And Moses replied: ‘We’ll be taking the young and the old, along with our sons, daughters, sheep, and bulls, because this is a feast of [Jehovah].’
[Exodus] [10]:[10] Then [PharaOh] said to them: ‘May [Jehovah] be with you. But if I send you away, must I also [send away] all that you own? ‘You have an evil [plan],
[Exodus] [10]:[11] so [I’m] not going to [allow that]! I’ll just allow the men to go and serve your God, because that’s all you really wanted. ‘Now, throw them out from before the presence of PharaOh!’
[Exodus] [10]:[12] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Raise your hands over the land of Egypt and let the locusts come to the land. They’ll eat every plant on the ground and all the fruit that wasn’t damaged by the hail on the trees!’
[Exodus] [10]:[13] So Moses raised his walking stick to the sky, and [Jehovah] sent a south wind [that blew] all day and all night long... Then the next morning, the south wind brought the locusts,
[Exodus] [10]:[14] sending them throughout the land of Egypt. And there they sat in huge numbers throughout all the borders of Egypt. Never had such locusts been seen before or since!
[Exodus] [10]:[15] They covered the entire ground and they devastated the land. They ate all the plants off the ground and any fruit in the trees that hadn’t been damaged by the hail… Nothing green was left on the trees or in the fields anywhere in the land of Egypt!
[Exodus] [10]:[16] Then PharaOh hastily called Moses and Aaron, and said: ‘I have sinned before [Jehovah] your God and against you.
[Exodus] [10]:[17] ‘[Please] pardon my sin one more time and pray to [Jehovah] your God… Ask Him to take away this death!’
[Exodus] [10]:[18] So Moses left PharaOh and prayed to God;
[Exodus] [10]:[19] then [Jehovah] sent a strong wind from the sea that blew in the opposite direction, picking up the locusts and throwing them into the Red Sea… And there wasn’t a single locust left anywhere in the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [10]:[20] But [Jehovah] continued to harden PharaOh’s heart, so he didn’t send the children of IsraEl away. [Plague #9 – Darkness]
[Exodus] [10]:[21] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Now lift your hands towards the sky and bring darkness to the land of Egypt… A darkness that can be felt.’
[Exodus] [10]:[22] So Moses raised his hands to the sky, and it stormed throughout the land of Egypt for three days… And the sky became totally black!
[Exodus] [10]:[23] Well, for the next three days, nobody could see anyone else, so no one even got out of bed. However, all the children of IsraEl had light where they were.
[Exodus] [10]:[24] Then PharaOh called Moses and Aaron, and said: ‘Now, go and serve your God [Jehovah]… But you must leave your sheep, your cattle, and your belongings here!’
[Exodus] [10]:[25] However, Moses said: ‘No! You must allow us the burnt offerings and sacrifices that we’re going to offer to our God [Jehovah]…
[Exodus] [10]:[26] Our cattle will be going with us! ‘We won’t leave a hoof behind, because we’re going to take them to serve [Jehovah] our God, and we won’t know how we’re supposed to serve Him until we get there.’
[Exodus] [10]:[27] But [Jehovah] kept hardening PharaOh’s heart and he wouldn’t let them go.
[Exodus] [10]:[28] So PharaOh said: ‘Get away from me, and be careful not to see my face again, because the next time you appear before me, you’re going to die!’
[Exodus] [10]:[29] And Moses replied: ‘That’s what you’ve said, so I won’t appear in your presence again!’
[Exodus] [11]:[1] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘I’m going to bring one more plague upon PharaOh and Egypt… And he will send you away with everything. In fact, he’ll drive you out!
[Exodus] [11]:[2] ‘Now, go to the people secretly and tell them to ask their neighbors for clothing, silver, and gold jewelry.’
[Exodus] [11]:[3] Well, [Jehovah] caused his people to be looked upon favorably by the Egyptians and they were willing to lend things to them, because the Egyptians considered Moses a great man… Even greater than PharaOh and his servants.
[Exodus] [11]:[4] Then Moses told [the children of IsraEl]: ‘This is what the Lord said: ‘About midnight I’ll be going throughout Egypt,
[Exodus] [11]:[5] and all the firstborn in the land will die, from the firstborn of PharaOh that sits on the throne, to the firstborn of the female slave that sits by the mill, as well as the firstborn of all the cattle.
[Exodus] [11]:[6] ‘Then a cry will [be heard] throughout the land of Egypt such as has never been heard before and will never be heard again!
[Exodus] [11]:[7] ‘However, among the children of IsraEl, not even a dog will snarl at a man or an animal. That’s when you’ll see the great difference that [Jehovah] will make between the Egyptians and IsraEl!
[Exodus] [11]:[8] ‘For they’ll then be your servants… They’ll come to [you] and bow, saying: ‘Leave, both you and all the people whom you’re in charge of.’ ‘And that’s when [you’ll] leave.’
[Exodus] [11]:[9] Meanwhile, Moses had left PharaOh [feeling very] angry. And the Lord told Moses: ‘PharaOh isn’t going to listen to you anymore, so now I’m going to bring great signs and wonders to the land of Egypt.’
[Exodus] [11]:[10] Yes, even though Moses and Aaron had been bringing all these signs and wonders to the land of Egypt and to PharaOh, [Jehovah] kept hardening PharaOh’s heart, so he wouldn’t listen and send the children of IsraEl out of the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [12]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron there in the land of Egypt, and said:
[Exodus] [12]:[2] ‘This will be your 1st month. It’s to be the first one [in your] year.
[Exodus] [12]:[3] ‘So, tell the whole gathering of the children of IsraEl that on the 10th day of this month, each man should select a lamb for his household (depending on the size of his family).
[Exodus] [12]:[4] And if there are just a few in his house (too few [to eat a whole] lamb), they may go to [the home of] a nearby neighbor. ‘They are to figure out how many people there’ll be, and then calculate how much lamb they’ll eat.
[Exodus] [12]:[5] ‘So, choose a perfect male yearling lamb from [your herd] of lambs and kids,
[Exodus] [12]:[6] and keep it nearby until the 14th day of this month. ‘Then the whole gathering of the children of IsraEl must slaughter [their lambs] towards the evening,
[Exodus] [12]:[7] and they must gather the blood and splash it on the top and both sides of the doorframes of the houses where they’ll be eating [the lamb].
[Exodus] [12]:[8] ‘Then that night, they must roast the flesh over a fire and eat it with fermentation-free bread and bitter herbs.
[Exodus] [12]:[9] ‘Now, you must not eat it raw or boiled in water, just roasted over a fire with the head, feet, and extremities.
[Exodus] [12]:[10] Nothing should be left over until morning, and you shouldn’t break any of its bones. ‘Then, any leftovers must be burned in the fire.
[Exodus] [12]:[11] ‘And this is how you must eat it: ‘With your thighs covered for work, your sandals on your feet, and your walking sticks in your hands. ‘You must eat it quickly, because it’ll be [Jehovah’s] Passover.
[Exodus] [12]:[12] For I’ll go throughout the land of Egypt that night and strike all the firstborn in that land (both the men and their animals), and I’ll bring My vengeance upon all the gods of Egypt… I am [Jehovah]!
[Exodus] [12]:[13] ‘Now, this blood will be the sign that you’re inside of each house; for when I see the blood, I’ll protect you, and you won’t be a part of the plague of destruction when I strike the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [12]:[14] ‘You must always remember this day and keep it as a feast to [Jehovah] through all your generations… [observance of] this feast will be the law throughout the ages.
[Exodus] [12]:[15] ‘You must eat fermentation-free bread for 7 days. ‘And starting on the 1st day, you must remove all the fermentation from your homes. For if anyone eats fermentation between the 1st and 7th days, that person must be destroyed in IsraEl.
[Exodus] [12]:[16] ‘The 1st day will be called holy, and the 7th day will be your holy day when you aren’t to do any hired work. ‘The only work that you may do will be for the things that you require.
[Exodus] [12]:[17] ‘You must observe this commandment, because this is the day that I will use My great power to bring you out of the land of Egypt… You must make this day a law throughout the ages for every generation!
[Exodus] [12]:[18] ‘You must eat fermentation-free bread from the evening of the 14th day of the 1st month until the evening of the 21st day.
[Exodus] [12]:[19] ‘Fermentation must not be found in your homes during those 7 days, and whoever eats anything with fermentation must have his life cut off from the gathering of IsraEl and he will be self-condemned in the land. ‘This applies to the native residents of your land and your neighbors (converts).
[Exodus] [12]:[20] Yes, nobody should eat anything that has fermentation… Only fermentation-free bread may be eaten in any of your homes.’
[Exodus] [12]:[21] Then Moses called all the elders of the children of IsraEl and told them: ‘Go find yourselves a lamb (according to your family needs) and slaughter the Passover.
[Exodus] [12]:[22] ‘Then [cut] bunches of hyssop branches and dip them into some of the blood next to the door, and touch it to the upper part and both sides of the door frame… With this blood that’s by the door. ‘Thereafter, no one should go outside the door of his house until morning,
[Exodus] [12]:[23] for the Lord will pass over you [as He] strikes the Egyptians… He will see the blood on the doorframes and the Lord will pass over that door, then He won’t allow the destroyer to enter your homes to strike you.
[Exodus] [12]:[24] ‘Now, keep this as a Law for yourselves and for your descendants throughout the ages!
[Exodus] [12]:[25] ‘And when you enter the land that [Jehovah] has promised to give you, you must keep on doing this.
[Exodus] [12]:[26] ‘Then if your sons should ever ask: ‘Why are we doing this?’
[Exodus] [12]:[27] ‘You should tell them: ‘The Passover is a sacrifice to [Jehovah] for when He protected the homes of the children of IsraEl in Egypt and He struck the Egyptians, but [passed over] our homes.’
[Exodus] [12]:[28] Well thereafter, the people bowed to their faces, then the children of IsraEl went and did exactly as [Jehovah] had instructed Moses and Aaron.
[Exodus] [12]:[29] It was midnight when [Jehovah] struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt… From the firstborn of PharaOh that was sitting on the throne, to the firstborn of the female slave that was sitting in a dungeon, and to the firstborn of all the cattle.
[Exodus] [12]:[30] So, PharaOh woke up that night (as did his servants and all the Egyptians) and there was a lot of screaming throughout the entire land of Egypt; for someone had died in every home.
[Exodus] [12]:[31] As a result, PharaOh called Moses and Aaron that night and told them this: ‘Get up and leave us, both you and the children of IsraEl! Go and serve your God [Jehovah] as you’ve asked,
[Exodus] [12]:[32] and take your sheep and bulls with you. ‘But please bless me… I beg you!’
[Exodus] [12]:[33] All the Egyptian people also urged them to leave their land quickly, because they were saying: ‘We’re all going to die!’
[Exodus] [12]:[34] So the children of IsraEl took all their bread dough that hadn’t fermented yet and wrapped it in cloths, and carried it on their shoulders.
[Exodus] [12]:[35] Then, following Moses’ instructions, they asked the Egyptians for clothing, as well as for items of silver and gold.
[Exodus] [12]:[36] And because [Jehovah] had caused the Egyptians to view them favorably, they [gave them these things]… So they plundered the Egyptians.
[Exodus] [12]:[37] Then the children of IsraEl got up and left RaMesse, traveling towards to SocChoth (some 600,000 men on foot) with everything they owned,
[Exodus] [12]:[38] along with a huge number of others who left with them, as well as with their sheep, bulls, and many cattle.
[Exodus] [12]:[39] [And when they got there], they baked the dough that they’d brought from Egypt into fermentation-free loaves (there was still no fermentation in the dough), because the Egyptians hadn’t allowed them to stay any longer. For, since they’d been literally thrown out, they hadn’t been allowed enough time to properly prepare for their journey.
[Exodus] [12]:[40] Now, even though it had been 430 years that the children of IsraEl lived in the land of CanaAn and in the land of Egypt,
[Exodus] [12]:[41] the whole army of [Jehovah] left the land of Egypt that [single] night!
[Exodus] [12]:[42] And since this was [the night] that they kept watching for [Jehovah] to bring them out of the land of Egypt, all the children of IsraEl were to observe it as a night of watch to [Jehovah] throughout all their generations.
[Exodus] [12]:[43] Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron: ‘This is the Law regarding the Passover: ‘No stranger may eat it,
[Exodus] [12]:[44] and any slave or servant that you buy must be circumcised before he can eat it.
[Exodus] [12]:[45] ‘However, visitors and people you hire can’t eat it.
[Exodus] [12]:[46] It must be eaten in one house, because you can’t carry the flesh outside of the house… And no bones should be broken.
[Exodus] [12]:[47] ‘The entire gathering of the children of IsraEl must continue to do this.
[Exodus] [12]:[48] ‘And if any converts come and want to observe the Passover to [Jehovah], you must circumcise all their males before they can [partake of] the sacrifice; for thereafter, they will be treated as residents in the land. ‘However, no one uncircumcised may eat it.
[Exodus] [12]:[49] ‘So, there will be just one Law, and it will apply to both the native residents and to those who come to be converts among you.’
[Exodus] [12]:[50] Then the children of IsraEl did exactly as [Jehovah] had instructed Moses and Aaron...
[Exodus] [12]:[51] And that was the day [Jehovah] brought the children of IsraEl out of the land of Egypt with all their armies.
[Exodus] [13]:[1] Then the Lord told Moses:
[Exodus] [13]:[2] ‘All the first-fathered and firstborn that open any womb among the children of IsraEl, whether of men or animals, are to be set aside as holy to Me, for they are now Mine!’
[Exodus] [13]:[3] And Moses said to the people: ‘Remember this day! [It’s the one] when you were brought out of the land of Egypt and out of the house of slavery; for, [Jehovah] brought you out of there with His strong hand. ‘So, fermentation must not be eaten
[Exodus] [13]:[4] on this day of new grain that you left.
[Exodus] [13]:[5] And when [Jehovah] your God brings you into the land of the CanaAnites, Chettites, Amorites, Evites, Jebusites, Gergeshites, and Pherezites, which He swore to your ancestors that He would give you (a land that’s flowing with milk and honey), you must perform the same service during this month.
[Exodus] [13]:[6] ‘You will all eat fermentation-free bread for 6 days, and the 7th day will be a feast day to [Jehovah]…
[Exodus] [13]:[7] So, you’ll eat fermentation-free bread for 7 days. ‘Nothing with fermentation may be seen among you, nor may you have fermentation inside all of your borders.
[Exodus] [13]:[8] ‘And you must say to your sons on this day: ‘This is how [Jehovah] dealt with me as I was leaving Egypt.’
[Exodus] [13]:[9] ‘Let this always serve as a sign on your hand and as something in front of your eyes to remember, so that [Jehovah’s] Law will always stay on your [lips]! Because, [Jehovah] God brought you out of Egypt with His mighty hand.
[Exodus] [13]:[10] ‘Therefore, each year at this same time and season, you must observe this Law.
[Exodus] [13]:[11] ‘And when [Jehovah] your God brings you into the land of the CanaAnites, which He swore to your ancestors that he would give to you;
[Exodus] [13]:[12] you must set aside every male who [first] opens a womb to [Jehovah]. ‘This includes those among your flocks and herds of cattle… As many as you have. [All the firstborn] males must be [set aside as] holy to [Jehovah]!
[Exodus] [13]:[13] ‘However, when it comes to your burros; you must offer a sheep instead… You can’t exchange it, you must buy it back [from [Jehovah]], and you must buy back every firstborn son.
[Exodus] [13]:[14] ‘And if your son should ever ask you: ‘Why are we doing this?’ ‘You must tell him: ‘[Jehovah] brought us out of Egypt and out of the house of slavery with His mighty hand.
[Exodus] [13]:[15] And when PharaOh’s heart hardened and [he refused] to send us away, [God] slaughtered all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the men and the animals. ‘So that’s why we offer every male that [first] opens a womb to [Jehovah], and that’s why we buy back all of our firstborn sons.’
[Exodus] [13]:[16] ‘Therefore, may this be a sign on your hand and something that’s always fixed in front of your eyes… Because, [Jehovah] brought you out of Egypt with His mighty hand.’
[Exodus] [13]:[17] Well, after PharaOh had sent the people away, God didn’t lead them towards the land of the Philistines (even though it wasn’t far away), because God said: ‘[I’m doing this to keep] the people from having a change of heart when they see war, and from thereafter returning to Egypt.’
[Exodus] [13]:[18] So God led them around the desert towards the Red Sea. It was the 5th generation of the children of IsraEl that left the land of Egypt.
[Exodus] [13]:[19] And Moses took JoSeph’s bones along, because [JoSeph] had made the children of IsraEl swear, saying: ‘God will surely visit you, so you must carry my bones back with you.’
[Exodus] [13]:[20] Thereafter, the children of IsraEl left SucCoth and went to camp at Othom, which is near the desert.
[Exodus] [13]:[21] God led them there using a tall column of clouds during the day (to show them the way) and a tall column of fire during the night...
[Exodus] [13]:[22] The column of clouds was there all day long, every day, and the column of fire was always there in front of the people all night long.
[Exodus] [14]:[1] Then the Lord said to Moses:
[Exodus] [14]:[2] ‘Tell the children of IsraEl to turn around and set up camp in front of the village of the MagDol (the watchtower)… Between it and the sea, across from BeEl-SepPhon. Camp there in front of them, next to the sea.
[Exodus] [14]:[3] For PharaOh will say to his people: ‘The children of IsraEl are just wandering around in the land, and now they’re boxed in!’
[Exodus] [14]:[4] ‘Then I’ll harden PharaOh’s heart, and he will chase after you. So, PharaOh and his whole army will bring glory to Me, and all the Egyptians will know that I am [Jehovah].’ And that’s exactly what happened.
[Exodus] [14]:[5] Well, a report was carried to the king of the Egyptians that the people had run away. And this changed the hearts of PharaOh and his servants against the [children of IsraEl], and they started asking: ‘What have we done by allowing the children of IsraEl to go, rather than having them [stay here and] serve us?’
[Exodus] [14]:[6] So PharaOh prepared his chariots and took his [whole army] with him…
[Exodus] [14]:[7] 600 of their best chariots, the entire Egyptian cavalry, and all his generals!
[Exodus] [14]:[8] And it was because [Jehovah] had hardened the hearts of PharaOh (the king of Egypt) and his servants that he chased after the children of IsraEl. For the children of IsraEl allowed them the upper hand,
[Exodus] [14]:[9] and when the Egyptians caught up with them, they found them camped next to the sea. Well, there was all of PharaOh’s cavalry, chariots, horsemen, and entire army at a village near BeEl-SepPhon!
[Exodus] [14]:[10] And as PharaOh approached, the children of IsraEl could see the Egyptians coming up behind them, which terrified them, so they started calling out to [Jehovah].
[Exodus] [14]:[11] And at that, they asked Moses: ‘Aren’t there enough graves in the land of Egypt so that you had to bring us out here to be killed in the desert? ‘What have you done to us by taking us out of Egypt?

[Exodus] [14]:[13] But Moses said to the people: ‘Don’t be afraid! ‘Stand here and watch the salvation that comes from [Jehovah] – through the things that He will do for us on this day. ‘Do you see all those Egyptians today? You won’t see them again in this age,

[Exodus] [14]:[16] ‘Just lift your walking stick and raise your hands over the sea, and it’ll split open… Then you can [lead] the children of IsraEl across on dry land through the midst of the sea!
[Exodus] [14]:[17] ‘And after that, {Look!} I’ll harden the hearts of PharaOh and all the Egyptians, and they’ll chase after you… For, that’s when PharaOh, his army, his chariots, and all his horses will glorify Me...
[Exodus] [14]:[18] Yes, everyone in Egypt will know that I am [Jehovah] when I’m glorified by PharaOh, his chariots, and his horses.’

[Exodus] [14]:[27] So Moses stretched his arms out over the sea, and the water returned to its place around daybreak. The Egyptians tried to run from the water, but [Jehovah] just kept shaking them back into the midst of the sea!
[Exodus] [14]:[28] Yes, it returned and covered the chariots and their riders, along with the whole army of PharaOh that followed them into the sea, leaving no survivors.
[Exodus] [14]:[29] Yet, the children of IsraEl had been able to cross through the midst of the sea on dry land with the water standing like walls on their right and on their left.

[Exodus] [14]:[31] And after IsraEl had witnessed [Jehovah’s] mighty hand in the things that He did to the Egyptians, they started fearing [Jehovah]… Trusting in God and in His servant Moses.

[Exodus] [16]:[4] And the Lord said to Moses: ‘Look! I’ll rain bread upon you from the skies! ‘Then the people will go out and gather their allotment for each day, so I can test them to see whether they’ll follow My Law...
[Exodus] [16]:[5] For on the 6th day they must gather all that they can, and it’ll be double that which they could gather on the previous days.’

[Exodus] [16]:[7] and tomorrow morning you’ll see the glory of the Lord, since He’s heard you complaining against Him… And what are we, that you should keep complaining about us?’
[Exodus] [16]:[8] Then Moses continued, saying: ‘This evening, [Jehovah] will give you meat to eat; and in the morning, He will provide enough bread to satisfy you. ‘For [Jehovah] has heard all the complaints that you’ve made against us… Yet, what are we? You aren’t complaining against us, but against God!’
[Exodus] [16]:[9] And Moses said to Aaron: ‘Now, tell the entire gathering of the children of IsraEl that they must go over and approach God, since He’s heard all their complaining!’
[Exodus] [16]:[10] So, after Aaron said this to them, they all turned and faced the desert… And the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud!
[Exodus] [16]:[11] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Exodus] [16]:[12] ‘I’ve heard all the children of IsraEl’s complaining, so tell them: ‘This evening you’ll eat meat, and in the morning you’ll have enough bread to satisfy you… And then you’ll know that I am [Jehovah] your God.’
[Exodus] [16]:[13] Well that evening, a [huge flock] of quail flew in and covered the camp!
[Exodus] [16]:[14] And the next morning, after the dew around about the camp had dried; {Look!} on the surface of the desert (lying there like frost) was small things that looked like white coriander seeds...
[Exodus] [16]:[15] And when the children of IsraEl saw them, they asked each other: ‘What is this [Hebrew: man-nah]?’...because they didn’t know what it was. And Moses told them:
[Exodus] [16]:[16] ‘This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat… It’s what [Jehovah] has approved. ‘So, every man should gather 1/3 of a bushel for each person in his family. You and those who are living with you should go out and gather it.’
[Exodus] [16]:[17] And that’s what the children of IsraEl did. Although some gathered more and others gathered less,
[Exodus] [16]:[18] the ones who gathered the full 1/3 of a bushel didn’t have any leftovers, and those who gathered less never went hungry. So, they all gathered just what their households required.
[Exodus] [16]:[19] Then Moses told them: ‘Now, none of you may save any of this for the next morning.’
[Exodus] [16]:[20] However, many of them wouldn’t listen to Moses, and they tried to keep it until the following morning… But by then it had worms and it smelled… And all of this irritated Moses.
[Exodus] [16]:[21] So each morning, everyone would collect all that they needed, and everything melted after the sun went down.
[Exodus] [16]:[22] Then on the 6th day, they gathered twice as much as they needed… 2/3 of a bushel per person. Well, all the chiefs of their gathering thereafter came and reported what was happening to Moses.
[Exodus] [16]:[23] And Moses asked: ‘Didn’t the Lord tell us that tomorrow is the Sabbath… A holy [day of] rest to [Jehovah]? ‘Therefore, bake all that you can bake and boil all that you can boil, so that the leftovers can be stored for tomorrow!’
[Exodus] [16]:[24] [So on the 6th day], they stored the leftovers until the next morning, just as Moses told them, and it didn’t stink and there weren’t any worms in it.
[Exodus] [16]:[25] [And then the next day], Moses said: ‘This is what you must eat today; for since this day is a Sabbath to [Jehovah], you won’t find any of it out in the fields.
[Exodus] [16]:[26] ‘You must collect it for 6 days, but because the 7th day is a Sabbath, there won’t be any then.’
[Exodus] [16]:[27] However, on the 7th day some of the people still went out to collect it, but they couldn’t find any.
[Exodus] [16]:[28] So the Lord said to Moses: ‘How long are they going to fail to listen to My commands and [obey] My laws?
[Exodus] [16]:[29] ‘Look; I’ve given them this day as the Sabbath, and I gave them enough bread to last for two days on the 6th day. So from now on, they must all just sit there in their homes… Don’t allow anyone to leave his place on the 7th day!’
[Exodus] [16]:[30] Well thereafter, the people started keeping the Sabbath on the 7th day.
[Exodus] [16]:[31] The children of IsraEl called this [food], manna. It looked like white coriander seeds and tasted like crackers and honey.
[Exodus] [16]:[32] Then Moses said: ‘This is what [Jehovah] has commanded: ‘We are to collect 1/3 of a bushel of manna and set it aside so that future generations can see the bread that you ate in the desert after [Jehovah] led you out of the land of Egypt.’
[Exodus] [16]:[33] And he told Aaron: ‘Take a gold pot and fill it with a full 1/3-of-a-bushel of manna, then store it away for God and keep it for future generations.’
[Exodus] [16]:[34] So, just as the Lord told Moses, Aaron stored it away as a testimony.
[Exodus] [16]:[35] As a result, the children of IsraEl ate manna for 40 years. They ate manna until they got to the land of Phoenicia.

[Exodus] [17]:[11] Well, whenever Moses raised his arms, IsraEl would be superior; but when he let them down, the Amalekites were more successful.
[Exodus] [17]:[12] But soon Moses’ arms got tired, so they found a rock and had him sit on top of it; then Aaron and Or supported his arms on either side, holding them there until the sun set.
[Exodus] [17]:[13] So, JoShua was able to drive the Amalekites and all their people away by slaughtering them with swords.

[Exodus] [17]:[16] because [Jehovah] was secretly waging war against all generations of the Amalekites.
[Exodus] [18]:[1] Meanwhile, His Excellence (the priest of MidiAn, Moses’ father-in-law) heard of all that [Jehovah] had done for his people IsraEl by bringing them out of Egypt.

[Exodus] [18]:[5] His Excellence then took [Moses’ family] to him in the desert… To his camp on the Mountain of God.
[Exodus] [18]:[6] And when Moses was told, ‘Look! His Excellence (your father-in-law) is coming and he’s bringing your wife and two sons with him,’

[Exodus] [24]:[7] Next, [Moses] took the scroll of the Sacred Agreement [that he wrote] and read it to the people. And they [again] said: ‘We will do and pay attention to everything that [Jehovah] has said.’
[Exodus] [24]:[8] Then Moses took the blood [from the bowls] and sprinkled it on the people, and he said: '{Look!} This is the blood of the Sacred Agreement that [Jehovah] has made with you over the things you’ve agreed to.’
[Exodus] [24]:[9] And thereafter, Moses, Aaron, NaDab, AbiUd, and 70 of the elders of IsraEl went up [the mountain],
[Exodus] [24]:[10] where they saw the place that the God of IsraEl was standing; and under His feet [they saw] what looked like slabs of cut sapphires that were as pure as the firmament.
[Exodus] [24]:[11] So, all the chosen ones of IsraEl stood there in the presence of God – none were missing (not one) – and they ate and drank.
[Exodus] [24]:[12] Then [Jehovah] told Moses: ‘[I want you to] come [back] up the mountain to Me and stay here; for I’ll now give you the tablets of stone containing the Laws and Commandments that I’ve written.’

[Exodus] [24]:[14] And they told the elders: ‘Rest here until we return. ‘Look! Aaron and Or will be here with you; so if there are any [cases] that have to be tried, let them handle it.’
[Exodus] [24]:[15] Then Moses and JoShua climbed the mountain, which was shrouded in a cloud.
[Exodus] [24]:[16] And the glory of The God came down on Mount SinAi, and the cloud covered it for 6 days... Then [Jehovah] called to Moses from the midst of the cloud on the 7th day.
[Exodus] [24]:[17] Well, to the Children of IsraEl, the glory of [Jehovah] looked like a fire that was burning on top of the mountain!
[Exodus] [24]:[18] Then Moses entered the cloud and climbed the mountain, where he stayed for 40 days and 40 nights.

[Exodus] [29]:[39] one in the morning and the other in the evening.

[Exodus] [35]:[20] And after the gathering of the children of IsraEl [had finished listening to] Moses, all that felt moved to do so brought whatever they thought would be appropriate as offerings...
[Exodus] [35]:[21] So, they donated (as offerings to [Jehovah]) everything that was needed for the Tent of Proofs and all of its services, as well as all the clothing for the Holy Place.
[Exodus] [35]:[22] Then, any man who felt moved to do so brought items from their wives, such as gold... Clasps, Earrings, Finger rings, Necklaces, Bracelets, and All sorts of gold items.
[Exodus] [35]:[23] Yes, many of them brought their gold jewelry to [Jehovah], as well as their fine linen and ram’s skins that were dyed blue or red.
[Exodus] [35]:[24] All those who brought offerings also brought items of silver and bronze to [Jehovah], and everyone who had durable wood or the tools to work it, brought these things too.
[Exodus] [35]:[25] Then the women who were skilled at spinning brought blue [thread], purple [yarn], scarlet [cloth], and fine linen.
[Exodus] [35]:[26] And thereafter, all the women who were moved to do so and were wise, spun the goats’ hair.
[Exodus] [35]:[27] In addition, the [tribal] rulers brought emeralds and gemstones for the settings in the shoulder pieces and the Words [of Judgment].
[Exodus] [35]:[28] They also brought the materials for the anointing oil and the things that would be used to make the incense.
[Exodus] [35]:[29] So, every man and woman who was moved to do so came to do all the work that [Jehovah] had assigned to them through Moses [using the things that] the children of IsraEl had donated as offerings to the Lord.
[Exodus] [35]:[30] And Moses told them: '{Look!} God has specifically called BeSeleEl (of Urias and Or) from the tribe of Judah,
[Exodus] [35]:[31] and filled him with a godly spirit of wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, in order to be creative in all fields of expertise.
[Exodus] [35]:[32] ‘For he’s skilled in all sorts of crafts, such as working gold, silver, and bronze,

[Exodus] [36]:[1] So BeSeleEl, EliAb, and all those who were wise and knowledgeable, were given the wisdom, knowledge, and necessary [skills] to do everything that had to be done for the holy offices in the way that [Jehovah] had instructed.
[Exodus] [36]:[2] Then Moses called BeSeleEl, EliAb, and all the wise men who had received the needed skills from God, as well as everyone who was willing to come and donate their work, to get the job done.
[Exodus] [36]:[3] Moses gave them everything that the children of IsraEl had brought to build the Holy Place. In fact, they continued to receive the gifts each morning,
[Exodus] [36]:[4] and wise people with many different skills kept showing up to work at the Holy Place.
[Exodus] [36]:[5] Then one of them said to Moses: ‘The people are bringing in too many of the things that [Jehovah] told them to bring!’
[Exodus] [36]:[6] So Moses sent a proclamation throughout the camp, saying: ‘No men or women should come to work or bring any more offerings to the Holy.’ So they actually had to stop the people from bringing things,
[Exodus] [36]:[7] since they had enough material to make all the furnishings, with much left over.
[Exodus] [36]:[8] The wise and thoughtful among those who were working on the Tent also produced 10 tent curtains: [They were made] from: Blue [thread], Purple [yarn], Spun-scarlet [cloth], and Fine-spun linen. [They were made] with [images of] cherubs carefully woven into them.
[Exodus] [36]:[9] Each curtain was 42 feet (12.8m) wide and 6 feet (1.8m) tall… And all the curtains were the same.
[Exodus] [36]:[10] Then, two groups of five curtains each were connected end-to-end.
[Exodus] [36]:[11] They also made blue loops along the edges of each curtain to join them to each other. And they made 50 [loops] along the outer edges of the following curtains to connect them all together…
[Exodus] [36]:[12] They put 50 loops on the first curtain and 50 corresponding loops on the next, so [the curtains] could be joined together at the loops.
[Exodus] [36]:[13] Then [BeSeleEl] made 50 gold hooks to join each of the curtains to each other, in order to assemble the Sacred Tent.
[Exodus] [36]:[14] After that, he also put together the 11 goat-hair coverings to serve as a roof for the Sacred Tent:
[Exodus] [36]:[15] Each of these was 45 feet (13.7m) long and 6 feet (1.5m) wide.
[Exodus] [36]:[16] He joined five of the goat-hair coverings to make one portion, and six to make the other.
[Exodus] [36]:[17] He also made 50 loops along the edge of the first group of goat-hair cloths and 50 loops along the edge of the second group (in the middle),
[Exodus] [36]:[18] then he formed 50 bronze hooks and joined both sections with the hooks, making it a single sheet.
[Exodus] [36]:[19] He also made the top covering for the Sacred Tent out of ram’s skins, some of which were dyed red, and some of which were dyed blue.
[Exodus] [36]:[20] Then he made the posts for the Sacred Tent out of durable wood:

[Exodus] [36]:[22] It had two joints that butted against each other… And that’s how he made all the posts for the Sacred Tent.
[Exodus] [36]:[23] There were 20 posts on the side facing the south,
