[Leviticus] [1]:[1] Then the Lord called Moses again and spoke to him in the Tent of Proofs. He said:
[Leviticus] [1]:[2] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them that anyone who brings an ox as a gift to [Jehovah] must bring one that the Lord will find acceptable.
[Leviticus] [1]:[3] ‘If his gift for a burnt offering is from the herd, he will bring a male that has no defects. He will bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Proofs [where it will be] accepted on his behalf before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [1]:[4] ‘He must put his hands on the head of the offering [to show that] it’s something he wishes to do so as to be forgiven by [God],
[Leviticus] [1]:[5] and they must slaughter the calf before [Jehovah]. ‘Then Aaron’s sons (the Priests) must collect its blood and pour it around the Altar at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs.
[Leviticus] [1]:[6] ‘The meat of the offering should thereafter be butchered and divided into quarters.
[Leviticus] [1]:[7] Then the sons of Aaron (the Priests) must light a fire on the Altar and pile wood on the fire,
[Leviticus] [1]:[8] and the Priests must put the head and the fat over the fire in the Altar,
[Leviticus] [1]:[9] then wash the [animal’s] entrails and feet in water, and then put the rest of it on the Altar as a burnt-offering sacrifice and as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [1]:[10] ‘However, if [the person] is offering a sheep as a gift to [Jehovah] (or a lamb, or a kid goat) as a whole-burnt offering, it must be a perfect male.
[Leviticus] [1]:[11] ‘He must put his hand on its head and they must slaughter it next to the Altar towards the north, before [Jehovah]. Then the sons of Aaron (the Priests) must pour its blood on and around the Altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[12] ‘They must quarter it and put its head and its fat over the burning wood on the Altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[13] Then they must wash its entrails and feet with water, and the Priest must put the rest on the Altar as a burnt-offering sacrifice and a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [1]:[14] ‘But if [the person] is offering a bird as a gift to [Jehovah], it must be a dove or a pigeon.
[Leviticus] [1]:[15] The Priest must bring it to the Altar, wring off its head and sprinkle its blood at the base of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[16] And before placing it on the Altar, he must remove the crop and the feathers, and throw them by the ashes, to the east of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [1]:[17] ‘He should then break off its wings, but not cut it up, and put the burnt-offering sacrifice on the Altar over the burning wood as a sweet-smelling odor to [Jehovah].’
[Leviticus] [2]:[1] ‘If a person brings fine flour as a gift to sacrifice to [Jehovah], he must pour oil over it and put frankincense on it, before offering it as a sacrifice.
[Leviticus] [2]:[2] ‘He must carry it to the Priests (the sons of Aaron) and take a handful of the fine flour with the oil and the frankincense, and then a Priest must put it on the Altar as a sacrifice and as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [2]:[3] ‘The rest of the sacrifice must then be [given to] Aaron and his sons as their holy portion from the sacrifices to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [2]:[4] ‘And if he brings [bread] that has been baked in an oven as a gift sacrifice to [Jehovah], it must be fermentation-free and kneaded with oil into fermentation-free cakes.
[Leviticus] [2]:[5] But if the gift of fermentation-free fine flour is brought in a pan,
[Leviticus] [2]:[6] it must be broken into pieces and then oil must be poured over it as a sacrifice to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [2]:[7] ‘However, if the gift of fine flour with oil that’s to be offered as a sacrifice to [Jehovah] [consists of whole loaves] that were baked in an oven,
[Leviticus] [2]:[8] they must be brought to the Priest,
[Leviticus] [2]:[9] and the Priest must take it to the Altar and offer a portion of it as a burnt offering and as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [2]:[10] ‘The rest of the sacrifice must then be [given to] Aaron and his sons as their holy portion from the burnt offerings of [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [2]:[11] ‘You must not have fermentation in any of the sacrifices that are brought to [Jehovah] [at the Altar], and no honey will be brought as a gift to [Jehovah] [at the Altar].
[Leviticus] [2]:[12] ‘Such things may be brought to [Jehovah] as though they were fruit, but they must not be offered on the Altar as a sweet-smelling odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [2]:[13] ‘All gifts of sacrifices must be seasoned with salt. Don’t leave the salt of [Jehovah’s] Sacred Agreement out of your sacrifices! No matter what type of gift it is, it must be offered to [Jehovah] your God with salt.
[Leviticus] [2]:[14] ‘And when you offer the first fruits of your new grain as a sacrifice to [Jehovah], it should be ground and roasted before bringing it as a sacrifice...
[Leviticus] [2]:[15] You must also pour oil and frankincense over it, because it’s a sacrifice.
[Leviticus] [2]:[16] ‘Then the Priest must offer a portion of the grain with all the oil and frankincense as a burnt offering to [Jehovah].’
[Leviticus] [3]:[1] ‘If the gift to [Jehovah] is to be a peace offering and it’s selected from among your cattle, it can be a male or a female, but it must be perfect to bring it before Him.
[Leviticus] [3]:[2] ‘The [person] must put his hands on the head of the gift and they must slaughter it before [Jehovah] next to the entrance to the Tent of Proofs. Then the Priests (the sons of Aaron) must pour the blood on and around the Altar of burnt offerings.
[Leviticus] [3]:[3] ‘For peace offerings, [the following portions] should be offered as burnt-sacrifices to [Jehovah]: The belly and all the fat in and around it,
[Leviticus] [3]:[4] The kidneys and the fat on them, [The fat] on the thighs and the membrane around the liver and kidneys.
[Leviticus] [3]:[5] ‘The Priests (the sons of Aaron) must offer them on the Altar of burnt offerings over the burning wood on the Altar as a sweet-smelling odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [3]:[6] ‘And if the peace-offering gift to [Jehovah] is a sheep, it may be either a male or a female, but it must be perfect.
[Leviticus] [3]:[7] ‘If the gift is a lamb; he must bring it before [Jehovah],
[Leviticus] [3]:[8] put his hands on the head of his offering, and they must slaughter it by the entrance to the Tent of Proofs. Then the Priests (the sons of Aaron) must pour its blood on and around the Altar.
[Leviticus] [3]:[9] ‘The peace offering to be burned to [Jehovah] shall be [the following portions] which you’ll remove: The healthy, fat hind parts and loins, All the fat that’s in and around the belly,
[Leviticus] [3]:[10] The kidneys and the fat around them, The fat around the thighs and the membrane around the liver and kidneys.
[Leviticus] [3]:[11] ‘[All this] must be offered on the Altar by the Priest as a sweet-smelling odor and burnt offering to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [3]:[12] ‘And if he’s offering a goat, he must bring it before [Jehovah],
[Leviticus] [3]:[13] put his hands on its head, and they must slaughter it before [Jehovah] next to the entrance to the Tent of Proofs. Then the Priests (the sons of Aaron) must pour the blood on and around the Altar.
[Leviticus] [3]:[14] ‘The parts of the burnt offering [that will be offered] to [Jehovah] must be: The fat in and around the belly,
[Leviticus] [3]:[15] Both kidneys and all the fat on them, [The fat] on the thighs and the membrane around the liver and kidneys.
[Leviticus] [3]:[16] ‘Then the Priest must offer it on the Altar as a burnt offering and as a sweet odor to [Jehovah]. ‘All of the fat is [Jehovah’s]!
[Leviticus] [3]:[17] ‘And this is the rule throughout the ages of your generations wherever you may live: ‘You must not eat the fat or the blood!’
[Leviticus] [4]:[1] Then the Lord said to Moses:
[Leviticus] [4]:[2] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘If a person sins against [Jehovah] by doing something that He says you mustn’t do, in any of the Commandments, but unintentionally...
[Leviticus] [4]:[3] ‘Or if the Anointed Priest sins and that causes the people to sin... ‘The person must bring [an offering] for his sin. [He must bring] a perfect calf from his herd to [Jehovah], [to cover] his sin.
[Leviticus] [4]:[4] ‘He must bring the calf before [Jehovah] at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs, put his hand on its head, and they must slaughter it in [Jehovah’s] presence.
[Leviticus] [4]:[5] ‘And when the Anointed Priest who has been made perfect receives the calf’s blood, he must carry it into the Tent of Proofs.
[Leviticus] [4]:[6] ‘The Priest must then dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it at the base of the Holy Veil before [Jehovah], 7 times.
[Leviticus] [4]:[7] And he must put some of the calf’s blood on the horns of the incense Altar that’s before [Jehovah] (inside the Tent of Proofs) and pour the rest of the blood at the base of the Altar, by the entrance to the Tent of Proofs.
[Leviticus] [4]:[8] ‘[Thereafter, he must take] all the fat from the calf of the sin offering and remove it. [From:] The inner fat, The outer fat,
[Leviticus] [4]:[9] The kidneys and the fat on them, and [The fat on] the thighs and the membrane around the liver and kidneys.
[Leviticus] [4]:[10] ‘Then the Priest must offer it on the Altar of burnt offerings.
[Leviticus] [4]:[11] ‘As for the calf’s skin, flesh, head, extremities, belly, and dung...
[Leviticus] [4]:[12] It must all be carried outside the camp into the clean place where they pour the ashes, and it must be totally burned among the wood ashes that will be poured out there.
[Leviticus] [4]:[13] ‘Also, if the whole gathering of IsraEl should unknowingly commit a sin and it goes unnoticed by them (if they should do something that’s forbidden, shouldn’t be done, and is a sin against any of the Commandments of [Jehovah]),
[Leviticus] [4]:[14] but they later realize what they’ve done; the gathering should bring a perfect calf from the herd as a sin offering to the entrance of the Tent of Proofs.
[Leviticus] [4]:[15] ‘Then [all] the elders of the gathering must lay their hands on the calf’s head and slaughter it before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [4]:[16] ‘Thereafter, the Anointed Priest must bring the calf’s blood into the Tent of Proofs,
[Leviticus] [4]:[17] then dip his finger in some of the blood and sprinkle it 7 times before the veil of the Most Holy, there before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [4]:[18] ‘The Priest must also put some of the blood on the horns of the incense Altar that stands before [Jehovah] inside the Tent of Proofs. Then he must pour the rest of the blood at the base of the Altar of whole-burnt offerings, which is by the entrance to the Tent of Proofs.
[Leviticus] [4]:[19] ‘He must cut off all its fat and offer it on the Altar,
[Leviticus] [4]:[20] dealing with it in the same way as he does with the calf of the sin offering. That’s how the Priests must pay for their sins, and then their mistakes will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[21] ‘After that, they must take the rest of the calf outside of the camp and burn it in the same way as the other calf. ‘This is the sin offering for the [entire] gathering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[22] ‘And if one of the leaders should unknowingly break one of the Commandments of his God [Jehovah] (something he shouldn’t have done in sin and error),
[Leviticus] [4]:[23] and then he realizes that he’s sinned... The gift he must offer is a perfect male kid goat.
[Leviticus] [4]:[24] ‘He must put his hand on the head of the kid and slaughter it where they slaughter the whole-burnt offerings before [Jehovah], as a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [4]:[25] Then the Priest must put some of the blood of the sin offering on the horns of the Altar of whole-burnt offerings with his finger, and pour the rest of the blood at the base of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[26] ‘Thereafter, he must offer all of its fat on the Altar as the sacrifice of the peace offering. [This is how] the Priest must pay for [the leader’s] sin, so that it may be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[27] ‘And if a person among the people of the land should sin unknowingly against any of the Commandments of [Jehovah] by doing something that shouldn’t be done,
[Leviticus] [4]:[28] and then he realizes that he’s sinned... He must bring a perfect female kid goat for the sin that he’s committed.
[Leviticus] [4]:[29] ‘He must put his hand on the head of his sin offering and slaughter the kid of the sin offering where they slaughter the whole-burnt offerings.
[Leviticus] [4]:[30] And the Priest must then take some of its blood on his finger and wipe it on the horns of the Altar of whole-burnt offerings. ‘After that, he must pour the rest of the blood out at the base of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[31] Then he must remove all the fat and offer it as a sacrifice of a peace offering. The Priest must offer it on the Altar as a sweet odor to [Jehovah]. ‘[This is how] the Priest must pay for [the person’s] sin, so that it may be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [4]:[32] ‘But if he offers a lamb for his sin offering, it should be a perfect female...
[Leviticus] [4]:[33] He must put his hand on the head of the sin offering and slaughter it where they kill the whole-burnt offerings.
[Leviticus] [4]:[34] ‘Then the Priest must take some of the blood of the sin offering on his finger and wipe it on the horns of the Altar of whole-burnt offerings, and he must pour the rest of the blood around the base of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [4]:[35] ‘He must also cut off all its fat, the same as he would for the lamb of the peace-offering sacrifice, and the Priest must put it on the Altar as a whole-burnt offering to [Jehovah]. ‘[This is how] the Priest must atone for the person’s sin, so that it can be forgiven.’
[Leviticus] [5]:[1] ‘And if a person sins by witnessing, seeing, or knowing of someone who has sworn an oath [of vengeance] against another and fails to report it, he’s guilty of a sin.
[Leviticus] [5]:[2] ‘And whoever touches anything that’s dirty, such as: The filth of animals, Dead things ([like] a dead unclean animal or [the rotting] body of cattle),
[Leviticus] [5]:[3] Any kind of filth from a man that would make him unclean... '...whoever touches [any of this,] even if he doesn’t realize it, but comes to know about it later – he’s sinned.
[Leviticus] [5]:[4] Or if some unrighteous person has decided to use his lips to swear an oath to do evil or good – even if a person doesn’t realize it, but comes to know of it [later] – he’s sinned by doing this.
[Leviticus] [5]:[5] ‘He must admit that he’s sinned
[Leviticus] [5]:[6] and [pay for] his sin against [[Jehovah] by bringing] a female lamb from his flock or a goat kid as a sin offering, which the Priest must [offer] in payment for his sin. ‘Then he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[7] ‘And if he can’t afford a sheep... He must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to [Jehovah]. One [must serve] as a sin offering, and the other as a burnt offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[8] ‘He must carry them to the Priest, and the Priest must [sacrifice] the sin offering first. He must pinch off the head at the neck, but not cut up the body.
[Leviticus] [5]:[9] Then he must sprinkle the blood of the sin offering on the side of the Altar, and pour the rest of the blood at the base of the Altar… Because this is a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[10] ‘Then the 2nd [bird] must serve as a whole burnt offering for the Priest, to atone for the sins that the person has committed.
[Leviticus] [5]:[11] ‘And if he can’t afford a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons... The gift that he should bring for his sin offering must be a quart of fine flour. He shouldn’t put frankincense or oil on it, because it’s a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[12] ‘He must carry it to the Priest, who must take a handful of it and lay a portion of it on the Altar as a whole-burnt offering to [Jehovah] and as a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [5]:[13] So the Priest must offer payment for the way that the person has sinned in these matters, and [the person] will be forgiven. ‘Then, whatever remains of the flour offering will belong to the Priest.’
[Leviticus] [5]:[14] And the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [5]:[15] ‘The person who is truly unaware and unknowingly sins against any of the holy things of [Jehovah] must carry something to [Jehovah] for his error. ‘[It must be] a perfect ram from his flock (or its value in the type of silver coins that are accepted in the Holy Place) [to pay] for his mistake.
[Leviticus] [5]:[16] ‘He must pay for his sin against any of the holy things, and add 1/5th more to it. He must give it to the Priest, and the Priest must cover his sin with the ram of his error, and then [the person] will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[17] ‘And if any person sins and does something that isn’t right and is against any of [Jehovah’s] Commandments – even if he doesn’t realize it – he’s guilty of a sin.
[Leviticus] [5]:[18] ‘So, he must bring a perfect ram from his flock (or its value in silver) to the Priest for his mistake, and the Priest will [use it] to pay for the sin that he committed in ignorance... Then he will be forgiven.
[Leviticus] [5]:[19] ‘However, he’s truly been found guilty of sinning before [Jehovah].’
[Leviticus] [6]:[1] And the Lord told Moses:
[Leviticus] [6]:[2] ‘Whoever sins by: Ignoring the Commandments of [Jehovah], Lying about something entrusted to them by a neighbor, Something shared, or stolen, or in any way wrongs his neighbor
[Leviticus] [6]:[3] Finds something lost but lies about it, or Lies about any sins like these...
[Leviticus] [6]:[4] ‘Then when he sins by making such errors, he should return whatever he wrongly acquired by theft, misplaced trust, chance,
[Leviticus] [6]:[5] or lying. Then he must repay the total sum, plus 1/5th. ‘Yes, when he’s disciplined, he will pay back whatever he owes.
[Leviticus] [6]:[6] And for his sin offering to the Lord, he will bring a perfect ram from the flocks, of [the same] value of his error.
[Leviticus] [6]:[7] Then, before [Jehovah], the priest will see that his sin is paid for; and he’ll be forgiven for whatever sin he committed.’
[Leviticus] [6]:[8] And the Lord told Moses:
[Leviticus] [6]:[9] ‘Give Aaron and his sons these instructions… This is the law concerning whole-burnt offerings: ‘Because whole-burnt offerings are to be left burning on the Altar all night long, the fire on the Altar must be kept burning and not be put out.
[Leviticus] [6]:[10] ‘Then the Priest must put on the linen tunic and the linen underwear, and carry everything that’s been thoroughly burned and consumed by the fire (the whole-burnt offerings) from the Altar and throw [the ashes] nearby.
[Leviticus] [6]:[11] And after that, he must take off that robe, put on another robe, and carry the burned [ashes] to a clean place outside of the camp.
[Leviticus] [6]:[12] ‘The fire on the Altar must be kept burning all the time and never be allowed to go out. The Priests must stoke it with wood each morning, so whole-burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings can be piled on it.
[Leviticus] [6]:[13] ‘The fire must always be kept burning on the Altar and it must never be extinguished.’
[Leviticus] [6]:[14] ‘This is the law concerning the sacrifices that the sons of Aaron must bring to the Altar before [Jehovah]:
[Leviticus] [6]:[15] ‘[The Priest] must scoop a handful of the fine flour of the sacrifice that was offered along with its oil and all the frankincense, and put it on the Altar as a burnt offering and a sweet-smelling odor for [Jehovah] to remember.
[Leviticus] [6]:[16] ‘Then Aaron and his sons may eat all that’s left. However, it must be eaten without fermentation inside the courtyard of the Tent of Proofs…
[Leviticus] [6]:[17] And it must not be baked with any fermentation. ‘I’m giving a portion of [Jehovah’s] burnt offering to them, for it’s very holy, as are the offerings for sin and the offerings for errors.
[Leviticus] [6]:[18] ‘All the male Priests must eat it. This is to be the rule for burnt offerings to [Jehovah] throughout your generations and throughout the ages, for whoever touches them will be made holy.’
[Leviticus] [6]:[19] And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
[Leviticus] [6]:[20] ‘This is the gift that Aaron and his sons must offer to [Jehovah] on the day that you anoint him: ‘A quart of fine flour must be sacrificed, half of it in the morning and the other half in the evening.
[Leviticus] [6]:[21] It must be kneaded with oil into rolls [and cooked] in a pan, then offered [on the Altar] in pieces, as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [6]:[22] ‘The Anointed Priest (one of [Aaron’s] sons who is serving in his place) will offer it, and it must all be burned. ‘This is to be a rule throughout the ages:
[Leviticus] [6]:[23] ‘All the sacrifices for the Priests must be totally burned and never be eaten.’
[Leviticus] [6]:[24] Then the Lord told Moses:
[Leviticus] [6]:[25] ‘Speak to Aaron and his sons and tell them that this is the law of the sin offerings: ‘The sin offerings must be slaughtered before [Jehovah] in the same place as the whole burnt offerings, for they’re very holy.
[Leviticus] [6]:[26] The Priest who offers it must also eat it in a holy place in the courtyard of the Tent of Proofs.
[Leviticus] [6]:[27] ‘Anyone who touches its flesh must be holy, and all those whose clothes have been sprinkled with its blood must be washed in the Holy Place.
[Leviticus] [6]:[28] ‘Thereafter, the clay pots that held [the sacrifice] must be broken. However, if it was put in a brass pot, [the pot] must be scoured and washed in water.
[Leviticus] [6]:[29] ‘Then all the male Priests must eat it as something that’s very holy to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [6]:[30] But, none of the blood of the sin offering that’s carried into the Tent of Proofs to pay for sins in the Holy Place may be eaten. It must be burned with fire.’
[Leviticus] [7]:[1] ‘This is the law of the Ram Offering for Errors, because it’s the most sacred of the offerings:
[Leviticus] [7]:[2] ‘They must butcher the Ram-Offering for Errors before [Jehovah] in the same place that they butcher the whole-burnt offerings, and the blood must then be poured around the base of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [7]:[3] ‘Thereafter, they must remove all of the fat that’s on: The loins, Around the entrails,
[Leviticus] [7]:[4] The two kidneys and the fat on them, and The thighs. ‘The lobe of the liver should be removed along with the kidneys.
[Leviticus] [7]:[5] ‘Then the Priest must offer them on the Altar as an offering of submission to [Jehovah], because this is an offering for errors.
[Leviticus] [7]:[6] This [sacrifice] should thereafter be eaten by all of the males among the Priests in the Holy Place, because this is the holiest of the holies.
[Leviticus] [7]:[7] ‘The offering for errors is performed just like the offering for sins, since these are considered to be the same thing. And [the sacrifice] will thereafter belong to whichever Priest does the offering.
[Leviticus] [7]:[8] ‘Also, the hide of any animal that’s brought as a whole-burnt-offering will belong to the Priest.
[Leviticus] [7]:[9] ‘In addition, any sacrifice that’s baked, or grilled, or fried will belong to the Priest who offers it.
[Leviticus] [7]:[10] And every sacrifice that’s prepared with or without olive oil will be divided among the sons of Aaron equally.
[Leviticus] [7]:[11] ‘This is the Law of the Sacrifice of Salvation that they must bring before [Jehovah]:
[Leviticus] [7]:[12] ‘If it’s to be an offering of praise, he must bring a sacrifice of unfermented bread made of fine flour mixed with olive oil, and pan-fried flat bread that’s made of fine flour mixed with olive oil and smeared with olive oil.
[Leviticus] [7]:[13] ‘Then along with the unfermented bread, he must offer a gift as part of the sacrifice of praise for his salvation.
[Leviticus] [7]:[14] And along with his gift offerings, he must bring a portion that’s to be set aside for [Jehovah], which will then belong to the Priest who pours out the blood of the offering.
[Leviticus] [7]:[15] ‘Also, the meats of the Sacrifice of Praise for Salvation will belong to the Priest. This must be eaten on the day it’s presented, and none may be left over until the next morning.
[Leviticus] [7]:[16] ‘If an offering is being made voluntarily as part of a vow, the person should bring his gift offering on whichever day he’s chosen for his sacrifice, and it can be eaten on the following morning.
[Leviticus] [7]:[17] ‘But any meats that are brought must be incinerated on the 3rd day.
[Leviticus] [7]:[18] ‘And if he eats any of the meat on the 3rd day, the sacrifices will have been rejected and are no longer accepted on his behalf, because they’re viewed as defiled. So, the person who eats it will continue to bear his sins.
[Leviticus] [7]:[19] ‘Also, all meats that have touched anything unclean may not be eaten. Rather, they must be incinerated in a fire, since all that are clean must eat meat that’s clean.
[Leviticus] [7]:[20] And no person may eat any of the meat of the Sacrifice for Salvation that has been offered to [Jehovah], for this will make him unclean and he must be destroyed from among his people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[21] ‘In addition, any person who touches something unclean, such as the uncleanness of a person, or of a four-footed animal, or something disgusting from anything that’s unclean, and then the person eats some of the meats of the Peace Offering that’s presented to [Jehovah]... That person must be destroyed from among his people.’
[Leviticus] [7]:[22] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [7]:[23] ‘Speak to the sons of IsraEl and tell them that they must not eat the fat of sheep, oxen, or goats.
[Leviticus] [7]:[24] ‘And while the fat of decaying flesh or of that which has been killed by wild animals may be used for work, it may not be eaten.
[Leviticus] [7]:[25] ‘Also, anyone who eats the fat of cattle that he’s brought to [Jehovah] as an offering of submission must be destroyed from among his people.
[Leviticus] [7]:[26] ‘Nor may you eat the blood of any cattle or birds in your home,
[Leviticus] [7]:[27] for any person who eats blood must be destroyed from among his people.’
[Leviticus] [7]:[28] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [7]:[29] ‘Speak to the sons of IsraEl and tell them that anyone who brings a Peace Offering to [Jehovah] must also bring the gift of a Salvation Offering.
[Leviticus] [7]:[30] ‘In his own hands, he must carry these offerings to [Jehovah]: ‘The fat on the breast and on the lobe of the liver… He must bring this and place it as a gift before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [7]:[31] Then the Priest will offer it on the Altar, and the breast will be given to Aaron and to his sons.
[Leviticus] [7]:[32] ‘You must also cut off the right shoulder of the Salvation Offering and give it to the Priest.
[Leviticus] [7]:[33] The right shoulder of the Salvation Offering belongs to the one from among the sons of Aaron who offers up the blood and the fat.
[Leviticus] [7]:[34] ‘So, I’ve taken the breast of the Offering of the Blessings and the cut-off portion of the right shoulder from the sacrifices of the sons of IsraEl and given it all to Aaron the Priest and to his sons. ‘This is to be a law throughout the ages for IsraEl,
[Leviticus] [7]:[35] since this is [part of] the anointing of Aaron and his sons… It’s their portion of the Offering of the Blessings that [Jehovah] gave to them on the day that He appointed them to officiate as Priests to Him,
[Leviticus] [7]:[36] and when He appointed them and anointed them from among the sons of IsraEl as an age-long law through the generations.’
[Leviticus] [7]:[37] These are the laws of the whole burnt offerings, of the sacrifices for sins and for errors, of the consecration, and of the sacrifices of the Salvation Offerings,
[Leviticus] [7]:[38] in the way that the Lord gave these instructions to Moses on Mount SinAi on the day that He ordered the sons of IsraEl to bring their gift offerings before [Jehovah], there in the SinAi Desert.
[Leviticus] [8]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [8]:[2] ‘Go get Aaron and his sons, along with their robes, the anointing oil, a calf for a sin offering, two rams, and a basket of fermentation-free bread;
[Leviticus] [8]:[3] then assemble the whole gathering at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs.’
[Leviticus] [8]:[4] So Moses did just as the Lord told him. He assembled the gathering at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs,
[Leviticus] [8]:[5] and Moses told them: ‘This is what [Jehovah] has commanded us to do.’
[Leviticus] [8]:[6] So, he brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.
[Leviticus] [8]:[7] Then he wrapped him in the robe, tied on the sash, and he put the tunic and the Word of Judgment on him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[8] He wrapped [the tunic] so the Word of Judgment would fit, and clasped it tightly before putting on the Word of Judgment, and he laid the Revelation and the Truth on top of that.
[Leviticus] [8]:[9] Next, he put the turban on [Aaron’s] head and mounted the gold plate (this most holy thing) on the front of the turban, just as [Jehovah] had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[10] Then Moses took the anointing oil
[Leviticus] [8]:[11] and sprinkled it on the Altar 7 times to anoint the Altar and make it holy (along with everything on it, including its base and the basin). He made them holy, and he anointed the Tent and all its furniture, making them holy...
[Leviticus] [8]:[12] Then Moses poured anointing oil on Aaron’s head to anoint him and make him holy.
[Leviticus] [8]:[13] And Moses brought up Aaron’s sons, put on their robes and wrapped on their sashes; then he put on their turbans, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[14] Next, Moses brought over the calf for the sin offering. So, Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the sin-offering calf,
[Leviticus] [8]:[15] and Moses slaughtered it. Then he took some of the blood and rubbed it on the horns of the Altar with his finger, to purify it; and he poured the rest of the blood at the base of the Altar, to make it holy, so that it could be used to pay for sins.
[Leviticus] [8]:[16] Thereafter, Moses took all the inner fat plus the liver and kidneys and the fat around them, and he offered it on the Altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[17] Then he burned the rest of the calf (its skin, flesh, and dung) in a fire outside of the camp, just as The Lord had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[18] Moses then brought over the ram for the whole-burnt offering. Aaron and his sons also laid their hands on its head and Moses slaughtered the ram, pouring the blood around the Altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[19] Then he divided the ram by each of its limbs, and Moses offered up the head, the limbs, and the fat, after washing the feet and belly with water.
[Leviticus] [8]:[20] So Moses offered the whole ram on the Altar as a burnt offering, and it was burned as a sweet-smelling odor to [Jehovah], just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[21] After that, Moses brought over the second ram (the last ram), and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head, and he slaughtered it.
[Leviticus] [8]:[22] So Moses took its blood and put some on the tip of Aaron’s right ear, on the thumb of his right hand, and on the big toe of his right foot.
[Leviticus] [8]:[23] Then Moses brought in Aaron’s sons and put the blood on the tips of their right ears, on the thumbs of their right hands, and on the big toes of their right feet; and Moses poured the rest of the blood around the Altar.
[Leviticus] [8]:[24] Then he took the fat, the rump, the belly fat, the liver and kidneys and the fat that’s on them, as well as its right shoulder.
[Leviticus] [8]:[25] And from the basket of consecration that was before [Jehovah], he took one fermentation-free loaf, one loaf made with oil, and one cake (along with the fat and the right shoulder),
[Leviticus] [8]:[26] and put them all in the hands of Aaron and his sons, who waved them before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [8]:[27] Then Moses took it from their hands and put it all on the Altar as the whole-burnt offering of the last lamb; and it was burned as an offering to [Jehovah], providing a sweet-smelling odor to Him.
[Leviticus] [8]:[28] Finally, Moses took the last lamb’s breast and set it aside before [Jehovah], and this was given to Moses as his portion, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [8]:[29] Thereafter, Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood that was on the Altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron and his garments, and on his sons and their garments.
[Leviticus] [8]:[30] [By doing this], he made Aaron and his garments, as well as his sons and their garments, holy.
[Leviticus] [8]:[31] Then Moses said to Aaron and his sons: ‘Now, boil the flesh in the Holy Place inside the Tent of Proofs, and eat it there along with the loaves in the last basket, just as the Lord told me when He said: ‘Aaron and his sons must eat this.’
[Leviticus] [8]:[32] ‘After that, you must burn whatever’s left of the flesh and loaves in a fire.
[Leviticus] [8]:[33] And then you must stay inside the entrance to the Tent of Proofs until the end of 7 days. For in 7 days, He will make you perfect
[Leviticus] [8]:[34] in the same way as He did on the day that the Lord commanded me to do this to pay for your sins.
[Leviticus] [8]:[35] ‘You must remain inside the entrance to the Tent of Proofs for 7 days and nights… You must obey this rule of [Jehovah] so that you won’t die, for that’s what [Jehovah] God has commanded.’
[Leviticus] [8]:[36] Well, Aaron and his sons then followed the instructions that the Lord gave as commandments to Moses.
[Leviticus] [9]:[1] It was on the 8th day that Moses called Aaron and his sons out before IsraEl’s elders.
[Leviticus] [9]:[2] And Moses said to Aaron: ‘Now, select a perfect young calf from the herd as a sin offering and a ram as a whole-burnt offering, then offer them before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [9]:[3] And tell the elders of IsraEl: ‘Take one goat kid to be a sin offering, and take a young calf and a perfect yearling lamb as whole-burnt offerings,
[Leviticus] [9]:[4] as well as a calf and a ram as peace offerings to [Jehovah], along with fine flour that’s mixed with oil, because the Lord is going to appear among you today!’
[Leviticus] [9]:[5] So, just as Moses commanded, they brought [the animals] to the Tent of Proofs, and the entire gathering came and stood before [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [9]:[6] Then Moses said: ‘This is what [Jehovah] told us to do… For after that, the glory of the Lord will appear among you.’
[Leviticus] [9]:[7] And Moses told Aaron: ‘Now, approach the Altar and offer your sin offering and your whole-burnt offering so as to pay for the sins of you and your family… And then you must offer gifts for the people to pay for their sins, just as the Lord commanded.’
[Leviticus] [9]:[8] So Aaron went to the Altar and slaughtered the calf as his sin offering.
[Leviticus] [9]:[9] Then Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, and he dipped his finger in it and put some on the horns of the Altar; and thereafter, he poured the rest of the blood at the base of the Altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[10] Next, he offered the fat, the kidneys, and the liver on the Altar as a sin offering, just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [9]:[11] Then the flesh and hide were burned in a fire outside of the camp.
[Leviticus] [9]:[12] After that, he slaughtered the whole-burnt offering; and Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, which he poured all around the Altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[13] Then they brought the whole-burnt offering (which they’d cut in pieces), and he laid the head on the Altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[14] Then he washed the belly and feet with water, and put them on the Altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[15] Thereafter, he brought up the gifts for the people. He took the goat, which was the people’s sin offering, and slaughtered it and washed it, as before.
[Leviticus] [9]:[16] Next, he brought the whole-burnt offering, and he offered it in the proper way,
[Leviticus] [9]:[17] carrying the sacrifice in his hands and laying it on the Altar beside the whole-burnt offering that had been offered up in the morning.
[Leviticus] [9]:[18] Then he slaughtered the calf and the ram as peace-offering sacrifices for the people. So, Aaron’s sons brought the blood to him, which he poured all around the Altar,
[Leviticus] [9]:[19] and he put the calf’s fat, as well as the hindquarters of the ram, the fat on its belly, its kidneys and the fat on them, the membrane around the liver,
[Leviticus] [9]:[20] as well as the fat on the breasts, and offered it on the Altar.
[Leviticus] [9]:[21] Then Aaron set aside the breast and right shoulder as a choicest offering before [Jehovah], just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [9]:[22] Then, after he’d offered up the sin offering, the whole-burnt offerings, and the peace offerings, Aaron raised his arms over the people and blest them before coming back down,
[Leviticus] [9]:[23] and both Moses and Aaron went into the Tent of Proofs... Then when they came out, they blest all the people. And at that, the Lord’s glory appeared to all the people!
[Leviticus] [9]:[24] Also, fire came from [Jehovah] that consumed the offerings on the Altar (both the whole-burnt offerings and their fat)! And when all the people saw this, they were stunned and fell to their faces.
[Leviticus] [10]:[1] Then two of Aaron’s sons (NaDab and AbiUd) took their censers, put incense and fire in them, and offered it before [Jehovah] in a way that’s quite different from what they’d been commanded...
[Leviticus] [10]:[2] And after they did that, fire came from the Lord and consumed them, causing them to die there before [Jehovah]!
[Leviticus] [10]:[3] So Moses said to Aaron: ‘[Jehovah] told us that He must be treated as holy by those who approach Him, and He must be glorified before the whole congregation!’ Well, Aaron was devastated by this.
[Leviticus] [10]:[4] Then Moses called MisaDae and EliShaphan ([two of] the sons of Aaron’s uncle OziEl) and said to them: ‘Come here and remove your brothers from in front of the Holy Place, then [carry their bodies] outside of the camp!’
[Leviticus] [10]:[5] So they came and took them (while they were still wearing their [Priestly] outfits) outside of the camp, just as Moses had said.
[Leviticus] [10]:[6] Then Moses said to Aaron, EliEzer, IthaMar, and his remaining sons: ‘Now, don’t uncover your heads or tear your clothes, unless you also want to die and bring [God’s] rage down upon the entire congregation, for then your brothers and the entire house of IsraEl would start mourning this burning that came from [Jehovah]!
[Leviticus] [10]:[7] ‘And don’t leave the entrance to the Tent of Proofs or you’ll die, because [Jehovah’s] anointing oil is upon you!’ Well, they did just as Moses told them.
[Leviticus] [10]:[8] Then the Lord spoke to Aaron and said:
[Leviticus] [10]:[9] ‘Hereafter, you and your sons must not drink any wine or liquor before you enter the Tent of Proofs or before you approach the Altar, lest you should die! ‘This is [to be] a law throughout the ages [for all your] generations!
[Leviticus] [10]:[10] ‘For [you must be able to] recognize the difference between what’s sacred and what’s profane, and between what’s clean and what’s unclean!
[Leviticus] [10]:[11] ‘And [you must] teach the children of IsraEl all the laws that [[Jehovah] gave] them through Moses.’
[Leviticus] [10]:[12] Then Moses told Aaron, EliEzer, IthaMar, and Aaron’s surviving sons: ‘Now, take the remaining sacrifices among the burnt offerings for [Jehovah] and eat [them with] fermentation-free bread close to the Altar; because, that is a very holy [place].
[Leviticus] [10]:[13] ‘Eating the burnt offerings to [Jehovah] in the Holy Place will be the law for you and your sons; for He’s commanded
[Leviticus] [10]:[14] that you, your sons, and your families must eat the breast that has been set aside [for you], as well as the choicest shoulder, in the Holy Place. ‘This is the rule for you and your sons concerning the peace-offering sacrifices [that are brought by] the children of IsraEl.
[Leviticus] [10]:[15] ‘They must bring the choicest shoulder and [they must] separate the breast from the burnt offerings of fat as a separate division before [Jehovah]. This is to be the rule for you, as well as for your sons and daughters throughout the ages, just as the Lord commanded Moses.’
[Leviticus] [10]:[16] Well, when Moses started looking for the goat of the sin offering, [he found that] it had already been burned in the fire! So Moses became very angry with EliEzer, IthaMar, and Aaron’s remaining sons, and he said:
[Leviticus] [10]:[17] ‘Why didn’t you eat the sin offering here in the Holy Place? It’s a very holy [thing that [Jehovah]] has given you to eat before Him, so you can remove and pay for the sins of the entire gathering!
[Leviticus] [10]:[18] ‘Not even its blood was brought into the Holy Place… And [Jehovah] commanded you to eat [the sacrifice] here before Him!’
[Leviticus] [10]:[19] So Aaron asked Moses: ‘Well, if they bring their sin offerings and whole-burnt offerings to [Jehovah] today, and we eat the sin offerings that are brought today (despite what we’ve done), would that be pleasing to the Lord?’
[Leviticus] [10]:[20] And when Moses heard this, he was pleased.
[Leviticus] [11]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and told them:
[Leviticus] [11]:[2] ‘Speak to the sons of IsraEl and tell them that these are the animals that you may eat among all the animals on the ground:
[Leviticus] [11]:[3] ‘You may eat any animal with a split hoof or that has a split between its two claws and chews the cud.
[Leviticus] [11]:[4] However, you may not eat those that just chew the cud or those that just have split hoofs or a split between the claws, [such as] the camel, because it chews the cud, but it doesn’t have a split hoof; so, this is something that’s unclean to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[5] ‘[This includes] the rabbit, because it chews the cud but it doesn’t have a split foot; so, it’s unclean to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[6] ‘This [is also true] of the hare, because it doesn’t chew the cud and it doesn’t have a split foot; so, it’s unclean to you,
[Leviticus] [11]:[7] as are pigs, because they have split hoofs and claws on each hoof, but they don’t chew the cud; so, they’re also unclean to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[8] ‘You must not eat their flesh or touch their dead bodies, because they’re unclean to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[9] ‘These are the things that you may eat, [which live] in the water: ‘You may eat anything that has fins and scales [that lives in] the water, whether in the seas or in the rivers.
[Leviticus] [11]:[10] ‘However, anything that lives in the water but doesn’t have fins or scales (whether in the seas or in the rivers)… All else that lives in the water or comes out of the water is disgusting, and you are to consider it disgusting.
[Leviticus] [11]:[11] ‘You must not eat their flesh and you must dislike their dead bodies.
[Leviticus] [11]:[12] You must view anything that lives in the water and doesn’t have fins or scales as disgusting!
[Leviticus] [11]:[13] ‘These are the things that you must dislike among the flying creatures… Things that must not be eaten but are to be considered disgusting: Eagles, ospreys, sea eagles,
[Leviticus] [11]:[14] vultures, kites, and the like;
[Leviticus] [11]:[15] Ostriches, owls, seagulls, and the like;
[Leviticus] [11]:[16] Ravens and the like; Hawks and the like;
[Leviticus] [11]:[17] Night ravens, cormorants, storks,
[Leviticus] [11]:[18] ibis, pelicans, swans,
[Leviticus] [11]:[19] herons, sandpipers, and the like; Hoopoes and bats.
[Leviticus] [11]:[20] ‘Also, all winged creatures that crawl on all fours are [to be considered] disgusting by you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[21] ‘You can eat crawling winged creatures that move on all fours but have legs above their feet and jump around on the ground.
[Leviticus] [11]:[22] ‘These include: Migratory locusts and the like, Tree locusts and the like, Crickets and the like, and Ggrasshoppers and the like.
[Leviticus] [11]:[23] ‘But, any [other thing] that crawls and flies is to be considered disgusting by you;
[Leviticus] [11]:[24] and if you touch their dead bodies you’ll be unclean and will remain unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[25] ‘All who touch their dead bodies must wash their clothes and then be [considered] unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[26] ‘Any dead bodies of animals that have split hooves and claws but don’t chew the cud will be unclean to you, and everyone who touches them will be unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[27] ‘Also, any wild animals that walk on four paws are unclean to you, and anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[28] If you touch their dead bodies, you must wash your clothes and be [considered] unclean until the evening. For all of such things are unclean to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[29] ‘These crawling [animals are also] unclean for you among the slithering creatures: Weasels, Mice, Crocodiles,
[Leviticus] [11]:[30] Ferrets, Chameleons, Geckos, Newts, Sand lizards.
[Leviticus] [11]:[31] ‘Among all the crawling animals on the earth, these are unclean for you, and anyone who touches their dead bodies will be unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[32] ‘And if one of the dead bodies of these unclean [things] should fall on a wooden container, or on clothing, or on leather, or on a sack, or on anything that’s used for work; [the item] should be washed in water and be unclean until the evening… Then it will be clean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[33] ‘Also, if one of these [animals] should fall into a clay pot or bowl, whatever is inside it will be unclean and it must be broken.
[Leviticus] [11]:[34] Any edible food that the water was poured on, or any beverage that was in such a vessel, will be unclean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[35] ‘Everything that their dead bodies fall on will be unclean. Ovens and tables must be broken down, because they’re unclean, and they’re unclean for you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[36] ‘Springs, pools, and moving water will be clean, but anyone who touches dead bodies will be unclean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[37] ‘If one of these dead bodies should fall on seeds that have been planted, the [seeds] are clean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[38] However, if water has been poured on the seeds and then one of their dead bodies fall on it, it is unclean to you.
[Leviticus] [11]:[39] ‘If one of the cattle that the Law allows you to eat should die [naturally]; whoever touches the body will be unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[40] Whoever eats such a body must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. And anyone who carries their bodies must wash their clothes, take a bath, and be unclean until the evening.
[Leviticus] [11]:[41] ‘All slithering animals that crawl on the ground must be [considered] disgusting by you and never be eaten.
[Leviticus] [11]:[42] ‘And any slithering creatures that crawl along the ground on their bellies must not be eaten… You should consider them disgusting.
[Leviticus] [11]:[43] You shouldn’t dirty your lives with any slithering creatures that crawl on the ground. If you don’t allow them to pollute you, they won’t make you unclean.
[Leviticus] [11]:[44] ‘For I am [Jehovah] your God who makes you holy, and you must remain holy, since I, [Jehovah] your God, am holy. Therefore, you must not dirty your lives with any of the slithering things that crawl on the ground.
[Leviticus] [11]:[45] ‘For I am [Jehovah] who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. So, you must be holy, because I, [Jehovah], am holy.’
[Leviticus] [11]:[46] These are the laws concerning [four-footed] animals, flying creatures, everything that lives and moves in the water, and all creatures that crawl on the ground,
[Leviticus] [11]:[47] [so you can know] the difference between what’s clean and unclean, and between those that give birth alive that can be eaten, and those that shouldn’t be eaten.
[Leviticus] [12]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [12]:[2] ‘You must speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘Whenever a woman gets pregnant and gives birth to a male child, she must be [considered] unclean for 7 days, just as she is [considered] unclean during her monthly [menstrual] periods.
[Leviticus] [12]:[3] ‘Then on the 8th day, she must circumcise [her son’s] foreskin flesh.
[Leviticus] [12]:[4] ‘And for [the next] 33 days, she must continue as in [a state] of an unclean blood [flow]; so, she should not touch anything holy and [she] must not enter the Holy Place until the full period of her purification is fulfilled.
[Leviticus] [12]:[5] ‘But if she gives birth to a female child, she must be considered unclean for 14 days, and for the next 66 days she will remain [as in a state] of an unclean blood flow.
[Leviticus] [12]:[6] ‘When her period of purification for [giving birth to] a son or daughter is completed, she must bring a perfect yearling lamb to the Priest at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs as a whole-burnt offering, and bring a young pigeon or a turtledove as a sin offering.
[Leviticus] [12]:[7] ‘Then [the Priest] must present it before [Jehovah] and offer it to pay for her sins and her flow of blood. ‘This law applies to her, whether she gives birth to a male or a female.
[Leviticus] [12]:[8] ‘However, if she can’t afford a lamb, she must bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons… One [to be sacrificed] as a whole-burnt offering, and the other as a sin offering. ‘The Priest will use these to pay for her sins and to purify her.’
[Leviticus] [13]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and said:
[Leviticus] [13]:[2] ‘If anyone should [develop] a bright clear spot on his skin that looks like the plague of infection, he must be brought to Aaron the Priest, or to one of his sons, the Priests,
[Leviticus] [13]:[3] and the Priest should examine the spot. ‘If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot is under the skin, it’s an infection; so, the Priest who looked at it must pronounce him unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[4] ‘But if the spot on the skin is clear and white and doesn’t appear to be deep under the skin, and the hair hasn’t turned white, but is dark, the Priest must quarantine him for 7 days...
[Leviticus] [13]:[5] Then on the 7th day, the Priest must look to see if the spot is still there. [If it is], and if the spot hasn’t spread, the Priest should quarantine him for 7 more days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[6] ‘Then on the 7th day, the Priest should examine him a second time to see if the spot has started to darken. If it hasn’t, and if it isn’t spreading in his skin, the Priest will pronounce him clean, for it is just a scar. Then the person must wash his clothes and [he will] be [considered] clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[7] ‘However, if the bright spot changes and spreads in the skin after the Priest has looked at him and called him clean; he must return to the Priest again,
[Leviticus] [13]:[8] and the Priest must reexamine him. ‘Then if he finds that the mark has spread inside the skin, the Priest must pronounce him unclean… For it’s infection.
[Leviticus] [13]:[9] ‘If a man [thinks he] has the plague of infection, he must go to the Priest
[Leviticus] [13]:[10] and the Priest should examine him. ‘Then if [he finds] a white spot under the skin where all the hair has turned white and there are signs of good flesh in the sore;
[Leviticus] [13]:[11] this is an infection that has matured in the skin. So the Priest must pronounce him unclean and quarantine him, because he’s unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[12] ‘But if the infection becomes very visible and it covers all the person’s skin wherever the Priest looks, from his head to his feet,
[Leviticus] [13]:[13] and this is what the Priest finds; {Look!} the Priest must pronounce him clean of the plague, because once everything has turned white, he’s clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[14] ‘But if new flesh starts to appear again, he must be pronounced unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[15] ‘For if the Priest finds sound flesh; this sound flesh proves that he’s unclean and that he has an active infection.
[Leviticus] [13]:[16] ‘Then if the sound flesh changes back to white once again, he must return to the Priest,
[Leviticus] [13]:[17] and the Priest must examine him. If he then sees that the plague has all turned white, the Priest must pronounce him clean, for he’s clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[18] ‘And if [anyone] should develop a sore in his skin that heals,
[Leviticus] [13]:[19] then it turns white, or lighter, or very red; it should be examined by the Priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[20] ‘And if, when the Priest looks at it, he finds that it’s growing under the skin and that the hair has turned white; the Priest must pronounce him unclean, because an infection has broken out in the sore.
[Leviticus] [13]:[21] But if the Priest finds that there’s no white hair, and that it isn’t growing under the skin, but that it has a dark color; then the Priest must quarantine him for 7 days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[22] ‘And if he finds that it’s spreading over the skin, the Priest must pronounce him unclean; for an infection has broken out in the sore.
[Leviticus] [13]:[23] ‘However, if the bright spot stays the same and doesn’t spread, it’s just a scar, and the Priest must pronounce him clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[24] ‘But if the skin becomes inflamed and bright red, then appears to heal, but develops splotches that are bright, clear, and white, mixed with red or very white;
[Leviticus] [13]:[25] the Priest should examine him... If he finds the hair turning white and that the bright color is under the skin, an infection has broken out.
[Leviticus] [13]:[26] But if he sees that there isn’t any white hair in the inflammation and it isn’t growing under the skin, but is dark; the Priest must quarantine him for 7 days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[27] ‘Then on the 7th day, the Priest should examine him to see if the spot has spread in the skin. [If it has], the Priest will pronounce him unclean, because of the plague of infection that has broken out in the sore.
[Leviticus] [13]:[28] ‘But if the bright spot doesn’t move and doesn’t spread in the skin, but gets darker; it’s [just] the inflammation of a scar and the Priest will pronounce him clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[29] ‘And if a man or woman [thinks that they have] developed the plague of infection on the head or in the beard,
[Leviticus] [13]:[30] the Priest must examine it. ‘And if he finds that it’s growing under the skin and that the hair has turned thin and yellow, then the Priest will pronounce the person unclean; for the skin is dead and it’s an infection of the head or of the beard.
[Leviticus] [13]:[31] ‘However, if the Priest finds dead skin, but he sees nothing growing under the skin and there’s no yellowish hair; the Priest must quarantine the person for 7 days...
[Leviticus] [13]:[32] Then on the 7th day, the Priest must examine the person again. And if the dead skin hasn’t spread and there’s no yellowish hair on it, and there doesn’t appear to be a hollow spot under the skin,
[Leviticus] [13]:[33] the skin must be shaved everywhere except where the dead skin is, and the person should be quarantined a second time… For 7 more days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[34] ‘Then on the 7th day, the Priest must look to see if the dead skin has spread to the area that was shaved. [If it hasn’t], and if there doesn’t appear to be a hollow spot under the skin, the Priest will pronounce him clean, and he must wash his clothes and be clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[35] ‘However, if the dead skin does spread after he’s been purified,
[Leviticus] [13]:[36] the Priest must examine it and affirm that the dead skin has spread… And even if he finds no yellow hair, the person is unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[37] ‘But if the dead skin doesn’t spread and dark hair grows from it, the dead skin has healed and he’s clean; so, the Priest must pronounce him clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[38] ‘Now, if a man or woman develops bright white spots on his or her skin,
[Leviticus] [13]:[39] the Priest must look at it. ‘And if he just finds bright white spots on the skin, it’s psoriasis and he or she is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[40] [The same is true] when someone starts losing his hair; he’s just balding and he’s clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[41] If he loses his hair in the front, he has forehead baldness and is clean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[42] ‘But if white or red blotches should develop in the baldness on [the top of] his head or on his forehead, it’s an infection.
[Leviticus] [13]:[43] ‘The Priest must examine him, and if he finds white spots or an inflammation in the bald places on top or in the front that look like an infection,
[Leviticus] [13]:[44] he’s [to be considered] infected. The Priest must absolutely pronounce him unclean because of the plague on his head.
[Leviticus] [13]:[45] ‘Those who are infected must wear unbelted clothing and they must cover their heads and their mouths, and they are to call out: ‘Unclean!’
[Leviticus] [13]:[46] ‘They are always to be unclean as long as they have the plague on them. They are to separate themselves and travel outside of the camp.
[Leviticus] [13]:[47] ‘And if an infection is found in any wool or linen clothing,
[Leviticus] [13]:[48] or in anything that’s been woven with wool or linen thread, or in any leather or things that have been made with skin...
[Leviticus] [13]:[49] Or if you find a greenish or reddish coloring in the skin or in the clothing, or in the weaving, or in anything made of skin... It’s an infection, and you must show it to the Priest.
[Leviticus] [13]:[50] ‘Then the Priest must examine it and quarantine it for 7 days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[51] ‘Then on the 7th day, the Priest must examine it again; and if he finds that the plague has spread in the clothing, weaving, leather, or in whatever may be made from skin, it’s confirmed as an infection and it’s unclean.
[Leviticus] [13]:[52] ‘Then the clothing, or the wool or linen weaving, or the thing made of skin in which there’s the confirmed plague of infection, must be burned in a fire.
[Leviticus] [13]:[53] ‘However, if the Priest sees that the plague hasn’t spread in the clothing, weaving, or things made of skin,
[Leviticus] [13]:[54] he must instruct someone to wash the thing that held the plague, and the Priest will quarantine it a second time for 7 days.
[Leviticus] [13]:[55] ‘Then if the Priest sees that the plague hasn’t changed its appearance in the clothing or woven things after it’s been washed – even if it hasn’t spread – it’s unclean and it must be burned in a fire.
[Leviticus] [13]:[56] But if the Priest sees that the spot has turned dark after it was washed, he must cut it out of the clothing, weaving, or skin.
[Leviticus] [13]:[57] ‘However, if it still looks the same in the clothing, weaving, or skin; it’s an active plague of infection and it must be burned in a fire.
[Leviticus] [13]:[58] ‘But if the clothing, weaving, or thing made from skin washes clean, the plague has been removed. It must then be rewashed and be clean.’
[Leviticus] [13]:[59] These are the laws concerning the plague of infection on wool or linen clothing, weaving, and leather goods, to [show whether to] pronounce them as clean or unclean.

[Leviticus] [15]:[3] ‘This is the law concerning the uncleanness caused by gonorrhea in a body, and it describes the uncleanness that’s caused by the discharge that’s affecting his body, for as long as it keeps coming from his body, and of how his body is unclean due to the discharge.

[Leviticus] [15]:[24] ‘But if anyone lies with her and gets her uncleanness on him, he will be unclean for 7 days, and any bed that he lies on will be unclean.
[Leviticus] [15]:[25] ‘And if a woman has a blood flow for a long time (not just during her period of separation, but if her blood continues to flow after that), as long as it continues the unclean flow, she must separate herself and be unclean.

[Leviticus] [23]:[4] ‘Here are the feasts to [Jehovah]… The Holy Assemblies that you are to [observe] in each of their seasons:
[Leviticus] [23]:[5] The 14th day of the 1st month, from evening to evening, is [Jehovah’s] Passover.
[Leviticus] [23]:[6] Then the 15th day of that month is the Feast of Fermentation-free bread, so you must eat fermentation-free bread for 7 days.
[Leviticus] [23]:[7] The 1st [of these] days must be a Holy Assembly for you, and you must not work for anyone on that day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[8] Then you must offer whole-burnt offerings to [[Jehovah] during those] 7 days. And the 7th day will be [another] Holy Assembly for you, [during which] you must not work for anyone.’
[Leviticus] [23]:[9] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [23]:[10] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them: ‘When you enter the land that I’ll give to you and you start reaping its harvests, you must bring a bundle of [cut stalks] from the first fruitage of your harvest to the Priest,
[Leviticus] [23]:[11] and he must hold them up and wave the bundle before [[Jehovah], in order for Him to] accept it from you. ‘This must be done on the morning of the 1st day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[12] ‘And on that same day, you must offer a perfect yearling lamb as a whole-burnt offering to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[13] Then, along with this offering of meat, you [must offer] 2 quarts (1.9l) of fine flour mixed with oil as a sweet-smelling sacrifice and a quart of wine as a drink offering to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[14] ‘You may not eat any new bread or roasted grain until this day that you offer the sacrifices to your God. ‘This is a Law throughout the ages and throughout your generations for as long as you live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[15] ‘Thereafter, you must count the days, starting from the day after the Sabbath (when you offered the bundle of grain that was waved before [Jehovah]) and after 7 full weeks,
[Leviticus] [23]:[16] on the morning following the last week (or after 50 days), you must bring a food offering to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[17] ‘You must also bring two loaves [of bread] from your homes that are made from 2 quarts (1.9l) of fine flour baked with fermentation as an offering of your first fruitage to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[18] ‘And with the bread, you must bring 7 healthy yearling lambs, a calf from your herd, and two perfect male kid goats as whole-burnt offerings to [Jehovah]. These food and drink offerings are to be sacrificed as a sweet-smelling odor to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[19] ‘One of the kid goats must be sacrificed as a sin offering, and the 2 yearling lambs are to be offered with the first-fruit bread as a peace offering.
[Leviticus] [23]:[20] ‘The Priest must set them aside with the first-fruitage loaves as an offering before [Jehovah]. They will be holy to [Jehovah], and they’ll belong to the Priest who [offers] them.
[Leviticus] [23]:[21] ‘You must designate this as an Assembly Day, and it must be holy to you; so, you may not work for anyone on that day. This is a rule throughout all your generations, wherever you may live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[22] ‘And when you harvest your land, you must not reap everything in your field, nor may you gather anything that falls during the harvest. You must leave it for the poor and for strangers… For I am [Jehovah] your God!’
[Leviticus] [23]:[23] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [23]:[24] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them: ‘The 1st day of the 7th month will be a Sabbath, the Memorial of Trumpets... It will be a Holy Assembly.
[Leviticus] [23]:[25] You won’t do any work for anyone else, and you’ll offer a whole-burnt offering to [Jehovah].’
[Leviticus] [23]:[26] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [23]:[27] ‘Also, the 10th day of the 7th month is to be the Day of Atonement [when you must pay for your sins]. It [is also] to be a [day of] Holy Assembly for you. You must be very humble [on that day] and present a whole-burnt offering to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[28] ‘You must not do any work on that day, for it’s a day when you must pay for your sins before [Jehovah], your God.
[Leviticus] [23]:[29] ‘Any person who doesn’t show humility on that day must be cut off from among his people.
[Leviticus] [23]:[30] And any person who works on that day should have his life destroyed from among his people.
[Leviticus] [23]:[31] ‘Also, you must not do any sort of work! This is a law throughout the ages and throughout all your generations, wherever you may live.
[Leviticus] [23]:[32] ‘The 9th day of that month[that is, the 7th month], from evening to evening, is [also] to be a Holy Sabbath for you, and you must humble yourselves and keep your Sabbaths.’
[Leviticus] [23]:[33] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [23]:[34] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘The 15th day of the 7th month and the next 7 days are to be the Feast of Temporary Dwellings to [Jehovah]:
[Leviticus] [23]:[35] The 1st day must be a Holy Assembly [during which] you may not work for anyone.
[Leviticus] [23]:[36] You must offer whole-burnt offerings to [Jehovah] for the next 7 days... Then the 8th day will be a Holy Assembly to you [during which] you must offer whole-burnt offerings to [Jehovah]. This is [to be] a free day, so you must not work for anyone.
[Leviticus] [23]:[37] ‘These are the feasts to [Jehovah] that you are to call Holy Assemblies, [and during which] you are to offer burnt offerings to [Jehovah]… Whole-burnt offerings, food offerings, and drink offerings, each on its day.
[Leviticus] [23]:[38] ‘This is in addition to the Sabbaths to [Jehovah], to your gifts, to all your vows, and to all the free-will offerings that you’ll bring to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [23]:[39] ‘On the 15th day of the 7th month, after you have completely harvested all the fruitage of the ground, you must hold a feast to [Jehovah] for 7 days… And both the 1st and 8th days will be for resting.
[Leviticus] [23]:[40] ‘On the 1st day, you must bring: A large amount of fruit from your trees, Some palm-tree branches, Some thick tree branches, Willow branches, and Branches from water willows. ‘[All of this must be brought] as a rejoicing to [Jehovah] your God… [do this] for 7 days each year.
[Leviticus] [23]:[41] ‘This is to be the law throughout the ages for all your generations… You must observe this in the 7th month.
[Leviticus] [23]:[42] You must live in temporary structures for 7 days… Yes, all the native people of IsraEl must live in temporary structures,
[Leviticus] [23]:[43] so your descendants can see that I made the children of IsraEl live in such structures when I brought them out of the land of Egypt… For I am [Jehovah] your God!’
[Leviticus] [23]:[44] So, this is how Moses explained [Jehovah’s] feast days to the children of IsraEl.

[Leviticus] [24]:[11] Then, [during the fight], the IsraElite woman’s son used God’s Name while cursing… So, they brought him to Moses (his mother’s name was ShalomIth, and she was the daughter of DaBri of the tribe of Dan),

[Leviticus] [24]:[17] ‘Also: ‘Whenever a man strikes another man and kills him, he must absolutely be put to death.
[Leviticus] [24]:[18] And whenever a man strikes [someone’s] animal and it dies; he must give a life for the life.
[Leviticus] [24]:[19] ‘And whoever harms his neighbor must have the same thing done to him…
[Leviticus] [24]:[20] Bruise for bruise, eye for eye, tooth for tooth. Whatever damage he does to a man must be done to him.
[Leviticus] [24]:[21] ‘And if a man strikes a man and kills him, he must be put to death.
[Leviticus] [24]:[22] ‘This one judgment must be the same for both the natives and the aliens… For I am [Jehovah] your God!’
[Leviticus] [24]:[23] Well, after Moses said all these things to the children of IsraEl, they took the man who had done the cursing outside the camp and stoned him with rocks… The children of IsraEl did just as [Jehovah] had commanded Moses.
[Leviticus] [25]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses [while he was] on Mount SinAi and told him:

[Leviticus] [25]:[3] ‘You may plant your fields, prune your vines, and gather their fruitage for 6 years.
[Leviticus] [25]:[4] However, the 7th year will be a Sabbath, during which the land must rest. ‘During this Sabbath to [Jehovah], you may not plant your fields, prune your vines,
[Leviticus] [25]:[5] or gather anything that starts to grow of its own in your fields, nor may you completely gather all the sacred grapes; for it’s to be a year of rest for the ground.
[Leviticus] [25]:[6] ‘However, during the Sabbaths on the land, [there’ll be enough] food for you and for your male and female servants, those who work for you, as well as for any aliens that live among you.
[Leviticus] [25]:[7] ‘But, as for your cattle and the wild animals that live on your land... They may eat whatever they wish.
[Leviticus] [25]:[8] ‘Thereafter, you must keep track and [count off] 7 Sabbaths of years (7 times 7 years) to make 7 weeks of years, or 49 years.

[Leviticus] [25]:[11] The 50th year must be a Signal of Release among you. ‘So, you may not plant or harvest any of the produce that grows from the ground on its own, or gather any of its sacred fruit...
[Leviticus] [25]:[12] For it’s to be the Signal of Release, and it must be holy to you, during which you must eat the [stored] crops that you’ve harvested from the fields.
[Leviticus] [25]:[13] ‘In the year of the Release Signal, everyone must [be allowed] to return home...
[Leviticus] [25]:[14] ‘So, if you sell [your land] to a neighbor, or if you should buy your neighbor’s [land], it must not be [held permanently].
[Leviticus] [25]:[15] You must count the number of years after each Release Year from the time that you purchase [land] from your neighbor, then [figure out] how many years [you may own it] and how much you’ll likely harvest from it…
[Leviticus] [25]:[16] The more years, the higher the [land’s] value. ‘So, when there are few years, there’s less value, since there’ll be fewer crops, and [the price] should be [set lower].
[Leviticus] [25]:[17] No man should oppress his neighbor, for you must fear your God [Jehovah]… I am [Jehovah] your God!
[Leviticus] [25]:[18] ‘You must keep all My Laws and decisions and obey them. For if you follow and obey them, you’ll live in the land in safety,
[Leviticus] [25]:[19] the ground will provide abundantly, you’ll have plenty to eat, and you’ll live there in security.
[Leviticus] [25]:[20] ‘Now, if you should ask what you’ll eat during the 7th year if you don’t plant anything or pick your fruit;
[Leviticus] [25]:[21] I will send My blessings in the 6th year, and the land will produce abundant crops during [the previous] three years.
[Leviticus] [25]:[22] ‘Then you’ll start planting again in the 8th year and eat from your stored crops until the 9th year… Yes, until its crop comes in, you will eat from the stored crops.
[Leviticus] [25]:[23] ‘Therefore, no land may be sold permanently, since all the land is Mine and you’re just aliens and travelers before Me!
[Leviticus] [25]:[24] So, any land that you [buy] must also be repurchased.
[Leviticus] [25]:[25] ‘If your brother who lives near you is poor and has to sell [you] some of his land, and his relative should thereafter come to assist him; he must be allowed to buy back the land that his brother sold.
[Leviticus] [25]:[26] Or, if he has no such relative and he starts to prosper and finds enough money to buy it back himself...
[Leviticus] [25]:[27] He must calculate how many years the land has been sold, and pay the person to whom he sold it a fair amount… And then it should be returned.
[Leviticus] [25]:[28] ‘But if he hasn’t prospered enough to buy back the property; the one who bought it will own the land through the 6th year before the year of Release… Then it should be returned and its owner can go back to his land.
[Leviticus] [25]:[29] ‘If anyone sells an inhabited house within a walled city, it [can be] bought back again before a one year buying-back time runs out...
[Leviticus] [25]:[30] But if it’s not bought back within that year, the house in the walled city will be transferred to the buyer throughout his generations – and it won’t be returned in the Release [Signal].
[Leviticus] [25]:[31] ‘But houses in villages that don’t have a wall around them will just be considered like the fields of the countryside... They’ll always be available to buy back, and they’ll be returned [automatically] in the release [year].
[Leviticus] [25]:[32] ‘The houses within cities owned by the Levites shall be always available to buy back by the Levites.
[Leviticus] [25]:[33] And if anyone buys a Levite house, their purchased house will return in the Release [Signal]... Because the houses in the Levite cities are their possession within the children of Israel.
[Leviticus] [25]:[34] ‘Also, the land reserved for their cities can’t be sold, because this is their age-long possession.
[Leviticus] [25]:[35] ‘Also, if your brother who lives among you becomes poor and needs to [borrow some money] from you, you must help him as you would an alien or a traveler, so that your brother may continue to live among you.
[Leviticus] [25]:[36] You must not charge him interest or [tell him] to pay you more; for you must fear your God… I am [Jehovah]! ‘And you must [help] your brother to keep living among you.
[Leviticus] [25]:[37] ‘You must not lend your money to him for interest, and you must not lend him any food and expect him to pay you back with more,
[Leviticus] [25]:[38] for I am [Jehovah] your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt to give you the land of CanaAn and to be your God.
[Leviticus] [25]:[39] ‘And if your brother should become so poorly off that he sells himself to you, he must not serve and work as your slave…
[Leviticus] [25]:[40] You must treat him like a hired person or as a traveler, and he will only work for you until the Year of Release.
[Leviticus] [25]:[41] ‘Then, during the Release, he and his children will leave as a family, and they will hurry back to their family possessions,
[Leviticus] [25]:[42] because they are My servants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt. ‘So, they can’t be sold as slaves,
[Leviticus] [25]:[43] nor may you force them into hard labor... For you must fear [Jehovah] your God.
[Leviticus] [25]:[44] ‘If you wish to purchase male and female slaves, buy them from the nations that live around you.

[Leviticus] [25]:[46] and may be left as an inheritance to your children after you, and be your [family] possession throughout the ages. ‘However, you must never oppress your brothers of the children of IsraEl by forcing them to do hard labor.
[Leviticus] [25]:[47] ‘And if an alien or a traveler who lives among you should become rich, and your brother who is in need is sold to the alien or traveler who lives among you, or to an [IsraElite] convert...
[Leviticus] [25]:[48] After he has been sold, one of his brothers must buy him back.
[Leviticus] [25]:[49] An uncle, a cousin, or another close relative from his tribe must be allowed to buy him… Or if he gets wealthy, he may buy himself back.
[Leviticus] [25]:[50] ‘The person who buys him must calculate how many years there were from the time that he sold himself until the Year of Release, and then pay the amount that would be paid to a hired person during that number of years.
[Leviticus] [25]:[51] ‘And if anyone has [enough money] to pay [the wages] for all those years, he must pay the ransom.

[Leviticus] [25]:[54] ‘And if he can’t pay his own fair ransom, he and his children must be set free in the Year of Release.
[Leviticus] [25]:[55] For the children of IsraEl are My servants… They are My attendants whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.’
