[Leviticus] [27]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Leviticus] [27]:[2] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘Whenever anyone wishes to make a vow to offer the value of a person to [Jehovah]:
[Leviticus] [27]:[3] The value of a male between 20 and 60 years old must be 50 double-silver coins by the standards of the Holy Place.
[Leviticus] [27]:[4] The value of an [adult] female must be 30 double-silver coins.
[Leviticus] [27]:[5] The value for a male child between 5 and 20 years old must be 20 double-silver coins. And 10 double-silver coins for a female [child].
[Leviticus] [27]:[6] ‘As for a child between 1 month and 5 years old: The value for a male must be 5 double-silver coins, and For a female, 3 double-silver coins.
[Leviticus] [27]:[7] ‘And for those who are over 60, the value must be: 15 double-silver coins for a male, and 10 double-silver coins for a female.
[Leviticus] [27]:[8] ‘But if a person is too poor to pay these values, he must go before the Priest, and the Priest will value him at whatever the man says he can afford in his vow; and that’s [the price] that the Priest must set for him.
[Leviticus] [27]:[9] ‘When cattle are offered as gifts to [Jehovah] by anyone, they become holy.
[Leviticus] [27]:[10] So, the [person] may not trade a good one for a bad one, or a bad one for a good one... If someone does decide to make a trade, it must be with an equal… And both animals will be holy.
[Leviticus] [27]:[11] ‘If [someone should bring] an unclean animal (which must never be offered as a gift to [Jehovah]), He must lead the animal to the Priest,
[Leviticus] [27]:[12] and the Priest must determine whether it has any value. Then, whatever value the Priest sets is what must be paid for it.
[Leviticus] [27]:[13] ‘And if he wishes to buy it back, he must pay 1/5th more than that amount.
[Leviticus] [27]:[14] ‘If a man chooses to set aside his house as holy to [Jehovah], the Priest must determine whether or not it has any value, and whatever value the Priest sets is what must be paid.
[Leviticus] [27]:[15] ‘Then if he wishes to buy it back, he must pay 1/5th more for it than the valuation.
[Leviticus] [27]:[16] ‘If a man should choose to designate a portion of a field that he owns as holy to [Jehovah], it must be valued by whatever is planted there. ‘It will be worth 50 double-silver coins for every 250 quarts (230l) of barley…
[Leviticus] [27]:[17] That is, that’s how much it should be valued if he should [set aside] his field as holy on the Year of Release.
[Leviticus] [27]:[18] ‘But if he donates his field sometime after the Release, the Priest must figure its value to the next Year of Release and deduct the appropriate amount from the full valuation.
[Leviticus] [27]:[19] ‘However, if the one who made the field holy wishes to buy it back [before the Year of Release], he must add 1/5th more to its value and it will be his once again.
[Leviticus] [27]:[20] ‘But if he doesn’t buy back the field, it may be sold to someone else… And then he can’t buy it back later.
[Leviticus] [27]:[21] For after the Release, the field will be holy to [Jehovah] and thereafter be subdivided… Because the Priests will then own it.
[Leviticus] [27]:[22] ‘And if a man should set aside a field to [Jehovah] that he has bought and it isn’t a family possession...
[Leviticus] [27]:[23] The Priest must calculate its value to the Year of Release, and that’s how much he must pay that day, as something holy to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [27]:[24] ‘Then in the Year of Release, the land must be restored to the man who sold it and [really] owns the land.
[Leviticus] [27]:[25] ‘All the values must be determined by using the holy weights; a double-silver coin is worth 20 copper coins.
[Leviticus] [27]:[26] ‘All the firstborn cattle are already [Jehovah’s], so no man can [set them aside] as holy… Whether it’s a calf or a sheep, it belongs to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [27]:[27] ‘If [a man] should choose to buy back an unclean animal, he must add 1/5th more to its valuation. But if he doesn’t buy it back, it may be sold at its stated value.
[Leviticus] [27]:[28] ‘Anything a man has that he chooses to curse before [Jehovah], whether it’s a man, an animal, or a field that he owns... It may never be sold or taken back. Everything that is cursed for destruction becomes very holy to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [27]:[29] And anyone from among mankind who is cursed may never be ransomed, but must surely be put to death.
[Leviticus] [27]:[30] ‘Anything in the land that is to be offered, whether it’s seeds or the fruit of trees, is [Jehovah’s]… It’s holy to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [27]:[31] ‘And if any man should ever wish to buy back his offering, he must add 1/5th more to its [value], and it will be his.
[Leviticus] [27]:[32] ‘A 1/10th of everything, including bulls, sheep, and anything else that is taxable, is also holy to [Jehovah].
[Leviticus] [27]:[33] ‘So, you may never exchange anything good for anything bad, or anything bad for anything good... If you should make an exchange, it must be with an equivalent; and since it is holy, it cannot be repurchased.’
[Leviticus] [27]:[34] These are the commandments that the Lord gave to Moses for the sons of IsraEl on Mount SinAi.
[Numbers] [1]:[1] On the 1st day of the 2nd month ([while they were still] in the desert at SinAi), 2 years after their departure from the land of Egypt, the Lord spoke to Moses inside the Tent of Proofs and said:
[Numbers] [1]:[2] ‘Take a census of the entire gathering of IsraEl by families and lines of descent. [Record] the names of all the males
[Numbers] [1]:[3] that are 20 years old and older… All who serve as the army of IsraEl. ‘You and Aaron must count them and calculate their strength.
[Numbers] [1]:[4] ‘Also, the rulers of each of the tribes (the paternal heads of the families) should accompany you as you do this.
[Numbers] [1]:[5] ‘These are the names of the men who should help you: From the tribe of ReuBen, EliSur son of SediUr.
[Numbers] [1]:[6] From the [tribe of] SymeOn, SalamiEl son of SuriSadai.
[Numbers] [1]:[7] [From the tribe] of Judah, NaAsson son of AmiNadab.
[Numbers] [1]:[8] [From the tribe] of IshSachar, NathaniEl son of Sogar.
[Numbers] [1]:[9] [From the tribe] of ZebuLon, EliAb son of ChaElon.
[Numbers] [1]:[10] [From the two tribes] of JoSeph, EliSama son of EmiUd for Ephraim, and GamaliEl son of PhadaSur for ManasSeh.
[Numbers] [1]:[11] [From the tribe] of BenJamin, AbiDan son of GadeOni.
[Numbers] [1]:[12] [From the tribe] of Dan, AchiEzer son of AmiSadai.
[Numbers] [1]:[13] [From the tribe] of Asher, PhagaiEl son of Echran.
[Numbers] [1]:[14] [From the tribe] of Gad, EliSaph son of RaguEl.
[Numbers] [1]:[15] [From the tribe] of NaphTali, AchiRe son of AiNan.’
[Numbers] [1]:[16] These were the most famous men among the gathering. They were the heads of the tribes by their families, and each one was a leader of thousands in IsraEl.
[Numbers] [1]:[17] So Moses and Aaron gathered these men who’d been called by name.
[Numbers] [1]:[18] Then they assembled the entire gathering that day and registered the [men] by tribes and family lines, recording the names and numbers of all those who were 20 [years old] and older,
[Numbers] [1]:[19] as the Lord had commanded Moses there in the desert of SinAi.
[Numbers] [1]:[20] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of ReuBen (the first-born of IsraEl), the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[21] was: 46,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[22] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of SymeOn, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[23] was: 59,300.
[Numbers] [1]:[24] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of Judah, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[25] was: 74,600.
[Numbers] [1]:[26] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of IshSachar, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[27] was 54,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[28] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of ZebuLon, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[29] was: 57,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[30] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of JoSeph: From the Tribe of Ephraim, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[31] was 40,500.
[Numbers] [1]:[32] From the Tribe of ManasSeh, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[33] was: 32,200.
[Numbers] [1]:[34] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of BenJamin, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[35] was: 35,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[36] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of Gad, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[37] was: 45,650.
[Numbers] [1]:[38] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of Dan, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[39] was: 62,700.
[Numbers] [1]:[40] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of Asher, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl
[Numbers] [1]:[41] was: 41,500.
[Numbers] [1]:[42] Among the families, divisions, and households of the sons of NaphTali, the number of males 20 years old and up that were counted as the strength of IsraEl,
[Numbers] [1]:[43] was: 53,400.
[Numbers] [1]:[44] This was the census that Moses, Aaron, and the 12 rulers of IsraEl conducted… A man from each tribe.
[Numbers] [1]:[45] They counted all the males 20 years old and up among the children of IsraEl that could [serve in their army],
[Numbers] [1]:[46] [and there was a total of] 618,550.
[Numbers] [1]:[47] However, those of the Tribe of Levi weren’t counted,
[Numbers] [1]:[48] for the Lord had told Moses:
[Numbers] [1]:[49] ‘You must not gather the Tribe of Levi and count them among the children of IsraEl.
[Numbers] [1]:[50] Rather, put the Levites in charge of the Tent, its furnishings, and everything in it. ‘They must serve there and camp around the Tent.
[Numbers] [1]:[51] ‘And whenever the Tent is moved, the Levites must take it down and [be in charge of] setting it up again. Anyone else who goes near it must die.
[Numbers] [1]:[52] ‘The [rest of] the children of IsraEl must camp in the order and grouping of their own armies...
[Numbers] [1]:[53] But the Levites must camp around and in front of the Tent of Proofs, so there may be no sins among the children of IsraEl. ‘For the Levites must protect the Tent of Proofs.’
[Numbers] [1]:[54] And the children of IsraEl did everything that [Jehovah] commanded Moses and Aaron.
[Numbers] [2]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
[Numbers] [2]:[2] ‘Each man of the sons of IsraEl must set up his tent according to the signals, in his own order, and according to the house of his father, in a circle around the Tent of Proofs:
[Numbers] [2]:[3] ‘The first in the camp, starting on the east side, shall be the [Tribe] of Judah with their armies. Their leader is NaShon (son of AmmiNadab).
[Numbers] [2]:[4] ‘There are 74,600 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[5] ‘The Tribe of IshSachar, whose leader is NathanEl (son of Zuar), should camp next to them.
[Numbers] [2]:[6] ‘There are 54,400 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[7] ‘The Tribe of ZebuLon, whose leader is EliAb (son of Helon), should camp next to them.
[Numbers] [2]:[8] ‘There are 57,400 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[9] ‘Altogether, there are 186,400 under the army of Judah. They and their armies must be the first to move.
[Numbers] [2]:[10] ‘This is the order for the camp of ReuBen, whose army [will camp] towards the south. The leader of the children of ReuBen is EliZur (son of ShedeUr).
[Numbers] [2]:[11] ‘There are 46,500 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[12] ‘The Tribe of SimeOn, whose leader is ShelumiEl (son of ZuriShadDai), should camp next to them.
[Numbers] [2]:[13] ‘There are 59,300 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[14] ‘The Tribe of Gad, whose leader is EliAsaph (son of DeuEl), will camp next to them.
[Numbers] [2]:[15] ‘There are 45,650 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[16] ‘Altogether, there are 151,450 under the army of ReuBen. They and their armies will follow second.
[Numbers] [2]:[17] ‘Then the Tent of Proofs should follow them, surrounded by the Levites who’ll travel between the armies. In whatever order they camp, that’s the order that they should follow in their march, each group traveling in the order of their divisions.
[Numbers] [2]:[18] ‘The Tribe of Ephraim and their armies must camp on the west side. Their leader is EliShama, (son of AmmiHud).
[Numbers] [2]:[19] ‘There are 40,500 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[20] ‘The Tribe of ManasSeh should camp next to them. Their leader is GamaliEl (son of PedahZur).
[Numbers] [2]:[21] ‘There are 32,200 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[22] ‘The Tribe of BenJamin should camp next to them. Their leader is AbiDan (son of Gideoni).
[Numbers] [2]:[23] ‘There are 35,400 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[24] ‘Altogether, there are 108,100 in the army of Ephraim. They and their armies must follow third.
[Numbers] [2]:[25] ‘The Tribe of Dan and their armies should camp on the north side. Their leader is AhiEzer (son of AmmiShadDai).
[Numbers] [2]:[26] ‘There are 62,700 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[27] ‘The Tribe of Asher should camp next to them. Their leader is PagiEl (son of OcRan). ‘
[Numbers] [2]:[28] There are 41,500 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[29] ‘The Tribe of NaphTali should camp next to them. Their leader is AhiRa (son of Enan).
[Numbers] [2]:[30] ‘There are 53,400 in his army.
[Numbers] [2]:[31] ‘Altogether, there are 157,600 in the armies of Dan, and they must be last in the marching order.’
[Numbers] [2]:[32] This is how the children of IsraEl were counted (by family lines), and there were [a total of] 603,550 in their army.
[Numbers] [2]:[33] However, the Levites weren’t counted among them, just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
[Numbers] [2]:[34] And the children of IsraEl did everything that [Jehovah] told Moses. They each camped in their [specified] locations, and they marched in order by family lines.
[Numbers] [3]:[1] These are the generations of Aaron and Moses in the day in that the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount SinAi.
[Numbers] [3]:[2] These are the names of the sons of Aaron: NaDab (the firstborn), AbiUd, EliEzer, and IthaMar.
[Numbers] [3]:[3] They were the Anointed Priests who were made perfect for the Priesthood.
[Numbers] [3]:[4] However, NaDab and AbiUd died before [Jehovah] when they offered [incense] to Him in an unauthorized way, while they were in the SinAi Desert. And because they had no children, just EliEzer and IthaMar served as Priests with their father Aaron.
[Numbers] [3]:[5] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and told him:
[Numbers] [3]:[6] ‘Bring the Tribe of Levi up in front of Aaron the Priest, for they’re all going to serve him
[Numbers] [3]:[7] and they must follow his instructions. You must explain this to the children of IsraEl in front of the Tent of Proofs, and show how [the Levites] will thereafter perform their duties at the Tent.
[Numbers] [3]:[8] ‘[The Levites] are to take care of all the furnishings of the Tent of Proofs and they must teach the children of IsraEl about everything that has to do with the Tent.
[Numbers] [3]:[9] ‘You are to give the Levites to Aaron and his sons (the Priests)... For they’ve been given to Me as a gift from the children of IsraEl.
[Numbers] [3]:[10] ‘Appoint Aaron and his sons to be in charge of the Tent of Proofs, and they must give [the Levites] instructions about the Priesthood, everything that belongs to the Altar, and everything inside the veil… Anyone else who touches these things must die.’
[Numbers] [3]:[11] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [3]:[12] ‘Look, I have chosen the Levites from among the children of IsraEl [to take the place] of [all of] the [firstborn] males who are among the children of IsraEl. [The Levites] are their ransom, and they’re Mine.
[Numbers] [3]:[13] For all their firstborn have been Mine since the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. I chose all the firstborn in IsraEl as holy to Myself – both the men and the animals – and they’re Mine! ‘For I am [Jehovah]!’
[Numbers] [3]:[14] Then the Lord spoke to Moses in the SinAi Desert and said:
[Numbers] [3]:[15] ‘Take a census of the sons of Levi by family lines and divisions… Count every male from a month old and up.’
[Numbers] [3]:[16] So thereafter, Moses and Aaron counted them all following [Jehovah’s] instructions.
[Numbers] [3]:[17] The sons of Levi were: GedSon, CaAth, and MeraRi.
[Numbers] [3]:[18] GedSon’s sons (and family lines) were: LoBeni, and Semei.
[Numbers] [3]:[19] CaAth’s sons (and family lines) were: AmBram, IsSaAr, HebRon, and OziEl.
[Numbers] [3]:[20] MeraRi’s sons (and family lines) were: MoOli, and Musi. These were the families of the Levites by family lines.
[Numbers] [3]:[21] GedSon‘s [sons] were LoBeni and Semei,
[Numbers] [3]:[22] and the number of males descending from them that were a month old and older was 7,500…
[Numbers] [3]:[23] The sons of GedSon were to camp behind the Tent on its west side.
[Numbers] [3]:[24] The ruler of the family of GedSon was EliSaph (son of DaEl).
[Numbers] [3]:[25] The instructions that were given to the sons of GedSon concerning the Tent of Proofs included taking care of the tent itself, the veil that covers the entrance to the Tent of Proofs,
[Numbers] [3]:[26] the curtains for the courtyard, the veil to the courtyard that was around the Tent, and such things.
[Numbers] [3]:[27] The divisions that were counted [in the family line] of CaAth were those of AmBram, IsSaAr, HebRon, and OziEl,
[Numbers] [3]:[28] and they included 8,600 males a month old and older, who were given these instructions regarding the holy things.
[Numbers] [3]:[29] The families of the sons of CaAth were to camp next to the Tent, along its south side.
[Numbers] [3]:[30] The ruler of the family line and divisions of CaAth was EliShaphan (son of OziEl).
[Numbers] [3]:[31] They were told that they were to be in charge of the Chest, the Table, the Sacred Lamp, the Altars, and all the furnishings in the Holy Place that were used in holy service inside the veil, and all their parts.
[Numbers] [3]:[32] The head over the chiefs of the Levites was EliEzer, the son of Aaron the Priest. He was appointed to give all the instructions regarding the holy things.
[Numbers] [3]:[33] The family lines of MeraRi were those of MoOli and Musi.
[Numbers] [3]:[34] All the males a month old and older among his line were counted at 6,050.
[Numbers] [3]:[35] The head of the family line and divisions of MeraRi was SuriEl (son of AbiChail). They were to camp next to the Tent, along its north side.
[Numbers] [3]:[36] The sons of MeraRi were told that they were to be in charge of the Tent’s caps, rafters, posts, sockets, all their fittings and pieces,
[Numbers] [3]:[37] the posts for the courtyard, and their bases, pins, and ropes.
[Numbers] [3]:[38] Moses, Aaron, and their sons were to camp in front of the Tent of Proofs on its east side. They were to take care of the Holy Place and give instructions about it to the children of IsraEl. Anyone else who touched it was to die.
[Numbers] [3]:[39] All the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted that were a month old and older (by family lines) following [Jehovah’s] instructions, were 22,000.
[Numbers] [3]:[40] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said: ‘Now, count all the firstborn males among the children of IsraEl who are a month old and older, and record their names.
[Numbers] [3]:[41] Thereafter, take the Levites for Me in place of all the firstborn of the sons of IsraEl. ‘Also, take all the Levites’ cattle in place of the first-born of the cattle of the children of IsraEl… For I am [Jehovah]!’
[Numbers] [3]:[42] So Moses counted all the firstborn of the children of IsraEl, just as the Lord had commanded him to do.
[Numbers] [3]:[43] And all the male firstborn a month old and older that were counted by name were 22,273.
[Numbers] [3]:[44] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [3]:[45] ‘Now, take the Levites in place of all the first-born of the sons of IsraEl, and take the Levite’s cattle in place of their cattle, for they must be Mine… I am [Jehovah]!
[Numbers] [3]:[46] ‘And the ransom [that must be paid] for all the firstborn of the sons of IsraEl that exceed the number of Levites (the 273),
[Numbers] [3]:[47] [must be paid for] with 5 silver-coins per person. They must be paid for using the holy double-silver coins at 20 copper coins per silver coin...
[Numbers] [3]:[48] Then, give the money to Aaron and his sons as the ransom for those who exceed their number.’
[Numbers] [3]:[49] So Moses took the silver as the ransom for those who exceeded the number that were bought by the Levites.
[Numbers] [3]:[50] The amount of holy silver coins that he took from the firstborn of the sons of IsraEl was 1,365.
[Numbers] [3]:[51] Then Moses gave the ransom for these extra ones to Aaron and his sons, according to the instructions that the Lord had given to Moses.
[Numbers] [4]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
[Numbers] [4]:[2] ‘Take a census of the children of CaAth separate from the sons of Levi, by family lines.
[Numbers] [4]:[3] Count those from 25 to 50 years old that work at and serve inside the Tent of Proofs.
[Numbers] [4]:[4] ‘For, these are the very holy things that the sons of CaAth must do at the Tent of Proofs:
[Numbers] [4]:[5] ‘Whenever the camp is about to move, Aaron and his sons must enter and take down the [inner] veil, then use it to cover the Chest of Proofs...
[Numbers] [4]:[6] It must be covered with a blue skin and a blue [cloth] over that, and then they must put the carrying poles through [the rings on the Chest].
[Numbers] [4]:[7] ‘They must also put a purple cloth over the Table that holds the showbread, along with its dishes, incense holders, cups, pitchers for drink offerings, and the loaves (which must always be left on the table)...
[Numbers] [4]:[8] Then they must cover it with a scarlet cloth and cover that with a blue skin, and mount [the table] on its staves.
[Numbers] [4]:[9] ‘They must cover the Sacred Lamp that provides the light, along with its lanterns, snuffers, funnels, and all the oil jars, with a blue cloth,
[Numbers] [4]:[10] and put it and all its utensils inside a blue skin bag, and mount it on its staves.
[Numbers] [4]:[11] ‘Also, the gold [Incense] Altar must be wrapped in blue cloth, then covered with blue skins and mounted on its staves.
[Numbers] [4]:[12] ‘Thereafter, they must take all the rest of the things that are used in the services at the Holy Place and put them in a blue cloth [bag], then cover them with blue skins and mount them on staves.
[Numbers] [4]:[13] ‘They must cover the Altar with purple cloth,
[Numbers] [4]:[14] along with all the utensils that are used with it (the fire pans, flesh-hooks, cups, covers, and all the utensils), wrap it all in a blue covering of skins and mount it all on the staves. ‘They must also cover the Basin and its base with blue cloth, then wrap it in blue skins and mount it on staves.
[Numbers] [4]:[15] ‘Aaron and his sons must finish covering the holy things and all the holy utensils before the camp can move... Thereafter, the sons of CaAth must bear all [the Tent’s] furnishings… But they must not [actually] touch the holy things, or they’ll die. These [are the things] that just the sons of CaAth are to carry from the Tent of Proofs.
[Numbers] [4]:[16] ‘EliEzer, the son of Aaron the Priest, is to be their overseer... He is to give instructions concerning the oil for the lamp, the incense, the daily food offerings, and the anointing oil. He is to be in charge of the whole Tent, everything that’s in it, and everything that’s done there.’
[Numbers] [4]:[17] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
[Numbers] [4]:[18] ‘You must protect the family of CaAth (this tribe among the Levites) from being destroyed,
[Numbers] [4]:[19] and this is what you must do for them so they can live and not die: ‘Whenever they approach the Holy of Holies, Aaron and his sons must take the lead... They’re the ones who must mount the [sacred items] to be carried on the staves.
[Numbers] [4]:[20] That way, [the family of CaAth] won’t [be tempted to] rush in to look at the holy things and die.’
[Numbers] [4]:[21] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [4]:[22] ‘Now, take a census of the children of GedSon by family lines...
[Numbers] [4]:[23] Count all those between the ages of 25 and 50 years old that go in to serve and work in the Tent of Proofs,
[Numbers] [4]:[24] because the public service of the family of GedSon is that of serving and carrying.
[Numbers] [4]:[25] ‘They must carry and attend to the skins for the Tent, the Tent of Proofs itself, its veil, the blue covering that goes over its top, the cover for the entrance to the Tent of Proofs,
[Numbers] [4]:[26] all the curtains for the courtyard, the mountings, and all the other utensils of service.
[Numbers] [4]:[27] ‘The sons of GedSon must take their direction from Aaron and his sons in everything that they do in their assignments and jobs. ‘You must count them by names and [show them] all the things that they must carry…
[Numbers] [4]:[28] This is the job of the sons of GedSon in the Tent of Proofs, and IthaMar, the son of Aaron the Priest, is to give them their instructions.
[Numbers] [4]:[29] ‘Also, take a census of the sons of MeraRi by family lines.
[Numbers] [4]:[30] Count all those between the ages of 25 and 50 years old that enter to serve and work inside the Tent of Proofs.
[Numbers] [4]:[31] ‘These are the things you are to tell them about and what they must carry as their job at the Tent of Proofs... They must carry the Tent’s caps, rafters, poles, and sockets, as well as the sockets and poles for the veil and the curtain at the entrance to the Tent.

[Numbers] [5]:[1] Thereafter, the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [5]:[2] ‘Give these instructions to the children of IsraEl... ‘Tell them to drive everyone out of the camp who has an infection or gonorrhea, and anyone who has made himself unclean [by touching a dead] person,
[Numbers] [5]:[3] whether they’re males or females... Drive them out of the camp so they don’t dirty the place where I dwell among them.’
[Numbers] [5]:[4] And that’s what the children of IsraEl did; they drove them out of the camp, just as the Lord told Moses.
[Numbers] [5]:[5] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [5]:[6] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘Any man or woman who has committed any of the sins that are common to mankind, or has in any way overstepped [My] Commandments and erred,
[Numbers] [5]:[7] must confess the sin he committed and make restitution for his sin. ‘He [must pay] the price to restore [everything] to whomever he’s sinned against… And add 1/5th more to it.
[Numbers] [5]:[8] ‘Now, if a man isn’t in debt to anyone for his sins against them, a sin-offering must still be paid to [Jehovah], and he must offer a ram to the Priest as the payment for his sins.
[Numbers] [5]:[9] ‘When it comes to the first fruitage of all the holy things among the children of IsraEl, everything that they offer to [Jehovah] must be [given to] the Priest for himself…
[Numbers] [5]:[10] All the holy things that men [offer] or choose to donate must be given to the Priest, and it will be his as a gift.’
[Numbers] [5]:[11] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [5]:[12] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘Whenever a wife rebels against [her husband] and tries to dominate and rule over him,
[Numbers] [5]:[13] and then someone goes to bed with her and has sex with her behind her husband’s back... If she hides her filth and there’s no proof of it, and [the other man] doesn’t take her,
[Numbers] [5]:[14] and [her husband] thereafter develops a jealous spirit and suspects that she’s dirtied herself – or even if he’s developed a jealous spirit when she hasn’t dirtied herself –
[Numbers] [5]:[15] he must bring his woman to the Priest, along with the gift of a quart of barley meal. ‘He must not pour any oil or frankincense on the barley meal, for it’s a sacrifice of jealousy… It’s a sacrifice of memory and of recalling sins to mind.
[Numbers] [5]:[16] ‘Then the Priest must take [the woman] to stand before [Jehovah],
[Numbers] [5]:[17] and the Priest must pour clean running water into a clay pot, then take some of the dirt that’s on the floor of the Tent of Proofs and throw it into the water...
[Numbers] [5]:[18] Thereafter, the Priest must stand the woman before [Jehovah], uncover her head, and place the sacrifice of memory (the sacrifice of jealousy) into her hands. ‘Next, the Priest must take the water that brings a curse into his hands,
[Numbers] [5]:[19] and the Priest must make the woman swear [in reply to the words]: ‘If you aren’t guilty and no one has reclined with you, and if you haven’t sinned and dirtied yourself, and if you haven’t [been disrespectful] to your husband; [then, swear that you’re innocent] before this water that brings the curse.
[Numbers] [5]:[20] ‘But if you have sinned and dirtied your marriage, and [if you’ve allowed] someone to lie with you other than your husband...’
[Numbers] [5]:[21] ‘Then the Priest must make the woman swear [to accept] the oaths of this curse. ‘The Priest must say to her: ‘May [Jehovah] bring a curse upon you by the oath [you’ve sworn] in the midst of your people. ‘May [Jehovah] cause your [sexual parts] to rot away and your belly to swell.
[Numbers] [5]:[22] ‘May this water that brings the curse enter your womb and cause your belly to swell and your [sexual parts] to rot away.’ ‘And the woman must say: ‘May it be so... May it be so.’
[Numbers] [5]:[23] ‘Thereafter, the Priest must write these curses on a scroll, then rinse them away with the water that brings the curse.
[Numbers] [5]:[24] And he must make the woman drink the water that brings the curse.
[Numbers] [5]:[25] ‘Next, the Priest must take the sacrifice of jealousy from the woman’s hands and carry it to the Altar to present it before [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [5]:[26] Then the Priest must take a handful of the sacrificial [grain] and offer it on the Altar as a reminder, and he must make the woman drink the water.
[Numbers] [5]:[27] ‘For, this is what will happen: ‘If she has dirtied herself and her husband hasn’t been able to [prove] it, the water that brings the curse will enter her and cause her belly to swell and her [sexual parts] to rot away. And thereafter, the woman must be cursed among her people.
[Numbers] [5]:[28] ‘But if the woman hasn’t dirtied herself and has remained chaste, she must be declared free of guilt and thereafter give birth to a [child].’
[Numbers] [5]:[29] This is the law of jealousy [that covers the cases in which] a married woman sins and dirties herself,
[Numbers] [5]:[30] or where a man develops a jealous spirit and becomes jealous of his woman. He should take his woman before [Jehovah], and the Priest must make her follow this law.
[Numbers] [5]:[31] And whereas the man will be cleared from his sin [of jealousy], the woman must be responsible for hers.
[Numbers] [6]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [6]:[2] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘Whenever a man or woman wishes to make a great vow, to set him or herself aside as holy to [Jehovah],
[Numbers] [6]:[3] they may not eat or drink anything made from grapes, such as wine, brandy, fresh grapes, raisins, or vinegar that’s made from wine or other alcoholic products
[Numbers] [6]:[4] during the period of their vow. Nor may he or she eat anything that comes from the vine, not even the seeds or skins
[Numbers] [6]:[5] during the whole period that he or she is set aside! ‘Nor may a razor be used to cut the person’s hair until the period of the vow to [Jehovah] has been completed. Such ones must be holy and cherish the long hair of their heads
[Numbers] [6]:[6] for as long as this vow to [Jehovah] lasts, and they must not go near any dead bodies…
[Numbers] [6]:[7] Not even [the corpse] of their own father, mother, brother, or sister. They must not dirty themselves with dead bodies, because the vow of God is on them and on their heads.
[Numbers] [6]:[8] ‘So, they must remain holy to [Jehovah] during the entire period of their vow.
[Numbers] [6]:[9] ‘And if anyone should suddenly die near this person, his or her head will immediately be considered unclean and it must be cleansed. The person must shave his or her head on the 7th day,
[Numbers] [6]:[10] then bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the Priest at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs on the 8th day...
[Numbers] [6]:[11] The Priest must offer one as a sin offering and the other as a whole-burnt offering to pay for the sin [of being close to] a dead body. ‘Then the person’s head will [once again] become holy on that day,
[Numbers] [6]:[12] and he or she will [again] be made perfect to [Jehovah] during the rest of [the period of] the vow. And thereafter, the person must bring a yearling lamb as an offering for the error; and because the vow on his/her head was polluted, the full period of [the vow] must be [restarted].
[Numbers] [6]:[13] ‘It’s also the law for the person who made such a vow, that on the day the vow is completed, he or she must bring gifts to the entrance of the Tent of Proofs...
[Numbers] [6]:[14] ‘The gifts that they must bring to [Jehovah] include: One perfect yearling male lamb as a whole-burnt offering, One perfect yearling female lamb as a sin offering, One perfect male sheep as a peace offering,
[Numbers] [6]:[15] A basket of fermentation-free bread made with fine flour kneaded with oil, Fermentation-free cakes that have been anointed with oil, plus A food offering and a drink offering.
[Numbers] [6]:[16] ‘The Priest must then lead the person before [Jehovah] and [sacrifice] the sin offering and the whole-burnt offering.
[Numbers] [6]:[17] Then he must sacrifice the male sheep as a peace offering to [Jehovah], along with the basket of fermentation-free bread, followed by the food offering and the drink offering.
[Numbers] [6]:[18] ‘Then the one who made the vow must shave their head that was made holy, there at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs, and put the hair on the fire while it’s burning the peace-offering sacrifice.
[Numbers] [6]:[19] ‘Then, after the person has shaved off their holy hair, the Priest must take the larger of the ram’s two shoulders, along with one fermentation-free loaf and one fermentation-free cake from the basket and lay them in the person’s hands...
[Numbers] [6]:[20] The Priest must then present them as an offering before [Jehovah], and this holy portion will belong to the Priest, along with the breast and the shoulder of the wave offering. ‘And after that, the person who made the oath must drink some wine.
[Numbers] [6]:[21] ‘This is the law for any person who makes a vow to [Jehovah]. [He must give all] his gifts that were promised to [Jehovah], along with anything else that he may be able to afford, [in addition to] the things that are [required by] the strong vow of setting himself aside as holy.’
[Numbers] [6]:[22] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [6]:[23] ‘Speak to Aaron and to his sons and tell them to bless the sons of IsraEl who bear My Name with these words:
[Numbers] [6]:[24] ‘May [Jehovah] bless you and watch over you.
[Numbers] [6]:[25] May [Jehovah’s] face shine upon you, and may He have mercy on you.
[Numbers] [6]:[26] May [[Jehovah] always keep His eyes] on you and bring you peace.’

[Numbers] [8]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

[Numbers] [8]:[4] The Sacred Lamp’s base and stem were made of solid gold, as were its lilies. They were made following the pattern that [Jehovah] had shown to Moses.
[Numbers] [8]:[5] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [8]:[6] ‘Remove the Levites from among the children of IsraEl and purify them…
[Numbers] [8]:[7] And this is how you should perform their purification: ‘Have them rinse themselves in clean water and shave all the hair from their bodies, then have them wash their clothes… Make sure that they’re clean!
[Numbers] [8]:[8] ‘Then they must bring 2 yearling calves from the herd along with a food offering and some fine flour mixed with oil.
[Numbers] [8]:[9] And thereafter, assemble the entire gathering of the sons of IsraEl and bring the Levites up before them at the Tent of Proofs...
[Numbers] [8]:[10] Stand them there in front of [Jehovah], and have the sons of IsraEl lay their hands on the Levites.
[Numbers] [8]:[11] ‘Aaron must set the Levites aside as a gift to [Jehovah] from the children of IsraEl, and they must be made ready to perform [Jehovah’s] work.
[Numbers] [8]:[12] Then have the Levites lay their hands on the heads of the calves, and you should sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a whole-burnt offering to [Jehovah], to pay for their sins.
[Numbers] [8]:[13] ‘Thereafter, stand the Levites in front of [Jehovah] and in front of Aaron and his sons, and offer them to [Jehovah] as a gift…
[Numbers] [8]:[14] Separate the Levites from among the sons of IsraEl as Mine!
[Numbers] [8]:[15] ‘Then the Levites must go to the Tent where they are to work, and you must purify them and present them there before [Jehovah],
[Numbers] [8]:[16] for they’ll have been given to Me as a gift from the children of IsraEl.... I’ve taken them as Mine in place of all the firstborn sons of IsraEl that open a womb.
[Numbers] [8]:[17] ‘For, all the firstborn among the children of IsraEl (both the men and the animals) became Mine on the day that I struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt… Yes, that’s when I made them holy to Myself.
[Numbers] [8]:[18] ‘But now, I’m taking the Levites instead of the first-born of the children of IsraEl,
[Numbers] [8]:[19] and I’m presenting them as a gift to Aaron and his sons to serve the children of IsraEl at the Tent. There they must make the payments for the sins of the children of IsraEl, so none of the sons of IsraEl will have to approach the holy things.’
[Numbers] [8]:[20] Well, Moses, Aaron, and the entire gathering of the children of IsraEl did everything that the Lord had commanded Moses concerning the Levites.
[Numbers] [8]:[21] The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes... Then Aaron presented them as a gift before [Jehovah], and [he sacrificed] the payments for their sins in order to purify them.
[Numbers] [8]:[22] Thereafter, the Levites entered the Tent to serve before Aaron and his sons, just as the Lord had instructed Moses.
[Numbers] [8]:[23] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [8]:[24] ‘This is the rule for the Levites: ‘Those who are 25 years old and older must enter to serve at the Tent of Proofs.
[Numbers] [8]:[25] But when they reach 50 years old, they may no longer serve or work there.
[Numbers] [8]:[26] ‘They may supervise their brothers that serve at the Tent of Proofs, but they may not work there anymore. ‘Give the Levites these instructions.’
[Numbers] [9]:[1] It was in the 1st month of the 2nd year after they’d left the land of Egypt that the Lord spoke to Moses there in the SinAi Desert, and He said:
[Numbers] [9]:[2] ‘Tell the children of IsraEl to keep the Passover at the proper time.
[Numbers] [9]:[3] You must keep it and obey all the laws and instructions concerning it, starting on the evening of the 14th day of the 1st month.’
[Numbers] [9]:[4] So Moses ordered the children of IsraEl to sacrifice the Passover
[Numbers] [9]:[5] on the 14th day of the 1st month, there in the SinAi Desert. And the children of IsraEl did just as the Lord told Moses.
[Numbers] [9]:[6] However, there were some men who were unclean due to [touching] a dead body, and they were unable to keep the Passover on that day. So they went before Moses and Aaron
[Numbers] [9]:[7] and said: ‘We’re unclean, because we touched the dead body of a man... Will we not to be allowed to offer our gifts to [Jehovah] at this time along with the rest of the children of IsraEl?’
[Numbers] [9]:[8] Then Moses told them: ‘Stay here, and I’ll listen to whatever instructions [Jehovah] gives to me about this.’
[Numbers] [9]:[9] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [9]:[10] ‘Tell the sons of IsraEl that whenever a man among you or your descendants has become unclean because of touching a dead body, or is far away on a journey, he must still keep the Passover to [Jehovah]…
[Numbers] [9]:[11] But he must do it on the evening of the 14th day of the 2nd month. ‘[The Passover sacrifice] must be offered then and eaten with fermentation-free bread and bitter herbs.
[Numbers] [9]:[12] They must not leave any of it over until the next day, nor may they break any of its bones. They must offer the sacrifice just as they would on the Passover.
[Numbers] [9]:[13] ‘But if anyone is clean and isn’t away on a trip, he must be sure to [do this on] the Passover day! Any person who doesn’t offer the gift to [Jehovah] at the proper time is guilty and must be cut off from his people!
[Numbers] [9]:[14] ‘And if an alien should come into your land and wishes to observe the Passover to [Jehovah], he must do so according to the laws and instructions concerning the Passover. For there’s just one law, and it applies to both the natives and the aliens.’
[Numbers] [9]:[15] Well, from the time that the Tent was [first] assembled, a cloud covered the Tent of Proofs all day long, and what looked like fire covered the Tent from evening until morning.
[Numbers] [9]:[16] And that’s how it always was… A cloud cover by day and the appearance of fire by night.
[Numbers] [9]:[17] Also, whenever the cloud left the Tent, the children of IsraEl were to leave that place; and whenever the cloud just stayed there, the children of IsraEl were to remain encamped.
[Numbers] [9]:[18] So, the children of IsraEl camped by the commands of [Jehovah] and they moved by the commands of [Jehovah]… As long as the cloud covered the Tent, the children of IsraEl were to camp.
[Numbers] [9]:[19] And even if the cloud stayed over the Tent for a long time, the children of IsraEl were to follow God’s instructions and not move.
[Numbers] [9]:[20] For whenever the cloud covered the Tent for a number of days, they were to camp, following the words of [Jehovah], and they were to stay camped there by the commands of the Lord.
[Numbers] [9]:[21] But whenever the cloud moved up from over the Tent, they were to move, whether it was day or night...
[Numbers] [9]:[22] If the cloud covered the Tent for a full month, the children of IsraEl had to camp and were not to leave;
[Numbers] [9]:[23] for they were only to move by the commands of the Lord. And this is what they did. They followed the instructions and commands that the Lord gave them through Moses.
[Numbers] [10]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [10]:[2] ‘Make two silver trumpets for yourselves that are to be used to call assemblies and to move the camp. Make them of hammered [silver]. ‘
[Numbers] [10]:[3] There is to be one type of call to assemble the whole gathering at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs,
[Numbers] [10]:[4] and another type to assemble just the rulers and leaders there.
[Numbers] [10]:[5] ‘You must [also use them to] sound the alarms for the camp to move, starting with the one in the east...
[Numbers] [10]:[6] ‘Then when you sound a 2nd alarm, the camp to the south must move. ‘When you sound the 3rd alarm, the camp in the west must move. ‘When you sound the 4th alarm, the camp in the north must move. ‘And they must also sound alarms while they’re leaving.
[Numbers] [10]:[7] ‘Also, blow the horns to signal assemblies (but it shouldn’t be the same signal as the alarms).
[Numbers] [10]:[8] The Priests (the sons of Aaron) must blow these trumpets, and this is to be the rule for you through all your generations and throughout the ages.
[Numbers] [10]:[9] ‘And if you must go to war against your enemies who will oppose you in your land, you must also blow the trumpets as a reminder to [Jehovah]… So that He will save you from your enemies.
[Numbers] [10]:[10] ‘In addition, you must blow the trumpets on joyful days, such as your feasts, New-Moon festivals, and when you sacrifice your whole burnt offerings and peace offerings.
[Numbers] [10]:[11] ‘This must be done as a reminder to you before your God… ‘For I am [Jehovah] your God!’
[Numbers] [10]:[12] Well thereafter, the children of IsraEl packed their things in the SinAi Desert, for the cloud came to rest in the Pharan Desert.
[Numbers] [10]:[13] So, following the instructions of [Jehovah] through Moses, the first group started their march...
[Numbers] [10]:[14] The first to leave were the children of Judah with their army, headed by NaAsson, son of AmiNadab.
[Numbers] [10]:[15] They [were followed by] the sons of IshSachar under NathaniEl, son of Sogar.
[Numbers] [10]:[16] Then came the army of the Tribe of the sons of ZebuLon under EliAb, son of ChaElon.
[Numbers] [10]:[17] Thereafter, the Tent was taken down and the sons of GedSon started out, followed by the sons of MeraRi, who carried the Tent.
[Numbers] [10]:[18] Then came the camp of ReuBen and their army that was led by EliSur, son of SediUr.
[Numbers] [10]:[19] They were followed by the army of the Tribe of the sons of SymeOn under SalamiEl, son of SuriSadai.
[Numbers] [10]:[20] Next came the army of the children from the Tribe of Gad under EliShaph, son of RaguEl.
[Numbers] [10]:[21] Then the sons of CaAth came forward bearing the holy things, because the Tent was to be set up before they arrived.
[Numbers] [10]:[22] Next the camp of Ephraim set out with their army under EliSama, son of SemiUd.
[Numbers] [10]:[23] They were followed by the armies of the Tribe of the sons of ManasSeh under GamaliEl, son of PhadasShur.
[Numbers] [10]:[24] Then came the army of the Tribe of the children of BenJamin under AbiDan, son of GadeOni.
[Numbers] [10]:[25] Next in the order of the camp came the sons of Dan and their army under AchiEzer, son of AmiSadai.
[Numbers] [10]:[26] Then came the army of the Tribe of the sons of Asher under PhageEl, son of Echran.
[Numbers] [10]:[27] They were followed by the army of the Tribe of the sons of NaphTali under AchiRe, son of AiNan.
[Numbers] [10]:[28] These are the armies of the children of IsraEl, and it’s the way that they started their march.
[Numbers] [10]:[29] Then Moses said to Jobab (son of RaguEl the MidiAnite): ‘We’re traveling to the place about which [Jehovah] said: ‘I’m going to give this to you.’ ‘So come with us and we’ll treat you well, because [Jehovah] has promised good things for IsraEl.’
[Numbers] [10]:[30] But [Jobab] replied: ‘No, I won’t go. I’m going to return to my family and to my land.’
[Numbers] [10]:[31] However, [Moses insisted], saying: ‘Don’t leave us, for you’ve been with us all through the desert, and you should be considered an elder among us.
[Numbers] [10]:[32] If you go with us, when [Jehovah] does good things for us, we’ll do good things for you!’
[Numbers] [10]:[33] Then they left the Mountain of [Jehovah] and traveled for three days. And the Chest of [Jehovah’s] Sacred Agreement was carried ahead of them for all three days, as a comfort to them all.
[Numbers] [10]:[34] Also, the cloud hung over them during the day, starting from when they left the camp.
[Numbers] [10]:[35] And when the Chest was brought forward, Moses said: ‘Arise, O [Jehovah]! ‘Let Your enemies be scattered and may all that hate You flee in terror!’
[Numbers] [10]:[36] Then when they reached its resting place, he said: ‘Turn [Your face] again, O [Jehovah], to the thousands and tens of thousands in IsraEl!’
[Numbers] [11]:[1] Well after that, the people started murmuring sinful things against [Jehovah], and He heard them. This made Him very angry, and [Jehovah] sent a fire that started to burn among them, which consumed part of the camp!
[Numbers] [11]:[2] So the people called for Moses; and after he prayed to [Jehovah], the fire died out...
[Numbers] [11]:[3] And thereafter, they called that place ‘The Burning,’ because that was where a fire from [Jehovah] had burned among them.
[Numbers] [11]:[4] Then the [ethnics] that were mixed among them started [complaining]. They and some of the children of IsraEl sat down and started crying and saying: ‘Who is going to give us meat to eat?
[Numbers] [11]:[5] ‘We remember all the fish that we used to eat in Egypt, as well as the cucumbers, melons, leeks, garlic, and onions.
[Numbers] [11]:[6] But now our lives have become [empty], because all we can see is this manna!’
[Numbers] [11]:[7] Well, the manna looked like coriander seeds and it appeared [on the ground] like frost...
[Numbers] [11]:[8] The people would go out to collect it, and then they’d grind it in a mill or pound it in a mortar and bake it in a pan to make loaves from it. It tasted like sweet crackers that had been mixed with oil.
[Numbers] [11]:[9] And during the night, when the dew was settling on the camp, the manna would just come down upon it.
[Numbers] [11]:[10] Well, Moses heard them as they were sitting in front of their [tents] in family groups, crying! This made [Jehovah] very angry, and Moses also viewed these actions as evil.
[Numbers] [11]:[11] So Moses asked [Jehovah]: ‘Why have You done this to your servant, and why haven’t I found favor in Your eyes, so that You should lay the burden of these people upon me?
[Numbers] [11]:[12] Am I the one who carried and gave birth to all these people, so that You should tell me to take them into my arms like a nursing mother would take her new-born baby, then carry them into the land that You promised to give to their fathers?
[Numbers] [11]:[13] ‘Where can I find enough meat to feed all these people? For, here they’re crying before me and saying: ‘Give us meat to eat!’
[Numbers] [11]:[14] ‘I can’t carry all these people by myself… They’re just too heavy for me!
[Numbers] [11]:[15] If You’re going to do this to me and if I’ve found Your favor, just kill me so I don’t have to [endure] this pain!’
[Numbers] [11]:[16] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Gather 70 men from among the elders of IsraEl to Me… [Make sure that] they’re the elders and scribes among the people. Then bring them to the Tent of Proofs and have them stand there with you.
[Numbers] [11]:[17] For I’m going to come down and speak with you there... Then I’ll take [some] of [My] breath that’s on you and put it on them, so they’ll have to share the burden of the people with you, and you won’t have to handle it all by yourself.’
[Numbers] [11]:[18] ‘After that, go to the people and tell them this: ‘Now, purify yourselves, because tomorrow you’re going to eat meat! Yes, you who have bawled before [Jehovah] and asked: ‘Who will give us meat and the other things that [we used to enjoy back in Egypt]?’ ‘For [Jehovah] will provide meat, and then you’ll have to eat it!
[Numbers] [11]:[19] ‘You aren’t going to eat it for 1 day, or for 7, 10, or 20 days,
[Numbers] [11]:[20] you’re going to eat it for a full month… Until it comes out of your noses! You’re going to be sick of it, because you disobeyed [Jehovah] who is here among you! ‘You bawled before Him and asked: ‘Why did we ever leave Egypt?’
[Numbers] [11]:[21] Then Moses replied: ‘There are some 600,000 of just the soldiers among us, and are You telling me to give everyone enough meat to eat for a whole month?
[Numbers] [11]:[22] Must we slaughter all of our sheep and cattle to feed them all… And would even that be enough? Or must we catch all the fish in the sea for them, and would that be enough?’
[Numbers] [11]:[23] And the Lord said to Moses: ‘Isn’t the hand of [Jehovah] large enough? ‘By now you should know whether My words will come true!’
[Numbers] [11]:[24] So Moses went out and told the people what the Lord had said. Then he gathered 70 men from among the people’s elders and stood them around the Tent…
[Numbers] [11]:[25] And the Lord came down in a cloud to speak to [Moses]. Thereafter, He took some of the breath that was in Moses and put it into the 70 elders. And when [God’s] breath came to rest upon them, they all started prophesying… But then they stopped.
[Numbers] [11]:[26] However, two of the men were still back in the camp at the time; one was ElDad and the other was MoDad. They were part of the group that [Moses] had chosen, but they hadn’t made it to the Tent yet. Nevertheless, [God’s] breath came to rest upon them also, and they started prophesying there in the camp!
[Numbers] [11]:[27] So, a young man ran and told Moses… He said: ‘ElDad and MoDad are prophesying in the camp!’
[Numbers] [11]:[28] Well, JoShua (son of NaWeh) who was Moses’ assistant and chosen successor, said: ‘Lord Moses, ‘Make them stop!’
[Numbers] [11]:[29] But Moses replied: ‘Are you jealous for me? I wish that [Jehovah] would put His breath in all of His people and make them all Prophets!’
[Numbers] [11]:[30] And with that, Moses and the elders of IsraEl returned to the camp.
[Numbers] [11]:[31] Then [Jehovah] blew His breath, and [flocks of] quail were blown over the sea and into their camp… They covered the ground several feet deep for a day’s journey all around the camp.
[Numbers] [11]:[32] So the people went out all that day, all that night, and all the next day to gather quail... Even those who gathered the least gathered hundreds! Then, all around the camp, everyone [sat down to feast].
[Numbers] [11]:[33] Well, they were still picking the meat that was stuck between their teeth when [Jehovah] showed them how angry He was with them, for He then struck them with a great plague!
[Numbers] [11]:[34] And thereafter, that place was called The Graveyard of the Greedy, because it’s where they buried all the greedy people.
[Numbers] [11]:[35] Then the people moved away from the Graveyard of the Greedy [and went to] AsherOth, where they [set up camp].
[Numbers] [12]:[1] It was then that MiriAm and Aaron started condemning Moses because of the Ethiopian whom he’d taken as his woman.
[Numbers] [12]:[2] They asked: ‘Is Moses the only one to whom the Lord has spoken? Hasn’t He also spoken to us?’ And [Jehovah] heard them say this.
[Numbers] [12]:[3] Now, Moses was the humblest man on the earth;
[Numbers] [12]:[4] so the Lord immediately spoke to Moses, Aaron, and MiriAm, and said: ‘All three of you, come to the Tent of Proofs!’
[Numbers] [12]:[5] So, the three of them went to the Tent of Proofs, and the Lord descended in a column of clouds... He stood there at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs and called Aaron and MiriAm, and they stepped forward.
[Numbers] [12]:[6] Then He said to them: ‘Listen to Me. ‘If either of you are Prophets of [Jehovah], I’ll make things known to you in visions and speak to you as you sleep.
[Numbers] [12]:[7] ‘However, this isn’t the way [that I speak] to My servant Moses who has so faithfully [served] in My House...
[Numbers] [12]:[8] I’m not hidden to him, I appear and speak to him mouth to mouth… And he’s even seen the glory of [Jehovah]! ‘So, why aren’t you afraid to speak against My servant Moses?’
[Numbers] [12]:[9] Well, [Jehovah] was very angry with them. Then, as He left,
[Numbers] [12]:[10] the cloud disappeared from the Tent… And {Look!} MiriAm had a skin infection that was [as white] as snow! Well when Aaron saw that MiriAm had an infection,
[Numbers] [12]:[11] he said to Moses: ‘I beg you my lord; don’t hold this sin against us, because we did this in ignorance!
[Numbers] [12]:[12] Don’t allow her to be one of the [walking] dead like a miscarriage from her mother’s womb… And for half of her flesh to be eaten away.’
[Numbers] [12]:[13] So Moses called to [Jehovah] and said: ‘Oh God, I beg You; please heal her!’
[Numbers] [12]:[14] And the Lord replied to Moses: ‘If her father had just spit in her face, wouldn’t she have been shamed for 7 days? Therefore, she may not enter the camp for 7 days… Only then may she return.’
[Numbers] [12]:[15] So MiriAm was driven away from the camp for 7 days, and the people didn’t break camp until after MiriAm had been cleansed.
[Numbers] [12]:[16] Well after that, the people left AsherOth and camped in the Pharan Desert.
[Numbers] [13]:[1] There the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [13]:[2] ‘Send some men as spies into the land of the CanaAnites that I’ll be giving to the sons of IsraEl. Choose men who are leaders from each of the tribes and family lines.’
[Numbers] [13]:[3] So, following [Jehovah’s] instructions, Moses chose leaders from among the sons of IsraEl and sent them away from the Pharan Desert.
[Numbers] [13]:[4] From the Tribe of ReuBen [he sent] SamuEl, son of ZachUr.
[Numbers] [13]:[5] From the Tribe of SymeOn [he sent] Saphat, son of Suri.
[Numbers] [13]:[6] From the Tribe of Judah [he sent] Caleb, son of JePhonNe.
[Numbers] [13]:[7] From the Tribe of IshSachar [he sent] IlaAl, son of JoSeph.
[Numbers] [13]:[8] From the Tribe of Ephraim [he sent] Ause, son of NaWeh.
[Numbers] [13]:[9] From the Tribe of BenJamin [he sent] Phalti, son of Raphu.
[Numbers] [13]:[10] From the Tribe of ZebuLon [he sent] GadDiEl, son of Sudi.
[Numbers] [13]:[11] From the Tribe of JoSeph’s son ManasSeh [he sent] GadDi, son of Susi.
[Numbers] [13]:[12] From the Tribe of Dan [he sent] AmiEl, son of Gamali.
[Numbers] [13]:[13] From the Tribe of Asher [he sent] Sathur, son of MichaEl.
[Numbers] [13]:[14] From the Tribe of NaphTali [he sent] Nabi, son of Sabi.
[Numbers] [13]:[15] And from the Tribe of Gad [he sent] GaudiEl, son of MacKi.
[Numbers] [13]:[16] These are the men whom Moses sent as spies into the land. However, Moses started calling Ause (son of NaWeh), JoShua.
[Numbers] [13]:[17] As Moses sent them to spy in the land of CanaAn, he told them this: ‘Travel through this desert, then climb the mountain and
[Numbers] [13]:[18] peer into the land to see what it looks like. ‘Watch the people who live there to [determine] whether they’re strong or weak, many or few.
[Numbers] [13]:[19] Then, notice whether the land that they live on is good or bad, what cities are there, and whether or not they have walls.
[Numbers] [13]:[20] ‘Also, pay attention to the ground… See whether it’s rich or poor, and if there are any trees. Then venture in and take some of the fruitage of the land.’ Well, it was springtime, and the grapes were ready to be harvested,
[Numbers] [13]:[21] as they went and surveyed all the land from the Sin Desert to RhoOb (on the road to AiMath).
[Numbers] [13]:[22] They traveled through the desert and got as far as HebRon, where they found AchiMan, SesSi, and ThelAmi, the descendants of Enach (HebRon had been built 7 years before Tanis in Egypt).
[Numbers] [13]:[23] Well, when they got to the valley where the grapes were growing, after surveying it, they cut down a cluster of grapes and carried it on carrying poles. They also picked some pomegranates and figs.
[Numbers] [13]:[24] Then they called that place, The Valley of the Cluster, because of the cluster of [grapes] that the children of IsraEl had cut down there.
[Numbers] [13]:[25] Well after 40 days, they returned from their survey of the land
[Numbers] [13]:[26] and they went before Moses, Aaron, and the entire gathering of the children of IsraEl ([who were] in the desert at Pharan KaDesh at the time). Then they spoke to the whole gathering and showed them the fruit from the land,
[Numbers] [13]:[27] giving this report: ‘We went into the land where you sent us and found a land that is indeed flowing with milk and honey! Here’s some of the fruit from that place.
[Numbers] [13]:[28] ‘However, the nation that lives there is aggressive, and they have large, strong, walled cities. ‘We also saw the children of Enach there...
[Numbers] [13]:[29] The AmaLechites live in the land towards the south, while the Hittites, Evites, Jebusites, and Amorites live in the hill country, and the CanaAnites live between the Sea and the Jordan River.’
[Numbers] [13]:[30] Then Caleb stopped them from speaking before Moses, and said: ‘We must surely go there and inherit [that land], because we can conquer them!’
[Numbers] [13]:[31] But [the other] men disagreed and said: ‘We must not go there! ‘There’s no way we can beat nations like that, for they’re much stronger than we are!’
[Numbers] [13]:[32] Well, they really terrified the children of IsraEl when they said: ‘The land that we walked through and surveyed swallows up the people who live there... And all the people who we saw there were huge!
[Numbers] [13]:[33] ‘We saw giants who [were so large] that we looked like grasshoppers in comparison!’
[Numbers] [14]:[1] Well at that, the whole gathering started wailing and crying, and this went on throughout the night!
[Numbers] [14]:[2] Then all the children of IsraEl started grumbling against Moses and Aaron, for they came to them and said:
[Numbers] [14]:[3] ‘We would rather have died in the land of Egypt than in this desert! ‘Why is [Jehovah] bringing us to this land… Just to be killed in war and to have our women and children serve as their prey? ‘It would be better for us to return to Egypt!’
[Numbers] [14]:[4] Then they started saying to each other: ‘Let’s appoint [someone else] as our ruler who’ll take us back to Egypt!’
[Numbers] [14]:[5] So Moses and Aaron just fell to their faces before the entire gathering of the children of IsraEl...
[Numbers] [14]:[6] But then, JoShua (son of NaWeh) and Caleb (son of JePhonNe), who were among those who’d spied in the land, started ripping their clothes,
[Numbers] [14]:[7] and they said to the gathering of the children of IsraEl: ‘The land that we surveyed is really very good!
[Numbers] [14]:[8] ‘And if [Jehovah] has chosen us, won’t He take us into this land and give it to us… Into this land that flows with milk and honey?
[Numbers] [14]:[9] ‘Don’t leave [Jehovah], and don’t be afraid of the people in that land, because they’re just meat for us! ‘Since [Jehovah] is with us, their time has ended! So, don’t be afraid!’
[Numbers] [14]:[10] But at that, all the people started throwing rocks at them! [Then suddenly], the glory of [Jehovah] appeared in the cloud over the Tent of Proofs before all the children of IsraEl!
[Numbers] [14]:[11] And the Lord said to Moses: ‘How much longer will these people continue to anger Me, and how much longer will they refuse to believe Me after all the signs that I’ve sent to them?
[Numbers] [14]:[12] ‘So now, I’m going to strike them and kill them all! ‘Yes, I’ll destroy them and then I’ll make a great nation of you and of your father’s house… One that’ll be much greater than this!’
[Numbers] [14]:[13] However, Moses replied: ‘But then the Egyptians would hear about this! ‘Because You used Your power to bring these people out from among them,
[Numbers] [14]:[14] and the people who live in that land have heard that You’re our Lord, that You’re with these people, that You, O [Jehovah], have been seen face-to-face, that Your cloud rests upon them, and You lead them each day in a column of clouds and by a column of fire all night long…
[Numbers] [14]:[15] ‘If You destroy this whole nation, then all the nations that have heard of Your Name will say:
[Numbers] [14]:[16] ‘Because [Jehovah] couldn’t bring His people into the land that He swore to give them, He [killed] them all in the desert!’
[Numbers] [14]:[17] ‘So, O Lord, show Your power to them instead… And may this thing that You’ve said prove to be true:
[Numbers] [14]:[18] ‘[Jehovah] is patient, merciful, and true. He removes mistakes, errors, and sins... He will never acquit the guilty, but He will bring the sins of the fathers upon their children for three or four generations’.
[Numbers] [14]:[19] ‘Therefore, in Your great mercy, forgive these people for their sins and show them the same favor [that You’ve shown] them [since You led them out of] Egypt!’
[Numbers] [14]:[20] Then the Lord replied to Moses: ‘I’ll be [patient] with them as you’ve requested.
[Numbers] [14]:[21] ‘For, as I live and as My Name is living; the glory of [Jehovah] must fill the whole earth,
[Numbers] [14]:[22] since everyone has seen My glory through all the signs that I gave in Egypt and in the desert. ‘But, this is the 10th time that [IsraEl] has tested Me and refused to listen to My voice!
[Numbers] [14]:[23] ‘Therefore, they will not see the land that I promised to their fathers. Rather, I’ll give it to their children who are with Me here… Those who are inexperienced and don’t yet know good from bad. ‘I’m going to give the land to them… But, those who angered Me will never see it!
[Numbers] [14]:[24] My servant Caleb [will see it], because he had a different spirit and he followed Me... I’ll bring him into the land that he traveled through, and his offspring will inherit it.
[Numbers] [14]:[25] But until then, the AmaLechites and CanaAnites will [continue to] live in this valley. ‘So tomorrow [you must] turn around and return to the desert by way of the Red Sea!’
[Numbers] [14]:[26] And thereafter, the Lord spoke to both Moses and Aaron and said:
[Numbers] [14]:[27] ‘How much longer will this gathering remain wicked? ‘I’ve heard the grumbling against Me coming from the children of IsraEl as well as all their complaints about you.
[Numbers] [14]:[28] ‘So, tell them that [Jehovah] said this: ‘As I live; whatever I’ve heard you say is exactly what I’m going to do to you...
[Numbers] [14]:[29] ‘Your bodies will fall in this desert, and all those who were reviewed and counted from 20 years old and up – all that grumbled against Me –
[Numbers] [14]:[30] will never enter the land that I stretched out My hand to give to you, except for Caleb son of JePhonNe), and JoShua son of NaWeh.
[Numbers] [14]:[31] ‘Then I’ll bring your little ones (whom you’ve said would serve as prey) into the land, and they’ll inherit what you’ve rejected,
[Numbers] [14]:[32] while your bodies will fall in this desert!
[Numbers] [14]:[33] ‘So your sons must be fed in this desert for 40 years, and they must carry the weight of your infidelity, as your bodies rot in the desert.
[Numbers] [14]:[34] For each day that was spent spying in that land – 40 days – you must bear your sins a day for a year – for 40 years – and you’ll get to know My rage.
[Numbers] [14]:[35] ‘Now, I, [Jehovah] have spoken, and that’s what I’ll do to this evil gathering that has raised itself against Me… You will be totally destroyed and die here in this desert!’
[Numbers] [14]:[36] Then, all the men whom Moses sent to spy in the land and who then returned and grumbled before the group and said evil things about the land
[Numbers] [14]:[37] were struck with a plague from [Jehovah] and they all died.
[Numbers] [14]:[38] So, among the men who served as spies in the land, only JoShua (son of NaWeh) and Caleb (son of JePhonNe) survived!
[Numbers] [14]:[39] Well after that, Moses explained all these things to the children of IsraEl, and the people became very depressed.
[Numbers] [14]:[40] Then early the next morning, [the people] climbed to the top of a hill and said: '{Look!} We have sinned! ‘So, those of us who are left must travel to the place where [Jehovah] told us to go!’
[Numbers] [14]:[41] But Moses asked them: ‘Why didn’t you just obey the words of [Jehovah] and prosper?
[Numbers] [14]:[42] ‘However, now you can’t [enter the land], because [Jehovah] isn’t with you, and you’ll [be cut down] before your enemies!
[Numbers] [14]:[43] The AmaLechites and the CanaAnites that are standing there before you will cut you down with their swords, because you disobeyed [Jehovah] and turned aside. ‘So, the Lord won’t be there among you!’
[Numbers] [14]:[44] Well, they went up to the top of the mountain and tried to force their way [into the land] anyhow… But the Chest of [Jehovah’s] Sacred Agreement and Moses never left the camp.
[Numbers] [14]:[45] As a result, the AmaLechites and the CanaAnites who lived on the mountain attacked them, drove them away, and destroyed them all the way to [Mount] Herman; and they [had to] run back to their camp.
[Numbers] [15]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [15]:[2] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘When you enter the land that I’ll give to you (this place where you’ll live);
[Numbers] [15]:[3] whenever you offer whole burnt offerings to [Jehovah], or offerings to fulfill a vow, or free-will offerings, or feast sacrifices from the herd or flock as a sweet odor to [Jehovah]…
[Numbers] [15]:[4] ‘The person who offers the gift must also bring a food offering of a quart of flour mixed with oil,
[Numbers] [15]:[5] and a quart [of wine] as a drink offering with each lamb that you sacrifice as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [15]:[6] ‘And when you offer a ram as a whole-burnt offering or sacrifice, you must also prepare a food offering of 2 quarts (1.9l) of fine flour mixed with oil,
[Numbers] [15]:[7] and 2 quarts (1.9l) of wine as a drink offering, as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [15]:[8] ‘And if you offer a sacrifice from the herd as a whole-burnt offering, or a sacrifice to fulfill a vow or as a peace offering to [Jehovah]...
[Numbers] [15]:[9] Along with the calf, you must add a food offering of 3 quarts (2.8l) of fine flour mixed with oil,
[Numbers] [15]:[10] and provide 3 quarts (2.8l) of wine as a drink offering, as a sweet odor to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [15]:[11] ‘You must do this for each calf, ram, lamb, sheep, or kid goat that you offer.
[Numbers] [15]:[12] ‘You must do the same thing for each one, no matter how many you may offer.
[Numbers] [15]:[13] ‘All the natives in the country must do this whenever they offer sacrifices as a sweet odor to [Jehovah]…
[Numbers] [15]:[14] Whether the person is an alien in your land or someone who was born among you, they must offer [the same] sacrifices as a sweet odor to [Jehovah]. ‘Yes, everyone among the gathering must offer sacrifices to [Jehovah]!
[Numbers] [15]:[15] There must be just one law for you and for the aliens who live among you... It’s a law throughout the ages and throughout your generations, that the aliens must act as you do before [Jehovah]!
[Numbers] [15]:[16] Both you and the aliens who live among you must follow the same laws and regulations!’
[Numbers] [15]:[17] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [15]:[18] ‘Speak to the sons of IsraEl and tell them this: ‘When you enter the land where I’m taking you

[Numbers] [15]:[20] You must set aside and offer your bread as a wave offering in the same way that you offer grain
[Numbers] [15]:[21] as the first fruitage of your dough… And you must give it to [Jehovah] as a wave offering throughout your generations.
[Numbers] [15]:[22] ‘Now, if you fail to follow all these commandments that [Jehovah] has been giving to Moses,
[Numbers] [15]:[23] and which Moses has been telling you about since the day that [Jehovah] selected you (and on throughout your generations),
[Numbers] [15]:[24] and if you commit an error or mistake without the knowledge of the gathering... The whole gathering must offer a perfect calf from the herd as a whole-burnt offering and as a sweet odor to [Jehovah], along with food and drink offerings (according to the rules), and one kid goat as a sin offering.
[Numbers] [15]:[25] ‘Then the Priest must make payment for the sins of the entire gathering of the children of IsraEl, and they’ll be forgiven, because it was a mistake… And because they brought their gift as a burnt-offering to [Jehovah] for their error and involuntary sin. [v26’]If it’s a mistake, everyone must be forgiven, whether they’re from the children of IsraEl or from the aliens who are living among you.
[Numbers] [15]:[27] ‘So, whenever a person sins by mistake, he must bring a yearling nanny goat as a sin offering.
[Numbers] [15]:[28] Then the Priest must [sacrifice it] to pay for the sin that was committed in error.
[Numbers] [15]:[29] ‘This same law applies to the natives of the children of IsraEl and to the aliens who are living among them… To anyone who unwittingly commits an error.
[Numbers] [15]:[30] ‘And whenever any person – a native or an alien – does anything so presumptuous as to anger God, he must be cut off from among his people!
[Numbers] [15]:[31] For when he disregards the Word of [Jehovah] and breaks His Laws, that person must be found guilty of sin and destroyed.’
[Numbers] [15]:[32] Well, it was while the children of IsraEl were still in the desert that they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath.
[Numbers] [15]:[33] And those who found him doing this brought him before Moses, Aaron, and the entire gathering of the children of IsraEl...
[Numbers] [15]:[34] Then he was placed in custody, because they didn’t know what to do with him.
[Numbers] [15]:[35] But thereafter, the Lord spoke to Moses and said: ‘The man must absolutely be put to death by the entire gathering… Stone him with rocks!’
[Numbers] [15]:[36] So the entire gathering dragged him outside of the camp and stoned him with rocks, just as [Jehovah] had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [15]:[37] Thereafter, the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

[Numbers] [15]:[39] ‘Then, whenever they look at these fringes, they must think of all the Commandments of [Jehovah] and remember to obey them, instead of turning back and following the immoral things of their imaginations.
[Numbers] [15]:[40] ‘They must remember to obey all My Commandments, and to be holy before Me...
[Numbers] [15]:[41] For I am [Jehovah], the God who brought them out of the land of Egypt to be their God... ‘I am [Jehovah], your God!’

[Numbers] [16]:[3] They went up to Moses and Aaron and said: ‘That’s enough of you! ‘Since the whole gathering of IsraEl is holy, and [Jehovah] is among them, why have you elevated yourselves over the gathering of [Jehovah]?’
[Numbers] [16]:[4] Well when Moses heard this, he fell to his face.
[Numbers] [16]:[5] Then he spoke to KorAh and his group and said: ‘God has visited us, and He knows who are His, who are holy, who are set aside to Him, whom He’s chosen, and whom He’s purchased for Himself.
[Numbers] [16]:[6] So, we’ll allow [Jehovah] to choose [the ones whom He finds] to be holy. ‘KorAh and his entire group should take their incense holders

[Numbers] [16]:[8] Then Moses [turned and] addressed KorAh, saying: ‘Listen to me, you son of Levi.
[Numbers] [16]:[9] ‘Is it so unimportant to you that the God of IsraEl has separated you from the rest of the gathering of IsraEl, and brought you close to Him to serve His people at His Tent,

[Numbers] [16]:[11] ‘[Understand that] you and your group have now gathered in opposition to God! ‘For, who is Aaron that you should be complaining against him?’
[Numbers] [16]:[12] Then later, Moses sent for Dathan and AbiRam (the sons of EliAb), and they told him that they wouldn’t be coming.

[Numbers] [16]:[24] ‘Then, tell the gathering that they must move away from KorAh and his group!’

[Numbers] [16]:[34] Well at that, all the IsraElites that were standing nearby fled from the noise, shouting: ‘[Run], so the earth doesn’t swallow us too!’

[Numbers] [16]:[38] [and they must now serve as a sign against] those sinners and against their lives. ‘Beat [the metal] into plates to cover the Altar; for, since these [censors] were brought before [Jehovah] as holy, they must be used as a sign to the children of IsraEl!’
[Numbers] [16]:[39] So, EliEzer (son of Aaron, the Priest) took the bronze incense holders that the men who were burned carried, and he had them shaped into a covering for the Altar,
[Numbers] [16]:[40] as a reminder to the children of IsraEl that no one other than the offspring of Aaron might approach to offer the incense before [Jehovah], and so that what happened to KorAh and those who conspired with him wouldn’t happen to them. [He did just] as [Jehovah] told him through Moses.
[Numbers] [16]:[41] But the next day, the people again started grumbling against Moses and Aaron, and they shouted: ‘You’ve killed the people of [Jehovah]!’
[Numbers] [16]:[42] So, a mob gathered against Moses and Aaron, and they foolishly ran into the Tent of Proofs – and at that, the cloud immediately covered it and the glory of [Jehovah] appeared!
[Numbers] [16]:[43] Then Moses and Aaron entered through the front of the Tent of Proofs,

Then, quickly carry it into the camp to atone for [the people’s] sins... For, [Jehovah’s] rage has come upon us and He’s already started destroying them!’
[Numbers] [16]:[47] So Aaron took it (just as Moses had told him) and he ran around throughout the whole gathering, since a plague had already started among them! And he used the incense to atone for the sins of the people.

This is to be a rule throughout the ages. It’s a Sacred Agreement of Salt throughout the ages between Me and you, and with your offspring that descends from you.’
