[Numbers] [18]:[32] ‘They won’t sin by doing this, as long as they [set aside] a portion of the first-fruitage [for Aaron], and as long as they don’t dirty the holy things of the children of IsraEl... ‘Otherwise, they must be put to death.’
[Numbers] [19]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said:
[Numbers] [19]:[2] ‘This is a commandment of the Law that [Jehovah] has given to you: ‘Speak to the sons of IsraEl and tell them to bring you a red heifer that has no blemishes or defects and which has never worn a yoke,
[Numbers] [19]:[3] then give her to EliEzer the Priest. ‘He must thereafter have them take it to a clean place outside of the camp and slaughter it there before him.
[Numbers] [19]:[4] Then EliEzer must take some of its blood and sprinkle it in front of the Tent of Proofs 7 times,
[Numbers] [19]:[5] and they must burn it to ashes before him, making sure that its skin, flesh, blood, and dung are totally consumed.
[Numbers] [19]:[6] ‘Afterward, the Priest must take some cedar wood, some hyssop, and some scarlet-colored wool, and throw it into the [fire] that’s burning the heifer.
[Numbers] [19]:[7] ‘Then the Priest must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and go into the camp. However, he must remain unclean until that evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[8] Also, the person who burns [the heifer] must wash his clothes, take a bath, and be unclean until that evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[9] ‘Then a clean man must gather up the heifer’s ashes and lay them aside in a clean place outside of the camp for the gathering of the children of IsraEl, so as to make a water to sprinkle for purification...
[Numbers] [19]:[10] And this man who gathers up the heifer’s ashes must wash his clothes and be unclean until the evening. ‘This is a law for the children of IsraEl and for the aliens that join with them throughout the ages:
[Numbers] [19]:[11] ‘Whoever touches a human corpse must be unclean for 7 days.
[Numbers] [19]:[12] ‘He must then be purified both on the 3rd day and on the 7th day, and he will be clean. But if he isn’t purified on the 3rd and 7th days, he won’t be clean.
[Numbers] [19]:[13] For, anyone who touches the carcass of a man who has died, and doesn’t get purified, will defile the Tent of [Jehovah]. ‘So, that person must be cut off from IsraEl… If the cleansing water isn’t sprinkled on him, he will be unclean and will remain unclean!
[Numbers] [19]:[14] ‘This is also the law: ‘Whenever a man dies inside a house, anyone who enters that house and everything in that house must be unclean for 7 days.
[Numbers] [19]:[15] All jars that are open and don’t have lids that are tightly sealed, must be unclean.
[Numbers] [19]:[16] ‘Also, anyone who touches a man who was murdered, or a cadaver, or a human bone, or even a tomb, must be unclean for 7 days.
[Numbers] [19]:[17] ‘Then they must take the burnt ashes of purification and pour them into a jar with running water to make the [water of] purification.
[Numbers] [19]:[18] Thereafter, a clean man must take some hyssop and dip it into the water, and sprinkle the house, the furniture, and all the people who are there that may have touched the human bone, or the murdered man, or the cadaver, or the tomb.
[Numbers] [19]:[19] ‘The clean man must sprinkle it upon the unclean people on the 3rd and 7th days. Then on the 7th day, he must purify himself, wash his clothes, take a bath, and be unclean until the evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[20] ‘Any man who has become unclean and chooses not to purify himself must be cut off from among the gathering, because he’s dirtied the holy things of [Jehovah]… If the cleansing water hasn’t been sprinkled on him, he will remain unclean.
[Numbers] [19]:[21] ‘And it’s the law throughout the ages that whoever sprinkles the water of purification must wash his clothes, and whoever even touches the water must be unclean until evening.
[Numbers] [19]:[22] Also, everything that an unclean man touches must be unclean, and anyone who touches [that thing] must be unclean until the evening.’
[Numbers] [20]:[1] It was during the 1st month that the people (the whole gathering of the children of IsraEl) traveled to the Sin Desert and stayed in KaDesh; and it was there that MiriAm died and was buried.
[Numbers] [20]:[2] Well, there was no water in that place, so all the people came to Moses and Aaron
[Numbers] [20]:[3] and they started shouting at Moses, saying: ‘We would rather have died when our brothers were destroyed before [Jehovah]!
[Numbers] [20]:[4] ‘Why have you brought the gathering of [Jehovah] into this desert… To kill us along with our cattle?
[Numbers] [20]:[5] ‘Just what kind of a place is this?! You brought us out of Egypt and took us into this evil place where we can’t plant grain, or figs, or vines, or pomegranates… And there’s no water for us to drink here!’
[Numbers] [20]:[6] Then Moses and Aaron went to the entrance of the Tent of Proofs and stood before the people, and [they both] fell to their faces. Thereafter, the glory of [Jehovah] appeared to them,
[Numbers] [20]:[7] and [God] spoke to Moses, saying:
[Numbers] [20]:[8] ‘Call an assembly. ‘Then take your walking stick, and you and your brother Aaron must call out to the rock that stands before them, and it’ll give you its water! You must bring the water out of the rock for them and give it to the gathering and to their cattle to drink.’
[Numbers] [20]:[9] So Moses took his walking stick that was there before [Jehovah], just as the Lord had commanded him...
[Numbers] [20]:[10] Then Moses and Aaron assembled the whole gathering in front of the rock, and he said to them: ‘Listen to me, you rebels! ‘Must we bring water for you out of this rock?’
[Numbers] [20]:[11] And at that, Moses raised his hand and hit the rock twice with his rod, and water came gushing out of it for the gathering and their cattle to drink!
[Numbers] [20]:[12] But after that, the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said: ‘Because you didn’t put enough trust in Me to mention Me before the children of IsraEl, you won’t be allowed to lead this gathering into the land that I’ve given to them!
[Numbers] [20]:[13] ‘This is [to be called] The Water of Rebellion, because this is where the children of IsraEl spoke rebelliously before [Jehovah], as I remained holy among them.’
[Numbers] [20]:[14] Then Moses sent messengers from KaDesh to the king of Edom to tell him: ‘This is what your brother IsraEl is saying: ‘You know of all the hard times we’ve seen,
[Numbers] [20]:[15] of how our fathers went down to Egypt and of the many [years] that we spent there, and of how the Egyptians oppressed us and our fathers...
[Numbers] [20]:[16] But when we called out to [Jehovah], He heard our voices and sent His messenger who brought us out of Egypt! ‘Well, now we’re in the city of KaDesh at the edge of your land,
[Numbers] [20]:[17] and we wish to pass through it! ‘We won’t walk through your fields or through your vineyards, nor will we drink water from your cisterns... We’ll just travel along the King’s Highway (Via Nova Traiana), and we won’t turn to the right or left until we’ve passed your borders.’
[Numbers] [20]:[18] But the Edomites replied: ‘You may not pass through [our land]! ‘And if you try to do so, we’ll go to war against you!’
[Numbers] [20]:[19] So the children of IsraEl said: ‘Then we’ll go around the mountain... And if we and our cattle drink any of your water, we’ll pay you for it. ‘It shouldn’t bother you if we travel around the mountain.’
[Numbers] [20]:[20] But [the Edomites] replied: ‘You may not pass through [our land]!’ Well thereafter, the Edomites came out to meet them with a huge, well-prepared army,
[Numbers] [20]:[21] and they refused to allow IsraEl to cross their borders. So IsraEl turned and went another way…
[Numbers] [20]:[22] The whole gathering left KaDesh and traveled on to Mount Hor.
[Numbers] [20]:[23] It was while they were at Mount Hor (on the border of the land of Edom) that the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, and said:
[Numbers] [20]:[24] ‘Aaron is now going to be laid [to rest] with his people… ‘And you may not enter the land that I’ve given to the children of IsraEl, because you angered Me at The Water of Rebellion!
[Numbers] [20]:[25] ‘So, take Aaron and his son EliEzer up Mount Hor before the whole gathering,
[Numbers] [20]:[26] then remove Aaron’s [official] garments and put them on EliEzer. And thereafter, Aaron will die and be added to [his people].’
[Numbers] [20]:[27] So Moses did just as [Jehovah] had commanded him. He took them up Mont Hor before the whole gathering,
[Numbers] [20]:[28] then he removed Aaron’s clothes and put them on his son EliEzer… And Aaron died on top of the mountain. Well, when Moses and EliEzer walked down the mountain,
[Numbers] [20]:[29] the gathering realized that Aaron had died. Then the whole house of IsraEl wept for Aaron for 30 days.
[Numbers] [21]:[1] After that, the CanaAnite king of Arad (who lived near the desert) heard that IsraEl had traveled through Atharin, so he went to war against IsraEl and carried some of [their people] off as captives.
[Numbers] [21]:[2] So, IsraEl swore a vow to [Jehovah], saying: ‘If You’ll hand them over to us, we’ll dedicate them and their cities to You.’
[Numbers] [21]:[3] Well, [Jehovah] heard what [the people of] IsraEl said and He gave the CanaAnites into their hands. They [destroyed] them and their cities, and they started calling that place the Cursed!
[Numbers] [21]:[4] Thereafter, they left Mount Hor and traveled towards the Red Sea, circling the land of Edom. But somewhere along the way, the people lost their courage
[Numbers] [21]:[5] and started speaking against God and Moses, saying: ‘Why have you brought us out of Egypt just to kill us here in the desert? ‘[We have] no bread or water, and we’ve come to hate the worthless bread!’
[Numbers] [21]:[6] So, [Jehovah] sent poisonous snakes among them that bit [many] people, and quite a few of the children of IsraEl died.
[Numbers] [21]:[7] As a result, the people went to Moses and said: ‘We have sinned, for we’ve spoken against [Jehovah] and against you! ‘Please pray to [Jehovah] and [ask] Him to take these snakes away from us!’
[Numbers] [21]:[8] Well, Moses prayed to [Jehovah] for the people, and the Lord told Moses: ‘Make [the sign of] a snake and [post it high]. ‘Then, whenever someone is bitten by a snake, they can look at [this sign] and they’ll live.’
[Numbers] [21]:[9] So Moses made a brass snake and raised it as a sign; and whenever a snake bit a person, he [or she] could look at the bronze snake and survive.
[Numbers] [21]:[10] Thereafter, children of IsraEl left that place and started camping in ObOth.
[Numbers] [21]:[11] And from ObOth, they moved to AchalGai, which is on the eastern edge of the desert across from MoAb.
[Numbers] [21]:[12] From there they traveled on and camped in the Zared Valley.
[Numbers] [21]:[13] Then they left [Zared] and camped on the other side of the Arnon, in the desert that runs along the border of the Amorites. The Arnon is the border between the MoAbites and the Amorites,
[Numbers] [21]:[14] for this is what was written about ZoOb in the book of the Wars of [Jehovah]: ‘The dry river beds of Arnon were set on fire,
[Numbers] [21]:[15] and MoAb’s [Capital] Er [was built] along the river beds at their border.’
[Numbers] [21]:[16] It was there that they found a well, and [Jehovah] said: ‘I have given this well to Moses; so, gather the people and I’ll give them water to drink.’
[Numbers] [21]:[17] Then IsraEl started singing this song at the well:
[Numbers] [21]:[18] ‘It was there that their leaders dug it; The kings of their nation and kingdom. They, in their kingship, sank it in rock; This well of ManthaNain.
[Numbers] [21]:[19] ‘From ManthaNain to NaAliEl, And from NaAliEl to BamOth, Then, on from BamOth to Janen; And from the plains of MoAb, And the quarry that faces the desert.’
[Numbers] [21]:[20] Well after that, Moses sent ambassadors to SeOn (the king of the Amorites) with words of peace. They [said to him]:
[Numbers] [21]:[21] ‘We [wish to] pass through your land. ‘We’ll just travel along the road… We won’t step into your fields or vineyards,
[Numbers] [21]:[22] and we won’t drink any water from your wells. ‘We’ll just travel along the King’s Highway until we pass through your borders.’
[Numbers] [21]:[23] But SeOn wouldn’t allow IsraEl to cross his borders. Rather, he gathered all his people and set up battle lines against IsraEl from the desert [all the way] to JasSa!
[Numbers] [21]:[24] However, IsraEl beat them and slaughtered [many of their people with] swords. So thereafter, they owned all the land from the Arnon to the JaBoc as far as the children of AmMon (for, JaZer borders the [land of] the children of AmMon).
[Numbers] [21]:[25] IsraEl also captured all of the Amorite cities in the [district of] Hesh-EbonEh, and they started living in them!
[Numbers] [21]:[26] Hesh-EbonEh had been the city of SeOn the king of the Amorites, and he had previously fought against the king of MoAb and captured all the land from AroEr to the Arnon.
[Numbers] [21]:[27] That’s why there was a saying among those who speak of such dark things: ‘Come to Hesh-EbonEh, in order to build, And prepare the city for SeOn.
[Numbers] [21]:[28] ‘Then a fire came out of Hesh-EbonEh… Flames from the City of SeOn. And there they burned and consumed To the banks of the Arnon in MoAb.
[Numbers] [21]:[29] ‘So, woe to you, O MoAb; For you’ve lost, O you people of CheMosh. Your sons that survived have now all been sold, And your daughters are the captives of SeOn, Who is the Amorite king.
[Numbers] [21]:[30] ‘From Hesh-EbonEh to DaEbon All your offspring is now gone, And their women light the fires that are burning in MoAb.’
[Numbers] [21]:[31] It was while IsraEl was living in the cities of the Amorites
[Numbers] [21]:[32] that Moses sent spies to JaZer. Then he captured it and its [surrounding] villages, and he drove out the Amorites that lived there!
[Numbers] [21]:[33] And after their return, they [marched] up the road that leads to BaShan. And BaShan’s king Og sent his army from EdraIn to meet them.
[Numbers] [21]:[34] Then the Lord told Moses: ‘Don’t be afraid of him; for I’m putting him, his people, and his land into your hands! ‘Now, do to him like you did to SeOn the king of the Amorites, who lived in Hesh-EbonEh.’
[Numbers] [21]:[35] So they attacked and destroyed [Og], his sons, and all his people – there were no survivors, and [IsraEl] inherited their land.
[Numbers] [22]:[1] Thereafter, the children of IsraEl left that place and camped on the west side of MoAb, by the Jordan River near JeriCho.
[Numbers] [22]:[2] And when Balak (son of SepPhor) saw what the IsraElites had done to the Amorites,
[Numbers] [22]:[3] [he] and the people of MoAb became very concerned and upset, because there were so many IsraElites!
[Numbers] [22]:[4] Then the MoAbites said to the elders of MidiAn: ‘This gathering is going lick up everything around us like a calf swallows down grass in a field!’ Well, Balak (son of SepPhor) was the king of MoAb at the time.
[Numbers] [22]:[5] And he sent ambassadors to call BalaAm son of BeOr, who was at Phathura (which is beside a river in the land of his people). [And he told them] to say: ‘Look! These people who have come from Egypt are covering the entire land… And now they’re camping close to me!
[Numbers] [22]:[6] ‘So, come and curse them for me, because they’re stronger than we are. Then we’ll be able to attack them and drive them out of the land! Because, I know that whomever you bless will be blest, and whomever you curse will be cursed.’
[Numbers] [22]:[7] So the elders of MoAb and MidiAn went out carrying their charms in their hands, and they went to see BalaAm. Then they told him everything that Balak had said,
[Numbers] [22]:[8] and he replied to them: ‘Spend the night here, and I’ll tell you whatever the Lord says to me.’ So the leaders of MoAb spent the night there with BalaAm.
[Numbers] [22]:[9] And [during the night], God came to BalaAm and asked him: ‘Who are these men who are with you?’

[Numbers] [22]:[12] But God told BalaAm: ‘You must not go with them, nor should you curse these people; for they are blest.’
[Numbers] [22]:[13] So when BalaAm got up the next morning, he told Balak’s [ambassadors]: ‘Hurry and return to your lord, because God won’t allow me to go with you.’
[Numbers] [22]:[14] As a result, the MoAbites got up and returned to Balak and told him that BalaAm had refused to come with them.
[Numbers] [22]:[15] So Balak then sent some [of his] rulers that were even more respected than the first ones.

[Numbers] [22]:[18] However, BalaAm answered Balak’s leaders in these words: ‘If Balak were to give me his whole house filled with silver and gold, I wouldn’t be able to violate the words of the God [Jehovah] and do anything good or bad, for I know [that this is wrong].

[Numbers] [22]:[20] Then God came to BalaAm during the night and said to him: ‘When these men who came to call you [awaken], get up and go with them... But just do the things that I tell you to do!’
[Numbers] [22]:[21] Well when BalaAm arose the next morning, he saddled his burro and went with the leaders of MoAb.
[Numbers] [22]:[22] But then God became very angry and sent His messenger to stop him. So, while he was riding along on his burro (accompanied by two of his servants),
[Numbers] [22]:[23] when the burro saw the messenger of God standing in her way with a sword in his hand, she turned aside and ran into a field! Well, BalaAm started hitting the [animal] with a stick to make her [behave].
[Numbers] [22]:[24] Then [later on,] [Jehovah’s] messenger went and stood in the Avenue of Vines, which had walls on both sides...
[Numbers] [22]:[25] And when the burro saw God’s messenger, she pushed up against the wall, squeezing BalaAm’s foot, and he started beating her again.
[Numbers] [22]:[26] And after that, [Jehovah’s] messenger went ahead and stood in a narrow place where it was impossible to turn to either the right or to the left.
[Numbers] [22]:[27] And when the burro saw the messenger of God, she just sat down under BalaAm. Well, BalaAm was furious! And he again started beating the burro with his stick.
[Numbers] [22]:[28] But God opened the burro’s mouth, and she asked BalaAm: ‘Just what have I done to you that you’ve started beating me a third time?’
[Numbers] [22]:[29] And BalaAm told the burro: ‘You’re making a fool of me, so if I had a sword in my hand I’d kill you!’
[Numbers] [22]:[30] Then the burro said to BalaAm: ‘I’m the burro that you’ve ridden since you were young, and have I ever disobeyed you?’ And [BalaAm] replied: ‘No.’
[Numbers] [22]:[31] Then God opened BalaAm’s eyes so he could see the messenger of [Jehovah] standing in the way with his sword in his hand! So he fell down and bowed with his face to the ground.
[Numbers] [22]:[32] And God’s messenger asked him: ‘Why did you beat your burro this third time? ‘Look; I came and stood in front of you three times, because the way that you’re heading is wrong! ‘And when this burro saw me, she turned away from me all three times.
[Numbers] [22]:[33] For if she hadn’t turned away, I would have killed you and left her alive!’
[Numbers] [22]:[34] Then BalaAm said to [Jehovah’s] messenger: ‘I have sinned! I didn’t realize that it was you standing in our way! ‘So, if it’s displeasing to you for me to go on, I’ll turn back.’
[Numbers] [22]:[35] But [Jehovah’s] messenger told BalaAm: ‘Go on with these men. ‘However, make sure that whatever I say to you is what you’ll tell them!’ So, BalaAm traveled on with Balak’s governors.

[Numbers] [24]:[4] Who hears the prophecies of the [great] Mighty One… Whose eyes opened and saw a vision of God… While he slept, his eyes opened wide.

[Numbers] [24]:[8] For, out of Egypt, God brought him. ‘The glory of the rhinoceros is his, And he’ll consume the nations that hate him… Yes, he will drink all their marrow, And shoot those who hate him with arrows. 9 ‘He’ll lie down and rest like a lion, And as a young lion, who’ll wake him? [Numbers] [25]:[1] Well, it was while IsraEl was camped at SatTin that [many of] the people made themselves dirty by engaging in immoral sex with the daughters of MoAb.

[Numbers] [25]:[3] So IsraEl had become totally devoted to BeEl Phegor, which made [Jehovah] very angry with them.
[Numbers] [25]:[4] And as a result, the Lord told Moses: ‘Take all their leaders, then lay them out in the sunlight before [Jehovah] to make examples of them, and this will turn His anger away from IsraEl!’
[Numbers] [25]:[5] Then Moses told the tribes of IsraEl: ‘You must each kill any of your friends who have devoted themselves to BeEl Phegor.’
[Numbers] [25]:[6] And just then, an IsraElite man came and led his brothers over to [have sex with] a MidiAnite woman… Doing this right in front of Moses and the whole gathering of the children of IsraEl that had been weeping at the entrance to the Tent of Proofs!
[Numbers] [25]:[7] And when PhineAs (son of EliEzer and grandson of Aaron the Priest) saw this, he stood up in the midst of the gathering, took a spear in his hand,
[Numbers] [25]:[8] and he followed the IsraElite man right into his bedroom... There he ran the spear through the IsraElite man and through the woman’s womb! Well at that, the plague [that had come] on the children of IsraEl stopped.
[Numbers] [25]:[9] But by then, 24,000 people had died.
[Numbers] [25]:[10] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [25]:[11] ‘PhineAs (son of EliEzer and grandson of Aaron the Priest) has brought an end to My rage against the children of IsraEl. ‘And although I had become very zealous, I didn’t consume them all in My zeal.
[Numbers] [25]:[12] So, tell him that I’ll now make a sacred agreement of peace
[Numbers] [25]:[13] with him and with the offspring that descends from him. ‘They will be Priests throughout the ages because of his zeal for his God, and because he paid for the sins of the children of IsraEl.’
[Numbers] [25]:[14] Now, the name of the IsraElite man who was killed with the MidiAnite woman was ZamBri. He was SalMon’s son, and a leader of one of the lines of the Tribe of SymeOn.
[Numbers] [25]:[15] The name of the MidiAnite woman who was killed was ChasBi. She was the daughter of Sur, who was a leader of the nation of OmMoth and a chief among the people of MidiAn.
[Numbers] [25]:[16] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said: ‘Tell the children of IsraEl
[Numbers] [25]:[17] that the MidiAnites are to be considered their enemies! So from now on, they must be treated as a plague and destroyed!
[Numbers] [25]:[18] ‘For the treachery that they used to trap you (as in the case of PhoGor and ChasBi, who was a daughter of a leader of MidiAn and who was killed on the day of the plague) has proven that they’re truly your enemies!’
[Numbers] [26]:[1] Well, after the plague had ended, the Lord spoke to Moses and EliEzer (the Priest) and said:

[Numbers] [30]:[1] So Moses spoke to the children of IsraEl and told them everything that [Jehovah] had commanded.
[Numbers] [30]:[2] Then Moses spoke to the heads of the tribes of the children of IsraEl and said: ‘This is what [Jehovah] has commanded:
[Numbers] [30]:[3] ‘Whenever a man makes a vow to [Jehovah], or swears an oath, or accepts a responsibility, he must not break his word… He must do whatever he says!
[Numbers] [30]:[4] ‘And the same is true of a woman. She must do whatever she vows to [Jehovah]. ‘If she says that she will do something while she is young and still living in her father’s house, and her father hears her say it – as long as he doesn’t disagree with her making [such a vow] – all her vows must be fulfilled,
[Numbers] [30]:[5] and she is bound to any obligations that she has taken upon her life.
[Numbers] [30]:[6] ‘However, if her father forbids [her vow] (or any other obligation that she agrees to) on the same day that he hears it, she isn’t bound to it, and [Jehovah] won’t hold her accountable, because it was forbidden by her father.
[Numbers] [30]:[7] ‘And if she’s married and speaks a vow to accept an obligation upon her life,
[Numbers] [30]:[8] and her husband hears it – as long as he doesn’t disagree with her making it – all her vows must be fulfilled and she is bound to any obligations that she has taken upon her life.
[Numbers] [30]:[9] ‘However, if her husband forbids [her vow] (or any other obligation that she agrees to) on the same day that he hears it, she isn’t bound to it and [Jehovah] won’t hold her accountable, because it was forbidden by her husband.
[Numbers] [30]:[10] ‘Also, whatever a widow or divorced woman vows to do with her life must be done.
[Numbers] [30]:[11] And if she made the vow when she was still [living] with her man,
[Numbers] [30]:[12] and he heard it and didn’t object; then, all her vows must be fulfilled and she is bound to any obligations that she has taken upon her life.
[Numbers] [30]:[13] ‘However, if her man cancels [her vow] (or any other obligation that she agrees to) on the same day that he hears it, she isn’t bound to it and [Jehovah] won’t hold her accountable, because her man forbade it.
[Numbers] [30]:[14] ‘So, any vow [that a woman] makes which will affect her life must be heard by her man, and he must either agree to it or disallow it.
[Numbers] [30]:[15] And if he chooses to say nothing, then she’s bound to it, and he must agree to any obligations that she has accepted, because he didn’t disagree with it on the day that he heard it.
[Numbers] [30]:[16] ‘But if her man – for any reason – should choose to cancel a vow after that, he’s guilty of a sin.’
[Numbers] [30]:[17] These were the laws that [Jehovah] gave to Moses regarding a man and his woman, and regarding a father and his young daughter who is still living in his home.
[Numbers] [31]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [31]:[2] ‘I want you to avenge the wrongs that the MidiAnites have committed against the children of IsraEl. And after that, you’ll be added to your people.’
[Numbers] [31]:[3] So Moses spoke to the people and said: ‘Arm yourselves, then stand before [Jehovah] in battle lines and [prepare yourselves] to bring the Lord’s vengeance upon MidiAn…
[Numbers] [31]:[4] Select 1,000 from each of the tribes of the children of IsraEl to go to war!’
[Numbers] [31]:[5] So they counted off the 1,000 from each Tribe of IsraEl – 12,000 men – and armed them for war.
[Numbers] [31]:[6] Then Moses sent them off, along with PhineAs (son of EliEzer the Priest and the grandson of Aaron) carrying the holy instruments and the signal trumpets,
[Numbers] [31]:[7] and they arranged themselves in battle lines against MidiAn, just as [Jehovah] had commanded Moses… And they went and destroyed them!
[Numbers] [31]:[8] Thereafter, they killed the 5 kings of MidiAn (Evi, Rocon, Sur, Ur, and Roboc)… And they even killed BalaAm (son of BeOr) with a sword, along with all the rest!
[Numbers] [31]:[9] Then (after they’d destroyed their army) they took all the women of MidiAn as captives, along with their food, cattle, and all their possessions,
[Numbers] [31]:[10] and they burned all their cities, villages, and homes with fire…
[Numbers] [31]:[11] They plundered everything, including the people and their animals.
[Numbers] [31]:[12] So they carried all the captives, spoils, and loot (planning to give them to Moses, EliEzer the Priest, and to divide them among the children of IsraEl) back to their camp in the plains of MoAb, which was near the Jordan River [across from] JeriCho.
[Numbers] [31]:[13] Then Moses, EliEzer (the Priest), and all the leaders of the gathering went to their camp to meet their army.
[Numbers] [31]:[14] But Moses was furious with the captains of the army (the leaders of thousands and of hundreds) that had returned from the battle,
[Numbers] [31]:[15] for he asked them: ‘Why have you kept these women alive?
[Numbers] [31]:[16] ‘They were the ones [who listened to] BalaAm and misled the children of IsraEl by inciting their revolt and by teaching them to despise the word of [Jehovah] at PhoGor… And that’s why [Jehovah] sent a plague on the gathering!
[Numbers] [31]:[17] ‘So now, kill all the men, destroy all their food, and kill all the women whom you know aren’t virgins…
[Numbers] [31]:[18] You may spare any women whom you suspect are virgins.
[Numbers] [31]:[19] ‘Then, all who have killed or touched dead bodies must stay outside of our camp for 7 days; and thereafter, you and those whom you’ve captured must be purified on the 3rd day and on the 7th day.
[Numbers] [31]:[20] ‘You must also purify all your clothes, all your leather utensils, all your goatskin items, and all your wooden bowls.’
[Numbers] [31]:[21] Then EliEzer (the Priest) said to the men from the army that had just returned from battle: ‘This is what the Law that [Jehovah] gave to Moses says:
[Numbers] [31]:[22] ‘The items of gold, silver, brass, iron, lead, and tin
[Numbers] [31]:[23] must be passed through fire to be cleansed. And whatever can’t be passed through a fire must be sprinkled with the purifying water to be made clean.
[Numbers] [31]:[24] ‘Then on the 7th day, you must be cleansed and you must wash your clothes. Only after that, may you enter our camp.’
[Numbers] [31]:[25] Well, the Lord then spoke to Moses again and said:
[Numbers] [31]:[26] ‘I want you and EliEzer the Priest to take an inventory of the captured people and animals.
[Numbers] [31]:[27] Then you must divide them among the soldiers that went out to battle and with the rest of the gathering.
[Numbers] [31]:[28] ‘Also, as a tribute to [Jehovah] from the warriors that went out to battle; take 1 out of every 500 of the people, oxen, sheep, and burros,
[Numbers] [31]:[29] and give them to EliEzer the Priest as the first fruits of [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [31]:[30] ‘Then, from among those things that are given to the children of IsraEl, you should take 1 out of 50 of the people, oxen, sheep, and burros, and give them to the Levites who teach at the Tent of [Jehovah].’
[Numbers] [31]:[31] So Moses and EliEzer (the Priest) did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [31]:[32] The plunder that was given to the soldiers included: 675,000 sheep,
[Numbers] [31]:[33] 72,000 oxen,
[Numbers] [31]:[34] and 61,000 burros.
[Numbers] [31]:[35] There were also 32,000 virgins who were given to them…
[Numbers] [31]:[36] Half of everything was given to the soldiers that went to war. And of the 337,500 sheep,
[Numbers] [31]:[37] they offered 675 sheep as a tribute to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [31]:[38] Of their 36,000 oxen, they gave 72 as a tribute to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [31]:[39] Of their 30,500 burros, they gave 61 as a tribute to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [31]:[40] And of the 16,000 people, they gave 32 of them as a tribute to [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [31]:[41] For Moses presented all the tributes as a wave offering to [Jehovah] God, [and they were given] to EliEzer the Priest (just as the Lord had commanded Moses)
[Numbers] [31]:[42] from the half that belonged to the children of IsraEl whom Moses had separated as soldiers.
[Numbers] [31]:[43] Thereafter, 337,500 sheep were divided among the gathering as their half,
[Numbers] [31]:[44] plus: 36,000 oxen,
[Numbers] [31]:[45] 30,500 burros,
[Numbers] [31]:[46] and 16,000 people.
[Numbers] [31]:[47] And from their half, Moses took a 1/50th of the people and the cattle, and gave them to the Levites who teach at the Tent of [Jehovah], as the Lord had commanded Moses.
[Numbers] [31]:[48] Well then, all those who’d been appointed as officers over the army (the captains of thousands and of hundreds) approached Moses and said:
[Numbers] [31]:[49] ‘Your servants have counted the men of war among us, and none have been lost.
[Numbers] [31]:[50] ‘So, those among us who found things that were made of gold, such as armlets, chains, rings, bracelets, and hair clasps have brought them as our gift to [Jehovah], to pay for our sins.’
[Numbers] [31]:[51] And when Moses and EliEzer (the Priest) accepted all the items of gold from them,
[Numbers] [31]:[52] [they found that] the gold that the captains of thousands and of hundreds offered to [Jehovah] was valued at 16,750 silver coins.
[Numbers] [31]:[53] However, the soldiers kept the rest of the loot for themselves.
[Numbers] [31]:[54] Then Moses and EliEzer (the Priest) took all the gold items that the captains of thousands and hundreds had contributed and placed it all in the Tent of Proofs to serve as a reminder to the children of IsraEl, there in front of [Jehovah].
[Numbers] [32]:[1] Now, the [tribes] of ReuBen and Gad both had huge herds of cattle, and when they saw that the area of JaZer and GalaAd had good grazing land,
[Numbers] [32]:[2] they went to Moses, EliEzer the Priest, and the leaders of the gathering, and said to them:
[Numbers] [32]:[3] ‘The areas of: AtarOth, DaEbon, JaZer, NamRa, Hesh-EbonEh, ElAle, Sebama, Nabau, and BaeAn...
[Numbers] [32]:[4] ’...which [Jehovah] has delivered into the hands of the children of IsraEl, is pasture land, and we (your servants) have many cattle!
[Numbers] [32]:[5] ‘So, if it pleases you, may your servants be given this land as our inheritance. Don’t make us cross the Jordan River.’
[Numbers] [32]:[6] But Moses asked: ‘Then when your brothers go to war, are you just going to sit here?
[Numbers] [32]:[7] “Why are you twisting the minds of the children of IsraEl by encouraging them not to cross into the land that [Jehovah] is giving to them?
[Numbers] [32]:[8] ‘Isn’t this the same thing that your fathers did when I sent them from KaDesh-Barne to spy in the land?
[Numbers] [32]:[9] For, after they went into the Valley of Grape Clusters as spies, they twisted the hearts of the children of IsraEl so that they didn’t want to enter the land that [Jehovah] gave to them,
[Numbers] [32]:[10] and this made [Jehovah] very angry! ‘So He swore and said:
[Numbers] [32]:[11] ‘All these men who were 20 years old and older when they left Egypt and that knew the difference between good and evil won’t see the land that I swore to give to AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob, because they’ve chosen not to follow Me!
[Numbers] [32]:[12] ‘The only exceptions are Caleb son of JePhonNe, and JoShua son of NaWeh… They were the only ones who followed Me closely.’
[Numbers] [32]:[13] ‘And because this made [Jehovah] so angry with IsraEl, He forced them to wander in the desert for 40 years, until the whole generation that did this evil thing before Him was gone.
[Numbers] [32]:[14] ‘Look! Now you’re following in the same footsteps as your fathers and you’ve allied yourselves as sinful people so as to make [Jehovah] even angrier with IsraEl;
[Numbers] [32]:[15] for you want to turn away from Him and stay in the desert again! ‘By choosing to do this, you’re sinning against the whole gathering!’
[Numbers] [32]:[16] But they came to him and said: ‘If we can build pens for our cattle here and have these cities as our possessions,
[Numbers] [32]:[17] we’ll arm ourselves and march ahead of the children of IsraEl to lead them into their land. ‘We’ll leave our possessions inside the walled cities (because of the people who live in this land),
[Numbers] [32]:[18] and we won’t return to our homes until after the children of IsraEl have each been given their own inheritance and are settled there...
[Numbers] [32]:[19] Then, we won’t take any of the land on the other side of the Jordan as our inheritance, because we’ll have taken our full inheritance here on the east side.’
[Numbers] [32]:[20] So Moses said to them: ‘If you’ll do everything that you’re saying… If you’ll arm yourselves and march in battle before [Jehovah],
[Numbers] [32]:[21] and if you’ll cross the Jordan and stay there until our enemies are destroyed
[Numbers] [32]:[22] and our land has been totally settled before you return home... You will be free of guilt before [Jehovah] and this land can be yours.
[Numbers] [32]:[23] ‘But if you don’t do that, you’ll be sinning against [Jehovah] and you’ll see the results of your sin when bad things happen to you!
[Numbers] [32]:[24] ‘So now, go on and build the cities in which you can store your things, along with the pens for your cattle; and thereafter, you must do everything that you’ve proposed.’
[Numbers] [32]:[25] And the [tribes] of ReuBen and Gad replied: ‘Your servants will do as our lord commands.
[Numbers] [32]:[26] ‘We will leave all our possessions, our women, and our cattle in the cities of GalaAd.
[Numbers] [32]:[27] And after that, we’ll march ahead [of IsraEl] all armed and ready for battle before [Jehovah], as you said.’
[Numbers] [32]:[28] Then Moses gave these instructions to EliEzer the Priest, JoShua (son of NaWeh), and all the heads of the families and tribes of IsraEl.
[Numbers] [32]:[29] He said: ‘If the sons of ReuBen and Gad cross the Jordan armed and ready for war before [Jehovah] and they help to conquer the land before you, you must give them the land of GalaAd as theirs.
[Numbers] [32]:[30] ‘However, if they don’t cross [the Jordan] all armed and ready for war, you must make them bring their possessions, women, and cattle into the land of CanaAn, where they’ll receive their inheritance among you.’
[Numbers] [32]:[31] And the sons of ReuBen and Gad answered: ‘We will do whatever [Jehovah] tells his servants!
[Numbers] [32]:[32] ‘We’ll arm ourselves and march into the land of CanaAn before [Jehovah], and you must give us our inheritance on this side of the Jordan.’
[Numbers] [32]:[33] So Moses gave the sons of Gad, the sons of ReuBen, and half of the Tribe of ManasSeh (one of the sons of JoSeph) the land of the Amorite king SeOn, the land of Og the king of BaShan, and all their cities and borders, as well as the cities and lands around them.

[Numbers] [32]:[35] Sophar, and JaZer.
[Numbers] [32]:[36] And they also built and fortified NamBran and BaethAran, where they then made pens for their sheep.
[Numbers] [32]:[37] The sons of ReuBen built: Hesh-EbonEh, ElAle, KariathAm,

[Numbers] [32]:[39] Also, the family of MachIr (of the Tribe of ManasSeh) went to GalaAd and captured it, destroying all the Amorites who lived there.

[Numbers] [33]:[1] These are the places where the children of IsraEl and their army stayed (under the direction of Moses and Aaron) after they left the land of Egypt.

[Numbers] [33]:[3] They left RamesSe on the 15th day of the 1st month. Then after the Passover, the children of IsraEl proudly walked away from the Egyptians,

[Numbers] [33]:[6] Then they left SocChoth and camped in BuThan, near the desert.

[Numbers] [33]:[13] And when they left RaPhaca, they camped in AiLus.
[Numbers] [33]:[14] When they left AiLus, they camped in RaphiDin (where there was no water for the people to drink).
[Numbers] [33]:[15] Then they left RaphiDin and camped in the SinAi Desert.
[Numbers] [33]:[16] When they left the SinAi Desert, they camped at the Graveyard of the Greedy.

[Numbers] [33]:[22] Then they left ResSan and camped in MakelLath.
[Numbers] [33]:[23] After MakelLath, they camped in Saphar.
[Numbers] [33]:[24] When they left Saphar, they camped in CharaDath.
[Numbers] [33]:[25] Then they left CharaDath and camped in MakelOth.
[Numbers] [33]:[26] When they left MakelOth, they camped in KataAth.
[Numbers] [33]:[27] Then they left KataAth and camped in TarAth.
[Numbers] [33]:[28] After leaving TarAth, they camped in MathecKa.
[Numbers] [33]:[29] Then they left MathecKa and camped in SelMona.
[Numbers] [33]:[30] After SelMona, they camped in MasurUth.
[Numbers] [33]:[31] After camping in MasurUth, they went to BanaYa.
[Numbers] [33]:[32] And after leaving BanaYa, they camped at Mount GadGad.
[Numbers] [33]:[33] Then after leaving Mount GadGad, they camped in EteBatha.
[Numbers] [33]:[34] When they left EteBatha, they camped in Ebrona.
[Numbers] [33]:[35] After Ebrona, they camped in GesiOn Gaber.
[Numbers] [33]:[36] Then they left GesiOn Gaber and camped in the Sin Desert. Then they left the Sin Desert and camped in the Pharan Desert at KaDesh.
[Numbers] [33]:[37] And when they left KaDesh, they camped at Mount Hor, near the land of Edom.
[Numbers] [33]:[38] It was at Mount Hor that Aaron the Priest climbed the mountain (following [Jehovah’s] instructions) and died on the 1st day of the 5th month, 40 years after they left the land of Egypt.
[Numbers] [33]:[39] Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
[Numbers] [33]:[40] And after the CanaAnite king Arad heard that the children of IsraEl were in his land,
[Numbers] [33]:[41] they left Mount Hor and camped in SelMona.
[Numbers] [33]:[42] Then from SelMona, they went to Phino.
[Numbers] [33]:[43] And after leaving Phino, they camped in ObOth.
[Numbers] [33]:[44] When they left ObOth, they camped in Gai at the border of MoAb.
[Numbers] [33]:[45] Then they left Gai and camped in DaEbon Gad.
[Numbers] [33]:[46] When they left DaEbon Gad, they camped in Gelmon DeblaThaim.
[Numbers] [33]:[47] After leaving Gelmon DeblaThaim, they camped on the Mountains of Abarim, which border Nabau.
[Numbers] [33]:[48] Then when they left the Mountains of Abarim, they camped on the west side [of the land] of MoAb by the Jordan River near JeriCho.
[Numbers] [33]:[49] There they stayed camped by the Jordan (from AiSimOth to Belsa, west of MoAb).
[Numbers] [33]:[50] It was there (west of MoAb by the Jordan River, close to JeriCho) that the Lord spoke to Moses and said:

[Numbers] [33]:[52] where they must destroy everyone who lives in that land. ‘They must tear down their altars, destroy all their molded images, and demolish all their [sacred] columns!
[Numbers] [33]:[53] All the inhabitants of the land must be destroyed so they can live there... For I have given them this land as their inheritance.
[Numbers] [33]:[54] ‘The land that each tribe inherits must thereafter be divided in a lottery. The more people there are in each tribe, the larger their inheritance must be; and the smaller the tribe, the smaller its inheritance… The inheritances must be divided by [the sizes of] their tribes and families.
[Numbers] [33]:[55] ‘Now, if you don’t destroy the people who live in that land; those who are left over will eventually become thorns in your eyes and darts in your sides! They will always be your enemies in this land...
[Numbers] [33]:[56] And the things that I had planned to do to them, I’ll do to you!’

[Numbers] [35]:[1] Then the Lord spoke to Moses by the Jordan River near JeriCho (west of MoAb) and said:
[Numbers] [35]:[2] ‘Now, give orders to the children of IsraEl and tell them that they must allot cities for the Levites to live in and own. They must provide them with suburbs around their cities to live in,
[Numbers] [35]:[3] which have pens for their cattle and all their animals.
[Numbers] [35]:[4] ‘These suburbs that they are to give to the Levites must run out and around their city walls for 3,000 feet (914m).
[Numbers] [35]:[5] So, they must measure out: 3,000 feet (914m) on the east side, 3,000 feet (914m) on the south side, 3,000 feet (914m) on the west side, and 3,000 feet (914m) on the north side... '...and their cities must be in the center.
[Numbers] [35]:[6] ‘They must also give the Levites 6 refuge cities, which will become havens for those who kill someone [accidentally]. In addition, they must provide them 42 more cities.
[Numbers] [35]:[7] ‘So altogether, they must give the Levites 48 cities, in addition to their suburbs.
[Numbers] [35]:[8] ‘[As to the size and location] of these cities that the children of IsraEl are to give them; those who have much must give much, and those who have less may give less... But all [the tribes] must give some of the cities that they’re going to inherit to the Levites.’
[Numbers] [35]:[9] Then the Lord spoke to Moses and said:
[Numbers] [35]:[10] ‘Speak to the children of IsraEl and tell them that when they cross the Jordan into the land of CanaAn,
[Numbers] [35]:[11] they must assign refuge cities to which those who accidentally kill someone may run.
[Numbers] [35]:[12] ‘These cities must be havens of refuge from those who would avenge the blood [of the one who was killed]. And there, no killer may be executed before he stands trial in a court.
[Numbers] [35]:[13] ‘There must be six of these cities that you are to set aside as places of refuge:
[Numbers] [35]:[14] Three on the east side of the Jordan, and Three in the land of CanaAn.
[Numbers] [35]:[15] ‘They must serve as places of refuge for the children of IsraEl, for aliens, and for those who are just visiting in your land. These cities must be places of refuge where anyone may run who has killed a man unintentionally.
[Numbers] [35]:[16] ‘However, if [a man] strikes [and kills a person] with something that is made of iron, the man must die, for he is a murderer and all murderers must be put to death!
[Numbers] [35]:[17] And if he throws a rock in an attempt to kill him and the person dies, he’s a murderer and all murderers must be put to death.
[Numbers] [35]:[18] And if he hits him with a wooden instrument that he’s holding in his hands and kills him, he’s a murderer and all murderers must be put to death.
[Numbers] [35]:[19] ‘Those who would avenge the blood [of the one who was killed] must execute the murderer… When they catch him, they must kill him!
[Numbers] [35]:[20] ‘If someone is angry and stabs another, or throws something at him from ambush,
[Numbers] [35]:[21] or if he beats him in anger and the man dies; the one who struck him must be put to death, for he is a murderer. The blood avenger must absolutely kill the murderer when he finds him.
[Numbers] [35]:[22] ‘However, if someone is accidentally stabbed (where no anger is involved), or something hits him (other than from ambush),
[Numbers] [35]:[23] or he is accidentally hit with a rock and he dies when no enemy was looking to harm him...
[Numbers] [35]:[24] Then the court must use these rules to judge between the one who did the striking and the blood avenger.
[Numbers] [35]:[25] ‘And [if he is found innocent], the gathering must save the slayer from the blood avenger and allow him to stay in the refuge city that he ran to. And he must live there until the High Priest (the one who was anointed with the holy oil) dies.
[Numbers] [35]:[26] ‘But if the person who did the killing should ever leave the city that he ran to for refuge,
[Numbers] [35]:[27] and the blood avenger should find him outside the refuge-city limits, and the blood-avenger kills him, he has done no wrong.

[Deuteronomy] [33]:[18] And to ZebuLon [and IsSachar] he said: ‘Rejoice O ZebuLon, as well as all those Who dwell in IsSachar’s tents. For, you’ll arise
