[1 Samuel] [26]:[16] so what you’ve done isn’t a good thing! ‘As [Jehovah] lives; you’re all sons of death, because you weren’t guarding your lord the king… The anointed of [Jehovah]. ‘For look! Where is the king’s spear? And where is his canteen of water? These things that he kept by his head?’
[1 Samuel] [26]:[17] Well, Saul recognized the voice of David and said: ‘Is that the voice of my child David?’ And David replied: ‘It’s my voice O lord… Your servant, O king!’
[1 Samuel] [26]:[18] And he asked: ‘So, why is my lord chasing his servant? ‘How have I sinned and what’s the charge against me?
[1 Samuel] [26]:[19] ‘Now listen, O my lord the king to these words of [mine,] his servant! ‘If it’s God who is sending you against me, then may you smell your sacrifice. But if it’s the sons of men, may they be cursed before [Jehovah], because they’ve driven me away from the inheritance that I received from [Jehovah], telling me to go and serve other gods!
[1 Samuel] [26]:[20] ‘May my blood not be spilled on the ground away from the face of [Jehovah]... For the king of IsraEl is searching for this ‘flea’ as though he were hunting for long-eared owls in the mountains!’
[1 Samuel] [26]:[21] And Saul said: ‘I have sinned. Come back to me, my child David… ‘I won’t do anything bad to you anymore, now that you’ve shown me how much you value my life. ‘I’ve acted foolishly and ignorantly!’
[1 Samuel] [26]:[22] And David replied: ‘Look! Here’s the king’s spear... Send one of your servants to take it.
[1 Samuel] [26]:[23] ‘The Lord will repay each one for his righteousness and faithfulness, just as [Jehovah] has saved you from my hands today, since I didn’t wish to raise a hand against the anointed of [Jehovah].
[1 Samuel] [26]:[24] ‘And look… As I’ve valued your life today, may my life be considered more valuable before my lord. May he shelter me and rescue me from all of my problems.’
[1 Samuel] [26]:[25] Then Saul said to David: ‘You’re blest, my child David... For whatever you do will succeed, and you can accomplish whatever you wish.’ So David went his way, and Saul returned home.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[1] But David said in his heart: ‘I’d best run to the land of the Philistines where I’ll be safe, because things don’t look too good for me here! Saul will keep searching for me in IsraEl, and by tomorrow I could be handed over to him.’
[1 Samuel] [27]:[2] So David got up and left, taking his 600 men with him, and he went to see AchIsh (son of MaOch), the king of Gath.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[3] Then David, his men, and both of his women (AhiNoam the JezreElite, and AbiGail the woman of NaBal the CarMelite) sat down to meet with AchIsh there at his house in Gath.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[4] And when Saul was told that David had fled to Gath, he stopped searching for him.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[5] Well when David went to AchIsh, he said this: ‘If your servant has found favor in your eyes, please give me a place in one of your rural cities, and I’ll settle there; for, why should you settle your servant in a city to rule right next to you?’
[1 Samuel] [27]:[6] And AchIsh gave him ZikLag, which still belongs to the Judean kings to this day.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[7] Then, after David had stayed there in the land of the Philistines for 4 months,
[1 Samuel] [27]:[8] he and his men attacked the Geshurites, the Gezrites, and the AmaLechites… These are the people who inhabited the land all the way from Shurand to the land of Egypt.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[9] He attacked the entire land and he didn’t leave a man or woman alive. However, he took their flocks, herds, burros, camels, and clothing, and thereafter, he returned to AchIsh.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[10] So then AchIsh asked David: ‘Whom did you attack today?’ And David replied: ‘The [land] south of Judea, from JerahMeEl south to the [land of the] Kenezites…
[1 Samuel] [27]:[11] And I didn’t bring anyone back alive to Gath, so that no one can say, Look at what David did!’ Well, that’s the way David handled matters for as long as he stayed in the land of the Philistines.
[1 Samuel] [27]:[12] And AchIsh trusted David, for he said: ‘It’s a shame that he’s being treated [so badly] by his own people in IsraEl. However, he’s welcome to serve me here throughout the age.’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[1] After that, the Philistines gathered their troops to go to war with IsraEl, and AchIsh said to David: ‘I’m sure that you and your men who are staying with me will join us in this war.’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[2] And David replied: ‘May this prove your servant’s faithfulness.’ So AchIsh said to David: ‘Then I’ll appoint you as the chief of my royal guards during this period!’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[3] Well, SamuEl had already died (after which IsraEl had mourned for him at his tomb in his city of RamAh), and Saul had also [killed off] all those who searched for omens and those who called out to [the dead] in his land.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[4] Then the Philistines went and set up camp at ShuNem, and Saul gathered the army of IsraEl and set up camp in GilBoa.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[5] But when Saul looked at the camp of the Philistines, it frightened him and he became weak at heart.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[6] So he asked for [direction from [Jehovah]], but the Lord wouldn’t answer him in his dreams, give him any signs, or answer him through the prophets.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[7] So he said to his servants: ‘Then search for a woman who can tell the future, and I’ll go ask her!’ And his servants told him: ‘Look, there’s a woman who can tell the future in EnDor.’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[8] So Saul disguised himself [by wearing] different clothes, and he covered his face; then he took two men with him and they went to see the woman at night. And he said to her: ‘Use your powers for me and lead me to the one I want to speak to!’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[9] And the woman replied: ‘Look! Now you know as much as Saul did… The one who killed off everyone in the land who ask the [dead] and who look for omens. ‘So are you coming here to trap and kill me?’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[10] But Saul swore an oath to her by God, saying: ‘As [Jehovah] lives, I won’t treat you unjustly in this matter.’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[11] So the woman asked Saul: ‘Then, who do you want me to bring up for you?’ And Saul replied: ‘Bring up SamuEl for me!’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[12] Well when the woman saw SamuEl, she screamed and she said to Saul: ‘Why have you misled me, for you’re Saul!’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[13] And the king said to her: ‘Don’t be afraid! Whom did you see?’ And she said: ‘I see judges rising from the ground.’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[14] Then he asked her: ‘What else did you see?’ And she replied: ‘A very old man coming up [from the ground] wearing a doubled robe.’ Well, Saul recognized this as SamuEl; so he fell with his face to the ground and bowed low before him.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[15] And SamuEl said: ‘Why are you bothering me and why did you bring me up?’ And Saul said: ‘I’m in a lot of trouble; for the Philistines have come to war against me, and God has left me. ‘He doesn’t listen to me anymore, nor does He answer the prophets or reply to me in my dreams… All I want to know is what I should do!’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[16] Then SamuEl replied: ‘If [Jehovah] has left you and taken up with your neighbor, why are you asking me?
[1 Samuel] [28]:[17] ‘For, all that [Jehovah] is doing to you is what I told you that He would do! He’s going to rip your kingdom from your hands and give it to your neighbor David,
[1 Samuel] [28]:[18] because you didn’t listen to His voice when He was showing His rage on the AmaLechites.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[19] ‘Therefore, [Jehovah] is going to give IsraEl into the hands of the Philistines… By tomorrow, you and your sons will be with me, while the camp of IsraEl will be handed over to the Philistines!’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[20] Well at that, Saul dropped to the ground shaking, because he was so afraid of what SamuEl had said! He was already weak in the knees, because he hadn’t eaten anything all that day or night.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[21] Then the woman went up to Saul, and when she saw that he was shaking, she said: ‘Now, look at me and listen to your female servant, for I’ve put my life into your hands, and I’m trusting in what you said.
[1 Samuel] [28]:[22] ‘Do what I tell you… I’m going to give you a little food to eat so you can regain your strength, and then you should leave.’
[1 Samuel] [28]:[23] However he wouldn’t listen to her, because he didn’t want anything to eat. Yet his aids and the woman kept insisting; so he got up off of the ground and sat in a chair,
[1 Samuel] [28]:[24] then the woman went out and butchered a calf that was by her house. After that, she took some flour and made some fermentation-free bread,
[1 Samuel] [28]:[25] and she brought it all to Saul and his servants, and they ate… Then they returned [to their camp] that night.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[1] Well, the Philistines had marched all their troops to Aphek, and IsraEl had set up camp at EnDor in JezreEl.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[2] Meanwhile, the Philistine governors were coming by the hundreds and thousands… Then David and his men showed up last, with AchIsh.
[1 Samuel] [29]:[3] Well, [on seeing him], the Philistine governors asked AchIsh: ‘Who is [this person] that’s with you?’ And AchIsh replied: ‘That’s David, the servant of Saul the king of IsraEl. ‘This is the 2nd year he’s been with me, and I’ve found no fault in him.’
[1 Samuel] [29]:[4] However, the Philistine governors were outraged, and they said to him: ‘Return this man to the people over whom you’ve assigned him… Don’t allow him to come with us to the battle, because he could be a traitor in our camp! ‘After all, how do we know that he won’t reconcile with his lord? And if he does, our men will pay with their heads!
[1 Samuel] [29]:[5] ‘For, isn’t this the same David of whom the dancers sang: ‘Saul killed his thousands and David his ten thousands?’
[1 Samuel] [29]:[6] So AchIsh then called for David and said to him: ‘As [Jehovah] lives, I know that you’re a good and honest man, and that’s why I invited you to come with me into the camp. ‘But although I haven’t found anything evil in you since you came to me, the governors don’t trust you...
[1 Samuel] [29]:[7] So, return to [your city] in peace, and don’t allow yourself to be seen doing anything wrong in the eyes of the Philistine governors.’
[1 Samuel] [29]:[8] But David asked: ‘What have I done? What have you found wrong with your servant? ‘Let me fight against the enemies of my lord the king!’
[1 Samuel] [29]:[9] And AchIsh told him: ‘I know that you’re a good man… Like a messenger from God. ‘But the Philistine governors are saying, ‘He shouldn’t come with us to this battle.’
[1 Samuel] [29]:[10] So when you and your men get up early in the morning, you should return to the city that I gave to you!’
[1 Samuel] [29]:[11] As a result, when David and his men got up early the next morning, they went back and guarded the land of the Philistines, as the Philistines started their war against IsraEl.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[1] Well, while David and his men were returning to ZikLag (it was a 3-day journey), the AmaLechites had come from the south and attacked ZikLag… They captured it and burned it!
[1 Samuel] [30]:[2] However, they didn’t kill any of the young men or any of the women, they just led them away as captives.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[3] So when David and his men got back to the city and found it burned, and that their women, sons, and daughters had been carried away as captives,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[4] David and his men sat down and cried… They wailed until they were just too weak to cry anymore.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[5] Well, both of David’s women (AhiNoam the JezreElite, and AbiGail, the woman of NaBal the CarMelite) had been captured,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[6] which hurt David so much that his men said that they should stone him, because he was so grieved over the people and for each of his sons and daughters. However, his God [Jehovah] then gave him strength,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[7] and he said to the Priest AbiAthar (son of AhiMelech): ‘Bring the sacred vest to me.’ So AbiAthar came to David carrying the vest,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[8] and David asked [Jehovah]: ‘Should I chase after them?’ And [Jehovah] replied: ‘Chase after them; for if you chase them, you’ll catch up with them and rescue [your people].’
[1 Samuel] [30]:[9] So David went after them with all of his 600 men; and when they reached the Bosor Wadi, he left 200 of them behind [to guard their things]…
[1 Samuel] [30]:[10] So he only had about 400 men. However, he traveled on with the 400 men (after leaving 200 on the other side of the Bosor Wadi).
[1 Samuel] [30]:[11] Well, on the way, [his men] found an Egyptian man [lying] in a field, and they took him to David, who gave him some food and water.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[12] They also gave him part of a dried cluster of figs and two portions of raisins, which revived him… For he’d gone without anything to eat or drink for more that three days.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[13] Then David asked him: ‘What are you doing here, and where did you come from?’ And the Egyptian man replied: ‘I’m the servant of an AmaLechite man. ‘My master left me here because I was sick… And I’ve been lying here for three days.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[14] We’d just attacked parts of Judah that are south of the Cherethites and south of Caleb, and we burned the city of ZikLag.’
[1 Samuel] [30]:[15] Then David asked him: ‘Can you lead me to his troops?’ And he said: ‘Yes… If you’ll swear by God that you won’t kill me or return me to my master, I’ll lead you to them!’
[1 Samuel] [30]:[16] So he led them, and by the time they caught up with them, everyone was scattered throughout the land and they were eating, drinking, and celebrating over the great quantity of loot that they’d taken from the land of the Philistines and from the land of Judah.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[17] Well, David started slaughtering them from morning until evening and then into the next day… He left no survivors, other than 400 boys who were able to escape by fleeing on camels.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[18] Then David took back everything that the AmaLechites had captured, and he rescued both of his women.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[19] Yet, none [of his men] (from the small to the great) had been killed, and all the sons and daughters, as well as the loot that had been taken, was returned.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[20] Meanwhile, David also took all their flocks and herds, and he looted everything (which was thereafter referred to as ‘the spoils of David’).
[1 Samuel] [30]:[21] Then when they got back to the 200 men whom David had left behind at the Bosor Wadi, everyone came to greet David and the men who returned with him. So David went up to them and wished them peace.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[22] However, all the wicked men and troublemakers among the warriors that went with David said, ‘They didn’t go with us, so why should we divide any of the loot that we recovered with them? ‘Let them just take back their own women and children, and [be satisfied with that]!’
[1 Samuel] [30]:[23] However, David said: ‘You must not mistreat the brothers of this confederation. ‘For it was [Jehovah] that guarded us and gave the enemy to us, and He’s the One who protected the troops that came with us...
[1 Samuel] [30]:[24] So, watch your words, because these men are in no way less than you, and they’ll receive their share of the battle for staying here and watching our equipment! ‘Yes, they’ll be given the same share as everyone else!’
[1 Samuel] [30]:[25] Well from that day on, this became the rule in IsraEl.
[1 Samuel] [30]:[26] And when David got back to ZikLag, he sent [a portion of] the spoils to the elders of Judah, as well as to some of his neighbors, saying: ‘Look, here is a blessing from the spoils of the enemies of [Jehovah].’
[1 Samuel] [30]:[27] [He also sent some of the spoils to the people in:] BethEl, Southern RamOth, JatTir,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[28] AroEr, SiphMoth, EshTemoa,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[29] RachAl, to those in the JerahMeElite cities, the Kenite cities,
[1 Samuel] [30]:[30] the people in HorMah, BeerAshan, AthAch, and
[1 Samuel] [30]:[31] to those in HebRon. David and his men carried it to each of those places.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[1] Meanwhile, in the war between the Philistines and IsraEl, the IsraElites had been routed by the Philistines, who slaughtered them all the way to Mount GilBoa.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[2] The Philistines also caught up with Saul and his sons, and they were able to cut down Saul’s sons JoNathan, AbiNadab, and MelchiShua.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[3] However, the battle got bogged down as they were fighting Saul… But then a bowman shot at Saul and wounded him in the spleen.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[4] And Saul said to his weapons bearer: ‘Unsheathe your broadsword and run me through with it, so that one of these uncircumcised men doesn’t make fun of me before he kills me!’ Well, the man who was carrying his weapons was afraid and he didn’t want to do it; so Saul took his broadsword and fell on it.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[5] And when the man carrying his weapons saw that Saul was dead, he fell on his sword and died also.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[6] So Saul, all three of his sons, his weapons bearer, and all of his men died that same day.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[7] And when the men of IsraEl that were on the other side of the Jordan Valley saw that Saul and his sons were dead, they all ran away… They just fled their cities and ran; and thereafter, the Philistines took [their cities] and lived there.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[8] Well, it was when the Philistines came to strip the dead that they found Saul and his three sons dead on Mount GilBoa.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[9] So they cut off [Saul’s] head and took his weapons, and they sent them all around the land of the Philistines to announce the good news to their idols and to their people.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[10] Thereafter, they presented his weapons [to the goddess] Astarte, and they nailed [Saul’s] body to a wall in BethSham.
[1 Samuel] [31]:[11] However, when the people in JabIsh GileAd heard what the Philistines had done to Saul,
[1 Samuel] [31]:[12] all their mighty men went out that night and recovered the bodies of Saul and his son JoNathan from the wall in BethSham, and brought them back to JabIsh, where they were burned [in a funeral pyre].
[1 Samuel] [31]:[13] Then they took their bones and placed them in a tomb in the plowed field of JabIsh, and they fasted for 7 days.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[1] After Saul died and after David had returned from his battle with the AmaLechites, David spent a couple of days in ZikLag.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[2] Then on the 3rd day, a man came to him from the camp of the army of Saul. His clothes were all torn and his face was covered with dirt. And when he reached David, he fell to the ground and bowed low before him.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[3] Then David asked him: ‘Where have you come from?’ And he said: ‘I’ve struggled to make it here from the camp of IsraEl.’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[4] Then David asked: ‘What message are you bringing? Tell me!’ And he said: ‘Our army has fled the field of battle… Many have been injured and many more have been killed! ‘Why, Saul and his son JoNathan have both been killed!’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[5] Then David asked: ‘How do you know that both Saul and JoNathan are dead?’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[6] And the young man said: ‘I happened to be on Mount GilBoa when I saw Saul leaning on his spear. ‘The chariots and cavalry started coming towards him, so I went over to his side.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[7] And when he looked back and saw me, he called to me and I said: ‘Look, I’m here.’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[8] ‘And he asked: ‘Who are you?’ ‘And I said: ‘I’m an AmaLechite.’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[9] ‘And he said to me: ‘Stand over me and kill me, because an awful darkness is coming over me!’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[10] ‘So I stood over him and put him to death, because I knew that he couldn’t survive his wound. Then I took the [turban] from his head and the armlet from his biceps, and I’ve brought them here to you, my lord.’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[11] Well, David started grabbing his clothes and ripping them, and all of his men started ripping their clothes,
[2 Samuel] [1]:[12] beating on their chests, and crying. Then they fasted for the rest of that day over Saul, his son JoNathan, the people of Judah, and the people of IsraEl who had been cut down with broadswords.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[13] After that, David asked the man who’d brought him the message: ‘Where are you from?’ And he replied: ‘I’m the son of an AmaLechite man who is living in your land.’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[14] Then David asked him: ‘So, why weren’t you afraid to lift your hand and kill the anointed of [Jehovah]?’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[15] And thereafter, David called one of his servants and said: ‘Come here and kill him!’ So he struck the man and he died.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[16] For David told him: ‘Your blood is on your own head, because your own mouth spoke against you when you said: ‘I have killed the anointed of [Jehovah].’
[2 Samuel] [1]:[17] Well after that, David went into mourning over Saul and his son JoNathan.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[18] And to teach the sons of Judah, he sang this song, for look, it’s written in the scroll of the righteous:
[2 Samuel] [1]:[19] ‘Erect a stele, O IsraEl, For those who have died in your hills, For how the mighty have fallen!
[2 Samuel] [1]:[20] ‘Don’t allow them to announce it in Gath, Or announce it as good news in AshKelon’s streets, So the daughters of Philistia won’t rejoice… So the daughters of the uncircumcised will never know joy.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[21] ‘May dew not fall on GilBoa, And may no more rain fall upon it, There in the fields of the first fruits; For the shields of the mighty have been treated with contempt. ‘Saul’s shield was not anointed with oil,
[2 Samuel] [1]:[22] Nor with the blood of the slain, Or with the fat of the mighty. But, JoNathan’s bow didn’t come back void, Nor did the broadsword of Saul return bare.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[23] ‘Saul and JoNathan, beloved ones… These delightful men were not parted in life, Nor were they parted in death. They were swifter than eagles, And they conquered more than great lions.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[24] ‘IsraEl’s daughters, You should weep over Saul, For he dressed you in scarlet and jewels… He dressed you in clothes, and in gold, and in gems.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[25] How these mighty have fallen in battle! ‘O JoNathan, ‘You were killed in the mountains.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[26] I grieve over you, JonNathan, O my brother, you were always there for me. Your affection for me amazed me, More so than the love of women.
[2 Samuel] [1]:[27] ‘O how the mighty fell, And the weapons of war were destroyed.’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[1] Then after that, David asked this of [Jehovah]: ‘Should I now return to one of the cities of Judah?’ And the Lord replied: ‘Go!’ Then when David asked where he should go, the Lord told him: ‘To HebRon.’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[2] So David thereafter moved to HebRon with his women (AhiNoam the JezreElite own house and they all started living in and around HebRon.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[4] And after that, the men of Judah came and anointed David to be the ruler over the house of Judah. Well later, when David received the report that the men of JabIsh GileAd had put Saul’s [body] in a tomb,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[5] he sent a message to the leaders of JabIsh of GileAd that said: ‘May you be blest by [Jehovah] for showing such mercy to your lord Saul the anointed of God by building a tomb for him and his son JoNathan,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[6] and may [Jehovah] grant you mercy and truth. ‘From now on, I’ll treat you in the same [kind] way that you’ve treated [Saul and JoNathan].
[2 Samuel] [2]:[7] ‘So, prepare yourselves for this and make yourselves strong; because, now that your lord Saul has died, I’ve been anointed to rule over the house of Judah and to become your king!’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[8] However, AbNer (son of Ner), Saul’s commander-in-chief, took Saul’s son IshBosheth from his camp to ManaEm
[2 Samuel] [2]:[9] and set him up as the ruler over: GileAd, ThasiRi, JezreEl, Ephraim, BenJamin, and All the rest of IsraEl.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[10] Well, when IshBosheth was appointed the king over IsraEl, he was 40-years old, and he ruled from there for the next 2 years. However, the house of Judah followed David as their ruler,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[11] and he ruled from HebRon for the next 7 years and 6 months.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[12] Then AbNer (son of Ner) and the servants of IshBosheth came from ManaEm to GibeOn,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[13] and JoAb (son of ZeruJah) and David’s servants came from HebRon to meet with them at the spring of GibeOn. So they all sat down together at the spring, with each group sitting on opposite sides of the spring.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[14] And AbNer said to JoAb: ‘Have your servants get up and play [in combat] in front of us.’ So JoAb said to them: ‘[Okay men], get up!’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[15] Then 12 of IshBosheth’s servants (BenJaminites) stood up as 12 of David’s men stood up,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[16] and they all grabbed each other by the head and jabbed each other in the side with their swords… And they all fell together. So from then on, that place was known in GibeOn as ‘The Place of the Plotters.’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[17] As a result, a battle started that day, which was hard fought; and AbNer and the men of IsraEl lost to the servants of David.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[18] Now, ZeruJah had three sons that were there; JoAb, AbiShai, and AshaEl… And AshaEl was very light on his feet… Like a deer in the field.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[19] Well, he chased AbNer without slowing or swerving.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[20] And when AbNer looked back and saw him, he shouted: ‘Is that really AshaEl?’ And he replied: ‘It’s me!’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[21] Then AbNer shouted: ‘You should really turn aside and put on one of your servant’s armor.’ However, AshaEl didn’t want to slow down, because he was hot on the heels of AbNer.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[22] Then AbNer said to AshaEl: ‘Turn back or I’ll have to kill you! And if I do that, how could I ever show my face to JoAb again?
[2 Samuel] [2]:[23] ‘What are you doing? Go back to your brother JoAb!’ However, AshaEl wasn’t willing to stop! So AbNer threw his spear and hit him in the stomach, running him completely through, and he fell and died there under [AbNer]. Well, everyone went to the place where he fell and just stood there looking [at the body].
[2 Samuel] [2]:[24] Then JoAb and AbiShai chased AbNer until the sun set, getting as far as the hill of AmManin in front of Gai on the road between GibeOn and the desert.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[25] Meanwhile, the sons of BenJamin had assembled and were coming to help AbNer (they’d reached to the top of one of the hills).
[2 Samuel] [2]:[26] So AbNer called to JoAb and said: ‘Do you really think that you can beat me with your broadsword… Don’t you know that this will lead to your own bitter end? ‘Tell your people to stop chasing their brother!’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[27] Then JoAb said: ‘As [Jehovah] lives, it’s good that you said this; for our people would’ve been chasing each other all night long!’
[2 Samuel] [2]:[28] So JoAb blew his trumpet, and all his people withdrew and stopped chasing after IsraEl, and the battle ended.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[29] Well, AbNer and his men left at sunset and traveled throughout the night, crossing the Jordan and returning all the way to their camp,
[2 Samuel] [2]:[30] since JoAb had stopped chasing AbNer. Thereafter, [JoAb] gathered all his men to find out how many of David’s servants had been lost, and he found that they’d only lost 19, plus AshaEl.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[31] However, David’s men had killed 360 of the sons of BenJamin under AbNer.
[2 Samuel] [2]:[32] Then he picked up AshaEl’s [body] and put it in the tomb in BethLehem where his father was buried. And JoAb and his men also traveled all night long, reaching HebRon at dawn.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[1] Well, the war between the house of David and the house of Saul lasted a long time and the house of David kept getting stronger while the house of Saul kept getting weaker.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[2] In the meantime, David had sons born to him in HebRon. His firstborn was AmNon through AhiNoam the JezreElite.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[3] The second was DaluJah through AbiGail the CarMelite. The third was AbSalom through MaAcha the daughter of TholMi, the king of Gesir.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[4] The fourth was Ornia through PhegGith. The fifth was SabaTia through AbiTal.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[5] The sixth was JetheraAm through AiGla. These were all David’s women and all of his sons that were born in HebRon.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[6] Well, during the war between the house of Saul and the house of David, AbNer became [more powerful] in IsraEl.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[7] Now, Saul used to have a concubine named ResPha (the daughter of Jal). Then Saul’s son IshBosheth went to AbNer and asked him this: ‘Why are you [sleeping] with my father’s concubine?’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[8] Well, this made AbNer furious with IshBosheth, and AbNer said: ‘How dare you to speak to me like a dog after the mercy I’ve shown to the house of your father Saul and to his family and friends! ‘Since I never went over to the side of the house of David, why are you coming to me and complaining that I’ve been unjust over some woman today?
[2 Samuel] [3]:[9] ‘Now, as [Jehovah] swore in an oath to David; may God curse AbNer and add to it if I don’t do this:
[2 Samuel] [3]:[10] ‘I will now remove the kingship from the house of Saul and raise the throne of David to be over all of IsraEl and Judah from Dan to BeerSheba!’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[11] Well, IshBosheth didn’t say anything more, because he was so frightened!
[2 Samuel] [3]:[12] Then AbNer sent messengers to David right away (who was in ThaiLam at the time), with the message: ‘Make a treaty with me, because I’m on your side now, and I’m going to give the whole house of IsraEl to you.’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[13] And David replied: ‘Yes, I’ll make a treaty with you! ‘However, there’s one thing that I want to ask of you… I don’t want to see your face unless you bring Saul’s daughter Michal with you when you come to me.’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[14] Meanwhile, David also sent messengers to Saul’s son IshBosheth, telling him: ‘Give back my woman Michal, for whom I paid with the foreskins of 100 Philistines!’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[15] As a result, IshBosheth sent and had her taken from her man PhaltiEl (son of SelLe),
[2 Samuel] [3]:[16] who then followed her all the way to BarAkim. But after AbNer warned him to go back, he turned around and went home.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[17] Thereafter, AbNer spoke to the elders of IsraEl and said this: ‘Since you’ve been looking for David to rule over you a long time,
[2 Samuel] [3]:[18] you should do something now. For [Jehovah] has said concerning him: ‘I will deliver IsraEl from the hands of the Philistines and all their other enemies at the hands of David!’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[19] Then AbNer also went and spoke to the people of the tribe of BenJamin (before he went to speak to David at HebRon), and everyone in the house of BenJamin and the rest of IsraEl was pleased with this idea.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[20] It was then that AbNer went with 20 of his men to see David in HebRon… And David prepared a banquet for them.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[21] So AbNer said this to David: ‘I’ll go and gather all IsraEl to my lord the king, and I’ll conclude a treaty with you for you to rule over whomever you may wish.’ Then David sent AbNer away in peace.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[22] However, shortly thereafter, JoAb returned to David with his army after a battle, carrying many spoils of war. Well, AbNer was no longer there with David in HebRon, since he’d been sent away in peace.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[23] But when JoAb and his men heard that AbNer (son of Ner) had come to David and that he’d been sent away in peace,
[2 Samuel] [3]:[24] JoAb came to the king and asked: ‘What have you done? ‘Look! AbNer actually came here and you sent him away in peace?
[2 Samuel] [3]:[25] ‘Don’t you know that AbNer just came here to deceive you? He just came to find out your plans!’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[26] So, after JoAb left David, he sent messengers to AbNer (who was at the well of SeiRam), asking him to return… But David didn’t know anything about this.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[27] And when AbNer returned to HebRon, JoAb called to him as he arrived at the city gate, saying that he wanted to speak to him. Well, it was a trap; for he stabbed him in the stomach and killed him! He did this to [avenge] the blood of his brother AshaEl.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[28] Then when David heard about [what AbNer had done], he said: ‘My kingdom and I are innocent before [Jehovah] throughout the ages over the blood of AbNer, son of Ner!
[2 Samuel] [3]:[29] ‘But may the guilt of this rest upon JoAb and the house of his father! May the house of JoAb always suffer from gonorrhea and skin infection; may they walk on crutches; may they starve and be cut down in battle...
[2 Samuel] [3]:[30] For it was JoAb and his brother AbiShai [that did this to] AbNer, because he’d killed their brother AshaEl at the battle of GibeOn.’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[31] Then David told JoAb and all of his men to rip their clothes, wrap themselves in sackcloth, and to mourn for AbNer! And after that, David walked behind AbNer’s casket in his funeral procession.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[32] For they buried him in a tomb in HebRon, where David screamed and cried, as did all the people.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[33] The king mourned over AbNer, saying these words: ‘Should AbNer have died like NaBal?
[2 Samuel] [3]:[34] ‘For his hands and feet were not tied, Nor like NaBal, was he led away… He was cut down by an unrighteous man.’ So, all the people gathered to weep for him,
[2 Samuel] [3]:[35] and David invited them all to eat loaves of bread in a funeral meal that day. Then David swore an oath, saying: ‘May God curse me and add more to it if I eat anything before the sun sets today.’
[2 Samuel] [3]:[36] As a result, all the people were pleased by these things that the king had done before them.
[2 Samuel] [3]:[37] And all IsraEl got to know that the king had nothing to do with killing AbNer (son of Ner).
[2 Samuel] [3]:[38] Then the king said to his servants: ‘Don’t you know that a great leader has fallen in IsraEl today?
[2 Samuel] [3]:[39] ‘I feel like one of his closest relatives and like someone who is stood in the presence of a king! ‘However these men, these sons of ZeruJah, are hard for me to bear... May [Jehovah] repay the one who did this wicked thing with the evil that he deserves.’
[2 Samuel] [4]:[1] Well, when Saul’s son IshBosheth heard that AbNer (son of Ner) had been killed in HebRon, he and all the men in IsraEl just fell weak.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[2] And at the time, there were two men who were leaders of the confederation of IshBosheth; one was BaAna and the other was RechAb. They were both sons of RimMon the BeerOthite of the tribe of BenJamin (for BeerOth was considered part of the tribe of BenJamin).
[2 Samuel] [4]:[3] These BeerOthites had fled to GetThaim, where [their families] live to this day.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[4] (Also, Saul’s son JoNathan had a 5-year-old son who was lame. For when the message came from JezreEl about [the death] of Saul and JoNathan, his nurse picked him up and ran away… But then she dropped him, which damaged his legs. His name was MephiBosheth.)
[2 Samuel] [4]:[5] Well, as the sons of RimMon the BeerOthite (RechAb and BaAna) were leaving, they went to the house of [Saul’s son] IshBosheth in the heat of the day during his noontime nap.
[2 Samuel] [4]:[6] And because the doorman was out sifting wheat, they were able to slip in without being noticed…
[2 Samuel] [4]:[7] And there was IshBosheth in his bedroom asleep in his bed. So they struck him, killed him, and cut off his head, then they traveled west all that day and night so as to
[2 Samuel] [4]:[8] bring IshBosheth’s head to David in HebRon! Then they said to the king: ‘Look, here’s the head of Saul’s son IshBosheth… Your enemy who would’ve killed you! ‘[Jehovah] has given him to our lord the king as punishment to the enemies of his offspring. For Saul and his offspring have been your enemies down to this day.’
[2 Samuel] [4]:[9] But David told RechAb and his brother BaAna: ‘As [Jehovah] (the One who has protected my life) lives,
[2 Samuel] [4]:[10] the man who reported to me that Saul had died thought he was bringing me good news... However, I had him taken away and killed in ZikLag, despite what he thought!
[2 Samuel] [4]:[11] ‘And now, you wicked people have killed a righteous man while he was in his house asleep in bed! So, I’ll require his blood from you… I’ll wipe you out of this land!’
[2 Samuel] [4]:[12] Well at that, David gave orders to his servants, and they killed them both… They cut off their hands and feet and hung their bodies near the spring in HebRon, then they took the head of IshBosheth and placed it in the tomb of AbNer (son of Ner) in HebRon.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[1] Well thereafter, all the tribes of IsraEl came to David in HebRon, and they said to him: ‘Look, we are your own flesh and bones.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[2] ‘And although Saul used to be our king, you were the one who led the people of IsraEl in our [battles], so you must be the leader over IsraEl.’
[2 Samuel] [5]:[3] Then all the elders of IsraEl came [and met with] the king in HebRon, and King David made a treaty with them there in HebRon, in the presence of [Jehovah]. And thereafter, they anointed David to be the king over all IsraEl.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[4] Well, David was 30 years old when he started his rule, and he reigned for 40 years.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[5] He reigned over [the tribe of] Judah in HebRon for 7-1/2 years, and he reigned over all IsraEl and Judah from JeruSalem for 33 years.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[6] Thereafter, David and all his men [marched on] JeruSalem, where the Jebusites were living at the time. And the [Jebusites] said to him: ‘You’re not going to enter here, for the blind and the lame will oppose you! Even they are saying: ‘David will never enter [this city]!’
[2 Samuel] [5]:[7] However, David took the citadel on Zion, and he made it his own city.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[8] Then he told his men: ‘Everyone who cuts down a Jebusite should also use his dagger on the lame, the blind, and on anyone else who hates the person of David. ‘And thereafter, the people must say, ‘The blind and the lame will never enter the Temple of [Jehovah]!’
[2 Samuel] [5]:[9] Well, David took up living there in the citadel, and the place became known as the City of David. Then he built a city around his tower and palace.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[10] And from that point on, David kept getting greater, because [Jehovah] the Almighty was with him.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[11] Then King HiRam [I] of Tyre sent envoys to David, who brought along much wood from his cedar trees, as well as some stoneworkers that built a palace for David.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[12] Now, David knew that it was [Jehovah] who had made him king over IsraEl, and that He was the One who was blessing [David’s] kingdom, because of His people IsraEl.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[13] Well, after David moved from HebRon to JeruSalem, he took more wives and concubines, so he had even more sons and daughters.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[14] These are the names of the children that were born to him in JeruSalem: SamMous, SoBab, Nathan, Solomon,
[2 Samuel] [5]:[15] EbeAr, EliSoWe, NapPek, JePhies,
[2 Samuel] [5]:[16] EliSama, EliDae, EliPhalath, SamaE, JessiBath, YalaMaAn, YeBaAr, TheaEsous, EliPhalar, NaGed, NaPhek, JaNathan, LeAsamus, BaAlImath, and EliPhaAth.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[17] However, when the Philistines heard that David had been anointed to be the king over IsraEl, they went looking for him. And when David heard about this, he made it back to his citadel
[2 Samuel] [5]:[18] just as the Philistines were forming for an attack in the Valley of the Titans.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[19] So David went to [Jehovah] and asked: ‘Should I fight the Philistines, and if so, will You give them into my hands?’ And the Lord replied: ‘Go, for I’ll save you and give the Philistines into your hands!’
[2 Samuel] [5]:[20] So David attacked them from the mountain passes, and he breached their lines, defeating the Philistines. Then David said: ‘Since [Jehovah] cut through my enemies the Philistines like He cuts through water, we’ll name this place the High Breaches.’
[2 Samuel] [5]:[21] Well at the time, the [Philistines] had left behind all [the images of] their gods. So David and his men picked them up and carried them along.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[22] But then the Philistines attacked again, coming to meet them in battle in the Valley of the Titans.
[2 Samuel] [5]:[23] So David asked [Jehovah] once more, and the Lord replied: ‘Don’t confront them; go around them to the other side of the Forest of Tears, and I’ll give them into your hands...
[2 Samuel] [5]:[24] Then, when you hear the sound of them marching from the Forest of Tears, you must attack! For I’ll lead you in your battle with the Philistines.’
[2 Samuel] [5]:[25] So David did just as the Lord told him, and he cut down the Philistines all the way from GibeOn to the land of GeZer.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[1] Well, after [some 20 years], David gathered the young men of IsraEl (about 70,000 of them)
[2 Samuel] [6]:[2] and he and all his men, along with rulers from Judah, went to bring back the Chest of God which was used to call on the Name of [Jehovah] of Armies, which had the [covering of] cherubs.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[3] So they went to the house of AmiNadab (which was on a hill) and picked up the Chest of [Jehovah], and mounted it on a new wagon. Then the sons of AmiNadab walked ahead of the wagon that carried the Chest.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[4] Well, as AmiNadab’s sons were leading the wagon along,
[2 Samuel] [6]:[5] David and his men were dancing in front of [Jehovah] and playing musical instruments (they were playing appropriate lively tunes on lyres, harps, tambourines, cymbals, and pipes).
[2 Samuel] [6]:[6] And when they arrived at the threshing-floor of NaChon, the oxen [that were hauling the chest] bolted; so, Oza stuck out his hand to grab the Chest of God in order to steady it.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[7] But this enraged [Jehovah], so God struck Oza and he fell dead next to the Chest of [Jehovah]… There, in the presence of God!
[2 Samuel] [6]:[8] Of course, David was very depressed over the fact that [Jehovah] had cut down Oza. So he started calling that place ‘the Cutting Down of Oza,’ which is what it’s still called to this day.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[9] And on that day, David became afraid of [Jehovah]; for he asked: ‘How would it be possible for me to transport the Chest of God?’
[2 Samuel] [6]:[10] So he decided not to move the Chest of the Sacred Agreement of [Jehovah] into his city. Rather, he turned around and carried it to the house of Obed-Edom the GitTite,
[2 Samuel] [6]:[11] and that’s where the Chest of [Jehovah] was kept for the next three months. But as a result, [Jehovah] blest the household of Obed-Edom and everything that he owned.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[12] Then when King David was told that that the house of Obed-Edom and all his things were being blest because of the Chest of God, David went and took the Chest of [Jehovah] from there and brought it into the city of David in a joyful [parade].
[2 Samuel] [6]:[13] However, this time when the Chest of [Jehovah] was being transported, it was led by 7 companies of dancers, followed by the calf and the lambs that were to be sacrificed, and then by David, as [musicians] played music that was appropriate for the presence of [Jehovah].
[2 Samuel] [6]:[14] Well, David was wearing a fine robe
[2 Samuel] [6]:[15] as he and the whole house of IsraEl danced in front of the Chest of [Jehovah], shouting and blowing trumpets.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[16] But when the Chest reached the city of David, Michal (Saul’s daughter) happened to be watching from her window... And when she saw King David dancing and playing music before [Jehovah], in her heart she was disgusted.
[2 Samuel] [6]:[17] Then they brought the Chest of [Jehovah] in and set it in its place in the middle of the Tent that David had made for it, and David sacrificed whole burnt offerings and peace offerings there before [Jehovah].
[2 Samuel] [6]:[18] He also blest the people in the name of [Jehovah] of Armies,
[2 Samuel] [6]:[19] and he distributed bread loaves, grilled meat, and pancakes among all the people of IsraEl, both the men and the women, some of whom had come from as far way as Dan and BeerSheba. So after that, everyone went back home,
[2 Samuel] [6]:[20] and David returned to bless his own house... But when he got there, Michal (the daughter of Saul) came out to meet David and she started shouting at him. She asked: ‘So, how was the king of IsraEl glorified today as he danced naked in front of the daughters of his servants? ‘For you exposed yourself while you were dancing!’
[2 Samuel] [6]:[21] And David replied: ‘When I’m in the presence of [Jehovah], I’m going to dance! ‘May [Jehovah], who chose me over your father and his house, be praised for allowing me to take the lead over His people IsraEl. ‘I’ll [always] strum and dance in His presence,
[2 Samuel] [6]:[22] and I’ll be uncovered again in front of the girls – before whom you said I dishonored myself – so that I can become even more useless in your eyes!’
[2 Samuel] [6]:[23] Well, because she said this, Michal (the daughter of Saul) remained childless until the day that she died.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[1] It was after [Jehovah] had conquered all [of David’s] enemies roundabout him, that one day, as the king was sitting in his palace,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[2] he said to the prophet Nathan: ‘Look, here I am, living in a palace of cedars, while the Chest of God is just sitting there in a tent!’
[2 Samuel] [7]:[3] And Nathan said to the king: ‘Then, do whatever your heart moves you to do, because [Jehovah] is with you!’
[2 Samuel] [7]:[4] But that night, the word of the Lord came to Nathan, which said:
[2 Samuel] [7]:[5] ‘Go and speak to My servant David, and tell him that this is what [Jehovah] says: ‘You must not build a house for Me to dwell in,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[6] because I haven’t stayed in a house from the time that I led the sons of IsraEl out of Egypt until now. ‘Rather, I’ve been moving about in a tent
[2 Samuel] [7]:[7] in all the places where IsraEl has traveled.’ ‘Now, as you speak to him, ask him this: ‘Have I spoken to any of those whom I’ve assigned over My people, the tribes of IsraEl, and asked them to build a house of Cedars for Me?’
[2 Samuel] [7]:[8] ‘Then tell my servant David that [Jehovah] the Almighty says this: ‘I took you away from your sheep pens to be the leader over My people IsraEl,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[9] and wherever you went I’ve been with you... I’ve destroyed all your enemies and I’ve made your name famous among all the great men of the earth.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[10] ‘And now I’ll establish a place for my people IsraEl… I’ll plant it in a place where they’ll camp by themselves, and where they won’t have to worry anymore. ‘It’s a place where the sons of the unrighteousness won’t humble them as they did in ancient times,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[11] back when I put judges over My people IsraEl. And it’s only then, after I provide you with rest from all your enemies, that I’ll show you how to build a Temple for [Jehovah].
[2 Samuel] [7]:[12] ‘And after your days are finished and you’ve gone to sleep with your ancestors, I’ll raise up your offspring after you – someone who has come from within you – and I’ll prepare his kingdom.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[13] ‘He’s the one who’ll build a Temple to My Name, and I’ll establish his throne throughout the ages…
[2 Samuel] [7]:[14] I’ll be a father to him, and he will be a son to Me. ‘So, whenever he misbehaves, I’ll discipline him with the type of switch that men use, and spank him in the same way that the sons of men do [to their sons].
[2 Samuel] [7]:[15] ‘But I’ll never remove My mercy from him in the same way that I’ve removed My mercy from others.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[16] Rather, his house and his kingdom will stand before Me throughout the age, and his throne will last throughout the ages.’
[2 Samuel] [7]:[17] Well after that, Nathan went and spoke to David about all the words that he’d heard in the vision.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[18] Then King David went in and sat down before [Jehovah] and asked: ‘Just who am I, O my Lord [Jehovah], and what is my house that You’ve shown such love for me?
[2 Samuel] [7]:[19] ‘Even though I was once very small before You, O my Lord [Jehovah], You spoke about my house long ahead of time... So now, what laws are you giving to me, O my Lord,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[20] and what should David say before You? ‘You know Your servant, O my Lord [Jehovah],
[2 Samuel] [7]:[21] and You’ve treated Your servant as Your heart has directed…
[2 Samuel] [7]:[22] You’ve brought about all these great things to let your servant know that he should glorify You, O my Lord [Jehovah]; for there’s no one else like You, and we’ve heard of no God other than You.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[23] ‘And what are Your people IsraEl? For, no other nation on the earth is being guided by their God! ‘However, now You’ve purchased a people to establish Your Name and to show Your greatness and grandeur! You drove nations away in front of these people whom You purchased out of Egypt, and then You had them live in tents.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[24] ‘So, You’ve set aside IsraEl to be Your people throughout the ages… And You, O [Jehovah], have become their God!
[2 Samuel] [7]:[25] ‘And now, O my Lord [Jehovah], may the things that You said about Your servant and his house prove to be true throughout the ages, just as You said.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[26] ‘And may Your Name,
[2 Samuel] [7]:[27] [Jehovah] the Almighty God over IsraEl, be glorified throughout the ages! ‘For You’ve uncovered the ears of your servant and told me that I’ll build a Temple for You. This is why Your servant’s heart has been moved to speak this prayer to You.
[2 Samuel] [7]:[28] ‘And now, O my Lord; you are The God! ‘So, the words that You said about the good things that You’ll do for Your servant will prove to be true!
[2 Samuel] [7]:[29] Therefore, start blessing this house of Your servant, which will stand before You throughout the ages. ‘For You, O my Lord [Jehovah], have spoken, and You’ve promised to bless the house of your servant throughout the ages.’
[2 Samuel] [8]:[1] So after that, David attacked the Philistines and routed them, and he took back everything that [IsraEl] had lost to them.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[2] David also attacked [and captured] MoAb, and he divided their army into two lines as they lay on the ground. Half were to be killed and the rest were to survive. Then the MoAbites became David’s servants and they were required to pay him a tribute.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[3] Next, David attacked HadraAzar (son of RaAb) the king of Soba as he was marching towards the Euphrates River...
[2 Samuel] [8]:[4] There David captured 1,000 chariots, 7,000 of his cavalry, and 20,000 of his foot soldiers! Then David had all the chariots destroyed, except for 100 that he kept for himself.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[5] And when the Syrians came from Damascus to help HadraAzar (the king of Soba), David cut down 22,000 of their men!
[2 Samuel] [8]:[6] Then David sent a detachment to Syria, where they garrisoned near Damascus, and the Syrians had to pay a tribute to David also. So, [Jehovah] was with David wherever he went.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[7] Well, David took the gold armlets that the sons of HadraAzar wore and brought them to JeruSalem. However, these were eventually taken by SusAkim [possibly Amenemope] the king of Egypt, when he attacked JeruSalem during the reign of RehoBoam, son of Solomon.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[8] Then David attacked HadraAzar’s principal cities and he brought back huge amounts of brass, which was thereafter used by Solomon to create the Temple's sacred Brass Sea, its columns, its bathing tubs, and all its utensils.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[9] Well when the king of HaMath heard that David had conquered the armies of HadraAzar,
[2 Samuel] [8]:[10] he sent his son JedDouran to King David to sue for peace. He also congratulated David for beating HadraAzar (since HadraAzar was his enemy), and he brought along many items of silver, gold, and brass,
[2 Samuel] [8]:[11] which King David dedicated to [Jehovah], as he’d done with all the silver and gold that he’d taken from the cities that he’d conquered,
[2 Samuel] [8]:[12] [which were] those of: Edom, MoAb, The sons of AmMon, The Philistines, The AmaLechites, From the spoils of HadraAzar son of RaAb, the king of Soba.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[13] Well, after he did that, David became quite famous… And then on his return, he attacked the Idumeans in the Salt Valley, killing 18,000.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[14] Then he put detachments throughout all of Idumea, and the Idumeans became the king’s servants. Well, no matter where he went, [Jehovah] was with David,
[2 Samuel] [8]:[15] and he remained the ruler over all IsraEl; for he was fair and just with his people.
[2 Samuel] [8]:[16] [At the time:] JoAb (son of ZeruJah) was in charge of his army. JoShaphat (son of AchiAd) was in charge of the records.

[2 Samuel] [12]:[1] As a result, [Jehovah] sent the prophet Nathan to David, who went in and told him this story: ‘There were two men who lived in the same city; one was rich, and the other was poor.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[2] ‘Now, the rich man had huge flocks and herds,
[2 Samuel] [12]:[3] but the only thing that the poor man owned was a small female lamb that he’d purchased... He protected it and fed it, and it grew up with his children. It ate the same bread, drank from his cup, and slept inside of his robe; for it was just like a daughter to him!
[2 Samuel] [12]:[4] ‘Well, it so happened that a traveler came along who stopped in to see the rich man. Then, because he didn’t want to take anything from his own flocks or herds to prepare [a meal] for a stranger, he took the lamb that belonged to the poor man and prepared it for the person who had come to visit.’
[2 Samuel] [12]:[5] Well, when he heard this, David was outraged and he said: ‘As [Jehovah] lives, that man deserves to die!
[2 Samuel] [12]:[6] ‘He should also have to pay for the lamb with 7 of his own, because of this evil thing that he did!’
[2 Samuel] [12]:[7] And Nathan said to David: ‘But, you are the man who did this! ‘So, [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl told me to say this to you: ‘I’m the One who anointed you to be the king over IsraEl, and I’m the One who saved you from the hands of Saul.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[8] ‘I’m also the One who gave you the house of your lord and I brought his women to your chest; and thereafter I gave you the houses of IsraEl and Judah... And if you had remained faithful, I would have given you even more!
[2 Samuel] [12]:[9] ‘So, why have you treated the Word of [Jehovah] as worthless by doing this wicked thing before His eyes? For you cut down UriAh the Hittite with the broadsword and took his woman as yours… When the sons of AmMon killed him, it was really you who killed him!
[2 Samuel] [12]:[10] ‘And because you did this, the broadsword won’t leave your house throughout the ages! For you treated Me with contempt by taking the wife of UriAh the Hittite as your woman.’
[2 Samuel] [12]:[11] ‘And [Jehovah] also said this: ‘Look, I will cause evil things to awaken in your own house… I will take your women from before you and give them to your neighbor, then he will go to bed with them in the daylight.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[12] ‘Although you did it in secret, I will do this in the daylight and before all IsraEl!’
[2 Samuel] [12]:[13] Well at that, David said to Nathan: ‘I have truly sinned against [Jehovah]!’ And Nathan said to David: ‘Well, [Jehovah] has forgiven your sin, so you’re not going to die...
[2 Samuel] [12]:[14] However, by doing such an unrighteous thing, you’ve even made [Jehovah’s] enemies angry. ‘Therefore, the son who’ll be born to you will die.’

[2 Samuel] [12]:[19] Well, David noticed that his servants had been whispering, and he suspected that the boy had died. So he asked his servants: ‘Has the boy died?’ And they replied: ‘He has.’
[2 Samuel] [12]:[20] Then David got up from the ground, took a bath, rubbed himself with oil, and changed his clothes. And thereafter, he went to the [Tent] of God and bowed before Him. And when he got back home, he asked for some food to eat, which they brought to him, and which he ate.
[2 Samuel] [12]:[21] So his servants asked: ‘Why have you acted this way concerning the boy? ‘For while he was still alive you fasted, cried, and wouldn’t sleep, but after he died, you got up and ate and drank something.’
[2 Samuel] [12]:[22] And David replied: ‘I fasted and cried while the boy was still living, because I hoped that [Jehovah] would show mercy on me and allow the boy to live.
