[1 Kings] [3]:[1] Well, under Solomon, the kingdom was united. Then Solomon contracted a marriage with PharaOh, the king of Egypt... He took PharaOh’s daughter and brought her to the city of David. He did this after he’d finished building his palace, the Temple of [Jehovah], and after building the wall around JeruSalem.
[1 Kings] [3]:[2] Now, before the Temple was built, the people had been burning incense [to [Jehovah]] in the high places.
[1 Kings] [3]:[3] And since Solomon loved [Jehovah] (and because he was following the orders of his father David), he also offered his sacrifices and burned incense there.
[1 Kings] [3]:[4] So Solomon then got up and went to offer sacrifices at GibeOn (since that was the highest place at the time). There he had 1,000 whole burnt offerings placed on the Altar.
[1 Kings] [3]:[5] And then the Lord appeared to Solomon while he was sleeping that night, and said to him: ‘Solomon, ‘Ask for whatever you wish for yourself.’
[1 Kings] [3]:[6] So Solomon replied: ‘You’ve shown great mercy to your servant, my father David, and he walked with You in truth, justice, and with a pure heart... Then You guarded him and showed him great mercy by allowing his son, to sit upon his throne, which has come true today.
[1 Kings] [3]:[7] ‘And now, O [Jehovah] my God; although You have appointed Your servant in place of my father David, I’m still just a boy that doesn’t know when to enter or when to leave!
[1 Kings] [3]:[8] ‘Yet Your servant [now rules] in the midst of this mighty [nation] that You’ve chosen, which has [so many people] that they can’t be counted...
[1 Kings] [3]:[9] Therefore, please give your servant a heart to listen so as to make [wise] decisions for Your people in justice, and to recognize the difference between what’s good and what’s bad. ‘For, who could possibly bear the weight of such judgments?’
[1 Kings] [3]:[10] Well, this thing that Solomon asked of [Jehovah] was pleasing to Him,
[1 Kings] [3]:[11] so He replied: ‘Because you’ve asked this thing from Me and you didn’t ask for a long life, or for wealth, or for the lives of your enemies, and all you asked for yourself is the understanding to judge righteously...
[1 Kings] [3]:[12] {Look!} I’ve done what you asked! '{Look!} I’m giving you an intelligent and wise heart… There has never been anyone before you, nor will there ever be anyone who shall arise after you who’ll be like you!
[1 Kings] [3]:[13] ‘And I’m also giving you the things that you didn’t ask for… Including wealth and glory; for there’s never been a king like you.
[1 Kings] [3]:[14] ‘And if you’ll do things My way and obey My Commandments and instructions as did your father David, I’ll also grant you a long life.’
[1 Kings] [3]:[15] Well, after Solomon awoke, he remembered the dream. So he got up and returned to JeruSalem; and there he went and stood before the Altar that was in front of the Chest of the Sacred Agreement of [Jehovah] in Zion. Then he sacrificed whole burnt offerings and peace offerings, and he held a great banquet for himself and for all his servants.
[1 Kings] [3]:[16] It was sometime later that two women who were prostitutes came to stand before the king for a [judgment].
[1 Kings] [3]:[17] One of the women said: ‘Hear me, my lord! ‘This woman and I both live in the same house and we both gave birth to [sons] there...
[1 Kings] [3]:[18] It was three days after I gave birth that this woman also gave birth in the same place while no one else was around… There was just the two of us in the house.
[1 Kings] [3]:[19] ‘Then this woman’s son died during the night when she rolled over on top of him!
[1 Kings] [3]:[20] So she got up in the middle of the night and took my son from my arms and put him to her breasts; then she took her son who’d died and laid him at my breasts!
[1 Kings] [3]:[21] ‘Well, when I got up in the morning to nurse my son, I saw the one who had died... But I studied him, and then I realized that this wasn’t my son to whom I’d given birth.’
[1 Kings] [3]:[22] But then the other woman shouted: ‘That isn’t true! ‘The living one is my son, and the dead one is hers!’
[1 Kings] [3]:[23] Then the king said to her: ‘So you’re saying that the living son is yours, and the dead one is hers... And she’s saying that isn’t true; hers is the living son, and yours is the one who is dead.’
[1 Kings] [3]:[24] Then the king said: ‘Now, bring me a sword!’ And they brought him a sword.
[1 Kings] [3]:[25] Then he said: ‘Cut this living, nursing child in halves, and give half to this one and the other half to that one.’
[1 Kings] [3]:[26] Well, the real mother of the living son spoke to the king, because she was disturbed to the womb about what was going to happen to her son! So she said: ‘Hear me, O lord! ‘Give the child to her… Don’t kill him!’ But the other [woman] said: ‘May he be neither mine nor hers… ‘Cut him in two!’
[1 Kings] [3]:[27] Then the king said: ‘I’m giving the child to the woman who said, ‘Give it to her, don’t kill him,’ because she’s his mother.’
[1 Kings] [3]:[28] Well, all IsraEl soon came to hear of this decision of the king, and they were in fear whenever they were in his presence! For they knew that the intelligence of God was in him, and that justice would prevail.
[1 Kings] [4]:[1] Back when King Solomon was reigning in IsraEl,
[1 Kings] [4]:[2] these are the men who were with him and that were in charge: AzariAh (son of ZaDok) was the [High] Priest.
[1 Kings] [4]:[3] EliAm and AhiJah (the sons of Saba) were his scribes. JehoShaphat (the son AchiLud) was the recorder.
[1 Kings] [4]:[4] BenaiJah (son of JehoiAda) was the commander-in-chief of the army. ZaDok and AbiAthar were the Priests.
[1 Kings] [4]:[5] AzariAh (son of Nathan) directed his staff. ZaboUth (son of Nathan) was the king’s right-hand man.
[1 Kings] [4]:[6] AciSar was his manager. EliAb (son of Saph) was over his family. AdoniRam (son of AphDon) was in charge of the tributes.
[1 Kings] [4]:[7] So Solomon assigned 12 men over all IsraEl to handle matters for him and his house.
[1 Kings] [4]:[8] Then there were others who were assigned to [bring the things that Solomon required] for just 1 month each year, and these are their names: The son of Or was responsible in the mountains of Ephraim.
[1 Kings] [4]:[9] The son of DaKar was responsible in MachEmas, SalaBin, BethSamus, AiLon, and BethAnan.
[1 Kings] [4]:[10] The son of Esdi was responsible in ArabOth, SochOth, and all the land of Opher.
[1 Kings] [4]:[11] The son of AmiNadab (who was married to Solomon’s daughter) was responsible in all of NephthaDor and TephAth.
[1 Kings] [4]:[12] BaAna (son of AchiLouth) was responsible in IthAnak, MegidDo, and over the whole house of San near SesaThan and below EsraE, from BethSan to SebelMaula, to MaEber and Lucam.
[1 Kings] [4]:[13] The son of Gaber from GileAd was over a piece of measured land around EreGaba (which is in BaShan) and which included 60 great walled cities that were [protected by] bronze bars.
[1 Kings] [4]:[14] AchiNadab (son of SadDo) was responsible in MaAnaim.
[1 Kings] [4]:[15] AchimaAs (who was married to Solomon’s daughter BasEmath) was responsible in [the land of] NaphTali.
[1 Kings] [4]:[16] BaAnah (son of HushAi) was in charge of BaAlOth and [the land of] Asher.
[1 Kings] [4]:[17] JehoShaphat (son of ParuAh) was responsible in [the land of] IsSachar.
[1 Kings] [4]:[18] Shemei (son of ElAh) was responsible in [the land of] BenJamin.
[1 Kings] [4]:[19] Gaber (son of AdAi) was responsible in the land of GileAd, [the land of] King SeOn of HeshBon, [the land of] King Og of BaShan, and [the land of] NaSeb (in the land of Judah).
[1 Kings] [4]:[20] Now, Judah and IsraEl had grown so large that [their people] were as the sands of the seas in number, and they all ate, drank, and rejoiced;
[1 Kings] [4]:[21] for Solomon was the ruler in all their kingdoms from the river in the land of the Philistines to the borders of Egypt. They also brought Solomon many gifts, and they served him throughout all the days of his life.
[1 Kings] [4]:[22] These are the things that Solomon required at his table each day: 200 bushels of fine flour, 400 bushels of beaten flour,
[1 Kings] [4]:[23] 10 choice calves, 20 grass-fed oxen, 100 sheep, plus Well-fed male and female antelope.
[1 Kings] [4]:[24] Solomon was also the ruler of all the land on the [east] side of the [Jordan], and there was peace throughout the whole country.
[1 Kings] [4]:[25] [So, during all the days of Solomon, the people] in Judah and IsraEl (from Dan to BeerSheba) harvested their own grapevines and [lived] under their own fig trees.
[1 Kings] [4]:[26] During his lifetime, Solomon had gathered some 40,000 breeding horses for his chariots and 12,000 more for his cavalry.
[1 Kings] [4]:[27] Those whom he put in charge brought the required things to the king’s table (each one in his own month) did just as they were told and they didn’t change a word...
[1 Kings] [4]:[28] They brought barley and hay for the horses, and they took the chariots wherever the king needed them and arranged for them to be.
[1 Kings] [4]:[29] Well, [Jehovah] gave intelligence and great wisdom to Solomon, and it kept growing in his heart like the sands of the seas!
[1 Kings] [4]:[30] Solomon’s intelligence grew greater than that of all the men of ancient times, including all the wise men of Egypt…
[1 Kings] [4]:[31] His understanding was greater than everyone, so he was wiser than GaitThan the Zarite, or AiNan, or ChalKal, or DarDa (the sons of Mal).
[1 Kings] [4]:[32] [During his lifetime], Solomon spoke 3,000 parables and he [wrote] 5,000 songs!
[1 Kings] [4]:[33] He spoke of the cedars of Lebanon, of the hyssop, and of [plants that grow] through walls. He spoke about cattle, flying creatures, things that crawl, and about things that live in the water…
[1 Kings] [4]:[34] And people from everywhere on the earth would come to hear the wisdom of Solomon. Also, all their kings, when they heard of his wisdom, would bring him gifts.
[1 Kings] [5]:[1] Then King HiRam [I] of Tyre sent his servants to anoint Solomon in place of his father David; for HiRam loved David throughout his whole life.
[1 Kings] [5]:[2] And Solomon sent [a message] to HiRam, saying:
[1 Kings] [5]:[3] ‘You know that my father David was unable to build a Temple to the Name of my God [Jehovah], because he was fighting the wars that were going on around him, until [Jehovah] finally put his enemies under the soles of his feet.
[1 Kings] [5]:[4] ‘And now, my God [Jehovah] has provided rest for me all around [my land], for there are no more plotters or wicked people anywhere near me...
[1 Kings] [5]:[5] So now I’m talking about building a Temple to the Name of my God who once said to my father David: ‘Your son whom I’ll put on your throne after you will build a Temple to My Name.’
[1 Kings] [5]:[6] ‘Therefore, please have your men cut some timber for me from the trees in Lebanon, and I’ll pay whatever you ask for their wages... {Look!} I’ll also send my servants to go with your servants; for no one understands timber cutting better than the Sidonians!’
[1 Kings] [5]:[7] Well, when HiRam received Solomon’s message, he was overjoyed and said: ‘May the God who gave David such an intelligent son to rule over this great people be praised today!’
[1 Kings] [5]:[8] So he sent [a message] to Solomon replying: ‘I’ve heard everything that you asked of me, and I’ll send all the pine and cedar lumber that you’ve requested!
[1 Kings] [5]:[9] My servants will cut it in Lebanon then carry it to the sea and haul it all on barges to wherever you tell me to drop it off… You can carry it on from there. ‘All I ask from you in return, is that you send me some loaves of bread for my house.’
[1 Kings] [5]:[10] So HiRam gave Solomon all the cedars and pines that he wanted,
[1 Kings] [5]:[11] and Solomon sent HiRam 130,000 bushels of wheat and 120,000 gallons (450,000l) of beaten olive oil for his house. In fact, he sent that amount to HiRam every year after that!
[1 Kings] [5]:[12] Well, [Jehovah] gave Solomon all the wisdom that he’d asked for, and there was peace between HiRam and Solomon, for they’d concluded a treaty between themselves.
[1 Kings] [5]:[13] And the king sent him (as a tribute from all IsraEl) 30,000 men…
[1 Kings] [5]:[14] He would send 10,000 of them to Lebanon each month in rotation, and they’d thereafter spend a month in Lebanon and 2 months at home. AdoniRam was the person whom he’d put in charge of this tribute.
[1 Kings] [5]:[15] Meanwhile, Solomon had 70,000 laborers and 80,000 stonecutters [working] in the mountains...
[1 Kings] [5]:[16] And in addition to those whom Solomon placed in charge of his construction project, he had 3,600 supervisors on the job,
[1 Kings] [5]:[17] whom the king had instructed to set huge, valuable stone blocks in place as the foundations for the building.
[1 Kings] [5]:[18] Also, the sons of Solomon and HiRam [were in charge of] assembling everything after all the blocks and timbers had been cut (which took three years).
[1 Kings] [6]:[1] It was 400 and [80] years after the sons of IsraEl had left Egypt (in the 4th year and 2nd month of King Solomon’s reign over IsraEl) that the Temple of [Jehovah] [began construction].
[1 Kings] [6]:[2] It was [going to be]: 90 feet (27.4m) long, 30 feet (9.1m) wide, and 30 feet (9.1m) tall.
[1 Kings] [6]:[3] The Temple had a columned front entryway that was about 30 feet (9.1m) deep and it was as wide as the building.
[1 Kings] [6]:[4] There was also a window in the Temple that was hidden, because it leaned inward...
[1 Kings] [6]:[5] And there was an eve along [the top] of the wall that ran all the way around the Temple Sanctuary to the entryway. He then built side [rooms] around the structure.
[1 Kings] [6]:[6] The lowest [part of the] side [room] was 7-1/2 feet (2.3m) wide, the one in the middle was 9 feet (2.75m) wide, and the one at the [top] was 10-1/2 feet (3.2m) wide... He built the rooms around the Temple on the outside, so they wouldn’t touch the Temple walls.
[1 Kings] [6]:[7] The Temple was constructed from rough-chiseled stone; for the sound of hammers, axes, and other metal tools wasn’t to be heard during its construction.
[1 Kings] [6]:[8] There was a vestibule that was attached to the right side of the bottom room of the building, which had a winding stairway in the middle that led up to the third story.
[1 Kings] [6]:[9] Then, after the [exterior] was built, Solomon had the [interior walls] covered with cedar [panels].
[1 Kings] [6]:[10] He also built the interior chamber in the middle of the Temple, which stood 7-1/2 feet (2.3m) high, and it was held together with cedar beams.
[1 Kings] [6]:[11] Thereafter, [Jehovah] sent word to Solomon, saying:
[1 Kings] [6]:[12] ‘Regarding this Temple that you’re building for Me... If you’ll follow My instructions and decisions, and obey all My Commandments, the thing that I said to your father David will prove true;
[1 Kings] [6]:[13] I will camp in the midst of the sons of IsraEl, and I won’t abandon My people IsraEl.’
[1 Kings] [6]:[14] Well after that, Solomon went on to finish the Temple.
[1 Kings] [6]:[15] He covered all its interior walls with cedar panels, from its floors to its beams. It was vaulted with timbers on the inside, and the walls were ribbed with pine.
[1 Kings] [6]:[16] So inside, the measurement from the floor to the ceiling beams was 30 feet (9.1m). And inside the entryway, he built the Holy of Holies.
[1 Kings] [6]:[17] However, the Temple Sanctuary itself was 60 feet (18.3m) in front of the entrance.
[1 Kings] [6]:[18] Now, the interior cedar panels were all carved with decorations of gourds and spread leaves, and none of the stonework could be seen from the inside.
[1 Kings] [6]:[19] Also, [they made] the entrance within in the center of the Temple, to make a place to hold the Chest of the Sacred Agreement of [Jehovah].
[1 Kings] [6]:[20] That room was 30 feet (9.1m) long, 30 feet (9.1m) wide, and 30 feet (9.1m) tall, and it was totally enclosed and covered in gold.
[1 Kings] [6]:[21] Then he built an Altar in front of the entrance and he covered it with gold.
[1 Kings] [6]:[22] In fact, by the time of its completion, the whole Temple [interior] was covered with gold!
[1 Kings] [6]:[23] He also made two wooden cherubs of cypress, which he placed in the entrance. These stood 15 feet (4.6m) tall,
[1 Kings] [6]:[24] each of their wings were 7-1/2 feet (2.3m) long, and the distance from wing-tip to wing-tip was 15 feet (4.5m).
[1 Kings] [6]:[25] Both of these cherubs were the same size.
[1 Kings] [6]:[26] He [also made] a 17-foot (5.2m) tall cherub, along with a second one, and he placed these in the innermost part of the Temple.
[1 Kings] [6]:[27] They too had spread wings that touched each other and ran to the walls on either side of the building’s interior.
[1 Kings] [6]:[28] These cherubs were also covered in gold,
[1 Kings] [6]:[29] and the walls around the Temple were engraved with cherubs and palms… Both the innermost and outermost portions.
[1 Kings] [6]:[30] And he even covered the floors of the whole building with gold… Both the innermost portions and the outermost portions.
[1 Kings] [6]:[31] For the entrance doorway, he made doors of juniper wood. Now, there were [a total of] 5 doorways...
[1 Kings] [6]:[32] Two of the doors were made of pines that were carved with cherubs and palms, panels that could open and spread out. And everything was covered with gold, including the engraved cherubs and palms.
[1 Kings] [6]:[33] The Temple Sanctuary vestibule had juniper doorposts and 4 columns.
[1 Kings] [6]:[34] Both of the doors were made of pine, and they were hinged into a bi-fold configuration.
[1 Kings] [6]:[35] They also had panels that were carved with cherubs and palm leaves, and then they were entirely covered in gold.
[1 Kings] [6]:[36] Thereafter, [Solomon] built the inner courtyard... It had three rows of uncut stones who were surrounded by cedar posts.
[1 Kings] [6]:[37] So, it was in the 4th year [of his reign], during the month of Ziv, that the Temple foundation was laid...
[1 Kings] [6]:[38] And it was in the 11th year and the 8th month (Bul) that the Temple was finally completed per [Solomon’s] instructions and design. So he took 7 years to build it.
[1 Kings] [7]:[1] Then over the next 13 years, Solomon finished building his palace,
[1 Kings] [7]:[2] which was also constructed of wood from the forests of Lebanon. It was: 150 feet (45.7m) long, 75 feet (22.8m) wide, 40 feet (12.2m) tall, and It had 4 rows of cedar columns that ran up to cedar rafters.
[1 Kings] [7]:[3] The whole building was decorated with latticework on the upper parts of the columns, and there were 45 columns in rows of fives and tens.
[1 Kings] [7]:[4] There were also three windows on each of three sides, to provide lighting,
[1 Kings] [7]:[5] and the windows and doorways were four-cornered, with arches over the three doorways.
[1 Kings] [7]:[6] The palace had a columned entryway that was 75 feet (22.8m) long and 40 feet (12.2m) wide, which had a porch in front with columns and thick beams.
[1 Kings] [7]:[7] This was where [Solomon’s] throne was located and where he did his judging. There was a [special] columned porch for his judgment seat,
[1 Kings] [7]:[8] and then there was a courtyard in front of the place where he sat, which could be expanded whenever needed. He also built a house for the daughter of PharaOh whom he’d taken as his woman, which looked a lot like his columned porch.
[1 Kings] [7]:[9] Everything was constructed of valuable stones that had been chiseled at intervals on the insides (from the foundations to the windows) and on the outsides, up to the great courtyard.
[1 Kings] [7]:[10] The foundation was constructed of valuable stones that were each 12 feet (3.65m) by 15 feet (4.6m) wide,
[1 Kings] [7]:[11] and the roof was made of valuable stones of the same size, which were mounted over cedar beams.
[1 Kings] [7]:[12] In addition, there was also a large courtyard that was circled by three rows of uncut stones and a row of carved cedar posts... It was built much like the courtyard and the columned porch at the Temple of [Jehovah].
[1 Kings] [7]:[13] Solomon had called for HiRam at Tyre
[1 Kings] [7]:[14] (who was a widow’s son from the tribe of NaphTali and his father was a Tyranian man); for he was gifted when it came to working bronze (as well as at other crafts), and he was filled with knowledge on how to do all sorts of metalwork. So he was brought to King Solomon, because he was able to do everything that needed to be done.
[1 Kings] [7]:[15] It was [HiRam] who smelted and cast the two columns for the Temple’s columned porch. They were both 24 feet (7.3m) tall, 18 feet (5.5m) in circumference, and grooved to a depth of 4 fingers.
[1 Kings] [7]:[16] He also molded two bronze capitals for the tops of the columns that were each 7-1/2 feet (2.3m) tall.
[1 Kings] [7]:[17] Then he made bronze decorations for each capital,
[1 Kings] [7]:[18] which consisted of rows of hanging pomegranates,
[1 Kings] [7]:[19] and the top of each column was shaped like a lily. Thereafter, he finished off the columns for the porch with a ridge that ran between the capitals. It was 6 feet (1.8m) wide
[1 Kings] [7]:[20] and it was covered with 200 rows of pomegranates.
[1 Kings] [7]:[21] He then erected these columns at the columned porch of the Temple Sanctuary, and he named one column JaKin, and the other BoAz.
[1 Kings] [7]:[22] He also topped [the rest of] the columns with [bronze] lilies. And with that, he finally finished his work on the columns.
[1 Kings] [7]:[23] Next, he cast the [Sacred] Sea. It was round and 15 feet (4.6m) wide from rim to rim. It was 7-1/2 feet (2.3m) tall and [about] 45 feet (13.7m) in circumference.
[1 Kings] [7]:[24] The base beneath it was 15 feet (4.6m) wide, and it was made of 2 rows of supports that were cast in a foundry furnace.
[1 Kings] [7]:[25] The Sea itself was supported by 12 metal oxen, three of which faced north, three faced west, three faced south, and three faced east... The Sea was then placed on top of them,
[1 Kings] [7]:[26] and of course, all the posteriors faced inward. The middle of the Sea was shaped like a palm, but its rim was like that of a cup, with lily buds around the top. It had a capacity of about 1,100 gallons (4,100l).
[1 Kings] [7]:[27] Then [HiRam] made 10 bronze carts. They were each 6 feet (1.8m) long, 6 feet (1.8m) wide, and 4-1/2 feet (1.4m) tall.
[1 Kings] [7]:[28] The carts were made of panels that were joined into frames
[1 Kings] [7]:[29] that were [engraved with] lions, oxen, and cherubs. In fact, lions, oxen, and cherubs covered all parts of the carts, including their bases.
[1 Kings] [7]:[30] Each of the carts had 4 bronze wheels, and all their fastenings were made of brass. Then, coming up from the base were 4 supports that held the washtubs, each of which were 20 inches (50cm) long.
[1 Kings] [7]:[31] [The tub supports] were round, 2 feet (60cm) wide at the top, and they were covered with engravings. However, the 4 supports were rectangular, not round.
[1 Kings] [7]:[32] There were bronze wheels mounted at the base of the supports, and the wheels each had spokes that were 2 feet long…
[1 Kings] [7]:[33] In fact, they looked like chariot wheels. And all the spokes were joined to cast axels.
[1 Kings] [7]:[34] There were supports that stuck out at the corners of each of the cart’s bases as handles,
[1 Kings] [7]:[35] and they were mounted along the top of each base. They were 9 inches (23cm) around and stood high enough [to serve as] handholds.
[1 Kings] [7]:[36] All these connecting parts [were carved] with cherubs, lions, and palms that were standing next to each other on the front, on the inside, and all around.
[1 Kings] [7]:[37] He made all 10 carts exactly alike and to the same dimensions.
[1 Kings] [7]:[38] Then he made the 10 bronze washtubs. They each held 230 gallons (870l) [of water], and they were 8 feet (2.4m) long. Each of the washtubs was then mounted on a cart.
[1 Kings] [7]:[39] 5 were placed on the Temple’s right side, and the other 5 on its left side. The [Sacred] Sea was placed to the right of the Temple, on its southeast corner.
[1 Kings] [7]:[40] Next, HiRam made the cooking pots, the tongs, and the bowls.
[1 Kings] [7]:[41] And soon he’d completed making all the things for King Solomon at the Temple of [Jehovah]… The two columns, the twisted decorations that were put on the capitals of the two columns, the carvings for the tops of the columns,
[1 Kings] [7]:[42] and the pomegranates (400 of which were used as decorations). Two rows of [pomegranates] were put on each column, and the rest were used as decorations
[1 Kings] [7]:[43] for the carts, the metal washtubs that were mounted on them, and their axels, rims, and spokes, as well as for
[1 Kings] [7]:[44] the [Sacred] Sea and its 12 oxen that supported it,
[1 Kings] [7]:[45] and for the cooking pots, tongs, and bowls. He [personally] made all these things for King Solomon and for the Temple of [Jehovah]. Altogether, he [decorated] 48 columns for the palace of the king and for the Temple of [Jehovah]. And everything that HiRam made for the king was entirely of bronze.
[1 Kings] [7]:[46] He did all his casting near the Jordan River, underground, in a place that was located between SokChoth and ZarEthan.
[1 Kings] [7]:[47] Solomon already had all the materials stored away, since he’d received so much bronze.
[1 Kings] [7]:[48] Then Solomon went on to make the rest of the items [used] in the Temple of [Jehovah]… The gold Altar, the gold table for the showbread,
[1 Kings] [7]:[49] the solid-gold lampstands that were placed at the entrance (5 on the right side and 5 on the left side), as well as their gold bowls, lamps, and oil funnels,
[1 Kings] [7]:[50] plus the gold thresholds, fasteners, bowls, saucers, and incense pans. The doorways for the Temple’s doors to the innermost [room] (the Holy of Holies) and the doors of the Temple’s Inner Sanctuary were [both covered with] gold.
[1 Kings] [7]:[51] So, Solomon finally finished all his work for [Jehovah’s] Temple. Then he carried in all of his father David’s holy things, plus all of his own holy things, including much silver and gold, and other things for the treasury of the Temple of [Jehovah].
[1 Kings] [8]:[1] Thereafter, King Solomon held a meeting of all the elders of IsraEl there on [Mount] Zion, to talk about bringing the Chest of the Sacred Agreement of [Jehovah] out of the city of David (which was on Mount Zion).
[1 Kings] [8]:[2] This was in the month of Athanim (the 7th month), and because it was a holiday, all the elders of IsraEl were already there.
[1 Kings] [8]:[3] Then the Priests removed the Chest
[1 Kings] [8]:[4] from the Tent of Proofs (along with all the holy items that were there),
[1 Kings] [8]:[5] and the king and all IsraEl stood before the Chest and sacrificed multitudes of oxen and sheep.
[1 Kings] [8]:[6] Thereafter, the Priests carried the Chest and put it into its place inside the Holy of Holies (which was near the entrance of the Temple) under the wings of the cherubs
[1 Kings] [8]:[7] (for the cherubs had open, spread wings that covered the Chest and the other holy things that were on its lid).
[1 Kings] [8]:[8] And the only parts that stuck out of the Holy [of Holies] were the sacred carrying poles… But even these couldn’t be seen from outside [the Temple].
[1 Kings] [8]:[9] Of course, there was nothing in the Chest except the two stone tablets of the Sacred Agreement that [Jehovah] made with the sons of IsraEl after they had left the land of Egypt, and which were put there by Moses at the Dry Place (Horeb).
[1 Kings] [8]:[10] Well, as the Priests were coming out of the Holy Place, a mist then filled the whole building!
[1 Kings] [8]:[11] So the Priests were unable to stand and officiate before the mist, because the glory of [Jehovah] filled the whole Temple!
[1 Kings] [8]:[12] Then Solomon said this concerning the Temple after he’d completed its construction: ‘[Jehovah] made the sun in the sky, and [yet] said he would live in a dimly-lit place.
[1 Kings] [8]:[13] ‘[He said:] ‘You [must] build a House for me.’ ‘[Yes,] a good, brand-new house for you to live in! ‘Look! Isn’t this written in the song scroll?’
[1 Kings] [8]:[14] Then he turned around, and all IsraEl started praising the king; for the whole gathering of IsraEl was standing there.
[1 Kings] [8]:[15] And [the king] said: ‘Praise [Jehovah], the God of IsraEl, who spoke with His mouth about my father David, and that filled his hands, saying: ‘From the day that I led My people IsraEl out of Egypt, I had never chosen a city [for Myself] in one of the chiefdoms of IsraEl where a Temple would be built to My Name.
[1 Kings] [8]:[16] But now, I’ve chosen JeruSalem as the place to put My Name, and I’ve chosen David to lead My people IsraEl.’
[1 Kings] [8]:[17] And that’s why the heart of my father David was moved to build a Temple to the Name of [Jehovah], the God of IsraEl.
[1 Kings] [8]:[18] ‘Then the Lord said to my father David: ‘Because your heart was moved to build a Temple to My Name, you’ve done a good thing, since it came from your heart!
[1 Kings] [8]:[19] However, you may not personally build the Temple… It will be built by a son who comes from you.’ ‘He will build the Temple to My Name.’
[1 Kings] [8]:[20] ‘So [Jehovah] caused these things that He spoke of, to happen. I replaced my father David and sat down on the throne of IsraEl, just as [Jehovah] said... ‘And now I’ve built the Temple to the Name of the Lord God of IsraEl.
[1 Kings] [8]:[21] ‘I’ve also created a place for the Chest that contains the Sacred Agreement that [Jehovah] made with our ancestors when He led them out of the land of Egypt.’
[1 Kings] [8]:[22] Then Solomon stood before the Altar of [Jehovah], there in front of the whole gathering of IsraEl, and he raised his arms towards heaven,
[1 Kings] [8]:[23] and said: ‘O [Jehovah], God of IsraEl, ‘There are no gods in the skies above or on the earth below who are like You. ‘For You’ve kept Your promise and shown mercy to Your servant… The one who has walked before You with his whole heart, Your servant David, my father.
[1 Kings] [8]:[24] ‘You spoke to him with Your mouth, and with Your hands, You’ve fulfilled what [You promised to him].
[1 Kings] [8]:[25] ‘And now, O [Jehovah], God of IsraEl, ‘Keep [the promise] that You made with my father David when You said: ‘There will always be a man who sits before Me on the throne of IsraEl for as long as your children continue to follow Me the same as you have followed Me.’
[1 Kings] [8]:[26] ‘So now, O [Jehovah], God of IsraEl, ‘May the words that You said to my father David prove to be true.
[1 Kings] [8]:[27] ‘However, will You really live on the earth with men, when the heavens of the heavens can’t contain You? Therefore, how can this Temple that I built to Your Name expect to do so?
[1 Kings] [8]:[28] ‘Please listen to my prayer, O [Jehovah], God of IsraEl… Hear the prayer that Your servant is praying before You today!
[1 Kings] [8]:[29] ‘May Your eyes watch over this Temple both day and night... For it’s the place where You said that You’d put Your Name. ‘Then from Your home in the heavens, please listen to the prayers that Your servants will pray in this place both day and night,
[1 Kings] [8]:[30] and provide the things for which Your servant and all Your people IsraEl will ask when they pray here… ‘Answer them and provide!
[1 Kings] [8]:[31] ‘And if they should sin against their neighbors by vowing an oath to curse them, and then they come and openly confess such a thing before Your Altar in this Temple,
[1 Kings] [8]:[32] may You listen from the heavens and act… Judge Your people IsraEl! ‘Declare the lawless one lawlessness and bring his [evil] ways down upon his own head; but, give justice to the righteous… Treat the righteous with righteousness!
[1 Kings] [8]:[33] ‘And when Your people IsraEl sin against You; may they fall before their enemies until they return and acknowledge Your Name, and then pray and beg before You in this Temple.
[1 Kings] [8]:[34] ‘Please listen to them from the heavens and forgive the sins of Your people IsraEl, and return them to this land that You gave to their ancestors.
[1 Kings] [8]:[35] ‘And when You hold back the sky and don’t allow rain to fall because of their sins against You, and then they come to pray in this place and acknowledge Your Name and turn away from their sins after You’ve humbled them...
[1 Kings] [8]:[36] ‘Please listen from the heavens and forgive the sins of Your servants… Your people IsraEl. Show them a better way to act, and then provide rain for this land that You’ve given to Your people as their inheritance.
[1 Kings] [8]:[37] ‘And if there should be a famine, a plague, a fire, an infestation of locusts, or a blight [on the crops], or if an enemy should come against one of our cities (no matter what the event or misery)... ‘May all the prayers and supplications of every man be heard, so that You’ll come to know the pain in their hearts.
[1 Kings] [8]:[38] ‘And whenever a man spreads out his arms in this
[1 Kings] [8]:[39] Temple that’s been prepared for You; may You hear him from the heavens, forgive him, and act. ‘Give each man what he deserves according to the way that he behaves; for, only You can know what’s really in their hearts. ‘Yes, You alone know what’s in the hearts of all the sons of men.
[1 Kings] [8]:[40] So, they should fear You all the days of their lives that they spend on this land that You’ve given to our ancestors.
[1 Kings] [8]:[41] ‘And as for the aliens who are not from Your people...
[1 Kings] [8]:[42] ‘When they come to this place that’s been prepared as Your Home to pray,
[1 Kings] [8]:[43] please listen to them from the heavens and do everything that they ask, so that all the people on the earth will know Your Name and come to fear You… ‘Just as Your people IsraEl should know that Your Name has been called upon this Temple that I built.
[1 Kings] [8]:[44] ‘And if Your people must go to war against their enemies (following Your directions), and if they pray in the Name of the Lord in this city that You’ve chosen and in this Temple that I’ve built to Your Name...
[1 Kings] [8]:[45] Please listen to their prayers and supplications from heaven and bring them justice.
[1 Kings] [8]:[46] ‘And when they sin against You (for there’s no man who doesn’t sin) and You hand them over to their enemies who thereafter carry them away as captives into a land that’s nearby or far away;
[1 Kings] [8]:[47] ‘And if, in the land where they are, they turn back and start begging for Your [help], saying: ‘We have sinned; we have done wrong; we have acted lawlessly!’
[1 Kings] [8]:[48] ‘And they turn back to You with their whole hearts and souls – there in the land of their enemies who took them there, and pray to You in the direction of the land that You gave to their ancestors, to the city that You’ve chosen, and to the Temple that I built to Your Name...
[1 Kings] [8]:[49] Please listen from the heavens and from the home that has been prepared for You.
[1 Kings] [8]:[50] ‘Forgive the wrongs that they did when they sinned against You, and for the wicked ways in which they’ve disregarded You, then give compassion to the ones who took them as captives so they’ll pity them.
[1 Kings] [8]:[51] ‘For they’re Your people and Your inheritance… They’re the ones whom You led out of the land of Egypt and from the midst of that iron-foundry furnace.
[1 Kings] [8]:[52] ‘May Your eyes and Your ears [always] be open to the cries of Your servants and to the pleas of Your people, IsraEl. ‘Please listen to them, no matter why they’re calling to You...
[1 Kings] [8]:[53] Because, You’ve drawn them and set them apart for Yourself as an inheritance from among all the peoples of the earth, and You spoke to them through Your servant Moses when You led our ancestors out of the land of Egypt, O Lord [Jehovah].’
[1 Kings] [8]:[54] And after Solomon finished his prayer and his requests to [Jehovah], he stood up before the Altar of [Jehovah] (because he’d been kneeling before it), then he raised his arms towards heaven
[1 Kings] [8]:[55] and he blest the whole assembly of IsraEl in a loud voice, saying:
[1 Kings] [8]:[56] ‘Praise [Jehovah], for He’s brought rest to His people IsraEl today, just as He promised among all the many things that He said. For, not a word of the many things that He said through His servants has failed to come true!
[1 Kings] [8]:[57] ‘May [Jehovah] our God be with us, as He has been with our ancestors. ‘May He not abandon us or turn from us.
[1 Kings] [8]:[58] ‘May He move our hearts towards Him, so we will follow in all His ways and keep the Commandments and orders that He gave to our ancestors.
[1 Kings] [8]:[59] ‘And may all the things that I’ve begged for here before [Jehovah] our God come true today! ‘May they be heard by [Jehovah] our God day and night, and may He always do the right thing for His servant and for His people IsraEl, day in and day out,
[1 Kings] [8]:[60] so that all the people on the earth will come to know that [Jehovah] is The God, and that there is no other!
[1 Kings] [8]:[61] ‘May our hearts become perfect to [Jehovah] our God, and may we follow His orders and keep His Commandments in holiness, as we are doing today.’
[1 Kings] [8]:[62] Then the king and all the sons of IsraEl offered sacrifices before [Jehovah].
[1 Kings] [8]:[63] King Solomon offered 22,000 oxen and 120,000 sheep as a peace offering to [Jehovah]. Then the king inaugurated the Temple of [Jehovah] before all the sons of IsraEl.
[1 Kings] [8]:[64] On that holy day, the king stood in the middle of the courtyard (in front of the Temple of [Jehovah]) and prepared whole burnt offerings as sacrifices. He offered the fat of the peace offerings there, since the bronze Altar that was before [Jehovah] was just too small and it couldn’t handle all the whole burnt-offerings, gift offerings, and peace-offering sacrifices.
[1 Kings] [8]:[65] Thereafter, Solomon held a holiday feast that was attended by all in IsraEl. It was a huge gathering, for people had come from as far away as HaMath and the [Nile] River to stand before [Jehovah] God at the Temple that [Solomon] had built. They ate, drank, and rejoiced before [Jehovah] their God for 7 days!
[1 Kings] [8]:[66] Then on the 8th day, [Solomon] sent the people away, and they offered ages of blessings to the king as they left... So they all returned to their tents rejoicing over all the good things that [Jehovah] had done for His servant David and for His people IsraEl.
[1 Kings] [9]:[1] Well, after Solomon had finished building the Temple of [Jehovah], his own palace, and all the other things that he wanted to do,
[1 Kings] [9]:[2] the Lord appeared to him a second time (like He had appeared to him in GibeOn)
[1 Kings] [9]:[3] and said to him: ‘I heard what you said in your prayer, and of the things that you asked and begged of Me. So, I’ve now done everything that you asked for in your prayer… I’ve made this Temple (which you built to [honor] My Name) holy throughout the ages, and I’ll [always] watch over it and keep it in My heart.
[1 Kings] [9]:[4] ‘And if you’ll continue to follow Me uprightly with holiness in your heart like your father David did, and do everything that I told him to do –following My orders and Commandments–
[1 Kings] [9]:[5] I’ll lift the throne of your kingdom over IsraEl throughout the ages, as I promised to your father. ‘For I told him: ‘There will always be a man [descended from you] to lead IsraEl.’
[1 Kings] [9]:[6] ‘However, if you or your descendants should turn away from Me and fail to keep My Commandments and orders that Moses set before you, and you then go and serve other gods and bow before them...
[1 Kings] [9]:[7] I’ll remove IsraEl from the land that I’ve given to them, and I’ll turn My face away from this Temple that I’ve made holy to My Name! ‘Then IsraEl will become extinct and a topic of discussion among all the people!
[1 Kings] [9]:[8] ‘And everyone who passes this lofty Temple will be amazed and whistle, asking: ‘Why did [Jehovah] do such a thing to this land and to this Temple?’
[1 Kings] [9]:[9] ‘And they’ll be told: ‘Because they abandoned their God – the God of their ancestors, [Jehovah] – who led them out of the house of slavery in Egypt! ‘Then they took hold of alien gods, and bowed before them and served them… This is why [Jehovah] brought all these bad things upon them!’
[1 Kings] [9]:[10] Well, this all took place some 20 years after Solomon had [started] construction of the two houses – the Temple of [Jehovah] and the palace of the king.
[1 Kings] [9]:[11] King HiRam of Tyre had helped Solomon by providing the cedar and pine boards, [some of] the gold, and everything else [that Solomon had asked for]. So King Solomon gave HiRam 20 cities in the land of Galilee.
[1 Kings] [9]:[12] But when HiRam traveled from Tyre to Galilee to look at the cities that Solomon had given to him, he wasn’t pleased with them.
[1 Kings] [9]:[13] And he asked: ‘What kind of cities have you given to your brother?’ So from then on, he just referred to them as ‘the border lands.’
[1 Kings] [9]:[14] Now, HiRam had sent Solomon 4-1/2 tons (4,000kg) of gold
[1 Kings] [9]:[15] that he’d plundered for the construction of the Temple of [Jehovah], the king’s palace, the walls around JeruSalem (to fortify the city of David), as well as the cities of MegidDo and GeZer.
[1 Kings] [9]:[16] Also, after PharaOh, the king of Egypt, took GeZer (he burned it and killed all the CanaAnites who lived in the city), he then gave it to Solomon as a dowry for his daughter when he gave her to Solomon.
[1 Kings] [9]:[17] Thereafter, Solomon rebuilt GeZer,
[1 Kings] [9]:[18] as well as Lower BethHoron, BaAlAth, and TadMor (which is in the desert).
[1 Kings] [9]:[19] He also built many other fortified cities, as well as forts for his chariots and cavalry; and he had many other construction projects in JeruSalem, Lebanon, and throughout all the land that he ruled.
[1 Kings] [9]:[20] However, the Hittites, Amorites, Pherezites, CanaAnites, Hivites, Jebusites, and Gergesites (all those who weren’t sons of IsraEl)
[1 Kings] [9]:[21] and their children remained in the land, because the sons of IsraEl weren’t able to wipe them out; so, Solomon forced them to pay a tribute to him, which they’ve continued to do down to this day.
[1 Kings] [9]:[22] And many of these non-IsraElites served Solomon as soldiers and as lieutenants over his chariots and cavalry.
[1 Kings] [9]:[23] Also, many of them (some 550 of them) were put in charge over Solomon’s construction projects and they supervised the people who were doing the work.
[1 Kings] [9]:[24] The daughter of PharaOh didn’t actually live in the city of David, for she lived in a house that Solomon had built for her. And thereafter, he built MilLo.
[1 Kings] [9]:[25] Well, three times each year, Solomon would sacrifice whole burnt offerings and peace offerings on the Altar that he’d built to [Jehovah]. He also burned incense upon it there before [Jehovah], until he had completed the Temple.
[1 Kings] [9]:[26] Then King Solomon built a ship at GeBer (which is next to the seaport of ElAth on the border of Edom),
[1 Kings] [9]:[27] and HiRam sent some of his servants who were mariners and knew the sea [both] to do the rowing and as assistants to the servants of Solomon.
[1 Kings] [9]:[28] Then they [attacked] SopheRam and brought back gold to King Solomon – some 16 tons (14,500kg) of it!
[1 Kings] [10]:[1] Well, the Queen of SheBa had heard of Solomon’s fame and of the Name [Jehovah]; so, she came to test him with problems.
[1 Kings] [10]:[2] When she came to JeruSalem, she brought a very large contingent [of servants], as well as camels that were carrying spices, a huge amount of gold, and many valuable gems. Then she went to King Solomon and spoke to him about all the things that were in her heart...
[1 Kings] [10]:[3] And Solomon answered all her questions… He didn’t overlook a thing, but explained everything to her!
[1 Kings] [10]:[4] And when the Queen of SheBa saw how knowledgeable Solomon was and the palace that he’d built,
[1 Kings] [10]:[5] as well as all the food that he had, the ways that his servants were assigned, the jobs that his officials were given, how they were dressed, and all of his wine servers and the whole burnt offerings that he sacrificed at the Temple of [Jehovah]... She was beside herself!
[1 Kings] [10]:[6] Then she said to King Solomon: ‘Everything that I’ve heard about you in my land and about your knowledge is true!
[1 Kings] [10]:[7] I had to come here, because I didn’t believe the things that I was being told. ‘However, I’ve found that it’s all beyond what was reported in my land!
[1 Kings] [10]:[8] ‘Your wives and servants are blest to be able to stand before you all the time and listen to your wisdom.
[1 Kings] [10]:[9] And your God [Jehovah], who chose you and put you on the throne of IsraEl, must love IsraEl and [plan to] watch over it throughout the ages, since He’s the One who set you as king over them and to righteously hear and judge their cases.’
[1 Kings] [10]:[10] Then she gave Solomon 1-1/2 tons (1,300kg) of gold, a huge amount of spices, and many precious gems... Never before had anyone brought so many spices as those that the Queen of SheBa brought to King Solomon.
[1 Kings] [10]:[11] Thereafter, HiRam also sent a ship carrying gold from Ophir, as well as cut lumber and valuable stones.
[1 Kings] [10]:[12] The king then used this timber to fortify the Temple of [Jehovah] and the king’s palace, and to make stringed instruments and lutes for the musicians. Never before had such wood been seen in the land (or anywhere else, for that matter).
[1 Kings] [10]:[13] Then King Solomon gave the Queen of SheBa everything that she asked for and desired… In addition to all the other gifts that King Solomon gave to her. And thereafter, she returned to her land with all her servants.
[1 Kings] [10]:[14] Well, the weight of the gold that came to Solomon that year was about 32 tons (29,000kg)…
[1 Kings] [10]:[15] Which didn’t include the tributes that the people or the merchants brought, or that which was brought by kings on the other side of the Jordan or from the governors of the land.
[1 Kings] [10]:[16] Thereafter, King Solomon had 300 spears made from hammered gold, each of which was made from 600 gold coins.
[1 Kings] [10]:[17] And he also had 300 small shields made of hammered gold that was equal to the weight of three large gold coins. Then the king had them all mounted in his Palace of the Forests of Lebanon.
[1 Kings] [10]:[18] The king also had a huge throne made from ivory that was plated with pure gold,
[1 Kings] [10]:[19] which had 6 stairs that led up to the throne! There were [carved] reliefs of young bulls on its back, and handrails on each side, with [carved] lions standing beside them…
[1 Kings] [10]:[20] Plus 12 [more] lions on both sides, next to the six steps. There had never been anything like it in any kingdom!
[1 Kings] [10]:[21] Also, all the [dishes, cups, and bowls] that were used by Solomon were entirely made of gold, as were the bathtubs and vases in the Palace of the Forests of Lebanon. Nothing there was made of silver, because it was too common in the days of Solomon.
[1 Kings] [10]:[22] In addition, Solomon owned a ship that sailed the sea from TarShish along with the ships of HiRam [the king of Tyre]. And once every three years, the ship would carry gold, silver, and cut gems to the king.
[1 Kings] [10]:[23] So Solomon became greater than all the other kings of the earth in both wealth and in intelligence...
[1 Kings] [10]:[24] And all the kings of the earth came to Solomon to hear the wisdom that [Jehovah] had put into his heart.
[1 Kings] [10]:[25] Each one brought gifts of silver, gold, clothing, balsam, spices, horses, and mules every year.
[1 Kings] [10]:[26] Solomon also obtained chariots and horsemen. He had 1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen, which he kept in forts throughout the land and with himself in JeruSalem.
[1 Kings] [10]:[27] The king’s silver was as common as stones in JeruSalem, and his cedars were as common as trees in the plains.
[1 Kings] [10]:[28] Solomon’s horses were from Egypt and the king’s merchants were from Kue, and they could come out from Kue [and pass through Israel] for a fee.
[1 Kings] [10]:[29] So those [traders] who left Egypt [to pass through Israel] would pay [at least]: 100 large silver coins for each chariot [of goods], and 50 large silver coins for each horse [carrying goods]. So all the Hittite and Syrian kings came out by sea [to avoid paying the fees].
[1 Kings] [11]:[1] King Solomon was also very fond of women, so he took several foreigners as wives, such as the daughter of PharaOh, as well as some: MoAbites, AmMonites, Idumeans, Sidonians, and Hittites…
[1 Kings] [11]:[2] ...which [Jehovah] had forbidden the sons of IsraEl to do! For He said: ‘You must not [marry] them and they must not come to you, because they will turn your hearts to their idols.’ However, Solomon [was a slave] to love...
[1 Kings] [11]:[3] So before long, he’d taken 700 [wives] as well as 300 concubines! These foreign women changed his heart;
[1 Kings] [11]:[4] they quickly turned his heart to bowing before other gods, and his heart was no longer perfect towards his God [Jehovah], as was the heart of his father David.
[1 Kings] [11]:[5] For Solomon started serving Astarte, the goddess of the Sidonians, and Melchom, the disgusting thing of the AmMonites!
[1 Kings] [11]:[6] So Solomon started doing evil things before [Jehovah], and he no longer followed he Lord, as did his father David.
[1 Kings] [11]:[7] Then Solomon built high places to Camus (the idol of MoAb) and to Melchom (the idol of the sons of AmMon) on the mountain across from JeruSalem.
[1 Kings] [11]:[8] And there, all his foreign wives were burning incense and sacrificing to their idols!
[1 Kings] [11]:[9] Of course, this made [Jehovah] very angry with Solomon, for his heart had turned from [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl, who had actually appeared before him twice,
[1 Kings] [11]:[10] warning him not to serve other gods and to be careful to do everything that the Lord God had told him.
[1 Kings] [11]:[11] So, the Lord said to Solomon: ‘Because you’ve done these things and you haven’t followed My Commandments or the instructions that I gave to you; I will take your kingdom from your hands and rip it in two, then I’ll give it to your servant.
[1 Kings] [11]:[12] ‘However, I won’t do this during your lifetime [out of respect for] David your father. Rather, I’ll take it from the hands of your son.
[1 Kings] [11]:[13] I won’t take your whole kingdom; I’ll leave your son as chief over part of it because of My servant David and because of JeruSalem, the city that I’ve chosen.’
[1 Kings] [11]:[14] So, [Jehovah] sent an enemy against Solomon under Ader (who was from the offspring of the kingdom of the Idumeans).
[1 Kings] [11]:[15] David had wiped out [many of] the Edomites, and when his General JoAb went to [their land] to bury his dead, he also cut down more of their men,
[1 Kings] [11]:[16] because JoAb had stayed there for the next 6 months. Yet, although JoAb had destroyed all the men there,
[1 Kings] [11]:[17] Ader (who was just a small boy then) got away, along with many of his father’s servants, and they headed to Egypt...
[1 Kings] [11]:[18] Then, after the men of Media attacked Pharan, the [people there] also went with him as he was on his way to the PharaOh (the king of Egypt).
[1 Kings] [11]:[19] Well, when Ader went to PharaOh, he was given a house, food, and some land, because he was well-liked by PharaOh. He also gave him his sister-in-law as his woman (the older sister of [Queen] ThekeMina),
[1 Kings] [11]:[20] and she gave birth to GaneBath, whom ThekeMina raised in her house as one of the sons of PharaOh.
[1 Kings] [11]:[21] But when word reached Ader in Egypt that David had gone to sleep with his ancestors and that JoAb (the commander of his army) had been killed, Ader said to PharaOh: ‘Please allow me to return to my country.’
[1 Kings] [11]:[22] And PharaOh asked him: ‘What have I failed to give you that you now wish to return to your country?’ To which Ader replied: ‘Not a single thing! But please send me away.’
[1 Kings] [11]:[23] Meanwhile, [Jehovah] had also raised another enemy against [Solomon]: Rezon (son of EliAdah), who had run away from his master HadadEzer, the king of ZoBah.
[1 Kings] [11]:[24] He then gathered an army and became the ruler of a confederation that captured Damascus, where he settled in and started ruling as king,
[1 Kings] [11]:[25] and where he (as the ruler of the land of Edom) remained an enemy to IsraEl during all the days of Solomon.
[1 Kings] [11]:[26] Then one of Solomon’s servants, JeroBoam (son of NaBat the Ephrathite from SariRa), whose mother was a widow,
[1 Kings] [11]:[27] rebelled against King Solomon. This happened after King Solomon had built the Akra (high fort) and after he’d completed the outer wall around the city of his father David.
[1 Kings] [11]:[28] Now, JeroBoam was a mighty man, and when Solomon noticed that this young man was someone who could get things done, he put him in charge of the tributes from the house of JoSeph.
[1 Kings] [11]:[29] But one day, as JeroBoam was coming from JeruSalem, he met the prophet AhiJah (the Selonite), who stopped along the road to talk to him. Well at the time, AhiJah was wearing a new cape and they were alone there in the plain.
[1 Kings] [11]:[30] Then AhiJah took off the cape that he was wearing and tore it into 12 pieces.
[1 Kings] [11]:[31] And he said to JeroBoam: ‘Take 10 of these pieces for yourself, because this is what [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl said: '{Look!} I’m ripping the kingdom from the hands of Solomon and giving 10 of its [tribes] to you!
[1 Kings] [11]:[32] ‘However, two of the [tribes] will remain his because of My servant David and on account of JeruSalem, the city that I’ve chosen from among all the tribes of IsraEl.
[1 Kings] [11]:[33] [I’m doing this] because [Solomon] has abandoned Me and is now making offerings to Astarte, the disgusting thing of the Sidonians, to Camus, the idol of MoAb, and to Melchom, the loathsome thing of the sons of AmMon! ‘He is no longer walking in My ways or doing the right things before Me as did his father David.
[1 Kings] [11]:[34] ‘I’m not going to remove the kingdom from him entirely, but I’ll oppose him throughout the rest of the days of his life... It was only because of My servant David that I chose him.
[1 Kings] [11]:[35] But now, I’m going to take the kingdom from the hands of his son and give 10 of the [tribes] to you!

[1 Kings] [12]:[8] However, he chose not to listen to the advice that the elders had given to him, and he took the advice of some young men whom he’d grown up around and whom he’d selected to be his advisors.
[1 Kings] [12]:[9] So when he asked what they recommended he tell the people who came to him and told him to lighten the neck-yoke that his father had put on them,

[1 Kings] [12]:[11] ‘Therefore, as my father saddled you to a heavy yoke, I’ll add more weight to it! ‘And as my father disciplined you with whips, I’ll discipline you with scorpions!’
[1 Kings] [12]:[12] So when all IsraEl came before King RehoBoam on the 3rd day (the king of IsraEl had told them, ‘Return to me on the 3rd day’),
