[Job] [8]:[16] ‘Whenever it’s wet under the sun, From things that are rotten, a branch starts to sprout.
[Job] [8]:[17] So, on a pile of stones, a man goes to bed, And he lives there amidst all the gravel;
[Job] [8]:[18] His place then swallows him down, And thereafter, it covers him over. Haven’t you witnessed such things?
[Job] [8]:[19] ‘Yes, that’s how the godless all come to their end… And then, from the ground, sprouts another.
[Job] [8]:[20] ‘No way will the Lord harm the good, And He accepts no gifts from the godless.
[Job] [8]:[21] With laughter, He fills the mouths of the true And those who use their lips in His praise.
[Job] [8]:[22] To their enemies, He will always bring shame, And the homes of the Godless, He soon wipes away.’
[Job] [9]:[1] Then Job spoke. He said:
[Job] [9]:[2] ‘I know for a fact, what you’re saying is true; For, how can a man say he’s righteous to God?
[Job] [9]:[3] So, if he wishes to argue this point, He won’t prove God wrong with thousands of words.
[Job] [9]:[4] For, all of God’s thoughts are wise, strong, and great. ‘Thus, who can approach Him in anger And still have some hope of survival?
[Job] [9]:[5] Do the mountains know who destroys them in rage?
[Job] [9]:[6] ‘All that’s under the sky, He can shake to its core… And then He can shake all its columns.
[Job] [9]:[7] He can speak to the sun and it won’t rise, And He can also close up the stars.
[Job] [9]:[8] ‘By Himself, He can stretch out the sky, And walk on the sea like a floor.
[Job] [9]:[9] He’s the One who made the PleiAdes, As well as Hesperus and ArcTurus… He’s the One who arranged the skies in the south.
[Job] [9]:[10] ‘He does things that are great and unfathomed… Honorable things beyond number and odd. If He passed over me, I’d not see it… If He passed me by, I’d not be aware.
[Job] [9]:[12] ‘When He sends someone away, Who can thereafter return him, And who can ask why He did it?
[Job] [9]:[13] ‘For, God doesn’t turn back His rage… To Him, even the whales bow under the skies!
[Job] [9]:[14] ‘So, why should He ever obey me, Or why should He judge all my problems?
[Job] [9]:[15] And if could I prove myself righteous, He’d [have no reason to] hear men… Although I’d still ask Him for His decisions.
[Job] [9]:[16] ‘Thus, should I call, He may not give an ear, Nor should I trust that He’s heard my voice.
[Job] [9]:[17] ‘But He shouldn’t destroy me in darkness, Nor bruise me without any reason.
[Job] [9]:[18] For, although He’s allowed me to breathe, I’m now filled with what’s bitter.
[Job] [9]:[19] ‘Because He’s so mighty and strong, Who can stand and oppose Him?
[Job] [9]:[20] So, even if I’ve been righteous, My mouth would still say wicked things. And although I might [truly] be blameless, I’d still produce what’s wrong.
[Job] [9]:[21] ‘But, if I’m really ungodly, In my soul, I remain unaware… Even though my life has been taken away.
[Job] [9]:[22] ‘I’ve said: ‘The mighty kill in their rage;
[Job] [9]:[23] And for the vile, death isn’t uncommon. ‘They’re the ones who laugh at the righteous
[Job] [9]:[24] When they’re handed to those who are Godless. ‘For He covers the eyes of the judges… And if He doesn’t do it, who does?’
[Job] [9]:[25] ‘O that my soul was as light as a sprinter… Yet, my days have passed by without notice.
[Job] [9]:[26] Can my ship still be seen on the horizon By eagles in search of their prey?
[Job] [9]:[27] ‘So to you here before me, I’ll say: If I’d just forget about speaking, Then bow my head and just groan;
[Job] [9]:[28] And if I’d just let my limbs shiver, Wouldn’t you still find me guilty?
[Job] [9]:[29] ‘But, if I’m someone who is godless; Why haven’t I already died?
[Job] [9]:[30] If I’d wash myself in the snow, And if I scrubbed all the dirt from my hands,
[Job] [9]:[31] You’d still dip me in filth, And even my clothes would detest me.
[Job] [9]:[32] ‘Yet, you are men just like me By whom I’m judged and compared. Before His Judgment Seat, we all stand together…
[Job] [9]:[33] Before the lawyers and accusers, And in front of the One [who] listens to both.
[Job] [9]:[34] ‘So, may He set me free from the [whip], And may I not be twisted in fear.
[Job] [9]:[35] Then, I’ll speak and I won’t be afraid, For I’m still unaware of my crimes.’
[Job] [10]:[1] ‘Since my soul has become tired of groaning; I’ll now tell Him how bad I now feel.
[Job] [10]:[2] Yes, to [Jehovah], I’ll say: ‘Don’t tell me that I’m ungodly… So, why have You judged me that way?
[Job] [10]:[3] ‘Would You think it good if I’d sinned, Or if I’d disavowed the works of Your hands? Why do You believe what the godless have said
[Job] [10]:[4] And look at things the way humans do? ‘When You look, do You see as men see?
[Job] [10]:[5] Is Your existence like that of a man? Are Your years as those of just men?
[Job] [10]:[6] ‘Since You’ve searched for all my law breaking And You’ve traced out all of my sins,
[Job] [10]:[7] You must know that I’m not ungodly; But, from Your hands, who can wrest me away?
[Job] [10]:[8] ‘It was Your hands that made me and shaped me, Then You turned around and You struck me.
[Job] [10]:[9] O remember the day that You shaped me, Then, stand me erect on the ground once again!
[Job] [10]:[10] ‘You extracted me as though milking, And then I was curdled like cheese.
[Job] [10]:[11] You put me together with meat, skin, and bones, And then, with nerves, You entwined me.
[Job] [10]:[12] In mercy, You put life within me, Then You watched over me and guarded my breath.
[Job] [10]:[13] ‘You did all these things by Yourself; And it’s a fact that You can do all… There’s nothing that You can’t do.
[Job] [10]:[14] So, if I should sin, please protect me… Declare me free of law breaking.
[Job] [10]:[15] ‘[Don’t count me] among the ungodly! Yet, even though I’m righteous, I can’t raise my head; For, I’ve become so dishonored.
[Job] [10]:[16] ‘I’ve been caught like a lion for slaughter… For You’ve turned around to destroy me.
[Job] [10]:[17] You’ve disciplined me once again, And dealt with me in great rage By bringing these trials upon me.
[Job] [10]:[18] ‘Why did you lead me out of the belly? Why didn’t I die, so my eyes wouldn’t see
[Job] [10]:[19] As one whom had never been born? Why wasn’t I just sent away… Sent to the tomb like how I came from the womb?
[Job] [10]:[20] And why have I lived for so many years? ‘Now, allow me to rest for a while
[Job] [10]:[21] And go to the place where I’ll not return… To a land that’s shrouded and dim…
[Job] [10]:[22] A land that’s dark throughout the ages, Where light and life can’t be seen.’
[Job] [11]:[1] Then Zophar the Minaean spoke, saying:
[Job] [11]:[2] ‘This One who has so much to say Should also listen in turn; Is this one who is so very well-spoken Proclaiming himself to be just? ‘Those born of women who only live short lives
[Job] [11]:[3] Are blest, because they have much less to say.
[Job] [11]:[4] ‘Now, no one’s comparing himself to you, And don’t try to say that your deeds are all pure… That you’re blameless, as you’re standing before Him.
[Job] [11]:[5] ‘O that [Jehovah] would speak And tell you what He has to say.
[Job] [11]:[6] ‘Should He speak to you of His wisdom? His wisdom is so much greater than yours! But if He did, you’d know that what’s happened Has come about because of your sins against God.
[Job] [11]:[7] ‘Search for the ways of [Jehovah], And you’ll find the Almighty’s prepared for your end.
[Job] [11]:[8] ‘Because the heavens are ever so high; What can you do, and what do you know? ‘There are things much deeper than the place of the dead…
[Job] [11]:[9] They’re longer than the span of the land, And wider than the breadth of the seas.
[Job] [11]:[10] And if He’d destroy all those on the earth, Who could question His reason?
[Job] [11]:[11] ‘He knows the deeds of those who break laws, And He doesn’t overlook their wrongdoing…
[Job] [11]:[12] Yet, men keep swimming in words. For all men who are born of a woman, Are no wiser than the desert’s wild burros.
[Job] [11]:[13] ‘But, if you have a truly pure heart, And you can spread your hands out before Him;
[Job] [11]:[14] Should He find that you’ve broken no laws, And you’ve stayed a long way from injustice (That you’ve kept it away from your home);
[Job] [11]:[15] Your face would then have a shine… Pure water would wash off your filth, And you’d have nothing to fear.
[Job] [11]:[16] ‘You’d forget all your troubles like waves passing by, And you’d have no reason for terror.
[Job] [11]:[17] In the morning, your vows would be like the stars, And at noon, your life would return.
[Job] [11]:[18] ‘You’d have some hope, if you would comply, And have peace in place of trouble and strife.
[Job] [11]:[19] For you, there would be no more battles, And many would turn and beg for your aid.
[Job] [11]:[20] ‘But for them, will come no salvation, Since their only hope is destruction, And the eyes of the godless will melt.’
[Job] [12]:[1] Then Job spoke. He said:
[Job] [12]:[2] ‘Have you and the men who are with you Reached the end of your wisdom?
[Job] [12]:[3] ‘I too have a heart that’s like yours.
[Job] [12]:[4] But it seems that a man who is righteous and just Has only been born to be taunted!
[Job] [12]:[5] ‘There’s a time appointed when each man must fall, And for his house to be pillaged by crooks… But, may the wicked not trust [in their ways]. For the guileless will [be given] support,
[Job] [12]:[6] While [the bad] will be taught by God’s rage.
[Job] [12]:[7] ‘You could ask the four-footed creatures (If they could give you an answer), Or ask the things that fly in the sky (If they could give a report)
[Job] [12]:[8] To explain all they know of the earth, Or to even describe all the fish in the sea.
[Job] [12]:[9] ‘Are there any among them that don’t realize That they were made by God’s hand?
[Job] [12]:[10] For, in His hands are the lives of all things, As well as the breath of every man.
[Job] [12]:[11] ‘Men listen with their ears and examine each word, Then they taste the meanings inside their throats.
[Job] [12]:[12] ‘Wisdom is ancient, and knowledge is old,
[Job] [12]:[13] For from Him comes all wisdom and power… Along with understanding and all good advice.
[Job] [12]:[14] ‘So, if He chooses to tear something down, Who can thereafter rebuild it? And if He chooses to lock up a man, Who can thereafter release him?
[Job] [12]:[15] ‘If He should choose to hold back the rain, All the lands would go dry. But, He can also choose to release it, To destroy them and wash them away.
[Job] [12]:[16] ‘In Him, there’s both might and strength; In Him, there’s knowledge and all comprehension.
[Job] [12]:[17] He strips council away from advisors, And He [can also make fools of] earth’s judges.
[Job] [12]:[18] ‘He’s the One who sets kings on their thrones And who ties a sash ‘round their waists.
[Job] [12]:[19] But He’s also the One who sends priests off as slaves, And can wipe away all the mighty.
[Job] [12]:[20] ‘The lips of the honest, He understands, And the words of the elders, He knows.
[Job] [12]:[21] Upon rulers, He can pour out dishonor, While to those who are humble, He heals.
[Job] [12]:[22] ‘He uncovers the darkness of very deep things, And from the shadow of death, He can lead into light.
[Job] [12]:[23] ‘He destroys the nations that stray, And He cuts down those who mislead them.
[Job] [12]:[24] He knows the hearts of the rulers of lands, And He leads them in ways they don’t know.
[Job] [12]:[25] ‘So, may they corrupt the darkness, not light… May they wander like they’re drunk.
[Job] [13]:[1] '{Look!} I’ve seen such things with my eyes, And I’ve heard such things with my ears.
[Job] [13]:[2] ‘I know the same things that all of you know, And I have as much sense as do you.
[Job] [13]:[3] Thus, I’ll speak before God, And I’ll scold you, if He will allow it.
[Job] [13]:[4] ‘For, you’ve been unrighteous doctors, And as healers, you’ve done a very poor job.
[Job] [13]:[5] So, it would be a blessing if you’d stay still… Yes, that would be the course that’s wise.
[Job] [13]:[6] ‘Now, hear these things that I’ll tell you, And heed the judgments that come from my lips.
[Job] [13]:[7] ‘Aren’t you speaking here before God, And before Him, aren’t you being deceitful?

[Job] [13]:[13] ‘So, stay still as I pour out my rage;

[Job] [13]:[15] ‘But, if the Almighty should grab me, I’d still speak to Him and complain…
[Job] [13]:[16] I’d argue that I should be spared, For He’d not find me guilty of evil.
[Job] [13]:[17] ‘Listen to me… Hear my words, For I’ll shout them into your ears!
[Job] [13]:[18] Look at me… Yes, gaze upon me! For, as I stand here before you in judgment, I know that you’ll not call me righteous…
[Job] [13]:[19] Yet, the One who is my judge is impartial. ‘Now, I’ll say nothing more, because I’m through,
[Job] [13]:[20] And I’ll allow you two things to finish me off… Then I’ll go and hide from your presence.
[Job] [13]:[21] But, keep your hands at a distance, And give me no reason to fear you.
[Job] [13]:[22] ‘You can call out to me and I’ll listen; So, speak and I’ll give a reply.

[Job] [13]:[24] ‘What are you hiding from me, And why do you think I’m lesser than you?
[Job] [13]:[25] Will you avoid me like leaves in the wind, Or face me like grass in the air?
[Job] [13]:[26] ‘Against me, you’ve written so many bad things, And accused me of sins that are common to youth…
[Job] [13]:[27] You’ve opposed me, although I’m righteous. But by now, you’ve examined all of my deeds, And to the roots of my feet, you’ve reached.
[Job] [13]:[28] ‘Yet, I’ve been aging [so quickly], And I look like a bag made of leather, Or like a robe that’s been eaten by moths!’
[Job] [14]:[1] ‘For men born of women, life is too short, And our lives are filled with rage…
[Job] [14]:[2] Then we drop like flowers that have blossomed, And escape like shadows that have passed.
[Job] [14]:[3] ‘But, you’ve required an accounting of me, And although I’ve stood in judgment before You;
[Job] [14]:[4] Which [of you] can claim that you’re free of all filth? I’m sure there’s not one among you!
[Job] [14]:[5] ‘Men live but a day on the earth, And we count off the months of our lives Until we reach the time we’re allowed… [A time that] we can’t go past.
[Job] [14]:[6] Therefore, leave me alone so that I can be still, And think well of the work that I’ve done.
[Job] [14]:[7] ‘For a tree, there’s still hope after it’s cut, Since it may blossom again; For the sprouting of its shoots never fail,
[Job] [14]:[8] Although its roots may be old in the ground. Yet, even rocks will grow old, And even the stones [eventually] melt away.
[Job] [14]:[9] ‘When the trunk of a tree can smell water, It’ll blossom and fruit once again, Like it was something that’s new.
[Job] [14]:[10] But, when a man reaches his end, That won’t be undone… When he falls, he no longer exists.
[Job] [14]:[11] ‘In time, even the seas will be gone, And all the rivers will become barren and dry.
[Job] [14]:[12] But, when man goes to sleep, he won’t rise again Until [the stars] are all sewn together… From that sleep, we never awaken.
[Job] [14]:[13] ‘O that in the grave, You’d hide me and guard me Until all Your anger has passed. Please order a time to be set for me, When You’ll mention my name once again.
[Job] [14]:[14] ‘Can a man live again after he dies, Once the days of his life have all past? As for me; I’ll wait ‘til I live again,
[Job] [14]:[15] When You’ll call out to me and I’ll hear You… Please don’t undo the work of Your hands!
[Job] [14]:[16] ‘You’ve counted all the things that I’ve done in my life, And none of my sins have You overlooked.
[Job] [14]:[17] So, take all the laws that I’ve broken, Then seal them up in a bag, And [remove] the ones that I meant not to do.
[Job] [14]:[18] ‘A mountain will fall into ruin, And a rock wears out where it stands.
[Job] [14]:[19] In water, even stones become smooth, And floods wash away the earth’s cliffs. This is how You’ve destroyed the lengths of men’s lives…
[Job] [14]:[20] You stab them through and they die… You just turn Your face and they’re gone.
[Job] [14]:[21] ‘We don’t know how many descendants we’ll have, And we’re unaware if they’re few.
[Job] [14]:[22] For, our flesh just knows aches and pains, And in mourning, our lives have been spent.’
[Job] [15]:[1] Then EliPhaz the Temanite spoke. He said:
[Job] [15]:[2] ‘May I reply to a man who is so wise, And in a spirit that he understands… Who has known misery since he came from the womb,
[Job] [15]:[3] But, who scolds with words that will never be true, And with things that will never bring profit?
[Job] [15]:[4] ‘Have you forgotten your fear As you speak before God?
[Job] [15]:[5] What’s come from your mouth has proven your guilt; For you’ve failed to examine the words of the great.
[Job] [15]:[6] So, may your own mouth now correct you (not me); Since against your own lips, you’ve spoken.
[Job] [15]:[7] ‘Were you the first man to ever be born Before the hills had been piled?
[Job] [15]:[8] Did you hear how [Jehovah] arranged it, And did God then ask your advice… Did He gain all His wisdom from you?
[Job] [15]:[9] ‘What do you know that we don’t know, And what do you see that we’ve missed?

[Job] [15]:[31] May they not trust that they’ll survive, For soon, they’ll have nothing at all.
[Job] [15]:[32] ‘Corruption will prune them away, So their branches won’t grow into trees.

[Job] [18]:[3] Why must we stay silent before you Like beasts that walk on four feet?
[Job] [18]:[4] ‘Anger has gotten the better of you… So what, if you have to die? Will all life under heaven then come to an end? Will mountains be wiped from their bases?
[Job] [18]:[5] ‘The light of the godless will soon be put out, And his flame will be there no longer.
[Job] [18]:[6] The light in his home will be darkness, And his lamp will thereafter be gone.
[Job] [18]:[7] ‘The least of men search for the things they once owned, And they trip on their own good advice.
[Job] [18]:[8] So, may his feet fall into a snare, And in a net, may they get entangled.
[Job] [18]:[9] ‘Yes, let him fall into a trap, And may the snare hold him tighter.
[Job] [18]:[10] For the trip line is hidden under the ground… Yes, the thing that’ll grab and destroy him Is already there in the road!
[Job] [18]:[11] ‘May grief surround and destroy him,
[Job] [18]:[12] And may hunger encircle his feet. For him, a downfall has been prepared,
[Job] [18]:[13] And the soles of his feet will be eaten away. ‘May death now consume his beautiful things,
[Job] [18]:[14] And may the place of his healing be taken away… For these things have happened by royal decree
[Job] [18]:[15] That will camp in his tent throughout the night. ‘May his beautiful things be covered with sulfur;
[Job] [18]:[16] May his roots dry out underneath him. May what he has reaped fall upon him,
[Job] [18]:[17] And the memory of his face be wiped from the land.
[Job] [18]:[18] ‘May he be pushed from the light into darkness…
[Job] [18]:[19] May even his family forget his name. May his house remain under the sky;
[Job] [18]:[20] But, may it be lived in by others. ‘For, even though he once lived in wonder, In the end, he just sits here and moans.
[Job] [18]:[21] This is the home of someone unrighteous… It’s the place where [Jehovah] is no longer known.’
[Job] [19]:[1] Then Job spoke again and said:
[Job] [19]:[2] ‘How long are you going to weary my soul, And demolish me with your words? All you know is the things God has done,
[Job] [19]:[3] And speak ill of me with no shame… You just keep on pressing against me.
[Job] [19]:[4] ‘It’s a fact that I’ve been misled, And delusions are lodging within me. For I’m speaking words that should never be said… That mislead, and at the wrong time.
[Job] [19]:[5] ‘Now you use me to look more important, And you attack me in scorn.
[Job] [19]:[6] But, know that the Lord is the One who is disturbed… He’s the One who built this fortress against me.
[Job] [19]:[7] So look; I now laugh at your scorn! ‘Therefore, I’ll stop all this banter; For if I shout, it won’t bring me justice.
[Job] [19]:[8] I’m stuck in a circle that I can’t get out of, And darkness now covers my face.
[Job] [19]:[9] He’s taken away all my glory, And removed the garland that I wore on my head.
[Job] [19]:[10] ‘He’s pulled me apart and scattered [my bones]; I was marked and cut down like a tree.
[Job] [19]:[11] In His rage, He’s treated me badly, As though I’d been His opposer.
[Job] [19]:[12] His marauders have gathered and attacked me, And in an ambush, they have me surrounded.
[Job] [19]:[13] ‘Now, all my brothers have left me, Preferring strangers to me; And my friends no longer feel pity, Pretending that they don’t know me!
[Job] [19]:[14] ‘Those dearest to me have forgotten my name…
[Job] [19]:[15] I’m a foreigner to all of my neighbors And a stranger to the women who have served me.
[Job] [19]:[16] ‘When I call to my servant, he doesn’t obey, Even though, with my mouth, I keep begging.
[Job] [19]:[17] I call out to even my wife, And call sweetly to my concubines’ sons.
[Job] [19]:[18] But they listen not… They just stand there.
[Job] [19]:[19] ‘Those who once knew me, dislike me, And those I once loved, now oppose me.
[Job] [19]:[20] For, my skin and flesh are festered with sores, And my teeth have come loose from my jaws.
[Job] [19]:[21] ‘Please show mercy… Show mercy my friends; For the hand of [Jehovah] has touched me!
[Job] [19]:[22] Why treat me the same as [Jehovah] has done… Aren’t you filled enough with my flesh?
[Job] [19]:[23] ‘May my words be written down in a scroll, And be preserved throughout the ages.
[Job] [19]:[24] With a pen of iron, inscribe them on lead, And may they be set within stone.
[Job] [19]:[25] ‘For I know that the One who made me this weak Has walked ‘round the earth throughout the ages;
[Job] [19]:[26] And it’s due to Him, that my skin has grown tired… I’m worn out because of [Jehovah].
[Job] [19]:[27] ‘All I’m aware of and seen with my eyes, Has happened to me, not to others.
[Job] [19]:[28] But, what can I ask and what can I say… Is the root of my problem in Him?
[Job] [19]:[29] ‘Please turn around and send me what’s good, Or just cover me over. May Your rage be sent to the lawless instead… May they be the ones who reap this reward.’
[Job] [20]:[1] Then Zophar the Minaean spoke, saying:
[Job] [20]:[2] ‘So far, I’ve not disagreed With any of the words that you’ve spoken, Since we both view things in much the same way.
[Job] [20]:[3] So I’ll heed your instructions that shame me, And note the spirit of your reply.
[Job] [20]:[4] ‘But, haven’t you known about all these things… That since man was put on this earth,
[Job] [20]:[5] The irreverent one’s glee brings his downfall, And the joy of lawbreakers brings their destruction?
[Job] [20]:[6] ‘For, even if his gifts should ascend to the heavens, And his offerings should reach to the clouds;
[Job] [20]:[7] When he thinks that all’s going well, That’s when he’ll meet with his end. ‘Then, those who know him will ask where he is.
[Job] [20]:[8] But like dreams, he’ll no longer be found.
[Job] [20]:[9] From then on, all eyes will overlook him, And no one will note where he’s been.
[Job] [20]:[10] ‘Even though his sons once destroyed weaker [peoples], And their hands lit fires that brought others grief…
[Job] [20]:[11] Their bones that once held the vigor of youth Will make their beds under the ground.
[Job] [20]:[12] ‘For, evil was sweet in their mouths, So they hid it under their tongues.
[Job] [20]:[13] It wasn’t left or abandoned, But they brought it up from their throats.
[Job] [20]:[14] ‘So, now they can’t help themselves; For, the poison of asps is inside of their guts.
[Job] [20]:[15] And all the wealth that they’ve unjustly gained Will be collected and vomited out, As angels drag them out of their homes.
[Job] [20]:[16] ‘May they have to endure the rage of wild beasts… May the tongues of snakes now destroy them.
[Job] [20]:[17] May they never again see cows being milked, Or see pastures of butter and honey.
[Job] [20]:[18] ‘Then their wealth will seem empty and vain, And for such things, they’ll lose all their taste, Since they’ll become too tough to be chewed, And they’ll find that they can’t take it with them.
[Job] [20]:[19] ‘And although they once crushed the homes of the mighty, And by force, took their houses; What they have will no longer be theirs…
[Job] [20]:[20] For, what they owned, will no longer be safe, And they won’t keep the things that they loved.
[Job] [20]:[21] ‘For them, there’ll be no more food, And good things will no longer blossom.
[Job] [20]:[22] Even though they once had [all they desired], Problems arose and then it was cursed.
[Job] [20]:[23] ‘When they’ve had enough to fill up their bellies, God sends someone else to succeed them. So, may He now send His anger and rage, And upon them, pour out floods of grief.
[Job] [20]:[24] ‘From hands of iron, may they not be saved… May they be shot through by a brass bow.
[Job] [20]:[25] May the arrows go clean through their bodies, And may fear then walk through their homes.
[Job] [20]:[26] ‘May they have to wait in the darkness, To be burned by the fire of the ages. May strangers bring what’s bad to their homes;
[Job] [20]:[27] May the heavens uncover all their lawless deeds; And may the ground rise up against them.
[Job] [20]:[28] ‘May their homes be destroyed ‘til the end, And may the day of rage come upon them.
[Job] [20]:[29] For, this is what the irreverent get… It’s their reward from the One who keeps watch.’
[Job] [21]:[1] Then Job spoke, saying:
[Job] [21]:[2] ‘Listen to me… Hear my words! I don’t need such comfort from you!
[Job] [21]:[3] Now, please help me up, and I’ll speak; For, I won’t accept such abuse!
[Job] [21]:[4] ‘Since it’s by men that I’m being accused, Don’t I have a good reason for rage?
[Job] [21]:[5] ‘Why are you looking at me in such wonder, As you put your hands under your jaws?
[Job] [21]:[6] When I try to think of a reason, I tend to be a bit quick to conclude, Because of the grief in my flesh.
[Job] [21]:[7] ‘Why do the godless continue to live, And why do they grow rich and old?
[Job] [21]:[8] For, they plant whatever their souls might desire, And their children are there in front of their eyes.
[Job] [21]:[9] ‘Their houses continue to prosper, And they don’t seem to know any fear; For they fail to feel the whip of the Lord.
[Job] [21]:[10] ‘None of their cattle are stillborn, And their pregnant are also protected; So, none of them stumble or fall.
[Job] [21]:[11] ‘Their sheep remain throughout the ages, And their children are playing before them.
[Job] [21]:[12] They hold their flutes to their mouths, And enjoy sacred hymns strummed on harps.
[Job] [21]:[13] ‘For as long as they live, they have good things… Then they lie down to rest in the grave.
[Job] [21]:[14] They say that God doesn’t see, Since they’ve chosen not to know of His ways.
[Job] [21]:[15] ‘So, why should we continue to serve Him… For us, what good does it do,
[Job] [21]:[16] Since He doesn’t inspect godless hands; So, they’re always filled with what’s good?
[Job] [21]:[17] ‘But, their lamps will soon be extinguished… Their reward is to feel the pain of His rage.
[Job] [21]:[18] They’ll be like straw that’s blown in the wind, And as clouds of dust in a storm.
[Job] [21]:[19] ‘May their possessions and sons all be lost, And may they know that God has repaid them.
[Job] [21]:[20] May they see their slaughter with their own eyes, When God won’t be there to save them.
[Job] [21]:[21] Then, what joy will they have in their homes When they see that their months have been numbered?
[Job] [21]:[22] ‘Doesn’t [Jehovah] send wisdom? For who else gives people their insight… Isn’t He the One who makes judges wise?
[Job] [21]:[23] ‘Yet, this one dies doing just as he wished, Enjoying prosperity and pleasure…
[Job] [21]:[24] Full, fat, and filled up with marrow.
[Job] [21]:[25] While another ends life with what’s bitter, Having never tasted what’s good.
[Job] [21]:[26] Then they both go to sleep in the ground; And with decay, they’re both covered.
[Job] [21]:[27] ‘So, I know what you’ll say as you’re pressuring me:
[Job] [21]:[28] Where are the houses where princes will live And safe tents where the godless will dwell?
[Job] [21]:[29] ‘Ask those passing by on the roads, and you’ll see That the signs are all very clear;
[Job] [21]:[30] For the day of destruction will come When He will enlighten the wicked… And in that day of His rage, they’ll be gone.
[Job] [21]:[31] ‘Then, to their faces, He’ll accuse them, And speak of the bad things they’ve done. Yes, He will come to repay them
[Job] [21]:[32] As they lie awake upon heaps of trash, And then, to their tombs, they’ll be led.
[Job] [21]:[33] ‘In gravel, thereafter, they’ll be covered, As other men come to see them… Yes, they’ll come in great numbers to stand there.
[Job] [21]:[34] ‘So, why waste your time to offer me comfort, Since you’ve done nothing to bring any rest!’
[Job] [22]:[1] Then EliPhaz the Temanite spoke, saying:
[Job] [22]:[2] ‘Doesn’t wisdom and understanding come from the Lord?
[Job] [22]:[3] So, why should He be concerned If what you’ve been doing is pure? ‘What good [do you think] it would do Him If all of your ways had been clean?
[Job] [22]:[4] Will He discipline you for the things that you say, Or join with you in your judgments?
[Job] [22]:[5] ‘Haven’t you done many bad things… Could anyone count all your sins?
[Job] [22]:[6] Haven’t you taken what your brothers need Without any justification? Haven’t you claimed the clothes of the naked…
[Job] [22]:[7] Refused to give water to the thirsty… And taken scraps of food from the famished?
[Job] [22]:[8] ‘You’ve shown favor to the faces of some, While you removed the poor from their land.
[Job] [22]:[9] You’ve sent away widows with nothing at all, And orphans, you’ve treated badly.
[Job] [22]:[10] So, the snares that you’ve set have now captured you, And this is why such a war has arrived.
[Job] [22]:[11] ‘So, light for you is now darkness, And when you sleep, you’re covered in dew.
[Job] [22]:[12] For the Living One is paying attention, And He humbles those who think themselves high.
[Job] [22]:[13] ‘You’ve asked, What does the Almighty know? And, Can He judge what happens in darkness?
[Job] [22]:[14] He’s concealed by the clouds, so He can’t be seen As He travels across the arc of the sky!
[Job] [22]:[15] ‘You can’t guard the roads of the ages, Which have been walked by the righteous
[Job] [22]:[16] Who were taken away in untimely [deaths], Like rivers overflowing their banks!
[Job] [22]:[17] Yet, even they had once asked: ‘What will God do to us… Yes, what will the Almighty bring?’
[Job] [22]:[18] ‘He’s the One who filled their homes with good things, While the council of the the Godless, He’s pushed away.
[Job] [22]:[19] The righteous all laugh when they see this, And the blameless sneer at such ones.
[Job] [22]:[20] For, their supports will soon vanish, And their clothes will be burned up in fire.
[Job] [22]:[21] ‘So you must be strong if you want to survive, And then you’ll receive your reward For all the good things that you’ve done.
[Job] [22]:[22] Remove all the [bad] from your mouth, And keep His words in your heart!
[Job] [22]:[23] ‘Turn back and be humbled by God, And stay away from wrongdoing!
[Job] [22]:[24] Then you’ll lay away gold as though it were dust From the rivers of Ophir…
[Job] [22]:[25] The Almighty will then watch over you, And you’ll have plenty of silver.
[Job] [22]:[26] ‘So, confess [your sins] to [Jehovah], And look to the heavens in joy.
[Job] [22]:[27] Make vows to Him and He’ll listen to you, Then He’ll give you the strength to do as you’ve vowed
[Job] [22]:[28] And restore you to a righteous condition, So your ways can be bright once again.
[Job] [22]:[29] ‘For, those who humble themselves Will admit that they’ve been too proud; And [God] will save those who are humble.
[Job] [22]:[30] Yes, He’ll rescue those free from guilt… But first, you must keep your hands clean!’
[Job] [23]:[1] Then Job spoke, saying:
[Job] [23]:[2] ‘I know for a fact that my change of state Is something that’s out of my hands. For, it’s His hand that’s been heavy on me, And He’s the source of my groaning.
[Job] [23]:[3] So who knows if I’ll ever find Him again, And bring these things to a conclusion.
[Job] [23]:[4] ‘Now, on myself, I’ll pass judgment, And with scolding words, I’ll fill my mouth.
[Job] [23]:[5] Then I’ll learn the cure, for He’ll show it to me… I’ll understand, because He’ll explain it!
[Job] [23]:[6] ‘He’ll come to me with great strength, And I know He won’t do so unsurely.
[Job] [23]:[7] He’ll send me truth and correction, And bring an end to my case.
[Job] [23]:[8] ‘But, if I should be the first one to go, And if I should no longer be; How could I know how it ends?
[Job] [23]:[9] ‘With His left hand, He acts… I can’t stop Him; And what He covers with His right, I can’t see.
[Job] [23]:[10] He already knows all my ways; For He’s searched me through as if I were gold.
[Job] [23]:[11] ‘My feet have walked in His footsteps… I’ve kept His ways and not swerved.
[Job] [23]:[12] I’ve never rejected commands from His lips, And I’ve held in esteem the words from His mouth.
[Job] [23]:[13] But, if He’s judged me as guilty, Who can say that He’s wrong?
[Job] [23]:[14] ‘So I’ve always turned towards Him quickly, And when I’m corrected, I keep Him in mind.
[Job] [23]:[15] For, grave are the things that come from His face… They’re things that leave me in terror.
[Job] [23]:[16] ‘Yet, [Jehovah] has softened my heart… The Almighty has moved me to action.
[Job] [23]:[17] For, I never suspected that darkness would come And that before my face, all would go dim.
[Job] [24]:[1] ‘Why hasn’t [Jehovah] noticed this time
[Job] [24]:[2] When the godless are overrunning our borders… Those who seize both the shepherds and sheep?
[Job] [24]:[3] ‘From the orphans, they’ve taken their burros, And the cows upon which the widows relied.
[Job] [24]:[4] They keep the disabled from walking upright, So the gentle of the land must run off and hide.
[Job] [24]:[5] ‘They act like burros that stray into fields And find the bread of infants delicious.
[Job] [24]:[6] They harvest in fields not their own, And reap it before it’s ripe. ‘The godless hire the disabled And put them to work in their vineyards… But then, they don’t pay them or feed them!
[Job] [24]:[7] They leave them naked, without any clothes, And they take all they need to survive.
[Job] [24]:[8] So, in mountain mists, such poor ones must bathe, And hide in the rocks for protection.
[Job] [24]:[9] ‘They then snatch away babies… They take them away from the breasts In payment for debts that are owed.
[Job] [24]:[10] They mistreat and rest of the naked, And take scraps of food from the famished.
[Job] [24]:[11] ‘In alleys, they lie in wait to do harm, And righteous ways, they don’t know.
[Job] [24]:[12] They throw people from their homes in the cities, And bring groaning to the lives of their children.
[Job] [24]:[13] ‘So, why does the One who is watching Fail to act on this earth, While people like this just ignore Him, Disregarding all that’s just And taking the easiest way?
[Job] [24]:[14] ‘In the cover of darkness, they murder, And during the night, they break in and steal.
[Job] [24]:[15] ‘The adulterer waits for darkness and says: ‘They won’t know that my eyes will be watching!’ And as he keeps his face hidden, He carves peepholes in homes in the night.
[Job] [24]:[16] ‘Then, during the day, he locks himself in, So he never comes to know light.
[Job] [24]:[17] For at dawn, he would see the shadow of death, And observe the bad things that it brings…
[Job] [24]:[18] But when he looks in the [reflection of] water, he still sees a good face. ‘May his portion on the earth be forever cursed, And may all that he plants wither and dry…
[Job] [24]:[19] For he even grabs the arms of orphans!
[Job] [24]:[20] ‘So, [please] remember his sins! Like fog, may he soon pass away, And may he vanish like dew. ‘Please repay him for all that he’s done… Like rotting wood, may he just waste away.
[Job] [24]:[21] For, those with no sons, he’s mistreated, And he shows no mercy to those who need aid.
[Job] [24]:[22] ‘The disabled, he’s knocked to the ground in his rage; So, no man’s life can ever feel secure.
[Job] [24]:[23] Thus, may he get sick and never be healed… And may his illness then lead to his death!
[Job] [24]:[24] ‘Since many are harmed by his arrogant ways, Like mallows, may he wither in heat… Like an ear of grain that just falls on its own.
[Job] [24]:[25] ‘If such things aren’t so, then say that I’ve lied, And disregard everything I’ve said!’

[Job] [25]:[4] For, which man can say that he’s righteous to God… Can men born of women make themselves pure?
[Job] [25]:[5] ‘[God] can order the moon not to shine, And before Him, the stars are impure.
[Job] [25]:[6] [So to Him], all mankind is rotten, And the sons of men are like worms.’

[Job] [26]:[14] '{Look!} These are just a small part of His ways; For when He breathes a word, we’ll listen! So, who knows when He will bring change… When He’ll bring the strength of His thunder?’
[Job] [27]:[1] Then Job continued in his own defense:
[Job] [27]:[2] ‘As God lives, He’s the One who has judged me… It’s the Almighty who has made my life bitter.
[Job] [27]:[3] But, as long as my spirit is in me, And the Divine One’s breath remains in my nose...
[Job] [27]:[4] My lips won’t speak lawless things, And my inner person won’t contemplate wrong;
[Job] [27]:[5] For, such things bring the sentence of death! ‘I’m not saying that I’m free from blame…
[Job] [27]:[6] But, I’ll cling to what’s right and never let go, For, I know when I’m doing what’s wrong.
[Job] [27]:[7] ‘May my enemies disappear with the godless, And my opposers be destroyed with lawbreakers.

[Job] [27]:[9] That God will hear what they pray, Or He’ll come when they’re in need?
[Job] [27]:[10] Can they stand before Him as securely As those who can call and be heard?
[Job] [27]:[11] ‘I’ll tell you about the things [God] holds in His hands… I won’t lie about the Almighty.
[Job] [27]:[12] {Look!} For He piles what’s foolish upon the foolish…

[Job] [27]:[14] ‘Should the Almighty One come to their aid, And should the sons [of the wicked] grow many? No! Their purpose is just to be slaughtered, And they’ll beg to be allowed to grow into men.

[Job] [27]:[21] A burning wind will snatch him away, And like chaff, he’ll be blown from his place.
[Job] [27]:[22] ‘He’ll be sent where nobody can save him… By [God’s] hands, he’ll be taken to exile.
[Job] [27]:[23] Then, all men will be clapping their hands, And they’ll whistle at him from wherever they are.’
[Job] [28]:[1] ‘There’s a place where silver is mined, And a place where gold is refined.
[Job] [28]:[2] Men take iron out of the ground, And copper is quarried like stones.
[Job] [28]:[3] This is how He’s established an order for darkness, And precisely set all its limits. ‘Like the darkness [that’s inside a mine]… So is the shadow of death...
[Job] [28]:[4] And as they [pan for gold] in fast-running streams, The ways of the just are discovered… By mortal men, they’re sifted.
[Job] [28]:[5] Even our bread comes out of the ground As if roasted in fires down below.
[Job] [28]:[6] ‘There are places where sapphires are found, And places where gold may be mined.
[Job] [28]:[7] There are also roads that birds don’t know… By the eyes of eagles, they’re overlooked.
[Job] [28]:[8] They haven’t been walked by sons of the rich, Nor have lions ever been there.
[Job] [28]:[9] ‘For He sticks out His hand and chisels a place, And the roots of mountains, He overturns.

[Job] [28]:[11] ‘The depths of rivers, He’s laid bare, And in the [day]light, He’s shown all their might.
[Job] [28]:[12] But where can wisdom be found? And what’s the source of great knowledge?
[Job] [28]:[13] ‘For no man really knows of its ways, Since such ways can’t be found among men.

[Job] [36]:[17] ‘To the righteous, He’ll always bring justice,

[Job] [36]:[30] '{Look!} He’s stretched the light out above us, And the roots of the seas, He’s covered.

[Job] [42]:[1] Then Job spoke to the Lord saying:
[Job] [42]:[2] ‘I know that You can do all, And there is no end to Your power.
[Job] [42]:[3] So, who can hide their thoughts before You, And who can hold back their words, Thinking that You cannot [hear them]? ‘You’ve just told me some things that I never knew… Great and wonderful things, Of which I had no understanding.
[Job] [42]:[4] ‘So, listen to me, O my Lord, For, there are things that I’d like to say… I’ll ask You, and You can teach me!
[Job] [42]:[5] ‘In the past, I’ve heard men talk about You, But now that I’ve seen You with my own eyes,
[Job] [42]:[6] I think of myself as having no value. For before You, I’ve melted away, And I think of myself as ashes and dirt.’
[Job] [42]:[7] Well, after the Lord had spoken about all these things to Job, [Jehovah] then said this to EliPhaz the Temanite: ‘You and your two friends have sinned; For, you haven’t spoken the truth, As did My faithful friend Job.
[Job] [42]:[8] ‘So, take seven calves and seven rams, And carry them to My faithful friend Job, So that he can offer them on your behalf… For, no way do I hold him in blame. ‘If not for him, I would’ve destroyed you, Because of what you’ve said to My faithful friend.’
[Job] [42]:[9] So, EliPhaz the Temanite, Baldad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Minaean went and did as [Jehovah] had told them. Then He forgave the sins that they’d committed against Job.
[Job] [42]:[10] Thereafter, [Jehovah] blest Job. And because they were his friends, he vowed to forgive those men for all their sins. Then [Jehovah] [blest Job] with double, giving him twice as much as he had before!
[Job] [42]:[11] And when his brothers and sisters heard of the good things that had happened to him, they all went to see him, and he ended up with twice as many friends as he had at first. Everyone ate and drank with him, and they offered him much consolation. Yet, they each wondered about all the things that had happened, and about all the things that [Jehovah] had done. Then each one gave him a lamb and an unmarked 4-drachma coin.
[Job] [42]:[12] So, [Jehovah] blest the ending for Job, and he gained much more than he had before. For He came to have: 10,000 cows, 4,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 oxen teams, and 1,000 grazing mares.
[Job] [42]:[13] Seven more sons were also born to him, and he had three more daughters.
[Job] [42]:[14] He named the first daughter Day, he named the second one Cinnamon, and he named the third one Horn of Plenty.
[Job] [42]:[15] And among all the women under the sky, nobody was prettier than Job’s daughters. He also gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
[Job] [42]:[16] Well, after his calamity had passed, Job lived on for 170 more years, reaching the age of 240. Job lived to see his sons, and the sons of his sons, through to the fourth generation.
[Job] [42]:[17] Thereafter, Job finally came to his end, an old man who had lived a full life.

[Psalms] [32]:[2] Blest are those in whom He doesn’t find sin, Or treacherous words in their mouths.
[Psalms] [32]:[3] I’ve become more settled as my bones have aged… I no longer cry out all day long.
[Psalms] [32]:[4] For, day and night, Your hand pressed against me, And in misery, I writhed, as though run through by thorns.
[Psalms] [32]:[5] My lawless deeds, I’ve admitted to You, And my sins, I’ve not tried to hide. I’ve openly confessed to the Lord About all of my lawless ways, And You forgave the godless thoughts in my heart.
[Psalms] [32]:[6] For this, the holy should pray at right times, So the flood will never approach them:
[Psalms] [32]:[7] ‘You’re my refuge from the troubles I face, And You’ve ransomed my soul From those who had me surrounded.’
[Psalms] [32]:[8] [And in response, God will reply]: ‘I’ll send understanding to you… I’ll teach you the ways you should go, And I’ll always watch over you.
[Psalms] [32]:[9] So don’t act like horses or mules That have to be bridled and don’t understand, And whose jaws must be squeezed to behave.’
[Psalms] [32]:[10] Sinners will be whipped many times, But, mercy surrounds those who trust in the Lord.
[Psalms] [32]:[11] So, you should find joy in [Jehovah]; Shout about Him in joy, all you righteous… Wholeheartedly boast about Him!
[Psalms] [33]:[0] A Psalm by David.
[Psalms] [33]:[1] You righteous ones – rejoice in [Jehovah], Because He blesses the upright.
[Psalms] [33]:[2] Play psalms to [Jehovah] on harps; Strum to Him on your lutes of 10 strings;
[Psalms] [33]:[3] Then before Him, sing a new song… Yes play, shout loudly, and cheer!
[Psalms] [33]:[4] The words of [Jehovah] are righteous; So, trust in the things that He does.
[Psalms] [33]:[5] For our God loves charity and fairness, And the earth is filled with His mercy.
[Psalms] [33]:[6] By the Word of [Jehovah], the skies came to be, And the breath from His mouth formed their powers.
[Psalms] [33]:[7] As in a leather bag, He pulled them together, And in treasuries of the deep, He put water.
[Psalms] [33]:[8] So, fear [Jehovah], all dwellers on earth; Before Him, let all stand in awe.
[Psalms] [33]:[9] For, He just spoke and it all came to be… When He gave the orders, it started.
[Psalms] [33]:[10] He wipes the plans of nations away, And annuls the devices and plots of their kings.
[Psalms] [33]:[11] But [Jehovah’s] Will lasts throughout the ages… From generation to generation are the things in His heart.
[Psalms] [33]:[12] So, Blest is the nation whose God is [Jehovah]… Those whom He’s chosen to inherit.
[Psalms] [33]:[13] From the heavens, [Jehovah] looks down, And He watches the things that sons of men do.
[Psalms] [33]:[14] From the home that He’s prepared, He watches those dwelling on earth.
[Psalms] [33]:[15] He’s the One who fashioned their hearts, And He keeps watch on the things that they do.
[Psalms] [33]:[16] So, Kings can’t be saved by large armies, And giants may not be saved by their might.
[Psalms] [33]:[17] So don’t look to a horse for salvation, For, even with their strength, you can lose.
[Psalms] [33]:[18] {Look!} [Jehovah] watches all those who fear Him… Those who put faith in His mercy.
[Psalms] [33]:[19] Only He can keep their lives from destruction, And in times of famine, provide them with food.
[Psalms] [33]:[20] So, we must wait on [Jehovah], For He’s our defender and helper.
[Psalms] [33]:[21] With your whole hearts, find joy in Him, And trust in His Holy Name.
[Psalms] [33]:[22] Please send us Your mercy, [Jehovah]; For in You, we’ve put all our faith.

[Psalms] [34]:[1] Throughout the age, I’ll give praise to [Jehovah]… His praises will stay on my lips,
[Psalms] [34]:[2] And I’ll praise the Lord with my life. So, listen you meek and be glad…
[Psalms] [34]:[3] Glorify [Jehovah] with me… Let’s praise His great Name together.
[Psalms] [34]:[4] I searched for the Lord and He heard me… He rescued me during my travels.
[Psalms] [34]:[5] So, come to Him… Be enlightened, And your faces will never be shamed.
[Psalms] [34]:[6] A poor man once called out to God and He heard, Then He rescued him from all his problems.
[Psalms] [34]:[7] God’s messengers camped all around him, And He saved this one who showed fear of His Name.
[Psalms] [34]:[8] Taste and see that our God is good, For those trusting in Him will always be blest!
[Psalms] [34]:[9] Yes, fear [Jehovah], you holy; For those fearing Him will lack nothing.
[Psalms] [34]:[10] And although the rich may become hungry and poor, Those seeking the Lord won’t lack anything good.
[Psalms] [34]:[11] Come to me, children, then listen, As I teach you the fear of [Jehovah]!
[Psalms] [34]:[12] Who is the man who doesn’t want life, And to see better days?
[Psalms] [34]:[13] Remove all that’s evil from your lips… Take treachery away from your tongues…
[Psalms] [34]:[14] Turn from what’s bad and do what’s good… Search for peace and pursue it!
[Psalms] [34]:[15] For, [Jehovah] keeps His eyes on the righteous, And His ears hear the things that they ask.
[Psalms] [34]:[16] But the face of [Jehovah] opposes the bad, And He wipes their memory from the land.
[Psalms] [34]:[17] The righteous call out and God hears them, Then He rescues them from all their problems.
[Psalms] [34]:[18] God’s near to those who have broken hearts, And He saves the humble in spirit.
[Psalms] [34]:[19] Although the righteous will have many problems; From such things, God will save them.
[Psalms] [34]:[20] For, [Jehovah] watches over their bones, And not a single one will be broken.
[Psalms] [34]:[21] In sadness, the sinners will come to their end, And condemned are those hating the righteous.
[Psalms] [34]:[22] But [Jehovah] will ransom the lives of His servants, And no way will He harm those who trust Him.
[Psalms] [35]:[0] A Psalm by David.
[Psalms] [35]:[1] O [Jehovah], Bring judgment on those who are doing me wrong… Wage war with those waging war!
[Psalms] [35]:[2] Take up Your weapons and shield me, my God; Arise and come to my aid!
[Psalms] [35]:[3] Swing Your sword at those who pursue me… Say that You’ll deliver my soul!
[Psalms] [35]:[4] May those seeking my life feel shame and remorse… May those wishing me bad retreat in disgrace.
[Psalms] [35]:[5] May they be like dust in the wind… May God’s messengers squeeze them all dry.
[Psalms] [35]:[6] May their road become slippery and dark, And may they be chased by God’s angels.
[Psalms] [35]:[7] Although I’ve done them no wrong; Snares, they’ve hidden before me, And about my inner person, they speak badly.
[Psalms] [35]:[8] So, let them be caught in the snares that they’ve set… May the snares that they hunt with, catch them… Into the traps that they’ve set, may they fall.
[Psalms] [35]:[9] I’ll praise [Jehovah] with my whole soul… Of His salvation, I’ll shout.
[Psalms] [35]:[10] With my bones, I’ll say to [Jehovah]: ‘O Lord, there’s no one else like You! For You rescue the poor with a hand that’s greater Than those who tear the needy to shreds.
[Psalms] [35]:[11] ‘For, they sent lying witnesses against me, And asked questions that I didn’t understand.
[Psalms] [35]:[12] They’ve repaid me with bad for the good things I’ve done, And left my soul barren.
[Psalms] [35]:[13] ‘Because of the troubles they’ve caused me, I’ve had to wear sackcloth and fast. So now, I pray that I might be restored.
[Psalms] [35]:[14] ‘As neighbors and brothers, they once were so kind; So in mourning and sadness, I’ve humbled my soul.
[Psalms] [35]:[15] But they happily gathered against me, And they were not sad when they cut me with whips.
[Psalms] [35]:[16] ‘They tried me and then they made fun… Against me, they were grinding their teeth.
[Psalms] [35]:[17] O [Jehovah], how long will You let this go on? Rescue my soul from their evil plans!’
[Psalms] [35]:[18] [Then God replied:] ‘O My only begotten, From those lions, I’m coming to save you. Then, before the assembly, I’ll praise you, And before those bad ones, I’ll lift you!’
[Psalms] [35]:[19] So, may those who hate me unjustly Not [be allowed to] rejoice… Those who detest me without any charge… Those who looked away with their eyes.
[Psalms] [35]:[20] Even though to me, they once spoke of peace, In anger and treachery, they’ve plotted.
[Psalms] [35]:[21] They’ve opened their mouths against me and said: ‘Well done… Yes, very well done. For we’ve seen it all happen with our own eyes.’
[Psalms] [35]:[22] O [Jehovah], You’ve witnessed it all! So, don’t remain silent or leave me.
[Psalms] [35]:[23] Awaken, O Lord… Pay attention! Take notice of my cause, O my God.
[Psalms] [35]:[24] Judge me, O Lord, and bring justice… My God, don’t let them rejoice!
[Psalms] [35]:[25] Don’t allow them to say of my soul in their hearts: ‘Well done… Yes, very well done.’ And please don’t allow them to say: We’ve swallowed him down!
[Psalms] [35]:[26] May those who have rejoiced at my harm feel ashamed, And may those who witnessed against me feel bad,
[Psalms] [35]:[27] As those who seek justice are joyful. Then, may they cry: ‘Praise [Jehovah], Because He brought peace to His servant!’
[Psalms] [35]:[28] Then I’ll use my tongue to sing of Your justice, And I’ll praise You throughout the rest of my days.

[Psalms] [37]:[0] A Psalm by David.
[Psalms] [37]:[1] Never be jealous of the wicked, Nor envy those who break laws.
[Psalms] [37]:[2] For like grass, they’ll quickly be dried, And they’ll wilt away like young shoots.
[Psalms] [37]:[3] Rather, put your hope in [Jehovah], And always act in kind ways. Its wealth will serve those who live off the ground,

[Psalms] [37]:[8] And never be angry… Abandon your rage! Don’t let jealousy move you to do what’s wicked,
[Psalms] [37]:[9] For the wicked will soon be destroyed, As those who wait on [Jehovah] Will thereafter inherit the land.
[Psalms] [37]:[10] Soon the sinners will no longer be here… You’ll look where he was and not find him.
[Psalms] [37]:[11] But, the meek will inherit the land, And find great delight in the abundance of peace.
[Psalms] [37]:[12] For, sinners keep their eyes on the righteous And grind their teeth when they see them.

[Psalms] [37]:[15] But, may their swords strike their own hearts, And may their bows be broken to bits.
[Psalms] [37]:[16] A little is better to the righteous Than an abundance of wealth is to sinners.
[Psalms] [37]:[17] For the arms of sinners will be broken, And the Lord will support all the just.
[Psalms] [37]:[18] He knows the ways of the flawless, And their inheritance will last throughout the ages.
[Psalms] [37]:[19] They won’t be disgraced in hard times, And when famine arrives, they’ll be filled.

[Psalms] [37]:[21] The sinners borrow and don’t repay, But the righteous feel mercy and lend.
[Psalms] [37]:[22] So, those praising them will inherit the land, While those who curse them will be wiped away.
[Psalms] [37]:[23] [Jehovah] straightens the footsteps of men, And all should [walk in] His ways.
[Psalms] [37]:[24] Then, if you should fall, you won’t break; For the Lord will be holding your hand.
[Psalms] [37]:[25] I was once young, and now I’ve grown old; Yet I’ve never seen the righteous abandoned, Or his offspring ever begging for bread.
[Psalms] [37]:[26] Because, each day, he shows mercy and lends; His offspring will always be blest.
[Psalms] [37]:[27] So, turn from evil… Do what’s good, And live throughout ages of ages!
[Psalms] [37]:[28] For [Jehovah] is a lover of justice, And throughout the ages, He won’t abandon the holy… So the righteous will always be guarded, As the lawless are driven away. The offspring of the Godless will perish;
[Psalms] [37]:[29] But the righteous will inherit [the] land, And throughout ages of ages, they’ll camp there.
[Psalms] [37]:[30] Mouths of the righteous think first and then speak… They talk of fairness and justice.
[Psalms] [37]:[31] And because they have God’s Law in their hearts, They won’t stumble and fall.
[Psalms] [37]:[32] But, when the sinner thinks of the righteous, He searches for ways to destroy them.
[Psalms] [37]:[33] Yet, [God] won’t abandon them into their hands, Nor in the judgment, will they be condemned.

[Psalms] [38]:[15] For in You, O [Jehovah], I’ve put all my trust… And my God, I’ve hoped that You’d listen.

[Proverbs] [9]:[16] ‘You who are the most foolish; Turn aside and come here to me!’ She arouses the stupid by saying:
[Proverbs] [9]:[17] ‘You’ll touch secret ‘bread loaves’ in pleasure, And steal ‘sweet water’ to drink!’
[Proverbs] [9]:[18] But the thing that they don’t understand, Is that she brings destruction upon earthly men… That she’s perching them on the edge to the grave!

[Proverbs] [31]:[22] ‘A doubled coat made of goat’s hair, She has sewn for her man; And from the bolt-ends of linen and purple, She’s also made one for herself.
[Proverbs] [31]:[23] So, her man is admired when he sits at the gate, And meets with the rest of the elders.
[Proverbs] [31]:[24] ‘She takes fine linen to make loincloths For all of her CanaAnite [servants].
[Proverbs] [31]:[25] She’s [proud] of her strength and her beauty, And is happy throughout the rest of her days.
[Proverbs] [31]:[26] ‘She opens her mouth to speak wisdom and Law, And charity rests on her tongue.
[Proverbs] [31]:[27] Her pastimes are things that shelter her home, And the grain of laziness, she doesn’t eat.
[Proverbs] [31]:[28] ‘She raises her sons so they will grow rich, And her man sings praises of her.
[Proverbs] [31]:[29] Her many daughters will also be rich By doing the things that she’s [taught them]. ‘But, you are still the first [in her eyes]… Above all the rest, she holds you.
[Proverbs] [31]:[30] ‘For, beauty and allurement are false; So, that isn’t what you should seek. Rather, find a woman who has praised and discerning… One who is known for her fear of God.
[Proverbs] [31]:[31] Take from her, the fruit of her lips, And you’ll always be praised at the gates.’
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[1] These are the sayings of the great congregator, son of David, the king of IsraEl in JeruSalem.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[2] The Great Congregator said: ‘All is foolishness and waste, Foolishness and waste… All that’s done is in vain.’
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[3] ‘What value does man gain from the things he’s done, And the things he’s worked hard for under the sun?
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[4] ‘For, one generation passes away, And then another arrives… Yet, the earth remains throughout the ages.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[5] ‘The sun keeps on rising and setting As it draws to it’s place,
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[6] And the winds blow in from the south, As they move north in a circle… Then they go back and come ‘round again.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[7] ‘Even though all the rivers flow into the sea, The sea doesn’t become filled. For, to the places from which they all came, They return and flow back again.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[8] ‘So, no man can speak all the words he might say, And his eyes can’t be filled with all he can see, Nor can his ears handle all that they hear.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[9] ‘What’s this thing that [just] happened? The same thing will happen again! What’s this thing being done? The same will be done in the future… For there’s nothing that’s new under the sun!
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[10] ‘Who can say, Look, here’s something new? For the same thing has happened for ages To those who have lived before us.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[11] But the things that they did were forgotten, And those who are born in the future Won’t remember the things that we’re doing now.’
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[12] The great congregator is the king over all of IsraEl from JeruSalem.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[13] ‘So I set my heart to survey and inquire About all that has happened under the sky. God gave me this to distract me from bad, And to lead sons of men back to Him.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[14] ‘I’ve seen all that’s done under the sun, And I find it to be a waste of [good] breath.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[15] For, things that go wrong are never made right, And there’s too much that’s wrong to be counted.
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[16] ‘Once I spoke in my heart and I said: ‘Look how great I’ve become! For, I’ve been given more wisdom Than all who have lived before me!’ ‘So, I set my heart to learn wisdom and knowledge;
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[17] And wisdom and knowledge, my heart then beheld, As well as higher learning and proverbs. ‘So, it became the resolve of my spirit
[Ecclesiastes] [1]:[18] To gain an abundance of wisdom, Along with vast volumes of knowledge. But, those who gain knowledge also gain pain.’
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[1] ‘Then I said to my heart: ‘Well come now; I’ll [fill] you with joy and then you’ll know good!’ ‘But, even that was just folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[2] ‘To laughter, I said, ‘You’re a burden!’ And to joy, I asked, ‘What have you achieved?’
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[3] So I thought in my heart: ‘I’ll drink wine for my flesh!’ ‘But my heart then led me towards wisdom. ‘Next, I decided to hold onto joy Until I could see just what kind of good There is to be found among sons of men, And what they can do in their short years of life.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[4] ‘So thereafter, I went into action… I planted vineyards and built many homes.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[5] I made myself gardens and parks, Which I planted with all sorts of fruit.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[6] ‘Around them, I dug ponds and lakes To water the groves filled with trees.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[7] I acquired many slaves (both men and women), And many native servants were born. ‘I also acquired great herds and flocks… More than all who had come before me.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[8] I collected much silver and gold for myself… The possessions of kings and estates. ‘I prepared for myself, many singers… Men and women, I brought to amuse me. I had men and women who just served me wine.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[9] ‘Then, I became great as my wisdom increased (More than all who had come before me); And indeed, my wisdom was proven.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[10] ‘Everything that I could ask for Was there in front of my eyes, And no joy was withheld from my heart. But, although these efforts of my heart brought me joy; This was the sum of all I’d achieved.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[11] ‘For, when I looked at the things I had done, And the things that I’d made with my hands… When I considered the effort it took, I saw that it all was just folly. Since, no matter what our spirits may choose to do; It brings no advantage under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[12] ‘So thereafter, I examined my wisdom, And I saw that it too was just folly. For, who under the sun will follow my words… Which man will do [what I’ve said]? And although the wise may have eyes in their heads, The fools will still travel in darkness. ‘I also realized that both them and I Will eventually all meet together.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[15] So, in my heart I said this: ‘Since the fate of fools will also take me; What value is there in my wisdom?’ ‘And I also said this in my heart: ‘The things that I’ve said about being a fool Are also just [wasted breath];
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[16] For, both the wise the fools are forgotten, And what they do won’t be remembered. So, how are the wise any better than fools?’
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[17] ‘Then, I became disgusted with life; For, all that I’ve done under the sun Will eventually end up as bad… It’s all foolish and a waste [of good] breath.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[18] ‘I became disgusted with all of the things That I had accomplished under the sun, For I’ll leave it to the one who comes next…
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[19] And who knows if he’s wise or another poor fool… Who knows if he’ll care for the things I’ve made, Or the things I’ve learned under the sun? So, all of this is just folly!
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[20] ‘Thus I turned to dismiss it all from my heart… All the results of my efforts, And all that I’d made under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[21] ‘For there’s a man who worked hard to gain wisdom, As well as knowledge and courage. But, there’s also a man who made no such effort, And he will receive the same fate. So, this is a great wicked folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[22] ‘What happens to a man and his efforts, And the resolves of his heart under the sun?
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[23] During all of his days there’s pain, And rage over things that are being destroyed; So, during the night, his heart knows no rest… Indeed, this too is just folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[24] ‘Nothing worthwhile comes to a man But eating, drinking, and searching for good… These things truly come from God’s hands;
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[25] For, without Him, who is able to eat or to drink?
[Ecclesiastes] [2]:[26] ‘To those whom He declares to be good, He bequeaths wisdom, knowledge, and joy… But, from the sinners, He rips this away! They’re just given to those whom He finds to be good, And to those who can stand before Him. Yet, this is also just folly, And just a waste of [good] breath.’
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[1] ‘For all that’s under the sky There’s a season and time…
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[2] ‘There are times to give birth and times that bring death; There are times to plant and to harvest;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[3] ‘There are times to heal and times to destroy; There are times to build and tear down;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[4] ‘There are times to laugh and to cry; There are times for mourning and dancing;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[5] ‘There are times to pick stones and to throw them; There are times to hug and times to reject;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[6] ‘There are times to lose and to find; There are times to collect and discard;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[7] ‘There are times to plant and times to rip out; There are times to speak or be quiet;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[8] ‘There are times to love and times to show hate; There are times for peace and for war…
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[9] ‘So, what can your efforts accomplish?
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[10] ‘I’ve seen the amusements God’s given To the sons of men to distract them…
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[11] Yes, all that God’s made is good in its time. And although He’s put the ages into our hearts, No man can know all that’s been done From the most ancient times to the present.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[12] ‘I knew that there’s nothing good in [his efforts], Unless they please [him] And do him good in life;
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[13] So, when a man has it all (All that he needs to eat and to drink), He will know that his ways have been blest, And he’ll know that these gifts came from God.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[14] ‘All that God does lasts through ages; So to them, you can add nothing more, Nor can you take it away. For, all that God has accomplished Was done so we’d live before Him in fear.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[15] And all that is, has been before… Yes, it’s all happened before, And God searches to see what we’ve chosen.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[16] ‘I’ve also noticed that under the sun, There’s a place where the godless are judged And a place where the righteous are judged.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[17] So, in my heart, I’ve concluded That both the unrighteous and just will be judged. Yes, there’s a season for all, And for every deed, there’s a right time.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[18] ‘I said in my heart what sons of men say… That God views us like we’re cattle.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[19] For, man’s outcome is the same as his herds… As this one dies, so dies the other, Since we all share the very same breath. ‘So, how are men better than cattle? They aren’t, And it’s all just a joke!
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[20] For we all return to the very same place… We come from the dust and return to the dust.
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[21] So, who knows if man’s breath goes upward, Or the breath of his cattle goes into the ground?
[Ecclesiastes] [3]:[22] In all of this, I saw [little] that’s good, Except to find joy in the things that we do… Yes, this is all we’ve been given. For, who’ll lead us to see The things that will happen after [we’re gone]?
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[1] ‘Yes, I’ve turned and I’ve seen it all… The extortions and other such things That will happen to all under the sun. I’ve seen power in the hands of extorters, And I’ve seen the tears of the swindled… Then, no one arrived to bring comfort.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[2] ‘I’ve also praised the things of the dead; For, more have died than have lived,
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[3] And the best of these two is the one not yet born… The one who has not seen the evil In what will be done under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[4] ‘I beheld all their efforts and acts of great courage… Men’s rivalries with their companions. And I see that it all is just foolish… It’s all a huge waste of breath.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[5] ‘The fool folds his hands… Then he eats his own flesh!
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[6] But it’s better to enjoy a handful in peace Than to have twice as much in distress; For, this is also a waste of good breath.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[7] ‘I turned and noticed man’s foolish ways… All that he’s done under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[8] For, there are those who live all alone, And who have had no dependents. But, although they have no brothers or sons, They deprive their lives of things that are good. And indeed, this too is just folly… It’s just a distraction from evil.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[9] ‘Two are better than living alone, For the efforts of two return a good wage…
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[10] If he stumbles, his partner will lift him. But, woe to the one who stumbles and falls, And has no partner to raise him.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[11] ‘When two share a bed, they’ll be warm… But, one alone can’t keep himself warm.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[12] And a person alone can be beaten, While two make a better defense… Yet a three-corded rope is harder to break.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[13] ‘It’s better to be a poor but wise child Than a king who is foolish and old… One who no longer listens [to council].
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[14] For he reigns within his own ‘prison,’ And in his own kingdom, has nothing.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[15] ‘I’ve gazed upon all of the living (All who are walking under the sun), And I see the next generation That will soon become their replacements.
[Ecclesiastes] [4]:[16] ‘There’s no limit to all of the people, Or to those who have come before. And since the last take no joy in the first; This too is foolish and a waste of good breath.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[1] ‘Watch your feet as you enter God’s House (Whenever you go there to listen), And bring an offering that’s better Than the rest of the gifts of the foolish Who are unaware of the evil that comes.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[2] ‘Don’t let your mouths speak too quickly Or let your hearts be too hasty When making [a vow] in the presence of God. For, God is up in the heavens, And you’re here on the earth; So, let your words remain few.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[3] ‘As many [concerns] bring [bad] dreams; Many words are heard from the voices of fools.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[4] So, when you make a vow to [your] God, Don’t waste any time to repay it, Since He doesn’t like vows that are foolishly made. ‘So, whatever you vow, you should bring!
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[5] And it’s best that you don’t make a vow Than to vow and then fail to pay it!
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[6] ‘Don’t let your mouth lead your flesh into sin, And don’t say too much in the presence of God. [Don’t say] stupid things, And don’t make Him angry with your words, Or He’ll bring destruction to the works of your hands.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[7] ‘So, although you may have many daydreams and follies, Fear to say many words, Whenever you stand before God.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[8] ‘If you see the needy extorted and robbed By lawsuits or other legal actions; Don’t give this too much attention. For, from above, the High One keeps watch… He sees all that happens under [the sky].
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[9] ‘And although the land’s bounty is there for us all, Even a king needs his fields to be worked.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[10] ‘But for those who love silver, there’s never enough, And with plenty comes even more young… And indeed, this too is just folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[11] For, when you have many good things, There’ll also be many to eat it. So what value is there in getting much more, When it’s just to be seen by your eyes?
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[12] ‘Sleep is always sweet to a slave, Whether he has little or much… But the rich never get enough sleep.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[13] ‘I’ve seen all this illness under the sun… For there are those who store up much treasure,
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[14] Which is thereafter lost in hard times. So, wealth is just a distraction from bad. ‘When a man fathers a son, The child arrives here with nothing at all.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[15] Naked he comes from his mother’s womb, And when he dies, he leaves the same way… With nothing to show for his efforts, And nothing to carry back in his hands.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[16] ‘Indeed, this is illness that’s evil; For, as he arrives is how he returns. And what advantage has he gained from his efforts, When they’re [blown away] in the wind?
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[17] ‘In darkness and mourning, men fill their days… In anger, illness, and rage.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[18] Yet, I’ve seen good in the things that we eat and drink, And I’ve also seen good from man’s efforts… In the things he’s accomplished under the sun, And in the portion that God has allowed him.
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[19] ‘For, those who gain wealth and possessions from God, Are allowed to own them and eat them. Thus, they reap the joy of their efforts… And these are [the true] gifts from God!
[Ecclesiastes] [5]:[20] So, although they’ll forget most days of their lives, God amuses them with the joy in their hearts.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[1] ‘There’s something bad that I’ve seen, Which is common to all under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[2] It’s when God gives a man wealth, Along with possessions, and glory, So that he lacks nothing his soul could desire… Then he’s not allowed the time to [enjoy] it, And thereafter, it’s given to strangers… Yes, this is a sickness and folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[3] ‘If a man should live to 100 (No matter how long the days of his years), And his life has never known good things; Before he’s buried, I’d say: ‘It would have been better if he’d been miscarried.’
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[4] For, from darkness he came and in darkness he left, And in darkness his name will be covered.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[5] ‘Indeed, he knew not the sun, And none would know him from others.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[6] And if he came back and lived thousands [of years], But he still never saw any good; Wouldn’t things still be the same?
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[7] ‘So, all men can do is just fill their mouths, Since their lives never reach their fulfillment.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[8] And what advantage have the wise over fools? For, only the poor put just living first.

[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[10] ‘Whenever something new comes along, It was already named [in the past]. And although a man may know his own [strength], He can’t know when someone is stronger.
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[11] ‘There’s so much that makes foolishness grow,
[Ecclesiastes] [6]:[12] And what does this mean for a man? Who knows what will be the best parts in his life, Or how many of his days will be foolish? For, his life is much like a shadow, And who can report to a man What under the sun will succeed him?’
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[1] ‘A good name is better than oil, And the day that you die is much greater Than the day you were born.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[2] ‘So it’s better to go to a funeral Than to spend time at a banquet… For, that’s the end of all men, And it’s good for all who are living To take such good warnings to heart.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[3] ‘Indignant rage is better than laughter; For a face that’s been hurt creates a good heart.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[4] So the wise at heart are at funerals, While the foolish heart [searches for] pleasure.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[5] ‘It’s better to hear the scolding of the wise Than to listen to the [praising] of fools.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[6] ‘As the [crackling] of tinder under a pot, Is the sound of the laughter of fools; For, this is also just folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[7] ‘Extortion makes wise people crazy; For it destroys the greatest plans of their hearts.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[8] ‘The way that a matter turns out Is [more important] than how it began. ‘It’s better [for a man] to forgive Than to have a high-minded spirit.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[9] ‘Don’t get angry too quickly; For, rage rests in the bosoms of fools.
[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[10] ‘Don’t ask why past days were better; For in asking such things, there’s no wisdom.

[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[13] ‘Behold the actions of God; For, who can add to the things that He brings?

[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[17] Nor should you be disrespectful of them, Lest you harden and die before it’s your time.

[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[24] It’s too high above me and too deep below; So, who is able to find it?

[Ecclesiastes] [7]:[28] Seeking for such ones with my whole soul… But, I was unable to find A man in a thousand who is [righteous], And none at all among women!

[Ecclesiastes] [8]:[4] And then, who can ask of the king: ‘Why did you make [that decision]?’
