And although the wise speak of knowledge, They too are unable to find it. But because I gave my heart to discernment; These are the things that my heart came to see.’
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[1] ‘The deeds of the righteous and wise Are in the hands of our God. And with all of their loves and dislikes, Man can’t really comprehend it…
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[2] For, foolish are the ways of all men! ‘There are things that happen to the righteous, And things that happen to the godless… And to either, can come good or evil. ‘There are also the clean and unclean; There are those who bring sacrifices, And those who offer God nothing. Yet, the same things [can happen to] both… To the good as well as the sinners… To those who choose to swear oaths, And to those who fear to swear oaths.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[3] In all of this, there’s evil In what’s done under the sun… For the same things can happen to both. ‘Indeed; men’s hearts are filled with what’s bad, And it leads them to madness throughout their lives… Then they go to the grave.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[4] ‘But, for the living, there’s still hope, Since a living dog is much greater Than a mighty lion that has died.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[5] For the living know that they’ll die, While the dead know nothing at all, Nor do they have a wage, Since the memory of them is forgotten.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[6] ‘Their loves and dislikes are both gone, And their zeal has already perished. Then, throughout the age they’ll not be involved In whatever is done under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[7] ‘So, eat your bread in contentment, And drink to your heart with fine wines… And God will think well of your actions.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[8] ‘May your clothes always be white, And may there be plenty of oil for your head.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[9] ‘Share what you have with the woman you’ve loved All the days of your wasted life. For it’s all that you’ll get under the sun, Since the days of your life are a folly… Yes, this is the sum of your life For all of your efforts under the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[10] ‘So whatever your hands find to do, Do it with all of your power! For, there’s no doing, thinking, wisdom, or knowledge In the place of the dead, where you’re going.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[11] ‘I turned and I saw that under the sun, The race isn’t won by those quick on their feet, Nor are battles all won by the mighty. The wise aren’t always those who eat bread, And the discerning aren’t always the rich; Nor are those with knowledge shown favor. ‘Yet, there’s a time and a meeting for all,
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[12] And no one knows when this time will arrive. As fish being caught in a net, And as birds being trapped in a snare; The sons of men will be swiftly caught In a bad time that arrives all too quickly.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[13] ‘I’ve beheld all this wisdom under sun, And it rests heavily upon me.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[14] ‘If a city is small with just a few men, And a mighty king comes to attack, Building high siege mounds around it;
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[15] And if a wise man who is poor can be found there, And his wisdom results in saving that town; All will forget that he’d been poor.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[16] ‘So, this is what I can tell you: ‘Wisdom is better than power.’ But the wisdom of the poor is treated with contempt, And none pay attention to their words.
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[17] Yet, the words of the wise who have nothing Should be heeded over the words of the foolish Who may have been given the power,
[Ecclesiastes] [9]:[18] Since wisdom is better than weapons of war, And a single error can wipe out the good.’
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[1] ‘As a dead fly can spoil a good ointment; A little folly can conquer great wisdom.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[2] ‘The hearts of the wise are at their right hands, But the hearts of fools stay on their left.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[3] So, whichever way a fool chooses to go; In his heart, he’s sure that he’ll fail, Since he thinks that he can’t succeed.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[4] ‘If the spirit of a ruler flares against you, Don’t turn away from your place; For, [patience] heals all great sins.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[5] ‘I’ve observed a wickedness under the sun… It’s when a ruler does something in haste,
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[6] And puts a fool over important things, While those who have proven their worth are put low…
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[7] I’ve seen ‘slaves’ who are riding on horses, And ‘princes’ who are walking as slaves on the ground.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[8] ‘The one who is digging a cesspool Is also the one who’ll fall in it; And those who move boundary markers, Will find themselves bitten by snakes.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[9] ‘Quarry workers may be harmed by the rocks [they’ve hewn], And those who split logs are in danger.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[10] ‘If the axe isn’t sharp, you’ll work harder; So, doing what’s wise paves the way to success.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[11] ‘If a snake-charmer whispers and the serpent still bites; All of his charming is worthless.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[12] ‘Words from a wise mouth bring favor, While foolish lips rip it away.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[13] And if foolish words are accepted; It’ll end in what’s wicked and crazy.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[14] ‘The fool often speaks many words, Although he doesn’t really know what will happen, Or what will soon come to be. So, who’ll walk behind and announce him?
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[15] ‘The efforts of fools bring them trouble… For, they know not the right ways to enter a town.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[16] ‘Woe to you, O great city, Where your king is just a young [man], And your princes eat meals in the mornings.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[17] Rather, blest is the land Where the king has been born of nobles, And whose princes eat at the right times. For, the things that they eat makes them strong, So they will never be shamed.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[18] ‘By sloth and neglect a home [falls apart], And with idle hands, [its roof] starts to leak.
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[19] ‘Bread, wine, and oil are made to cause laughter, And to bring joy to the living… But, they must also be [paid for].
[Ecclesiastes] [10]:[20] ‘Never curse a king in your mind, Nor curse the rich in your bedrooms or closets. For your words will be carried by birds in the skies, And those with wings will report what you’ve said.’
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[1] ‘Scatter your seeds on the water, And after some time, you’ll find them.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[2] Yes, share what you have with seven or eight [other people], Since you don’t know what bad may come to the land.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[3] ‘If clouds become filled, they’ll send rain to the ground. And if a tree falls towards the north of the south, Wherever it falls, it’ll stay.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[4] So, those who look to the wind may not plant, And those who look to the clouds may not reap.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[5] For, attempting to know which way the wind blows, Is like knowing the bones in the womb of a mother… You don’t know the actions of God, Or any of the things He will do.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[6] ‘So, start your planting in the morning, And don’t rest your hand ‘til the evening; For, you never know what will grow over there, Or what will grow best over here… Or if the two will grow well together.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[7] ‘Daylight is sweet and it’s good for the eyes To be able to see by the sun.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[8] But, although a man’s years may bring him much joy, He will also know many days that are dark… And all that will come is just folly.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[9] ‘Take joy, young man, in your youth; And may your heart do good while you’re young. May your heart walk in ways that are pure, Not in the ways that you see with your eyes… For, know that this leads to God’s judgment.
[Ecclesiastes] [11]:[10] ‘So, remove all the rage from your heart, And all the wicked ways from your flesh; For, youth’s thoughtless ways are all folly!’
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[1] ‘Remember your Creator in the days of your youth; For, bad days will come [all too soon], And the years will arrive when you’ll say: ‘I never really wanted [to see] them!’
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[2] ‘[It’s a time when] the ‘sun’ becomes dark, And you’ll not see the light of the moon or the stars, Or the clouds passing by after rain.
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[3] ‘It’s a day when the ‘watchman’ starts to tremble… When the powerful man is bent double, And the grinders cease, because they are few. Then, ‘women’ will stare from their ‘windows’ at darkness,
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[4] And they will lock all their doors In fear of the sounds of those grinding in the market. ‘Then the sound of a sparrow will wake you, And the daughters of song will be humbled.
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[5] From above, you’ll look down and see Frightening things on the road. ‘Then, at the time when ‘almonds’ should blossom, The ‘locusts’ will grow to be many, And ‘capers’ will drop on the ground… For, you’ll have gone to your home of the ages. ‘Then, people will circle the market, Beating their chests in mourning for you.
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[6] For the silver cord has been severed; The gold decoration is broken; The bucket at the well has been shattered; And the wheel has rolled into the pit.
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[7] ‘For, that which is dust went back to the ground From which it once had been taken; And the breath has also returned To the God by whom it was given.’
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[8] Says the great congregator: ‘Oh how silly and foolish!’
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[9] Yet to him, came even more wisdom, And he taught all his knowledge to men… He traced it all out and composed it as proverbs.
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[10] The Great Congregator searched for the words, And he wrote them as right ways of truth:
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[11] ‘As words to the wise and as ox goads… As nails that are hammered in tight. They’re agreeable things from a shepherd;
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[12] So, carefully guard them, my son! ‘For, many scrolls have been written (Yes, to them, there’s no end), And spending much time thinking about them Is just a weariness to the flesh.
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[13] ‘But listen, for this is what I’ve concluded: ‘Fear God and keep His Commandments… This is all that there is for a man!
[Ecclesiastes] [12]:[14] ‘The rest just leads to judgment by God, Who decides whether we have been bad or good.’

[Isaiah] [33]:[2] O [Jehovah], Show mercy upon us, For we are relying on You. Destroy the offspring of those who oppose us, But save us in our time of oppression!
[Isaiah] [33]:[3] Your fearful sounds will startle the people, And in fear, the nations will scatter.
[Isaiah] [33]:[4] But then, You will gather Your spoils great and small As though You were picking up locusts.

[Isaiah] [33]:[6] In that time, He’ll become [a] foundation that’s firm… A source of salvation, wisdom, and knowledge. For in Him, all wisdom and knowledge exists… And fear of God [is the key] to this treasure.

[Isaiah] [33]:[8] Since that will bring [an] end to their [evil] ways. And the nations will also have reasons for fear, Because of the treaties they’ve broken, And because they’ve [not shown You] respect.

[Isaiah] [33]:[11] When you see it, you’ll then understand That their other efforts have all been in vain. ‘For their spirits will be burned as by fire…
[Isaiah] [33]:[12] By the gentiles, they will be consumed Like thorn bushes out in the fields, Which have been tossed in the flames.
[Isaiah] [33]:[13] ‘Then, from far away, they’ll hear what I’ve done; And those who come here will know of My might.
[Isaiah] [33]:[14] For, when the lawless are taken from Zion, The irreverent will all start to shake. ‘So, who will make the announcement… The announcement that the fire has been lit? Yes, who will speak of such things In this ancient place of the ages?
[Isaiah] [33]:[15] Just the one who is walking uprightly; The one who tells things just as they are; The one who hates lawless ways and injustice; The one whose hands shake off bribes; The one who won’t listen to judgments of blood And whose eyelids are closed to injustice.
[Isaiah] [33]:[16] ‘At that time, he will stay in [a] cave in the heights, Which is surrounded by boulders. His bread will also be given to him, And he can trust [that he will have] water.

[Isaiah] [33]:[18] And your souls will contemplate fear. ‘Then, what will happen to all of the scribes… What will happen to all the advisors… What will happen to the accountants and their records?
[Isaiah] [33]:[19] ‘From the small to the great, they don’t take advice, Nor do they heed any warnings About the ways they’re mistreating the people… So, none understand what [I’m saying].
[Isaiah] [33]:[20] ‘O great city on Zion; Look and see your salvation… See JeruSalem as [a] city of wealth, Filled with unshakable tents. ‘There the tent poles will last throughout the ages, So their cords won’t have to be pulled,
[Isaiah] [33]:[21] And they’ll be called by the Name of [Jehovah]. ‘There’ll be aqueducts and wide rivers; But, you will not travel upon them, For boats will never be rowed there.’
[Isaiah] [33]:[22] So my God, [Jehovah], won’t pass me by, Because the Lord is our judge… Yes, He is our ruler and king, And He will bring us salvation!
[Isaiah] [33]:[23] But now, all their ropes will be pulled up, And the masts on their boats will be weak… They’ll lean, so their sails cannot be unfurled, And their flags will never be raised Until all that they have has been plundered… Yes, taken by even the lame!
[Isaiah] [33]:[24] But those who are left won’t say they are tired, For their sins will have all been forgiven.

[Isaiah] [36]:[1] It was in the 14th year of the reign of [King] HezekiAh [of Judah] that King SenNaCherib of Assyria [marched against] the fortified cities of Judah and took them.
[Isaiah] [36]:[2] Then the king of Assyria sent RabShakeh from LachIsh to King HezekiAh in JeruSalem with [a] huge army, and he [set up camp] by the aqueduct to the upper pool, which is on the road to the field of the washerwomen.
[Isaiah] [36]:[3] So, EliAkim (son of HilkiAh) [the King’s] house manager, the scribe ShebNa, and JoAh (son of Asaph) the recorder, went out to meet with him.

[Isaiah] [36]:[6] ‘Look! If you’re relying on that fractured reed cane Egypt… If [a] man should put his weight on [that reed], it will go all the way through his hand! Yes, this is all that PharaOh, the king of Egypt, and those who are relying on him amount to!
[Isaiah] [36]:[7] ‘And if you should say that you’re relying on your God [Jehovah]… Isn’t He the same One whose high places and altars were removed by HezekiAh, and who then told Judah and JeruSalem that they had to come and bow before the Altar here in this place?
[Isaiah] [36]:[8] ‘Why not rather join with my lord the king of Assyria? For if you do, I’ll give you 2,000 horses… That is, if you’re able to provide enough riders for them!
[Isaiah] [36]:[9] ‘Can your governors who are relying on the Egyptians provide you with that many horses and riders?
[Isaiah] [36]:[10] ‘And do you think that we were able to come up to this place and wage war against it without [the aid of] [Jehovah]? It was [Jehovah] that told us to come to this land and destroy it!’

[Isaiah] [36]:[15] And don’t let HezekiAh tell you that his God will rescue you; for there’s no way that He can save this city from the hands of the king of Assyria!’
[Isaiah] [36]:[16] ‘The king of Assyria says: ‘Don’t listen to HezekiAh! ‘If you want to receive his blessings, come here to me and you’ll each eat from your own grapevines and fig trees, and drink water from your own wells.

[Isaiah] [36]:[18] ‘So, don’t let HezekiAh deceive you and say: ‘Our God will come and save us!’ ‘Have any of the gods of the nations been able to rescue their own places from the hands of the king of Assyria?

[Isaiah] [36]:[20] Since none of these gods of the nations could rescue their lands from my hands, how can [Jehovah] save JeruSalem from my hands?’

[Jeremiah] [1]:[3] All of this happened from the time of JehoiAkim (son of JosiAh) the king of Judah, until the 11th year of ZedekiAh (son of JosiAh) the king of Judah – and [the beginning of] the captivity of JeruSalem, [which happened] in the 5th month.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[4] The Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Jeremiah] [1]:[5] ‘I knew you before you were formed in the womb And before you came from the belly. So I chose you and I made you holy To serve as a Prophet to the nations.’
[Jeremiah] [1]:[6] But I said: ‘O Great Being… O Lord… O [Jehovah], '{Look!} I don’t know how to speak, for I’m just a young man.’
[Jeremiah] [1]:[7] And the Lord told me: ‘Don’t say that you’re just a young man; For you’ll go to whomever I send you And you’ll speak whatever I tell you to say!
[Jeremiah] [1]:[8] So, don’t be afraid when you go before them, Since I’m with you and I will protect you.’

[Jeremiah] [1]:[12] Then the Lord said to me: ‘You are [very observant]; And I’m [watching to see if you’ll] do as I [say].’
[Jeremiah] [1]:[13] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me a second time and asked: ‘What do you see now?’ And I replied: ‘I see a kettle over a fire, and the front side of it is facing the north.’
[Jeremiah] [1]:[14] Then the Lord said to me: ‘Thus, from the face of the north, All those who are bad will be burned away From among those who live in the land.
[Jeremiah] [1]:[15] For, {Look!} this is what was said by [Jehovah]: ‘From the north, I’ll be gathering kingdoms That will come, and then, they’ll each place their thrones On the thresholds of JeruSalem’s gates, And on the walls of the cities of Judah.

[Jeremiah] [2]:[27] ‘For they’ve said to a tree, ‘You’re my father;’ And they’ve said to a stone, ‘You gave me life.’ ‘Yet, although they have all turned their backs (But not their faces) towards Me; When hard times arrive, they’ll still say: ‘O [Jehovah], please save us!’
[Jeremiah] [2]:[28] ‘Will [your idols] still save you in difficult times, And will [you turn] to these gods that you’ve made? ‘In Judah, each city now has its own gods, And in all of JeruSalem’s streets They offer sacrifices to BaAl.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[29] So, why are you even talking to me?’ ‘[Jehovah] says: ‘You’ve been irreverent and lawless towards Me,
[Jeremiah] [2]:[30] And it’s in vain that I’ve spanked you like children; For, from My correction, you’ve failed to learn! ‘So, although your prophets were devoured by swords, And although lions came and wiped them away, This hasn’t [taught you] to fear Me.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[31] ‘Therefore, hear the Word of [Jehovah], For [Jehovah] is asking you this: ‘To IsraEl, am I now a desert… Am I a land that’s barren to you? ‘Why is it that My people say: ‘Because you aren’t our Lord anymore, We’ll no longer be coming before You’?
[Jeremiah] [2]:[32] ‘Will the bride forget her tiara, And will virgins forget the bands for their breasts? Yet, I’ve been forgotten by you Through too many days to be counted.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[33] ‘What good can you make of your ways, So that you can seek [My] affection again? It just won’t do any good, Because you’ve made yourselves wicked. ‘All of your ways are now dirty, And innocent blood is found in your hands.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[34] No, I don’t find [their bodies] in ditches, But [hanging] from every [tall] tree.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[35] Yet you still say, I’m not guilty… So, please turn back You rage! '{Look!} I’m the One who is passing judgment on you When you say that you have not sinned!
[Jeremiah] [2]:[36] And for you, I’ve come to feel great disdain Because of the things that you’re doing. ‘Therefore, by Egypt, you will be disgraced, As Assyria has disgraced you before.
[Jeremiah] [2]:[37] You’ll be taken from here with your hands on your heads, For [Jehovah] has thrust you away… And then, none of your hopes will succeed.’
[Jeremiah] [3]:[1] ‘If a man releases his woman And she [then moves in with] another… Then, if she thereafter [also leaves him], Can she return [to first one] again? For, once she has been defiled, Isn’t she always defiled? ‘Yet, after [you’ve had] many shepherds, You want to come back to Me, said [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [3]:[2] So now, raise your eyes to see the right way… See how you’ve been defiled! ‘For you sat by the road [and waited] for them Alone and defiled like a crow In this land of your evil and whoring.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[3] ‘You’ve stumbled and had many shepherds, And because you looked like a whore, You have brought shame on them all.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[4] ‘Yet, didn’t you call Me [your] Father… The One who founded your virgin condition!
[Jeremiah] [3]:[5] [And wasn’t it you who once said], Throughout the age, I’ll still be a virgin… I’ll guard this state ‘til I’ve won? {Look!} Yet, although you made such a vow, You went and did this vile thing!’
[Jeremiah] [3]:[6] Well, it was during the days of King JosiAh that the Lord came and said this to me: ‘You saw what the house of IsraEl has done… For she’s climbed upon every high mountain And crawled under every tree in the woods, And there, she’s committing [adultery].

[Jeremiah] [3]:[8] I knew that in order to benefit all, I had to stand up [for what’s right]. ‘For the house of IsraEl fell into seduction, And then she committed adultery. So with a certificate of divorce I sent her away. ‘But the [vow]-breaker Judah wasn’t bothered by this, And she continued in her whoring ways.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[9] For, whoring was nothing to her… She even did it with wood and stone things…
[Jeremiah] [3]:[10] Her heart refused to turn back, And all she offered was lies.’
[Jeremiah] [3]:[11] Then the Lord said this to me: ‘Even IsraEl was better than this [vow]-breaker Judah;
[Jeremiah] [3]:[12] So, go to the north and then read these words… Tell [those in the north] that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘O house of IsraEl, if you’ll come back to Me, Against you, I’ll not set My face… I will show mercy upon you, says [Jehovah], And throughout the age, I won’t be outraged.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[13] ‘Just be aware of your sins! For you’ve shown disrespect to [Jehovah] your God… [Your love] you’ve given to strangers Beneath every tree in the woods, And you chose not to do what I said, says [Jehovah].

[Jeremiah] [3]:[16] ‘Then, as you grow and spread in the land, says [Jehovah]; In those days, they’ll not speak anymore Of IsraEl’s Holy Chest of the Sacred Agreement… No, it won’t come into their hearts… It won’t be named or examined… This won’t be done anymore!
[Jeremiah] [3]:[17] ‘For, in those days and during that time, JeruSalem will everafter be known As the place of the Throne of [Jehovah], And it’s where all the nations will gather With no wicked thoughts in their hearts.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[18] ‘And in those days, the houses of IsraEl and Judah Will become one [nation] again. They’ll be gathered from the lands of the north To the place that I gave to their fathers.’
[Jeremiah] [3]:[19] Well at that, I shouted: ‘May it happen, O Lord! ‘For You told me that You will let me have children again, and that I will receive a choice piece of land… The inheritance of the Almighty God… [The God] that will be over all the nations! Yes, Father; you’ve called me, and now I’ll never turn away from You!’
[Jeremiah] [3]:[20] But the Lord said: ‘The house of IsraEl has left me, Like a woman who has rejected her man.
[Jeremiah] [3]:[21] And for this, her lips will thereafter weep. ‘So, tell IsraEl’s sons to turn back and beg, Because their ways have led them to sin, And they’ve forgotten their Most Holy God.

[Jeremiah] [3]:[25] go to bed in shame and they’re covered by their dishonor. Yes, like our fathers, we have sinned before God from the time of our youth down to this day, and we’ve failed to pay attention to the voice of our God [Jehovah]!’
[Jeremiah] [4]:[1] Then the Lord said: ‘If IsraEl should [choose to] return, I’ll also turn back to them. If they’ll wash the disgusting things from their mouths… If they’ll show that they will respect me,

[Jeremiah] [4]:[3] ‘So to the men of Judah and JeruSalem [Jehovah] gave these instructions: ‘Prepare your [hearts]… Yes, get them ready to plow… Don’t allow thorn bushes to grow here again!’
[Jeremiah] [4]:[4] ‘O men of Judah and JeruSalem, ‘Circumcise yourselves to your God… Snip the hardness out of your hearts So He doesn’t send the fire of His rage… [A fire] that can’t be extinguished Because of the bad things you’re doing!

[Jeremiah] [4]:[7] ‘Now the lion has come from his lair, And he is wiping out nations. He’s arisen and now he’s come from his place To desolate lands and destroy them! ‘So your cities will all be demolished, And you’ll no longer be living within them.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[8] Because of this, put on sackcloth… Yes, be sad, and then start to bawl! For the anger and rage of [Jehovah] Will not be diverted from you.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[9] ‘And in that day,’ said the Lord, ‘There’ll be no heart in the king… The hearts of the rulers and priests will be shocked And the prophets will all be confused.’
[Jeremiah] [4]:[10] Then I replied: ‘O Almighty Lord, ‘You must surely be joking… Aren’t you misleading these people? Aren’t you saying that there’ll really be peace for JeruSalem and that the sword won’t be coming into our lives?’
[Jeremiah] [4]:[11] [But He replied]: ‘At that time, I’ll say to these people (To those who live in JeruSalem): ‘An addiction to delusions has come from the desert; For the ways of the daughters of my people Can no longer be thought of as pure… None have kept themselves holy.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[12] So the spirit of fulfillment is coming from me, And I’m now speaking judgments against them.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[13] ‘Look! Like a cloud, someone has arisen Whose chariots are sending out blasts, And whose horses are lighter than eagles. So woe, for misery is headed your way!
[Jeremiah] [4]:[14] ‘Therefore, O JeruSalem, ‘Rinse the evil out of your hearts So that somehow, you might be saved! For, how long did you think you can do all those things That are [the root] of your [problems]?
[Jeremiah] [4]:[15] ‘So from Dan, you’ll start hearing voices, And from Ephraim will come misery.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[16] '{Look!} Remind your nation of this, And shout this aloud in JeruSalem: ‘From a far-away land will come an alliance That’s speaking against the cities of Judah!’

[Jeremiah] [4]:[18] It’s because of your [bad] ways and [evil] deeds That they are coming against you… Because your evil is now so bitter That it has reached into your hearts!
[Jeremiah] [4]:[19] ‘This [thought] brings pain to My belly… It causes My heart to feel spasms and ache… But My Soul has been forced to take action!
[Jeremiah] [4]:[20] ‘So, since I’ll no longer stay silent, My Soul now hears trumpet blasts And the cries of misery and war. ‘This conflict is something that’s called for, And misery will come to your land. For, you have abandoned My Tent, And its covering of skins you have parted.
[Jeremiah] [4]:[21] ‘Why must I watch [people] fleeing And hear the blowing of trumpets?

[Jeremiah] [4]:[24] I also noticed that the mountains were shaking and all the hills were being disturbed.

[Jeremiah] [7]:[20] ‘It’s because of this,’ says [Jehovah], That I’ll pour out My anger and rage on this Place… Upon the men and their cattle… Upon every tree in their fields, As well as on the land’s produce. This fire has been lit and it won’t be put out!

[Jeremiah] [7]:[24] ‘But, they didn’t listen to Me, And their ears just paid no attention… They followed the evil thoughts in their hearts And became the butt not the head From the day that their fathers left Egypt ‘til now.

[Jeremiah] [19]:[7] ‘For there, I’ll slay the counselors of Judah, As well as those of JeruSalem… Before their enemies, I’ll cut them down Through the hands of those who are seeking their lives. Then I’ll hand their dead to the birds as their food, As well as to the wild beasts of the ground.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[8] ‘I’ll order the extinction of this city… It’ll be just a place where hissing is heard. And all that come here will look at it sadly, Then whistle [when they see] its disaster.
[Jeremiah] [19]:[9] ‘Here they’ll eat the flesh of their daughters and sons, And in their strongholds, the flesh of their neighbors, When their enemies (those seeking their lives) have arrived.’
[Jeremiah] [19]:[10] ‘Then, break that pitcher in front of their eyes, And before those who have traveled there with you,
[Jeremiah] [19]:[11] Then tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘This is how I will do it; I’ll break your city and its people Just like this pot has been shattered So that it cannot be repaired. Then they will be buried here in this place Where [they now play] tambourines… And there’ll be no other place to be buried.’
[Jeremiah] [19]:[12] ‘[Jehovah] says: This is what I will do to this place, And to all those who live here… I’ll hand this city to destruction…
[Jeremiah] [19]:[13] Yes, all of JeruSalem’s homes And the palaces of all of its rulers. ‘It will all fall into ruin Because of the bad things they’ve done here. For here, they’ve burned incense on roofs To each of the [Zodiac signs], And they’ve offered drinks to strange gods.’
[Jeremiah] [19]:[14] Then JeremiAh left [the valley] where The Lord had sent him to prophesy, and he went and stood in the courtyard of the [Temple] of [Jehovah] and said this to all the people who were there: ‘Thus says [Jehovah] of Armies: '{Look!} I’ll bring calamity on this city And to the rest of its cities and towns. I’m bringing all of the evils that I’ve spoken against her; For, you have hardened your necks, And not listened to the instructions that I sent.’
[Jeremiah] [20]:[1] Well, when PashUr son of ImMer (the Priest who had been anointed as the leader of the Temple of [Jehovah]) heard what JeremiAh was prophesying,
[Jeremiah] [20]:[2] he had him beaten and thrown into the dungeon near the Upper Gate of the House of BenJamin, which was near the Temple of [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [20]:[3] Then the next morning, as PashUr was leading JeremiAh out of the dungeon, JeremiAh said to him: ‘[Jehovah] won’t call your name PashUr anymore. Rather, He’s going to call you Refugee.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[4] Because, [Jehovah] says this: '{Look!} I will hand over you and your friends, And you’ll be taken away from this place. Then, each one will be cut down by enemy swords… And your eyes will see it all happen. ‘Then I’ll hand over Judah to Babylon’s king, And he’ll move the people away Or cut them to pieces with swords.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[5] ‘I’ll remove the strength from this city – All its works and all the king’s treasures – And give them into their enemy’s hands. ‘Then to Babylon, they all will be led;
[Jeremiah] [20]:[6] And you and all that live in your house Will be taken to Babylon as captives, And that is the place where you’ll die… It’s where you’ll be entombed with your friends To whom you prophesied lies.’
[Jeremiah] [20]:[7] Then I said: ‘You’ve deceived me, O Lord… Yes, I was truly deceived! Although You’ve held on and won, I’m the butt of their laughter every day and I’m the one they’re all sneering at!
[Jeremiah] [20]:[8] So from now on, I’m just going to laugh at the bitterness and call for more misery and rebellion, since all that speaking the word of [Jehovah] has brought me is scorn and taunting every day.’
[Jeremiah] [20]:[9] And I said: ‘There’s no way that I’m going to [speak of] [Jehovah] anymore… I won’t even mention His Name!’ However, soon it became like a fire that burned and blazed in my bones and made me weak on the inside, until I was no longer able to bear it. [So I said:]
[Jeremiah] [20]:[10] ‘I’ve heard that they’ve said in their meetings: ‘We should all rise up against him… Yes, let’s stand together against him As well as against all his friends! ‘Let’s ignore what he says will be coming… Yes, let him keep on being deceived. For against him, we will prevail, And then, we’ll take vengeance upon him!’
[Jeremiah] [20]:[11] ‘However, [Jehovah] is with me, As a warrior that’s making me strong. So, they have chased me in vain… And although they will all meet with shame, They’ll fail to see their dishonor, Which will not be forgotten throughout ages.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[12] ‘O Lord, ‘Try me according to Your righteous ways… Examine my kidneys and heart. May I witness Your punishment on them… For before You, I’ve laid out my pleas for defense.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[13] ‘So, sing to [Jehovah] and praise Him, Because He’ll save the lives of the poor From the hands of those who have power!
[Jeremiah] [20]:[14] ‘O cursed is the day I was born… May the day that my mother gave birth Never be longed for again!
[Jeremiah] [20]:[15] ‘And may that person be cursed Who brought this as news to my father: ‘Rejoice, for you have a male child!’
[Jeremiah] [20]:[16] May he be as the cities that did not repent And were destroyed by [Jehovah]! ‘Let him hear their cries in the mornings, As well as their shouting at noon!
[Jeremiah] [20]:[17] For [God] failed to kill me in my mother’s womb And let it serve as my tomb throughout the ages.
[Jeremiah] [20]:[18] ‘Why did I come from the womb… Just to see all of this misery And to spend all my days in such shame?’

[Jeremiah] [24]:[1] Well, after NebuChadNezzar (the king of Babylon) had taken JeconiJah (son of JehoiAkim) the king of Judah and the governors from JeruSalem as prisoners and led them into Babylon; the Lord showed me two reed baskets of figs sitting before the Temple of [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [24]:[2] The first basket of figs was much fresher and better than the other, for the second basket of figs was so bad that they couldn’t be eaten.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[3] Then the Lord asked me: ‘What do you see, JeremiAh?’ And I replied: ‘Figs… Some are good, but the others are so rotten that they can’t be eaten.’
[Jeremiah] [24]:[4] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Jeremiah] [24]:[5] ‘[Jehovah], the God of IsraEl, says this: ‘These good figs are like those Judeans Whom I already sent away from this place Into the land of Chaldea.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[6] ‘I will fix My eyes upon them for good, And I’ll bring them back to this land… I’ll rebuild them and not destroy them again… I’ll plant them and not pluck them up.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[7] ‘I’ll give them hearts that will know Me… So they’ll realize that I am their Lord. Then they’ll be My people and I’ll be their God, And with their whole hearts, they’ll turn back to Me.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[8] ‘But, when it comes to those bad figs That no one could possibly eat… Because he has made himself rotten’, says [Jehovah], I’ll hand over King ZedekiAh Along with all his great men. ‘Then the rest of the people in JeruSalem And those who have remained in this land, As well as all those [fleeing to] Egypt,
[Jeremiah] [24]:[9] Will be scattered throughout the whole earth. ‘As a parable of hatred, they will be scorned And cursed everywhere that I’ll push them.
[Jeremiah] [24]:[10] Upon them, I will bring famine, As well as plagues and the sword, Until they’ve been forced out of this land That I gave to their fathers and them.’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[1] Well, it was in the 4th year [of the reign] of JehoiAkim (son of JosiAh) the king of Judah that these words came to JeremiAh concerning all the people of Judah. And then, during the 1st year [of the reign] of NebuChadNezzar king of Babylon [over Judah],
[Jeremiah] [25]:[2] the Prophet JeremiAh went and spoke to all the people of Judah and to those who were living in JeruSalem. This is what he said to them:
[Jeremiah] [25]:[3] ‘From the 13th year of JosiAh son of Amon – for [the past] 23 years – [Jehovah’s] word has been coming to me, and I’ve been getting up early each morning to tell you [what God has said]. However, you just haven’t listened.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[4] [‘So now, [Jehovah] says this]: ‘Every morning, I sent you My servants the Prophets, But your ears refused to listen to them, And you chose to pay no attention.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[5] ‘They told you to turn from your wicked ways, And then, you’d continue to live in the land That I gave to your fathers and you Throughout the age and into the ages.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[6] ‘I told you not to follow strange gods… Not to serve them or bow down before them, So you wouldn’t provoke Me to rage With these things that you made with your hands, And I wouldn’t bring bad things upon you…
[Jeremiah] [25]:[7] However, you just wouldn’t listen!
[Jeremiah] [25]:[8] ‘So because of this,’ says [Jehovah]… ‘Since you didn’t trust the things that I said;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[9] {Look!} I’ve called for a family that lives in the north And led them down to this land… I’ve brought them against those who live here And against the nations roundabout, To bring desolation upon you… They’ll appoint you to extinction, hissing, and scorn Throughout [the rest of] the age.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[10] ‘They’ll destroy the sounds of happiness and joy… The voices of grooms and their brides, As well as the scent of lamps and perfumes,
[Jeremiah] [25]:[11] There’ll be an extinction throughout the whole land! ‘And you’ll serve that nation for 70 years… As well as Babylon’s king.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[12] ‘And after the 70 years are fulfilled; On the king of Babylon and his wicked nation, I will then bring My vengeance For the unrighteous things that they’ll do, says [Jehovah]. ‘I’ll appoint the land of Chaldea To extinction throughout the rest of the age.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[13] And against that land, I’ll bring all the words That I have spoken against them… All the things that JeremiAh will write in this scroll, And which he will speak against them!
[Jeremiah] [25]:[14] ‘For, they will force many nations, And their great kings to serve them. Then I’ll pay them back for the bad things they’ll do… According to the works of their hands.’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[15] ‘Then [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl said: ‘Take this cup of pure wine from My hand And give it to those nations where I’ll send you… Yes, give it to them as their drink!
[Jeremiah] [25]:[16] Then they’ll drink it and vomit it out, And go mad before the sword that I’ll send.’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[17] So after that, I took the cup that the Lord had given to me and I gave it to the nations to drink (all of those to whom He had sent me… To JeruSalem and the cities of Judah… To the king of Judah and his governors),
[Jeremiah] [25]:[18] so as to appoint desolation upon them and to be lands that are no longer walked (places of hissing and curses),
[Jeremiah] [25]:[19] as well as on PharaOh (the king of Egypt), on his children, on his people, and on all his great men (yes, all that live in his realm),
[Jeremiah] [25]:[20] and upon the kings of Philistia and Uz; on AshKelon, Gaza, EkRon, and those who are left in AshDod,
[Jeremiah] [25]:[21] and on those in Edom and in MoAb. ‘For He said: ‘The sons of AmMon will then be extinct,
[Jeremiah] [25]:[22] As will be the kings of Sidon and Tyre, And the kings who [live] ‘cross the sea,
[Jeremiah] [25]:[23] Such as DeDan, Tema, and Buz (All those who are shaving their faces),
[Jeremiah] [25]:[24] And the kings of Arabia and their subjects (Those who rest in the desert)…
[Jeremiah] [25]:[25] ‘All the kings of ZimRi and ElAm; All the kings of the Medes;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[26] And all the kings from the east wind (Both those who are near and those far away), Along with all of their brothers, And the rest of the kingdoms on the face of the earth… Then Shishak will also drink with them!’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[27] ‘Yes, tell them that thus says [Jehovah] the Almighty: ‘They all will drink it and all will get drunk, And then, they will vomit and fall, For they will be unable to stand Before the sword that I’m sending to them!’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[28] ‘And if they refuse to drink from the cup; Explain that [Jehovah] of Armies said this: [‘You have no choice] but to drink it;
[Jeremiah] [25]:[29] For this affliction has already started In the city that carries My Name. ‘And if you should try to clean yourselves up, There’s no way that you’ll ever be holy; For now, I have called for a sword To come upon all your lands, Says [Jehovah] of Armies.’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[30] ‘You must speak these words against them and say: ‘From high above in His Holy Place, [Jehovah] will bring execution… He’ll speak a word with His voice, And against your place, He’s sending destruction. ‘Then, those who gather this vintage will say To those who have settled the land:
[Jeremiah] [25]:[31] ‘Part of the earth has been ruined; And from [Jehovah], this judgment of nations has come. For, with all flesh, He’s contending, And the irreverent will be given to the sword.’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[32] ‘[Jehovah] of Armies also said this: '{Look!} From a nation, evil will come to the nations, And a storm will rage to the ends of the earth.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[33] And in that day; From one part of the earth to the other, Those who are slain by [Jehovah] Won’t be lamented, gathered, or buried… They’ll be like manure on the face of the ground!’
[Jeremiah] [25]:[34] ‘So shout, O shepherds, and cry out! Yes, beat on your chests, O rams of the flocks! For your days until slaughter have now been fulfilled, And you will fall like the choicest of rams.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[35] ‘For the shepherds; their chance for flight will be gone, And safety will flee from the rams of the flocks.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[36] So from the shepherds, cries will arise, As well as the bleating of rams, When [Jehovah] wipes their pastures away.
[Jeremiah] [25]:[37] ‘Then there’ll no longer be peaceful places to rest, In the face of [Jehovah’s] anger and rage. For He’ll arrive like a lion that’s abandoned its lair To make their lands unwalked places, With the face of His mighty sword.’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[1] It was in the first part of the reign of King JehoiAkim (son of JosiAh) that this word came from [Jehovah]. [The Lord] said:
[Jeremiah] [26]:[2] ‘Go and stand in [the Temple] courtyard And there, give orders to those in Judea… To all who are coming to bow here. Tell them all the things that I said, And don’t forget any words!
[Jeremiah] [26]:[3] ‘Then perhaps they will listen and turn from their bad, And I can bring an end to the evil That I’ve arranged to send upon them Because of the bad things they’re doing.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[4] ‘So, tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: If you refuse to listen to Me And obey all the Laws that I’ve set before you… [If you won’t] obey the words of My servant
[Jeremiah] [26]:[5] The words of the Prophet I sent, But to whom you chose not to listen,
[Jeremiah] [26]:[6] I’ll make this Temple like ShiLoh And appoint this city as a curse Before all the nations on earth.’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[7] Well, all the priests and false prophets, as well as all the people heard what JeremiAh said when he spoke those words in the Temple of [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [26]:[8] And after he finished saying everything that the Lord had ordered him to say to the people, the priests, and the false prophets, they grabbed him and said:
[Jeremiah] [26]:[9] ‘We’re going to kill you for prophesying in the Name of [Jehovah] and for saying that this Temple will become like ShiLoh and that this city will be desolate with no one living in it!’ So thereafter, they all gathered inside the Temple of [Jehovah] and put JeremiAh on trial.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[10] But when the rulers of Judah heard [what JeremiAh was saying], they went from the king’s [palace] up to the Temple of [Jehovah], and they all sat down on the threshold of the New Gate.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[11] Then the priests and false prophets said this before the rulers and all the people: ‘This man deserves the judgment of death for prophesying against this city… Something that you all heard him say with your own ears!’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[12] And [in reply], JeremiAh said this to the rulers and the people: ‘It was [Jehovah] that sent me here to prophesy all these words that you heard me speak against this Temple and this city.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[13] So, it would really best for you to change the ways that you’re acting and the things that you’re doing, and to start listening to the voice of your God [Jehovah]. For then the Lord would bring an end to all of these evils that He has spoken against you here.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[14] ‘However, {Look!} here I am in your hands! So, do to me whatever you think is going to be advantageous and best for yourselves!
[Jeremiah] [26]:[15] But know and understand that if you do away with me, you will have brought the guilt of innocent blood against yourselves, this city, and everyone who lives here; for it was really [Jehovah] that sent me to you to speak all these words in your ears!’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[16] Well at that, the rulers and people said to the priests and false prophets: ‘This man doesn’t really deserve the sentence of death, for he was speaking in the Name of our God [Jehovah]!’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[17] Then, men from among the elders of the land stood up and spoke before the whole gathering and said:
[Jeremiah] [26]:[18] ‘MicAh the Morasthite was a Prophet in the days of HezekiAh, the king of Judah, and he spoke to all the people of Judah and told them that [Jehovah] of Armies had said this: ‘Zion is now a field to be plowed, For JeruSalem will be a storehouse of fruits, And the Temple Mount will soon be converted Into a grove of sacred poles.’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[19] ‘However, King HezekiAh and the people of Judah didn’t do away with him, because they were afraid of [Jehovah]. So they begged and bowed before [God], and He brought an end to the evils that He had spoken against them… And once again, we have [for a fact, been sinning] in a great way against our own souls!’
[Jeremiah] [26]:[20] Well, around that same time, there was another man who had been prophesying in the Name of [Jehovah], UriAh son of ShemaiAh (from KiriAth JaiRim). For he had also prophesied about the city and the land, using the very same words as JeremiAh.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[21] But when he heard what King JehoiAkim and all the rulers had said about seeking to kill [JeremiAh], UriAh became afraid and he fled down to Egypt.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[22] However, the king sent his men (ElNathan son of AchBor, and some others) to Egypt
[Jeremiah] [26]:[23] and they brought him back from there. Then when he stood before the king, he was cut down with a sword and [his body] was thrown into the tomb of the sons of his people.
[Jeremiah] [26]:[24] But because the hand of AhiKam (son of ShaPhan) was with JeremiAh, he stopping him from being handed over to the people so they could do away with him.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[1] [Editor note: These words are factually incorrect, and are probably an interpolation introduced in the Hebrew Masoretic text, not present in the original Greek Septuagint ordering of Jeremiah.]

[Jeremiah] [27]:[3] Then send them to the kings of Edom and MoAb, And to those of AmMon, Sidon, and Tyre By the hands of those who have come here To see ZedekiAh, king of Judah.

[Jeremiah] [27]:[8] And upon any nation or kingdom That refuses to serve King NebuChadNezzar (That won’t wear his yoke on their necks), I’ll send the sword, famine, and plague,’ says [Jehovah], ‘Until they yield to his hand.

[Jeremiah] [27]:[11] ‘To the nation that puts its neck in the yoke And chooses to serve Babylon’s king; I’ll allow them to stay in their land, says [Jehovah], ‘They’ll continue to work there and live.’

[Jeremiah] [27]:[13] and work for him and his men, you’ll live! ‘Why should you and your people choose to die by the sword, famines, and plagues, as [Jehovah] told the nations would happen to them if they don’t wish to serve Babylon’s king?
[Jeremiah] [27]:[14] ‘You shouldn’t listen to the words of those prophets when they tell you that you must not serve him, for they’re prophesying unrighteous things!
[Jeremiah] [27]:[15] [Jehovah] says that He didn’t send them, and what they’re prophesying in His Name is unrighteous, so He’ll have to destroy both them and you… ‘Yes, you’ll die along with those prophets who are lying to you!’
[Jeremiah] [27]:[16] Then I spoke to the priests and to all the people, and told them that [Jehovah] said this: ‘Don’t listen to the words of the prophets When they speak prophecies and they tell you That the items of the Temple of [Jehovah] Will soon be returned from Babylon. For, they are lying to you!
[Jeremiah] [27]:[17] ‘No, do not listen to them… Serve Babylon’s king and you’ll live… Why bring your city to ruin?’
[Jeremiah] [27]:[18] [Then I said]: ‘If they truly are Prophets And if they really have the word of [Jehovah]; Then, have them all come here and meet me, So that the things which are left in the Temple And the things that belong to Judea’s kings (Whatever is left in JeruSalem) Will not be taken to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[19] ‘For [Jehovah] sent me this warning About the [Temple’s sacred] columns, And about the [Sacred] Sea and its base, As well as about all the rest that is left,
[Jeremiah] [27]:[20] Which Babylon’s king didn’t already take When he removed JehoiAkim’s son, JeconiJah… The king of Judah and all of his rulers, Then took them from Judah and JeruSalem, And carried them to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [27]:[21] ‘For [Jehovah] of Armies (the God of IsraEl) Said this about the things left behind At the Temple of [Jehovah], And all that is left in the homes of the kings In Judah and JeruSalem:
[Jeremiah] [27]:[22] ‘To Babylon, it will be carried, And there is where it will stay Until the day that I come to visit, And they bring it back to this place.’
[Jeremiah] [28]:[1] It was in the 5th month of the 4th year of the reign of ZedekiAh (king of Judah) that HananiAh (son of Azur) the false prophet from GibeOn spoke to me in the Temple of [Jehovah] before the eyes of the priests and all the people. He said:
[Jeremiah] [28]:[2] ‘[Jehovah] of Armies the God of IsraEl spoke to me and said this: I will break the yoke of Babylon’s king.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[3] And in two more years, I will return All the things of the Temple of [Jehovah],
[Jeremiah] [28]:[4] As well as JeconiJah and the [people] of Judah Whom they have moved away. For I’ll break the yoke of Babylon’s king.’
[Jeremiah] [28]:[5] Then the Prophet JeremiAh replied to HananiAh, there before the priests and before the eyes of all the people who were standing in the Temple of [Jehovah]. He said:
[Jeremiah] [28]:[6] ‘May [Jehovah] indeed do what you’ve said in the words of your prophecy and return all the things of the Temple of [Jehovah] along with all the [people] that were carried off to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[7] However, listen to the words that I’ll speak into your ears before all of these people!
[Jeremiah] [28]:[8] ‘Throughout the ages, long before you and me, there have been many men who have prophesied great things against this land concerning war, oppression, and plagues…
[Jeremiah] [28]:[9] And there were also those who prophesied peace. Then after it happened, the [people] started believing whichever prophet that had really been sent by [Jehovah].’
[Jeremiah] [28]:[10] Well at that, HananiAh tore the yoke from the neck of JeremiAh and broke it.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[11] And he said (there before the eyes of all the people): ‘[Jehovah] told me that this is how He will break the yoke of the king of Babylon from the necks of all the nations in just two more years!’ Well when he did that, JeremiAh left. And as he was leaving
[Jeremiah] [28]:[12] (after HananiAh had broken the yoke from his neck), the Word of [Jehovah] came to [JeremiAh] and said this:
[Jeremiah] [28]:[13] ‘Go back and tell HananiAh that [Jehovah] said this: ‘Because you have broken that wooden yoke, I’ll turn the wooden yokes into iron!
[Jeremiah] [28]:[14] So JeremiAh [went back and said]: ‘[Jehovah] of Armies, the God of IsraEl, said this: ‘On the necks of all nations, I’ll put an iron yoke, Then they’ll serve and work for Babylon’s king… And to him, I’ll give all their cattle.’
[Jeremiah] [28]:[15] Then JeremiAh said this to HananiAh: ‘Listen, O HananiAh! ‘[Jehovah] hasn’t sent you to these people just so they can learn to rely on the things that they’ve been doing wrong.
[Jeremiah] [28]:[16] And because of what you’ve been telling them, this is what the Lord told me to say: '{Look!} I’ll remove you from the face of the earth… Yes, this very year, you will die For speaking against [Jehovah]!’
[Jeremiah] [28]:[17] Well, he did in fact die that year, in the 7th month.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[1] These are the words of the scroll that JeremiAh the Prophet sent from JeruSalem to the elders that had already been relocated, as well as to the priests and false prophets… To all the people whom NebuChadNezzar had moved from JeruSalem to Babylon
[Jeremiah] [29]:[2] after King JeconiJah, his queen, his eunuchs, and all the freemen, servants, and craftsman had been taken from JeruSalem.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[3] [He sent it] by the hand of ElAsah (son of ShaPhan) and GemariJah (son of HilkiJah). For they were the ones whom ZedekiAh king of Judah had sent to the king of the Babylonian [Empire] that lived in [the city of] Babylon. [The scroll] said:

[Jeremiah] [29]:[6] Take wives and also have children… Father both daughters and sons! ‘Then, take [mates] for your daughters and sons; And they’ll also give birth to daughters and sons… They’ll multiply and not be reduced!
[Jeremiah] [29]:[7] ‘Yes, seek peace in the land where I’ve sent you, And pray to [Jehovah] on its behalf; For, in its peace, you’ll find peace!

[Jeremiah] [29]:[9] ‘For, there will be those who will come in My Name, And they will prophesy falsely; But by Me, they were not sent!’ says [Jehovah].

[Jeremiah] [29]:[12] Then you can pray to Me and I’ll hear you…
[Jeremiah] [29]:[13] You can search for Me and you’ll find Me. And if wholeheartedly, you’ll search for Me,

[Jeremiah] [29]:[15] ‘But you say that the Lord has put Prophets among those who are living in Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[16] Well, [Jehovah] says this to the king who is sitting on the throne of David and to all the people who are living in this city, as well as to all your brothers that didn’t leave and weren’t taken into captivity along with you…
[Jeremiah] [29]:[17] Yes, [concerning these prophets], [Jehovah] of Armies said this: '{Look!} I’ll send them the sword, famines, and plagues… Like a bad fig, I will make them… [A fig] that’s too rotten to eat.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[18] ‘I’ll pursue them with swords, famines, and plagues, Then scatter them to all the kingdoms of earth. And to confusion, hissing, and scorn they’ll be cursed Among all the nations where I’ll send them.

[Jeremiah] [29]:[20] ‘Yet, those of you who have been moved away From JeruSalem to Babylon, Have also ignored the Word of [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [29]:[21] ‘For [Jehovah] once spoke against Ahab (son of KolaiJah) And ZedekiAh (son of MaAseJah) Who prophesied lies to you in His Name. And this is what He has said about them: '{Look!} To Babylon’s king, I will hand them, And he’ll cut them down in front of your eyes.
[Jeremiah] [29]:[22] So when Babylon’s Jews speak curses, they’ll say: ‘May [Jehovah] do the same thing to you That He did to ZedekiAh and Ahab… Those who Babylon’s king fried in fires.’
[Jeremiah] [29]:[23] ‘For, JeruSalem’s people are lawless… They’re committing adultery with their countrymen’s wives. Yet [their prophets] are saying things in My Name That I didn’t tell them to say… And I am the witness [against them],’ says [Jehovah]!

[Jeremiah] [29]:[27] ‘So, why haven’t you joined in and scolded JeremiAh from [the city of] AnathOth Who has served as a Prophet to you?’
[Jeremiah] [29]:[28] ‘For to us who are living in Babylon And in its most-distant places, He says that freedom is still far away. So, they should build houses and dwell there… Plant gardens and then eat their fruits.’

[Jeremiah] [29]:[32] Yes, because of this,’ says [Jehovah], ‘I’ll visit ShemaiAh and all of his kind, And there won’t be a man left among them Who will see the good I’ll do among you,’ says [Jehovah], ‘For he’s preached a turning from Me.’
[Jeremiah] [30]:[1] These words came to JeremiAh from the Lord. He was told that [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl said this:

[Jeremiah] [30]:[3] '{Look!} The days are coming,’ said [Jehovah], ‘When I will return those of IsraEl and Judah (All those who have been moved away)… Yes, I’ll bring them back to this land That I gave to their fathers, And once more, they will be its lords.’
[Jeremiah] [30]:[4] And after that, these were the words that the Lord spoke concerning IsraEl and Judah:
[Jeremiah] [30]:[5] ‘[Jehovah] says: ‘[But first], you will hear fearful sounds… You will hear fearful sounds and there’ll be no peace.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[6] ‘So, ask if a male has ever given birth… Yet I see all men with their hands on their hips As though they are women about to give birth, And their faces are [yellow with] jaundice.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[7] ‘For, that will be a great day of woe, And there couldn’t be any days worse… Yet, Jacob will still be returned to his land.’
[Jeremiah] [30]:[8] ‘For thus says [Jehovah] of Armies: ‘In that day, I’ll break all the yokes from their necks… I’ll also tear off their bonds, And they’ll no longer be toiling for strangers.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[9] At that time, they’ll work for [Jehovah], their God, And I will raise David to be their king.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[10] ‘So you, O My servant Jacob; Don’t be afraid,’ says [Jehovah]… ‘O IsraEl, do not be in terror, For {Look!} I’ll bring you back from those far-away lands! ‘I’ll bring your offspring from that captive place… Jacob will be returned and find rest. Then he’ll receive an abundance of good things, And he will have nothing to fear.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[11] ‘Because I’m with you, I’ll save you,’ says [Jehovah], ‘And I will appoint a conclusion To those nations where you have been scattered, For no way have I appointed your end. But I will correct you in fairness, And I’ll scrub you until you are clean!’
[Jeremiah] [30]:[12] ‘[Jehovah] said: ‘I’ll remove the pain of destruction;
[Jeremiah] [30]:[13] For, no one else will be judging your case, And no one else will be treating your [wounds] To bring consolation to you.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[14] ‘But by your friends, you will be forgotten, And none will ask why I struck you… Why I let your enemies beat you. ‘For My discipline will be very substantial, Because the things that you did were so bad!
[Jeremiah] [30]:[15] So don’t yell [to Me] about your destruction, And the incurable state of your misery! ‘It will happen because your sins were so great, And because of the harsh things you’ve done… This is why I’m bringing these bad things upon you.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[16] ‘But those who [are now] eating you Will find themselves being consumed, And your enemies will be taken as captives… Those scattering you, will be scattered, And those looting you, will be plundered.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[17] ‘Then your grievous wounds, I will cure… Yes, I will treat all your ailments,’ says God, ‘Then Zion will be called ‘The Replanted Place,’ And none will [attack] her again.’
[Jeremiah] [30]:[18] ‘[Jehovah] said: '{Look!} I’ll return those of Jacob who have been taken away… All that were led off as captives. Then, I will show mercy upon them And rebuild their city there in the heights, Where I will seat all the people According to the ways they’ve been fair.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[19] ‘And from among them, there will come singers, As well as the music of musicians That will grow in super abundance, And no way will it be diminished.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[20] ‘Each man will then enter [the Temple] Along with all of his sons, Just as they’ve done in the past, And their praises will rise up to Me, When I come against those who have oppressed them.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[21] ‘From among them, I’ll then choose a leader… Yes, their ruler will be one of them. I’ll collect them and bring them to Me All those whose hearts will want to return,’ says [Jehovah]…
[Jeremiah] [30]:[22] ‘Then they’ll be My people and I’ll be their Lord.’
[Jeremiah] [30]:[23] ‘For this is why the rage of [Jehovah] was sent… To change the godless, His anger went out In order to make them turn back to Him.
[Jeremiah] [30]:[24] ‘But no way will [God’s] anger and rage be turned back Until He has taken some action… Until He’s done what His heart has decided… And in the last days, you’ll understand why.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[1] Then the Lord told me this: ‘They’ll be the race of IsraEl’s God… Yes they’ll be His people once more.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[2] And the Lord said: ‘Although they found it hot in the desert When they were destroyed by the sword; IsraEl will again find places to rest!
[Jeremiah] [31]:[3] ‘For they’ll see [Jehovah] off in the distance, And this is what He will say: ‘With the love of the ages, I’ve loved you, So I’ve drawn you close to show mercy on you…
[Jeremiah] [31]:[4] I will rebuild you and you’ll be rebuilt, O virgin daughter of IsraEl. ‘Your tambourines will be raised once again And you’ll play them before the assembly.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[5] You will also plant vineyards again Upon Samaria’s mountains… Yes, you will go planting and plant, And you will go praising and praise!
[Jeremiah] [31]:[6] ‘Then, on the day that I call out to you; On Ephraim’s mountains, the watchmen will cry: ‘Get up and go to Mount Zion… Return to [Jehovah] your God!’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[7] ‘Then [Jehovah] said this concerning [the people of] Jacob: ‘Be glad and shout to those leading the nations… Do it… Shout loudly in praise! Say, ‘[Jehovah] has rescued His people… Those IsraElites who survived!’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[8] ‘Look… From the north, I will lead them, And I’ll gather them from the ends of the earth To observe a [glorious] Passover… They’ll return, and they’ll have many children!
[Jeremiah] [31]:[9] ‘Although when they left, they did so in tears; I’ll send them comfort and lead them to rest Along straight roads with [pure] streams… It’s a path from which they’ll not stray. Then I’ll be IsraEl’s Father again, And [a Father] to Ephraim, My firstborn.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[10] ‘O nations, hear the word of [Jehovah] And announce it as far as the islands! Say, ‘The One who blew IsraEl off like the chaff Will gather them back once again, And like a grazing flock, He will guard them!’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[11] ‘For [Jehovah] will [pay] Jacob’s ransom, And from mighty hands, He will save them…
[Jeremiah] [31]:[12] Then in joy, they’ll come back to Zion. ‘And there in a land filled with grain, They will find good things from their God… Wine, olive oil, fruit, cattle, and sheep. So their lives will then be like fruit trees, And they will go hungry no more.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[13] ‘Then the virgins will all be rejoicing, And men young and old will be shouting in joy. For their mourning will be changed into cries of glee… They’ll be happy, and He’ll bring them comfort.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[14] ‘Then I’ll magnify the lives of the Priests And [the lives of] the sons of Levi… My people will own many good things!’ ‘[Jehovah] said:
[Jeremiah] [31]:[15] ‘A voice was heard crying from RamAh… The sounds of weeping, wailing, and grief. It was RachEl crying over her sons… She refused to accept any comfort, Because they aren’t here anymore.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[16] ‘Then to her, [Jehovah] said this: ‘Stop crying and dry the tears from your eyes, For you’ll be paid a wage for your work… They’ll be returned from their enemies’ lands,
[Jeremiah] [31]:[17] And there is still hope for those who survived,’ says [Jehovah], For your sons will return to their borders.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[18] ‘Then I heard Ephraim grieving; So I listened and he told Me this: ‘You beat me and I was corrected; For I had acted like a [wild] calf. But You turned me around and now I’ve returned; For, You are [Jehovah], my God!
[Jeremiah] [31]:[19] ‘Captivity brought a change to my mind In that day when You brought me shame. But, after I moaned, I then understood… Plainly, I showed You that I had accepted That, from my youth, [I deserved] all the scorn.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[20] ‘Yes, Ephraim is My dearly loved son… A child in whom I find joy. And because My words are within him, I will never forget him. ‘It was because of this, that I hurried; For, when it comes to showing him mercy, I will show mercy upon him,’ said [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [31]:[21] ‘So erect the road signs and guideposts, And give your hearts to your shoulders, For they will be [coming back home]! Yes return, O IsraEl, the virgin… Return to the cities where they’re mourning [your loss]!’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[22] [And Jeremiah? said:] O My daughter, When will you return from those places Where you were being disgraced? For the Lord has made new places for you Where it will be safe to do planting, And where people can travel in safety. [And the Lord said:]
[Jeremiah] [31]:[23] ‘Then [Jehovah] of Armies (IsraEl’s God) told me this: ‘Once more, you’ll be speaking of Me In the land of Judah and in all your towns, When I bring back those who were carried away!’ ‘So, praise [Jehovah] on His Holy Mount!
[Jeremiah] [31]:[24] For, those who live in the cities of Judah And the farmers [that dwell] in His land Will grow once again, along with their flocks!
[Jeremiah] [31]:[25] [For [Jehovah] says:] ‘To thirsty souls, I’ll send something to drink, And all hungry souls, I will fill.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[26] Then, when you wake up [in the morning], You’ll see that your sleep has been peaceful.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[27] ‘Look! The days are coming,’ says [Jehovah], ‘When I’ll sow both IsraEl and Judah With the ‘seeds’ of men and the ‘seeds’ of wild beasts.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[28] ‘It’ll be as when I watched over them (Not when I brought them destruction). And then, over them, I’ll be watchful… They’ll be rebuilt and replanted,’ said [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [31]:[29] ‘In those days, no way will they say, ‘Although it was the fathers that ate unripe grapes, The teeth of their children felt chills.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[30] For then, only sinners will die Because of the bad things they do, And those eating green grapes will feel their own chills.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[31] ‘Look… The days are coming,’ says [Jehovah], ‘When I’ll make an arrangement with IsraEl’s house, As well as with the houses of Judah. ‘I’ll conclude a New Sacred Agreement
[Jeremiah] [31]:[32] That’s unlike the one that I made with their fathers In the day that I grabbed their hands To lead them from Egypt’s land. But because they didn’t keep My Sacred Agreement, I had to let them go,’ says [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [31]:[33] ‘So, this is My [New] Sacred Agreement That I will conclude with IsraEl then,’ said [Jehovah], I will put My Laws in their minds, And into their hearts, I will write them. Then, they’ll be My people and I’ll be their God.
[Jeremiah] [31]:[34] ‘There’s no way they’ll then teach their neighbors and brothers That they must learn of [Jehovah]; For, all will know Me from the least to the great. And when it comes to their errors and sins… I will kindly forget them!’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[35] ‘Yet, this is what [Jehovah] [says]... The One who appointed the sun To serve as light for the day, And the moon and the stars as light for the nights… The One who brought the roar of the seas, As well as the sounds of their waves… [Jehovah] the Almighty, is His Name:
[Jeremiah] [31]:[36] ‘If these Laws should [be voided] before Me, Then the race of IsraEl will no longer stand As a nation before Me Throughout the rest of the days.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[37] ‘[Jehovah] says: ‘If the skies can be raised even higher And the floor of the ground can be lowered, I can reject the race of IsraEl, says [Jehovah], For all the things that they’ve done.’
[Jeremiah] [31]:[38] ‘But, look! The days are coming,’ said the Lord, ‘When the city of [Jehovah] will be rebuilt. [It’s walls will run] from the HananEl Tower All the way to the gate at the corner…
[Jeremiah] [31]:[39] To the hills of Gareb, I’ll measure it out And surround it with most precious stones. ‘From the Valley of Phagarim and its ashes, And from AsaRemOth to the Wadi of Cedars, Then east to the corner of the Horse Gate, It’ll be a Holy Place to [Jehovah], And its roots won’t be pulled up again… Throughout the age, it won’t be destroyed.’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[1] Well, all these words had come from [Jehovah] to JeremiAh in the 10th year [of the reign] of ZedekiAh, the king of Judah, which was the 18th year of [the reign of] NebuChadNezzar the king of Babylon [over Judah].
[Jeremiah] [32]:[2] And at the time, the army of the king of Babylon had built a siege wall around JeruSalem, and JeremiAh [was under arrest and being kept in] the courtyard of the guard, which was located inside the [palace] of the kings of Judah,
[Jeremiah] [32]:[3] since King ZedekiAh had him thrown in jail. [For the king had asked him]: ‘Why did you prophesy and tell us that [Jehovah] said: '{Look!} I will hand this city over to the king of Babylon and he will take it…’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[4] And: ‘ZedekiAh won’t escape from the hands of the Chaldeans, but he will be delivered into the hands of the king of Babylon, where he will speak to him mouth to mouth and eye to eye…’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[5] And: ‘ZedekiAh will be taken into Babylon and stay there until I look favorably upon him. So, if you wage war against the Chaldeans, you won’t succeed.’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[6] Then JeremiAh told him: ‘The Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[7] '{Look!} Your paternal uncle HanamEl, son of ShalLum, will come to you and ask you to buy his field in AnathOth… And it will be advantageous for you to acquire it!’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[8] ‘And thereafter, that’s what happened… My paternal uncle HanamEl son of ShalLum did what the Lord said he would do. It was there in the courtyard of the guard that he said to me: ‘Buy my field, the one in AnathOth of the land of BenJamin, because you’re the eldest and it would be advantageous for you to acquire it!’ ‘And since I knew that this was the word of [Jehovah],
[Jeremiah] [32]:[9] I purchased the field in AnathOth from my paternal uncle HanamEl; I paid him 7 large silver coins for it,
[Jeremiah] [32]:[10] then I recorded [the transaction] in a scroll, put a seal on it before witnesses, and weighed out the silver in a balance scale.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[11] ‘So then I took the scroll that had been testified to and sealed and gave it to BarUch son of NeriAh, son of MaAseJah, before the eyes of my uncle HanamEl,
[Jeremiah] [32]:[12] as well as before those who had served as witnesses of the deed scroll, and before the eyes of all the Judeans that were sitting in the courtyard of the guard at the time.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[13] ‘Then before them all, I gave BarUch these orders:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[14] ‘[Jehovah] the Almighty God of IsraEl says that you should take this scroll that has been sealed as my proof of ownership, then you must read it and then store it away in an earthenware jar, so that it will last [a long time].
[Jeremiah] [32]:[15] Because, [Jehovah] of Armies the God of IsraEl told me this: ‘Fields, houses, and vineyards Will again be restored in this land.’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[16] ‘Well, after I gave the deed scroll to BarUch son of NeriAh, I prayed to [Jehovah], saying:
[Jeremiah] [32]:[17] ‘O Great Being, ‘O Lord God, ‘You who made the lands and the skies with Your mighty arm held high above You, and from whom nothing at all can be hidden,
[Jeremiah] [32]:[18] ‘O You who show mercy to thousands and who brings the sins of the fathers upon the chests of their children, ‘The great and Almighty God whose Name is [Jehovah] of Armies,
[Jeremiah] [32]:[19] ‘[You are the God] of great counsel, And mighty are all of Your works. Your eyes see the things that the sons of men do, And You pay each one back for their deeds According to the fruits of their works.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[20] ‘You’re the One who brought the miracles and signs To IsraEl when they were in Egypt And which continue to happen down to this day. For, You have made Your Name known To all who have been born on the earth until now.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[21] ‘You’re the One who led IsraEl from Egypt With signs and miracles from Your mighty right hand… With Your arm held high and through visions.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[22] And thereafter, You gave them the land About which You swore to their fathers… A land that’s flowing with honey and milk.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[23] ‘So they entered this land and they claimed it, But they chose not to listen to Your orders or voice… They wouldn’t do what You told them to do, So You brought all these bad things upon them.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[24] '{Look!} Now, a great army has come to this city, And they have made plans to destroy it. To the hands of Chaldeans, it has been given… To those who are warring against it, Bringing the sword, famine, and plague… {Look!} All that You said has now come to pass!
[Jeremiah] [32]:[25] ‘Then You’ve told me to bring along silver, And before witnesses, purchase a field… Despite the fact that this city’s been given To the hands of Chaldeans!’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[26] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said: [‘[Jehovah] says:]
[Jeremiah] [32]:[27] ‘Since I am [Jehovah], the God of all flesh; [Did you think] that such things were hidden from Me?’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[28] ‘Then [Jehovah] said: ‘I have allowed this city to be given Into the hands of the Chaldeans, And into the hands of Babylon’s king… So, he will [very soon] take it!
[Jeremiah] [32]:[29] ‘The Chaldeans will come and [capture] this city, Then they will burn it with fire, Consuming the houses where people burn incense Upon their roofs, before [a] BaAl, And where they offer [food] to their gods In order to make Me feel bitter.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[30] ‘Only the sons of IsraEl and Judah Would practice such evil in front of My eyes. For, since their youth, they’ve offered such things Before [those gods] that they made with their hands, In order to make Me feel bitter,’ says [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [32]:[31] ‘So My anger and rage has been on this place From the day it was built until now, To remove it from in front of My face
[Jeremiah] [32]:[32] For the bad ways of IsraEl and Judah. ‘They’ve done all these things to make Me feel bitter… Their kings, their rulers, their prophets, and priests… The men of Judah and JeruSalem.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[33] ‘They turned their faces and showed Me their backs… So each morning, I [sent someone] to teach them, But they chose not to listen or learn.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[34] ‘Then, in their unclean condition, They put disgusting things in the House That is called by My Name.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[35] ‘There, they built shrines to [a] BaAl; And to Molech, they’ve offered their daughters and sons Down in the Valley of Hinnom… Something that I never told them to do. Such disgusting things never entered My heart To make Judah sin [in this way].’
[Jeremiah] [32]:[36] Then [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl made a pronouncement against the city, for He told me to say this: ‘Through famine, sword, and the plague, I’ve handed this city to Babylon’s king.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[37] But {Look!} I’ll also gather them back from those lands Where I’ll scatter them in My rage… From all that I’ll do in My fury! ‘I’ll bring them back to this place, And in safety, I’ll resettle them here;
[Jeremiah] [32]:[38] Then, they’ll be My people and I’ll be their God.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[39] ‘I’ll give them new ways and new hearts So that they will learn how to fear Me For the rest of their days and for their own good, And for the good of their children.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[40] ‘A [New] Sacred Agreement of the ages I’ll make with them at that time… An Agreement that I won’t take away. Then I’ll put the fear of Me in their hearts, So from Me, they’ll not turn again.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[41] ‘Then I’ll visit them just to do good things; And with My whole heart and soul, I’ll plant them securely here in this land.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[42] Then [Jehovah] said: ‘And as I brought bad things upon them, I’ll also bring the good things that I promised.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[43] Then they will buy fields in this land That you say won’t be walked by man or by beast, For it’s been handed over to the Chaldeans. ‘So with silver, they’ll buy these fields once again, Which they’ll record and seal in a scroll, And to which, witnesses will then testify.
[Jeremiah] [32]:[44] ‘[It will happen] in BenJamin’s land, And in JeruSalem and the cities of Judah… In all the towns in the mountains, And in the ShepheLa and Negev… From wherever they were taken, I’ll be bringing them back,’ says [Jehovah].’
[Jeremiah] [33]:[1] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to JeremiAh a second time while he was still shackled in the courtyard of the guard.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[2] He said: ‘The Lord who shaped and created the earth Whose Name is [Jehovah], says this:
[Jeremiah] [33]:[3] ‘Call out to Me and I will reply… I’ll report of things both mighty and great About which, you’ve never known!’
[Jeremiah] [33]:[4] Then the Lord God of IsraEl told me how the houses of the city [of JeruSalem] and the [palace] of the king of Judah would be demolished for use as siege mounds and fortifications
[Jeremiah] [33]:[5] in their fight against the Chaldeans, and of how they would then be filled with the [bodies] of those whom [He will] strike down in His anger and rage when He turns His face away from the city because of all its wickedness.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[6] [He said]: '{Look!} Then I’ll bring a cure and a closing of wounds… I’ll treat them, and then I’ll make sure That they will all hear and then come to know That I’ll bring them peace they can trust.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[7] ‘I’ll return those of IsraEl and Judah That were [carried away] and resettled, And I will rebuild them as they once were.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[8] ‘I will cleanse them of all their errors, And from the ways that they’ve sinned against Me. No way will I remember their errors, Or all the ways that they left Me.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[9] ‘Then, before all those who live on the earth, I’ll give them a joyful, praised name. For, all will hear of the good things I’ll do, And they will be humbled and fearful Because of the good and the peace That I will be bringing upon them.’
[Jeremiah] [33]:[10] Then the Lord said to me: ‘In this place that you’ll call desolation, You’ll hear [the sounds of] both men and beasts Once more in the cities of Judah. ‘And then, outside of JeruSalem, In those desolate places where the sounds of men and beasts are not heard,
[Jeremiah] [33]:[11] There’ll be the voices of gladness and joy… The sounds of grooms and their brides, And the sounds of men who are saying: ‘Praise the Almighty God; For [Jehovah] really does care, And upon us, He’ll show mercy throughout the ages!’ ‘Then they’ll carry gifts to the House of [Jehovah]; And those taken from the land, I’ll return,’ said the Lord.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[12] ‘And [Jehovah] of Armies said: ‘But this first must become a desolate place, And its cities will be void of cattle and men… It will be a place where shepherds will lodge, And a place for them to bed down their flocks.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[13] ‘In all the cities in the mountains… In the cities of the ShepheLa and Negev… Throughout BenJamin’s land… In the places outside of JeruSalem And in all the cities of Judah, There will just be those who count sheep,’ said [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [33]:[14] ‘Look! The days are coming,’ says [Jehovah], ‘When I’ll [fulfill] all the good words I’ve spoken About the houses of IsraEl and Judah.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[15] ‘Yes, in those days and at that time; From David, a shoot that is righteous will sprout, And a king will reign who’ll bring understanding, As well as what’s righteous and fair to this land.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[16] ‘In those days, upon Judah, salvation will come, And JeruSalem will be lived in securely. Then they’ll call [Me] ‘[Jehovah] Our Justice.’
[Jeremiah] [33]:[17] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘There’ll always be a man of David’s [line] That will sit on IsraEl’s throne.
[Jeremiah] [33]:[18] ‘And from among the Levites and Priests, There will always be a man who will stand To bring burnt offerings before Me, Along with sacrifices, incense, and gifts Throughout the rest of the days.’
[Jeremiah] [33]:[19] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to JeremiAh saying:
