[Jeremiah] [51]:[28] Drag many nations [to fight] her… The king of the Medes and the rest of the earth… Their leaders and all their commanders!
[Jeremiah] [51]:[29] ‘Then the earth will be shaken and reel By [Jehovah’s] plans against Babylon, Since He’s arranged the extinction of Babylon’s land So that no one will live there again!
[Jeremiah] [51]:[30] ‘Babylon’s soldiers will fail to wage war… They’ll just sit in their forts as they’re losing control. They’ll become like women whose tents are ablaze, And then, her bars will be broken.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[31] ‘Those chasing will meet others chasing, As they pursue the announcers Who will meet with those who proclaim, And make the announcement to Babylon’s king That his great city was captured,
[Jeremiah] [51]:[32] And the last of his moats have been breached… That his ramparts have been burned by fire, And all of his men have surrendered.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[33] ‘For [Jehovah] of Armies (the God of IsraEl) says this: ‘The palace of Babylon’s king Will become a floor to do threshing… And now is the season for threshing, Because it’s time for the harvest!’
[Jeremiah] [51]:[34] ‘[And those living in Zion will say:] ‘By NebuChadNezzar, Babylon’s King, I was crushed and divided… He caught up with me in the darkness; Then, like a beast, he swallowed me down, And his belly was filled with My good things.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[35] So in misery and in great trouble, To Babylon, I was taken, And my blood was laid upon those Chaldeans.’ [‘And God says:]
[Jeremiah] [51]:[36] ‘But because of this,’ says [Jehovah], {Look!} I will judge your opponents And send My vengeance to them for the ways That they will be punishing you. ‘I’ll destroy her [rivers] and dry up her springs,
[Jeremiah] [51]:[37] And Babylon will become an extinction – A den for wild beasts and for snakes – Which won’t be lived in again.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[38] ‘As lions and their cubs are aroused in the heat, I’ll give them a drink that will make them all drunk… I’ll stupefy them and put them to sleep,
[Jeremiah] [51]:[39] Which will be a sleep for the ages From which they’ll never awaken,’ says [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [51]:[40] ‘I’ll bring them like lambs for the slaughter… Like rams that are mixed among [goats].
[Jeremiah] [51]:[41] ‘Thereafter, Sheshach will be captured, And the earth’s boastful ones will be hunted… For, Babylon will not be great again Among the rest of the nations.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[42] ‘May Babylon be covered up by ‘the sea'… May she be covered by the roar of its ‘waves'…
[Jeremiah] [51]:[43] May all her cities meet with destruction, And may her land become dry and unwalked. ‘Nothing alive will go there again, Nor will sons of men ever rest there.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[44] For, I will take vengeance upon Babylon, And from her mouth, I’ll snatch what she ate. No more will nations gather with her, And even her walls will soon fall.’
[Jeremiah] [51]:[45] So, get out of her midst, O my people… Let each man save his own life From the anger and rage of [Jehovah]. [The Lord continues:]
[Jeremiah] [51]:[46] ‘And don’t let your hearts be consumed… Don’t fear the reports that are heard in that land; For in one year, there’ll come a report, And in the next, another will come Of misery and sin in that land, And of one leader ruling another. [‘And [Jehovah] says:]
[Jeremiah] [51]:[47] ‘Because of this, {Look!} days will come When I’ll bring vengeance on Babylon’s idols. Then, all in their land will be shamed, As in her midst, the slain will be falling.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[48] ‘Heaven and earth will be joyful, As well as all those who live there. For her destroyer will come from the north,’ says [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [51]:[49] ‘And as Babylon murdered the IsraElites, The slain will fall in Babylon’s land.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[50] ‘So flee, O you who have been saved from the sword, For you should stay there no longer! Then speak of [Jehovah] in far-away lands… And JeruSalem should remain in your hearts! [‘You should say:]
[Jeremiah] [51]:[51] ‘We were shamed when we heard of our scorn, And in dishonor, we covered our faces; For, foreigners entered our Most Holy Place… They entered the Temple of [Jehovah]!’ [‘And [Jehovah] continues:]
[Jeremiah] [51]:[52] ‘And because of this, {Look!} days will come,’ said [Jehovah], ‘When I’ll take vengeance upon her carved idols, And the slain will fall in her land.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[53] ‘So if Babylon could climb up into the skies And fortify her strength in the heights; I’d still send those who’d destroy her,’ said [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [51]:[54] ‘So from Babylon, you will hear cries, As destruction comes to the Chaldeans.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[55] [Jehovah] will remove Babylon… With the sounds of waves, He’ll destroy her, And to her voice, He’ll bring ruin.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[56] ‘Misery will come upon Babylon, For her warriors will soon all be captured, And terror will come to her bowmen… Yes, this is her payback from God.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[57] ‘The Lord will repay her with what she is due, And he’ll make them all [reel like] drunks… Yes, her governors, commanders, and wise men,’ Says the King, [Jehovah] the Almighty.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[58] ‘And thus says [Jehovah] the Almighty: ‘The broad walls of Babylon will fall, And her gates will fail and be burned; For the nations and peoples will tire of her pride.’
[Jeremiah] [51]:[59] These were the words that the Lord had instructed JeremiAh the Prophet to say to SeraiAh (son of NeriAh and grandson of MaAseJah) [back] when he went with ZedekiAh (the king of Judah) into Babylon in the 4th year of his reign (SeraiAh was in charge of the gifts that were [brought to the king]).
[Jeremiah] [51]:[60] Then JeremiAh wrote of all the bad things that were to come upon Babylon in a scroll, including all the rest of these words that were written against Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [51]:[61] JeremiAh also told SeraiAh that when he got to Babylon, he was to read all of these words to [the people of Babylon], and then say:
[Jeremiah] [51]:[62] ‘It was [Jehovah] that spoke ill of this place… He’s the One who said He’d destroy it So that no one will ever live here again… Neither man nor beast, throughout the ages.’
[Jeremiah] [51]:[63] [Then JeremiAh told him:] ‘Then, when you finish reading this scroll, tie it to a rock and toss it into the Euphrates, and tell them:
[Jeremiah] [51]:[64] ‘This is how Babylon will sink And not be raised up again… She’ll vanish, because of the bad things He’ll bring.’ Yes, these were all the words of JeremiAh.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[1] Well, King ZedekiAh was 21 years old when he started his reign, and he ruled from JeruSalem for 11 years. His mother’s name was HamuTal, and she was the daughter of JeremiAh of LibNah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[2] For, like JehoiAkim, the things that he did were wicked before [Jehovah].
[Jeremiah] [52]:[3] And this is why the wrath of [Jehovah] stayed upon JeruSalem and Judah until He finally cast them away from His face… For then ZedekiAh rebelled against the king of Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[4] It was in the 9th year and 10th month of his reign, on the 10th day of the month that NebuChadNezzar the king of Babylon came against JeruSalem with all his armies. He camped outside of the city and built a rampart around it,
[Jeremiah] [52]:[5] and the city stayed under siege until the 11th year of King ZedekiAh.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[6] So by the 9th day of the 4th month, there was famine in the city, and there was no longer any bread for the people in the land.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[7] Thereafter, the city’s [walls] were breached and all its warriors fled… They escaped during the night by way of the gate in the middle of the wall and the area around the wall that was next to the king’s garden. [They did this] as the Chaldeans were already in and around the city… And then they headed towards the desert.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[8] Well, the army of the Chaldeans chased after the king, catching up with him on the other side of JeriCho, where all of his servants had left him.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[9] So they captured the king and led him to the king of Babylon (who was in RibLah in the land of HaMath at the time), where he spoke to him and then passed judgment on him.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[10] Then the king of Babylon had all the sons of ZedekiAh killed before his eyes, and he killed all the rulers of Judah there in RibLah.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[11] And thereafter, he blinded the eyes of ZedekiAh, bound him in shackles, and the king of Babylonian had him carried to Babylon, where he was kept in a mill house until the day that he died.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[12] It was during the 5th month, on the 10th day of the month, that NabuZarArdan (the chief of the guards who always stood before the king of Babylon) came to JeruSalem
[Jeremiah] [52]:[13] and he burned the [Jehovah’s] Temple, the king’s palace, and all the houses in the city, including all of its mansions.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[14] Then the chief of the guards had the Chaldean armies tear down all of the city walls,
[Jeremiah] [52]:[15] and he removed all of the poor people (those who had been left behind in the city) as well as those who had gone over to the king of Babylon, along with everyone else.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[16] However, the chief of the guards did leave some of the poor people behind to serve as vinedressers and farmers.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[17] Then the Chaldeans broke up the columns of brass that stood outside the [Jehovah’s] Temple, along with their bases and the brass Sea, and they carried all the brass off to Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[18] This included: The bowls, The meat hooks, and The rest of the brass items that were used to officiate [at the Temple]...
[Jeremiah] [52]:[19] As well as the silver things: The snuffers, The oil flasks, The lamp stands, The incense pans, And the cups. Then the chief of the guards took all the things that were made of gold and silver
[Jeremiah] [52]:[20] (along with the two columns, the Sea, and the 12 brass calves that were under the Sea, which King Solomon had made for the Temple of [Jehovah]) [back to Babylon].
[Jeremiah] [52]:[21] No one could know the weight of all the brass; for the columns were each 33 feet (10m) tall, they had a circumference of 22 feet (6.7m), and their walls were 4 fingers thick.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[22] The moldings were also 8 feet (2.4m) long (one of them was very fine), and there was a net of pomegranates around the moldings, all of which was made of brass.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[23] There were 96 pomegranates on each [molding] and 100 pomegranates on each of the nets that encircled them.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[24] Then the chief of the guards carried off: SeraiAh (the High Priest), ZephaniAh (his second in command), And three of the Temple’s entrance guards.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[25] And from the city, he took: One of the eunuchs who was in charge of the warriors, Seven of the famous men who stood before the king (all of whom were found in the city), The scribe of the armies, The one who acted as scribe for the people of the land, And 60 men from among the people of the land who were found in the midst of the city.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[26] NabuZarArdan (the chief of the guards) took them all away and led them before the king of Babylon in RibLah,
[Jeremiah] [52]:[27] and the king of Babylon had them all killed at RibLah (in the land of HaMath). Then the rest of the people of Judah were deported from the land.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[28] [To summarize:] In his 7th year [597 BC], there were 3,023 people whom King NebuChadNezzar deported.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[29] Then in the 18th year of NebuChadNezzar [586 BC], he deported another 832 souls from JeruSalem.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[30] And in the 23rd year of his reign [581 BC], the chief of the guards deported 745 more souls from among the Judeans. So, the total came to 4,600.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[31] Then in the 37th year, on the 25th day of the 12th month after the relocation of King JehoiAchin of Judah, King EvilMerodach of Babylon took King JehoiAchin of Judah and led him from the house where he’d been kept under guard (he did this in the 1st year of his reign).
[Jeremiah] [52]:[32] Then he spoke to him kindly and gave him a throne that was higher than all the thrones of the other kings who were there with him in Babylon.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[33] He took him from his prison, provided him with better clothes, and allowed him to eat bread before him for as long as he lived.
[Jeremiah] [52]:[34] He was also provided a daily allowance by the king of Babylon until the day that he died.
[Lamentations] [1]:[1] After IsraEl was captured and JeruSalem was desolated, JeremiAh sat down and cried, wailing this lamentation over the city: ‘O how that city, once filled with people Must now sit all alone. Among the nations, she [sits as] a widow… She is ruled and [must pay] a tribute.
[Lamentations] [1]:[2] ‘She cried and wept all through the night, As tears rolled down her cheeks; For, no one is left to offer her comfort Among all those who once loved her. Yes, those who cared have now left her, And her enemies, they’ve become.
[Lamentations] [1]:[3] ‘Humiliation has come upon Judah, For [all of her people] were [taken away] And she has become just a slave. ‘Now, she finds no way to rest, Because she [belongs to] the gentiles. Yes, all those who chased her have caught her, And [she lives] among those who oppress her.
[Lamentations] [1]:[4] ‘The roads to Zion now mourn, For there’s no one who comes there To celebrate her holiday feasts. ‘All of her gates have been broken, All of her Priests must now groan, And all of her virgins are captives; So, inside herself, she’s bitter.
[Lamentations] [1]:[5] For her head is those who oppose her, And to her enemies, [she now must submit]. ‘Her humiliation was brought by [Jehovah], Because she no longer showed Him respect. So her young were led off as captives Before those who have oppressed her.
[Lamentations] [1]:[6] ‘The daughters of Zion (her beauty) are gone, [And others now serve as] their rulers. As rams without pasture, they left without strength In front of those who’d pursued them.
[Lamentations] [1]:[7] So, when she thinks of these days of disgrace, She is very upset. ‘All of her beautiful things [are now gone]… Those things that she’s had since most ancient times. For her people fell into the hands of oppressors, And no one came to their aid. Then all her enemies laughed When they saw these things being taken away.
[Lamentations] [1]:[8] ‘It was because of JeruSalem’s sins That she was allowed to be battered. She was humbled by the One who’d loved her When He saw how indecent she’d become. So now, she [just sits there and] groans, And all she does is reflect.
[Lamentations] [1]:[9] ‘Her filth lies there at her feet, Because she forgot how things would work out. So, she’s now been brought low, And there’s no place where she can find comfort. ‘[She cries]: ‘O Lord, see how I’ve been shamed; For, to my enemies, I now must submit!’
[Lamentations] [1]:[10] ‘Those who oppressed her have reached out their hands To take her desirable things. She watched as the gentiles entered her [Temple]… Those whom [God] said should not enter Among the assembly [of His people].
[Lamentations] [1]:[11] ‘Now, all of her people are groaning Because they’re searching for bread. Her desirable things, they’ve traded for food, In order to save their own lives. ‘O [Jehovah], ‘Please look down upon this, For, she has been so disgraced! [And she says:]
[Lamentations] [1]:[12] ‘All those to whom You once became close But thereafter chose to reject You, Will see if there’s pain like the pain that I feel. For, I’ve been humbled by the One who addressed me… By [Jehovah], in the day of His rage.
[Lamentations] [1]:[13] ‘To my bones, He’s sent fire… Yes, fire is what He’s sent. Then He spread out a net for my feet To turn me back and make me retreat. He appointed me to be hidden from view And to grieve throughout the rest of my days.
[Lamentations] [1]:[14] ‘He was aware of my godless deeds; For, they were close to my hands… And then they [crawled] up my neck. So, all of my strength has now left me, Since [Jehovah’s] put grief in my hands And I’m unable to stand.
[Lamentations] [1]:[15] ‘All of my mighty have left me, As has [Jehovah], [my God]. For the time arrived for His visit, And to break the best of my men. So the Lord has trodden the winepress Of the virgin daughter of Judah.’
[Lamentations] [1]:[16] ‘It’s over such things that I weep… It’s why my eyes are now filled with tears. For, those who would offer me comfort (Those who would bring back my life) [Have now been carried] away. Yes, all of my sons are now gone… And by my enemies, I’ve been conquered.’
[Lamentations] [1]:[17] ‘So, although Zion has spread out her hands, There’s no one who’ll come to console her. For [Jehovah] gave a warning to Jacob That they’d be surrounded by those who’d attack. ‘JeruSalem was to serve as a woman Who was set apart from the unclean… Although she had to live in their midst.
[Lamentations] [1]:[18] Yet, [Jehovah] has been proven righteous; For, we’re the ones who embittered His mouth. [‘For she says:] ‘So, hear all you peoples and look at my pain, Since all my young men and virgins are gone… They’ve all been taken as captives!
[Lamentations] [1]:[19] ‘I was misled by those whom I loved… My priests and my elders had failed me! They just wanted food for themselves, So they could save their own lives.
[Lamentations] [1]:[20] ‘Behold, O Lord, my painful condition, For my stomach is very upset And my heart is rolling within me! ‘I’ve become very bitter, For the sword has left me without any sons… It’s as though there’s death in my home.
[Lamentations] [1]:[21] ‘Listen indeed to my groaning, For there’s no one to offer me comfort. Since our enemies had heard of our badness, They rejoiced at the things that they did. But upon them, You’ll bring a day and a time When they’ll become just like me!
[Lamentations] [1]:[22] ‘Yes, may their evils fall upon them… Glean them as they’ve gleaned me for my sins! For, [they’re the cause] of my groaning, And they’re the ones upsetting my heart.’
[Lamentations] [2]:[1] ‘O how dark was the rage of [Jehovah] When it came to the daughter of Zion. For He pulled IsraEl’s glory out of the heights And threw it down to the ground… Yes, in the day of His rage, He forgot the stool for His feet.
[Lamentations] [2]:[2] ‘[He] didn’t hold back, nor did He spare Jacob’s beautiful things. In His rage, He destroyed all the forts Of the virgin daughter of Judah. He cut them down to the ground, And profaned our rulers and king.
[Lamentations] [2]:[3] ‘He broke them to pieces in anger and rage, Taking all of IsraEl’s strength… He turned His hand from the enemy’s face And allowed them to set Jacob ablaze… To consume everything that’s around him.
[Lamentations] [2]:[4] ‘As an enemy, He stretched tight His bow, And as an opponent, he stiffened His hand To destroy all the things that my eyes had desired. On the Tents of the daughters of Zion, He poured out the flames of His rage.
[Lamentations] [2]:[5] ‘So [Jehovah] became our enemy… He sunk IsraEl and all its estates. He also destroyed all its forts… The strongholds of the daughters of Judah. ‘He multiplied those who were humbling us, And increased the numbers of humbled.
[Lamentations] [2]:[6] ‘Like a grapevine, He spread out His Tent, And His holiday feasts, He corrupted. He forgot all the things He’d appointed for Zion… The holiday feasts and the Sabbaths. He did this, because we’d provoked Him, Then He threatened our king and our priests in His rage.
[Lamentations] [2]:[7] ‘[He] thrust away His own Altar… His Holy Place, He’s brushed aside. So our enemies broke down our walls, And shouted in the House of [Jehovah] As we used to do on our holiday feasts.
[Lamentations] [2]:[8] ‘[Jehovah] made plans to ruin the walls Of the virgin daughter of Zion. First, He stretched out His ruler, Then His hand sent a trampling upon us, Which caused us to mourn around all our walls, Because the walls were destroyed,
[Lamentations] [2]:[9] And the gates had been cut to the ground… They broke and destroyed the bars for our gates! ‘So now, her king and her rulers Have been scattered among all the nations, And there’s no longer a Law, Nor do our prophets see visions.
[Lamentations] [2]:[10] ‘They silently sit on the ground (The elders of the daughter of Zion) As they throw dust on their heads… As they’re dressing in sackcloth… As the heads of JeruSalem’s virgins Are being pushed to the ground.
[Lamentations] [2]:[11] ‘Then the tears in my eyes started to fail, Because my heart had become so disturbed. My glory had just been poured on the ground By the destruction of all the daughters And the nursing mothers with babies, There in our city squares.
[Lamentations] [2]:[12] ‘From the mothers, they demanded their grain and their wine When they were as weak as the wounded. Then, in those squares, they poured out the lives [Of the babies] that nursed at their breasts.
[Lamentations] [2]:[13] ‘And now, what more can I say, O virgin daughter of JeruSalem… To what can you be compared? Who can now come and save you, O virgin daughter of Zion… Since the cup of destruction was widened for you, Who can now bring you healing?
[Lamentations] [2]:[14] ‘Although your prophets saw all of your folly, They refused to uncover your sins And save you from this captivity… Even though they were concerned about your foolish ways, And they knew that you had to be purged!
[Lamentations] [2]:[15] ‘Now, people clap hands as they’re passing, And whistle as they shake their heads Over JeruSalem’s daughter: ‘Isn’t she the one who was called glory’s crown… The most joyful place on the earth?’
[Lamentations] [2]:[16] ‘But your enemies opened their mouths And whistled, as they ground their teeth. They said: ‘We’ll swallow her down, And this is the day that we planned… We found it and [we made it happen]!’
[Lamentations] [2]:[17] ‘So [Jehovah] did what He’d decided… He finished what He said must be done… The things that He said [He must do] long ago. So He didn’t spare, He demolished… He brought your enemies joy over you, And raised the trumpets of those who attacked you!
[Lamentations] [2]:[18] ‘Before [Jehovah], they were yelling: ‘We’ll tear down all of Zion’s walls And make its people stream tears day and night! Don’t allow them the time to get sober, Or to let their eyes become still!’
[Lamentations] [2]:[19] ‘So, during the night, awaken and think… At the start of each watch, pour out your hearts Before the face of [Jehovah]! Raise your arms up before Him On behalf of the children who are starving, Which are found on every street corner!
[Lamentations] [2]:[20] ‘Behold, O Lord… ‘See what You’ve gleaned! Should women eat the fruit of their bellies? Should the babies be murdered as they’re nursing on breasts? Will you kill the priests and the prophets Inside the Holy Place of [Jehovah]?
[Lamentations] [2]:[21] ‘Young boys must now sleep in the streets Along with the old men and virgins. My young men were all taken captive, And then killed by the famine and swords. For, in the day of Your rage, You slashed and You haven’t spared any!
[Lamentations] [2]:[22] ‘As a festival day (as no other day), You called to those living around us. Then because of Your rage, no one was saved… They left no one behind… My enemies were filled, and You won.’
[Lamentations] [3]:[1] ‘Now, I’m a man who is helpless, For the rod of His rage has been laid upon me.
[Lamentations] [3]:[2] He took me, then led me away Into the darkness (not into the light).
[Lamentations] [3]:[3] ‘So, throughout the rest of my days, Against me, He’s turned His hand.
[Lamentations] [3]:[4] My flesh and my skin, He’s made old, And He’s broken my bones.
[Lamentations] [3]:[5] ‘Against me, He’s now built [a wall], And my head He’s encircled with trouble.
[Lamentations] [3]:[6] Inside a dark place, He has put me, As though I’d been dead throughout the ages.
[Lamentations] [3]:[7] ‘Against me, He’s constructed a wall Through which I can’t escape, And with a brass chain, He’s weighed me down.
[Lamentations] [3]:[8] ‘Although I cry out and yell, He’s shut out my prayers…
[Lamentations] [3]:[9] He’s blocked all my roads and my ways!
[Lamentations] [3]:[10] ‘He’s become a bear that’s lying in wait, And a lion that’s lurking, unseen.
[Lamentations] [3]:[11] When I rebelled, He then chased me down And caused me to no longer be… He established me to be wiped away.
[Lamentations] [3]:[12] ‘He’s stretched tight His bow, And set me on a stone as His target.
[Lamentations] [3]:[13] Into my kidneys, He’s shot poison arrows
[Lamentations] [3]:[14] And He’s made me a source of His laughter… A psalm throughout the whole day.
[Lamentations] [3]:[15] ‘With bitterness, He’s now filled me, And bile, I’ve been given to drink.
[Lamentations] [3]:[16] With a small rock, He knocked out my teeth, And then He gave me ashes to eat.
[Lamentations] [3]:[17] ‘He’s pushed peace from my life, And made me forget all the good things I had.
[Lamentations] [3]:[18] So I said that my victory had perished Along with my hope in [Jehovah].
[Lamentations] [3]:[19] ‘But, this is what I remembered: ‘Despite the state that I came to be in (My persecution, bitterness, and bile),
[Lamentations] [3]:[20] I haven’t been forgotten… Yes, my life will continue!
[Lamentations] [3]:[21] This is [the thought] that I’ve kept in my heart, And the reason why I keep on waiting.
[Lamentations] [3]:[22] ‘For the mercies of [God] never end, And His compassions will never fail.
[Lamentations] [3]:[23] Each morning, they are renewed, And on Him, we can always rely.
[Lamentations] [3]:[24] ‘The portion that’s mine is [Jehovah],’ said my soul. And because of this, I’ll keep waiting.
[Lamentations] [3]:[25] For [Jehovah] is good to all those who wait And wholeheartedly keep searching for Him.
[Lamentations] [3]:[26] ‘So it’s good [for us all] to be quiet And await [Jehovah’s] salvation.
[Lamentations] [3]:[27] And it’s also good for each man to bear His own yoke from the time he is young.
[Lamentations] [3]:[28] ‘Yes, we should sit all alone And quietly carry our loads,
[Lamentations] [3]:[29] Then put our mouths to the dust, And believe that there is still hope.
[Lamentations] [3]:[30] ‘We should turn the other cheek when they slap us, And we should accept all their scorn.
[Lamentations] [3]:[31] For, [in our hearts], we’ll know that [Jehovah] Won’t push us away throughout the ages.
[Lamentations] [3]:[32] Since, in His abundance of mercy, He shows pity for those who humble themselves.
[Lamentations] [3]:[33] ‘Harsh replies don’t come from His heart, As He teaches sons of men to be humble.
[Lamentations] [3]:[34] And now He’s humbled the feet Of those who have been carried away from this land.
[Lamentations] [3]:[35] ‘From before His face in the heights, He’s removed the decisions of men.
[Lamentations] [3]:[36] But [Jehovah] never said that He’d bring Condemnation upon all mankind.
[Lamentations] [3]:[37] And who could ever say such a thing… Yes, who could cause it to happen Without [Jehovah] saying it’s so?
[Lamentations] [3]:[38] ‘From His mouth in the heights can come good or bad.
[Lamentations] [3]:[39] So, why do the living choose to grumble At others concerning their sins?
[Lamentations] [3]:[40] For before Him, our ways are stretched and examined To see how we can be turned to the Lord.
[Lamentations] [3]:[41] So, we should lift our hearts with our hands Towards the Most High in heaven.

[Lamentations] [3]:[45] Then He pushed us away.

[Lamentations] [3]:[50] Until the time that I can look through And see [Jehovah] in the heavens.
[Lamentations] [3]:[51] ‘Now my eyes look back on my life in great rage For [what’s happened to] the daughters of my city.
[Lamentations] [3]:[52] ‘By our enemies, we were hunted like sparrows,
[Lamentations] [3]:[53] And now they have ended my life… they have tossed me into a grave And covered it up with a stone.
[Lamentations] [3]:[54] Then, as water dripped down on my head, I said: ‘I have just been thrown away.’
[Lamentations] [3]:[55] ‘So I called on Your Name, O [Jehovah], From out of the lowest of pits.
[Lamentations] [3]:[56] I said: ‘Don’t cover Your ears… Hear my voice and the things that I beg.’
[Lamentations] [3]:[57] ‘Then You came to my aid on the day that I called, And You told me that I shouldn’t be afraid!
[Lamentations] [3]:[58] ‘O Lord, ‘You have pleaded my case, And then You ransomed my soul.
[Lamentations] [3]:[59] For You’ve seen the things that they’ve done, O [Jehovah]; So pass judgement on them on my behalf.
[Lamentations] [3]:[60] ‘You’ve beheld their vengeance upon me, And the plans that they’ve laid out against me.
[Lamentations] [3]:[61] You listened to their scornful words And saw the [things that they did]…
[Lamentations] [3]:[62] You heard from the lips of those who attacked me And You knew what they thought all day long.
[Lamentations] [3]:[63] For, when they sat down and when they arose, You saw what they did through their own eyes!
[Lamentations] [3]:[64] ‘O [Jehovah], ‘Will You pay them back for what they deserve, According to the works of their hands?
[Lamentations] [3]:[65] Curse them for all the trouble they’ve caused,
[Lamentations] [3]:[66] Then pursue them in rage and remove them From all places under the sky, O Lord.
[Lamentations] [4]:[1] ‘O how the gold’s lost its luster And how the silver’s been tarnished; For the [Temple’s] holy stones have been tossed in the streets.
[Lamentations] [4]:[2] ‘For because the sons of Zion esteemed And gained their courage from things made of gold, They came to be looked on as earthenware pots… And as works in the hands of a potter.
[Lamentations] [4]:[3] ‘Then, nursing cubs were stripped from the breasts By those who’d become like the Dragon, And the daughters of my people were abandoned Like sparrows that are lost in the desert.
[Lamentations] [4]:[4] ‘Now the tongues of the nursing, stick to the breasts, In hope that their thirst can be quenched. And as the infants are crying for bread, It’s being snatched from their mouths.
[Lamentations] [4]:[5] ‘So from those who once ate the best, All been taken away… And those who were raised wearing purple Are found in the streets embracing manure.
[Lamentations] [4]:[6] ‘For the lawless ways of my people’s daughters Proved to be greater than Sodom… That place which none tried to save When it was being wiped away.
[Lamentations] [4]:[7] ‘Her Nazarites were once like the snow… Radiant and whiter than milk… Yes, even better than sapphires!
[Lamentations] [4]:[8] But now, their appearance is darker than soot, And they’re unrecognized in the streets. For their skin is now stuck to their bones, And they’ve dried up like lumber.
[Lamentations] [4]:[9] ‘It was better for those who were killed by the sword Than for those who have been pierced by starvation… Those in want of the produce of fields.
[Lamentations] [4]:[10] ‘And the hands of women [who were known for their] pity, Then boiled their own children as food… So amid the destruction of the daughters of my people,
[Lamentations] [4]:[11] [Jehovah] completed His rage. ‘Then, as He poured out the wrath of His rage, He lit a fire throughout Zion, Which burned her to her foundations.

[Lamentations] [4]:[13] ‘But it happened because of the sins of her prophets… The failures of all her priests… And the shedding of innocent blood in her midst.
[Lamentations] [4]:[14] ‘Then, in her streets, her watchmen were stunned; For, they became [spattered] with blood… It was something that they couldn’t avoid, Since the clothes that they wore had to touch it.

Get away… Get away… Don’t touch them!’ ‘Then, after we fled and wandered about, The gentiles said: ‘You can’t stay among us!’ ‘Yes the gentiles shouted at us: ‘There’s no way that we want you to come here!’
[Lamentations] [4]:[16] ‘Even though our portion was the person of [God], He no longer kept watch over us, For the people had shown no respect To their elders or Priests.
[Lamentations] [4]:[17] ‘So our eyes had started to fail As we were searching for aid… They just watched us and offered no help… A nation with no one to save them.
[Lamentations] [4]:[18] ‘Now, stay away from our city squares, For they’re hunting our young… Our time has approached and our days are fulfilled, So our end is now close at hand!
[Lamentations] [4]:[19] ‘For, those who chase us are even more agile Than eagles [that attack from] the mountains… They’re sitting there and waiting for us From their perches high over the desert.
[Lamentations] [4]:[20] ‘[Jehovah’s] anointed (our life’s breath and lord) Has also been seized and carried away Because we became so corrupt… Yes, this one about whom we’d once said: ‘Among the nations, we’ll dwell in his shadow.’
[Lamentations] [4]:[21] ‘So rejoice and be glad, O daughter of Edom… The one who is residing in Uz! Yet you’ll also go into the cup of the Lord, Where, after you’re drunk, you’ll be poured.’

[Ezekiel] [1]:[1] It was during the 30th year, in the 4th month and on the 5th day of the month, as I was amidst the captivity by the Chobar River, that the heavens opened up and I beheld visions [from] God.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[2] This was 5 years and 5 months after King JehoiAchin had been carried off as a captive.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[3] The Word of [Jehovah] came to me, EzekiEl son of Buzi (a Priest), near the Chobar river in the land of the Chaldeans. And this is what I received from the hand of the Lord...
[Ezekiel] [1]:[4] For I looked up and I saw a wind that could lift iron coming from the north, along with a huge cloud that had bright lights all around it and flashes of lightning. I also had a vision of a bright bronze casting in the middle of a fire.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[5] Then there in its midst was something that looked like four animals. But in this vision, they also looked like men.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[6] Each had four faces and four wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[7] Their legs were straight, there were feathers on their feet, there were sparks like flashes of brass, and they had very fine wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[8] Beneath each of their four wings was a man’s hand, and they had wings on each of their four parts. So, they each had four faces and four wings,
[Ezekiel] [1]:[9] and they traveled opposite to [the direction] they were facing. Also, their wings didn’t turn as they moved.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[10] Each of the faces [in the front] were like those of a man, the faces on the right looked like lions, the faces on the left looked like calves, and there was the face of an eagle on [the back side of] each of the four.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[11] [Two of] their wings stretched out high above the other [two] wings and they were yoked to each other, while their lower two wings were just used to cover their bodies.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[12] They followed each other [in a line], one in front of the other, and wherever [God’s] breath led them they went, not turning aside.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[13] Also, there among the animals, I had a vision of burning coals that looked like lamps that were spinning in their midst. The flames were very bright, and lightning shot from the flames.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[14] Also, the animals were moving up and back like lightning.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[15] Then I looked and I saw wheels on the ground that were next to each of the four animals,
[Ezekiel] [1]:[16] and the wheels [sparkled] like peridots. There also appeared to be four wheels within each wheel, and they worked as though there were wheels within wheels.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[17] Each [wheel] moved in the direction that [the animals] faced, and they [moved together]
[Ezekiel] [1]:[18] (the rims were tall and awesome). Then I looked again and I noticed that their back sides were full of eyes that went all around each of the four wheels.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[19] As the animals moved, the wheels moved next to them. And when the animals lifted up from the ground, the wheels went up also,
[Ezekiel] [1]:[20] along with a cloud that went wherever [God’s] breath led it. The animals and the wheels moved up along with [the cloud], because the breath of life was in the wheels.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[21] Wherever [the animals] traveled, the wheels went along. For when they stood still, the wheels stood still, but when they rose above the ground, the wheels went up with them, because the breath of life was in the wheels.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[22] Above the heads of the animals was what looked like a dome of ice that was stretched out over the tops of their wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[23] And under this dome, their wings were stretched out and flapping side by side, as the other two [wings] covered their bodies.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[24] The sound that I heard from the movement of their wings as they traveled was like the sound of a lot of rushing water and the sound of someone very important whenever they moved. However, it was like the sound of [many] words being spoken in a camp whenever the animals stood still and rested their wings.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[25] {Look!} There was also a sound that came from above the dome.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[26] In the vision [that I had], above their heads there was what looked like a huge sapphire stone; and sitting above it was a throne upon which was sitting what appeared to be a man from the heavens.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[27] I saw what looked like molten bronze that was filled with fire around and above His loins; and beneath that, I just saw fire and brightness all around Him.
[Ezekiel] [1]:[28] He was like a rainbow that forms in the clouds on a rainy day, and there was just brightness all around Him. This was, in fact, a vision of the likeness of the glory of [Jehovah]! And when I saw this, I fell to my face. Then I heard a voice that started speaking [to me]...
[Ezekiel] [2]:[1] He said to me: ‘Son of man; you must stand on your feet, And thereafter, I will address you!’
[Ezekiel] [2]:[2] And at that, His spirit came over me… It picked me up and lifted me up on my feet! Then I heard Him speaking to me.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[3] He said: ‘O son of man, ‘To the sons of IsraEl, I’ll send you… To those who’re rebelling against Me. For against Me, they and their fathers Have been in rebellion down to this day.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[4] ‘They’re a harsh and hard-hearted people, And these are the ones to whom you’ll be sent. So, tell them that thus says [Jehovah]:
[Ezekiel] [2]:[5] You should listen in terror, For you are a house in rebellion. And [after you do this], they’ll know That you’ve served as a Prophet among them.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[6] ‘And you, O son of man, should not be afraid Or be upset by their faces. For they will get all heated up, Then they will rise up against you, And they will have you surrounded. ‘So, among these scorpions, you’ll have to live… But don’t fear the things that they’ll say to your face, For they are a house in rebellion.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[7] ‘You must then tell them My words, So that they will hear them and fear… For they are a house in rebellion.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[8] ‘Now you, O son of man, must pay close attention To the One who’ll be speaking to you… Don’t rebel, like that house in rebellion! ‘Now, open your mouth very wide And eat this thing that I’m handing to you!’
[Ezekiel] [2]:[9] So at that, I looked and I saw a hand that was reaching out towards me with a rolled up scroll.
[Ezekiel] [2]:[10] But then He unrolled it before me… And written on both the front and backsides was a lamentation and a dirge.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[1] Then He said to me: ‘O son of man, you must eat this… And after you eat it, You must tell the sons of IsraEl [what it says]!’
[Ezekiel] [3]:[2] So He opened my mouth in order to feed me the scroll...
[Ezekiel] [3]:[3] Then He said to me: ‘O son of man’ ‘After I put this scroll in your mouth, Your belly will get filled with this thing That I am feeding to you.’ So I ate it and found it to be as sweet as honey in my mouth.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[4] Then He said to me: ‘O son of man, Now, go to the house of IsraEl And tell them all that I have to say!
[Ezekiel] [3]:[5] ‘You won’t have to speak to those with thick lips Or to those who speak foreign tongues… For to the house of IsraEl, you’re being sent.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[6] ‘I will not send you to other nations … To those who speak words that you won’t understand Or to those who have foreign, thick tongues Those who won’t know what you’re saying, But to those who will understand you.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[7] ‘Yet, the house of IsraEl will not listen To the things that I’ll tell you to say… They’ll not agree to listen to Me, Since they are a hard-hearted people And all they do is talk back.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[8] '{Look!} Now, against their faces, I’ve made your face strong, So your face will be firmer than theirs… Yes, it will be harder than rock.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[9] ‘So, don’t be afraid [when you go] before them, And you should not be afraid, For they are a house in rebellion.’
[Ezekiel] [3]:[10] And he said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Now, take My words into your heart, And listen to them with your ears.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[11] Then, tell the captive sons of your people That The Lord [Jehovah] has spoken, And surely they’ll listen and yield.’
[Ezekiel] [3]:[12] Well after that, [His] spirit stood me erect, and from behind me I heard a rumbling sound that spoke to me and said: ‘Praise the glory of [Jehovah] That has come [to you] from His realm!’
[Ezekiel] [3]:[13] Then I heard the sound of the flapping of the wings of the animals (because [the wings] were touching each other), as well as the sounds of the wheels that were moving next to them with a great rumbling.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[14] And thereafter, [God’s] breath lifted me up and carried me away… So my spirit was being lifted and motivated by the hand of [Jehovah] that had come over me, and this made me extremely powerful!
[Ezekiel] [3]:[15] Then, while I was in this elevated [condition], I traveled among the rest of captives that live next to the Chobar River, and I stayed there for 7 days.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[16] And at the end of the 7 days, the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said this:
[Ezekiel] [3]:[17] ‘O son of man, ‘Over the house of IsraEl, I have made you the watchman. So you must listen to the words from my mouth, And then, you must bring them my warnings.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[18] ‘For I’m saying that the lawless will die! And you will also die with them If you fail to give them my orders. ‘Give these warnings to those lawless people And tell them that they will only survive If they’ll turn from their unrighteous ways! But, if they should choose to stay lawless, They will die for their sins, And I won’t require their blood from your hands.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[19] ‘If you give my word to the lawless, And they refuse to turn from their ways; They will die in their sins, But I will still rescue you.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[20] ‘For, if a righteous man should turn from right ways And start doing things that are evil; I’ll torment his face ‘til he dies. But, if you’ve failed to bring him my word, And this is what caused him to die, So his righteous deeds are forgotten; I’ll require his blood from your hands.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[21] ‘But, if you will give [my] word to the righteous, And you warn them that they must not sin… And they choose not to sin because they’ve been warned, And this results in their being saved; You will have saved your own life.’
[Ezekiel] [3]:[22] And after that, the hand of the Lord came upon me and said: ‘Now arise and go out to the plains; For there, I will tell you much more!’
[Ezekiel] [3]:[23] So I got up and went out to the plains... And {Look!} there was the glory of [Jehovah] – the glory that I had seen by the Chobar River – and I fell to my face.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[24] Then [God’s] breath came over me and stood me up on my feet… And it spoke to me and said: ‘Go home and lock yourself inside your house;
[Ezekiel] [3]:[25] {Look!} For you, O son of man, are appointed to be bound… Yes, they will come here and then tie you up, And no way will you set yourself free.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[26] ‘They’ll also wrap your tongue in your throat, So you’ll be unable to speak, And you won’t be able to scold them; For, they are a house in rebellion.
[Ezekiel] [3]:[27] ‘But then, my voice will start speaking through you… I will open your mouth, and you’ll tell them That this was said by [Jehovah]: ‘All that wish to hear, should now listen! But, those who don’t wish to make any change Can continue to resist My persuasion; For you are a house in rebellion!’
[Ezekiel] [4]:[1] ‘And you, O son of man; Must go find a brick, Then set it in front of your face. ‘Draw a map of JeruSalem upon it,
[Ezekiel] [4]:[2] Then surround it with a circle of forts. Also draw a siege mound and camps, And encircle the city with weapons.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[3] ‘Then, go find an iron frying pan, And set it as a wall between you and the city, Then prepare your face to oppose it… Prepare for a siege, then attack it… And to the sons of IsraEl, this will serve as a sign!
[Ezekiel] [4]:[4] ‘Then, go to sleep on your left side, And lay the sins of the house of IsraEl upon you… You must bear their unrighteous ways For the number of days that you’ll sleep [on that side].
[Ezekiel] [4]:[5] ‘For I’ve appointed two things that you must do Because of their unrighteous deeds: ‘The unrighteous ways of the house of IsraEl Must be born upon you, For 390 [full] days.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[6] ‘Then, after that, you must sleep on your right For the house of Judah’s unrighteous ways. You must do this for 40 more days… A day for each year, is what I’ve established!
[Ezekiel] [4]:[7] ‘And as for the siege on JeruSalem; Prepare your face and stiffen your arm; For against [that city], you must then prophesy.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[8] '{Look!} Because I’ve appointed their bondage on you, Don’t turn from one side to the other, Until the days of your siege are fulfilled.

[Ezekiel] [4]:[10] And the weight of the food that you can consume Will be just 10 ounces a day, Which you may eat at various times.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[11] ‘You must also measure the water you’ll drink… You may drink just 10 ounces from time to time.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[12] ‘And bake the barley cakes that you’ll eat Over human manure, Which you must hide in the coals Before the eyes [of the people].’
[Ezekiel] [4]:[13] ‘For this was said by [Jehovah], the God of IsraEl: ‘This is the type of uncleanness That the sons of IsraEl will eat Among the nations where they will be thrown.’
[Ezekiel] [4]:[14] But I said: ‘Absolutely not, O Lord God of IsraEl! ‘For my soul has never been defiled or made unclean by decaying flesh, nor have I eaten wild animals from [the day] that I was born until now… Nothing unclean has ever entered my mouth!’
[Ezekiel] [4]:[15] So [the Lord] said to me: ‘Then, rather than using human manure, I’ll allow you to use cattle dung… You may bake your loaves over that.’
[Ezekiel] [4]:[16] And he said to me: ‘O son of man, '{Look!} I’ll break JeruSalem’s trust in its bread; For they’ll have to ration it out, And they’ll ration the water they drink ‘til it’s gone.
[Ezekiel] [4]:[17] ‘Since there won’t be enough water or bread, Each man [will steal] from his brother, And because of their unrighteous deeds, They will then melt away.’

[Ezekiel] [5]:[8] ‘So because of this,’ says [Jehovah], '{Look!} I am now standing against you, And I’ll bring My judgments upon you, There in front of the gentiles!

[Ezekiel] [5]:[13] ‘But, after I’ve brought My anger and rage, I’ll return and offer you comfort. For then, you’ll know that this happened Because I, [Jehovah], had warned you, And in My zeal, I showed you My rage.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[14] ‘I’ll turn you and your daughters into waterless lands In the presence of all that pass by.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[15] For the nations will squeeze you and scoff When I bring My anger and judgments on you, Along with My vengeance and rage. For I, [Jehovah], have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[16] ‘I’ll shoot the arrows of famine at you, And after you come to be in great need, I’ll send [the nations] to finish you off. Yes, I’m sending a famine among you, To break your reliance on bread.
[Ezekiel] [5]:[17] ‘I’ll not only bring a famine to you, But I’ll also send ferocious wild beasts! And with plagues, you will also be punished, Before your blood will be spilled; For upon you, I’m bringing the sword. Yes, I, [Jehovah], have spoken!’
[Ezekiel] [6]:[1] Thereafter, the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [6]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Now, turn your face towards IsraEl’s hills, And against them, you must now prophesy!
[Ezekiel] [6]:[3] ‘Speak to those in IsraEl’s mountains And tell them to hear the Word of [Jehovah]! Yes, hear what [God] has decreed To the mountains, hills, valleys, and forests: '{Look!} Against you, I’m bringing the broadsword And it will destroy your high places.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[4] I will also break all your altars; Your [incense stands], I’ll tear down; And before their idols, I’ll leave all your slain. ‘The bodies of IsraEl’s sons Will be offered in front of their idols;
[Ezekiel] [6]:[5] And then, on their altars, I’ll scatter their bones.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[6] ‘All the homes in your towns will be empty; All your high places will be wiped away; All your altars will be destroyed; Your idols will no longer be, And your incense stands will be lifted away… Your works will all be erased.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[7] Then, as the slain are falling among you, You will know that I am [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [6]:[8] ‘Then, those who escape from the broadsword Will be scattered among all the nations.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[9] And those who escape from the nations Where they will be taken as captives, Will start thinking of Me once again. ‘I vow this against the hearts of all those Who have committed adultery against Me And done so many bad things… They will slap their own faces Over the vile acts they’ve performed.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[10] Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah], And that this is why I sent them the warning That I’d bring such evil upon them.’
[Ezekiel] [6]:[11] ‘And thereafter, [Jehovah] said: ‘Clap your hands… Yes, stamp your feet and then say: ‘This is what they deserve For the disgusting things that IsraEl’s done!’ Yes, may they fall by the broadsword, As well as by famine and plague!
[Ezekiel] [6]:[12] ‘Then, those far away will die by the plague; Those who are near will fall by the sword; And those who remain after the siege Will be finished off by the famine, As I wear out My anger against them.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[13] ‘And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah], When among your idols, you’ll see all your slain… The idols that you’ve placed on all the high hills And under each shade tree and bush, Before which, you have burned incense.
[Ezekiel] [6]:[14] ‘For, against such ones, I’ll stretch out My hand, And I’ll bring an end to their homes and their lands… I’ll dry them out like figs in the desert, And they’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [7]:[1] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me again and said:
[Ezekiel] [7]:[2] ‘And to you, O son of man, ‘[Jehovah] says this about IsraEl: ‘To the 4 wings of the land, The end has finally come…
[Ezekiel] [7]:[3] Yes, the end has arrived; For upon them, I’m bringing My rage. ‘I’m the one who is standing against them And I’ll punish them for the things that they’ve done… I’ll hold them to blame for their evil,
[Ezekiel] [7]:[4] And my eyes won’t spare or show mercy! ‘Because they have been so disgusting, I’ll no longer forgive all the badness That’s being done in their midst… Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [7]:[5] ‘[Jehovah] said: '{Look!} Upon the evil, evil will come…
[Ezekiel] [7]:[6] For their end has reached its fulfillment, And their punishment has been awakened.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[7] '{Look!} The circle of the wreath has fallen on them (All those who live in the land), And the time has finally arrived… The day of tumult and distress.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[8] ‘For now, I’ll pour out My rage And finish My anger against them. They’ll be judged for the bad things they’ve done, And I’ll hold them to blame for their evil.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[9] ‘My eyes won’t spare or show mercy, For I’ll make them pay for their ways And the disgusting things that they’ve done. Then, they will know that it’s Me… I’m the One who is knocking them down!
[Ezekiel] [7]:[10] ‘Look! The day of the Lord has arrived, And his rod has [finally] blossomed.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[11] The time to injure has come, Which will break the resolve of the lawless. Then, nothing at all will remain… No wealth and nothing of value.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[12] ‘Look! The time has arrived… Today is truly the day! So, those who buy shouldn’t rejoice, And those who sell shouldn’t wail; For [God’s] wrath will cover such things.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[13] ‘Now the one who buys will not return What he bought to the person who sold it, Because neither one will survive. ‘This vision is for all of you (As many as live in this place), And it will not be turned back. ‘Yet, the eyes of these people won’t see [The things that are coming into] their lives.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[14] So, although they should be [preparing themselves] And knowing what is coming upon them, No one’s getting ready for war As My wrath is approaching her crowds!
[Ezekiel] [7]:[15] ‘For when the sword arrives on the outside, There’ll be famine and plagues on the inside. And those who carry their swords to the fields Will thereafter die [in those fields], While there’s famine and plague in their cities.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[16] ‘Then, those who try to escape Will sit on the mountains like pigeons and know That destruction has come because they’re so bad.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[17] ‘So, all their hands will be weak And all their loins will be wet,
[Ezekiel] [7]:[18] As around themselves, they’ll wrap sack cloth. For, they’ll be covered by shock; Upon every face will be shame; And every head will be bald.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[19] ‘Then they’ll toss their silver into the squares, And their gold won’t have any value; For their silver and gold will not save them In the day of the wrath of the Lord. ‘Then their lives will not find satisfaction, Nor will their bellies be filled, Since the torment for their sins will then have arrived.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[20] ‘Of their [silver and gold], they are now so proud, So they used it to create their foul idols… And for this, I’ve handed them over to filth.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[21] ‘Yes, I’ll hand them to strangers Who will then rip them to pieces. To the pests of the earth, I will give them, And as their spoils, they’ll profane them.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[22] ‘For from them, I’ve now turned My face; And to those over whom I kept watch, Sudden destruction will come. The attack will arrive when it isn’t expected… And then, they will all be profaned.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[23] ‘Yes, a great befouling will come To a land that is filled with judgments of blood. For with all of their lawless ways, This city is now filled to the brim! ‘So upon them, I will then bring The evil ways of the nations, And [the gentiles] will take all their homes.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[24] ‘So I’ll turn away all their neighing About how great they’ve become, And the things they hold holy will then be defiled.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[25] ‘Yes the time to repay has arrived, And those who seek peace will not find it.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[26] For there will come woe upon woe, As message after message arrives. ‘Then, from their prophets, they’ll search for a vision; But the law of their Priests will be gone, As will the counsel of the king’s elders.
[Ezekiel] [7]:[27] ‘Then, after their rulers are gone, The peoples’ hands will go limp, And I’ll do to them the same as they’ve done… I’ll punish them with their own judgments, So they’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [8]:[1] It was during the 6th year, in the 6th month, on the 5th day of the month, while I was sitting in my house and all the elders of Judah were sitting before me, that the hand of [Jehovah] came over me.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[2] For I looked and I saw what appeared to be a man… But from his loins down he looked like fire, and from his loins up he looked as bright as molten bronze...
[Ezekiel] [8]:[3] Then he stretched out what appeared to be a hand, and he lifted me by the decorative fringes on my clothes. With the wind, he lifted me up between the ground and the sky and he blew me back to JeruSalem! Then in this vision from God, I found myself looking north towards the [city] gate, and there [I saw] a monument to [the god], The Consumer.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[4] In this vision; {Look!} there in the plains, I saw the glory of [Jehovah] the God of IsraEl!
[Ezekiel] [8]:[5] And He said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Now raise your eyes and look towards the north!’ So I raised my eyes towards the north and I saw that just north of the gate (on the east side of the Altar) there was the idol of Jealousy that was standing at the entrance [to the city].
[Ezekiel] [8]:[6] And He said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Do you see these things that they’re doing… These lawless deeds of the house of IsraEl To push Me away from My Holy Place? Yet, you’ll see even greater and worse lawless deeds!’
[Ezekiel] [8]:[7] So then He carried me to the threshold of the Temple courtyard, and there {Look!} I saw an opening in the wall.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[8] Then He said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Dig [a hole] in this wall!’ So I dug [a hole] in the wall, and there {Look!} I found a door!
[Ezekiel] [8]:[9] And He said to me: ‘Now, enter and see all the evil… All the lawless things being done there!’
[Ezekiel] [8]:[10] So I went inside... And {Look!} I saw depictions of all sorts of crawling things, [unclean] animals, and all the idols of the house of IsraEl… Foolish and disgusting things that had been painted on the walls.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[11] Then I saw 70 men among the elders of the house of IsraEl, with JaAzaniAh (son of ShaPhan) standing in front of them, and each man was holding a smoking incense pan in his hands.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[12] And He said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘See what IsraEl’s elders are doing In the darkness of these hidden rooms… They’re saying that [Jehovah] is gone from the land!’
[Ezekiel] [8]:[13] And then He said: ‘But [I’ll show you] even greater lawless things.’
[Ezekiel] [8]:[14] So He carried me up to the threshold of the Gate of [Jehovah’s] Temple (the one that faces north), and there I saw women sitting and wailing for TamMuz.
[Ezekiel] [8]:[15] And He said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Now, after you’ve seen all of this, You’ll see even worse being done here.’
[Ezekiel] [8]:[16] So He carried me into the inner courtyard of [Jehovah’s] Temple, up to the threshold of the Temple of the Lord... And there between the columned porch and the Altar I saw about 25 men who were facing east with their backsides to [Jehovah’s] Temple… They were bowing to the sun in the east!
[Ezekiel] [8]:[17] Then He asked me: ‘Should I not be concerned About all of these lawless deeds That the house of Judah is doing? They’ve filled the land with their lawless ways… They’ve turned from Me and provoked Me to rage! ‘And look! They’re holding out branches of grapevines As though they are sneering at Me!
[Ezekiel] [8]:[18] ‘So I’ll deal with them in My rage, And My eyes will no longer spare them Nor will I show mercy upon them. So, no matter how loud they shout in My ears… I won’t listen to the things that they’re saying!’
[Ezekiel] [9]:[1] Then He shouted into my ears with a great voice and said: ‘The punishment on this city has arrived!’ [And at that, some men appeared], and each one was carrying implements of destruction in their hands...
[Ezekiel] [9]:[2] {Look!} There were 6 men coming along the road that leads to the upper gate (the one that faces north), and they were each carrying battle axes in their hands. There was also a man in their midst who was wrapped in a robe that reached to his feet and he had a belt [covered with] sapphires wrapped around his waist. Then they entered [the Temple area] and stood next to the brass Altar.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[3] And at that, the glory of the God of IsraEl ascended from between the cherubs and hung there between them in the open air of the Temple. Then He called out to the man who was dressed in the full-length robe and who wore the belt of sapphires,
[Ezekiel] [9]:[4] and said to him: ‘Now, go through the midst of the city – Through the midst of JeruSalem – And put a sign on the foreheads Of the men who are groaning and deeply upset For the lawless deeds being done here!’

[Ezekiel] [9]:[6] Kill and wipe out the old and the young, Including the women, children, and virgins… And start here at My Holy Place… But don’t approach those who are marked with the sign!’ So they started [by destroying] the elders who were there inside the Temple.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[7] For He said to [those who were carrying the axes]: ‘Now, go and start defiling My Temple… Fill its courtyards [with those whom you’ll slay], And strike down all that are [fleeing]!’
[Ezekiel] [9]:[8] Then as they started their destroying, I fell to my face and yelled out: ‘O Lord! ‘Are you going to wipe out all the remaining ones of IsraEl by pouring Your rage upon JeruSalem?’
[Ezekiel] [9]:[9] And He told me: ‘The sins of the houses of IsraEl and Judah Have now become just too great; For with [bloodshed], the land’s become filled, And the city is full of uncleanness and sin. ‘For they’re saying that [Jehovah’s] abandoned the land, And that He’s no longer paying attention.
[Ezekiel] [9]:[10] So My eyes won’t spare or show mercy, And I’ll hold them to blame for their evil.’

[Ezekiel] [10]:[1] Well at that, I looked up and I saw a sapphire stone shaped like a throne that was upon the dome over the heads of the cherubs.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[2] And [the One who was sitting on the throne] said to the man who was dressed in the robe: ‘Go between the wheels that are under the cherubs And fill your hands with the coals that you’ll find, Then scatter them over the city!’ So he went in [between the wheels] there in front of me
[Ezekiel] [10]:[3] (as the cherubs were standing to the right of the place where the man had entered), and a mist started to fill the inner courtyard...
[Ezekiel] [10]:[4] Then the glory of [Jehovah] (which had been hanging in the open air between the cherubs) entered the Temple, and the [inner] courtyard became filled with the cloud, as well as with the brightness of the glory of [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [10]:[5] Meanwhile, I could hear the sounds of the wings of the cherubs coming from the outer courtyard, which was like the voice of God when He speaks.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[6] And they said this to the man who was wrapped in the holy robe: ‘Go between the wheels that are under the cherubs And carry out some of the fire!’ So he entered and stood next to the wheels.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[7] Then a cherub stuck his hands into the midst of the fire that was under the cherubs and he grabbed some of the [fire] and placed it into the hands of the man who was wearing the holy robe… Who then took it and left.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[8] Well, as I was looking at the cherubs, I noticed that they had what appeared to be the hands of men between their wings.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[9] And {Look!} I noticed the four wheels that were standing beside each of the cherubs (there was one wheel for each cherub). These wheels looked like peridots,
[Ezekiel] [10]:[10] and there appeared to be wheels within each of the four wheels,
[Ezekiel] [10]:[11] but their four parts didn’t move as they traveled. Then, whichever way the [cherub’s] heads looked, the [wheels] would travel in that direction… But the [wheels] didn’t turn as they moved.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[12] I also noticed that there were eyes all over the flesh [of the cherub’s] hands and wings, as well as on the four wheels…
[Ezekiel] [10]:[13] And it was then that I heard that these wheels were called ‘The Chariots.’
[Ezekiel] [10]:[14] [I also noticed] that [each of the cherubs] had four faces: One face was that of a cherub, The 2nd was the face of a man, The 3rd was the face of a lion, and The 4th was the face of an eagle.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[15] Well thereafter, the cherubs started moving upward; and it was then that I started to realize that these were the [same] living creatures that I had seen [earlier] next to the Chobar River.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[16] Well, wherever the cherubs went, the wheels traveled alongside them. Yet when the cherubs flew high above the ground with their wings, the wheels next to them didn’t turn.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[17] And whenever they stood still, the wheels stood still; but when they flew upward, the wheels flew upward with them, because the breath of life was in [the wheels].
[Ezekiel] [10]:[18] Then the glory of [Jehovah] that was mounted on the cherubs left the open air inside the Temple.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[19] For the cherubs raised their wings and flew high above the ground in front of me (with their wheels alongside them), and [they settled] on top of the gate that’s in front of the [Jehovah]’ Temple, with the glory of the God of IsraEl above them.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[20] Well, it was after I had first seen these animals traveling beneath the God of IsraEl back at the Chobar River that I came to realize that they were in fact cherubs.
[Ezekiel] [10]:[21] Each one had four faces, four wings, and what looked like the hands of a man under each wing…
[Ezekiel] [10]:[22] And these [cherubs] had the same faces that I saw under the glory of the God of IsraEl in the vision by the Chobar River, and they also traveled in whichever direction that they faced.

[Ezekiel] [12]:[20] ‘Then the cities where you dwell will be [empty] As extinction comes to your land, And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’

[Ezekiel] [12]:[23] ‘Because of this, tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘I will turn their proverb around And the house of IsraEl will say this no more. Instead, they will say that the days have arrived, As have the words of the visions!’
[Ezekiel] [12]:[24] ‘And [you must also say this]: ‘False visions will come to an end, And there’ll be no more speaking of omens To curry the favor of IsraEl’s sons.
[Ezekiel] [12]:[25] For, after I tell them what I will do, I’ll act and not stretch out the time.’ ‘Yes, tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘In your days, O you house in rebellion, I’ll just say the words and then act!’
[Ezekiel] [12]:[26] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me again and said:
[Ezekiel] [12]:[27] ‘O son of man, ‘See how IsraEl is rebelling, For this is what they are saying: ‘The visions he sees are of some distant time, And he prophesies things [that won’t happen for years]!’
[Ezekiel] [12]:[28] ‘Because of this, tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘I’ll no longer stretch out the words that I speak; For now, I’ll speak and then do it!’
[Ezekiel] [13]:[1] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [13]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Against IsraEl’s prophets, you must now testify (Those who [say they can tell what will come])! You must speak to these prophets and tell them That their prophecies all come from their hearts. ‘So, you must prophesy and tell them To hear the Word of [Jehovah];
[Ezekiel] [13]:[3] For, these are the words that He spoke: ‘Woe to those who speak prophecies From ideas that come from their hearts While they have seen nothing at all… Those following the direction of their spirits!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[4] ‘O IsraEl, ‘Your prophets are like foxes that live in the fields,
[Ezekiel] [13]:[5] For they do not take firm positions. To the house of IsraEl, they don’t gather flocks, Nor are they getting them ready for war By warning them about the Day of the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[6] ‘The visions that they see are all false, And all of their omens are useless; For they say that [Jehovah] has spoken, And they make their words sound important; Yet, they were not sent by [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [13]:[7] ‘Haven’t your visions all proven false… Aren’t the words that you’ve spoken untrue? For you speak when I haven’t spoken,’ says [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[8] ‘Because of this, you must tell them,’ said [Jehovah], ‘That since their words are all false And they prophesy things that are foolish… Yes, because of this, I’m against them!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[9] ‘So, towards those prophets, I’ll stretch out My hand Towards those who are seeing false visions And those who declare foolish things When they give instructions to My people; Then, among [the faithful of] IsraEl, Their [names] will never be written, And they’ll know that I am [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[10] ‘For, they are misleading My people By saying there’s peace, when there’s really no peace… So the people are plastering walls that will fall.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[11] ‘Rather, they should say to those who are plastering walls: Your [walls] will soon fall and the rain will pour in. For I’m sending rocks to be hurled against them, And then your [walls] will just drop… [Yes, I’ll send] a mighty wind to destroy them!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[12] '{Look!} And after the walls have all fallen, They will then come here and ask: ‘What happened to all of the plaster That we used to make repairs on these [walls]?’
[Ezekiel] [13]:[13] ‘It’s because of this,’ says [Jehovah], ‘That I will send out a wind, Which will rip down [their walls] in My anger; And then, My rage will flood in. ‘In My rage, I’ll cause rocks to be thrown As I bring it all to an end!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[14] For I’ll raze the walls that they’ve plastered… I’ll lay them out on the ground, And then, I’ll expose their foundations. ‘And [you who have foretold better things] Will then be worn out by their shouting… And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [13]:[15] ‘Yes, against those walls I’ll wear out My rage, And on those who are plastering them; For, all their walls will soon fall. ‘Yet [the problem] is not with the walls Or with those applying the plaster;
[Ezekiel] [13]:[16] It’s with those who fortell a good future… Those who say there’ll be peace, When there really won’t be any peace,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [13]:[17] ‘And you, O son of man, must now fix your face Against the daughters of your people… Against those who now prophesy According to the things in their hearts. Against them, you must prophesy this…
[Ezekiel] [13]:[18] Tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘Woe to those who sew pillows That are made to be placed under elbows, And those who create all sizes of veils That they say will serve as protection… Those misleading the lives of My people!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[19] ‘You profane Me in front of My people For a handful of barley or a few scraps of bread. You’re ending lives that don’t have to die, And offer protection to souls that won’t live… You promise foolish things to My people!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[20] ‘And because of this, says [Jehovah], I am opposed to your pillows, Which you’re using to gather their souls. So from your arms, I’ll rip them away, And lead off those who you’ve misled… For soon, they all will be scattered.
[Ezekiel] [13]:[21] ‘I will also rip off your veils To save My people from your [wicked] hands. No, into your hands, they’ll not fall again… And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [13]:[22] ‘You’ve perverted the hearts of the righteous And strengthened the hands of the lawless… Yes you’ve failed to turn them from bad, so they’d live!
[Ezekiel] [13]:[23] ‘And because of this, You will not see false visions again, And you won’t see any more omens. For, from your hands, I’ll rescue My people… And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [14]:[1] Well after that, elders from among the people of IsraEl came to me and they all sat down in front of me.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[2] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [14]:[3] ‘Son of man, ‘The thoughts in the hearts of these people are set; So, lay out their badness before them, Since I will now give them an answer…
[Ezekiel] [14]:[4] Speak and tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘Any man from the house of IsraEl, Who may start to think in his heart That he’ll not be punished for his badness, Should arrange his face and then come to the Prophet, And I, [Jehovah], will tell him his thoughts
[Ezekiel] [14]:[5] So I can change the hearts of the house of IsraEl… Those whose hearts are so far from Me.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[6] ‘So, speak to the house of IsraEl And tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘Turn from the things that you’re doing… Turn your faces from your godless deeds!
[Ezekiel] [14]:[7] ‘For a man – any man – from the house of IsraEl Or from among foreign converts Who no longer chooses to [walk in My ways] And starts to think in his heart That he should never be punished For all the bad things that he’s doing, Must arrange his face and come to the Prophet, Then ask, and I will reply About the things over which he’s concerned.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[8] ‘For I’ll fix My face against such a man And assign him to a place in extinction… From the midst of My people, I’ll lift him away… And he’ll know that I am [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [14]:[9] ‘And if a prophet should say that he’s been misled, And he says I’m the One who misled him; Against him, I’ll stretch out My hand And remove him from IsraEl’s midst.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[10] ‘So each one who [comes before Me] and asks Must bear the punishment he’s due For all of his unrighteous acts… According to the things that he’s done. ‘Then the sins of the prophets will come upon them,
[Ezekiel] [14]:[11] So the house of IsraEl will not stay misled And remain defiled by its errors. Then they’ll be My people and I’ll be their God,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [14]:[12] Well after that, the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [14]:[13] [‘[Jehovah] says:] ‘O son of man, If a land sins against Me and falls into sin; Against [that land], I will stretch out My hand, And break its reliance on bread… Famine I’ll send [to that land] And remove men and beasts from upon it.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[14] ‘But, should such good men be found in that land As Noah, DaniEl, and Job; I will save such a man,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [14]:[15] ‘And if I must bring ferocious wild beasts As a punishment upon such a land; It will become an extinction… None will pass through it again Because of the faces of the wild beasts I’ll send.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[16] ‘But if three such good men can be found there; As I live,’ says [Jehovah], ‘Although its sons and daughters will not be saved… [Those three men] will be saved, And the land will thereafter be ruined.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[17] ‘Or if I should bring the sword to that land, If I say, ‘Let the broadsword pass through it,’ And I cause men and beasts to be lifted from there…
[Ezekiel] [14]:[18] If three such men can be found in its midst; As I live,’ says [Jehovah], ‘Although its sons and daughters will not be saved, Those [3 men] will be rescued.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[19] ‘Or, if I should send a plague to that land And pour My rage upon it in blood, Destroying both men and wild beasts…
[Ezekiel] [14]:[20] And among them, three such men can be found As Noah, DaniEl, and Job; As I live,’ says [Jehovah], ‘Its sons and daughters will not be saved… For the only thing that can save them Is becoming as righteous [as those three men]!
[Ezekiel] [14]:[21] ‘Then [Jehovah] said: ‘To JeruSalem, I’ll be sending 4 things: The sword, famine, and plague, As well as ferocious wild beasts… They’ll destroy all the men and their cattle.
[Ezekiel] [14]:[22] '{Look!} And any of those who remain Those who escape all these things, Will then be carried away, Along with their sons and their daughters. ‘Then {Look!} they will be brought here to you, And you’ll know of the things that they thought, As well as of the things they have done. ‘And although you’ll be saddened by the harm that I’ll bring – All that I’ll do to JeruSalem –
[Ezekiel] [14]:[23] [Your mind] will then be relieved, Because you will see their ways and their thoughts, And you’ll know all the things that I did Weren’t done without a good reason,’ says [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [15]:[1] And the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [15]:[2] ‘[Let Me ask] you this, O son of man: ‘What happens to the wood from all of the vines That live among trees in the forests?
[Ezekiel] [15]:[3] Do they find some use for this wood… Do they use their pieces as hangers?
[Ezekiel] [15]:[4] No! '{Look!} Each year, they’re thrown into the fire, As [people] are cleaning [their yards]. So, the wood disappears in the end, Since no use for it can be found!
[Ezekiel] [15]:[5] ‘And even whole pieces aren’t useful; For, after they’re burned in the flames, They no longer have any value.
[Ezekiel] [15]:[6] ‘So [Jehovah] said this: ‘As I’ve put the vines among trees To be burned in fires and consumed… That’s what I’ve done to those in JeruSalem.
[Ezekiel] [15]:[7] ‘For against them, I’ve now set My face, And fire, they’ll have to [endure]… For fire will [come and] consume them. And [when they see that] it’s My face against them, They’ll know that I am [Jehovah].

[Ezekiel] [16]:[5] ‘For their eyes didn’t feel enough pity for you To do such things on your behalf; They just threw you into the fields, Since your soul had been deformed since your birth.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[6] ‘Then I came and saw you defiled in your blood, And I said to you: ‘Come to life!’ Yes, I said this to you in your blood: ‘Come to life… Become many!’
[Ezekiel] [16]:[7] ‘I made you like crops that grow in the fields, Then you became many and great And you entered the city of cities. ‘Thereafter, your breasts and your hair both grew full… But you were still indecent and naked.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[8] ‘It was then that I came and beheld you, And I saw that it was your time… A time for you to find rest. ‘So I opened and spread out My wings over you And covered your indecent condition. Over you, I then swore an oath, And concluded a Sacred Agreement,’ says [Jehovah]. So, that’s when you became Mine.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[9] ‘I bathed you in water and washed off your blood, And then, I rubbed you with oil.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[10] I dressed you in [the best] colored clothes… In blue and linen, I wrapped you, And I placed a braided belt [on your hips].

[Ezekiel] [16]:[14] Among the nations, your name became known, And this was true of your beauty; For I’d made your beauty complete… I’m the One who ordered it for you,’ says [Jehovah].

[Ezekiel] [16]:[22] And this is much more disgusting Than the rest of the bad things you’ve done. ‘For, you forgot the days of your youth When you were indecent and naked, And lived befouled in your blood.

[Ezekiel] [16]:[29] So in CanaAn’s land, you also had sex, As well as with the Chaldeans… But you still couldn’t find satisfaction.

[Ezekiel] [16]:[32] An adulterous woman is all that you are… One whose husband acts as her pimp!
