[Ezekiel] [16]:[34] ‘Your perversions are worse than all others; For with other whores, you’ve even had sex… You paid them – they didn’t pay you; So, what you have done is perversion!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[35] ‘Because of this, O you whore, Hear the Word of [Jehovah]:
[Ezekiel] [16]:[36] ‘Because you paid others with your copper coins, Your shame will soon be uncovered… Your whoring with all of your lovers, As well as your evil thoughts… Your lawless deeds and the blood of your young, Which you have offered [to idols].
[Ezekiel] [16]:[37] ‘So, because of these things that you’ve done, I’ll gather your lovers against you And mix those you’ve hated among them. Together, I’ll bring them against you Until they have you surrounded. I’ll uncover your evils before them, And then, they’ll all see your shame.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[38] ‘I’ll punish you as an adulteress, And I will pour out your blood… In My zeal, I’ll appoint you for blood,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[39] And I’ll hand you over to them. ‘Then, they’ll cut down your whorehouses… They’ll demolish your base, and rip off your clothes, Then take all the things about which you boast… They’ll leave you indecent and naked again.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[40] ‘Against you, they will lead mobs Who’ll stone you with rocks and stab you with swords,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[41] Then burn your whorehouses with fire… They will wreak vengeance upon you, There before other women. ‘But I’ll turn you away from your whoring, And return the money that you’ve paid your lovers…
[Ezekiel] [16]:[42] Against you, I’ll slacken My rage And remove the jealous zeal I once had… So I can rest and be anxious no more.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[43] ‘Because you forgot the days of your youth And brought Me regret with your actions; {Look!} I’ll bring them down on your head,’ says [Jehovah], ‘And then, you’ll be godless no more!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[44] ‘For against you, they all have said this: ‘The daughter is just like the mother,’
[Ezekiel] [16]:[45] And truly, you are just like your mother… A woman released by her man, And one who abandoned her children, As well as her brothers and sisters… Yes, she also pushed them away, Along with her husband and children. ‘For an Amorite man was your father, And a Hittite woman, your mother.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[46] Samaria is your big sister, Whose daughters have lived to your left. ‘Your younger sister, who lives on your right, Along with her daughters, is Sodom.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[47] And in their ways, you have traveled – Their lawless deeds, you’ve done also – So their ways are now better than yours!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[48] ‘As I live,’ says [Jehovah], ‘Has your sister, Sodom, or her daughters Ever acted like you and those who are yours?
[Ezekiel] [16]:[49] ‘The sin of Sodom, your sister, was pride. For, although she had plenty of bread (She and her daughters had more than enough), This thing that was found among them was true: They offered no aid to the needy and poor…

[Ezekiel] [16]:[51] ‘Yet, Samaria didn’t sin with half of your sins, And you’re now more lawless than her. Yes, all the lawless things that you’ve done Prove your sisters more righteous.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[52] So now, you must carry your torment! ‘For by your sins, you’ve corrupted your sisters… And your lawless ways are much worse than theirs, So that they now look better than you! Yes, be ashamed and accept your dishonor, For it’s you who made them look better.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[53] ‘So from them, I’ll remove My rejection – The rejection of Sodom and her daughters – And I’ll remove Samaria’s rejection (As well as that of her daughters)… And then, I’ll wipe you out of their midst!
[Ezekiel] [16]:[54] ‘Therefore, you must now bear the torment and disgrace For all that you did to provoke Me.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[55] And your sister, Sodom, and her daughters Will be restored as they were at the first, Along with Samaria and her daughters, Who’ll become as they were [in their youth]. Yes, her daughters will all be restored As they had been [long ago].
[Ezekiel] [16]:[56] ‘Wasn’t Sodom, your sister, a reason to boast In the days of your pride,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[57] Before your evils were seen… Those evils for which you’re now being scorned By all of Syria’s daughters And by those who are living around you… Like the daughters of the Philistines… Those who live just next door?
[Ezekiel] [16]:[58] ‘So, because of your godless ways, And the lawless deeds that you’ve done,’ says [Jehovah],
[Ezekiel] [16]:[59] ‘I’ll do to you as you’ve done to Me… For you’ve disgraced the promise you made By breaking your Agreement with Me.
[Ezekiel] [16]:[60] ‘Yet, I will remember My oath… The one that I made with you in your youth, To establish My Agreement with you throughout the age…
[Ezekiel] [16]:[61] Then, perhaps you’ll remember the right ways to act. ‘But for following in the ways of your sisters – Both the younger and older – You will now be despised. ‘And thereafter, I’ll give them to you, Then you can start teaching them... But not of your Agreement with Me,
[Ezekiel] [16]:[62] For My Sacred Agreement will just be with you… And you’ll all know that I am [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [16]:[63] ‘So remember, and then be ashamed… Do not open your mouth, Since your face has been so dishonored. And I am the One who has born all the cost Of the sins that you have committed,’ says [Jehovah]!’
[Ezekiel] [17]:[1] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [17]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Tell this story and sing it as a song Before the house of IsraEl…
[Ezekiel] [17]:[3] Tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘There was a great eagle with very great wings Whose claws were long and outstretched. To Lebanon, He was then led, Where He perched on the choicest of cedars.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[4] ‘The most tender tips, He plucked off, And to the land of CanaAn, He took them; Then He placed them in a city with walls.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[5] ‘He also took a seed from that land And planted it in ground fit for sowing A place with plenty of water, And He arranged for it to be tended.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[6] ‘Thereafter, [the seed] grew into a vine, Which proved that it would be great. Above, it grew many branches of vines, As its roots [spread out] underneath it… It became a vine with layers of vines, And its tendrils kept spreading abroad.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[7] ‘There was also another great eagle That had large wings and [long] claws. So {Look!} the grapevine then twisted towards him, As did its roots and its branches. ‘[The vine] reached towards [the eagle] from her water, Which pulled her from her place in the sun…
[Ezekiel] [17]:[8] Even though the soil in which she was planted was good, And even though she had plenty of water. For, she was fat and putting out buds, And as a great vine, was bearing much fruit.’
[Ezekiel] [17]:[9] ‘Then [Jehovah] asked: ‘So, will she continue to prosper? Will she continue to have tender roots? Won’t all her fruits start to rot? ‘Yes, those early shoots will all dry, But not because of some great mighty arm Or because an army had pulled up her roots.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[10] '{Look!} This fat one will no longer prosper Because she’ll be touched by hot winds And she will be dried up by drought. Yes, when the east winds blow, she will shrivel!’
[Ezekiel] [17]:[11] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said: ‘Ask the rebellious house what all of this meant… Yes, [go ahead and just] ask them!
[Ezekiel] [17]:[12] '{Look!} Babylon’s king will come to JeruSalem And capture her king and her rulers; Then, they’ll be taken to Babylon.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[13] ‘Yes, he’ll take the offspring of the kingdom, Then force him to swear an oath of allegiance… As he carries the rulers away from their land.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[14] ‘So the kingdom will then be so weak That it won’t be able to lift itself up. And in order for them to survive, They’ll have to keep their treaty with him.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[15] ‘But [the king] will thereafter revolt And send his envoys to Egypt To beg them for horses and soldiers. ‘Will he succeed? Will the one who disobeyed be preserved? Will the one who broke his oath then be saved?
[Ezekiel] [17]:[16] ‘As I live,’ says [Jehovah], ‘Surely, here in the place of the king, He’ll disgrace the One who allowed him to rule And he’ll break the oath of his treaty. So to Babylon, he will be taken, And there is where he will die!
[Ezekiel] [17]:[17] ‘No, he won’t succeed despite his great power Or because of the [strength] of his [army]. For although PharaOh will join him in war And build many weapons and siege mounds, Which will bring many lives to an end;
[Ezekiel] [17]:[18] Because [the king] will have disgraced his oath – The one which he’ll swear before Me, When he breaks the agreement he made... {Look!} The one over which he held up his hand! For this, he will not escape.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[19] ‘So, tell him that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘As I live… You will be disgraced For breaking the agreement you made before Me. So upon your head, I’ll lay this:
[Ezekiel] [17]:[20] ‘Over you, I’ll spread out My net, And in it, you’ll be wrapped up and captured… Then off to Babylon, you will be led, Where I’ll judge you for your sins against Me.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[21] ‘Then your armies that are ready for battle Will all be cut down by swords, And the survivors will be scattered to the [four] winds… Then they’ll know that I, [Jehovah], have spoken.’
[Ezekiel] [17]:[22] ‘Thereafter, [Jehovah] said: But then, from the choicest of cedars, I will pluck off a top… Yes, out of its heart, I will pluck it, And on a high mountain, I’ll plant it.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[23] ‘On a Mountain in IsraEl, I’ll place it… I’ll plant it and then it will bud, And it will bear fruit once again. ‘Once more, it will be a great cedar, And a place of resting for birds… In the shadow of its branches, they’ll rest, For the branches of her vines will then be restored.
[Ezekiel] [17]:[24] ‘So then, all the trees in the plains Will know that I am [Jehovah]… I’m the One who humbles the trees in their heights And who raises those who have been laid low. ‘I’m the One who can dry up green trees Or make them flourish in dryness, Because, I am [Jehovah]… So I’ve spoken, and now I will act!’
[Ezekiel] [18]:[1] And the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [18]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘How does the proverb apply To the land of IsraEl, which goes: ‘When the fathers eat unripe grapes, The mouths of the children get toothaches?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[3] ‘[Jehovah] says: ‘As I live, Will this proverb prove true among IsraEl?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[4] ‘I’m the One who owns all their souls… Yes the lives of both the fathers and sons. And since they are all really Mine; The sinning soul among them will die!”
[Ezekiel] [18]:[5] ‘But the one who is fair, righteous, and just…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[6] Who doesn’t feast to idols on hills… Whose eyes are not [filled with pride]… Whose thoughts are of the House of IsraEl… Who doesn’t defile the wife of his neighbor Nor does he dirty his wife By approaching her in menstruation…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[7] Who does not tyrannize others… Who asks no collateral [for loans] – The things that he doesn’t return – Who takes nothing by force… Who gives bread to the hungry and clothes to the naked…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[8] Who doesn’t require interest on loans – Who asks no payment of interest – Who turns his hand from injustice… Who is fair when he serves as the judge Between a man and his neighbor…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[9] Who follows all of My orders… Who guards My Laws and obeys them… Such a man will be thought of as righteous, And he will then receive life,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [18]:[10] ‘But, if he should father a bad son… One who sins and sheds blood,
[Ezekiel] [18]:[11] And won’t follow his father’s righteous ways, But feasts before idols on mountains, And willingly defiles the wife of his neighbor…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[12] Who tyrannizes the needy and poor And seizes collateral by force, Then chooses not to return it… Who turns his eyes towards the idols, Then practices all that is lawless,
[Ezekiel] [18]:[13] And lends his things out for interest… He will not receive life. For his lawless deeds, he will die, And his blood will be upon his [own head].
[Ezekiel] [18]:[14] ‘Then, if he should father a son Who fears all the sins of his father, And refuses to act as he did…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[15] If he’s one who won’t feast to idols on hills, And remembers the house of IsraEl… If he doesn’t defile the wife of his neighbor…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[16] If he doesn’t act like a tyrant… If he doesn’t require collateral for loans… If he doesn’t take things by force… If he gives bread to the hungry and clothes to the naked…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[17] If he doesn’t turn his hand towards injustice Or charge interest for the loans that he makes… If he’s righteous and follows My orders… He’ll live and not die for his father’s sins!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[18] ‘But because his father was oppressive and bad… Because he took things by force And was contrary among his own people… For his unrighteous ways, he will die!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[19] ‘But then, you will ask: ‘Why won’t the son bear the sins of his father?’ ‘It’s because he is merciful, righteous, and fair… He’s kept My Laws and obeyed them, And as a result, he will live…
[Ezekiel] [18]:[20] Just the soul that is sinning will die! ‘So the son won’t be blamed for his father’s bad ways, And the father won’t be blamed for those of his son. Yes, the righteous ways of each person And lawless ways of each person Are what they will bring on themselves!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[21] But, if the lawless one turns from what’s bad And starts to keep My Commandments... If he becomes merciful, righteous, and just... He will be granted life, Yes, he will live and not die!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[22] I will forget all his sins, No matter how many there are… For his righteous ways, he will live!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[23] ‘Do I wish to bring death to the lawless,’ asks [Jehovah]? ‘No, I want them to turn from the bad, so they’ll live!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[24] But, if the righteous should turn from right ways And commit all the sins of the lawless… Yes, if they do such things, they will die… I’ll forget all the righteous things that they did And destroy them for their errors and sins.
[Ezekiel] [18]:[25] ‘But then, you will say: ‘The ways of [Jehovah] aren’t right!’ ‘Pay attention, O house of IsraEl! Haven’t My ways proven straight? Aren’t yours the ways that are crooked?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[26] ‘When a righteous man turns from right ways, Shouldn’t he die for his sins… Since he’s the one who is to blame, Isn’t he the one who should die?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[27] ‘And when the lawless turn from bad ways… When they start acting righteous and fair
[Ezekiel] [18]:[28] And recognize how godless they’ve been; All these people should live… No way should they have to die!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[29] ‘Yet, the house of IsraEl still claims That the ways of [Jehovah] aren’t straight. ‘O house of IsraEl, ‘Is it really My ways that aren’t straight? Aren’t yours the ways that are crooked?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[30] ‘Therefore, O house of IsraEl, ‘I’ll judge each man by the things that he does,’ says [Jehovah]. ‘So, if you will turn from your bad ways, You won’t be punished for the bad things you’ve done!
[Ezekiel] [18]:[31] ‘But, you must discard all your bad ways, As well as your irreverence towards Me… Create for yourselves new breaths and hearts! ‘O house of IsraEl, ‘Why should you die?
[Ezekiel] [18]:[32] I want no one to die,’ says [Jehovah]… ‘So return [to Me] and you’ll live!’
[Ezekiel] [19]:[1] ‘Now, against the rulers of IsraEl, I want you to sing this lament:
[Ezekiel] [19]:[2] ‘Your mother was a lion with cubs… For in the midst of lions, she had many cubs.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[3] Then, one of her cubs made the leap Into becoming a lion… He learned to attack and eat men.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[4] ‘But the nations soon heard about him, And in their corruption, they caught him, Then in a cage, they brought him to Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[5] ‘Well, when she saw that [her son] had been caught And that she had lost her support; She took another one of her cubs And made him grow into a lion.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[6] ‘So he started to walk among lions, And very soon, he became one… He captured prey and ate many men.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[7] ‘In their cities, he then boldly fed Until the whole land was destroyed And filled with the sounds of his roaring.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[8] ‘So the nations all came from their places… They surrounded and then they attacked him… In their corruption, they threw nets and caught him.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[9] ‘Into a cage, he was put, And to the king of Babylon, they took him. So, because he was kept in a cage, His roar was no longer heard In IsraEl’s mountains, thereafter.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[10] ‘Now, this mother was much like a grape vine Or a pomegranate planted near water. And because there was so much water, Soon she grew buds and fruit.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[11] ‘Among the head tribe, she became a strong rod, And she was esteemed for her greatness Amidst the rest of those great trunks [of trees]… And she saw that her branches were what made her great.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[12] ‘But in rage, she was thereafter broken… Yes, she was cut to the ground And by burning winds, she was dried. Then her choicest of branches – the rods of her strength – Were punished, dried out, and burned.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[13] ‘For, she’d moved herself into the desert… To a land that was thirsty and dry.
[Ezekiel] [19]:[14] So the flames on her choicest of branches Also reached down and consumed her, Which left her without the rod of her strength. So, to her tribe, she became a sad song About one who will surely be missed.’
[Ezekiel] [20]:[1] It was in the 7th year, in the 5th month, and on the 10th day of the month that men from among the elders of the house of IsraEl came before me to ask [things] from [Jehovah]. So after they all came and sat down in front of my face,
[Ezekiel] [20]:[2] the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [20]:[3] ‘O son of man, ‘Speak to IsraEl’s elders And tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘Have you come to ask something of Me? As I live, I will not reply,’ says [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [20]:[4] ‘But I’ll punish you, O sons of men, For the lawless deeds of your fathers… ‘Yes, this is what you must tell them!
[Ezekiel] [20]:[5] ‘And tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘From the day that I took the house of IsraEl And to Jacob’s offspring, became known, When I let them know Me in Egypt… Yes, when I took hold of their hands, And told them that I am [Jehovah] their God...
[Ezekiel] [20]:[6] Since the day that I took them into My hands And led them from Egypt’s land Into the land that I had prepared... A land that flowed with honey and milk… Honeycombs that are far greater Than those in all other lands...
[Ezekiel] [20]:[7] And I told them that they must abandon The disgusting things in front of their eyes And the defilements of Egypt… Since then, I’ve been [Jehovah] their God!
[Ezekiel] [20]:[8] ‘But then, they revolted against Me And refused to hear what I said. Their disgusting things, they didn’t remove The things [they could see] with their eyes, Nor did they leave the bad ways of Egypt. ‘So I threatened to pour out My rage upon them, And finish My anger among them in Egypt.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[9] But I acted so My Name would not be profaned Before the nations among which they were living Those to whom I had made [Myself] known… And I led them from Egypt’s land.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[10] ‘Then I led them from Egypt into the desert,
[Ezekiel] [20]:[11] Where I gave them My orders and all of My Laws… Which, if a man does them, bring life.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[12] ‘And I gave them My Sabbaths to serve as a sign That they knew that I am [Jehovah]… The One who is making them holy.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[13] ‘But, in the desert, they made Me feel bitter; For they didn’t follow My orders, And My Laws, they then pushed away... Which, if a man does them, bring life, And they profaned all My Sabbaths. ‘So, it was there in the desert That I threatened to pour out My rage And to completely wipe them away.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[14] Yet I didn’t, so My Name would not be profaned Among the gentiles who saw that I led them.

[Ezekiel] [20]:[16] For they’d pushed away all My Laws, And they chose not to follow My orders… They also profaned all My Sabbaths, And they followed the desires of their hearts.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[17] ‘Yet, My eyes continued to spare them… I did not wipe them away Or destroy them there in the desert.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[18] ‘In the desert, I then warned their children Not to follow the laws of their fathers, Nor to obey their [bad] rules… Not defile themselves with their fathers’ ways,
[Ezekiel] [20]:[19] For I am [Jehovah] their God. ‘[I told them that they must] follow My orders… They must keep My Laws and obey them,
[Ezekiel] [20]:[20] And keep My Sabbath days holy. For, this is the sign between Me and them That I am [Jehovah] their God.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[21] ‘But against Me, they also rebelled, And their children wouldn’t follow My orders… They didn’t guard My Laws or obey them – The Laws that bring life to all who’ll obey – And they profaned all My Sabbaths. ‘So I spoke to them in My anger… I threatened to pour My rage upon them And finish My wrath in the desert.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[22] ‘So against them, I then turned My hand And I acted because of Myself… That My Name would not be profaned Before the nations, from which they’d been led.
[Ezekiel] [20]:[23] ‘But in the desert, I lifted My hand To scatter them among all the nations,

[Ezekiel] [22]:[17] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [22]:[18] ‘O son of man, '{Look!} Before me, the house of IsraEl’s become Like brass that’s mixed in with iron, Or like tin and lead mixed with silver.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[19] ‘So because of their [wicked condition], You must tell them that thus says [[Jehovah]]: ‘Since you are all mixed together; I’ll bring you into JeruSalem’s midst
[Ezekiel] [22]:[20] As though you’re inside of a furnace. ‘Then, just as silver that’s become mixed With brass, tin, iron, and lead, And air is blown in to refine it… That’s what I’ll do to you in My rage. ‘In My anger, I’ll gather you all And throw you into a furnace.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[21] Then I’ll blow on you with the fire of My rage, And you’ll be refined in its midst.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[22] ‘Yes, as silver is refined in a furnace; I’ll throw you into an oven. Then you’ll know that I am [Jehovah] When I pour My rage out upon you.’
[Ezekiel] [22]:[23] Well after that, the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [22]:[24] ‘O son of man, ‘You must tell them [that [Jehovah] said] this: At that time, they’ll call yours the land… The land without any rain… For there’ll be no rain in the day of [My] rage.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[25] ‘Since the leaders in your midst are like lions Who roar and seize prey by force… Since they dominate, destroy, and consume, And take whatever has value… The numbers of widows will grow in your midst.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[26] ‘For your priests have annulled all My Laws, And My holy things, they’ve profaned… They can’t tell the holy from the profane Or what’s clean from the unclean.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[27] From My Sabbaths, they’ve hidden their eyes, And I’ve been profaned in their midst.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[28] ‘So her prophets that do the anointing Will soon all be cut down… Yes, those who can see only vain things And omens that really aren’t true, But who say that [Jehovah] has spoken to them When He hasn’t spoken at all.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[29] ‘And even the land’s [common] people Call for what is unrighteous And [ask for their share] of the loot. They are tyrants to the needy and poor, And they treat foreign peoples unfairly!
[Ezekiel] [22]:[30] ‘Then I searched among them for one righteous man… One who’ll stand firm in the day of My rage, So I wouldn’t have to bring her conclusion And totally wipe her away… But, no such man could I find.
[Ezekiel] [22]:[31] So, I will pour out My anger And send the fire of My rage In order to finish them off… I’m bringing their blame upon their own heads,’ said [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [23]:[1] And the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [23]:[2] ‘O son of man, [‘[Jehovah] says:] ‘Two women were the daughters of one mother,
[Ezekiel] [23]:[3] And they were immoral during their youth. For, they [had sex] down in Egypt… Yes, there is where their breasts fell [to others], And it’s where they lost their virgin condition.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[4] ‘The eldest one’s name was ‘Her Tent’, And her sister was named ‘Her Tent is Within Her’. To Me, they both had been given To bear My sons and My daughters. ‘Are these really their names? No! I’m calling Samaria, ‘Her Tent’, And ‘Her Tent is Within Her’ is JeruSalem.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[5] ‘‘Her Tent’ [that is, Samaria] had been unfaithful to Me, And she doted upon all her lovers… The Assyrians, with whom she had [slept]…
[Ezekiel] [23]:[6] Their blue-clad commanders and leaders, And the choicest of all their young men, As well as those who ride horses.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[7] ‘To them, she offered herself… To the choicest of Assyria’s sons. She gave herself to those she desired, And wholeheartedly made herself dirty.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[8] ‘But her affair with Egypt hadn’t ended... Those with whom she had [slept] in her youth... She gave her virginity to them, And they poured [their semen] upon her.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[9] ‘So I handed her to all her lovers, To the sons of the Assyrians, whom she desired...
[Ezekiel] [23]:[10] And they uncovered her shame. Then they took her sons and her daughters And slaughtered them all with their swords. The women also gossiped about her, When [the Assyrians] brought vengeance upon her.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[11] ‘But when ‘Her Tent is Within Her’ [that is, JeruSalem] saw what had happened, She became more corrupt [than her sister]… Yes, even more immoral than her.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[12] ‘For she loved the sons of Assyria… Those nearby commanders and leaders Who wore such elegant clothes, And the men who rode on their horses… Yes, all of their choicest young men.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[13] ‘So I saw that they’d both been defiled, And that both were the same [kind of ‘women’].
[Ezekiel] [23]:[14] ‘Then, to her bad ways, she added, As she looked upon men who were painted on walls… Images of the Chaldeans, Depicted with brush strokes on [stone],
[Ezekiel] [23]:[15] Wearing colored belts on their hips, As well as deeply-dyed turbans, All giving the appearance of officials Among the sons of Babylon… Of her fatherland, the Chaldeans.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[16] ‘She doted on them with her eyes, And she sent her messengers to them There in the land of Chaldea.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[17] ‘So those sons of Babylon arrived, And on her marriage-bed they then rested… In their immoral ways, they defiled her. ‘And as she was being defiled, She put her life in their hands…
[Ezekiel] [23]:[18] Her immoral shame, she uncovered… She removed My soul from her life As her sister had already done.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[19] Then, she became even worse, As she forgot the days of her youth When she [had sex] down in Egypt
[Ezekiel] [23]:[20] And started thinking about the Chaldeans. For, they had flesh just like burros, And genitals like those of horses.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[21] ‘She turned from the lawless ways of her youth And from the things that she did down in Egypt... That place in which she’d once lodged And where the breasts of her youth had first fallen [to others].
[Ezekiel] [23]:[22] ‘So, because of this, O ‘Her Tent is Within Her’ [that is, JeruSalem]; {Look!} I’ve awakened your ‘lovers’ against you… Yes, those to whom you once gave your soul. And now, I will bring them against you, Then they will come and surround you…
[Ezekiel] [23]:[23] The sons of Chaldea and Babylon – Pekod, Shoa, and Koa – Along with Assyria’s sons And all of their choicest young men… Their governors, commanders, and tribunes, And the famous ones riding on horses.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[24] ‘From the north, they’ll all come against you With weapons and chariot wheels… Many nations with chest plates, helmets, and shields. They’ll surround you and throw up a siege mound; Then judgment, I’ll put on their faces, So you’ll be punished by their form of justice.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[25] ‘Against you, I will then show My zeal, And I’ll deal with you in My rage. They’ll cut off your nose and your ears, And they’ll cut up what’s left with the sword. ‘Then they’ll take your sons and your daughters; And all that remains will be burned.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[26] They’ll strip off all of your clothes, And remove all the things of which you’re so proud.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[27] ‘Your impious deeds, I’ll remove, Along with the bad things you practiced in Egypt. To them, you won’t raise your eyes anymore, And you’ll not think of Egypt again.’
[Ezekiel] [23]:[28] ‘[Jehovah] says: '{Look!} I’ll hand you to those who detest you... Those to whom you’ve given your soul.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[29] Then they’ll deal with you in their hatred And take all the things for which you’ve worked hard, Leaving you naked and disgraced. Your immoral shame, they’ll uncover, Including your irreverence and whoring.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[30] ‘They’ll do all these things, because you’re a whore Who defiled herself by thinking of them.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[31] So, since you’ve followed in your sister’s ways, I’ll now put her cup in your hands.’
[Ezekiel] [23]:[32] ‘And [Jehovah] said: You’ll drink deeply from the cup of your sister… You’ll drink so much that you’ll laugh, And in your drunken condition, you’ll sneer.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[33] ‘For from the cup of extinction, you will be filled, And it will make you feel weak… The same cup of Samaria, your sister.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[34] ‘You will drink and then you will vomit… Shards of broken pots, you will eat, And you will start pulling your breasts. ‘Then, I will pervert your holiday feasts, As well as all your New Moons… Yes I’ve said that I will pervert them,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [23]:[35] ‘Then [Jehovah] said: ‘Because you forgot Me and pushed Me aside, You’ll get what you’re due for your whoring!’
[Ezekiel] [23]:[36] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘O son of man, ‘Now, judge between ‘Her Tent’ [Samaria] And ‘Her Tent is Within Her’ [JeruSalem]. Yes, speak to them of their lawless ways…
[Ezekiel] [23]:[37] Of their adultery and the blood on their hands. For, even their thoughts are adulterous, And they’ve led the children they bore Me through fire!
[Ezekiel] [23]:[38] ‘Then, as they did this against Me; They defiled My holy things in that day, And they have profaned all My Sabbaths.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[39] ‘They [offered] their children to idols, And entered My Holy Place to profane it… See what they’ve done in My Temple!
[Ezekiel] [23]:[40] ‘Then, to those in far-away lands, They sent messengers and begged them to come. And as they were coming, they bathed… They decked themselves out and [painted] their eyes.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[41] ‘Before a spread table, they sat on a bed And set before them My incense and oil... Which these men found very delightful.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[42] ‘Then the sounds of harmony and music Was played before men who were drunk… Men who’d just come from the desert. Then upon their arms, they put bracelets, And garlands of boasting, they put on their heads.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[43] ‘Although I told them that they must be [faithful]; In the ways of a whore, they [had sex].
[Ezekiel] [23]:[44] So, they entered within them As a man would enter a whore… They entered ‘Her Tent’ [Samaria] and ‘Her Tent is Within Her’ [JeruSalem]… Two lawless ‘women’ with lawless ways.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[45] ‘But because [their lovers] are also just men, They will punish them both With the punishment that’s due an adulteress. In justice, they’ll pour out their blood For the adultery and blood on their hands.’
[Ezekiel] [23]:[46] ‘Then [Jehovah] said: ‘Now, bring the armies against them… Bring disturbance and ravaging to them.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[47] ‘May those armies then stone them with rocks And run them through with their swords! Kill their sons and their daughters, And burn down all of their homes!
[Ezekiel] [23]:[48] ‘Yes, their godless [lovers], I’ll bring to this land In order to correct these two ‘women,’ So they’ll not be godless again.
[Ezekiel] [23]:[49] ‘I’ll bring their irreverence down on their heads, And they’ll bear their own sins and ideas… Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah]!’
[Ezekiel] [24]:[1] It was in the 9th year, in the 10th month, and on the 10th day of the month that the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [24]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Write the name of this day for yourself, Because this is the day that Babylon’s king Will conquer JeruSalem… Yes, that day has arrived!
[Ezekiel] [24]:[3] ‘And say these words to that house in rebellion… Tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘Prepare the pot… Ready the pot and fill it with water,
[Ezekiel] [24]:[4] Then, you must put in the pieces… All the best pieces… The shoulders and legs, Then, rip the flesh from the bones!
[Ezekiel] [24]:[5] ‘I have gathered the choicest of cattle; So, start the fire to boil up the bones… Boil and cook the bones in its midst!’
[Ezekiel] [24]:[6] ‘For their Sovereign Lord [Jehovah] said this: O you city of blood, ‘There’s a pot that is filled with your venom. So, when they bring out your limbs, [None] will claim your parts as their own.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[7] ‘Upon a rock, they will pour out your blood… But it won’t be poured on the ground Or be covered by dirt.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[8] For I’ll punish you in My rage And I’ll have them pour your blood on a rock So that [no one] can cover it over.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[9] ‘Because of this,’ said [Jehovah]; ‘Woe to you, O city of blood For your funeral pyre will be great.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[10] ‘I’ll add much wood and kindle a fire To melt away all the meat. And then, to render a broth, The bones will have to be stewed.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[11] ‘You’ll stay on the coals until you’re burned through And all your brass ornaments melt… Until your uncleanness [is gone] And all of your venom has failed…
[Ezekiel] [24]:[12] Until little venom remains.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[13] ‘The venom of your filth, I’ll bring to disgrace Until it is all boiled away. Since you dirtied yourself and wouldn’t get clean, You’ll no longer be able to do that Until My rage on you is complete.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[14] ‘For, I [Jehovah], have spoken… I’ll do it and I’ll make it happen! I’ll not warn you or show any mercy, Nor will I offer you comfort. ‘I will judge you for the things that you’ve done, As well as for the things that you think,’ says [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [24]:[15] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [24]:[16] ‘O son of man, '{Look!} With just one blow, I will now take away [The woman] you’ve treasured most dearly. ‘Yet, you must not show any sorrow…
[Ezekiel] [24]:[17] Do all your groaning in silence… Over her, you must quietly groan, And you may not wail at her grave. ‘Don’t take off your sandals or braid your hair, Nor let them offer you comfort… And don’t eat the [food] that they bring.’
[Ezekiel] [24]:[18] Well, the next morning I told the people what he said to me; and then that evening, my wife died. So the [next] morning I did as I was instructed.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[19] And when the people asked me to explain why I was doing these things,
[Ezekiel] [24]:[20] I told them that the Word of [Jehovah] had come to me and said this:
[Ezekiel] [24]:[21] ‘You must speak to the house of IsraEl And tell them that thus says [Jehovah]: '{Look!} My Holy Place, I’ll profane… That wonderful place about which you neigh And the thing that your eyes have desired. ‘Now, in order to save your own lives, You’ll have to abandon your daughters and sons… For, they will all fall by the sword.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[22] ‘Then, after you’ve done this, You won’t take comfort from anyone’s mouth, Or share in the bread of mankind!
[Ezekiel] [24]:[23] ‘Your hair will remain on your head, And your feet will be wearing sandals. So you won’t lament or be crying… You’ll just melt away in your sins, And none will comfort their brothers!
[Ezekiel] [24]:[24] ‘Now, EzekiEl will serve as an omen and sign; For, all that he says, you will do. And after these things have all happened, You’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [24]:[25] ‘[Then He said]: ‘O son of man, ‘This is how it will be in the day That I take away all their strength And the things about which they boast… The desirable things of their eyes… All of their sons and daughters, Those in whom their souls take most pride.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[26] ‘Then, those who escape in that day Will come and tell you what happened.
[Ezekiel] [24]:[27] And in that day, you’ll open your mouth… Yes you’ll speak to those who have escaped… You’ll speak and be mute no longer… You’ll explain how you were a sign, And they’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’

[Ezekiel] [26]:[1] It was in the 11th year, on the 1st day of the month, that the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [26]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Tyre has said this of JeruSalem: ‘Well done, because she’s now broken! For, she had destroyed many nations, And then, she turned her attention towards me. But this one who once was so full Has now become desolation!’
[Ezekiel] [26]:[3] ‘Because of this,’ said [Jehovah], '{Look!} I am against you, O Rock, And I’ll bring so many nations against you That they’ll be like the waves of the sea.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[4] ‘The walls of Tyre, they will tear down, And then they will knock down your towers. I’ll scatter your dust to the [four] winds And leave you like a smooth rock…
[Ezekiel] [26]:[5] A place where they will dry fish nets. For, I have spoken against you,’ says [Jehovah]. ‘You will be a place that nations will loot,
[Ezekiel] [26]:[6] And your daughters in the plains will be cut down by swords… Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’

[Ezekiel] [26]:[9] Then they will demolish your towers and walls, And they will destroy [all your] weapons.

[Ezekiel] [26]:[14] He will make you like a smooth rock And a place for the drying of dragnets. Then, no way will you be rebuilt, For I, [Jehovah], have spoken,’ said the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[15] ‘Then [Jehovah] asked this of Tyre: ‘When their swords are unsheathed in your midst; Won’t the sound of your downfall As well as the groans of your wounded Rumble all the way to the islands?
[Ezekiel] [26]:[16] ‘The rulers of the seas will step from their thrones, Then remove their crowns and colorful robes, Because they’ll be startled by this change of state. And of their destruction, they’ll then sit in fear, As they are groaning for you.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[17] So, this is what they will sing: ‘O how great has been her destruction! For, she was removed from her place by the sea Along with all of [her people] By the one who brought terror upon them. ‘You’re a city which was once so blest; For you got your strength from the sea.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[18] But now, all the islands are living in fear; For, since the day of your downfall, They’ve had many reasons to worry.’
[Ezekiel] [26]:[19] ‘Then the Lord [Jehovah] said this: ‘I’ll bring desolation to your cities And leave them without any people… By the waters of the deep, they’ll be covered.
[Ezekiel] [26]:[20] ‘I will drag both you and your people Into the pit throughout the age. I’ll settle you in the depths of the earth As a desolate place throughout the ages, Along with the rest who have gone down to the pit. ‘In the land of the living, you’ll no longer be;
[Ezekiel] [26]:[21] For I’ve appointed you to be wiped away So you won’t exist anymore… They’ll look for you and not find you,’ says [Jehovah].’

[Ezekiel] [27]:[24] Who bring blue [cloth] and great treasures In [boxes of] cypress bound in rough cords.

[Ezekiel] [27]:[26] ‘Your oarsmen row it all into you From [the boats that are blown] by south winds As they sail through the heart of the sea.
[Ezekiel] [27]:[27] ‘But your armies, your wages, and stores… Your counselors, navigators, and oarsmen, As well as the goods that come from your stores And all the warriors among you, Those who have gathered within you, Will be thrown into the heart of the sea In the day of your downfall.

[Ezekiel] [27]:[34] ‘But, there in the sea, you’ll lie broken, As your stores are sunk in deep waters, And those gathered there [will be carried away] Along with all of your oarsmen.

[Ezekiel] [33]:[1] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [33]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Speak to the sons of your people And this is what you should tell them: ‘To whichever land that I bring the sword; The people of that country should then choose a man And assign him to act as their watchman.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[3] Then, when he sees the sword coming, He should blow his trumpet to warn them.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[4] ‘And after they hear the sound of the horn; If they should refuse to prepare And the broadsword then overtakes them, Their blood will be upon their own heads.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[5] ‘So when they hear the sound of the trumpet, They should [quickly] prepare, Or their blood will be upon their own heads, While the one who kept watch on their souls will be saved.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[6] ‘But, if the watchman should see the sword coming And fail to trumpet the signal So the people are caught unprepared; This watchman must then be taken away Because of the lawless [thing that he did]… And I’ll require his blood by their hands.’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[7] ‘And you, O son of man, ‘You’re the watchman whom I have appointed Over the house of IsraEl. So whenever you hear a word from my mouth, You must announce it on my behalf.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[8] ‘Then, should I say that a sinner will die, And you fail to speak out and warn him; For this lawless deed, you will die… I’ll require his blood from your hands.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[9] ‘But, if you should warn an irreverent man And tell him to turn from [his bad] ways… If he refuses to make any change; For the bad things he’s done, he will die… But, you will have saved your own life.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[10] ‘Now, O son of man, ‘Say this to the house of IsraEl… Tell them that they have been asking: ‘Since we are the ones who’re to blame For our delusions and our lawless ways; If we should turn from them now, Can our lives still be spared?’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[11] ‘You should speak to them and give this reply… Tell them that [Jehovah] said this: ‘As I live… I don’t want the death of the godless, [I just want them] to turn from their evil ways So that they can continue to live! But first, you must turn away From all the bad things that you’re doing… O house of IsraEl, why must you die?’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[12] ‘And you, O son of man, ‘Say this to the sons of your people: ‘The good things that the righteous have done Won’t save them in the day that they turn away. And the blame that the lawless are due Won’t come to them in the day That they turn from their godless ways. And no way will the righteous be saved In the day that they are found sinning.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[13] ‘So, when I say that the righteous will live, And they come to rely upon this… But thereafter, they [do what is] evil; Their righteous ways will be forgotten… For the sins they commit, they will die!
[Ezekiel] [33]:[14] ‘And when I say that the godless will die, And then they turn from their sins And start being righteous and fair…
[Ezekiel] [33]:[15] If they give back the collateral they’ve taken, And return all the things that they’ve seized… If they’ll travel an orderly life And no longer [follow] wrong [paths]; They will continue to live… ‘No way will they have to die…
[Ezekiel] [33]:[16] Their sins will all be forgotten… For making their ways righteous and fair, Their lives will thereafter be spared!
[Ezekiel] [33]:[17] ‘But if the sons of your people should say, ‘The ways of [Jehovah] aren’t right,’ When it’s really their ways that aren’t right; This is what you should tell them:
[Ezekiel] [33]:[18] ‘If the righteous should turn from right ways And start doing things that are lawless, They will die [for their sins].
[Ezekiel] [33]:[19] But, if you turn back a sinner, And he becomes fair and righteous, he’ll live!’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[20] ‘So, although the House of IsraEl is saying That the ways of [Jehovah] aren’t straight, I will judge each man by the things that he does!’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[21] It was in the 12th year (on the 5th day of the 10th month from our captivity) that someone who had escaped from JeruSalem came and told me that the city had been taken.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[22] Then the hand of [Jehovah] came over me that evening. However, before that [escapee came with the news], earlier in the morning, [the Word] came and opened my mouth so that my mouth couldn’t stay closed any longer.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[23] For the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said this:
[Ezekiel] [33]:[24] ‘O son of man, ‘Those who live in the places that are being destroyed In the land of IsraEl, are saying: ‘Back in AbraHam’s time, He was given this land; And now that we’ve become many, We’ve also been given this land as our own!’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[25] ‘Because of this, tell them that thus says [Jehovah], their Lord: ‘Since you eat blood in your food, And to disgusting things, lift your eyes, And you shed [innocent] blood; Why do you think you’ll inherit this land?
[Ezekiel] [33]:[26] ‘For, there you stand with your broadswords As you’re doing things that are loathsome! If you profane the souls of your neighbors’ wives… Do you think that you will inherit this land?
[Ezekiel] [33]:[27] ‘So, tell them that the Lord [Jehovah] says this: As I live; Those who live in the places that are being destroyed Will all be cut down by the broadsword. And those who run out to the plains Will be given as food to wild beasts. While those who hide behind walls and in caves Will thereafter die from a plague!
[Ezekiel] [33]:[28] ‘Then I’ll turn their land into a desert, And the strength of their insolence will perish. I’ll devastate IsraEl’s mountains So that none will pass through them again.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[29] ‘Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah] When I turn their land into a desert For the disgusting things that they’ve done.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[30] ‘O son of man, ‘The sons of your people are talking about you Along the walls and in the gatehouses, As well as inside of their homes. Each one is saying this to his brother: ‘We should all gather and listen To what [Jehovah] has planned!’
[Ezekiel] [33]:[31] ‘So, after they all come to see you And they sit down before you To hear the things that you’ll say; There’s no way that they’ll do [what you tell them]! For the lie is still in their mouths, And they follow the disgusting ways of their hearts.
[Ezekiel] [33]:[32] ‘So, if you should be the sound of a harp, A sound that is sweet and well-tuned, They’ll listen to your words, but not do them!
[Ezekiel] [33]:[33] But after it’s done, they’ll admit: ‘Look… It has all come to pass!’ ‘And they’ll know that there’s been a Prophet among them.’
[Ezekiel] [34]:[1] Then the Word of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Ezekiel] [34]:[2] ‘O son of man, ‘Against the ‘shepherds’ of IsraEl You must now prophesy! Tell them that thus says [Jehovah], the Lord: ‘O ‘shepherds’ of IsraEl! You have been feeding yourselves When you should have been feeding My ‘sheep!’
[Ezekiel] [34]:[3] '{Look!} You have drunk all their ‘milk,’ And you’ve wrapped yourselves in their ‘wool'… You have slaughtered the best of My ‘sheep’ And you’ve failed to ‘graze’ [all the rest].
[Ezekiel] [34]:[4] ‘You haven’t strengthened the weak, And those that are ill, you’ve not treated; Those with broken [bones], you’ve not wrapped, And the strayed, you have failed to return. No, you haven’t searched for the lost, And for the strong, all you do is make trouble.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[5] ‘So now, My ‘sheep’ have been scattered Because they don’t have any shepherds.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[6] They’re being consumed by wild beasts in the fields, Since they’re scattered upon every mountain and hill… They’re scattered across the face of the land, And no one has searched to make them turn back!
[Ezekiel] [34]:[7] ‘Because of this, O you ‘shepherds;’ Hear the Word of [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [34]:[8] ‘As I live,’ says [Jehovah], the Lord; Instead of My ‘sheep’ being plundered And being eaten by beasts in the plains… Yes, because there aren’t any shepherds, Shepherds who will search for My sheep... And because the shepherds have grazed on My sheep While they’ve failed to provide them with grass...
[Ezekiel] [34]:[9] ‘Because of this, O you ‘shepherds,’ Hear the Word of [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [34]:[10] For the Lord [Jehovah] says this: ‘Look, I’m against all the ‘shepherds!’ So I’ll take My ‘sheep’ out of their hands… Yes from tending My ‘sheep,’ they’ll be fired, And the shepherds won’t graze upon them again. I’ll rescue My ‘sheep’ from their mouths… They’ll no longer be something to eat!
[Ezekiel] [34]:[11] ‘The Lord [Jehovah] also said this: '{Look!} I will search for My ‘sheep,’ And I will come visit with them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[12] Like a shepherd that looks for his flocks On dark cloudy days when they’ve strayed… Yes, that’s how I’ll search for My ‘sheep.’ ‘I’ll drive them back from where they were [lost] On that dark, cloudy day.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[13] I’ll lead them out of the nations… From many regions, I’ll gather them back And return them to their own land, Where on IsraEl’s mountains, I’ll ‘graze’ them… In the valleys and homes of their country.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[14] ‘I’ll provide good pastures for them, And on IsraEl’s mountains, they’ll ‘graze.’ For there, they will find a safe haven… A place where they can sleep and find rest In good and plentiful pastures Upon the mountains of IsraEl.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[15] ‘Yes I’ll graze My ‘sheep’ and bring them some rest, Says [Jehovah], the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[16] ‘I’ll search for the lost and the strayed, And I’ll bring back the ones who are broken. I will bind and strengthen those who are weak, And I’ll also watch over the strong… I’ll allow each one to ‘graze’ his fair share.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[17] ‘Then, from among you, My ‘sheep,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord, '{Look!} I’ll separate the ‘sheep’ from the ‘sheep’ And the ‘rams’ from the ‘goats’.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[18] ‘Were the ‘pastures’ you fed from so poor That you trampled on them with your feet? And weren’t there enough places to drink That you stomped and muddied the waters?
[Ezekiel] [34]:[19] ‘Yes, My ‘sheep’ have trampled their food with their feet, And muddied the waters they drank from.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[20] So because of this,’ says [Jehovah], the Lord; '{Look!} I’ll separate the strong from the weak.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[21] ‘For you pushed them away with your shoulders and sides, And the weak, you have gored with your ‘horns'… You squeezed them out and pushed them aside!
[Ezekiel] [34]:[22] ‘So, I will rescue My ‘sheep,’ And no more will they serve as [your] plunder; For between ‘ram’ and ‘ram,’ I will judge.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[23] ‘I will raise a ‘shepherd’ for them, And My servant ‘David’ will tend them… He’ll be a ‘shepherd’ who cares about them.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[24] Then, I, [Jehovah], will be their God, And My servant ‘David’ will rule in their midst… Yes, I, [Jehovah], have spoken.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[25] ‘Among them, I’ll make an Agreement of peace, And I’ll wipe the fierce ‘beasts’ from their land. Then, they will dwell in the deserts, And in the forests, they’ll sleep.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[26] ‘Around My Mountain, they will be spread, And I’ll give them rain when it’s due… It will be a rain of great blessings.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[27] ‘The trees in the plains will then yield their fruit; The ground will yield all her strength; And in the hope of peace, they’ll dwell in their land. ‘Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah], When I break the chains of their yoke And save them from those who are making them slaves.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[28] ‘By the nations, they’ll not be plundered again, Nor will they be eaten by ‘beasts.’ They will then dwell in hope, And no one will make them afraid!
[Ezekiel] [34]:[29] ‘For them, I’ll raise plants of peace, And they won’t be hungry or starving again, Nor will they be scorned by the nations.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[30] Then they’ll know that I am [Jehovah] their God, And that I will always be with them. ‘For, you are My people, O house of IsraEl,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [34]:[31] ‘You are the sheep of My pasture And I am [Jehovah] your God,’ Says the [Jehovah], the Lord.’

[Ezekiel] [37]:[2] He led me around them in a circle, and look; there were huge numbers [of bones] lying there in the field.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[3] Then he said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Will these bones ever come back to life?’ And I replied: ‘O Lord; only you know the answer to such things!’
[Ezekiel] [37]:[4] Then He told me to prophesy over the bones and say this: ‘O dry bones! ‘Hear the Word of [Jehovah]!
[Ezekiel] [37]:[5] ‘For the Lord [Jehovah] says to these bones: '{Look!} The breath of life, I will [blow] into you,
[Ezekiel] [37]:[6] Then upon you, I will lay nerves, And over that, I’ll put flesh. Then I will stretch skin over you, And I’ll [breathe] my breath into you So that you will then come to life… And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah].’
[Ezekiel] [37]:[7] Therefore, I started prophesying just as he had instructed me... And at the sound of my prophesying, {Look!} a great shaking occurred that joined those bones, bone against joint!
[Ezekiel] [37]:[8] And as I was watching, I saw nerves and flesh [starting to grow]; and then [I saw] the skin growing over them. However, there still wasn’t any breath in the bodies.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[9] Then he said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Now prophesy over the wind… Tell the wind that thus says [Jehovah] the Lord: From the four winds, send them breath… Blow into these dead ones and make them alive!’
[Ezekiel] [37]:[10] So I prophesied to the extent that he allowed me to do, and the wind entered them and they came to life… They stood up on their feet [and formed] a great crowd!
[Ezekiel] [37]:[11] And the Lord spoke to me and said: ‘O son of man, ‘These bones are the house of IsraEl; For they say these dry bones are just like their bones, Since their hope was destroyed and they’ve perished.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[12] ‘So, you must now prophesy, And tell them that thus says [Jehovah] their Lord: '{Look!} I’ll open your tombs and then lead you out… To IsraEl’s land, I’ll return you.
[Ezekiel] [37]:[13] Then you’ll know that I am [Jehovah], When I lead you out of your graves. ‘And, O my people… When I bring you up from your graves,
[Ezekiel] [37]:[14] I’ll breathe upon you and bring you to life. Then I’ll lead you back to your land, And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah]… That I spoke and then I took action,’ says [Jehovah]!’
