[Ezekiel] [38]:[4] I’ll be putting a bridle into your jaws, And thereafter, I will lead you around. ‘I’ll gather you and your army, And all your horses and horsemen… Yes, all [your men] wearing chest plates, And bearing shields, helmets, and swords…
[Ezekiel] [38]:[5] Persians, Ethiopians, and Libyans, All those people with their helmets and shields…
[Ezekiel] [38]:[6] Gomer and all those around him… The house of TogarMah from the far north As well as those dwelling around him… Yes, all those nations that partner with you!
[Ezekiel] [38]:[7] ‘So [it’s time] for you to prepare… Yes, you should get yourselves ready, You and those who have gathered with you; For, you will serve as [their leader].
[Ezekiel] [38]:[8] ‘Then, after many days, you’ll be ready; And towards the end of the years, You will come to this land With the swords that you have collected From among all the nations. Then, to the land of IsraEl, you’ll come… To a land that once was demolished. ‘For by then, they’ll all have returned, And together, they’ll be living in peace.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[9] Then upon them, you’ll pour down like rain, And like clouds, you will cover their land. Yes, you’ll arrive with all those around you… The many nations that will join with you then.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[10] ‘Then the Lord [Jehovah] said: ‘In that day, [bad] things will enter your heart… You’ll make wicked plans and you’ll say:
[Ezekiel] [38]:[11] ‘Against this land, I’ll arise, The land that once was rejected, I’ll come upon those who are resting And who are living in peace… Those in a land without walls And with no locks on their doors,
[Ezekiel] [38]:[12] In order to plunder and loot… To despoil and to take many spoils, And to turn my hand towards this place... This place, which was once desolation, And is now resettled by a nation That returned from among many nations... For now they have many possessions, And they dwell within the earth’s navel.’
[Ezekiel] [38]:[13] ‘Then SheBa, DeDan, and the merchants of Carthage, And those in their towns will be shouting That they have come to plunder and loot, And to take all they own as their spoils. They’ll gather to take all the silver And to carry off all of the gold… To take it all as their loot.’
[Ezekiel] [38]:[14] ‘Therefore, O son of man, Now, you must prophesy this… Tell Gog that thus says [Jehovah]: ‘Against IsraEl, My people, you’ll come in that day… Against those who have settled in peace.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[15] You’ll come from your place in the north And bring along many nations… Horsemen all riding horses… A huge crowd and a great army.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[16] ‘Against IsraEl, My people, you’ll come Like a cloud that covers the land… In the last days, this is what you will do. ‘Against My land, I will lead you, And then, all the nations will know Me When before them, I am made holy through you.’
[Ezekiel] [38]:[17] ‘Then Lord [Jehovah] said: ‘You’re the Gog of whom I spoke long ago By the hands of My servants the Prophets Yes, the Prophets in past days and years, In order to lead you against them.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[18] ‘And it will be in that day,’ In whichever day that Gog will attack, Says [Jehovah], the Lord, ‘That I will arise in My anger
[Ezekiel] [38]:[19] And I’ll speak in the fiery zeal of My rage. ‘Surely, it’ll be in that day, From IsraEl, a shaking will come,
[Ezekiel] [38]:[20] And before My face, all will tremble… The fish of the seas, the birds in the skies, All the wild beasts in the fields, As well as the things that crawl on the ground, And all men on the face of the earth; For, mountains will rip into valleys, And all walls on the earth will then fall.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[21] ‘All sorts of fear, I will send upon them, And against their own brothers, I’ll turn each man’s sword.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[22] Then I’ll bring My judgments against them With plague, blood, rain, and great hailstones. ‘Fire and sulfur, I’ll rain upon him, And upon all those who have come with him… Upon all the nations that joined him.
[Ezekiel] [38]:[23] ‘Then, I’ll be made holy and magnified… I’ll be known and glorified among all the nations, And they’ll know that I am [Jehovah]!’
[Ezekiel] [39]:[1] ‘O son of man, ‘Against Gog, you must prophesy this … Tell him that thus says [Jehovah] the Lord: '{Look!} I am against you, O Gog, Ruler of Mosoch, Tubal, and Ros!
[Ezekiel] [39]:[2] I’ll collect you and then lead you down… I’ll haul you down from the far north, And to the mountains of IsraEl, I’ll lead you.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[3] ‘Then I’ll break the bow in your left hand, And the arrows that you hold in your right.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[4] On IsraEl’s hills, I’ll then throw you down… And you and those who come with you will fall. ‘Then, all the nations that joined you Will be given to flocks of winged creatures… To all the birds in the skies And to all the wild beasts in the plains… I’ll give you to them as their food.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[5] ‘On the face of the plains you will fall… Yes, this is what I’ve declared,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [39]:[6] ‘I’ll also throw fire down Magog, And the islands will then live in peace. For they’ll know that I am [Jehovah]…
[Ezekiel] [39]:[7] And My Holy Name will also be known Among those in IsraEl, My people. ‘No more will My Name be profaned. For the nations will know that I am [Jehovah]… I am IsraEl’s Most Holy One.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[8] ‘Look, it’s coming… It will surely take place, Says [Jehovah], the Lord! And this is the day that I said it!
[Ezekiel] [39]:[9] ‘Then those who live in IsraEl’s cities Will thereafter light fires with their weapons, Yes, all their small shields and spears; All their bows and their arrows; All the lances and sticks in their hands… For the next 7 years, They will be used to light fires.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[10] ‘No they won’t cut shrubs in the plains, Nor chop trees in the woods for their fires… They will just be using those weapons. For they’ll loot all those who once looted them And despoil all those who despoiled them,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [39]:[11] ‘And in that day; I will make Gog a place of renown… A remembrance in IsraEl’s graveyards For those who come here by sea. They’ll bury Gog and his hordes in a valley, And call it, ‘The Graveyard of Gog.’
[Ezekiel] [39]:[12] ‘By IsraEl’s house, they’ll be buried… For 7 months, they will clean up the land.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[13] They’ll be buried by the people who live in the land, And among them, that place will be famous, As will be the day when I’m glorified,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[14] ‘Then they will give orders to the people To bury [all of the bodies] That are lying upon the face of the ground. ‘For 7 months, they will search,
[Ezekiel] [39]:[15] And when those going there find a man’s bones; Next to them, they’ll put up a sign For those in charge of digging the graves Within the Graveyard of Gog.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[16] For, Graveyard will be the name of that town, And it will be cleansed from the land.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[17] ‘And you, O son of man,’ Said [Jehovah], the Lord, ‘Must speak to all the winged creatures, And to the wild beasts of the plains. You must tell them to gather and come… They must gather there from all places [To consume] this great sacrifice That I will offer to them… A great sacrifice on IsraEl’s hills. ‘Come eat all the meat and drink all the blood!
[Ezekiel] [39]:[18] For the meat of giants, you will consume, And you’ll drink the blood of earth’s kings. ‘Then all the rams, calves, and goats will grow fat,
[Ezekiel] [39]:[19] Since they will eat fat ‘til they’re full And they will drink blood ‘til they’re drunk From this sacrifice that I’m giving to them.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[20] ‘They will be filled from My table That is covered with horses and horsemen, As well as with warriors and giants,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[21] ‘Then I’ll put My glory among them, And the nations will see all My judgments… The things that I’ll do with My hand, And the things that I have brought upon them.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[22] ‘And then every day after that, The house of IsraEl will learn That I am [Jehovah] their God.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[23] Also, all the nations will know That I let them take their houses away Because of IsraEl’s sins… Because they’d annulled their Agreement with Me. ‘Yes, this is the reason why I turned My face And gave them into their enemies’ hands… To let them be cut down by swords.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[24] It’s because of all their uncleanness And because they had broken [My] Laws That I turned My face and did this to them.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[25] ‘Yet, after that,’ says [Jehovah] the Lord, ‘I’ll return all the captives of Jacob, And to the house of IsraEl, I’ll show My mercy… I’ll also show them My zeal for My Name!
[Ezekiel] [39]:[26] ‘In peace, I’ll bring them back to their land, And they will accept their dishonor For the unrighteous things that they’ve done. ‘Then, no one will make them afraid anymore
[Ezekiel] [39]:[27] When I bring them back from the nations. And then, before all those nations, I will be holy among them.
[Ezekiel] [39]:[28] ‘For then, all the nations will know That I am [Jehovah] their God… When they see that I am among them. ‘Yes, I’ll gather them back to their land And never leave them again…
[Ezekiel] [39]:[29] From them, I’ll not turn My face, For I will have [ended] My rage,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord.’
[Ezekiel] [40]:[1] It was in the 25th year of our captivity, in the 1st month and on the 10th [day] of the month (14 years after the city had been captured) that the hand of [Jehovah] came upon me
[Ezekiel] [40]:[2] and I was led back into the land of IsraEl in a vision from God. There he put me on a very high mountain, where there was a city that was being built right in front of me.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[3] So He took me [into the city], and I saw a man who looked like shining brass carrying a builder’s string in his hand and a measuring reed. Then he laid them down in front of the city gate,
[Ezekiel] [40]:[4] and the man said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Now, look with your eyes and behold… Listen with your ears and pay close attention, Then prepare your heart for the things that you’ll see, Since this is why you were brought here. ‘And all the things that you’ll see Have to do with the house of IsraEl.’
[Ezekiel] [40]:[5] Well, {Look!} there was this outer wall that went all the way around the city. And in the man’s hand was a reed that measured 6 cubits (the length of each was a forearm and a palm). Then he measured the area around the wall, and he found that its width was the same as its height [as measured] by the reed.
[Ezekiel] [40]:[6] Thereafter, he went to the gate that could be seen in the east and measured it’s [threshold]… Which was about the same depth as the length of the reed.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[13] And he said to me: ‘The inner chambers facing the north And the inner chambers facing the south, Those in front of the spaces... Are the Holy-Place rooms where the Priests will eat… And it’s where they will come to [Jehovah] With the holiest of all holy things. ‘There, they must carry the holiest things – Sin offerings and the holiest things – As well as their offerings for errors; For, this is a most holy place.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[14] ‘No one may enter [this place] but the Priests, And from the Holy Place, they can’t leave To go to the outer courtyard, So that those who are leading will always be clean. Nor may people touch the garments they wear, For they are also most holy. So when touching the people, they must wear other clothes.’
[Ezekiel] [42]:[15] Now, after he had finished measuring the inside of the Temple, he led me outside along the path to the gate that faces east, where he then measured the area that surrounded the Temple.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[16] He stood facing the east with his back to the gate, and he measured 500 cubits in reed lengths.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[17] Then he turned towards the north and measured northward 500 cubits in reed lengths.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[18] Then he turned towards the west and measured westward 500 cubits in reed lengths.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[19] And he turned towards the south and measured southward 500 cubits in reed lengths.
[Ezekiel] [42]:[20] So he established the [size of] the perimeter [around the Temple] as being 500 cubits towards the east and 500 cubits roundabout, which is to serve as the separation between the Holy Place and its outer walls.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[1] Then he took me to the east gate to lead me out.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[2] But then {Look!} the glory of the God of IsraEl appeared, coming along the road from the east, and around me there were many voices that were chanting, while the ground all around me was bright and glorious.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[3] And after that, I had a vision that was like the vision that I had when I first entered the city to anoint it… I saw a [celestial] chariot like the one that I saw at the Chobar river. So I fell with my face [to the] ground.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[4] Then the glory of [Jehovah] entered the Temple by way of the east gate,
[Ezekiel] [43]:[5] and [God’s] breath picked me up and carried me into the inner courtyard, as {Look!} the glory of [Jehovah] filled the Temple.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[6] Well, as I was standing there watching, a voice started speaking to me from the Temple… And then I saw a person standing next to me,
[Ezekiel] [43]:[7] who said: ‘O son of man, ‘Now you can see the place of His throne As well as the tracks of His feet. This is the place where His Name will encamp In the house of IsraEl throughout the ages. ‘But, IsraEl will no longer profane His Name As they did when they and their rulers went whoring And murdered the leaders among them.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[8] ‘They won’t build their thresholds next to His threshold Nor set their doors by His doors As they did when they claimed that His wall Was the thing that bound them to Him… Or when they profaned His Most Holy Name By the lawless things that they did. For, this is what brought His rage upon them When He wiped them away in great carnage.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[9] ‘Now, they must reject all their whoring And the murders of those who would lead them to Him! Then, throughout the ages, He’ll camp in their midst.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[10] ‘And you, O son of man, Must give this description to IsraEl’s house, So they’ll be able to see it And understand its [dimensions].
[Ezekiel] [43]:[11] For, they must turn from their sins And accept the punishment [they’re due] For all of the [bad] things that they’ve done. ‘You must draw out the plans for this Temple And show them how it must be built… Show them its entrances and exits, As well as how its foundations are set. ‘Then, speak of its orders and laws, And explain to them all its rules. You must draw out the plans there before them, Then they must keep [God’s] commandments And they must follow His laws!
[Ezekiel] [43]:[12] ‘Describe the Temple on top of the mount, And set limits for the Holy of Holies… For, these are the rules for His Temple.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[13] ‘And these are the measurements for the Altar: ‘Its width is 2 cubits and a palm… Its recess is to be 2 cubits deep, And the molding that goes ‘round its lip Must be 1 forearm wide. ‘The height of the Altar
[Ezekiel] [43]:[14] from the bottom of its hollow Up to the [top of its edge], Must stand 2 cubits high, And its width is to be just 1 forearm. From the small to the large, is 4 cubits, And it must be 1 forearm wide.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[15] ‘The hearth of the Altar is 4 cubits deep, And from the hearth to the horns, is just 1.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[16] The hearth is to measure 12 cubits [square], And it must [be built with] four corners.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[17] ‘Its ledge must be 14 by 14, And the molding around it, half a forearm. Its encircling base is a forearm across, And its steps must face towards the east.’
[Ezekiel] [43]:[18] Then he said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘[Jehovah] [your] God now says this: ‘These are My orders for the Altar In the day that it will be made To sacrifice whole burnt-offerings, And to pour the blood out upon it.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[19] ‘Appoint Levite Priests from the offspring of ZaDok, And only they may approach Me,’ Says [Jehovah], [your] God. ‘Then, before they can come before Me to serve, [They must sacrifice] a calf from the oxen As an offering [to cover] their sins.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[20] ‘They must then take some of its blood And place it on the Altar’s four horns, Upon the four corners of its ledge, And upon its base roundabout To cleanse it and [to make it holy].
[Ezekiel] [43]:[21] ‘They must choose a calf as an offering for sins And burn it in the place that is set apart… Somewhere outside of this [most holy place].
[Ezekiel] [43]:[22] ‘And then, on the very next day, They must choose a perfect kid from the goats To serve as an offering for sins, Then [use it to] cleanse the Altar once more, As they had done with the calf.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[23] ‘And after [this cleansing] is done, They must choose a perfect calf from the oxen And a perfect ram from the sheep;
[Ezekiel] [43]:[24] Then, offer them there to [Jehovah], And they must add salt when they’re sacrificed As [holy] burnt offerings to the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[25] ‘And for 7 days, they must offer a kid So as to pay for [their] sins, As well as a calf from the oxen each day, Plus a perfect ram from the sheep.
[Ezekiel] [43]:[26] ‘[They must offer them] all 7 days To atone for the Altar and cleanse it, And [to empower] the hands [of the Priests].
[Ezekiel] [43]:[27] ‘Then, after these days are completed; On the 8th day, the Priests must then place The whole-burnt-offerings on the Altar Along with the offerings for their salvation… And only then may they enter the Temple,’ Says [Jehovah], [your] God.’
[Ezekiel] [44]:[1] Then he took me back to the outer gate of the Holies (the one facing east). However, it was locked.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[2] So the Lord said to me: ‘After this gate has been locked It may not be opened and no one may enter… Only IsraEl’s God, [Jehovah], may enter, And until He does, it must remain locked.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[3] ‘And only those guiding may sit here To eat their bread before God. They must enter by way of the columned-porch gate, And that’s the way they must leave.’
[Ezekiel] [44]:[4] Then he took me in the direction of the north gate, over against the Temple, and I looked and saw that the Temple of [Jehovah] had become filled with His glory… So I fell to my face!
[Ezekiel] [44]:[5] And the Lord said to me: ‘O son of man, ‘Now, prepare your heart and your eyes, And ready your ears, so you’ll hear All the things that I will now say Concerning the instructions that I’ll give you For the Temple of [Jehovah] and all of its laws. ‘Arrange your heart [so you’ll understand] The ways they must enter and leave From this Most Holy Place!
[Ezekiel] [44]:[6] ‘Then, speak to those who have rebelled Yes, to those of the house of IsraEl, And say that the Lord [Jehovah] said this: ‘O house of IsraEl, ‘You must bring an end to your lawless ways!
[Ezekiel] [44]:[7] For, into My Most Holy Place You have brought foreigner’s sons… Those with uncircumcised hearts And flesh that is uncircumcised. ‘And you have even profaned Your offerings of bread, fat, and blood. Yes, you’ve broken [your] Sacred Agreement with Me By all the lawless things that you’ve done.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[8] ‘You’ve not followed the rules of My Temple, And you’ve put other people in charge.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[9] So, no more may foreigner’s sons Whose hearts and flesh are uncircumcised Be allowed to enter My Most Holy Place. For, foreign peoples may never become Part of the house of IsraEl…
[Ezekiel] [44]:[10] And only My faithful Levites may enter! ‘Now, IsraEl has strayed far from Me And followed their own [thoughts and] ideas. So, they will now [pay for] their unrighteous ways.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[11] ‘But the Levites are [to be treated] as holy, For they serve as the keepers of My [Temple’s] gates, And that is the place where they’ll work. There the whole burnt-offerings will be slaughtered, And they’ll offer the things that the people will bring… For, before the people, they’ll stand.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[12] ‘But, because they have served before faces of idols [On behalf of] the house of IsraEl, They’ll be punished for their unrighteous ways… That’s why I’ve raised My hand against them,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[13] ‘Yes, they’ll bear the blame for their lawless ways, And they can no longer serve as My Priests, Or [touch] the holy things inside of the Holies. ‘Indeed, they must bear their dishonor For the delusions in which they have strayed.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[14] But I’ll order them to be watchmen, And to perform other tasks.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[15] ‘The Priests of the Levites, the sons of ZaDok, Were the only ones who truly kept watch As IsraEl was straying from Me. So, only they may approach Me, And only they can serve before Me… Before My face they will stand To offer the blood and the fat,’ Says [Jehovah], the Lord.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[16] ‘Only these may enter My Most Holy Place Or approach My table to serve Me, And stand guard in My Temple watches.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[17] ‘So, when entering the gates of the inner courtyard, They must wear their [official] linen clothes… They may not wear wool when they enter these gates.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[18] On their heads, they must wear linen turbans, And beltless linen pants on their loins.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[19] ‘And when they enter the people’s outer courtyard, They can’t wear the clothes in which they must serve… They must leave them inside the Holy’s inner chambers And wear other clothes when they go there. But no way can they make people holy When they are wearing such clothes.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[20] ‘They may not shave the hair from their heads, Nor may they leave their heads bare… All of their heads must be covered.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[21] And no way may the Priests drink any wine Before entering the [Temple’s] inner courtyard.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[22] ‘They may not marry a divorcee or a widow… Only a virgin from the house of IsraEl… However, they may wed the widow of a Priest.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[23] ‘Then they must teach all My people The difference between the holy and profane, And the difference between what’s clean and unclean.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[24] ‘They must handle the cases of judgments of blood, And attend to decide righteous matters. They must be fair when judging for Me According to My Laws and My orders. They must also observe My holiday feasts, And My Sabbaths, they must always keep holy.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[25] ‘They may not approach a dead person So that they will not be unclean. But they may approach their fathers, mothers, or sons, Or their daughters, brothers, sisters, or wives, Without becoming defiled.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[26] But even then, they must count 7 days Before they’ll be clean once again.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[27] ‘On the day that they enter the inner courtyard To serve in My Most Holy Place; They must bring an atonement [for sins],’ Says [Jehovah], [your] God.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[28] ‘And since I am what they’ll inherit; They will be given no land As their possession among IsraEl’s sons… For, I am to be their posession!
[Ezekiel] [44]:[29] ‘The sacrifices are what they’ll eat… The offerings for sins and for errors, And the separation offerings will also be theirs.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[30] All the first-fruits are theirs, As well as the first-born [of cattle]. ‘Then, for the Priests, they must set aside Some of the first-fruits [they’re given]. For, if they give part of the first-fruits Of all that is brought, to the Priests, This will bring [God’s] blessings upon all their homes.
[Ezekiel] [44]:[31] ‘And the Priests may not eat rotting flesh, Or cattle that are taken by wild beasts or birds.’
[Ezekiel] [45]:[1] ‘Then, as you’re measuring the inheritances of land; A place must be set aside As the first-fruits to [Jehovah]. 25,000 long, it must be, As well as 10,000 wide… And the area around it is holy.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[2] ‘There, the Holy Place’s four corners will be set; It will measure 500 by 500, Plus 50 cubits of space roundabout.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[3] ‘And from this place, you must also measure out 25,000, plus 10,000 wide Between it and the Holy of Holies.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[4] ‘And since all this land will be holy; A portion must be assigned to the Priests That will serve in My Most Holy Place. And then, for all that approach To serve in front of [Jehovah]; This will be the place where they’ll live, Since they must be separate and holy.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[5] ‘[Then a portion must be set aside] That’s 25,000 in length And 20,000 in width For the Levites who’ll serve at the Temple… To be theirs as the city in which they will dwell.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[6] ‘And for this city that they will own, You must set aside 25,000, Plus a width of 5,000, On behalf of the house of IsraEl; And this will serve in the same way As the Holy Place’s first-fruits.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[7] ‘Then a portion of this must be set aside As the place [where the Chief Priest will dwell], And as the Holy Place’s first-fruits. It will be his possession in the city Before the Holy Place of the first-fruits, And in front of the part of the city That runs from the east to the west. ‘It will be as long as the city, And will run from the east to the west in the land.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[8] In IsraEl, this will be his possession. For, I will no longer treat harshly Those who are leading My people. ‘And the rest of the land will then be What the house of IsraEl will inherit According to each of their tribes.’
[Ezekiel] [45]:[9] ‘Then [Jehovah] God said: ‘Let this be enough for IsraEl’s guides… Let their misery and unrighteous ways be removed… They must start being righteous and fair, And lift tyranny away from My people,’ Says [Jehovah], your God!
[Ezekiel] [45]:[10] ‘They must use proper scales and right measures… [Honesty] must be their guide!
[Ezekiel] [45]:[11] So if one should get a tenth measure, He must also receive a tenth measure. If someone should get a tenth weight, He should receive his tenth weight.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[12] And if he’s owed the weight of 25 coins, The full weight of the coins is what he should get! ‘Your bread must weigh 15 shekels.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[13] And the first-fruits that you set aside Should be a 1/6 of 10 bushels, Or 1/6 of 62 bushels for wheat, Or 40 quarts [38 litres], if it’s barley.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[14] ‘Olive oil is a cup from 10 cups… For 10 cups equals a homer.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[15] ‘And 1 sheep must be set aside Out of every 200 Among each of IsraEl’s families, As a whole burnt-offering sacrifice, And as an offering of salvation from sin,’ says [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [45]:[16] ‘Everyone must offer their first-fruits To the man who is IsraEl’s guide.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[17] And to this one who serves as your guide, Whole-burnt offerings must also be brought, As well as drink offerings and other sacrifices. ‘They must bring them on each holiday, As well as on New Moons and Sabbaths. And on each of IsraEl’s holidays, All must bring sacrifices to cover their sins, As well as one whole-burnt offering, And offerings for IsraEl’s salvation.’

[Ezekiel] [45]:[19] ‘Then the Priest must take some of its blood And put it on the Temple’s four corners, And upon each of its doorposts, As well as on the [horns of] the Altar, And on the posts of the gate to the inner courtyard.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[20] ‘And each 7th month, they must do the same thing… They must atone for the Temple On behalf of the senseless and simple On the 1st day of that month.

[Ezekiel] [45]:[22] And on that day, the one who is your guide Must offer a calf for himself, And one for the sins of the people.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[23] ‘And during that 7-day feast, They must bring as whole burnt-offerings to God 7 perfect calves, and 7 perfect rams on each day. Then for sins, he must also sacrifice A kid of the goats on each day.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[24] He must prepare a cake for each calf and each ram, And bring olive oil for each cake.
[Ezekiel] [45]:[25] ‘And from the 7th day to the 15th, He must offer the same things each day… Whole burnt-offerings and sin sacrifices, As well as gift offerings and oil.’
[Ezekiel] [46]:[1] ‘Then [Jehovah] the God said this: ‘The gate to the inner courtyard, The one that faces the east, Must stay locked for 6 days each [week]… It’s just to be opened on Sabbaths, As well as on every New Moon.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[2] ‘And the one who is guiding will enter Through the columned-porch gate. Then, he will stand at its threshold As whole burnt-offerings are made by the Priests, Along with an offering for him, And one for IsraEl’s salvation. Then he’ll bow as he leaves the gate’s threshold; And the gate won’t be locked until evening.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[3] ‘Then, on the Sabbaths and on the New Moons The people of the land must all come, And on that threshold, they’ll bow to [Jehovah].
[Ezekiel] [46]:[4] ‘Whole burnt-offerings must be brought on the Sabbaths By the one who is IsraEl’s guide, Of 6 perfect lambs and 1 perfect ram,
[Ezekiel] [46]:[5] As well as a gift of cakes for the ram And a hand-made gift sacrifice for each lamb, Plus a quart of olive oil for each offering of cakes.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[6] ‘And on the days of the New Moons, [He must offer] 1 perfect calf, Plus 6 lambs and a ram (All of which must be perfect),
[Ezekiel] [46]:[7] And an offering of cake for each ram, An offering of cake for each calf, A gift offering for each of the lambs (Whatever your hands might have made), And a quart of olive oil for each cake.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[8] ‘Then, whenever the one who is guiding comes in, He must do it through the columned-porch gate; And that’s also the way he must leave.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[9] ‘And when, on holidays, the people of the land Come [to bow] to [Jehovah]... They should enter through the north gate, Then bow and leave through the south gate. But, if they come through the south gate, They must then leave through the north gate… They may not return through the same gate, And they must leave straight away.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[10] ‘And the one who serves as the guide in their midst Must enter as they start to arrive, And leave after they are all gone.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[11] ‘And during the festivals and holidays, An offering of cake must be brought for each calf, As well as one for each ram, With whatever his hand should provide for the lambs, Plus a quart of olive oil with each cake.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[12] ‘And if the one who is guiding should offer A whole burnt-offering of salvation; The gate facing the east must be opened for him. So his whole burnt-offering must be given Along with his things for salvation In the same ways as he does on the Sabbaths. And after he leaves, they must lock all the gates.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[13] ‘He must offer a perfect 1-year-old lamb As a whole burnt-offering to [Jehovah], Which he must prepare every morning,
[Ezekiel] [46]:[14] Along with an offering as a gift Of 1/6 of a measure of olive oil, Mixed into 1/3 measure of finest flour As a continuous gift-offering to [God].
[Ezekiel] [46]:[15] ‘The lamb, the gift offering, and olive oil, Must be prepared and offered at dawn, As whole-burnt-offerings, each day.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[16] ‘Then [Jehovah] God said: ‘If the one who is guiding should choose to leave His inheritance as a gift to his sons, It will become the possession of his sons.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[17] But if he leaves a gift to his servant, It will only be his ‘til The Year of Release, And then it must be returned To the one who’ll be serving as [IsraEl’s] guide… But the inheritance of his sons, will be theirs.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[18] ‘There’s no way that the one who is guiding May leave them an inheritance that he took from the people, So as to tyrannize them. He may only leave the things that he owns As an inheritance to his own sons, So the possessions of My people won’t be scattered.’
[Ezekiel] [46]:[19] Then he took me out the back gate to the inner chamber of the Priests in the Holy Place (the one which faces north), and {Look!} within it I noticed a place that was off to the side,
[Ezekiel] [46]:[20] and he said to me: ‘This is where the Priests are to boil The offerings for all of their errors, As well as sacrifices for their sins. It’s where they’ll bake the gift offerings, So that nothing will be carried through the outer courtyard, And the people may always be holy.’
[Ezekiel] [46]:[21] Then he took me to the outer courtyard and led me around its four quarters. And {Look!} on each side of the courtyard was another courtyard…
[Ezekiel] [46]:[22] On each of the four sides of the courtyards were smaller courtyards that measured 40 cubits long and 30 cubits wide.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[23] And there were inner chambers around each of the four courtyards, and cooking pits were located beneath and around the chambers.
[Ezekiel] [46]:[24] And he said to me: ‘These are the homes of the cooks, And it’s where the sacrifices will be boiled That the people will bring as their offerings For those who serve at the Temple.’
[Ezekiel] [47]:[1] Then he brought me to the threshold of the Temple, and look… There was water pouring from an opening that was under its east side (because its front faced the east). And the water poured down to the right side of the Temple towards the south, and then on south past the Altar.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[2] So he led me through the north gate and took me around to the courtyard gate (the one which faces east), and {Look!} the water was flowing down along its right side.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[3] There I saw a man who came out from across that place that was carrying a ruler in his hand. He then went to the source of the water and measured out 1,000 [cubits]…
[Ezekiel] [47]:[4] He walked into the water and measured out 1,000, and it came up to his knees. Then he measured another 1,000, and the water came up to his hips.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[5] And after that, he measured out another 1,000, and he wasn’t able to walk through it anymore, because the water was flooding with such force that it became a [river] that couldn’t be crossed.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[6] Then he asked me: ‘O son of man, ‘What do you see?’
[Ezekiel] [47]:[7] So he led me over to the bank of the river; and when I turned around, I saw that all along the banks of the river there were huge numbers of trees growing on each side.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[8] And he said to me: ‘This water flows east towards Galilee, Then to Arabia and on to the sea. And where it exits, the waters bring healing.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[9] ‘To all the herds, it brings life, For all that come to this river will live! And huge numbers of fish will also be there, Because they’ll all come to this water That heals and gives life to all things… Yes, all that come to this river will live!
[Ezekiel] [47]:[10] ‘Then, fishermen from EnGedi to EnEglaim Will come here to dry out their nets; For there’ll be no other place like it, Because there’ll be so many fish… It’ll be like the fish in the Great Sea.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[11] ‘But, where it turns and then flows away, There’s no way that it can heal [anymore]; For [those places] have been given to the salt.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[12] ‘And on each side of the banks of that river Will grow fruit-bearing trees that will never grow old And will never fail to bear fruit. ‘From the beginning, they’ll start doing this; For these waters have flowed from the Most Holy. And as these waters flow past them, They’ll produce fruit [to be eaten], And their leaves will bring healing to all.

[Ezekiel] [47]:[18] ‘They’ll run east between Haran and Damascus, To GileAd, through IsraEl, and on to the Jordan, Where [the Jordan] flows from the east to the sea And through the palm groves in the east.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[19] ‘And these are the borders to the south and southwest: ‘They run from TeMan and the palm groves To the waters of MaribOth KaDesh; And from there, they flow to the Great Sea… These are the borders to the south and southwest.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[20] ‘The Great Sea is the border from the gates of HaMath, And it is the border to the west.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[21] ‘Among the tribes of IsraEl This land must be subdivided;
[Ezekiel] [47]:[22] You must throw lots for yourselves, And for the gentiles who will live in your midst… Those who will bear sons among you. For, they will be yours as native-born sons Among all the sons of IsraEl. Along with you, they will eat, And they’ll receive an inheritance among all your tribes.
[Ezekiel] [47]:[23] ‘Among the tribes that they came to, they’ll live, Along with others who have also been joined And will inherit [the land],’ Says [Jehovah], your God.’

[Daniel] [1]:[1] It was during the 3rd year of the reign of JehoiAkim (the king of Judah) that NebuChadnezzar (the king of Babylon) came to JeruSalem and attacked it.
[Daniel] [1]:[2] Then the Lord gave JehoiAkim into his hands, along with part of the things that were in the Temple of [Jehovah], which thereafter he carried back to the land of Shinar and put into the treasury of the temple of his god.
[Daniel] [1]:[3] Then after that, the king told his Chief Eunuch AshPenaz to go get some of the sons of IsraEl that were descended from royalty and nobility, and bring them to him as captives.
[Daniel] [1]:[4] They were to be young, perfectly formed, good looking, wise in all things, knowledgeable, intelligent, and bold enough to stand in the palace of the king. And [when they arrived], he told him to school the young men in the language and writing of the Chaldeans.
[Daniel] [1]:[5] The king also arranged for them to eat at his table each day, to share in his banquet wine, and to be given special care for three years, after which they were to be brought before the king.
[Daniel] [1]:[6] Among these sons of Judah were DaniEl, HananiAh, AzariAh, and MishaEl.
[Daniel] [1]:[7] However, the chief eunuch renamed DaniEl to BelTeShazzar, HananiAh to ShadRach, MishaEl to MeShach, and AzariAh to AbedNego.
[Daniel] [1]:[8] Now, DaniEl had decided in his heart that there was no way he’d pollute himself at the table of the king, nor would he drink any of his banquet wine. So, he petitioned the chief eunuch not to be forced to pollute himself,
[Daniel] [1]:[9] and God granted DaniEl the chief eunuch’s mercy and compassion.
[Daniel] [1]:[10] However, the chief eunuch said to DaniEl: ‘I’m afraid of my lord the king, and since he’s the one who is selecting your food and the things that you are to drink, I don’t want him to see your faces looking sadder than the faces of the other boys that are your peers. For if that happens, the king’ll have my head!’
[Daniel] [1]:[11] But DaniEl told MelZar (the man whom the chief eunuch had put in charge of DaniEl, HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh) this:
[Daniel] [1]:[12] ‘Then test your servants for ten days. Give us just the seeds of the fields to eat and just water to drink.
[Daniel] [1]:[13] Then compare us to the other boys that eat at the king’s table. Whichever looks better is what you should choose for your servants.’
[Daniel] [1]:[14] So he did what they asked and tested them for ten days.
[Daniel] [1]:[15] Then at the end of the ten days, he examined them and noticed how they looked… And he found that they were stronger and in better shape than the other boys that were eating at the king’s table!
[Daniel] [1]:[16] As a result, MelZar did away with their suppers and the wine that they were to drink, and gave them just seeds to eat.
[Daniel] [1]:[17] Then God gave them understanding and intelligence in all their studies, and He made them wiser. And it was then that DaniEl came to have an understanding of visions and dreams.
[Daniel] [1]:[18] Well, the time finally arrived when they were to be brought before the king, so the chief eunuch took them to NebuChadnezzar.
[Daniel] [1]:[19] Then, after the king questioned them, he found that there were no others like these four boys, DaniEl, HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh, and he allowed them to stand before him.
[Daniel] [1]:[20] In every matter of wisdom and knowledge (whatever the king asked them about), he found them ten-times greater than all the other dignitaries and sorcerers throughout his realm.
[Daniel] [1]:[21] Well after that, DaniEl went on to live all the way into the 1st year of the reign of King Cyrus.
[Daniel] [2]:[1] It was in the 2nd year of the reign of NebuChadnezzar that the king had a dream that so deeply disturbed his spirit that he couldn’t sleep.
[Daniel] [2]:[2] So he gave the order to call for [all his] officials, priests, sorcerers, and Chaldeans, to have them interpret the dream. Then when they came and stood before the king,
[Daniel] [2]:[3] he said to them: ‘I had a dream that bothered me so deeply that I must know what it means!’
[Daniel] [2]:[4] Well, the Chaldeans replied to the king in the Syrian language, saying: ‘O king, ‘May you live throughout the ages! Just tell your servants what you dreamed, and we’ll announce the interpretation to you!’
[Daniel] [2]:[5] But the king told the Chaldeans: ‘I’ve forgotten what it was about… And if you can’t tell me the dream and give me its interpretation, I’ll have you all destroyed and have your homes torn down!
[Daniel] [2]:[6] ‘However, if you can tell me the dream and give me its interpretation, I’ll give you many gifts, do many favors for you free of charge, and I’ll honor you greatly… But first you must tell me the dream, and then you must explain what it means to me!’
[Daniel] [2]:[7] Well, they answered him a second time, saying: ‘May the king tell the dream to his servants, and then we’ll announce its interpretation!’
[Daniel] [2]:[8] And at that, the king said to them: ‘I know for a fact that you’re just buying time for yourselves, because I told you how every word of the dream has left me. So now, if you can’t tell me the dream, I’ll know that you’re corrupt and lying, and that you’ve agreed to keep speaking before me just to [buy more] time.
[Daniel] [2]:[9] ‘First tell me my dream, and then I’ll know that I can believe the interpretation that you give to me!’
[Daniel] [2]:[10] But the Chaldeans then said the king: ‘There’s no man on dry land that can make known what the king is asking, for this is something that no great king or ruler has ever asked of an official, a priest, or a Chaldean.
[Daniel] [2]:[11] What the king is asking is so difficult that no one can tell him such a thing… Other than the gods who don’t live here in the flesh.’
[Daniel] [2]:[12] And at that, the king flew into a rage! He was so angry that he ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be destroyed,
[Daniel] [2]:[13] and he sent out a edict for them all to be put to death! Well, when they went looking for DaniEl and his friends to do away with them,
[Daniel] [2]:[14] DaniEl asked this of AriOch, the king’s head-of-the-guards (who had come to execute all the wise men of Babylon).
[Daniel] [2]:[15] He said to him: ‘O [servant] of the king! ‘Why was such a presumptuous decree put before him?’ Then AriOch told DaniEl about all the things that had been said.
[Daniel] [2]:[16] Well at that, DaniEl went before the king and petitioned him to give him enough time to find the interpretation so that he could announce it to the king.
[Daniel] [2]:[17] Then DaniEl returned to his house and there he [met with] his friends HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh, and he asked them to help him interpret [the dream].
[Daniel] [2]:[18] And they then trusted in the compassions of the God of heaven [to help them unlock] this mystery, and to keep DaniEl and his friends from being destroyed along with the rest of Babylon’s wise men.
[Daniel] [2]:[19] Then that night, DaniEl had a vision in which the mystery of the dream was revealed to him. So he praised the God of heaven, and said this:
[Daniel] [2]:[20] ‘May the Name of The Great God be praised Throughout the age and into the age of the ages. To Him, understanding and wisdom belong…
[Daniel] [2]:[21] He’s the One who changes the seasons and times. ‘He appoints kings and removes them… To the wise, He’s the One who gives wisdom As well as intelligence, so they’ll understand…
[Daniel] [2]:[22] He uncovers the things that are hidden and deep. ‘He knows all that happens in the darkness, For, He is the source of all light.
[Daniel] [2]:[23] So I acknowledge and praise You, O Great God of the ages. ‘For You’re the One who gave me the wisdom and power, And revealed what I petitioned from You, Regarding this matter of the king. Yes, You’ve revealed it to me!’
[Daniel] [2]:[24] Then DaniEl went to AriOch (the one whom the king had appointed to destroy all the wise men of Babylon) and said to him: ‘Don’t destroy the wise men of Babylon! I want you to take me before the king so I can announce the interpretation of the dream to him.’
[Daniel] [2]:[25] As a result, AriOch quickly took DaniEl before the king and told him: ‘I’ve found a man among the captive sons of Judah who can announce to the king the interpretation of his dream!’
[Daniel] [2]:[26] And the king asked DaniEl (whom he referred to as BelTeShazzar): ‘Are you really able to tell me the dream that I saw and then explain its meaning to me?’
[Daniel] [2]:[27] And there in the presence of the king, DaniEl said this: ‘The mystery that the king has asked the wise men, sorcerers, officials, and astrologers to announce to him isn’t theirs to explain.
[Daniel] [2]:[28] However, there’s a God in the heavens that can uncover mysteries, and He’s made known to King NebuChadnezzar what’s going to happen in the last days. ‘The dream that you saw in your head while you were lying in your bed was this:
[Daniel] [2]:[29] ‘You, O king, through the thoughts that you had in your bed, were elevated to see what will happen after this… For mysteries have been made known to you about things that will happen [in the future].
[Daniel] [2]:[30] ‘Now, I’m no wiser than any other living man; but this mystery has been uncovered to me so that the king may understand what it means, and so that you may know the thoughts that are in your own heart.
[Daniel] [2]:[31] ‘You looked, O king, and you saw a huge idol that was overwhelming in size… It stood right in front of your face and it frightened you!
[Daniel] [2]:[32] ‘This idol had: A head of pure gold; Its breast, arms, and hands were of silver; Its belly and thighs were of brass; Its legs were of iron; and Its feet were part iron and part baked clay.
[Daniel] [2]:[33] ‘Well, as you were staring at it, a rock was cut from a mountain without any hands, which thereafter flew and hit the image on its feet of iron and baked clay, which completely shattered them…
[Daniel] [2]:[34] And everything else was shattered at the same time (the baked clay, the iron, the brass, the silver, and the gold). Then it all became like a cloud of dust from a threshing floor during the harvest,
[Daniel] [2]:[35] and thereafter a wind came and blew it all away, leaving nothing at all. ‘Then the stone that had struck the image [grew into] a huge mountain that covered the whole earth.
[Daniel] [2]:[36] ‘So, that was your dream… And now I’ll tell the king what it means.
[Daniel] [2]:[37] ‘You, O king, are the king of kings to whom the God of heaven has given a strong, fortified, and honorable kingdom.
[Daniel] [2]:[38] And in every place where the sons of men live, as well as in every place where the wild animals of the fields and flying creatures of the skies live, has been given into your hands by Him, for He’s made you the lord over it all. So you, O king, are the head of pure gold.
[Daniel] [2]:[39] ‘But after you, another kingdom will arise that’s inferior to yours, and then a 3rd kingdom (the one of brass) will come to dominate the whole earth. [It will be followed by] a 4th kingdom that will become as strong as iron…
[Daniel] [2]:[40] For just as iron can crush and tame all things, it will crush and tame everything.
[Daniel] [2]:[41] ‘Then the feet and the toes that you saw, which were partly of iron and partly of baked clay, will be a divided kingdom. ‘However, because you saw the iron mixed with the baked clay; [this means that] some of the roots of the iron will be in it.
[Daniel] [2]:[42] And since the toes of the feet are partly of iron and partly of baked clay, part of the kingdom will be strong and part of it will be easily broken.
[Daniel] [2]:[43] For as you saw the iron mixed with the baked clay; [this kingdom] will be mixed with the offspring of mankind… And they won’t stick to each other, just as iron won’t stick to baked clay.
[Daniel] [2]:[44] ‘Then in the time of those kings, the God of heaven will establish a Kingdom that won’t be corrupted throughout the ages, and His Kingdom won’t be passed on to anyone else. ‘[First] it’ll crush and sift all the other kingdoms, and it will stand throughout the ages thereafter.
[Daniel] [2]:[45] ‘So, now that you’ve seen the stone cut from a mountain without hands, and how it crushed the baked clay, iron, brass, silver, and gold; the great God has revealed to the king what’s going to happen after this. ‘This dream is true, and you can trust its interpretation.’
[Daniel] [2]:[46] Well at that, King NebuChadnezzar fell to his face and bowed before DaniEl. Then he offered him some very nice cologne as a gift, and he [told his servants] to bring him something to drink.
[Daniel] [2]:[47] Then the king said this to DaniEl: ‘It’s a fact that your God is the God of gods, Lord of lords, and King of kings. For He alone can uncover mysteries… As you were able to uncover this mystery!’
[Daniel] [2]:[48] After that, the king honored DaniEl by giving him many great gifts, and he appointed him over all the [districts] of Babylon as the ruler over all the governors and wise men of Babylon.
[Daniel] [2]:[49] And because he then requested this of the king, ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego were appointed over the construction projects throughout all the regions of Babylon, and DaniEl [thereafter served] within the courtyard of the king.
[Daniel] [3]:[1] It was during his 16th year that King NebuChadnezzar had a gold-[plated] idol made that stood 100 feet (30.5m) tall and 10 feet (3m) wide, which he placed in the plains of Dura, near Babylon.
[Daniel] [3]:[2] So he then called for all of his top officials, generals, lieutenants, governors, vassal kings,
[Daniel] [3]:[3] and everyone else of authority throughout all of his districts, and decreed that they should come and [celebrate] a holiday of dedication for the idol that he had erected. So everyone came and stood before the idol that NebuChadnezzar had erected,
[Daniel] [3]:[4] and then the [king’s] herald yelled at the top of his voice: ‘O nations, peoples, tribes, and languages, ‘You’ve been told that
[Daniel] [3]:[5] when you hear the sound of the trumpets, woodwinds, harps, stringed instruments, and bagpipes playing the anthem, you must all fall to your faces and bow before the idol of gold that King NebuChadnezzar has erected.
[Daniel] [3]:[6] ‘And if anyone should choose not to bow before it, he will be immediately taken out and thrown into a blazing-hot furnace!’
[Daniel] [3]:[7] So when the people heard the sounds of the trumpets, woodwinds, harps, stringed instruments, and bagpipes playing the anthem, all the peoples, tribes, and languages bowed low before the gold idol that King NebuChadnezzar had erected.
[Daniel] [3]:[8] However, certain Chaldeans then went up and made an accusation against the Jews…
[Daniel] [3]:[9] They went to King NebuChadnezzar and said: ‘O king, ‘May you live throughout the ages!
[Daniel] [3]:[10] ‘However, the king gave an order that when we hear the sound of the trumpets, woodwinds, harps, stringed instruments, and bagpipes playing the anthem,
[Daniel] [3]:[11] any man who doesn’t fall and bow before the gold idol should be thrown into a blazing furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[12] ‘Now, there were three Jewish men whom you’ve put over construction in Babylon – ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego – and they didn’t obey your decree, O king! ‘For they’ve chosen not to serve your gods or to bow before the gold idol that you’ve erected.’
[Daniel] [3]:[13] Well at that, NebuChadnezzar flew into an angry rage and he had them bring ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego before him.
[Daniel] [3]:[14] Then NebuChadnezzar said to them: ‘ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego, is it true that you won’t serve my gods, and that you won’t bow before the gold idol that I’ve erected?
[Daniel] [3]:[15] ‘Well now, when you hear the sound of trumpets, woodwinds, harps, stringed instruments, and bagpipes playing the anthem, it would be best for you to fall to your faces before the gold idol that I’ve made. Because, if you don’t bow to your faces before it, you’ll be taken out immediately, and then thrown into a blazing-hot furnace… And then we’ll see which God can rescue you from my hands!’
[Daniel] [3]:[16] But ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego said this to King NebuChadnezzar: ‘We don’t really have to answer you about this matter,
[Daniel] [3]:[17] for our God in the heavens (whom we serve) can rescue us from the fire in the furnace… And He will rescue us from your hands, O king!
[Daniel] [3]:[18] ‘Yet, even if He shouldn’t choose to do this, you must know, O king, that we won’t serve your gods, or the gold idol that you’ve set up and told us to bow before.’
[Daniel] [3]:[19] Well, NebuChadnezzar was furious! The way that he viewed ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego suddenly started to change. So he gave instructions to heat the furnace seven times hotter than usual… Until they couldn’t get it any hotter!
[Daniel] [3]:[20] Then he gave some powerful men instructions to shackle ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego, and then throw them into the blazing-hot furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[21] So the three were shackled and then thrown into the midst of the blazing-hot furnace fully clothed, [wearing their] pants, underclothes, and official turbans.
[Daniel] [3]:[22] And following the instruction of the king, the furnace had in fact been made seven times hotter than usual.
[Daniel] [3]:[23] Well, the three men (ShadRach, MeShach, and AbedNego) fell into the midst of the blazing furnace wearing shackles… But then they started walking around in the midst of the flames, praising God and blessing their lord!
[Daniel] [3]:[24] They walked around in the flame, singing praises to The God and praising the Lord.
[Daniel] [3]:[25] Then Azariah stood up and, speaking from the fire, prayed this way:
[Daniel] [3]:[26] ‘You are praised, O [Jehovah], our fathers’ God. You are worthy of praise, And Your name is glorified into the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[27] ‘For You are righteous in all You’ve done. All Your works are true, Your ways are straight, And all Your judgments are truth.
[Daniel] [3]:[28] ‘You’ve carried out true judgments in all You brought on us And upon JeruSalem, our fathers’ holy city. For in truth and judgment, You brought all these things upon us, because of our sins.
[Daniel] [3]:[29] ‘We have sinned and acted lawlessly By turning away from You; We have sinned in every way.
[Daniel] [3]:[30] ‘We haven’t listened to Your commandments, Nor have we kept them, Nor have we done as You commanded us, So that things might go well for us.
[Daniel] [3]:[31] ‘All You have brought upon us, And all You have done to us, You have done in true judgment.
[Daniel] [3]:[32] ‘You have handed us over to lawless and very hostile enemies, To apostates, and to an unrighteous and very wicked king, Worse than any on earth.
[Daniel] [3]:[33] ‘And now we can’t open our mouths; Shame and disgrace have come upon Your servants And those who worship You.
[Daniel] [3]:[34] ‘Please don’t completely abandon us for Your name’s sake, And don’t cancel Your Sacred Agreement,
[Daniel] [3]:[35] And don’t withdraw Your mercy from us, For the sake of Abraham, Your beloved, And Isaac, Your servant, and Israel, Your holy one,
[Daniel] [3]:[36] To whom You promised to multiply their descendants Like the stars of heaven And the sand on the seashore.
[Daniel] [3]:[37] ‘O Master, we have been made smaller than all other nations, and we are humbled throughout the earth today because of our sins.
[Daniel] [3]:[38] ‘Right now, there’s no: ruler prophet or leader ‘No: burnt offering sacrifice grain offering or incense...No place to offer first fruits before You and find mercy.
[Daniel] [3]:[39] ‘But may we be accepted with a contrite inner person And a humble spirit.
[Daniel] [3]:[40] ‘Just as with burnt offerings of rams and bulls, And with tens of thousands of fat lambs, Let our sacrifice be before You today. May it accomplish Your will, For those who trust in You will not be shamed.
[Daniel] [3]:[41] ‘Now we follow You with our whole mind. We fear You and seek Your presence.
[Daniel] [3]:[42] Don’t put us to shame, But deal with us according to Your gentleness and Your abundant mercy.
[Daniel] [3]:[43] Rescue us by Your wondrous deeds, And give glory to Your name, O [Jehovah].
[Daniel] [3]:[44] ‘May all who inflict evil upon Your servants be shamed; May they be disgraced in all their power, And may their strength be broken,
[Daniel] [3]:[45] Let them know that You alone are [Jehovah] God, Glorious over all the inhabited earth.’
[Daniel] [3]:[46] Meanwhile, the king’s servants who had thrown them in didn’t stop stoking the furnace with naphtha, pitch, tow, and brushwood.
[Daniel] [3]:[47] The flame spread out above the furnace for 49 cubits [~80 feet / ~24m],
[Daniel] [3]:[48] and it swept through and burned up the Chaldean men it found around the furnace!
[Daniel] [3]:[49] But the [Jehovah]‘s messenger went down into the furnace with Azariah and his companions. He drove the fire’s flame out of the furnace.
[Daniel] [3]:[50] He made the furnace’s inside like a damp, whistling wind. The fire didn’t touch them at all; it neither hurt nor troubled them.
[Daniel] [3]:[51] Then the three, with one voice, began to sing praises, glorify, and praised The God in the furnace, saying:
[Daniel] [3]:[52] ‘You are praised, O [Jehovah], our fathers’ The God, Worthy of praise and highly exalted into the ages. And praised is Your holy, glorious name, Highly praised and highly exalted into all the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[53] ‘You are praised in Your holy glory’s temple, Highly praised and supremely glorious into the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[54] ‘You are praised, who looks down on the deeps, Who sits upon the cherubim, Worthy of praise and highly exalted into the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[55] ‘You are praised upon Your kingdom’s throne, Highly praised and highly exalted into the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[56] ‘You are praised in heaven’s firmament, Praised and glorified into the ages.

[Daniel] [3]:[58] ‘Praise the Lord, all [Jehovah]‘s messengers; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[59] ‘Praise the Lord, all heavens; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.
[Daniel] [3]:[60] ‘Praise the Lord, all waters and everything above the heavens; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.

[Daniel] [3]:[62] ‘Praise the Lord, O sun and moon; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.

[Daniel] [3]:[81] ‘Praise the Lord, all wild beasts and cattle; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.

[Daniel] [3]:[83] ‘Praise the Lord, O Israel; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.

[Daniel] [3]:[85] ‘Praise the Lord, O servants; Praise and highly exalt Him into the ages.
