[Daniel] [9]:[23] I’ve been coming since you started your prayer To tell you that you’ve been found to be A very desirable man. ‘So, you must now reflect on the things That you’ll see in this vision.
[Daniel] [9]:[24] 70 periods of 7 have been set On behalf of you and your people And for the Holy City on Zion ‘So as to bring an end to your sins, To set a seal on your errors, To wipe away all of your lawless deeds, And to atone for the [bad things you’ve done]… ‘To restore righteous ways throughout the ages, To set a seal on the prophecies and visions, And to anoint the holiest of the holy.
[Daniel] [9]:[25] ‘So, know this, and now understand: ‘From the delivery of the word and its response For JeruSalem to be built once again Until the Anointed (Greek: Christou) Leader arrives, Will be 7 periods of 7, Plus 62 periods of 7. They’ll rebuild the walls and the squares, But they’ll do it through difficult times.
[Daniel] [9]:[26] ‘And after the 62 periods of 7, The Anointed One will then be destroyed… For in that place, there’ll no longer be justice. ‘Then the Holy Place and the city Will be corrupted by a leader that will come And cut them off by a downpour… He’ll order an extinction upon them Until the end of his war.
[Daniel] [9]:[27] ‘He’ll strengthen the Sacred Agreement with many During one period of 7; But in half of that period of 7, Sacrifices and drink offerings will be lifted away. ‘Then, to the Temple will come the disgusting destroyer, And until that time is fulfilled, There’ll just be complete desolation.’
[Daniel] [10]:[1] Well, it was during the 3rd year of the reign of Cyrus, the king of Persia that these true words were uncovered to me DaniEl (who was also called BelTeShazzar), and I was able to gain a great understanding from this vision.
[Daniel] [10]:[2] At the time, I (DaniEl) had been in mourning for three weeks…
[Daniel] [10]:[3] I hadn’t eaten any meat or bread, nor drunk any wine. I also hadn’t rubbed myself with any oil during those three weeks.
[Daniel] [10]:[4] Then, (on the 24th day of the 1st month) as I was standing on the banks of the great Tigris River,
[Daniel] [10]:[5] I raised my eyes and I saw a man wearing linen clothes. His hips were wrapped in the gold of Ophir,
[Daniel] [10]:[6] his body looked like stone, and his face looked like lightning, his eyes looked like burning lamps, his arms and legs looked like shining brass! When he spoke it was like the sound of a large crowd!
[Daniel] [10]:[7] I was the only one who saw this vision. The men who were with me at the time didn’t see anything. However, something came over them that frightened them, so they all ran away –
[Daniel] [10]:[8] leaving me alone. Well, when I had this great vision, it left me weak… It took all my glory and corrupted it, leaving me without any strength.
[Daniel] [10]:[9] Then I heard a voice speaking words. When I heard what was being said, I was confused. So I fell with my face to the ground.
[Daniel] [10]:[10] Then, {Look!} a hand reached out and touched me and lifted me up on my knees and onto the palms of my hands.
[Daniel] [10]:[11] And this is what he said to me: ‘O DaniEl, you very desirable man... Understand the words I’m speaking to you. Get up and stand on your feet, For I’ve been sent here to help you!’ Well when he said that, I stood up, but I was still shaking.
[Daniel] [10]:[12] And he said to me: ‘Don’t be afraid, O DaniEl. For from the first day that you opened your heart So as to understand [all these things], And you started [your fast] to [Jehovah] your God, All of your words have been heard! And I’ve come here because of the things that you’ve prayed.
[Daniel] [10]:[13] ‘But the ruler of the kingdom of Persia Stood and opposed me for 21 days, Until MichaEl (one of the foremost rulers) [Finally] came to my aid. ‘So, that’s where I’d left him… With the ruler of the kingdom of Persia,
[Daniel] [10]:[14] And I’ve come here so as to explain What will happen to your people in the last days. For, this is a vision of things that will be.’
[Daniel] [10]:[15] Well as he was saying that, I fell with my face to the ground once again, because I was so confused.
[Daniel] [10]:[16] Then {Look!} someone who looked like one of the sons of men came and touched my lips, and I was able to open my mouth and speak. So, to the one standing in front of me I said: ‘O lord, seeing this vision of you has twisted my insides and left me weak.
[Daniel] [10]:[17] So, O Lord, how will your servant be able to speak to you, since I’m weak, I can’t stand up, and I can hardly breathe!’
[Daniel] [10]:[18] Then [somebody who] looked like a human came and touched me, and gave me strength.
[Daniel] [10]:[19] And he said: ‘Don’t be afraid, you most desirable man… ‘May you have peace! ‘But now you must be manly and strong!’ Well, as he was speaking to me, I did become stronger, so I said: ‘Now speak, O my lord, because you’ve given me the strength [I need]!’
[Daniel] [10]:[20] Then he asked: ‘Do you know why I’ve come here to you? Although I must now go back and fight a war Against the ruler of the kingdom of Persia, Before the ruler of the Greeks will arrive,
[Daniel] [10]:[21] I’ve come here to help you write words of truth. And no one is with me when it comes to these things Other than MichaEl, your ruler.’
[Daniel] [11]:[1] In the first year of King Cyrus’ reign, [the messenger] told me: ‘Since the 1st year of Cyrus, I’ve been standing nearby in power and might…
[Daniel] [11]:[2] And now, I’ll tell you the truth: '{Look!} In Persia, three kings will arise, Then a fourth will come who’ll be richer. And after he gains all his wealth, He will attack the kingdoms of Greece.
[Daniel] [11]:[3] ‘Then [from Greece], a mighty king will arise Who’ll gain a vast kingdom And he’ll do whatever he wishes.
[Daniel] [11]:[4] ‘But, after his kingdom has been established, It’ll be divided and broken Towards the four winds of the skies… And it won’t be as strong as during his rule. For his kingdom will then be plucked up And divided among the outsiders.
[Daniel] [11]:[5] ‘Then the king in the south will grow mighty, But another one will grow stronger And he’ll use the authority he’s given To rule a kingdom that’s vast.
[Daniel] [11]:[6] ‘However, after his time, They’ll all become allies; And the daughter of Egypt’s king Will go to the king in the north And she’ll make treaties with him. But his arm won’t be strong, and his offspring won’t survive. ‘Then, she’ll be handed over, Along with all those who brought her, As well as with her young women, And the one who made her strong in her time.
[Daniel] [11]:[7] ‘Then someone will arise from the root of her flower, And when he’s ready, he’ll attack The army of the king of the north And overrun his supporters… He will conquer and then win the war.
[Daniel] [11]:[8] ‘He’ll carry away all of their molded gods And all of their most desirable things (Including their silver and gold). Then, back to Egypt, he’ll take it… For he’ll dominate the king of the north.
[Daniel] [11]:[9] ‘Thereafter, [the king] of the north Will come and enter the kingdom Of the king of the south… But then, he will return to his land.
[Daniel] [11]:[10] ‘So his sons will gather an army, Which will quickly overrun and pass through. [In that land], they’ll thereafter settle, And they’ll fight all the way to his stronghold.
[Daniel] [11]:[11] ‘This will enrage the king of the south And he will raise a large army To fight against the king of the north, And he’ll take many captives.
[Daniel] [11]:[12] ‘Then his heart will become very proud, And thousands, he will cut to the ground… But the war that he will fight won’t be won.
[Daniel] [11]:[13] ‘Thereafter, the king of the north Will gather an army that’s larger, And towards the end of [his rule], He’ll attack and enter with power, Along with many [weapons of war].
[Daniel] [11]:[14] ‘But, during that time, there will be a rebellion Against the king of the south, As the rabble among your people grow many, So this vision will be proven true… But then, they will also get weaker.
[Daniel] [11]:[15] ‘Then the king of the north will attack, And he will build many siege mounds To capture their fortified cities. ‘And the chosen ones of the south will arise; Yet, they won’t be quite as strong.
[Daniel] [11]:[16] So the one who enters will do what he wants, And none will be able to stop him. ‘Then he’ll stand in the glorious land, And with his own hands, he will destroy it.
[Daniel] [11]:[17] ‘Thereafter, he will set his face To march against their whole kingdom With those who have been proven upright, And this is what he will do: ‘They’ll give him the daughter of a woman, So that he can thereafter corrupt her, But she will not stay and she’ll never be his.
[Daniel] [11]:[18] ‘So he’ll turn his attention to the islands, And many will be captured there. This will stop the ridicule of their kings… But, only for a short time.
[Daniel] [11]:[19] ‘At that time, he will turn his attention To making his land much stronger again; But then, he’ll get weaker and fall, And never be [heard from] again.
[Daniel] [11]:[20] ‘Yet, from out of his roots, will arise The shoot of a kingdom to oppose him, And demand all the glory of his kingdom. ‘Yet, in those days, he’ll be broken… But, not by rebellion or war.
[Daniel] [11]:[21] There’ll be someone who will stand in his place Whom he once treated with great contempt And not given any glory in his kingdom. But, in prosperity, he will return, And through treachery, he’ll then take the kingdom.
[Daniel] [11]:[22] ‘So the strength of the one who was bringing the flood Will be broken and washed away from his face… The one who is in charge of the Sacred Agreement.
[Daniel] [11]:[23] ‘For, after he’s made an alliance, He will then act in deceitful ways. ‘Through a nation that’s small, he’ll gain power,
[Daniel] [11]:[24] And he will go to a prosperous place To do what his fathers and even their fathers Had been unable to do… He’ll plunder and divide up the loot. ‘Then, he will plot against Egypt,
[Daniel] [11]:[25] And when he’s strong, he will set his heart Against the king of the south, And attack him with a great army. ‘But the king of the south will gather an army And beat him with their new weapons of war…
[Daniel] [11]:[26] He’ll devour everything that he wanted to take, And then, he will destroy their whole army… He’ll break them and he will kill many.
[Daniel] [11]:[27] ‘So, both kings will have wicked hearts, And when they sit down at a table, They’ll lie and settle nothing at all Until the end has arrived.
[Daniel] [11]:[28] ‘Then, when he goes back to his country, He will do so with things that he’s plundered And with his heart set firmly against The Holy Sacred Agreement. ‘But, after he returns to [his] land,
[Daniel] [11]:[29] He’ll invade the south once again… Yet it won’t be the same as he did at the first.
[Daniel] [11]:[30] ‘Then, [ships] of Cyprus will attack him And [teach him] that he must be humble; So he’ll return and show his rage once again Against the Holy Sacred Agreement. ‘He will launch an attack against those who supported The Holy Sacred Agreement,
[Daniel] [11]:[31] Then [they’ll come] and profane the great Holy Place… And bring an end to the daily sacrifices. Yes he will bring the disgusting destroyer
[Daniel] [11]:[32] Against all those who are breaking the Law And disregarding the Sacred Agreement. ‘But those who know God will grow stronger And they’ll do whatever needs to be done…
[Daniel] [11]:[33] For they will come to know many things. ‘Yet, they will be weakened by swords and by fire, And as captives, they will be carried away… they will be ravaged for a very long time.
[Daniel] [11]:[34] ‘Then, after they have become weakest, They will be given some help; For, many will be added to them… But, they won’t have the same zeal.
[Daniel] [11]:[35] ‘They’ll drag down those who do understand And purify them as through fire Until the time of the end, Which will still be a long time away.
[Daniel] [11]:[36] ‘Thereafter, the king will grow in his might And put himself higher than all of the gods… Including the God of all gods.
[Daniel] [11]:[37] ‘He will forget the Gods of his fathers, And not notice the desires of women… He will ignore all the gods, And put himself higher than all.
[Daniel] [11]:[38] ‘A god of war from his country, He will then glorify (A god whom his fathers never knew) With silver, gold, and most precious gems, And many desirable things.
[Daniel] [11]:[39] ‘Within a fortress of refuge, He will act with a strange god (Whichever one he chooses)… He’ll make it grow in its glory, And cause many to bow down before it, And then, he’ll divide the land up as gifts.
[Daniel] [11]:[40] ‘Then, in the time of the end, He’ll lock horns with the king of the south… And the king of the north will gather to him Many chariots, horsemen, and ships. So, he will then enter their land… He will break it and he will pass through it.
[Daniel] [11]:[41] ‘And then, he will enter the glorious land, And many there, will be weakened. But these ones will be saved from his hands: Edom, MoAb, and the sovereignty of AmMon’s sons.
[Daniel] [11]:[42] ‘Then he’ll stretch his hand out over the land, And the land of Egypt will not be saved.
[Daniel] [11]:[43] He’ll dominate all with the hidden reserves Of their silver and gold, And the best things of Libya, Ethiopia, and Egypt… [Things that he’ll find in] their forts.
[Daniel] [11]:[44] ‘Then, out of the north and the east, He will hear things that disturb him. So he’ll leave in a rage, bringing many along, To wipe away and destroy.
[Daniel] [11]:[45] ‘His royal tent, he will then set up Between the sea and the Holy Mountain of Glory Until he comes to his end… When no one will be able save him.’
[Daniel] [12]:[1] ‘And in that very same hour, The Highest Messenger, MichaEl, will come (The one who keeps watch on the sons of your people), And a difficult time will arrive Such as has never happened before, And will never happen again. ‘At that time, your people will be saved (Those whose [names] have been written in the scroll),
[Daniel] [12]:[2] And many that are sleeping in graves will arise, Some to life throughout the ages, And others to disgrace and ages of shame.
[Daniel] [12]:[3] ‘Then, those who understand what I’m saying Will shine like lights in the firmament. And the many that prove themselves righteous Will shine like stars throughout the ages.
[Daniel] [12]:[4] ‘And you, O DaniEl, ‘Cover these words and seal up the scroll Until the time of the end. [It’s a time when] many will be taught And knowledge will be multiplied.’
[Daniel] [12]:[5] Then I, DaniEl, looked and I saw two others that were also standing there, one on this side of the river, and the other on the opposite bank.
[Daniel] [12]:[6] One of them asked the man in the linen clothes that was standing over the water in the river: ‘When will all these wonders of which you spoke reach their conclusion?’
[Daniel] [12]:[7] And the man in the linen clothes who was standing over the river raised both his right and left hands high towards the heavens, and he swore an oath to The God who lives throughout ages, saying: ‘The holy ones will be scattered For 3-1/2 times, Before these things reach their end.’
[Daniel] [12]:[8] Well, I heard it, but I didn’t understand it. So I said: ‘O lord, when will these things that you’ve spoke about start to happen? And when will your judgment arrive?’
[Daniel] [12]:[9] And he said: ‘Go, O DaniEl, ‘Cover and seal up these words!
[Daniel] [12]:[10] ‘For, there will be many who are chosen And they will be [dressed] in white robes. ‘By fire, they will be purified… And thereafter, they will all be made holy. ‘But the sinners will continue to sin, And they won’t be seeking knowledge.
[Daniel] [12]:[11] ‘From the time the disgusting destroyer arrives And the sacrificing comes to an end Is 1,290 days.
[Daniel] [12]:[12] ‘And all of those will be blest Who endure all the way to the end, Of 1,335 days.
[Daniel] [12]:[13] ‘Now, [you will] go to your rest Until that day and hour arrives. For then, you will be resurrected, And you will receive your inheritance After those days reach their end.’
[Daniel] [13]:[1] There was [a] man named JoAchim living in Babylon.
[Daniel] [13]:[2] He had married [a] woman named Susanna, HilkiAh’s daughter. She was exceedingly beautiful and feared the Lord.
[Daniel] [13]:[3] Her parents were righteous, and they had taught their daughter to follow the Law of Moses.
[Daniel] [13]:[4] JoAchim was exceedingly wealthy and had [a] garden next to his house. All the Jews would come to him because he was more respected than anyone else.
[Daniel] [13]:[5] That year, two elders from the people were appointed as judges. Now, the Lord had spoken about these very men, saying that lawlessness had come from Babylon, specifically from elders and judges who seemed to be governing the people.
[Daniel] [13]:[6] These men regularly stayed at JoAchim’s house. Everyone who had a case to be judged would come to them there.
[Daniel] [13]:[7] One day, when people left in the middle of the day, Susanna went into her husband’s garden to walk around.
[Daniel] [13]:[8] The two elders watched her daily as she went in and walked about, and they became filled with desire for her.
[Daniel] [13]:[9] They corrupted their own minds and stopped looking to heaven or remembering what was right.
[Daniel] [13]:[10] Both were consumed by their desire for her, but they didn’t tell each other how troubled they were,
[Daniel] [13]:[11] because they were ashamed to admit they wanted to be with her.
[Daniel] [13]:[12] Still, they eagerly watched for her day after day. One said to the other:
[Daniel] [13]:[13] ‘Let’s go home now, for it’s lunchtime.’ So they went out and went their separate ways.
[Daniel] [13]:[14] But then they returned to the same spot. When they questioned each other about why they had come back, they confessed their desire. At that point, they jointly arranged a time when they could find her alone.
[Daniel] [13]:[15] As they were watching for [a] suitable day, she came in one day, just like the two days before, with only two maidservants. She wanted to bathe in the garden because it was hot.
[Daniel] [13]:[16] No one else was there except the two elders, who were hidden and watching her closely.
[Daniel] [13]:[17] She said to the maidservants: ‘Bring me oil and lotions, and close the garden doors so I can bathe.’
[Daniel] [13]:[18] They did as she said. They closed the garden doors and went out through the side entrance to get what she had requested. They didn’t see the elders, because the elders were hiding.
[Daniel] [13]:[19] As soon as the maidservants left, the two elders stood up and rushed toward her,
[Daniel] [13]:[20] and said: ‘Look, the garden doors are closed, and no one sees us. We desire you, so agree to lie with us!’
[Daniel] [13]:[21] ‘If you refuse, we will testify against you that [a] young man was with you, and that’s why you sent your maidservants away.’ Susanna groaned and said:
[Daniel] [13]:[22] ‘I’m in distress on every side. If I do this, it means death for me; and if I don’t, I won’t escape your hands.
[Daniel] [13]:[23] ‘It’s better for me to fall into your hands without having done it than to sin before [Jehovah].’
[Daniel] [13]:[24] Then Susanna cried out loudly, and the two elders also cried out against her.
[Daniel] [13]:[25] One of them ran and opened the garden doors.
[Daniel] [13]:[26] When those in the house heard the outcry from the garden, they rushed in through the side door to see what had happened to her.
[Daniel] [13]:[27] When the elders spoke their words, the servants were exceedingly ashamed, because such [a] thing had never been said about Susanna before.
[Daniel] [13]:[28] The next day, when the people gathered at her husband JoAchim’s house, the two elders arrived. They were full of their wicked plot against Susanna, intending to put her to death. They said to the people:
[Daniel] [13]:[29] ‘Send for Susanna, daughter of HilkiAh, who is JoAchim’s wife.’ So they sent for her.
[Daniel] [13]:[30] She came with her parents, her children, and all her relatives.
[Daniel] [13]:[31] Susanna was exceedingly delicate and beautiful.
[Daniel] [13]:[32] The wicked men commanded that she be unveiled (she was veiled) so they could feast their eyes on her beauty.
[Daniel] [13]:[33] All who were with her and all who saw her wept.
[Daniel] [13]:[34] Then the two elders stood up among the people and placed their hands on her head.
[Daniel] [13]:[35] As she wept, she looked up to heaven, because her heart trusted in [Jehovah].
[Daniel] [13]:[36] The elders then said: ‘While we were walking alone in the garden, this woman came in with two maidservants. She closed the garden doors and sent the maidservants away.
[Daniel] [13]:[37] ‘Then [a] young man, who had been hidden there, came to her and lay down with her.
[Daniel] [13]:[38] ‘We were in a corner of the garden, and when we saw this wickedness, we ran towards them.
[Daniel] [13]:[39] ‘When we saw them together, we could not overpower the man because he was stronger than us, and he opened the doors and leaped out.
[Daniel] [13]:[40] ‘But we seized this woman and asked her who the young man was.
[Daniel] [13]:[41] ‘She refused to tell us. This is our testimony.’ The assembly believed them, since they were elders and judges of the people, and they condemned her to death. Susanna cried out loudly:
[Daniel] [13]:[42] ‘O The God, eternal [one], you know hidden things, and you know all things before they come into being!
[Daniel] [13]:[43] ‘You know that they’ve testified falsely against me! Look, I’m dying, even though I’ve done nothing of what these men wickedly accused me.’
[Daniel] [13]:[44] Well, [Jehovah] heard her voice.
[Daniel] [13]:[45] As she was being led away to be executed, The God stirred up the holy breath of [a] young boy named DaniEl.
[Daniel] [13]:[46] He cried out loudly: ‘I’m innocent of this woman’s blood!’
[Daniel] [13]:[47] All the people turned back to him and asked: ‘What is this you have said?’
[Daniel] [13]:[48] Standing among them, he said: ‘Are you so foolish, O sons of Israel? You’ve condemned [a] daughter of Israel without examining the case or knowing the truth!
[Daniel] [13]:[49] ‘Return to the place of judgment, because these men have testified falsely against her.’
[Daniel] [13]:[50] All the people hurried back. The elders said to him: ‘Come, sit among us and tell us, because The God has given you the privilege of [an] elder.’
[Daniel] [13]:[51] DaniEl said to them: ‘Separate them far from each other, and I will examine them.’
[Daniel] [13]:[52] When they had been separated, he called one of them and said: ‘You old man, steeped in wickedness, now your former sins have caught up with you!
[Daniel] [13]:[53] ‘You used to give unjust judgments, condemning the innocent and setting the guilty free, even though the Lord has said: ‘You shall not execute the innocent and righteous.’
[Daniel] [13]:[54] ‘Now then, if you truly saw her, tell me: Under what tree did you see them together?’ He replied: ‘Under [a] mastic tree.’
[Daniel] [13]:[55] DaniEl said: ‘You’ve lied directly against your own head! Because [a] messenger of The God has already received the divine command to split you in two!’
[Daniel] [13]:[56] After he had him removed, DaniEl commanded the other man to be brought forward. He said: ‘You offspring of Canaan, not of Judah! Beauty has deceived you, and lust has corrupted your heart.
[Daniel] [13]:[57] ‘This is how you treated the daughters of Israel; they would comply with you out of fear. But [a] daughter of Judah wouldn’t endure your wickedness!
[Daniel] [13]:[58] ‘Now then, tell me: Under what tree did you catch them together?’ He replied: ‘Under [an] oak tree.’
[Daniel] [13]:[59] DaniEl said to him: ‘You too have lied directly against your own head! Because the messenger of The God is waiting with a sword to saw you in two, so he can destroy you both.’
[Daniel] [13]:[60] Then the entire assembly cried out loudly and praised The God, who saves those who hope in Him.
[Daniel] [13]:[61] So they rose up against the two elders. DaniEl had convicted them, from their own mouths, of being false witnesses. The people did to them just as they had wickedly intended to do to their neighbor,
[Daniel] [13]:[62] following the Law of Moses, and they executed them. In this way, innocent blood was saved that day.
[Daniel] [13]:[63] HilkiAh and his wife, along with Susanna’s husband JoAchim and all their relatives, praised their daughter, because no shameful thing was found in her.
[Daniel] [13]:[64] DaniEl became great in the eyes of the people from that day forward.
[Daniel] [14]:[1] King Astyages died and joined his ancestors, and Cyrus the Persian succeeded him on the throne.
[Daniel] [14]:[2] DaniEl was a close companion of the king and was more highly esteemed than all his other friends.
[Daniel] [14]:[3] Now, the Babylonians had [an] idol named [Marduk], and daily offerings were consumed for it: 12 artabas of fine flour [~85 US gallons / ~325 liters] 40 sheep And 6 measures of wine [~10 US gallons / ~46 liters]
[Daniel] [14]:[4] The king bowed down to it and went daily to bow down to it, but DaniEl bowed down to His own God. So the king asked him: ‘Why don’t you bow down to [Marduk]?’ DaniEl replied:
[Daniel] [14]:[5] ‘Because I don’t bow down to idols made by human hands, but the living God, who created heaven and earth and has dominion over all living things.’ The king said to him:
[Daniel] [14]:[6] ‘Don’t you think [Marduk] is [a] living god? Or don’t you see how much he eats and drinks every day?’ DaniEl laughed and said:
[Daniel] [14]:[7] ‘Don’t be mistaken, O king; because inside, it’s clay, and outside, it’s bronze, and it has never eaten anything!’ Enraged, the king called his priests and said to them:
[Daniel] [14]:[8] ‘If you don’t tell me who is consuming these provisions, you will die!
[Daniel] [14]:[9] ‘But if you can show that [Marduk] consumes them, DaniEl will die, because he has spoken blasphemy against [Marduk].’ DaniEl said to the king: ‘Let it be as you say.’ There were seventy priests of [Marduk], not counting their wives and children. The king went with DaniEl into the temple of [Marduk]. The priests of [Marduk] said:
[Daniel] [14]:[11] ‘Look, we will leave. But you, O king, set out the food and the mixed wine, then close the door and seal it with your signet ring.
[Daniel] [14]:[12] ‘If, when you return early tomorrow, you don’t find everything eaten by [Marduk], we will die, or DaniEl, who has slandered us.’
[Daniel] [14]:[13] But they were confident, because they had made a hidden entrance under the table, and through it they would continually enter and consume the offerings.
[Daniel] [14]:[14] So when they had gone out, the king set out the food for [Marduk]. DaniEl then ordered his servants to bring ash, and they scattered it over the entire floor of the temple in the presence of the king alone. Then they went out, closed the door, sealed it with the king’s signet ring, and left.
[Daniel] [14]:[15] Well, that night, the priests came as they usually did, along with their wives and children, and they ate and drank everything.
[Daniel] [14]:[16] The king got up early the next morning, and DaniEl was with him. He asked:
[Daniel] [14]:[17] ‘Are the seals intact, DaniEl?’ DaniEl replied: ‘They are, O king.’ As soon as the doors were opened, the king looked at the table and shouted loudly:
[Daniel] [14]:[18] ‘Great are you, [Marduk], and there is no deceit in you at all!’ But DaniEl laughed, and he stopped the king from entering. He said:
[Daniel] [14]:[19] ‘Look now at the floor and see whose footprints these are.’ The king said:
[Daniel] [14]:[20] ‘I see the footprints of men... And of women... And of children.’
[Daniel] [14]:[21] The king, enraged, then arrested the priests and their wives and children. They showed him the hidden doors through which they had been entering and eating the offerings on the table.
[Daniel] [14]:[22] The king killed them, and handed [Marduk] over to DaniEl, who destroyed it and its temple.
[Daniel] [14]:[23] There was also [a] great dragon, and the Babylonians bowed down to it. The king said to DaniEl:
[Daniel] [14]:[24] ‘You can’t deny that this is [a] living god, can you? So bow down to it!’ DaniEl said:
[Daniel] [14]:[25] ‘I will bow down to [Jehovah] my God, for He is the living God.
[Daniel] [14]:[26] ‘But you, O king, give me permission, and I will kill the dragon without a sword or a staff.’ The king said: ‘I grant it.’
[Daniel] [14]:[27] DaniEl took pitch, fat, and hair, boiled them together to make cakes. He fed them to the dragon, and when it ate them, the dragon burst open! Then DaniEl said: ‘Look at what you bow down to!’ When the Babylonians heard this, they were enraged and turned against the king, saying:
[Daniel] [14]:[28] ‘The king has become a Jew! He has torn down [the idol of] [Marduk], killed the dragon, and slaughtered the priests!
[Daniel] [14]:[29] ‘Deliver DaniEl to us! Otherwise, we will kill you and your household!’
[Daniel] [14]:[30] The king saw that they were pressing him hard, and, forced into it, he handed DaniEl over to them.
[Daniel] [14]:[31] So they threw him into the lions’ pit, and he was there for six days.
[Daniel] [14]:[32] Now there were seven lions in the pit, and they were usually given two bodies and two sheep each day. But this time, nothing was given to them, so they would eat DaniEl.
[Daniel] [14]:[33] Now Habakkuk the prophet was in Judea. He had cooked [a] stew and crumbled bread into [a] bowl, and was going to the field to bring food to the reapers. [A] messenger of [Jehovah] said to Habakkuk:
[Daniel] [14]:[34] ‘Take the meal you have to DaniEl in Babylon, to the lions’ pit.’ Habakkuk said:
[Daniel] [14]:[35] ‘[Jehovah], I’ve never seen Babylon, and I don’t know where the pit is.’
[Daniel] [14]:[36] Then the messenger of [Jehovah] took him by the crown of his head, and, lifting him by his hair, set him down in Babylon, directly above the pit, carried by the force of his breath. Habakkuk cried out:
[Daniel] [14]:[37] ‘DaniEl, DaniEl, take the meal which The God has sent you!’ DaniEl said:
[Daniel] [14]:[38] ‘Indeed, You The God have remembered me, and You have not forsaken those who love You.’
[Daniel] [14]:[39] DaniEl got up and ate. But the messenger of God at once returned Habakkuk to his home.
[Daniel] [14]:[40] On the seventh day, the king came to mourn DaniEl. He came to the pit and looked in, and look, DaniEl was sitting there! He shouted loudly:
[Daniel] [14]:[41] ‘Great are You, [Jehovah], DaniEl’s God, and there is no other God besides You!’
[Daniel] [14]:[42] He pulled DaniEl up. But those who had sought to destroy him, he threw into the pit, and they were at once eaten right before his eyes.
[Hosea] [1]:[1] The Word of [Jehovah] came to Hosea (son of BeEri) in the days of UzziAh, JoTham Ahaz, and HezekiAh the kings of Judah, and in the days of JeroBoam (son of JoAsh) the king of IsraEl.
[Hosea] [1]:[2] This is the beginning of the Word of [Jehovah] by Hosea. The [messenger of the] Lord spoke to Hosea and said this: ‘Take a woman for yourself from the whores So that children [can be born] from her whoring; Because, by chasing after immoral sex, The land has strayed from [Jehovah].’
[Hosea] [1]:[3] So [Hosea] went and took Gomer, the daughter of DiBlaim and she got pregnant and bore a son to him.
[Hosea] [1]:[4] Then [the messenger of] the Lord said to him: ‘Call his name JezreEl; For, in a short while, I’ll bring vengeance On the house of Judah for [the city of] JezreEl’s blood, And to the Kingdom of IsraEl, I’m also bringing an end.
[Hosea] [1]:[5] In that day, I’ll break IsraEl’s bow There in the valley of JezreEl.’
[Hosea] [1]:[6] Then she got pregnant again and gave birth to a daughter. And [the messenger of the Lord] said to him: ‘Call her name, Show No Mercy; For on IsraEl’s house, I’ll show no mercy… Yes I’ll stand against and oppose them.
[Hosea] [1]:[7] ‘Yet, by the power of [Jehovah] their God, I’ll show mercy upon Judah’s sons And I’ll bring them salvation. But, I’ll not save by the bow or the sword, Nor by battles of horses and horsemen.’
[Hosea] [1]:[8] Well, after she weaned Show No Mercy, she got pregnant again and bore another son to him.
[Hosea] [1]:[9] And [the messenger of the Lord] said: ‘Call his name, Not My People; For, you’re no longer my people, And I’m no part of you.
[Hosea] [1]:[10] ‘Yet the number of IsraEl’s sons Will become as great as the sands of the seas, So that no one can measure or count them. ‘And it’ll be in that place Where I told them that they’re no longer my people; They’ll be called, The Living God’s Sons.
[Hosea] [1]:[11] ‘Then they’ll gather the sons of IsraEl and Judah And appoint someone to rule over them. But, from this land, They’ll [now be taken away]; For, [the city of] JezreEl’s day [of reckoning] will be great!’
[Hosea] [2]:[1] [‘And God said:] ‘Now the brother, Not My People, should speak, As should his sister, Show No Mercy.
[Hosea] [2]:[2] They should plead with their mother, Although she’s not really My woman And I’m not really her man. ‘For I’ll bring an end to her whoring And the adultery she commits between her two breasts.
[Hosea] [2]:[3] Then I’ll strip her down ‘til she’s naked And make her like the day she was born. ‘To be wiped away, I’ll appoint her, And I’ll make her a waterless land… Then I’ll destroy her with thirst.
[Hosea] [2]:[4] ‘And on her children, I won’t show mercy, For, they’re the result of her whoring…
[Hosea] [2]:[5] Because their mother was immoral, The one who bore them, disgraced them. ‘For she said: ‘I’ll follow my lovers… Those who provided my water and bread, As well as my clothes and fine linen robes, Along with my olive oil, And the rest of the things that I truly deserve.’
[Hosea] [2]:[6] ‘For this, {Look!} with barbs, I’ll close up her way… I’ll block her ways and her roads So she’ll not be easily found.
[Hosea] [2]:[7] ‘Then, when she chases her lovers, She’ll not be able catch them… She’ll search for them, but not find them. ‘Then she’ll say: ‘I’ll return to my man, For with him, things had always been better.’
[Hosea] [2]:[8] ‘But she doesn’t know that I’m the one Who provided her grain and her wine, As well as her oil and her silver. ‘But then she took My silver and gold And used it to make things for BaAl.
[Hosea] [2]:[9] And for doing this, I’ll return And remove my grain in its season, As well as my wine in its time. ‘Then I’ll take away all of her clothes, As well as My linen robes, And leave her with nothing to cover her shame.
[Hosea] [2]:[10] ‘I’ll expose her filth to her lovers, And from My hand, she won’t be saved.
[Hosea] [2]:[11] I’ll remove the joy of her feasts, And her holidays, New Moons, and Sabbaths.
[Hosea] [2]:[12] I’ll also take all the grapes and the figs That she thought were the pay from her lovers. ‘Then I’ll appoint [those men] to witness [against her], And she’ll be eaten by the beasts in the fields, As well as by the birds in the skies And the things that crawl on the ground.
[Hosea] [2]:[13] ‘Yes, I’ll take vengeance upon her For each day that she offered to BaAl… When she put on her necklace and earrings And forgot Me to chase after lovers,’ said [Jehovah].
[Hosea] [2]:[14] ‘And for this, {Look!} I’ll cause her to wander, And I’ll order desolation upon her. But then, I’ll speak to her heart, And I’ll give back her things… I’ll turn that troublesome valley Into a valley of hope.
[Hosea] [2]:[15] I’ll make her as humble as she was in her youth… Like the day that she came up from Egypt.
[Hosea] [2]:[16] ‘And in that day, says [Jehovah], She will call Me her Husband… No more will she call out to a BaAl!
[Hosea] [2]:[17] For the name of a BaAl, I’ll lift from her mouth, And she won’t remember his name.
[Hosea] [2]:[18] ‘And in that day, I’ll conclude An agreement with the beasts of the fields, As well as with the birds in the skies, And with the things that crawl on the ground. ‘I’ll also break all the broadswords and bows… Yes, I’ll bring an end to the wars, And I’ll send hope to the land.
[Hosea] [2]:[19] ‘I’ll take her as My woman throughout the ages… I’ll take her rightly and fairly… In mercy and compassion, [I’ll welcome her back].
[Hosea] [2]:[20] I’ll take her to Myself in full trust, And she’ll think of Me as her Lord.
[Hosea] [2]:[21] ‘And in that day, says [Jehovah], To the skies, I’ll turn My attention. Then, they will tend to the land,
[Hosea] [2]:[22] And the land will tend to the grain As well as to the wine and the oil… To [the city of] JezreEl they’ll pay attention once more.
[Hosea] [2]:[23] ‘I’ll plant her in the ground for Myself, And I’ll love the one who is unloved. Then I’ll say: ‘You’re My people!’ ‘To those who weren’t really Mine; And she will say: ‘[Jehovah] is My God!’
[Hosea] [3]:[1] And the [messenger of the] Lord said to me: ‘Go again and love an adulteress Who wishes to do what’s evil! For, even though [Jehovah] loved IsraEl’s sons, They’ve looked to strange gods, And of raisin cakes, they’ve been fond!’
[Hosea] [3]:[2] So I hired [such a woman] for myself for 15 silver coins, 200 quarts (190l) of barley, and a skin flask of wine.
[Hosea] [3]:[3] And I said to her: ‘You must now sit next to me and you may not be immoral or be with [another man] for many days… You must be mine alone!
[Hosea] [3]:[4] For this is how the sons of IsraEl will sit for some time… Without a king or a ruler, and with no altar, sacrifices, priesthood, or anything else to give them direction.
[Hosea] [3]:[5] ‘But after these things are completed, IsraEl’s sons will return to search for their God [Jehovah] and for David to serve as their king. So at the end of the days, they’ll find joy in [Jehovah] and with the good things that He provides.’
[Hosea] [4]:[1] [Hosea now says:] ‘O sons of IsraEl, hear the Word of [Jehovah]! ‘For He has a case against all of you… Those who now live in this land, Because you have no mercy or truth, Or any knowledge of God:
[Hosea] [4]:[2] ‘Cursing, lying, murder, and fraud, As well as adultery, cover your land. You’ve also mingled blood with your blood… And for this, your land will now mourn.
[Hosea] [4]:[3] ‘So those living here will be fewer… And all the game in the fields, All the birds in the skies, And all the fish in the seas will now fail.
[Hosea] [4]:[4] ‘Then there’ll be no priests or judges to scold you;
[Hosea] [4]:[5] For each day, I’ll be making them weaker. And I’ll do the same to your prophets… So your mother will then be [the darkness of] night.
[Hosea] [4]:[6] ‘For, from my people, they’ve taken the knowledge… And because they’ve pushed higher knowledge away, I’ll push them away… They won’t be My priests anymore! ‘And because you’ve forgotten the laws of your God, I’ll be forgetting your children.
[Hosea] [4]:[7] So because of your sins against Me, Their glory, I’ll appoint to dishonor.
[Hosea] [4]:[8] Then My people will have to eat their own sins, As their lives will be claimed by their unrighteous ways.
[Hosea] [4]:[9] ‘And these things that will happen to the people Will also happen to the priests… Yes I’ll bring my vengeance upon them For all of their evil ways, And I’ll pay them back for their [unrighteous] thoughts.
[Hosea] [4]:[10] ‘Then they’ll eat and never be filled; For, they’ve become whores who can’t straighten their ways. They no longer look [to their God] anymore; Yes, they’ve abandoned [Jehovah]!
[Hosea] [4]:[11] For whoring, wine, and strong drink Have captured the hearts of My people.
[Hosea] [4]:[12] ‘They now look to omens for answers, And [wave magic] wands for replies. In a spirit of whoring, they’ve wandered, And to their God, they’re unfaithful.
[Hosea] [4]:[13] ‘They offer sacrifices upon the hill tops And beneath the oaks and white poplars, As well under the rest of the trees, [To ask] for good and protection. ‘For this, your daughters will all become whores And your brides will be filled with adultery.
[Hosea] [4]:[14] Then, I’ll not visit your daughters When they’re found guilty of whoring! Nor [will I visit] your daughters-in-law When they’re committing adultery! ‘Among prostitutes, they’ll all be mixed (Among those [that offer their bodies]). And since the men won’t understand, They’ll just treat them like whores.’
[Hosea] [4]:[15] ‘So IsraEl... Stop being stupid! And Judah... Stop going to GilGal And to the temple at BethEl! ‘Nor should you say, ‘As [Jehovah] is living,’ When you’re swearing your oaths!
[Hosea] [4]:[16] For since IsraEl is now like a heifer in heat, She’ll be fattened like a lamb in a feedlot.
[Hosea] [4]:[17] ‘And because Ephraim has partnered with idols, He’s set his own snares.
[Hosea] [4]:[18] For with CanaAnite whores he’s had sex, And he’s loved the dishonor of their neighing.
[Hosea] [4]:[19] So a mighty wind will now sweep him away, And his altars will bring him disgrace.’
[Hosea] [5]:[1] [And Hosea continues:] ‘Hear these things, O you priests… And house of IsraEl, you should pay close attention. O house of the king, you must listen too; For there’s a judgment that’s coming against you! [‘For God says:] ‘Despite your important positions, You’ve become your own snares. So I’m stretching a net on [Mount] Tabor
[Hosea] [5]:[2] (The type that they use to catch game), And I’ll be the One who corrects you.
[Hosea] [5]:[3] ‘I remember Ephraim and IsraEl Before they had strayed far from Me. But, Ephraim has since been immoral, And IsraEl is also defiled…
[Hosea] [5]:[4] Neither has remembered to turn to their God.’ ‘Now the spirit of whoring is in them, And they’ve [forgotten] [Jehovah].
[Hosea] [5]:[5] So because of her insolent ways, IsraEl’s face will be humbled. And for Ephraim’s unrighteous ways, I’ll bring weakness upon him… And I’ll also bring weakness on Judah.’
[Hosea] [5]:[6] ‘Although they bring before Him their sheep and their calves, There’s no way that they’ll follow [Jehovah]. So now, they can no longer find Him, Because they’ve all turned away.
[Hosea] [5]:[7] ‘Yes, they’ve abandoned [Jehovah], And to children of strangers, they’re now giving birth. So, they and all that they’d hope to inherit Will soon be eaten by blight.
[Hosea] [5]:[8] [‘For God says:] ‘So, blow the trumpets on the hill tops… Sound it from all the high places! In the house of On, you should proclaim it, So that BenJamin will also be shaken.
[Hosea] [5]:[9] For, Ephraim will soon be destroyed In the day of correction! ‘Although IsraEl’s tribes once put faith in Me,
[Hosea] [5]:[10] The rulers of Judah then joined with the rest That moved the property markers… So I’ll pour My rage upon them like water!
[Hosea] [5]:[11] ‘Yes, Ephraim [will be oppressed] Because he’s trampled on justice, And because he’s chased worthless things.
[Hosea] [5]:[12] So to Ephraim, I’m sending disturbance, And to the house of Judah, I’ll now be a spur.
[Hosea] [5]:[13] ‘Although Ephraim saw his disease, And although Judah understood his reasons for grief; Ephraim looked to Assyria And asked their king for his aid… But [that king] won’t be able to save them, And he won’t bring an end to their grief.
[Hosea] [5]:[14] ‘So to Ephraim, I’ll now be a panther, And to the house of Judah, a lion… For I’ll snatch them away and I’ll go… I’ll grab them and no one will save them.
[Hosea] [5]:[15] Then I’ll go back to My place, And I won’t be seen again ‘til the time That they turn and search for My face.’
[Hosea] [6]:[1] ‘But, when they’re oppressed, they’ll rise early; And then, about [Jehovah], they’ll say: ‘We should return to our God; For He’ll snatch us away and then heal us. He’ll attack them and then dress our wounds…
[Hosea] [6]:[2] Yes, after two days, He’ll restore us; Then, by the third day, we’ll be alive And we’ll be standing before Him!
[Hosea] [6]:[3] ‘Knowledge of Him, we’ll know and pursue… We’ll find Him at the first crack of dawn. Then like morning rain, He will arrive… Yes, like evening rain on the ground.’
[Hosea] [6]:[4] ‘[But right now God says:] ‘O Ephraim, what must I do? And Judah, what must I do? For your mercy is like morning fog, Which like the dew, fades away.
[Hosea] [6]:[5] ‘So, by the Prophets, I’ve mowed you down, And I’ve killed you with words from My mouth… My judgments upon you have gone forth like light.
[Hosea] [6]:[6] ‘What I want is mercy, not sacrifice… Higher knowledge instead of burnt-offerings!
[Hosea] [6]:[7] But you’ve broken your Sacred Agreement with Me, And you’ve shown Me your hatred.
[Hosea] [6]:[8] ‘GileAd is a city of wasted deeds… One which muddies the water.
[Hosea] [6]:[9] For her strength now comes from her thieves, And her priests also murder from ambush. ‘So, SheChem has committed unrighteous acts Against the house of IsraEl,
[Hosea] [6]:[10] And causes for shuddering, I’ve seen there; So because of Ephraim’s whoring, Both IsraEl and Judah have now been defiled.
[Hosea] [6]:[11] Thus they’ll reap [from the vine] of rebellion Until I bring back My people.’
[Hosea] [7]:[1] [‘And God continues:] ‘When I brought healing to IsraEl, It exposed the injustice of Ephraim, As well as Samaria’s evils. For at first, they all just told lies; Then, from among them, came thieves, And robbers led them out to the highways.
[Hosea] [7]:[2] ‘They sang together of the evil in their hearts, Remembering all the [bad things] they’d done. And now, they’re covered by the things that they chose… What they did in front of My face!
[Hosea] [7]:[3] ‘And all the bad things that they’ve done Have gladdened [the hearts] of their kings… Their lying ways delighted their rulers!
[Hosea] [7]:[4] ‘Now, all those who are committing adultery Are in an ‘oven’ that’s heated for baking by flames… They’ve been ‘kneaded’ and allowed to grow fat And the [whole ball] has ‘fermented.’
[Hosea] [7]:[5] ‘For, in the days of their kings, Their rulers became enraged by their wine, And they held out their [arms] towards vile men…
[Hosea] [7]:[6] Those whose hearts were burning like kilns. ‘Then, Ephraim’s sleep became filled With [thoughts of destroying] all night… And in the morning, they burst into flames.
[Hosea] [7]:[7] They all became heated like ovens, And then they devoured their judges. So, although all their kings have now fallen, No one has called out to Me.
[Hosea] [7]:[8] ‘Now, Ephraim’s people are all intermixed… They’re like a cake that’s been baked in hot ashes, Which [no one has bothered] to turn.
[Hosea] [7]:[9] ‘So, strangers have eaten his strength While he wasn’t paying attention… And after that, his hair all turned grey; Yet, he was still unaware.’
[Hosea] [7]:[10] [Hosea says:] ‘Now, IsraEl’s insolent ways Will bring humility to their faces; For, they haven’t turned towards [Jehovah] their God… No, after these things have all happened, They haven’t gone looking for Him.
[Hosea] [7]:[11] ‘So Ephraim has become like a dove That has no mind and no heart. First, he called out to Egypt, And then, to Assyria, he [turned].
[Hosea] [7]:[12] [‘And God says:] ‘But, when they go there, I’ll throw out My net And I’ll catch them like birds… I’ll drag them down and correct them, And listen as they’re tormented.
[Hosea] [7]:[13] ‘Yes, woe to them, for they’ve leaped away… O how wretched their lives have become In their irreverence towards Me. ‘Although I’m the One who once paid their ransom, They spoke against Me and lied…
[Hosea] [7]:[14] In their hearts, they failed to call out… They just laid there and shrieked in their beds, As they sold themselves for wine and for bread.
[Hosea] [7]:[15] ‘When they were corrected by Me, I also strengthened their arms! But then, against Me, they hatched wicked plots.
[Hosea] [7]:[16] ‘So when they return, they’ll have nothing… They’ll be like a bow that’s stretched tight, And their rulers will fall by the sword, Because they’ve said stupid things; Then in the land of Egypt, they’ll all be defiled.’

[Hosea] [9]:[2] But your threshing-floor grain [won’t feed you], And the wine in your vats will [soon fail].
[Hosea] [9]:[3] ‘For you chose not to dwell in the land of [Jehovah]… Yes, life in Egypt is what you preferred, And with the Assyrians, you ate what’s unclean.
[Hosea] [9]:[4] ‘You offered [Jehovah] no wine, And set nothing delicious before Him. So your sacrifices became like the bread That’s offered in mourning… It defiles all those who would eat it. ‘So, since you can’t bring your bread to [His Temple] For [the purpose of saving] your lives;

And because you’ve been so unrighteous, The pressures [in your lives] will increase.

[Hosea] [11]:[5] ‘But to the land of Egypt, he won’t return, For Assyria’s king will now rule him Because he refused to turn from [bad ways].

[Hosea] [11]:[12] ‘By Ephraim, I was circled with lies… By the irreverence of the houses of IsraEl and Judah.’ ‘But [Jehovah] will know them once more And call them The Holy People of God.’
[Hosea] [12]:[1] ‘Like an evil wind, Ephraim’s become… One who pursues burning winds all day long And does many things that are empty and vain. With Assyria, he’s made treaties of peace, And he’s traded olive oil down in Egypt.
[Hosea] [12]:[2] ‘And [Jehovah] has a case against Judah, So He’ll punish Jacob according to his ways, Then pay him back for the bad things he’s done.
[Hosea] [12]:[3] ‘For, while he was still in the womb, He caught the heel of his brother And grew in strength with his God.
[Hosea] [12]:[4] With an angel, he wrestled and won; Then he wept and begged [for a blessing].’ [‘And God said:] ‘So, there in [BethEl], he found Me.
[Hosea] [12]:[5] And it was also there where I said From now on, I must be remembered As [Jehovah], the Almighty.’
[Hosea] [12]:[6] ‘So, you should return to your God… Show mercy and learn to be fair… Yes, always [stay close] to [Jehovah]! [‘Yet God says:]
[Hosea] [12]:[7] ‘Yet, in [your land], you have unrighteous scales, And you love to tyrannize others.
[Hosea] [12]:[8] So, Ephraim is saying: ‘I’ve become rich, And I’ve found many ways to relax.’ ‘But he’ll never see the fruits of his work, Because of the evil he’s doing.
[Hosea] [12]:[9] ‘I am [Jehovah], your God… I’m the One who led you from Egypt. And I’ll settle you in your tents once again As I did in the days of My holiday feasts.
[Hosea] [12]:[10] ‘Once more, I’ll speak by My Prophets, And many visions, I’ll send them; For it’s through the hands of the Prophets That I’m being described.’
[Hosea] [12]:[11] [And Hosea says:] ‘GilGal no longer exists Because their kings offered things that were false. So their altars are heaps of turtle manure… The type that’s found in unplanted fields.
[Hosea] [12]:[12] ‘To the plains of Syria, Jacob had gone, As IsraEl’s servant searched for a wife; Then, for a woman, he watched over sheep.
[Hosea] [12]:[13] ‘And it was by [JoSeph], a Prophet of God, That IsraEl was led down to Egypt. Then, by that very same Prophet, IsraEl’s people were saved.
[Hosea] [12]:[14] ‘But now that Ephraim’s provoked [God] to rage; His blood will be poured out upon him… For [Jehovah] will pay him back for his scorn.’
[Hosea] [13]:[1] ‘According to what Ephraim said; IsraEl’s righteous laws came from Him… Then he turned to a BaAl and he died.
[Hosea] [13]:[2] ‘Yet, they’ve continued to sin, And cast images of idols with their silver, Which are thereafter finished by craftsmen Who say: ‘Now we must sacrifice men, Because there aren’t enough calves anymore!’
[Hosea] [13]:[3] ‘So, they’re like morning fog, Which like the dew, fades away… As chaff on the floors, they’ll just blow away, And like tears, they’ll dry.
[Hosea] [13]:[4] ‘[God says:] ‘I am [Jehovah] your God… I’m the One who led you from Egypt, And no other God, should you know, For there are no saviors other than Me!
[Hosea] [13]:[5] ‘I shepherded you in the desert, And in barren lands, made pastures for you.
[Hosea] [13]:[6] But then, your hearts became haughty, And because of this, you forgot Me.
[Hosea] [13]:[7] ‘So I’ll be like a panther or a leopard to you… Like the ways of the Assyrian people.
[Hosea] [13]:[8] Then like an angry bear, I’ll attack you! Yes, I’ll rip you to pieces, Then feed you to my cubs in the woods… Wild beasts of the fields will rip you apart!’
[Hosea] [13]:[9] ‘O IsraEl, ‘Because you’re now so corrupt, Who will come to your aid?
[Hosea] [13]:[10] ‘And what has happened to your king… Why isn’t he saving your cities… Why doesn’t he come and serve as your judge? ‘A long time ago you had asked Me To give you a king as your ruler!
[Hosea] [13]:[11] So I gave you a king in My anger, And My rage was then satisfied.
[Hosea] [13]:[12] ‘But from Ephraim, then came much injustice, And he tried to cover his sins.
[Hosea] [13]:[13] So the pangs of birth are now coming to him. And even his smartest of sons Won’t stop the destruction of his young.
[Hosea] [13]:[14] ‘Will I save them from the hands of the grave? Will I [pay] their ransom from death? Where is your punishment, O death, And where is your sting, O place of the dead? For, consoling them is far from My eyes!
[Hosea] [13]:[15] ‘This is why I will separate brothers And send burning winds from the desert to them, Which will dry up their veins And wipe away all their springs… Their land and good things will wither and dry.
[Hosea] [13]:[16] ‘Samaria will be wiped away Because she resisted her God. So her people will fall by the sword… Then those by her breasts will be dashed [to the ground] And those in the womb will be shredded!’
[Hosea] [14]:[1] [And Hosea continues:] ‘O IsraEl, ‘Return to [Jehovah], your God! For because of your sins, you’ve become weak.
[Hosea] [14]:[2] Follow your own [good advice] And then turn back to [Jehovah]! ‘Just ask Him to please overlook All of your unrighteous ways So that you can receive what is good And be repaid for the fruit of your lips.
[Hosea] [14]:[3] [‘For God says:] ‘Assyria will not be your savior, And upon their war horses, you’ll never ride. So stop calling those hand-made things gods, And start showing mercy to orphans!
[Hosea] [14]:[4] Then I will repair all your homes; I will turn back my rage; And I will confess that I love you!
[Hosea] [14]:[5] ‘To IsraEl, once more, I will become Like dew that arrives in the morning; Then, like a lily, he’ll blossom again And grow roots like Lebanon’s [trees].’
[Hosea] [14]:[6] ‘Yes his branches will grow very full; And like olive trees, he’ll bear so much fruit That to Lebanon, its scent will be carried.
[Hosea] [14]:[7] ‘Then, they will all be returned, And in His protection, they will sit. they will live amidst plenty of grain, And like grapevines, they will blossom… they will be remembered like Lebanon’s wines.
[Hosea] [14]:[8] [‘For God says:] ‘O Ephraim, ‘What good are all of your idols? Am I not the One who is humbling you And the One who can make you strong once again? For I’m a dense juniper tree, And it’s only by Me that you can bear fruit!’
[Hosea] [14]:[9] ‘So, who among you is wise, And who understands all these things… Who among you can recognize them? For the ways of [Jehovah] are straight, And the righteous will live by these ways While the irreverent will stumble and fall.’
[Joel] [1]:[1] These are words of [Jehovah] that came to JoEl (son of BathuEl).
[Joel] [1]:[2] [Joel says:] ‘Listen to these things, O you elders… Give ear, all you who live in the land! Have you seen such things in your [lives]? Were they seen in the days of your fathers?
[Joel] [1]:[3] ‘Describe these things to your children, And to all the generations that follow! [‘For God says:]
[Joel] [1]:[4] ‘For, caterpillars ate all that there was, And locusts devoured what they didn’t eat; Then, grasshoppers ate what remained from the locusts, And what the grasshoppers didn’t consume, Was thereafter destroyed by the blight.
[Joel] [1]:[5] ‘Now, sober up and start crying, All you who are drunk from your wine; For, joy and gladness are gone from your mouths,
[Joel] [1]:[6] Since a powerful and populous nation, Has now arrived in your land. ‘They have teeth that are like those of lions, And molars like those of young bears.
[Joel] [1]:[7] They’ve appointed your grapevines to extinction, And condemned your fig-trees to splinters. They’re searching for you and cutting you down, So now, all of your branches are white.
[Joel] [1]:[8] ‘Therefore, wail like woman wearing sackcloth, [Who mourns] for the man of her virgin years.
[Joel] [1]:[9] For the drink offerings and other sacrifices, Have been removed from [His Temple]. Yes mourn, O you Priests who serve at the Altar,
[Joel] [1]:[10] For all of the fields now lie bare! ‘And mourn, O land, for the grain is now gone, Also, the wine has all dried, And the oil is in short supply,
[Joel] [1]:[11] Because the farmers have withered away. ‘Therefore, wail for all that you own, Since the wheat and barley are gone from the fields!
[Joel] [1]:[12] ‘The grapes [have shriveled and] dried; Very few fig-trees remain; The pomegranates, palms, and the melons, And all the trees in the plains are now dry… Yes, all that brings joy to sons of men, Has been taken away!
[Joel] [1]:[13] ‘So Priests, tie your [hands] and beat on your chests… Yes wail, you who serve at the Altar! Go to bed wearing sackcloth, You who are serving before Me, Since there’s nothing left to be sacrificed, And nothing to bring as drink offerings, To the House of [Jehovah]!’
[Joel] [1]:[14] [And Joel says:] ‘Call for a period of fasting… Proclaim a solemn assembly! Gather the elders and all of the people, To the House of [Jehovah] your God, Where all must fervently call to the Lord!

[Joel] [1]:[16] Before your eyes, all the food was destroyed, With the rest that brings joy to your people.
[Joel] [1]:[17] ‘In the stables, the cows are now restless, Since all that they treasure is gone. The wine vats have all been cut down, And all of your grain is now parched…
[Joel] [1]:[18] So you’re left with nothing at all.’ ‘The herds of oxen are bawling, Because they don’t have any pasture, And your flocks of sheep have all been destroyed.
[Joel] [1]:[19] So, you should call out to [Jehovah], For your beautiful fields have been burned, And the flames have consumed all your trees. [‘For God says:]
[Joel] [1]:[20] ‘Now, even the beasts in the plains, Have all started looking to Me, Because their springs have gone dry, And the desert’s beauty has vanished.’
[Joel] [2]:[1] [‘For God says:] ‘So, sound the trumpets in Zion, And on the Holy Mountain, you must proclaim, That all should bow to their faces, For the Day of the Lord is at hand (it’s near)!
[Joel] [2]:[2] ‘It’s a day that’s gloomy and dark… It’s a day that’s cloudy with fog. And as dawn peaks over the mountains, [You can see] a vast, mighty people. ‘Throughout the ages, such a thing hasn’t happened, And through coming years, it won’t happen again… From one generation to another.
[Joel] [2]:[3] ‘A consuming fire is raging before you, And all that’s behind you is burning. A paradise of delights lies before you, But all that’s behind is extinction and desert, From which no man can escape.
[Joel] [2]:[4] ‘The sight of them is like horses… Like cavalry in hot pursuit.
[Joel] [2]:[5] Theirs is the sound of chariot wheels Leaping across tops of mountains… Like the sounds of flames burning stubble, And of a vast mighty hoard of warriors.
[Joel] [2]:[6] ‘Before them, the people will all be destroyed, And their faces will be like burnt pots.
[Joel] [2]:[7] For as soldiers, they’ll attack you; And as men of war, they’ll then scale your walls. ‘Each of their men will go their own ways, And they’ll not be turned from their paths…
[Joel] [2]:[8] But, none will stray far from their brothers. ‘They’ll arrive here with shields, And by their arrows, the people will fall… For no way will they tire [of killing].
[Joel] [2]:[9] ‘They’ll thereafter capture the city, And along its walls, they’ll run. Then, into your homes, they’ll descend And climb through your windows like thieves.
[Joel] [2]:[10] ‘Before their faces, there’ll be just confusion, And even the skies will be shaken. Then the sun and the moon will grow dark, And the brightness of the stars will decrease.
[Joel] [2]:[11] ‘Before his armies, the Lord will call out; For he’s leading a great mighty hoard. His power will be seen in the things that he does, For great is the Day of the Lord, Since none can stand and oppose him.
[Joel] [2]:[12] ‘Now run,’ says [Jehovah] your God! ‘Flee to Me whole-heartedly… Come fasting, weeping, and beating your chests!’
[Joel] [2]:[13] [Joel then says:] ‘So, tear at your hearts, not your clothes, And turn to [Jehovah] your God! For, He shows mercy and pity… He’s gentle and He’s forgiving, [So He’ll overlook] the bad things you’ve done.

[Joel] [2]:[21] ‘So, be courageous O land… Yes, you should rejoice and be glad, For [Jehovah] will be moved to take action!
[Joel] [2]:[22] ‘Also take courage, you cattle; For, pastures will burst from the desert, And all the trees will bear fruit… The fig-trees and grapevines will then yield their strength!
[Joel] [2]:[23] ‘And be glad, O children of Zion… Find joy in [Jehovah] your God. For to the righteousness, He will send food, And He’ll bring the rains (both the early and late) Just like He has done in the past.
[Joel] [2]:[24] ‘Then your threshing-floors will be covered with grain, As your vats of wine and oil overflow.
[Joel] [2]:[25] He will repay you for all of those years When your things were devoured by blight… By grasshoppers, caterpillars, and locusts, And by the great army that He sent against you.
[Joel] [2]:[26] ‘Then you will all eat and be filled, And you will praise the Name of your God… The One who sent you great wonders. And thereafter, His people won’t meet with disgrace Throughout the ages that follow.

[Joel] [2]:[28] ‘Then, in the last days, I will pour out my breath, And your sons and daughters will all prophesy, Your aged men will dream dreams, And young men in your midst will see visions.
[Joel] [2]:[29] ‘In those days, I will pour out my breath Upon My male and female attendants.
[Joel] [2]:[30] Miracles, I’ll bring to the skies, And fire, smoke and blood to the land.
[Joel] [2]:[31] ‘For the sun will then become dark, And the moon [will be changed] into blood, Before the great and apparent arrival, Of the Day of the Lord.
[Joel] [2]:[32] ‘Then, all who call on the name of the Lord Will be the ones who are saved,’ said [Jehovah]. ‘For, to Mount Zion and JeruSalem, Will come a person who saves, Announcing good news to all those Who have been called by the Lord.’

[Joel] [3]:[17] And you’ll know that I am [Jehovah] your God! ‘On Zion, My Holy Mountain, I’ll camp, And JeruSalem will be holy once more… The nations will not overrun her again.

[Joel] [3]:[21] Then I’ll avenge all the blood that I’ve not avenged, And the Lord will be camping on Zion.’
[Amos] [1]:[1] These are the words of Amos [which tell] of things that took place [while he was at] KiriAth JaiRim in Tekoa and of the things that he saw concerning JeruSalem in the days of UzziAh the king of Judah, and in the days of JeroBoam (son of JoAsh) the king of IsraEl, two years before the earthquake. [He said:]
[Amos] [1]:[2] ‘From Zion, [Jehovah] spoke out… From JeruSalem, He spoke and said this: ‘Over their pastures, the shepherds will mourn About the drought on [Mount] CarMel.’
[Amos] [1]:[3] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of these three godless deeds of Damascus (and even four), I won’t turn [My] attention away from them. For they used iron saws to saw open Those in GileAd with [babies] in their wombs.
[Amos] [1]:[4] ‘So, to the house of HazaEl, I’ll send fire And burn the foundations of the sons of Hadad. Damascus and those in On’s plains, I’ll destroy; I’ll cut the men of Edem to bits; And Assyria’s best men will be captured,’ says [Jehovah].
[Amos] [1]:[6] ‘Then [Jehovah] said: ‘For Gaza’s three godless deeds (and even four), I won’t turn [my] attention from them. For they captured Solomon’s captives, And handed them over to Edom.
[Amos] [1]:[7] ‘So, to Gaza’s walls, I’ll send fire, Which will eat her to her foundations.
[Amos] [1]:[8] I’ll also destroy those in AshDod; And from AshKelon I’ll remove a whole tribe. Then I’ll bring My hand against EkRon And destroy the remaining Philistines,’ says [Jehovah].
[Amos] [1]:[9] ‘And then [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of Tyre’s three godless deeds (and even four), I won’t turn [my] attention from them. For they handed captives to Edom… Forgetting their treaty of brothers.
[Amos] [1]:[10] So, to the walls of Tyre, I’ll send fire, Which will eat her to her foundations.’
[Amos] [1]:[11] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of Edom’s three godless deeds (and even four), I won’t turn [my] attention from them. For they chased their brothers with swords, And [cut down] the mothers throughout the land… They seized [the mothers] by force As proof of their awesome terror, And they continued to do this until they’d won.
[Amos] [1]:[12] So, I’ll send fire against TeMan Which will eat her to her foundations.’
[Amos] [1]:[13] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of the three godless deeds Of the sons of AmMon (and even four), I won’t turn [my] attention from them. For in GileAd they went and ripped open [Women] with [babies] in their wombs, Just to widen their borders.
[Amos] [1]:[14] ‘So I’ll light a fire upon RabBah’s walls, Which will eat her to her foundations. Then I’ll raise cries of war in that day… And they’ll shake in the day she’s consumed.
[Amos] [1]:[15] Into captivity, I’ll then send her king, Along with her rulers and priests,’ says [Jehovah].
[Amos] [2]:[1] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of MoAb’s three godless deeds (and even four), I won’t turn [my] attention from them. For, the king of Edom’s bones, they burned into dust.
[Amos] [2]:[2] ‘So, I’ll send fire upon MoAb, And it’ll devour their cities’ foundations. Then MoAb will be left without strength… She’ll hear cries and the blowing of trumpets.
[Amos] [2]:[3] I’ll destroy all her judges and rulers… Yes, I’ll kill them all,’ says [Jehovah].
[Amos] [2]:[4] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of the three [lawless] deeds Of the sons of Judah (and even four), I won’t turn [my] attention from them. For they pushed [aside all My] Laws, And refused to follow My orders. ‘So, I’ll cause them to wander And follow the foolish idols they’ve made, Which they’ve followed [since the time of] their fathers.
[Amos] [2]:[5] Then, I’ll send fire upon Judah, And wipe JeruSalem to her foundations.’
[Amos] [2]:[6] ‘And [Jehovah] said: ‘Because of IsraEl’s three godless deeds (and even four), I won’t turn [My] attention from them. For, from the righteous and needy They demanded silver for sandals…
[Amos] [2]:[7] [Things they need] to walk on the dust of the ground. ‘They also trampled the heads of the poor, And turned the humble away. Then, with the very same slaves, Fathers and sons both had sex, So that they could profane the Name of their God.
[Amos] [2]:[8] ‘Then, with their old clothes and rough cords, They erected booths next to My Altar, Where they drank the wine that they’d extorted There at the [Temple] of God!
[Amos] [2]:[9] ‘Yet for them, I had wiped out the Amorites, Even though they’d become as strong as the oaks And as tall as the cedars… I removed all the fruit from their boughs, As well as the roots underneath them.
[Amos] [2]:[10] ‘Then from the land of Egypt, I took them, And through the desert I led them During the next 40 years, So they could inherit the Amorites’ land.
[Amos] [2]:[11] ‘I also took their sons as [My] Prophets, And their young men to serve as My [Nazarites]. O Sons of IsraEl; Aren’t these the things that I did,’ asks [Jehovah]?
[Amos] [2]:[12] ‘But to those [Nazarites], you then offered wine, And you told the Prophets not to foretell!
[Amos] [2]:[13] So, because of this, I’ll roll over you Like a wagon loaded with stubble.
[Amos] [2]:[14] ‘Then all hope of flight into exile By those who can run, will be lost; For the strong won’t be able to maintain their strength, And no way will the soldiers save their own lives.
[Amos] [2]:[15] ‘Then you’ll find your bowmen unable to stand; Those fleet of foot won’t escape; Horseman won’t save their own lives;
[Amos] [2]:[16] The strong won’t have mighty hearts; And in that day, they’ll flee naked,’ says [Jehovah].
[Amos] [3]:[1] ‘O house of IsraEl, ‘Listen to these words of [Jehovah] That He’s pronouncing against you… To those tribes that He led out of Egypt. For, this is what He’s declared:
[Amos] [3]:[2] ‘I’ve known only you Among all the tribes of earth; And because of this (because of your sins), I’ll take vengeance upon you!’
[Amos] [3]:[3] ‘Can two walk together unless they’ve agreed? No!
[Amos] [3]:[4] ‘Will a lion roar from the woods If he hasn’t [caught] any game? No! ‘Will a cub call out from his lair If he hasn’t captured his prey? No!
[Amos] [3]:[5] ‘Will a bird fall to the ground If it hasn’t [been shot by] a hunter? No! ‘Will a snare snap shut without catching? No!
[Amos] [3]:[6] ‘Will the sound of the trumpet be heard in a town Without terrorizing its people? No! ‘Will harm ever come to a city Unless it’s been sent by [Jehovah]? No!
[Amos] [3]:[7] ‘There’s nothing that God [Jehovah] will do, Unless it’s revealed to His servants, the Prophets.
[Amos] [3]:[8] So as when a lion lets out a roar And all that hear it are fearful; When [Jehovah] God has something to say, What [Prophet] won’t prophesy?
[Amos] [3]:[9] ‘So, you must make this pronouncement To Assyria and those down in Egypt! Tell them to gather on Samaria’s hills, And as they gaze at her wonders, They should notice the tyranny within her.
[Amos] [3]:[10] Then, those who so treasure misery and injustice Will never see what’s coming,’ said [Jehovah].
[Amos] [3]:[11] ‘So [Jehovah], The God, sends them this message: ‘Tyre and all that’s around it Will soon become desolation. For, I’ll remove all their strength, And then rip their regions to pieces!
