[Jonah] [1]:[1] The Word of [Jehovah] came to Jonah (son of AmaThi), and said:
[Jonah] [1]:[2] ‘Get up and go to the great city of Nineveh and make this proclamation against it; for, cries of their evil have reached up to Me.’
[Jonah] [1]:[3] However, Jonah got up to flee from the face of [Jehovah] [all the way] to Tharsis! For he went down to JopPa and there he found a boat that was sailing to Tharsis... He paid his fare, boarded, and proceeded to sail with them to Tharsis, away from the face of [Jehovah].
[Jonah] [1]:[4] But then [Jehovah] raised a wind over the sea that created a huge swell, and the boat was in danger of breaking up!
[Jonah] [1]:[5] [Of course,] the sailors were so frightened that they each started crying out to their own gods, and they threw goods into the sea to lighten the ship. Yet Jonah had gone down into the ship’s hold and was asleep, snoring!
[Jonah] [1]:[6] So the ship’s captain went down to him and said: ‘Why are you [just lying there] snoring? Get up and call to your God so He will save us and we won’t be destroyed!’
[Jonah] [1]:[7] Well at that, each man started saying to his companion: ‘Come, let’s throw lots to find out why this evil has fallen on us!’ So they threw lots... And the lot fell to Jonah.
[Jonah] [1]:[8] So they asked him: ‘Tell us, what do you do for a living? Where did you come from? And what country and people are you from?’
[Jonah] [1]:[9] Then he told them: ‘I’m a servant of [Jehovah], I worship the Lord God of the heavens… the One who made the sea and the dry land.’
[Jonah] [1]:[10] Well at that, the men became very frightened. And they asked him: ‘What have you done?!’ Because the men knew that he was running away from [Jehovah], for he had explained [it] to them.
[Jonah] [1]:[11] Then, since the sea was moving and stirring up an even greater swell, they asked him: ‘So, what do we have to do to you, in order to calm the sea for us?’
[Jonah] [1]:[12] And Jonah told them: ‘Just pick me up and throw me into the sea… Then it’ll become calm for you. I know that these great swells have come upon you because of me.’
[Jonah] [1]:[13] [Nevertheless,] the men were really pushing themselves in trying to return to land… But they couldn’t – the sea was moving and rising up more against them.
[Jonah] [1]:[14] So they called out to [Jehovah] and said: ‘Please don’t let us die over this man’s life, and don’t hold the blood of the righteous against us! Because You, O Lord, have done what You wanted.’
[Jonah] [1]:[15] So they took Jonah and threw him into the sea… And the sea became still from its tossing about!
[Jonah] [1]:[16] As a result, the men became very frightened of [Jehovah], so they offered sacrifices to the Lord and made vows.
[Jonah] [1]:[17] Then [Jehovah] ordered a great sea creature to swallow Jonah, and he stayed in its belly for three days and three nights.
[Jonah] [2]:[1] Well, from from the belly of the sea creature, Jonah prayed to [Jehovah] his God,
[Jonah] [2]:[2] saying this: ‘In my affliction, I called out to You, O [Jehovah], my God, And You paid attention to me. I’ve called from the belly of the place of the dead, And from there, You listened to my voice!
[Jonah] [2]:[3] ‘You threw me into the heart of the sea… Into the depths [of its waters], By the currents, I was surrounded. All your surges and waves passed over me.
[Jonah] [2]:[4] ‘Then I said: ‘I have been pushed away from Your eyes… Will I ever gaze at Your Holy Temple again?
[Jonah] [2]:[5] ‘But the waters poured around me, And then, they reached my soul… By the deep, I was encircled, And my head went under the water, To the very foundations of the mountains.
[Jonah] [2]:[6] ‘Into the earth, I descended... Whose bars were eternal restraints. ‘[And I said:] ‘Let my life rise from corruption,’ O [Jehovah], my God.’
[Jonah] [2]:[7] ‘Then, as my life was failing within me, I remembered the Lord, For my prayer ascended to You… [Yes, it came] into Your Holy Temple!
[Jonah] [2]:[8] ‘Those who pay attention to vain things, And those who will listen to lies… They have abandoned their mercy.
[Jonah] [2]:[9] But, I’ll offer you [a] sacrifice, With [a] voice of praise and thanks! I’ll pay back everything I’ve vowed To you, the Lord of Salvation!’
[Jonah] [2]:[10] And at that, the Lord gave orders to the large sea creature, and it vomited Jonah out on dry land.
[Jonah] [3]:[1] Well thereafter, The Word of [Jehovah] came to Jonah a second time and said:
[Jonah] [3]:[2] ‘Now, you must get up and travel to the great city of Nineveh, and proclaim to it the message I told you before.’
[Jonah] [3]:[3] So Jonah got up and traveled to Nineveh, just as [Jehovah] had told him (for The God viewed Nineveh to be a great city), about [a] three-day road journey.
[Jonah] [3]:[4] Then when Jonah arrived at the city, he spent [a full] day traveling through it proclaiming: ‘In just three days, Nineveh will be destroyed!’
[Jonah] [3]:[5] Well, because the men of Nineveh believed in The God, they called for a fast, and then everyone (from their least to their greatest) put on sackcloth.
[Jonah] [3]:[6] And when [Jonah’s] words reached the king of Nineveh, he arose from his throne, removed all of his clothes and put on sackcloth, and then he sat in ashes.
[Jonah] [3]:[7] A proclamation was then sent throughout Nineveh by the king and his great men. It said: ‘The people, the cattle, the oxen, the sheep… They’re not allowed to eat, to graze, nor to drink water!
[Jonah] [3]:[8] ‘They must each wrap themselves and their cattle in sackcloth as they all fervently call out to God! Also, every man must turn from his wicked ways and from the sins of his hands and say:
[Jonah] [3]:[9] ‘Who knows if God will change His mind and turn from the anger of His rage, so that we’ll not perish?’
[Jonah] [3]:[10] Well, when The God saw what they were doing and that they’d turned from their wicked ways, He changed His mind about the evil that He said He’d do to them, and He didn’t do it.
[Jonah] [4]:[1] However, Jonah was very, very upset and confused by this...
[Jonah] [4]:[2] So he prayed to [Jehovah] and said: ‘O Lord, ‘Wasn’t this what I said [would happen] when I was back in my own land? ‘It was because of something like this that I thought about fleeing to Tharsis! For I knew that because You are kind, sympathetic, lenient, and full of mercy, You’d change Your mind about doing such evil!
[Jonah] [4]:[3] ‘So now, O Master and Lord, please take my life from me... For it’s better for me to die than to live!’
[Jonah] [4]:[4] And [Jehovah] asked Jonah: ‘Has this [really] grieved you that much?’
[Jonah] [4]:[5] Well after that, Jonah left the city and sat down in front of it… He built a shelter and sat in its shade, waiting to see what would happen to the city.
[Jonah] [4]:[6] Then [Jehovah] The God provided a gourd [plant] that grew up over Jonah’s head to shade him from his troubles. And Jonah became very happy over the gourd [plant] with great joy.
[Jonah] [4]:[7] But then, early the next morning, The God commanded a worm [to appear], and it attacked the [plant] and killed it, and [the plant] dried up.
[Jonah] [4]:[8] And just as the sun was rising, The God also commanded a scorching wind, and the sun beat down on Jonah’s head. He became so discouraged that he just wanted to resign from life. For he said: ‘It’s better for me to die than to live!’
[Jonah] [4]:[9] Then God asked Jonah: ‘Are you [really] that grieved over the gourd [plant]?’ And he replied: ‘Yes, I’m grieved to the point of death!’
[Jonah] [4]:[10] And [Jehovah] said: ‘You treated that plant so tenderly… Despite the fact that you didn’t work hard over it, didn’t nourish it, and even though it grew up in a single night and was gone in a single night!
[Jonah] [4]:[11] ‘So, shouldn’t I spare Nineveh, this great city, where more than 120,000 people live... [People] who haven’t known their right hands from their left, and many cattle?’
[Micah] [1]:[1] The Word of [Jehovah] came to MicAh the Morasthite in the days of JoTham, Ahaz, and HezekiAh (kings of Judah) and said this about the things he saw going on in Samaria and in JeruSalem:
[Micah] [1]:[2] ‘Hear these words, O you peoples; Also pay attention, you lands And those who are dwelling within you! For, from His Most Holy [Place], [Jehovah] will now testify.
[Micah] [1]:[3] '{Look!} [Jehovah] will come from His place And go down upon your high places, Then seat Himself in the heights.
[Micah] [1]:[4] ‘The mountains will shake underneath Him, And like beeswax in fire, the valleys will melt, Then flow like water that rolls down a slope.
[Micah] [1]:[5] ‘Yes, He will do all these things Because of Jacob’s irreverent ways And because of the sins of the house of IsraEl. [‘For God says:] ‘Isn’t Samaria the irreverence of Jacob And isn’t Judah’s sin, JeruSalem?
[Micah] [1]:[6] ‘So I’ll turn Samaria into a barn Where the fruits of the fields can be stored Along with the [grapes] of the vineyards. I’ll tear down her stones in great chaos, And her foundations, I’ll expose.
[Micah] [1]:[7] ‘I’ll cut her carved idols to pieces; Her temple whores, I’ll burn in a fire; And I’ll appoint her idols to extinction. For she hired whores and gathered them there… So the wages of whores are what I’ll destroy.
[Micah] [1]:[8] ‘For this, she’ll wail and beat on her breasts… She will go barefoot and naked… She’ll beat on her chest like a dragon, And mourn like chained demon’s daughters.
[Micah] [1]:[9] ‘This calamity upon her will surely arrive; For she went to Judah and JeruSalem And touched the gates of my people.’
[Micah] [1]:[10] ‘Now, those in Gath shouldn’t feel special, Nor should those who are living in BakaIm… And don’t laugh as you try to rebuild your homes, For the land will be strewn with your laughter,
[Micah] [1]:[11] And nothing good will come to your towns. ‘Then, those in ZaAnan will beat on their breasts On behalf of the houses next door… They’ll be grieved by the things that will happen to you.
[Micah] [1]:[12] ‘For then, who’ll console her when she is sad Over the bad things [Jehovah] will send, Which will reach all the way to JeruSalem’s gates?
[Micah] [1]:[13] ‘They’ll hear the sounds of chariots and riders [Attacking the City] of LachIsh. For, they’re the ones who have been taking the lead In the sins of the daughters of Zion… All of IsraEl’s godless deeds can be found there!
[Micah] [1]:[14] ‘Because of this, they’ll be carried away And become the inheritance of Gath… Yes, even their poorest of homes.
[Micah] [1]:[15] ‘There, IsraEl’s kings won’t be valued… The inheritance of Gath, they’ll become. The people of LachIsh will then be their [slaves]. And off to AdulLam, they’ll carry The glory of IsraEl’s daughters.
[Micah] [1]:[16] ‘So, shave [the heads of] your beloved young… Make them as bald as the vultures; For, they’ll all be carried away!’
[Micah] [2]:[1] ‘When they came here, they were looking for trouble And doing what’s bad in their beds. They did it all during the daytime, And they wouldn’t raise a hand to [Jehovah].
[Micah] [2]:[2] ‘Then, because they desired more fields, They plundered orphans and tyrannized homes… They plundered the people along with their homes… Both the men and the things they’d inherit.
[Micah] [2]:[3] ‘It’s because of this, that thus says [Jehovah]: '{Look!} Against their tribe, I’m bringing what’s bad, And thereafter, they won’t lift their necks Or in any way walk erect… Yes for them, it’ll be a very bad time!
[Micah] [2]:[4] ‘In that day, they’ll be saying these words… They’ll raise this lament in a song: ‘In our miserable condition, we knew misery; For our people were [led off in] lines, And no one [came here] to stop it Or to bargain for their return; So their fields were thereafter divided [as loot].’
[Micah] [2]:[5] ‘Now, no one will measure allotments For those in the Lord’s congregation.
[Micah] [2]:[6] You’ll weep and cry for these things; But I won’t remove all your scorn.
[Micah] [2]:[7] ‘Then, this is what they’ll say about you: ‘Because the house of Jacob provoked [Jehovah’s] spirit to rage, These are the things that He did; For His words and His ways are all straight and good!’
[Micah] [2]:[8] ‘[Throughout the years], my people have shown A hatred and resistance to peace. So they’ve flayed the skin [of those passing by], [And brought upon themselves] the conflict of war.
[Micah] [2]:[9] ‘Now the leaders of my people will be driven from their homes… They’ll be pushed away, because they’re so bad! So, flee to the mountains of the ages,
[Micah] [2]:[10] Since for you, there’ll be no rest, Because you’re corrupt and unclean!
[Micah] [2]:[11] ‘So you’ll run when no one is chasing, Because of your lying spirit, Which trickles upon you like the wine and strong drink That you’ve gained from the sweat of your people.
[Micah] [2]:[12] ‘But, after some time, they’ll return… I’ll gather Jacob along with the rest, And I’ll search for IsraEl’s remnants… I’ll collect them and I’ll return them Like sheep that have gone through hard times… They’ll jump away from those people, And in their own pastures, they’ll live as one flock.
[Micah] [2]:[13] ‘They’ll [run] through the breach that’s before them, For the gate will be cut so they can escape. And before them, will travel their king… Yes, they’ll be led by their Lord!’
[Micah] [3]:[1] [‘And God continues:] ‘So listen, you head ones of Jacob, And the rest that are left of IsraEl’s house! ‘When will you learn to do what’s fair?
[Micah] [3]:[2] Since you’ve hated what’s good and searched for what’s bad; They’ll reach out for you and tear off your skin, Then rip the flesh from your bones,
[Micah] [3]:[3] The same as you’ve eaten the flesh of my people And flayed off all of their skin… Then you broke their bones as flesh for the pot, And as meat for the cauldron!’
[Micah] [3]:[4] [Micah now explains:] ‘So, you’ll cry out to [Jehovah], But He won’t listen to you… He’ll just turn His face at that time, Because of the wicked things that you’ve done.

[Micah] [3]:[6] Because [you’ve told them] such things. ‘Then you’ll see no more visions during the nights… You’ll just see darkness (not light). For the sun won’t rise upon you prophets, And the days will darken before you.
[Micah] [3]:[7] ‘Disgrace will then come to those who dream dreams, And those telling the future will be ridiculed. About them, all will speak badly, And no one will listen to the things that they say.’

[Micah] [3]:[9] ‘Therefore, listen to this, O leaders of Jacob, And you remnants of the house of IsraEl… You who hate what’s fair and twist what’s straight…
[Micah] [3]:[10] You who have built Zion on blood And filled JeruSalem with injustice!
[Micah] [3]:[11] ‘For your leaders take bribes when they judge; Your priests require a wage for replies; And your prophets ask for silver when they prophesy. Yet they still rest upon [Jehovah] and say: ‘Isn’t [Jehovah] among us? No way will He bring bad things on us!’
[Micah] [3]:[12] ‘And it’s for all of these reasons That Zion will be plowed like a field... JeruSalem will become empty barns; And the Temple Mount, just a place in the woods!’
[Micah] [4]:[1] ‘But, in the last days, They will see the Mountain of [Jehovah] Sitting above the rest of the mountains, Raised higher than all of the hills, And to it, all the peoples will run.

[Micah] [4]:[3] Will serve as judge between peoples, And make decisions among distant tribes. ‘Then they’ll cut their swords into plows, And [they’ll beat] their spears into sickles. Nation won’t rise against nation again, Nor will they learn war anymore.

[Micah] [4]:[5] ‘And although other people may go their own way; You’ll walk in the Name of your God From the present and into the ages.
[Micah] [4]:[6] ‘And in that day, says [Jehovah], I’ll regather all those who were broken (The ones whom I had once discarded), And I’ll welcome back those whom I’ve pushed away.
[Micah] [4]:[7] ‘Yes, those who are broken, I’ll welcome, And I’ll make a great nation of them once again… Of those whom I once pushed away! And thereafter, and into the ages, Their Lord will rule from Mount Zion.’
[Micah] [4]:[8] [Micah then says:] ‘But now, upon you, O tower of the flock… Yes you, O JeruSalem’s daughter (You austere offspring of Zion); The foremost of Babylon’s kings Will come here and enter your [gates]!
[Micah] [4]:[9] ‘For, why did you learn to do such bad things… Wasn’t there a king here among you, And has all good council now perished? ‘So, pangs are what you’ll have to endure Like a woman who is about to give birth.

But your God, [Jehovah], will save you from there, And ransom you from your enemies’ hands.
[Micah] [4]:[11] ‘Now, many nations have come against you, And this is what they’re saying: ‘Our eyes will rejoice as we gaze on Zion!’
[Micah] [4]:[12] ‘But they don’t know the ways of [Jehovah], And His council, they don’t comprehend. For like sheaves [of grain], they’ll be gathered, And on a threshing floor, they’ll be piled,

[Micah] [5]:[4] ‘Yes, by the strength of [Jehovah], A shepherd will rise to [watch over] them, And they’ll bask in the glory of the Name of their God, Which will then become known to the ends of the earth.

[Micah] [5]:[10] ‘But [before] that day,’ says [Jehovah], ‘I’ll destroy all your horses and chariots…
[Micah] [5]:[11] All the cities in your land will wiped away, And I’ll remove all your forts.
[Micah] [5]:[12] ‘From your hands, I’ll wipe out your potions, And there’ll be no fortune tellers among you.
[Micah] [5]:[13] I’ll also destroy all the idols you’ve carved And remove the sacred pillars from your midst… You’ll [no longer] bow to the works of your hands.
[Micah] [5]:[14] ‘I’ll cut down all of your sacred poles And wipe away all of your cities.
[Micah] [5]:[15] Then, in My anger and rage, I’ll send My vengeance to the rest of the nations, Because they too failed to listen!’

[Micah] [7]:[19] ‘Please turn around and show pity on us, But, sink our unrighteous ways… Cast our sins into the depths of the seas.

[Nahum] [1]:[1] The concern over Nineveh. This is the scroll of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:
[Nahum] [1]:[2] ‘Because He’s very zealous, [Jehovah] won’t fail to punish. In His rage, [Jehovah] will punish All those who are standing against Him… He will destroy all those who oppose Him.
[Nahum] [1]:[3] ‘[Jehovah] is patient and mighty, And the [guilty], [He] won’t acquit. For His ways are rumbling and final.
[Nahum] [1]:[4] ‘There are clouds of dust under His feet, And He can squeeze the seas and cause them to dry. He also desolates rivers, Which is how He weakened BaShan and CarMel, And it’s why Lebanon’s blossoms have failed.
[Nahum] [1]:[5] ‘Before Him, the mountains have shaken, And [before Him], the hills have all trembled. They rise at His presence throughout the whole earth, As do all [the peoples] who dwell there.
[Nahum] [1]:[6] ‘Before His rage, who can stand… Yes, who can withstand His anger? For, sovereign rulers melt at His rage, And even the rocks split apart.
[Nahum] [1]:[7] ‘Yet He’s kind to those who [put faith] in Him In their day of affliction… And He knows all those who respect Him.
[Nahum] [1]:[8] ‘Like a downpour, He wipes away and consumes All those who have been roused [to oppose Him], And He chases His enemies into the dark.
[Nahum] [1]:[9] ‘So against [Jehovah], what plans can you make, For He can wipe you away. But He won’t punish you twice, Or punish you for the same [errors].
[Nahum] [1]:[10] ‘His enemy’s [cities], He will lay bare To their very foundations. Like twisted yews, they’ll be burned… As though they’re very dry stubble.
[Nahum] [1]:[11] ‘Yet, against [Jehovah], you’ve made plans… Against Him, you’ve made wicked plans.
[Nahum] [1]:[12] So [Jehovah] (who rules all the waters) says this: ‘I’ll send them away And they’ll not be heard from again.
[Nahum] [1]:[13] For I’ll lift their whips from [your backs], And I’ll remove all their shackles.’
[Nahum] [1]:[14] ‘It was concerning [the Assyrians], that [Jehovah] said this: ‘Your name won’t be mentioned again; For, I’ll destroy all your idols (Those which you molded and carved), Then a time will be set for your funeral, Which will arrive very soon!
[Nahum] [1]:[15] ‘Look! Upon the mountains, he’s coming… The feet of the one announcing good news And the one with reports about peace! ‘So in Judah, declare a holiday [feast], And you must get ready to pay all your vows, So that never again will they enter [your gates], Nor again, should they see your corruption.’
[Nahum] [2]:[1] ‘Now He’s finished [His work] and He’s consumed… This One who came and breathed in your face… This One who [brought] you affliction! ‘So, watch the roads and [wrap up] your loins… Be very manly and strong!
[Nahum] [2]:[2] For [Jehovah] has taken away The haughtiness of Jacob’s [tribes], As well as IsraEl’s insolent ways. ‘And now, He’s ready to shake off Those who have been shaking you, And He’ll bring their branches to ruin.
[Nahum] [2]:[3] For under Him, there are men who have weapons, And laugh at fire, because of their might. ‘Their chariots have now been prepared, And their horsemen will make many wail.
[Nahum] [2]:[4] Their chariots will wreak havoc along all the roads, And thereafter, they’ll meet in [Assyria’s] squares. ‘The sight of them is like burning lamps, And lightning [is found in their wake].
[Nahum] [2]:[5] ‘So all of [Assyria’s] mighty men Should stop and think about this… For in the daytime, they’ll flee. And as they leave, they’ll be feeble, Then between their walls, they’ll run From the troops in the lead that arrive.
[Nahum] [2]:[6] ‘Then their city gates will be opened wide, And all their great homes will be ruined…
[Nahum] [2]:[7] Yes, all their supports will lie bare. ‘Then their [women] will appear with their servants, And as meek as doves, they’ll be led away To the flutter of their own beating hearts.
[Nahum] [2]:[8] ‘For, Nineveh is a pool amidst waters, And her men won’t resist, they’ll just flee When no one is paying attention.
[Nahum] [2]:[9] ‘So their silver and gold will be looted… There are no limits to all that they’ll take. And those looters will then be weighed down With [the city’s] most desirable things.
[Nahum] [2]:[10] ‘There’ll be thrusting, shaking, and tumult… Hearts will be breaking and knees will be weak… Loins will all become loose, And their faces will look like burned pots!
[Nahum] [2]:[11] ‘So, where is this great lion’s den… Yes, where is the pasture [where she hides] her cubs… Where has the [great] lion gone? She’s gone away to be with her cubs Who ran when there was nothing to fear.
[Nahum] [2]:[12] ‘She is the same lion that once snatched away All that her cubs had required. And for her, the cubs strangled their prey, Until their den became filled with game… Their home was filled with the things she’d seized.
[Nahum] [2]:[13] [‘And God says:] ‘But look! I’m the One who is coming against you,’ '...says [Jehovah], the Almighty, ‘And all of your army, I’ll burn into smoke. ‘I’ll devour your lions with the broadsword, And I’ll take all the game from your land, So that none of the things you’ve accomplished Will ever be mentioned again.’
[Nahum] [3]:[1] ‘O you city of blood And of all that is false and unrighteous: ‘You’ll no longer be in charge of your game.
[Nahum] [3]:[2] For the sounds of whips, [you will hear], Along with the rumble of [chariot] wheels… The hot pursuits upon horses, And the dust that they’ll raise with their wheels…
[Nahum] [3]:[3] The attacks of men riding steeds… The shine of their swords and the flashing of shields. ‘Great multitudes will be slaughtered; For a downfall is coming to you. Unnumbered nations will come there, And from [looting and rape], they will tire.
[Nahum] [3]:[4] ‘You’re a whore who once satisfied men, And in the making of potions, you took the lead. Then you sold your whoring to the nations, And your potions, you sold to their tribes.
[Nahum] [3]:[5] ‘So look… I’m the One who is against you,’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty! ‘I will uncover your backside, And show all the nations your shame… Other kingdoms will see your dishonor!
[Nahum] [3]:[6] ‘Because of all your uncleanness, I’ll bring what’s disgusting upon you… I’ll use you as an example.
[Nahum] [3]:[7] ‘Then, all who see you will leave you and say: ‘O Nineveh, you great wretched one; Who will now mourn over you? And where can they search to send comfort?’
[Nahum] [3]:[8] ‘So, tune up the strings of your lyres, And prepare your potions for Amun ([Your god] who inhabits the rivers); For your walls are surrounded by water, From which you have ruled all the way to the sea.
[Nahum] [3]:[9] ‘Although Ethiopia and Egypt have served as your strength, They’ll [be no help] when you’re taken away… There’ll just be Libya and the Sudan That will come to your aid.
[Nahum] [3]:[10] ‘Your [people] will be captured and taken to exile, And your infant’s [heads] will be dashed on the walls. For your honorable things, they’ll cast lots, As your great men are tethered and bound.
[Nahum] [3]:[11] ‘So, you’ll be provoked and get drunk, As from your enemies, you seek shelter.
[Nahum] [3]:[12] But what will happen to those in your forts, Is the same as what will happen to you. ‘For, you will then be the fruit… And when they start shaking the [tree], You will fall into the mouths Of those who have come to consume you.
[Nahum] [3]:[13] '{Look!} Your enemies will view you as women, So they’ll burn the bars off your gates And open all doors throughout your land!
[Nahum] [3]:[14] ‘Then you’ll have to draw water from your rivers To rescue all of your burning forts! So, you should tread mortar and mix it with straw… Then make it stronger with bricks!
[Nahum] [3]:[15] For fire and the sword will destroy you… They will consume you like locusts, And by grasshoppers, you’ll be oppressed.
[Nahum] [3]:[16] ‘Although you once grew your trade higher Than all the stars in the skies; Grasshoppers are coming to spread [over you]…
[Nahum] [3]:[17] Small locusts will leap and consume, And cover your fences like frost. Then, as the sun rises, they’ll just hop away… And woe, because you won’t know where they’ve gone!
[Nahum] [3]:[18] ‘And you, O Assyria’s king; All of your shepherds have fallen asleep And all of your mighty are resting. Your people [have fled] to the mountains, And no one is searching for them.
[Nahum] [3]:[19] Thus there’ll be no one to heal your destruction, And your wounds will soon be inflamed. ‘Yet, those hearing this message about you Are all now clapping their hands… For to them, you have done evil things.’
[Habakkuk] [1]:[1] These are the things that Prophet Habakkuk saw:
[Habakkuk] [1]:[2] ‘How long, O Lord, must I cry out As You don’t listen [to me]? How long should I yell to You over wrong As You don’t bring us salvation?
[Habakkuk] [1]:[3] ‘Why have You shown toil and trouble to me, As you look upon misery and irreverence? Right opposite me, there’s judging going on… But it’s the judge that carries away!
[Habakkuk] [1]:[4] ‘Because of this, the Law has been shaken, And in the end, there’s no justice; For the godless are tyrannizing the righteous, And the justice they receive is perverted!’
[Habakkuk] [1]:[5] [Then the Lord replied]: ‘Look, O you who is speaking such words… Gaze and wonder at wonders, And thereafter, just pass away! For I’ll do a work in your day, Which you won’t believe and none can describe!
[Habakkuk] [1]:[6] '{Look!} I’ll awaken the Chaldean people, And they’ll travel across the breadth of the earth To inherit tents not their own.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[7] ‘[Their king] is known to be fearsome, And he [creates] his own kind of justice, For his only concern is himself.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[8] ‘His horses leap higher than leopards, And [their teeth] are like those of Arabian wolves. ‘His horsemen will make great advances… They’ll spread [their wings] out like eagles That are eager for something to eat.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[9] ‘Then, upon those who don’t show him respect, He will bring a consumption… It’ll come upon all who oppose him, And he’ll gather captives like sand.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[10] ‘Then among all their kings, he will revel… Their sovereignty will be things he plays with, And he will mock every fortress… He’ll build siege mounds around them and win!
[Habakkuk] [1]:[11] ‘But thereafter, his spirit will change; For, he will repent and then say, This power has come from my God!’
[Habakkuk] [1]:[12] [And Habakkuk replied:] ‘O [Jehovah], my God and most Holy One; You’re from the beginning! But, although there’s no reason for us to die, You’ve ordered up justice… For discipline and correction, You’ve shaped us.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[13] ‘If Your eyes are too pure to look at the bad, And You’ll not view any evil; Why do You endure those who hate You? ‘And why do You remain silent and watch As the impious are consuming the righteous?
[Habakkuk] [1]:[14] Will You let us be like the fish in the sea Or like things that crawl [on the ground] Where no one is taking the lead?
[Habakkuk] [1]:[15] ‘You’ve let [Babylon’s king] catch destruction… Yes, he pulled it up with a hook And lifted it up with his net… Then he brought it all in with his dragnet, And this is why he’s so joyful.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[16] ‘So to his dragnet, he’ll offer sacrifices, And to it, he will also burn incense. For by it, he’s fattened his portion, And provided himself the choicest of food.
[Habakkuk] [1]:[17] So he’ll keep on casting his net To destroy many nations, not spare them!’
[Habakkuk] [2]:[1] ‘[Now I’ve told You] that during my watch, I’ll be the one who stands guard… I’ll climb on the rocks and observe, Then listen to all that You’ll tell me, So I’ll know what I must say in reply When I’m receiving correction.’
[Habakkuk] [2]:[2] Then the [messenger of the] Lord told me this… He clearly said: ‘Now, you must write down this vision To elevate those who’ll read it.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[3] It’s a vision of a time in the future… It’s what will happen in the time of the end. ‘Be patient if it seems to be late; For it’ll surely arrive… No way will its coming be tardy.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[4] ‘To the depths of My core, I don’t find favor In one who would draw himself back. Yet, by their faith, the righteous will live!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[5] ‘But, those who are arrogant and filled with hate, And any man who is a braggart Will receive no [blessings] at all. ‘Now he’s widening his soul like the grave, And like death, he never gets filled.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[6] So, if he should assemble all nations And gather their peoples [under his rule]; Wouldn’t they say this against him… Wouldn’t they speak this riddle and say: ‘Woe to the one who takes what’s not his… How long [can he stand] all the pressure?
[Habakkuk] [2]:[7] For suddenly, there’ll come those who’ll bite him… Yes, those plotting against him will awaken And then they’ll saw him in two!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[8] ‘For, many nations, he’s ravaged. But those who remain, will soon ravage him Because of all the blood that he’s shed, And the things that he did to their cities and lands… What he did to all those who lived there.’
[Habakkuk] [2]:[9] ‘O you who have desired all their wealth; These same things will come upon you and your house… Yes, on you who have arranged your ‘nest’ in the heights, And whose hands have brought evil [to others].
[Habakkuk] [2]:[10] ‘For, you’ve shamed your own house! Since, throughout your life, you’ve sinned, And you’ve ended [the lives] of [many great] men.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[11] ‘Therefore, from your stone walls, I’ll yell, And the beetles in the woods will repeat it:
[Habakkuk] [2]:[12] ‘Woe to those who build their cities on blood, And [grow] their countries by doing what’s wrong!’
[Habakkuk] [2]:[13] ‘Yet, it’s by [Jehovah] the Almighty That so many have been tested by fire, And the nations have proven faint-hearted!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[14] ‘So, like the waters that cover the seas, The earth will soon become filled With the knowledge about all His glory.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[15] ‘But, you’ve forced your neighbors to drink Something intoxicating and cloudy In order to gaze on their private parts.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[16] ‘So drink deeply to the glory of your dishonor And get extremely excited! For thereafter, you’ll be completely surrounded Within the cup in [Jehovah’s] right hand, Where your glory will meet with dishonor.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[17] ‘By Lebanon’s irreverence, you’ll also be covered, And the misery of wild beasts will terrify you, Because of the blood of men that you’ve shed, And the badness within [your] cities and lands, Along with the [evil] of your people.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[18] ‘So, what good are the idols that they’ve carved, Or the molded castings they’ve shaped… The false things that they can see with their eyes? For your people rely on things that they’ve shaped… On idols that they’ve made, which can’t speak!
[Habakkuk] [2]:[19] ‘So, woe to those who say to the wood [idols]: ‘[It’s time for you to] awaken and rise!’ ‘And who say to things made of stone: ‘Become great!’ ‘For, they’re only things you can look at… Things that you’ve hammered from silver and gold, Which are still unable to breathe.
[Habakkuk] [2]:[20] ‘But, in His Temple, [Jehovah] is [alive]! So in every land, they should bow before Him!’
[Habakkuk] [3]:[1] The prayer of Prophet Habakkuk, in a song:
[Habakkuk] [3]:[2] ‘O Lord, ‘I heard Your report and I was afraid. ‘O [Jehovah], ‘I thought of your works and I trembled. ‘You stand between the two cherubs, And in coming years, all will know You… Yes, when that time arrives, You’ll be seen. ‘And when disturbance comes into my life, You’ll think of [me] and show mercy.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[3] For, God will come out of TeMan… Yes, from the shadow of Mount Paran, The Most Holy one will arrive.’ PAUSE ‘His virtues cover the skies And His praises fill the [whole] earth…
[Habakkuk] [3]:[4] Like all kinds of light is His brightness. ‘In His hands, He carries a trumpet; And by His might, He sends us His love.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[5] ‘So, from His face, a word will go forth, Which will travel from there to the plains;
[Habakkuk] [3]:[6] And where His feet stand, the [whole] earth will shake. ‘When He looks upon them, the nations dissolve… By [His] might, the mountains will break And the hills of the ages will melt.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[7] ‘On the tents of Ethiopian peoples, I saw distress about to arrive, And the tents of Media were also disturbed.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[8] ‘Were You provoked by their rivers, O Lord… Did their rivers make You so angry That against their sea, You took action? ‘O you who’re arriving on horses; As you ride, are you bringing salvation?
[Habakkuk] [3]:[9] No, [Jehovah] has told you to stretch out… Against their tents, you must stretch tight your bows!’ PAUSE ‘You’ll divide up their lands by their rivers,
[Habakkuk] [3]:[10] And when they see you, they’ll start having birth pangs; For they’ll know that the rivers will be their new borders. ‘Then the abyss will shout to the heights When it sees that you are arriving.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[11] For the sun will not rise in the sky, And the moon will fail and stand still. But, by the flash of your arrows And sparks from your weapons, they’ll move.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[12] ‘When [God] threatens, He’ll leave just few in their lands; For in His rage, He wipes nations away.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[13] But to His people, He’s bringing salvation, And He will save His anointed. ‘But to the heads of the lawless, He will send death… First, He’ll put chains on their necks, Which will shake and astonish the mighty, And then He will chop off their heads!’ PAUSE
[Habakkuk] [3]:[14] ‘Yes, He’ll split the heads of the mighty, After He makes them all shiver. So then they will put down their reins And look for places to hide… Where they will be fed like the poor.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[15] ‘For He’ll lead their horses into the sea, And there they will muddy its waters… Which will bring fear to all, when they see it.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[16] ‘On my lips, there was the sound of a prayer… Trembling entered my backside and bones… Yes, all of my ways were disturbed. But I will find rest in that day of distress… When I leave the people to whom I was sent.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[17] ‘For their fig trees won’t bear fruit anymore, And there will be no grapes on their vines. Their olives will also be gone, And there will be no crops in their fields. ‘At that time, there will be no more sheep, And there will be no oxen left in their barns.
[Habakkuk] [3]:[18] ‘But I’ll shout in joy to [Jehovah]… I’ll rejoice over my Savior, God!
[Habakkuk] [3]:[19] For [Jehovah] God is my strength, And He’s provided straight paths for my feet… Upon a high place, He has set me, And by His song, I will win!’
[Zephaniah] [1]:[1] The Word of [Jehovah] came to ZephaniAh (son of Cushi, grandson of GedaliAh, and great-grandson of AmariAh, son of HezekiAh) in the days of JosiAh (son of Amon) the king of Judah, and said:
[Zephaniah] [1]:[2] ‘When it comes to being in want, Let all on the face of the earth be in want,’ said the [messenger of the] Lord!
[Zephaniah] [1]:[3] ‘Let men and their cattle all be in want; Let things that fly in the sky be in want, As well as the fish in the seas. ‘May the irreverent all become ill Because of their lawless deeds; For, from the land, I’ll remove them,’ said the [messenger of the] Lord.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[4] ‘Then over Judah and JeruSalem I’ll stretch out my hand, And the name of the BaAl, I’ll remove from this place, Along with the names of his priests And the things dedicated [to him].
[Zephaniah] [1]:[5] ‘[I’ll remove] all those who bow on their roofs Before the [stars] in the skies, As well as those who bow low And swear their oaths by their masters, Or those who swear oaths by their king.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[6] For, they’ve all turned from [Jehovah], And they’re not seeking their Lord… [To Him], they haven’t stuck closely.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[7] ‘So be cautious before [Jehovah] [your] God, For the Day of the Lord is at hand! [Jehovah] has readied His [great] sacrifice, And made His Chosen One holy.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[8] ‘For the day of sacrifice will arrive When I’ll take vengeance upon all their rulers, As well as on the house of their king, And on those who wear foreign clothes.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[9] ‘When I take vengeance, you’ll see it; For, it’ll come to the gates in that day Of those filling the House of [Jehovah] With their treacherous, ungodly ways.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[10] ‘And in that day,’ said the [messenger of the] Lord, ‘There’ll come the sounds of cries from the gates… [The sounds] of people who are being stabbed through. And from the second quarter, the screams of the women, As the battles rage on in the hills.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[11] ‘So wail, all you who dwell in this place That soon will be cut to pieces. For [as happened] to the people of CanaAn; Those who carry silver will be slaughtered!
[Zephaniah] [1]:[12] ‘And in that day; I’ll search JeruSalem through with a lamp And take vengeance upon all the people Who have paid no attention to my orders, And on those who have said in their hearts: ‘[Jehovah] will do neither evil nor good!’
[Zephaniah] [1]:[13] ‘Then I’ll give them the power to ravage And ruin all of your houses. So, you’ll build homes in which you won’t live, And plant vineyards, from which you won’t drink the wine.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[14] ‘For the Day of the Lord has approached… Yes, it’ll come very soon! And the sounds of the Day of the Lord Are ordered to be bitter and harsh.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[15] ‘It’ll be a day of His rage; A day of distress and affliction; A day of misery and extinction; A day of dimness and darkness; A day of clouds and [thick] fog.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[16] ‘It’ll be a day when the trumpets are blown, And cries will arise from all your walled cities, As well as from your high towers.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[17] For, I’ll squeeze out the people, And then they’ll walk like the blind Because of their sins against [God]. ‘I’ll pour their blood out in the dust, And I’ll [pour] their flesh out like dung.
[Zephaniah] [1]:[18] Then their silver and gold won’t save them In the Day of the Rage of [Jehovah]. For the fire of His zeal will consume the whole land. ‘In a diligent way, He will bring it Upon all those who dwell in this land.’
[Zephaniah] [2]:[1] ‘So, gather and be bound together, You nation that can’t be taught,
[Zephaniah] [2]:[2] Before this day passes by like a blossom… Before [God’s] wrath has come upon you… Before the day of His anger and rage.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[3] ‘So, seek [Jehovah], you meek of the earth… Seek what’s righteous and fair! Give truthful answers to all, And tell them to hide in the Day of God’s wrath.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[4] ‘For, it’ll bring plundering to Gaza, And AshKelon will be wiped away. AshDod will fall at mid-day, And EkRon will soon be uprooted.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[5] ‘Woe to you in the lands by the sea… All you who have [moved there] from Crete. For the Word of [Jehovah] is coming against you (You Philistines within CanaAn’s land), And I’ll destroy all the places where you dwell.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[6] ‘[Your lands] will become pastures for flocks… They’ll be safe havens for sheep.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[7] And the lands of those who dwell by the sea Will be given to the remnants of Judah. ‘AshKelon’s homes will then become [pens] Where sheep will rest [in the heat of the day]. Then the sons of Judah, [Jehovah] will visit, And from captivity, return them.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[8] [‘For God says:] ‘For I’ve heard the scorning of MoAb And of their mistreatment by AmMon’s sons When they berated My people, And forced themselves over My borders.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[9] ‘Because of this, as I live; '...says IsraEl’s God, [Jehovah] of Armies, ‘MoAb will soon be like Sodom, And the sons of AmMon, like GomorRah. ‘Damascus will also come to its end And be heaps of salt throughout the age! They’ll be plundered by what remain of My people… They’ll be inherited by the remnant of My nation.’
[Zephaniah] [2]:[10] ‘This will happen because of their insolent ways… Because they berated [God’s people], And because they put themselves higher Than [Jehovah], the Almighty God.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[11] ‘Then before them, the Lord will appear To destroy the gods of those nations and countries, And thereafter, they’ll all bow before him… Each man within his own land And the gentiles that live in the islands.
[Zephaniah] [2]:[12] ‘Then, the Ethiopian peoples; I’ll put to death with my broadsword!
[Zephaniah] [2]:[13] And I’ll stretch out my hand towards the north, Then the Assyrians too, will be wiped away… I’ll turn Nineveh into a desert!
[Zephaniah] [2]:[14] ‘Flocks will then feed in her midst Beside the wild beasts of the land. Chameleons and hedgehogs will live in her fretwork, Wild beasts will roar in her ditches, And crows will nest in her gates. ‘But because she has been a tall cedar,
[Zephaniah] [2]:[15] This city that has paid no attention Will still have hope that she can survive. ‘For, she has said in her heart: ‘[Here] I am, and after me, there’ll be no others!’ ‘But soon, she won’t be anymore… She’ll be a place where wild beasts will dwell, And all that thereafter go through her Will whistle and just wring their hands.’
[Zephaniah] [3]:[1] ‘And you, O great city of [JeruSalem]… O my dove, whom I have repurchased;
[Zephaniah] [3]:[2] To His voice, you just wouldn’t listen, And you chose not to follow His orders… Upon [Jehovah], you wouldn’t rely… You refused to turn back to your God.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[3] ‘So your rulers are like roaring lions, And your judges are like Arabian wolves That leave nothing over ‘til morning.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[4] ‘Your prophets are all wanton liars [Whose words] are blown by the winds. And [God’s] Holy Things are profaned by your priests Who have no respect for His Laws.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[5] ‘But among you, [Jehovah’s] been righteous… No way has He been unjust… Each morning, He sends you justice and light. But, nothing is hidden from Him, And He doesn’t put up with injustice. ‘So the wicked will all come to shame,
[Zephaniah] [3]:[6] And He will tear down your proud, Then destroy all the places where they hide. ‘He’ll also wipe away all your roads, So that no one will pass through your cities. Then all of your towns will be wiped away… No one will dwell there, because they’ll be gone!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[7] [‘For God says:] ‘I told you to fear Me and do as I say, So I would not have to destroy you. But now, prepare for the vengeance That I will be bringing upon you. For, I will rise early and reap, And even your gleanings, I’ll ruin, said [Jehovah].
[Zephaniah] [3]:[8] ‘Then, upon the gathering of nations, I will thereafter pass judgment, And I’ll pour out My rage on their kings… Yes, all of My anger and rage And the fire of My zeal will consume them.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[9] ‘Then, to that generation, I’ll bring just one language So that all can call on the name of the Lord And serve him under one yoke.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[10] ‘From the ends of Ethiopia’s rivers I’ll welcome back those who were scattered, And to Me, they’ll bring sacrifices.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[11] ‘In that Day, you won’t be disgraced By the disrespect that you’ve shown Me. For I’ll remove your insolent ways And the careless attitudes that you’ve shown… Then about My Holy Mountain, you’ll boast once again.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[12] ‘But among you, I’ll leave the humble and meek (Those who respect the name of the Lord).
[Zephaniah] [3]:[13] And this remnant of IsraEl will not be unrighteous… Of vain things, they will not speak, And no way will their tongues then deceive. Then they will eat as they lie in their beds, And no one will make them afraid.’
[Zephaniah] [3]:[14] [And the messenger of the Lord continues:] ‘So rejoice, O daughter of Zion… O JeruSalem’s daughter, shout loudly… Whole-heartedly [cry out in] joy… JeruSalem’s daughter, yell in delight!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[15] For [Jehovah] has removed your offenses And ransomed you from your enemy’s hands. For IsraEl’s King, [Jehovah], is with you, So you’ll no longer see any evil!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[16] ‘To JeruSalem, I’ll say at that time: ‘Be courageous, O Zion, And don’t let your hands become weak!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[17] For [Jehovah] your God is among you… The Almighty has brought you salvation!’ ‘Then, He will spread gladness among you, And because He cares, He’ll revive you. He will be as glad and delighted with you As He was in the days of your holiday feasts.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[18] ‘Then I’ll gather back those who are broken, And bring woe upon any that scorn you!
[Zephaniah] [3]:[19] {Look!} In that time, I will act on your behalf… I will save all those who were pressured, And I’ll welcome back those whom I once pushed away. Then I’ll make them [a people] of boasting and fame In every place throughout the whole earth.
[Zephaniah] [3]:[20] ‘At that time, your enemies will all be disgraced And I’ll do whatever you think to be good; Because, in that time, I’ll accept you… I’ll make you famous and reasons to boast Before the rest of the nations on earth. For in front of their eyes, I’ll return you From the places where they once held you captive,’ '...said [Jehovah].’
[Haggai] [1]:[1] In the 2nd year [of the reign] of King Darius, in the 6th month and on the 1st day of the month, The Word of [Jehovah] came by the hand of HagGai the prophet and said: ‘Speak to ZerubBabel son of ShealtiEl from the tribe of Judah and to JoShua (son of JoZadek) the High Priest, and tell them
[Haggai] [1]:[2] that [Jehovah] the Almighty says this: ‘These people say that the time isn’t right To rebuild the Temple of [Jehovah].’
[Haggai] [1]:[3] Then the Word of [Jehovah] went on to say this through the hands of HagGai the prophet:
[Haggai] [1]:[4] [‘For God says:] ‘Is it, indeed, the right time For you men to live in nice houses, While this Temple is lying in ruins?
[Haggai] [1]:[5] ‘And now,’ says [Jehovah] the Almighty, ‘Arrange your hearts for the ways you must go!
[Haggai] [1]:[6] For you plant a lot, but you don’t harvest much; You eat, but not ‘til you’re full; You drink, but not ‘til you’re drunk; You wear clothes that don’t keep you warm; And those to whom you’ve paid wages Keep them in bags full of holes.’
[Haggai] [1]:[7] ‘So, thus says [Jehovah] the Almighty: ‘Get your hearts ready to travel,
[Haggai] [1]:[8] And go to the mountains to cut the wood With which you’ll rebuild My Temple. For, if you choose to do this, I’ll think well of you, Because that would glorify Me,’ says [Jehovah].
[Haggai] [1]:[9] ‘Now you look for much [but find] little, And after you carry it home, I just blow it away. This happens, says [Jehovah] the Almighty, Because you’ve abandoned My Temple While you each [repair] your own homes.
[Haggai] [1]:[10] So the sky is withholding its dew, And the ground is withholding its blessings.
[Haggai] [1]:[11] ‘Therefore, to your land and its mountains; Also, to your oil and your grain, And to the ground that brings wine to men, I will be sending the sword! I’ll also send the sword to your cattle, And [to the things that you make with] your hands.’
[Haggai] [1]:[12] Well, ZerubBabel (son of ShealtiEl) from the tribe of Judah, and JoShua (son of JoZadek) the High Priest (as well as all the rest of the people) listened to the voice of [Jehovah] their God and to the words of HagGai the prophet – to all [the words] that [Jehovah] their God had sent to them – and the people became fearful before [Jehovah].
[Haggai] [1]:[13] Then HagGai, one of the messengers of [Jehovah], told the people this: ‘[Jehovah] says: ‘I am with you!’
[Haggai] [1]:[14] So after that, [Jehovah] awakened the spirit of ZerubBabel (son of ShealtiEl) from the tribe of Judah, the spirit of JoShua (son of JoZadek) the High Priest, and the spirits of the rest of the people, and they went to work on the Temple of their God [Jehovah] the Almighty!
[Haggai] [1]:[15] They started [the project] on the 24th day of the 6th month in the 2nd year [of the reign] of King Darius.
[Haggai] [2]:[1] Then on the 21st day of the 7th month, the Word of [Jehovah] came again by the hand of HagGai the prophet. He said:
[Haggai] [2]:[2] ‘Speak to ZerubBabel (son of ShealtiEl) of the tribe of Judah, and to JoShua the High Priest (son of JoZadek), and to all the rest who are left there, and ask them this [from [Jehovah]]:
[Haggai] [2]:[3] ‘Who among you had seen this Temple In [the days of] its glory? Do you see what it has become… It no longer exists here before you!
[Haggai] [2]:[4] ‘So ZerubBabel, you must be strong,’ says [Jehovah]; And High Priest JoShua, you must be strong… And you people of the land must also be strong; For, if you choose to [obey Me], I will be there with you,’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty.
[Haggai] [2]:[5] ‘This is the same thing that I said to [your fathers] When they were fleeing from Egypt… And then, I sent them my breath. So now, you must also show courage!’
[Haggai] [2]:[6] ‘For, thus says [Jehovah] the Almighty: ‘Once again, I will shake the lands and the skies, As well as the seas and dry ground.
[Haggai] [2]:[7] I will also shake all the nations, And My chosen ones will return… Then I’ll fill this Temple with glory!’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty.
[Haggai] [2]:[8] ‘For, all the silver is Mine, And all the gold is Mine also...’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty.
[Haggai] [2]:[9] ‘So the glory of this Temple will be greater… The last will be greater than the first!’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty. ‘And to this place, I’ll bring peace...’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty… ‘Peace that will save all the lives Of those who rebuild this Temple.’
[Haggai] [2]:[10] Then it was on the 24th day of the 9th month in the 2nd year of Darius that these words came from the [messenger of the] Lord to HagGai the prophet. He told them that
[Haggai] [2]:[11] [Jehovah] the Almighty said this: ‘Ask the Priests [this question] concerning the Law:
[Haggai] [2]:[12] ‘If a man should touch holy meat With just the edge of his clothes, And the edge of his clothes should thereafter touch Bread, stew, wine, or olive oil (Or any other such food); Would it make those things holy?’ And all the Priests replied: ‘No!’
[Haggai] [2]:[13] Then HagGai asked: ‘But, if they should touch a dead person, Would any of these things still be clean?’ And the Priests replied: ‘[No, they’d] be defiled!’
[Haggai] [2]:[14] Then HagGai told them that this is what [Jehovah] said: ‘So it will be of these people (Of this nation that stands here before Me And of the works of their hands)… Those who come here will all be defiled If they’re more concerned about their own [homes]! ‘Such ones should rather be grieving About the wicked things that they have done; For they have hated [the prophets] That scolded them at their gates.
[Haggai] [2]:[15] ‘So, take [these words] to your hearts from this day Before laying stone upon stone To [rebuild] the Temple of [Jehovah]:
[Haggai] [2]:[16] ‘Remember when you went to your stores To get 20 measures of barley And found there were only 10 measures? Or, when you went to the wine vat To draw 50 measures [of wine] And found there were just 20 measures?
[Haggai] [2]:[17] ‘Well, I am the One who had struck you With this lack of production… [I am the One who struck] the works of your hands And sent hail and strong wind upon you, Because you refused to turn back to Me, says [Jehovah].
[Haggai] [2]:[18] ‘So, keep this in your hearts from this day… From the 24th day and 9th month… From the day the Temple’s foundation was laid… Yes, store it deep in your hearts!
[Haggai] [2]:[19] ‘Will the threshing-floor still [be empty]? No! And will the grapevines, fig trees, pomegranates, or olives Fail to put out their fruit? No! Because, from this day, I will bless them!’
[Haggai] [2]:[20] Then the Word of the [Jehovah] came to HagGai the prophet a second time [that day] (on the 24th day of the month), and he said:
[Haggai] [2]:[21] ‘Speak to ZerubBabel (son of ShealtiEl) of the tribe of Judah, and this is what you must tell him: ‘I will shake the ground and the sky, As well as the sea and dry land.
[Haggai] [2]:[22] Then I will wipe away the thrones of the kings And I will destroy all the power Of the nations [that are living around you]! ‘Their chariots and horsemen will be wiped away… Their horses and horsemen will fall, And they’ll each turn their swords on their brothers.
[Haggai] [2]:[23] ‘O ZerubBabel, ‘On this day, I’ve chosen you as My servant,’ '...says the Almighty [Jehovah]. ‘I’ve established you as a seal, For you’re the one whom I’ve chosen.’ '...says the Almighty [Jehovah].’
[Zechariah] [1]:[1] It was in the 8th month in the 2nd year [of the reign] of Darius that the Word of [Jehovah] came to ZechariAh (son of BarachiAh and grandson of IdDo) the prophet and said:
[Zechariah] [1]:[2] ‘[Jehovah] was provoked by your fathers And [driven] into great rage;
[Zechariah] [1]:[3] So, tell them that [Jehovah] of Armies now says: ‘Return to Me’, says [Jehovah] of Armies, ‘And then, I’ll turn back to you!
[Zechariah] [1]:[4] ‘Don’t be like your fathers Whom the prophets accused. For they came beforehand and warned them… They said that [Jehovah] of Armies Had warned them to turn from their wicked ways And from the bad things they were doing. But they just paid no attention, And chose not to listen to Me,’ says [Jehovah].
[Zechariah] [1]:[5] ‘Now, where are your fathers and where are those prophets… Have they lived into this age?
[Zechariah] [1]:[6] ‘You have My words and My Laws; Yes, all that I sent by my breath Through My servants the prophets… Those whom were seized by your fathers. ‘For [your fathers] gave this reply to [the prophets]: ‘Whatever [Jehovah] of Armies had planned Because of our sins and our evil ways Has already been fulfilled upon us!’
[Zechariah] [1]:[7] Well, it was on the 24th day of the 11th month (the month of Shebat), in the 2nd year [of the reign] of Darius, that the Word of [Jehovah] came to me (ZechariAh the prophet, son of BarachiAh and grandson of IdDo).
[Zechariah] [1]:[8] For during the night, I looked up and saw a man who was riding a red horse. He was standing in the shade between the mountains, and behind him were red horses with white spots.
[Zechariah] [1]:[9] So I asked: ‘What is this, O Lord?’ And [God’s] messenger (the person who was speaking to me) replied: ‘I’ll show you what all these things mean.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[10] Then the man who was standing between the mountains spoke to me and said: ‘These [men] were sent by [Jehovah] To travel throughout the whole land.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[11] And thereafter, the men who were standing between the mountains said to the messenger of [Jehovah]: ‘We’ve finished our travels throughout the whole land, And Look! It’s all tranquil and filled.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[12] So the messenger of [Jehovah] said this: ‘O [Jehovah] of Armies, ‘How long will you fail to show mercy On JeruSalem and the cities of Judah? For, this is the 70th year of Your rage.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[13] And [Jehovah] replied to the messenger: ‘You, the one who is speaking for Me, Must send him good words that bring comfort.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[14] So then the messenger spoke to me and told me that I should start shouting [in joy], because [Jehovah] the Almighty had said this: ‘I have a great zeal for JeruSalem… Over Zion, I’m very zealous!
[Zechariah] [1]:[15] And I’ve been provoked by the nations, Because they had joined to attack you. ‘But, although you people provoked Me, They planned their attack for bad [reasons].
[Zechariah] [1]:[16] And because of this,’ said [Jehovah], ‘On JeruSalem, I’ll show mercy, And My Temple will soon be rebuilt there.’ Then [Jehovah] added: ‘So, I’m stretching a line over JeruSalem.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[17] ‘[And the messenger said]: ‘Therefore, shout aloud [in joy] once again! For [Jehovah] of Armies said this: ‘To your cities, I’ll be sending good things; For, I’ll show mercy on Zion, Since JeruSalem is the place that I chose!’
[Zechariah] [1]:[18] Then, when I raised my eyes and looked, I saw four trumpets...
[Zechariah] [1]:[19] So I asked the messenger (the one who was speaking to me): ‘What are these, O Lord?’ And he replied: ‘These are the trumpets… The ones who brought scattering to Judah, As well as to IsraEl and JeruSalem.’
[Zechariah] [1]:[20] Then the Lord [messenger] showed me four workers.
[Zechariah] [1]:[21] So I asked him: ‘What have these come to do?’ And he replied to Me, saying: ‘They’ve come to cut down the trumpets That brought scattering [to the people of] Judah, And so much destruction upon IsraEl That those who lived there could not raise their heads… They’re the horns that the nations had raised To scatter the land of [Jehovah].’
[Zechariah] [2]:[1] Then I raised My eyes and I saw a man... And in his hand was the string of a surveyor.
[Zechariah] [2]:[2] So I asked him: ‘Where are you going?’ And he said: ‘I’m going to measure JeruSalem… To determine its length and its width.’
[Zechariah] [2]:[3] Well at that, {Look!} the messenger who was speaking to me stopped, and another of [God’s] messengers came to meet him,
[Zechariah] [2]:[4] and said: ‘Tell him that JeruSalem Will be lived in again… Within her, there’ll be crowds of cattle and men.
[Zechariah] [2]:[5] ‘And [tell him] that [Jehovah] says this: ‘I’ll be a wall of fire to surround her As well as the glory within her.
[Zechariah] [2]:[6] ‘So now, flee from the land in the north, says [Jehovah]; For I’ll gather you from the four winds,
[Zechariah] [2]:[7] And those who dwell among Babylon’s daughters Must get up and run back to Zion.’
[Zechariah] [2]:[8] Then [the messenger said]: ‘I was sent to the nations by [Jehovah], In order to establish your glory Among the people who sacked you. ‘For, those who have dared to touch you Have touched the pupil of my eye.
[Zechariah] [2]:[9] So {Look!} against them, I’ll now raise my hand, And they will then be the spoils Of those who had once been their slaves… And then you’ll know I was sent By [Jehovah] the Almighty.
[Zechariah] [2]:[10] ‘So be glad and rejoice, O daughter of Zion; For I’ll return and camp in your midst.
[Zechariah] [2]:[11] Then, many nations will come seeking refuge Among [Jehovah] and His people… For, I’ll be there in your midst, And you’ll know that [Jehovah] the Almighty Was the [One] who sent me to you.
[Zechariah] [2]:[12] ‘Yes, Judah will be His inheritance again (His portion in His holy land), And JeruSalem is His chosen city, once more.
[Zechariah] [2]:[13] So to [Jehovah], all flesh must now bow; For, from His holy cloud, He’s awakened.’
[Zechariah] [3]:[1] Then the Lord [messenger] showed me JoShua [Greek: Ιησούν, Jesus] the High Priest. And standing before him was the messenger of [Jehovah]… But the Slanderer was also there, standing to his right in order to serve as his opponent.
[Zechariah] [3]:[2] Then [the messenger] of [Jehovah] said to the Slanderer: ‘O Slanderer, ‘May [Jehovah] send His reproach upon you… May the Lord who chose JeruSalem Speak condemnation against you! For, doesn’t [JoShua now look like] an ember That has been snatched from the fire?’
[Zechariah] [3]:[3] Well, [I noticed that] JoShua was wearing filthy clothes as he was standing there in front of [God’s] messenger.
[Zechariah] [3]:[4] So the messenger said to those who were standing before him: ‘Now, remove all of his filthy clothes!’ Then he said: '{Look!} And after you’ve removed all of these dirty things; In a full-length robe, you must dress him!’
[Zechariah] [3]:[5] Then he said: ‘Dress him in the [robes of a Priest], And on his head, you must place a clean turban!’ So they dressed him in the official [garments], placed a clean turban on his head, and wrapped the [official] robe around him.
[Zechariah] [3]:[6] And thereafter, the messenger of [Jehovah] stood there and testified to JoShua saying:
[Zechariah] [3]:[7] ‘Thus says [Jehovah] the Almighty: ‘If you will walk in My ways And keep strict watch on My orders, I’ll [assign you to be over] My [Temple] And to keep watch on My courtyard. Then I’ll give you [guards] that will pace Between other [guards] that stand still.
[Zechariah] [3]:[8] ‘O High Priest JoShua, listen to this… Yes, you and your neighbors that are sitting before you! For these men [will serve as] observers of signs… They’ll be witnesses that I gave to My servant Something that will raise his position!
[Zechariah] [3]:[9] For I’ll place a stone before JoShua’s face, And on this stone, there’ll be seven eyes. '{Look!} Then upon it, I’ll engrave an inscription,’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty, ‘It will say that I’ll [wipe out] injustice… In a day, I’ll wipe injustice away In all places throughout the whole land.
[Zechariah] [3]:[10] ‘And then, in that day, says [Jehovah]; They will each call to their neighbors and brothers From under their own grapevines and fig trees.’
[Zechariah] [4]:[1] Then the messenger who was speaking to me returned and woke me up in the same way that you’d wake up a man who was sleeping.
[Zechariah] [4]:[2] Then he asked me: ‘Now, what do you see?’ Well when I looked, I saw a gold lampstand and a bowl of oil… There were seven lamps on [the stand] and seven oil funnels for the seven lamps.
[Zechariah] [4]:[3] There were also two olive trees… One was on the right of its bowl, and the other was on its left side.

[Zechariah] [4]:[5] And the messenger that had been speaking to me replied: ‘Don’t you know what all these things mean?’ And I answered: ‘No, O my Lord.’
[Zechariah] [4]:[6] Then he told me this: ‘They’re the words of [Jehovah] to ZerubBabel; For, you must say this to him: ‘Not by strength or great power, But just by My breath,’ '...says [Jehovah] the Almighty.
[Zechariah] [4]:[7] ‘So, who are you, O great mountain, To stand before ZerubBabel’s face? For, you’ll become just a plain Before My inherited rock Upon whom I’ll show My favor and care.’

[Zechariah] [4]:[12] And I asked him again: ‘What [is the meaning of] the two branches of the trees that are around the gold handles that are used to do pouring… And the gold funnels?’

[Zechariah] [4]:[14] And he said: ‘These are two sons of the oil [or ‘fat,’ possibly meaning ones anointed with oil], Who’ll stand beside the Lord of the earth.’
[Zechariah] [5]:[1] Then I turned and raised my eyes and saw what looked like a flying sickle.
[Zechariah] [5]:[2] And he asked me: ‘What do you see now?’ And I replied: ‘I see a flying sickle… It’s 20 forearms long and 10 forearms wide!’
[Zechariah] [5]:[3] Then he said: ‘This is the curse… The one that will go ‘cross the face of the earth. One side brings death to all thieves, And the other, to those who would lie in a trial.
[Zechariah] [5]:[4] ‘For [Jehovah] the Almighty says this: ‘I will [soon] send it forth… I’ll send it to the thieves who would enter My House And to those who swear false oaths in My Name. It will come and enter their houses, And then it will wipe them away, Along with their woodwork and stones.’

[Zechariah] [5]:[7] Look… I have a measure of lead. And look… There’s a woman inside of [that basket]!’
[Zechariah] [5]:[8] Then he said: ‘This [lead] is their lawless ways!’ And at that, he threw [the lead] at the basket, and it fell into the woman’s mouth.
[Zechariah] [5]:[9] Then I raised my eyes and I saw two more women coming. Both had wings that were like those of a hoopoe bird, and [their wings] thereafter became filled with the wind. Then they picked up the basket and lifted it between the land and the sky.

[Zechariah] [5]:[11] And he replied: ‘To the land of Babylon, they’ll take it, In which there [will be] a house, That they’ve prepared for it there.’

[Zechariah] [6]:[2] The 1st chariot [that I saw] was pulled by red horses, The 2nd was pulled by black horses,
[Zechariah] [6]:[3] The 3rd was pulled by white horses, and The 4th was pulled by horses that were spotted dapple gray.
[Zechariah] [6]:[4] So I spoke to the messenger and asked him (this one who was speaking to me): ‘What are these, O my Lord?’
[Zechariah] [6]:[5] And the messenger that was speaking to me replied: ‘These are the four winds of the heavens, And they’ll stand next to the Lord of the earth...
[Zechariah] [6]:[6] ‘The black ones will go to the land of the north; The white ones will follow behind them; And the spotted are going to the land of the south.’

[Zechariah] [6]:[8] Then he yelled out to me and said: ‘Look! The ones that are going to the land of the north Have brought rest to My rage in the north.’
[Zechariah] [6]:[9] Then the Word [messenger] of [Jehovah] came to me and said:
[Zechariah] [6]:[10] ‘Take [silver and gold] from the rulers, As well as from those who are wealthy, And from those who have greater knowledge! [You’ll find them] in the house of JosiAh (son of ZephaniAh), Who has just returned from Babylon.
[Zechariah] [6]:[11] ‘Then, with the silver and gold, make a crown, And place it upon JoShua’s head (The son of JoZadek, the High Priest).
[Zechariah] [6]:[12] And tell him that thus says [Jehovah]: '{Look!} There’s a male whose name is The Sprout, And he will grow from below To rebuild the Temple of [Jehovah].
[Zechariah] [6]:[13] ‘Then, he will receive all the greatness he needs To sit and rule from his throne. For there’ll be a Priest on [God’s throne], And there’ll be peace and purpose between [those two roles].’

[Zechariah] [6]:[15] ‘And thereafter, from far-away places, will come Those who’ll rebuild the Temple of [God]. Then you’ll know that I had been sent By [Jehovah] the Almighty. And all who hear this will [wish] That they’d paid closer attention To the voice of [Jehovah] their God.’
