[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[1] During King JehoIakim of Judah’s 3rd year, King NebuChadnezzar of Babylon came to JeruSalem and laid siege to it.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[2] Well, [Jehovah] let him capture it, as well as King JehoIakim of Judea, and also some of the Lord’s sacred objects from the temple, which he hauled off to Babylon and placed in his own god’s shrine in the land of Shinar. [2 Chronicles 36:5-7]
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[3] Then King NebuChadnezzar ordered his head eunuch, AbiEsdri, to recruit young men from IsraEl’s leading families, the royal bloodline, the top-tier candidates.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[4] He wanted young men who were: Without any flaws, Good-looking, Knowledgeable in all wisdom, Literate, Sharp-minded, Wise enough to serve in the king’s palace. They’d get [a] crash-course in Babylonian language and literature.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[5] The king’s household would cover their daily expenses, including meals from the king’s own food and wine. This training program would last three years, after which they’d stand before the king for evaluation.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[6] Among those chosen from Judah’s royal IsraElite families were: DaniEl, HananiAh, MishaEl, AzariAh.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[7] The chief eunuch gave them new Babylonian names: DaniEl became BelTeshazzar, HananiAh became Sedrach, MishaEl became Misach, AzariAh became AbedNego.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[8] But DaniEl thought about this and decided that he wouldn’t become ritually unclean by eating the king’s food or drinking his wine. So, he boldly asked the chief eunuch to exempt him so that he wouldn’t be defiled in this way.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[9] So [Jehovah] made the chief eunuch respect and favor DaniEl.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[10] However, the chief eunuch warned DaniEl: ‘I’m anxiously aware that my lord the king has decided what you’ll eat and drink. If he sees you looking worse than the other young men – those foreigners you’re training with – I’ll be risking my own neck!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[11] But DaniEl pressed AbiEsdri – the chief eunuch assigned to manage DaniEl, HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh – saying:
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[12] ‘Here’s [an] idea: Put us to the test for ten days. Just give us lentils from the ground to eat and water to drink.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[13] ‘If our faces start looking drawn compared to the other young men eating the king’s food, then do whatever you want with us!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[14] So he agreed to their plan and put them to the test for ten days.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[15] Well, ten days later, their complexions looked healthier and their bodies were in better shape than all the other young men eating the king’s food!
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[16] So AbiEsdri continued to take away their royal meals and wine, substituting them with lentils.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[17] The Lord gave these young men: Knowledge Insight Wisdom...in all kinds of learning. But to DaniEl, he gave special gifts: Understanding every vision Interpreting dreams Excelling in all wisdom
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[18] After this time, the king ordered their presentation, so the chief eunuch brought DaniEl, HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh before King NebuChadnezzar.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[19] The king spoke with them, and none of the wise men could compare to DaniEl, HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh! So they stayed on as advisors to the king.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[20] Whenever the king tested them on wisdom, insight, or education, they proved ten times smarter than all the magicians and philosophers in his empire! So [eventually] the king: Honored them Made them governors Promoted them as top advisors They became known as the wisest men for handling affairs across his entire kingdom.
[Daniel (Greek)] [1]:[21] DaniEl kept his position right up until King Cyrus of Persia’s first year.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[1] In the second year of King NebuChadnezzar’s reign [over Judah], he started having visions and dreams that disturbed him. Then his sleep left him entirely.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[2] So the king ordered his officials to bring in the enchanters, magicians, sorcerers of the Babylonians to explain his dreams. Then they came and stood before the king.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[3] The king told them: ‘I had [a] dream that’s left me deeply disturbed... So I want to understand what it means.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[4] Then the Babylonians replied to the king (in Aramaic), saying: ‘Lord King, may you live forever! Please tell your servants the dream, and we’ll explain its meaning.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[5] But the king snapped back: ‘I’ve said what I want! If you don’t tell me both the dream and its true meaning, you’ll be made [an] example of – and your houses will be seized for the royal treasury!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[6] ‘But if you explain the dream and its meaning, you’ll receive all kinds of gifts and be honored by me. Now tell me the dream – and interpret it!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[7] They answered again: ‘Your Majesty, first tell us the dream – then your servants will explain its meaning.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[8] But the king snapped back: ‘I know what you’re doing – you’re just trying to buy time! You’ve discerned that I can’t remember the dream! Well, my decree still stands...
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[9] ‘If you don’t tell me the truth and the don’t give me the interpretation, you’ll be executed! ‘You’ve clearly agreed to feed me lies until this blows over! Now prove your honesty – tell me the dream first, then I’ll know your interpretation isn’t made-up nonsense!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[10] The Babylonians answered the king: ‘Your Majesty, there’s no one on earth who can do what you’re asking! No king or ruler — no matter how great — has ever demanded such [a] request from any wise man, magician, or Babylonian.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[11] ‘What you’re asking is both serious and astonishing; no one can explain these things to the king… except maybe [an angelic] messenger — but those don’t live among physical beings. So, what you’re asking can’t be done — it’s simply not possible.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[12] Then the king became furious and deeply upset, and ordered all the wise men of Babylon to be arrested,
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[13] and then decreed that they all be executed! They subsequently came looking for DaniEl and his companions – so they could be executed too.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[14] Then DaniEl spoke up with tact and wisdom to AriOch, the king’s chief executioner (who was in charge of killing Babylon’s wise men).
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[15] DaniEl asked him directly: ‘Why did the king issue such [a] harsh decree?’ Then AriOch explained the king’s command to DaniEl.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[16] DaniEl hurried in to see the king and asked for some time to be able to explain everything to him.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[17] Then DaniEl went home and told his friends HananiAh, MishaEl, and AzariAh everything.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[18] He urged them to fast, pray, and ask the Lord Most High for help with this mystery. They needed divine help so they wouldn’t be executed along with Babylon’s other wise men.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[19] Well, that night, [a] vision clearly revealed the king’s mystery to DaniEl. Then DaniEl praised the Lord Most High, declaring aloud:
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[20] ‘May the Great Lord’s Name be blest into the age Because of his wisdom and greatness.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[21] ‘For he changes seasons and eras; He removes kings and appoints new ones; He gives wisdom to the wise And insight to those with understanding.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[22] ‘He uncovers deep, hidden truths – Knowing what lies in darkness While dwelling in radiant light!
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[23] ‘To you, Lord of my fathers, I thank and praise you! You’ve given me wisdom and insight, And now You’ve shown me all that I asked… So I can explain these things to the king!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[24] Then DaniEl went to AriOch (the king’s appointed executioner) and said: ‘Don’t kill Babylon’s wise men! Take me to the king, and I’ll explain everything to him.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[25] Then AriOch rushed DaniEl to the king and announced: ‘Your Majesty, I’ve found [a] wise man among the Judean exiles who can explain everything to you!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[26] The king turned to DaniEl (who was called BelTeshazzar in Babylonian) and asked: ‘Can you really tell me what this vision I saw means?’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[27] So DaniEl spoke up and said: ‘The mystery you saw isn’t something that wise men, magicians, sorcerers, or diviners can explain!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[28] ‘But there is [a] God in heaven who uncovers mysteries! He’s shown King NebuChadnezzar what must happen in the final days.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[29] ‘By revealing these secrets, he’s made clear to you what’s coming next.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[30] ‘Now, this wasn’t revealed to me because I’m wiser than everyone else… No! It’s so you, Your Majesty, can understand what’s been weighing on your mind.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[31] Then DaniEl continued: ‘Your Majesty, you saw {Look!} [a] single statue – enormous and awe-inspiring! It stood right in front of you, terrifying to behold.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[32] Its head was made of fine gold Its chest and arms of silver Its belly and thighs of bronze
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[33] Legs of iron, And the feet partly iron and partly clay.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[34] ‘Then you looked at it until [a] stone was cut from [a] mountain, but not by hand. It smashed the statue’s feet (made of iron and clay), shattering them completely…’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[35] ‘Then the iron, clay, bronze, silver, and gold all turned to dust—like husks on [a] threshing floor. The wind swept them away, leaving nothing behind. But the stone that struck the statue grew into [a] huge mountain, and it violently struck the entire earth!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[36] ‘So, that’s the vision... Now, we’ll explain its meaning to you, O King.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[37] [So DaniEl continued:] ‘Your Majesty, you’re the king of kings! The Lord of heaven has given you authority, the kingdom, power, honor, and glory!
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[38] ‘He’s put the entire inhabited world under your control—every human, wild animal, bird of the sky, and fish of the sea! Yes, you’re the golden head!
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[39] ‘And after you, another kingdom will rise—weaker than yours. Then [a] third kingdom will emerge, made of bronze, that’ll rule over the whole earth.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[40] ‘Then comes [a] fourth kingdom — as strong as iron! Just as iron subdues everything, and just as iron can cut down every tree, the whole earth will be shaken!
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[41] ‘You saw how the statue’s feet and toes were partly iron and partly clay pottery… Well, that means this kingdom will be two-fold, just like the iron mixed with clay pottery you saw.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[42] And the toes of the feet are indeed partly iron and partly clay, so some parts of the kingdom will be strong and others will be crushed.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[43] ‘Just like you saw iron mixed with clay pottery – they’ll be mixed with different peoples, but they won’t be in harmony or friendly with each other, just as iron and clay simply can’t stick together.’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[44] ‘But during those kings’ reigns, The God of heaven will establish another kingdom – one that’ll last into the ages and will never be destroyed... It won’t allow another kingdom to exist, it’ll attack and destroy these other kingdoms… and it will stand forever!
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[45] Yes, just like how you saw [a] stone cut from [a] mountain without hands, and it crushed the pottery, iron, copper, silver, and gold! ‘The Great God has shown the king what’s coming in the final days – this vision is accurate, and its interpretation can be trusted!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[46] Well, then King NebuChadnezzar fell face down and bowed low before DaniEl. He then ordered [a] sacrifice and [a] drink offering to be made on his behalf.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[47] Then the king declared to DaniEl: ‘Your God truly is The God of gods and Lord of kings — the only One who reveals deep mysteries! For you have uncovered this secret!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[48] After this, King NebuChadnezzar promoted DaniEl, lavished him with many gifts and put him in charge of all Babylon’s affairs. He even appointed him as ruler and chief administrator over all Babylon’s wise men.
[Daniel (Greek)] [2]:[49] DaniEl then requested that the king to put Sedrach, Misach, and AbedNego in charge of Babylon’s affairs. DaniEl himself stayed in the royal court.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[1] In the 18th year of King NebuChadnezzar’s reign — while he ruled cities, nations, and everyone on earth from India to Ethiopia — he made [a] gold image. It stood 60 cubits tall [~97.5 feet / ~29.7m] and 6 cubits wide [~9.75 feet / ~3m]. He set it up on [a] plain in the Babylonian province.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[2] Then NebuChadnezzar — king of kings and ruler of the whole world — sent out orders to gather: Every nation, tribe, and language, Satraps, Generals, Regional governors, Supreme officials, Administrators, Regional authorities, And everyone living in the empire. They were all commanded to attend the dedication ceremony for the gold statue King NebuChadnezzar had set up.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[3] So all the high-ranking officials gathered: Satraps, Generals, Regional governors, Supreme officials, Powerful rulers with authority, Every local leader from the provinces. These listed ones all stood before the statue King NebuChadnezzar had set up.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[4] Then the herald announced to the crowds: ‘People of all nations, regions, peoples, and languages! Here’s the king’s command for you:
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[5] ‘When you hear the sound of: Trumpet, Flute, Lyre, Sambuca, Psaltery, The symphony and every other instrument... ‘You’ll immediately drop to the ground and bow to this gold statue King NebuChadnezzar set up!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[6] ‘If anyone refuses to drop down and bow to [the] gold statue, they’ll be thrown into the blazing furnace!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[7] Well, here’s what happened. As soon as people heard: The trumpet, Flute, Lyre, Sambuca, Psaltery, And all other instruments... Everyone dropped to the ground — people from every nation, tribe, and language — and bowed before NebuChadnezzar’s gold statue.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[8] But right then, some Babylonian men came forward and accused the Judeans...
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[9] They took it upon themselves to say to King NebuChadnezzar: ‘Lord King, Long live the king!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[10] ‘You issued [a] decree that everyone, when they hear the sound of... Trumpet, Flute, Lyre, Sambuca, Psaltery, And all other instruments... ‘Must immediately drop to the ground and bow to your gold statue,
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[11] and that anyone who refuses to bow down will be thrown straight into the blazing furnace.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[12] ‘But there are some Judean men — Sedrach, Misach, and AbedNego — whom you appointed over the region of Babylon, who have ignored your order! They don’t serve your idol nor have they bowed down to the gold statue you set up!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[13] Burning with anger, NebuChadnezzar ordered Sedrach, Misach, and AbedNego to be brought to him, so the men were dragged before the king.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[14] When NebuChadnezzar saw them, he demanded: ‘Sedrach! Misach! AbedNego! Why don’t you serve my gods or bow down to the gold statue I set up?’
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[15] ‘So—are you ready? When you hear: The trumpet, Flute, Lyre, Sambuca, Psaltery, And all other instruments... Will you drop down and bow to my gold statue? If you don’t bow to it, you’ll be thrown straight into the blazing furnace! And what god would save you from my hands?’
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[16] But Sedrach, Misach, and AbedNego answered King NebuChadnezzar: ‘Your Majesty, we don’t need to defend ourselves to you.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[17] ‘There’s [a] God in heaven — the one Lord we revere — who can rescue us from the blazing furnace… And he will rescue us from your hands!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[18] ‘You’ll soon see for yourself that we don’t serve your idol nor will we bow down to that gold statue you set up!’
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[19] This made NebuChadnezzar furious, his face twisted as he glared at Sedrach, Misach, and AbedNego. Then he barked orders to heat the furnace seven times hotter than necessary!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[20] Next, he ordered his strongest soldiers to tie up Sedrach, Misach, and AbedNego and throw them into the roaring furnace!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[21] So those men were tied up — still wearing their sandals, turbans, and robes — and thrown into the blazing furnace!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[22] Well since the king’s order was urgent and the furnace had been cranked up seven times hotter than normal, the soldiers who’d bound them dragged them over and hurled them into the flames...
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[23] But then, on the one hand, flames shot out from the furnace and instantly burned to death the soldiers who’d tied up AzariAh and his friends, but on the other hand, AzariAh’s group were completely unharmed!
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[24] So HananiAh, AzariAh, and MishaEl prayed and sang to the Lord — at this time when the king had ordered them thrown into the furnace.
[Daniel (Greek)] [3]:[25] AzariAh stood up and prayed like this... He opened his mouth and praised the Lord — alongside his friends in the fire’s heart — while the Babylonians kept stoking the furnace to blazing extremes. Then they declared:

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[1] King Antiochus was traveling through the upper provinces when he heard about Elymais, a city in Persia known for its vast wealth in silver and gold...
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[2] Its temple was incredibly wealthy. It contained golden coverings, breastplates, and weapons that Philip’s son Alexander (the Macedonian king who was the first to rule the Greeks) had left there.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[3] Well, he arrived and attempted to capture and plunder the city, but he was unsuccessful because the residents discovered his plan.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[4] They resisted him, and he fled, returning to Babylon in great despair.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[5] While in Persia, a messenger arrived with news that the armies sent into the land of Judah had been utterly defeated.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[6] Lysias had initially advanced with a large army but was forced to retreat. The Jews had won, using weapons they had captured from the defeated armies.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[7] Also, they had destroyed the detestable thing he had built on the altar in JeruSalem, and they had built high walls around the [temple] sanctuary, restoring it to its previous state, and also around his city, Beth-Zur.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[8] When the king heard this news, he was utterly shocked and deeply disturbed! He collapsed onto his couch, falling ill from grief, because nothing had gone according to his plans.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[9] He stayed there for many days, as his profound sorrow intensified, and he began to realize his death was near.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[10] He called all his friends and said to them: ‘I can’t sleep, and this worry has broken my heart.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[11] ‘I said to my heart: ‘What terrible trouble and chaos have I fallen into? I was once good and well-regarded during my reign.’
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[12] ‘But now I remember the wicked things I did in JeruSalem... I seized all the silver and gold treasures from it, and I sent troops to destroy the people of Judah without cause.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[13] ‘I know that because of these actions, these troubles have come upon me. And now, I’m dying from profound sorrow in a foreign land.’
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[14] So he called Philip, one of his friends, and appointed him to oversee his entire kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[15] He gave him the diadem, his royal robe, and his ring, and instructed him to bring up his son Antiochus to become king.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[16] King Antiochus died there in the 149th year.

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[20] in the 150th year. He built missile launchers and siege machines against them.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[21] [However,] some of the ungodly Israelites managed to escape the siege and joined the enemy.

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[23] ‘We were willing to serve your father, to obey his decrees, and to follow his commands.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[24] Because of this, our own people turned against us! ‘In fact, whenever they found one of us, he was killed, and our property was plundered.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[25] They didn’t just attack us, but also our entire territory. ‘And look! Today they’ve camped against the citadel in JeruSalem, intending to capture it and the sanctuary. They’ve also fortified Beth-Zur’s defenses.

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[29] Mercenary troops also came to him from other kings and from the islands in the sea.

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[37] Strong, covered wooden towers, equipped with various weapons, were mounted on each elephant. Each tower held 32 men who fought from them, along with the Indian elephant driver.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[38] The rest of the cavalry he positioned on both sides of the army, brandishing their weapons and guarding the battle lines.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[39] When the sun shone on their golden shields, the mountains gleamed brightly from their reflection, like fiery torches.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[40] Part of the king’s army was positioned on the high mountains, and some in the valleys. They advanced steadily and in an orderly fashion.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[41] All who heard the sound of their immense numbers, the marching of the multitude, and the clashing of arms were shaken, for the army was exceptionally large and powerful.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[42] Judas and his camp approached to engage in battle, and 600 men were killed from the king’s army.

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[46] He crept under the elephant, stabbed it from below, killing it! The elephant fell to the ground on top of him, and he died there.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[47] Seeing the strength of the king’s army and its relentless attacks, the Jews retreated.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[48] From the king’s camp, troops advanced towards JeruSalem to confront them, and the king himself camped in Judea, at Mount Zion.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[49] He then spoke to the people of Beth-Zur. They came out of the city because they had no food or provisions to withstand a siege, since it was a sabbatical year for the land.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[50] The king captured Beth-Zur and stationed a military unit to guard it.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[51] He then laid siege to the sanctuary for many days, setting up: Missile launchers Siege machines Fire-throwers Stone-throwers And scorpions (machines for shooting darts) and slings.

[1 Maccabees] [6]:[53] However, there was no food in the sanctuary because it was the seventh year, and those who had been saved and gathered in Judea from other lands had consumed all the remaining provisions.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[54] Only a few men remained in the holy places, as famine had overcome them, and everyone dispersed to their own homes.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[55] Lysias heard that Philip (whom King Antiochus had appointed while still alive to raise his son Antiochus to become king)
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[56] had returned from Persia and Media with the king’s troops who had gone with him, and he was attempting to seize control of the kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[57] This made them eager to depart and urged them on. So Lysias said to the king, the army commanders, and the men: ‘We’re losing ground daily, and our food supply is dwindling; the place we’re attacking is well-defended, and the kingdom’s affairs are urgent.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[58] ‘Therefore, let’s now propose a ceasefire to these men and make peace with them and their entire nation.
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[59] Let’s allow them to live according to their own laws, as they did before. ‘After all, they only became furious and did all this because we abolished their laws.’
[1 Maccabees] [6]:[60] This proposal pleased the king and his officials, so he sent envoys to them to negotiate peace, and they accepted.

[1 Maccabees] [8]:[1] Judas heard about the Romans: they were very powerful, friendly to all their allies, and made friends with anyone who sought their help.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[2] They also told him about their wars and the brave actions they performed against the Galatians, whom they had defeated and forced to pay tribute.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[3] They described what they had acheived in Spain, how they had taken control of the silver and gold mines there,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[4] and conquered the entire region through careful planning and persistence, despite its great distance. They had also defeated kings who had attacked them from distant lands, crushing them completely, with the survivors paying them tribute every year.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[5] They had also defeated and subdued [King] Philip [of Macedon] and King Perseus of the Kittians, and everyone who had rebelled against them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[6] They even crushed the King of Asia, Antiochus the Great, who had attacked them with 120 elephants, horsemen, chariots, and a huge army.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[7] They captured him alive and forced him and his future rulers to pay a large tribute, hand over hostages, and agree to specific conditions.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[8] They took from him the land of India, Media, Lydia, and some of his finest lands, which they then gave to King Eumenes [of Pergamon].
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[9] They also learned that when the Greeks planned to attack and destroy them,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[10] the Romans discovered this and sent a general to fight them. A battle ensued, and many Greeks were wounded and killed. The Romans: Captured their women and children Plundered their possessions Conquered their land Tore down their strongholds And enslaved them They remain enslaved even now!
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[11] All other kingdoms and islands that had ever rebelled against them were destroyed and brought under their control.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[12] Yet, they maintained friendships with their allies and those who relied on them. They conquered kingdoms both near and far, and everyone who heard of them feared them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[13] They grant kingship to whomever they decide to help, and remove anyone they desire from power. Thus, they grew immensely powerful.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[14] Despite all their power, none of them wore a crown or dressed in purple robes to display their greatness.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[15] They established a senate for themselves, where 320 senators convened daily. They always deliberated on what was best for the people to maintain order.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[16] They elect one man to govern them for a year and rule over their entire land, and everyone obeys him; there is no envy or jealousy among them.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[17] So, Judas chose Eupolemus (son of John) from Accos, and Jason (son of EleAzar), sending them to Rome to establish a friendship and [an] alliance with them,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[18] and to alleviate their burden, as they saw that the Greek kingdom was enslaving Israel.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[19] They traveled to Rome — a very long journey — and entered the Senate chamber, stating:
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[20] ‘Judas Maccabeus, his brothers, and the Jewish people have sent us to you to establish [an] alliance and peace with you, and to be recorded as your allies and friends.’
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[21] The Romans accepted their proposal.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[22] This is the copy of the document they wrote on bronze tablets and sent to JeruSalem to serve as [a] lasting reminder of their peace and alliance:
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[23] ‘May the Romans and the Jewish nation prosper on land and sea into the age. ‘May they remain free from war and enemies.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[24] If war breaks out for Rome or for any of their allies anywhere within their territory,
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[25] the Jewish nation will fully ally with them from [a] full heart, as required.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[26] ‘They will not provide or supply Rome’s enemies with grain, weapons, silver, or ships, as Rome has determined. They will adhere to these terms without receiving anything in return.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[27] ‘Similarly, if war breaks out for the Jewish nation, the Romans will fully ally with them from [their] soul, as required.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[28] Grain, weapons, or silver will not be provided to the enemies of the Jews, as Rome has determined. They will adhere to these rules faithfully.’
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[29] These were the terms the Romans established with the Jewish people in this manner.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[30] If, after this agreement, either party decides to add or remove anything, they may do so independently, and whatever they add or remove will be binding.
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[31] [The Romans futher said:] ‘Also, concerning the injustices that King Demetrius is committing against them, we have written to him, stating: ‘Why have you placed such a heavy burden on our Jewish friends and allies?
[1 Maccabees] [8]:[32] Therefore, if they continue to complain about you, we will intervene on their behalf and fight you by sea and by land.’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[1] Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his forces had fought [and lost]. So, he decided to send Bacchides and Alcimus into the land of Judah a second time, bringing his army’s right wing with them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[2] They marched towards Gilgal and camped at Messaloth, which is in Arbela. They captured it, and he ended many lives there.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[3] In the first month of the 152nd year, they camped near JeruSalem.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[4] From there, they left and went to Berea with 20,000 men and 2,000 horses.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[5] Judas was camped at Elasa with 3,000 chosen men.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[6] When they saw the huge enemy army, they were very afraid. Many left the camp, and only 800 men remained!
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[7] Judas saw that his army had abandoned him, and the war was closing in on him. His mind was deeply troubled, because he had no time to muster them up [for battle].
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[8] Feeling discouraged, he said to those who remained: ‘Let’s get up and attack our opponents, to see if we can possibly fight them!’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[9] But they tried to talk him out of it, saying: ‘We definitely can’t do it! We should just save our lives for now. Let’s return to our brothers, and then we can fight them, because there are too few of us.’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[10] Judas replied: ‘I would never do such a thing and flee from them! ‘Our time has come... ‘Let’s die bravely for the sake of our brothers, and let’s not dishonor ourselves.’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[11] So, the army marched out of the camp and got into formation to fight them. The cavalry was divided into two parts, and the slingers and archers went ahead of the main army, along with all the brave warriors.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[12] Bacchides led the right wing. The armies moved closer from both sides, and they blew their trumpets... Judas’s men also blew their trumpets.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[13] The earth shook from the noise of their armies, and the battle continued fiercely from morning until evening.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[14] Judas saw that Bacchides and the strongest part of the enemy were on the right flank, so all the men brave in heart gathered around him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[15] They defeated the enemy’s right wing, and Judas pursued them as far as Mount Azotus!
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[16] When the enemy’s left wing saw that their right wing was defeated, they turned and attacked Judas and his men from behind.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[17] The fighting became intense, and many were wounded on both sides.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[18] Judas died, and the rest fled.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[19] Jonathan and Simon recovered their brother Judas’s body and buried him in his family’s tomb in Modein.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[20] They wept for him there, and all Israel mourned him deeply. They grieved for many days and said:
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[21] ‘Oh, how the mighty hero has died, who saved Israel!’ [2 Samuel 1:19, 25, 27]
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[22] The rest of Judas’s acts, his wars, his brave actions, and his greatness are not recorded, because there were so many of them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[23] After Judas’s death, the lawless people reappeared all over Israel, and everyone who did wrong gained power.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[24] In those days, there was [a] very severe famine, and the people of the country joined [these lawless ones].
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[25] Bacchides chose the ungodly men and made them rulers of the land.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[26] They searched hard for Judas’s friends and brought them to Bacchides, who executed them, and they were publicly humiliated.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[27] There was great suffering in Israel, the worst in the entire time since the prophets disappeared.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[28] Then all Judas’ friends gathered and said to JoNathan:
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[29] ‘Since your brother Judas has died, there’s no one left like him to lead us against our enemies, against Bacchides and our nation’s other enemies.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[30] Therefore, today, we’ve chosen you to be our ruler and leader in his place, to fight our battles!’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[31] JoNathan agreed to lead at that time, and he took the place of Judas, his brother.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[32] Well, Bacchides found out about this and tried to kill him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[33] JoNathan, his brother Simon, and all their men also found out. So, they fled into the wilderness of Tekoa and camped by the Well of Asphal.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[34] Bacchides found out where they were on the Sabbath day, and he himself came with all his army across the Jordan.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[35] JoNathan had sent his brother John to guide the people, and he had asked his Nabataean friends to store a large amount of their supplies for them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[36] But the sons of Jambri came out from [the city of] Medaba, seized John and all his possessions, and took them away.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[37] After this, they reported to JoNathan and his brother Simon that the sons of Jambri were having [a] big wedding feast and were bringing the bride from Nadabath, who was the daughter of one of Canaan’s great nobles, with [a] large group of attendants.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[38] They remembered their brother John, so they went up and hid in the mountain’s shelter.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[39] They looked up and saw [a] lot of activity and many supplies. The bridegroom came out with his friends and brothers to meet them, with drums, musical instruments, and many weapons.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[40] JoNathan’s men came out of ambush and attacked them, killing many. The rest fled to the mountain. They took all their belongings.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[41] The wedding became mourning, and their festive music became wailing.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[42] They avenged their brother’s death and returned to the Jordan [region’s] mountains.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[43] Bacchides heard about this and came to the banks of the Jordan on the Sabbath day with [a] large army.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[44] JoNathan said to his brothers: ‘Let’s get up now and fight for our lives, because this isn’t like yesterday or the day before.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[45] ‘Look! We’re attacked from the front and behind. The Jordan River is on both sides, with marshes and thick bushes, and there’s no way to escape.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[46] ‘Therefore, pray to Heaven, so we may be saved from our enemies.’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[47] The battle began, and JoNathan reached out to strike Bacchides, but he moved away from him quickly.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[48] JoNathan and his men jumped into the Jordan and swam to the other side. Bacchides’ forces didn’t follow them across the Jordan.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[49] On that day, about 1,000 men were killed by Bacchides’ forces.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[50] Bacchides’ forces returned to JeruSalem and strengthened cities in Judea: The fortress in Jericho Emmaus Beth-Horon BethEl Thamnata Pharathon Tephon [They strengthened them] with high walls, gates, and strong bars.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[51] They placed troops in them to trouble Israel.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[52] They also strengthened the city of Beth-Zur, Gazara, and the citadel [in JeruSalem], putting soldiers and food supplies in them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[53] They took the sons of the important men of the land as hostages and held them captive in the citadel in JeruSalem.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[54] In the second month of the 153rd year, [high priest] Alcimus ordered the wall of the sanctuary’s inner court torn down. He destroyed what the prophets had built and started tearing it down.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[55] [However,] at that time, Alcimus was struck by illness, and his work stopped. His mouth was shut, and he was paralyzed. He couldn’t speak [a] word or give orders for his household anymore!
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[56] Alcimus died at that time in great pain.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[57] When Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died, he went back to the king, and the land of Judah had peace for two years.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[58] All the lawless ones plotted together, saying: ‘Look, JoNathan and his men are living peacefully and safely. Now, let’s call for Bacchides, and he’ll capture them all in one night!’
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[59] So, they went and talked to him.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[60] Bacchides left with [a] large army and secretly sent messages to all his allies in Judea, telling them to capture JoNathan and his men. But they were unsuccessful, because JoNathan’s men found out about their plot.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[61] JoNathan’s men captured about 50 of the main wicked men from the country and killed them.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[62] JoNathan, Simon, and their men retreated to BethBasi in the wilderness. JoNathan rebuilt its ruined sections and strengthened it.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[63] Bacchides found out about this and gathered all his troops, also calling his allies from Judea...
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[64] He came and laid siege to BethBasi, fighting against it for many days and building siege machines.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[65] JoNathan left his brother Simon in the city, while he himself went out into the country with [a] large force.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[66] He attacked Odomera, his brothers, and the sons of Phasiron in their tents, and began to attack and push back the enemy forces.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[67] Simon and his men came out of the city and burned the siege machines.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[68] They fought Bacchides, and he was defeated by them — and very upset [about it], because his plan and his attack had failed.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[69] He and his men were furious at the lawless men who had persuaded him to come into the country, and they killed many of them! Bacchides then decided to return to his own land.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[70] JoNathan learned about this and sent representatives to [Bacchides] to discuss [a] peace agreement and to return their prisoners.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[71] Bacchides agreed and kept his word. He swore to JoNathan that he wouldn’t try to harm him for the rest of his life.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[72] He returned the prisoners he had previously taken from the land of Judah. Then, he went back to his own land and never again decided to invade their land.
[1 Maccabees] [9]:[73] So, fighting stopped in Israel, and JoNathan settled in Michmash. JoNathan began to rule the people and removed the ungodly people from Israel.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[1] In the 160th year, Antiochus Epiphanes’s son, Alexander, arrived and took control of [the city of] Ptolemais. The people welcomed him, and he began to rule there.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[2] [However,] when [King] Demetrius heard this, he gathered a very large army and marched out to fight Alexander.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[3] Demetrius, however, first sent letters trying to make peace with Jonathan, seeking to give him more power. He [privately] commented:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[4] ‘Let’s quickly make peace with them, before he makes an alliance with Alexander against us.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[5] He’ll remember all the wrongs we’ve done against him, his brothers, and his nation.’ He gave JoNathan permission to raise an army and prepare weapons, and to be his friend and helper. He also promised to give him the hostages held in the citadel.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[7] JoNathan arrived in JeruSalem and read the letters aloud so everyone, including those from the citadel, could hear.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[8] They were very afraid when they heard that the king had given them permission to raise an army.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[9] The people in the citadel gave the hostages to JoNathan, and he returned them to their parents.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[10] JoNathan then made JeruSalem his home and began to rebuild the city.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[11] He told the workers to build the walls and to strengthen Mount Zion all around with squared stones, and they did it.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[12] The foreigners who were in the forts that Bacchides had built, fled.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[13] Each one left his position and returned to his own land.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[14] Only in [the city of] Beth-Zur did some of those who had abandoned the Law and its rules remain, as it was a safe place for them.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[15] King Alexander heard about all the promises Demetrius had sent to JoNathan, and they told him about the wars and the brave things that JoNathan and his brothers had accomplished, and the difficulties they had endured. Alexander commented:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[16] ‘Can we find a man like this? So, let’s make him our friend and ally!’ He then wrote and sent him a letter with the following words:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[18] ‘King Alexander to his brother JoNathan: Greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[19] ‘We’ve heard that you’re a very strong man and a good person to be our friend.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[20] ‘Today, we make you the high priest of your nation and grant you the title ‘Friend of the King.’ We also send you a purple robe and a golden crown, expecting you to support us and stay our friend.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[21] So, JoNathan put on the sacred vestments in the seventh month of the 160th year, during the Festival of Temporary Structures. He then gathered an army and prepared many weapons.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[22] When Demetrius heard these words, he was greatly distressed and said:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[23] ‘What a mistake we’ve made! ‘Alexander has outsmarted us by getting the Jews to be his friends and support him.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[24] I’ll also write to them, offering appealing words, high status, and gifts, so that they may join me as allies.’ So he sent them a message with the following terms:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[25] ‘King Demetrius to the Jews’ nation: Greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[26] ‘Since you have kept your agreements with us, stayed loyal to our friendship, and have not sided with our enemies, we’ve heard this and are pleased.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[27] Now, continue to maintain your loyalty to us, and we will reward you generously for your cooperation.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[28] We will grant you many exemptions and give you gifts.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[29] ‘I now release you and all the Jews from tribute payments, the salt tax, and the crown taxes.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[30] ‘Furthermore, I remit from today onward the third of the sown produce and half of the fruit from the trees that would normally be due to me. This remission applies to Judah’s land, and to the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day forward and into the age.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[31] ‘Let JeruSalem be holy and free, along with its borders, from tithes and tolls!
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[32] ‘I also relinquish my authority over the citadel in JeruSalem and grant the high priest the right to appoint men of his own choosing to guard it.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[33] ‘Every Jewish person taken captive from Judah’s land into any part of my kingdom, I release as a gift, granting them freedom. ‘Furthermore, let all be exempt from taxes on their cattle.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[34] ‘All festivals, Sabbaths, New Moons, and appointed days, as well as the three days before and three days after any feast, shall be days of exemption and release for all Jews throughout my kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[35] No one shall have the authority to exact tribute or trouble any of them in any matter.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[36] ‘Let 30,000 men from among the Jews be enrolled into the king’s forces, and they shall receive pay, as is customary for all the king’s forces.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[37] ‘Some of them shall be appointed to the king’s great strongholds, and from these, trustworthy men shall be appointed to positions of responsibility within the kingdom. Their officers and commanders shall be chosen from among themselves, and they shall live according to their own laws, just as the king has commanded for Judah’s land.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[38] ‘The three districts that were added to Judea from Samaria’s territory shall be fully incorporated into Judea, so that they are considered one unified territory and are subject to no other authority but that of the high priest.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[39] ‘Ptolemais and its dependent territories I have given as a gift to the holy ones in JeruSalem, for the necessary expenses of the [temple] sanctuary.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[40] I also grant 15,000 shekels of silver annually from the king’s revenues, from the appropriate places.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[41] Any surplus funds that were not previously paid from the revenues, as in former years, shall now be given for the work of the temple.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[42] ‘Furthermore, the 5,000 shekels of silver that were formerly collected annually from the temple’s revenues are now remitted, as they belong to the priests who minister there.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[43] ‘Anyone who flees to the temple in JeruSalem or within its borders, owing royal debts or for any other matter, shall be released, and all their possessions throughout my kingdom shall be theirs.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[44] ‘As for the building and restoration of the sacred works, the expenses shall be paid from the king’s treasury.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[45] ‘Also, for the building of the walls of JeruSalem and their fortification all around, the expense shall be paid from the king’s treasury, as well as for the building of walls throughout Judea.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[46] However, when JoNathan and the people heard these words, they neither believed them nor accepted them, because they remembered the great wickedness Demetrius had inflicted upon Israel, and how severely he had oppressed them!
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[47] They were pleased with Alexander, because he had initiated peaceful overtures to them, and they remained his allies throughout his reign.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[48] King Alexander assembled a large army and encamped opposite Demetrius.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[49] The two kings engaged in battle. Demetrius’s army fled, and Alexander pursued him and gained a decisive victory.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[50] He pressed the battle hard until sunset, and Demetrius was killed that day.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[51] Alexander then sent envoys to Ptolemy, King of Egypt, with the following message:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[52] ‘Now that I’ve returned to my kingdom, I have ascended my father’s throne, taken control of the realm, crushed Demetrius, and gained control of our land.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[53] I fought him in battle and we crushed both him and his army; we have taken the throne of his kingdom.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[54] ‘Therefore, let’s establish friendship between us. Now, give me your daughter as a wife, and I will become your son-in-law, and I will give you and her gifts worthy of you.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[55] King Ptolemy replied: ‘It’s a good day that you’ve returned to your fathers’ land and have ascended their kingdom’s throne!
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[56] ‘I’ll now do as you’ve written, but come to Ptolemais, so that we may meet in person, and I’ll become your son-in-law, just as you said.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[57] Ptolemy himself, with his daughter Cleopatra, departed from Egypt and arrived in Ptolemais in the 162nd year.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[58] King Alexander met him there, and Ptolemy gave him his daughter, Cleopatra. Alexander celebrated her marriage in Ptolemais with great splendor, as is customary for kings.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[59] King Alexander then wrote to JoNathan, inviting him to meet him.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[60] JoNathan went to Ptolemais with great honor and met the two kings. He presented them and their friends with much silver and gold and many gifts, and found loving kindness in their eyes.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[61] However, some troublesome and lawless men from Israel gathered to bring accusations against him, but the king paid no attention to them.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[62] Instead, the king gave orders that JoNathan be stripped of his garments and clothed in purple, and this was done! The king seated him beside himself and said to his rulers:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[63] ‘Go out with him into the center of the city and proclaim that no one is to bring any accusation against this man, nor is anyone to trouble him in any way.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[64] When those who had come to accuse him saw the honor bestowed upon him, just as the king had proclaimed, and saw him clothed in fine linen, they all fled!
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[65] The king further honored him and enrolled him among his chief friends, and appointed him as general and governor of a district.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[66] JoNathan returned to JeruSalem in peace and with great joy.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[67] In the 165th year, Demetrius’ son, [also called] Demetrius, came from Crete to the land of his ancestors.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[68] When King Alexander heard this, he was greatly distressed and returned to Antioch.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[69] Demetrius appointed Apollonius as governor of Coele-Syria. Apollonius assembled a large army and encamped at Jamnia. He then sent a message to JoNathan the high priest, saying:
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[70] ‘You alone defy us, and I have become an object of ridicule and scorn because of you. Why do you presume to hold sway over us in the mountains?
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[71] ‘Therefore, if you are confident in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us meet in battle there, for I have the support of the cities’ armies.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[72] ‘Ask and learn who I am, and who are the others who assist us. They will tell you: ‘You cannot stand your ground against us, for twice your fathers were put to flight in their own land.’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[73] ‘And now, you won’t be able to withstand such cavalry and forces in the plain, where there’s no stone or pebble, nor anywhere to flee!’
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[74] When JoNathan heard Apollonius’s words, he was stirred in mind. He selected 10,000 men and marched out of JeruSalem, and his brother Simon met him to offer assistance.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[75] He encamped against Joppa, but the people of the city shut him out because Apollonius had a garrison there. So JoNathan attacked the city.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[76] Fearing for their lives, the people of the city opened the gates, and JoNathan took control of Joppa.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[77] When Apollonius heard this, he assembled 3,000 cavalry and a large army and marched towards Azotus, seemingly passing through, but at the same time he advanced into the plain, confident in his large cavalry force.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[78] JoNathan pursued him to Azotus, and the armies clashed in battle.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[79] Apollonius had secretly left 1,000 cavalry behind them in ambush.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[80] JoNathan knew there was an ambush behind him. Apollonius’s forces surrounded JoNathan’s army and shot darts at the people from morning until evening.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[81] But JoNathan’s men held their ground as he commanded, and the enemy’s horses grew weary.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[82] Then Simon led his force forward and attacked the enemy phalanx, for their cavalry was exhausted. They were crushed by him and fled.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[83] The cavalry scattered across the plain and fled to Azotus, entering their idol Dagon’s temple for safety.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[84] JoNathan then burned Azotus and the surrounding cities and took their spoils. He also burned Dagon’s temple and its sanctuary.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[85] The number killed with the sword, along with those burned, came to a total of [about] 8,000 men.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[86] JoNathan departed from there and encamped at Ashkelon. The city’s residents came out to meet him with great honor.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[87] JoNathan returned with his men, carrying lots of the spoils [of war].
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[88] Well, when King Alexander heard these reports, he resolved to honor JoNathan even more.
[1 Maccabees] [10]:[89] He sent him a golden brooch, such as is customarily given to members of the royal family, and granted him ownership of Accaron and all its surrounding territory.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[1] King [Ptolemy] of Egypt gathered [a] huge army, as vast as the sand on the seashore, along with many ships. He planned to take the [Syrian] kingdom of [his son-in-law] Alexander by trickery and to incorporate it into his own.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[2] He entered Syria peacefully, and the cities opened their gates to him, with their people coming out to meet him. This was because King Alexander had ordered them to welcome him, because he was, after all, his father-in-law.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[3] When he entered the cities of Ptolemais, he stationed his troops in each one as garrisons.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[4] When he reached Azotus, they showed him the burned temple of Dagon. Azotus itself and the surrounding areas were also in ruins. They also pointed out the bodies of those whom [Jewish high priest] Jonathan had burned during the war, as their corpses were piled in heaps along his path.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[5] They told the king what JoNathan had done, hoping to discredit him — but the king said nothing.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[6] JoNathan then met King [Ptolemy] in Joppa with great ceremony... They greeted each other and spent the night there.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[7] JoNathan traveled with the king up to the river called Eleutherus, then he returned to JeruSalem.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[8] King Ptolemy took control of the coastal cities all the way to Seleucia-by-the-Sea. Throughout this time, he was plotting evil against [King] Alexander.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[9] Then he sent messengers to [Alexander’s rival] King Demetrius, suggesting: ‘Let’s make [an] agreement between us! I’ll give you my daughter, who’s currently with Alexander, and you can rule your father’s kingdom!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[10] ‘I regret giving him my daughter, because he tried to kill me.’
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[11] He also accused [King] Alexander of trying to seize the [Egyptian] kingdom of Ptolemy.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[12] So, Ptolemy took his daughter from Alexander and gave her to Demetrius. Alexander’s attitude changed, and they became openly hostile toward each other.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[13] Ptolemy then entered Antioch and crowned himself [as king of Syria] with the crown of Asia. So, he wore two crowns: Asia’s and Egypt’s.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[14] At that time, King Alexander was in Cilicia, because the people there were rebelling.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[15] When Alexander heard this, he marched to battle Ptolemy. But Ptolemy led out his forces and met him with overwhelming force, forcing him to flee
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[16] into Arabia, hoping to find safety there... Meanwhile, King Ptolemy’s power grew stronger.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[17] Then, Zabdius the Arab cut off Alexander’s head and sent it to Ptolemy!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[18] However, three days later, King Ptolemy himself died! Further, his men in the strongholds were killed by others inside the strongholds.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[19] [Alexander’s rival] Demetrius then began to rule [Syria] in the 167th year.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[20] During those days, [high priest] JoNathan gathered the people of Judea to attack the citadel in JeruSalem. They built many siege machines to attack it.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[21] However, some lawless individuals who hated their own nation went to the king and told him that JoNathan was attacking the citadel.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[22] When the king heard this, he was furious! As soon as he heard, he immediately broke camp and came to [the city of] Ptolemais. He wrote to JoNathan, ordering him to stop the attack and to come meet him in Ptolemais without delay.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[23] When JoNathan heard this, he ordered the attack to continue anyway. Then he selected some of Israel’s elders and priests, and took the risk of going.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[24] Taking silver, gold, clothing, and many other gifts, he went to the king in Ptolemais and gained his favor.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[25] Some lawless individuals from his own nation, however, continued to accuse him.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[26] But the king treated him as previous kings had, and he honored JoNathan in front of all his friends.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[27] He confirmed JoNathan as high priest and restored all the other honors he previously held. He also appointed him as one of the king’s closest advisors.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[28] JoNathan then asked the king to make Judea, the three toparchies, and Samaria exempt from tribute. In return, they promised him 300 talents.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[29] The king was pleased with this, and he wrote letters to JoNathan regarding all these matters, as follows:
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[30] ‘King Demetrius to his brother JoNathan and to the Jewish nation: Greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[31] ‘Here’s a copy of the letter we wrote to our relative Lasthenes concerning you. We’ve also written it to you, so you can see it:
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[32] ‘King Demetrius to Lasthenes, Father: Greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[33] ‘To the Jewish nation, our friends, who support our rightful claims: ‘We’ve decided to grant them favors because of their goodwill toward us.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[34] Therefore, we’ve confirmed for them the borders of Judea, along with the three districts of Apharema, Lydda, and Ramathaim (which were added to Judea from Samaria). ‘All revenues from these, which previously went to the king annually from the land’s produce and its fruits, are now to belong to those who perform sacrifices in JeruSalem.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[35] ‘Also, all other revenues owed to us from now on, including tithes, taxes, the income from the salt lakes, and the crown taxes, we will grant them entirely.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[36] None of these concessions will ever be taken back, from this time forward, permanently!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[37] ‘So now, make [a] copy of these provisions. It should be given to JoNathan and placed on the holy mountain in [a] suitable, prominent location.’
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[38] King Demetrius saw that the land was at peace under his rule and that no one was resisting him. So he dismissed all his forces, sending every man home, except for the foreign mercenaries he had hired from the foreign islands... As a result, all the forces he had inherited from previous rulers began to hate him.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[39] Now Tryphon, who had previously served [King] Alexander, saw that all the forces were very unhappy with [King] Demetrius. So he went to Sinmalcue the Arab, who was raising Alexander’s young son, Antiochus.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[40] Tryphon tried to persuade Sinmalcue to hand the boy over to him, so that Antiochus could rule in his father’s place. They told Sinmalcue everything Demetrius had done, and how his own forces now despised him. Tryphon stayed there for many days.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[41] JoNathan sent a message to King Demetrius, asking him to remove the garrison from the citadel in JeruSalem and from the other strongholds, because they were constantly harassing Israel.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[42] Demetrius replied to JoNathan, saying: ‘Not only will I grant these things to you and your nation, but I’ll also honor you and your nation greatly, if I get the chance.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[43] ‘Therefore, I ask that you send me men to fight alongside me, because all my forces have rebelled.’
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[44] So JoNathan sent 3,000 strong and capable men to Antioch. When they arrived, the king was very pleased by their arrival.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[45] Meanwhile, the citizens of Antioch gathered in the center of the city, a force of 120,000 men, and they planned to kill the king!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[46] The king fled into the palace courtyard, but the citizens seized control of the city’s passages and began to attack...
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[47] The king called upon the Jews for help, and they all rallied to him. They spread out through the city and on that day killed 10,000 men inside it.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[48] They set the city ablaze and looted extensively that day, saving the king.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[49] When the citizens saw that the Jews had taken control of the city as they pleased, they lost their will to fight and cried out to the king, pleading:
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[50] ‘Grant us peace, and make the Jews stop fighting us and attacking the city!’
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[51] The citizens threw down their weapons and agreed to peace. The Jews were greatly honored by the king and before everyone in his kingdom; they then returned to JeruSalem, carrying a great deal of plunder.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[52] King Demetrius then took his place on the throne of his kingdom, and the land was at peace under his rule.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[53] However, he broke all his promises and alienated JoNathan. He didn’t return the favors JoNathan had shown him, and instead severely oppressed him.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[54] After these events, Tryphon returned with [Alexander’s son] Antiochus, [a] younger boy. Antiochus then began to rule and was crowned [king of Syria].
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[55] All the forces that [King] Demetrius had dismissed gathered in support of Antiochus, and fought against Demetrius, who was then forced to flee.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[56] Tryphon captured the war elephants and took control of [the Syrian capital of] Antioch.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[57] Antiochus the younger wrote to JoNathan, saying: ‘I confirm you as high priest, appoint you over the four districts, and declare you to be one of the king’s closest advisors.’
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[58] He also sent him golden vessels and [gave him a] special rank that granted him the privilege of drinking from golden cups, wearing purple, and having [a] golden brooch.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[59] He also appointed JoNathan’s brother Simon as [a military] general, [having authority] from the Ladder of Tyre all the way to the borders of Egypt.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[60] JoNathan then set out, traveling through the region [east] beyond the river and visiting the cities. All the forces of Syria rallied to him as allies. He came [back west] to [the city of] Ashkelon, and the people of the city received him with great honor.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[61] From there he went [south] to [the city of] Gaza, but the Gazans shut their gates against him. So he attacked the city, burned the surrounding areas, and plundered them.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[62] The Gazans then pleaded with JoNathan, and he made peace with them. He took their rulers’ sons as hostages and sent them to JeruSalem. JoNathan then traveled through the country up [north] to Damascus.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[63] JoNathan heard that [deposed King] Demetrius’s commanders were in Kadesh in Galilee with [a] large force, planning to depose him.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[64] He went to confront them, leaving his brother Simon in the country.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[65] Simon camped at Beth-Zur, and he besieged it for many days, attacking it.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[66] [The inhabitants] asked to make peace with them, and he agreed. He then expelled them from the city, took control of it, and placed [a] garrison there.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[67] JoNathan and his forces camped by Gennesar’s Waters. Early the next morning, they advanced into the plain of Nasor.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[68] Suddenly, [a] camp of foreigners encountered him in the plain! They had set [an] ambush for him in the mountains, while their main force came from the opposite direction...
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[69] The ambushers rose up from their positions and joined the fight. All of JoNathan’s men fled;
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[70] not [a] single man was left, except Mattathias (son of Absalom) and Judas (son of Chalphi), who were commanders of the forces.
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[71] JoNathan tore his clothes, put dust on his head, and prayed...
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[72] He then returned to fight them, defeated them, and they fled!
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[73] When those who had fled saw this, they returned to [join] him and pursued the enemy alongside him all the way up to their camp at Kadesh; [then] they set up camp there [themselves].
[1 Maccabees] [11]:[74] On that day, about 3,000 foreigners died. JoNathan then returned to JeruSalem.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[1] [High priest] Jonathan realized it was an opportune time for him. So, he selected men and sent them to Rome to re-establish and renew their friendship with the Romans.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[2] He also sent similar letters to the [Greek] Spartans and to other places.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[3] When they arrived in Rome, they went into the Senate and announced: ‘JoNathan, the high priest, and the Jewish nation have sent us to you to renew the friendship and agreement that we had before.’
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[4] The Romans gave them letters for various places, so they could be safely escorted back to the land of Judah.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[5] Here is a copy of the letter JoNathan wrote to the Spartans:
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[6] ‘JoNathan, the nation’s high priest, along with the elders’ council, the priests, and all the rest of the Jewish people, to our brothers, the Spartans: Greetings.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[7] ‘Previously, letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areius, your king, stating that you are our brothers, as the attached copy confirms.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[8] Onias received the envoy honorably and accepted the letters, which clearly mentioned an agreement and friendship.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[9] ‘Therefore, even though we don’t require these things ourselves (since we find comfort in our holy books)
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[10] we’ve made an effort to send this message to renew our brotherhood and friendship with you, so we don’t become estranged. ‘It has been a long time since you last sent [a message] to us.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[11] Therefore, continually, during our feasts and on other appropriate days, we remember you in our sacrifices and prayers, as it is right and proper to remember brothers.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[12] We’re also pleased by your good reputation.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[13] ‘However, we’ve been surrounded by many troubles and wars, and the neighbouring kings have waged war against us.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[14] Therefore, we didn’t want to trouble you or our other allies and friends during these conflicts.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[15] For we’ve received help from heaven, which assisted us; we were rescued from our enemies, and our enemies were defeated!
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[16] ‘Therefore, we’ve selected Numenius (son of Antiochus) and Antipater (son of Jason), and sent them to the Romans to renew our previous friendship and agreement with them.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[17] We also told them to visit you and convey our greetings, and to deliver our letters concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[18] ‘Now, it would be good for you to send us a reply about these things.’
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[19] Here is a copy of the letter they sent to [King] Onias:
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[20] ‘Areius, the King of the Spartans, to Onias, the high priest: Greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[21] ‘A document has been discovered concerning both the Spartans and the Jews, stating that they are brothers and descendants of Abraham.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[22] ‘Now that we’ve learned this, it would be good for you to write to us to inform us of your well-being.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[23] ‘We also write to you in return: ‘Your livestock and your possessions are ours, and our possessions are yours.’ Therefore, we instruct them to report this to you as well.’
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[24] JoNathan heard that Demetrius’s commanders had returned with a larger army than before, intending to fight him.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[25] So he left JeruSalem and confronted them in the Hamathite country, because he wouldn’t let them to enter his territory without a fight.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[26] He sent spies into their camp... They returned to report that the enemy was preparing to attack them during the night.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[27] When the sun set, JoNathan ordered his men to remain vigilant and armed, preparing for battle throughout the night. He also established outposts around the camp.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[28] When the opponents heard that JoNathan and his men were prepared for war, they became afraid and lost courage. So they then lit fires in their camp [and fled].
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[29] JoNathan and his men, however, didn’t realize [they had fled] until morning, because they saw the burning lights [during the night].
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[30] He went in pursuit, but didn’t catch up to them, because they had already crossed the Eleutherus River.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[31] JoNathan then turned his attention to the Arabs known as Zabadaeans. He attacked them and took their possessions.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[32] After that, he came to Damascus and traveled throughout the region.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[33] Meanwhile, Simon advanced as far as Ashkelon and the nearby strongholds. He then turned toward Joppa and captured it before anyone else could.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[34] You see, he had heard that the inhabitants were planning to hand over the stronghold to Demetrius’s forces, so he stationed soldiers there to guard it.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[35] JoNathan returned and convened a meeting of the people’s elders. He consulted with them regarding the construction of fortifications in Judea,
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[36] and raising [the height of] JeruSalem’s walls. They also planned to build [a] great wall between the citadel and the city to separate it from the city, so that the citadel would be isolated, and its occupants couldn’t buy or sell anything.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[37] They assembled to begin building. A section of the wall near the winter torrent on the east side had collapsed, and JoNathan repaired the area known as Chaphenatha.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[38] Also, Simon built Hadida in the Shephelah, reinforcing its gates and bars.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[39] Tryphon wanted to become king of Asia, to wear the diadem, and to seize King Antiochus.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[40] He was concerned that JoNathan might not allow this to happen, and might even [need to] fight him. So he looked for a way to capture and kill JoNathan. With this intention, he left and came to Bethsa.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[41] JoNathan went out to confront him with 40,000 chosen men prepared for battle, and he arrived at Bethsa.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[42] Tryphon saw that JoNathan was there with a large force, so he hesitated to attack him.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[43] Instead, he received JoNathan honorably, introduced him to all his friends, gave him gifts, and instructed his friends and forces to obey him similarly.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[44] Then he said to JoNathan: ‘Why have you brought all these people here, when we are not at war?
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[45] ‘Now, send them back to their homes, but select a few men to accompany you. Come with me to Ptolemais, and I will hand the city over to you, along with the remaining strongholds, the many forces, and everyone responsible for administration. ‘Then I’ll depart and return [home], because this is why I am here.’
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[46] JoNathan trusted him and acted as he suggested. He sent the forces away, and they returned to the land of Judah.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[47] However, he retained 3,000 men with him; about 2,000 he left in Galilee, while 1,000 came with him.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[48] When JoNathan entered Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais closed the gates, captured him, and killed everyone who had accompanied him.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[49] Tryphon then sent soldiers and cavalry into the Great Plain of Galilee to destroy all of JoNathan’s men.
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[50] JoNathan’s men realized that he had been captured and [wrongly thought that he must have been] killed, along with those accompanying him. They encouraged one another and marched together, prepared for battle...
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[51] The pursuers saw that JoNathan’s men were fighting for their lives, so they retreated
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[52] and all of JoNathan’s men returned safely to the land of Judah. They mourned JoNathan and those who had accompanied him, and they were very afraid. Yes, Israel mourned profoundly!
[1 Maccabees] [12]:[53] All the neighbouring nations attempted to wipe them out, because they said: ‘They don’t have [a] leader or [a] helper any longer. In that case, let’s now fight them and erase their memory from among humanity!’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[1] [Jonathan’s brother] Simon heard that Tryphon had assembled a large army to invade and destroy the land of Judah...
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[2] He saw the people trembling with terror! So, he went up to JeruSalem, brought them together, and encouraged them by saying:
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[3] ‘You all know what my brothers, my family, and I have done to protect our laws and holy places, and how we’ve faced wars and hardships...
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[4] ‘As a result, all my brothers died for Israel, and I am the only one left.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[5] I will never hesitate to risk my own life in times of trouble. ‘Even though I’m certainly not stronger than my brothers [were],
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[6] I will nevertheless avenge my nation, our holy places, and our women and children, since all the nations have gathered to destroy us because they hate us!’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[7] His words really stirred up the spirit of his people.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[8] So they responded loudly, saying: ‘You’re our leader in place of Judas and your brother JoNathan!
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[9] Lead us in battle, and we’ll do whatever you tell us!’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[10] So, he assembled all the fighting men and quickly finished building JeruSalem’s walls, strengthening the city’s defenses all around.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[11] He also sent JoNathan (son of Absalom) with a powerful force to Joppa. They expelled the inhabitants and stayed there.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[12] Meanwhile, Tryphon left Ptolemais with a large army to enter the land of Judah, holding [Simon’s brother] JoNathan captive.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[13] But Simon camped at Adida, overlooking the plain.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[14] Tryphon realized Simon had taken over from his brother JoNathan and was getting ready for war against him. So, he sent messengers to Simon, saying:
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[15] ‘We are holding your brother JoNathan [as a hostage] because of the money he owed the royal treasury for different costs!
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[16] ‘Now, send 100 talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, to ensure he won’t rebel against us if we release him. Then we will release him.’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[17] Simon knew they were trying to trick him. Even so, he sent the money and the children, fearing that if he didn’t, he might make the people very angry,
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[18] (fearing the people would say, “He died because I didn’t send him the money and the children.”)
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[19] So, he sent the children and the 100 talents. But Tryphon tricked him and did not release [his brother] JoNathan.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[20] Afterward, Tryphon came to invade and destroy the city [of JeruSalem]. He marched along the road to Adora, but Simon and his army marched alongside him, blocking his path wherever he went.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[21] Meanwhile, those in the citadel sent messengers, urging Tryphon to come to them by way of the desert and send them provisions.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[22] Tryphon got all his cavalry ready to come, but that night there was a very heavy snowfall, which prevented him from coming. So, he departed and went into Gilead.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[23] As he approached Bascama, he executed [Simon’s brother] JoNathan, and JoNathan was buried there.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[24] Tryphon then went back to his own land.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[25] Simon sent for and retrieved the remains of his brother JoNathan, burying him in Modein, the city of his ancestors.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[26] All Israel mourned him deeply and grieved for many days.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[27] Simon built [a] monument over the tomb of his father and brothers, making it tall and out of polished stone, visible from all sides.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[28] He set up seven pyramids, arranged to face each other, for his father, mother, and four brothers.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[29] Around these, he placed large pillars. On the pillars, he crafted full sets of armor as an eternal memorial. Beside the armor, he carved ships, so that everyone sailing the sea could see them.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[30] This is the tomb he built in Modein, which remains to this day.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[31] Tryphon, however, betrayed King Antiochus the Younger and murdered him.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[32] He then replaced him as ruler, took the crown of Asia, and caused great devastation throughout the land.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[33] In response, Simon strengthened Judea’s defenses, building high towers, strong walls, gates, and bars around them. He also stocked these strongholds with supplies.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[34] Simon also selected men to send to King Demetrius to ask for the land to be freed from tribute payments, because Tryphon’s actions had all been acts of plunder.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[35] King Demetrius sent him a reply, agreeing to his request, and wrote him the following letter:
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[36] ‘King Demetrius to Simon, the high priest and friend of kings, and to the elders and the nation of the Jews, greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[37] ‘We’ve received the golden crown and the palm branch you sent. We’re ready to grant you great peace and to write to our officials to exempt you from taxes.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[38] All agreements we made with you remain valid, and the fortifications you’ve built will belong to you.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[39] ‘Also, we forgive you for any mistakes or offenses committed until now, and also the crown tax you owed. If anything else in JeruSalem was taxed, it will no longer be taxed.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[40] ‘And if any of your people are qualified to be appointed as our officials, they may be appointed, and let peace exist between us.’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[41] So, in the 170th year, Israel was freed from the burden of [rule by] the other races.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[42] The people of Israel started writing in their documents and contracts this: ‘In the 1st year of Simon, the great high priest, general, and leader of the Jews.’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[43] In those days, Simon set up camp against Gaza, surrounding it with his forces. He built [a] siege engine, moved it against the city, attacked one tower, and captured it.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[44] The men operating the siege engine then rushed into the city, creating a great uproar.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[45] The city’s residents, along with their women and children, climbed onto the wall, tearing their clothes. They cried out loudly, begging Simon to offer them terms of surrender.
