[1 Maccabees] [13]:[46] They said: ‘Don’t punish us for our wickedness, but show us your mercy.’
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[47] Simon made peace with them and didn’t fight them. [However,] he expelled them from the city, purified the houses that contained idols, and then entered the city with hymns and blessings.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[48] He removed all impurities from it and settled men in it who observed the Law. He strengthened the city’s defenses even more and built his own residence there.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[49] However, those in the citadel in JeruSalem were prevented from going out into the countryside to buy and sell, so they suffered from severe hunger, and many of them died of starvation.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[50] They cried out to Simon, asking to surrender. He agreed to their request, expelled them from there, and purified the citadel of its defilements.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[51] On the 23rd day of the 2nd month in the 171st year, he entered it with praise and palm branches, accompanied by: Lyres Cymbals Harps Hymns Songs Yes, because a great enemy had been defeated in Israel.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[52] He decreed that this day should be celebrated every year. He also strengthened the Temple Mount’s defenses even more, which was next to the citadel, and he and his men started living there.
[1 Maccabees] [13]:[53] Simon saw that his son John [Hyrcanus] was [a] competent man, so he appointed him as commander of all the forces, and John then lived in [the city of] Gazara.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[1] In the 172nd year, King Demetrius gathered his army and traveled to Media to gather support for his fight against Tryphon.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[2] [However,] when Arsaces, the king of Persia and Media, learned Demetrius was in his territory, he dispatched a commander to capture him alive...
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[3] The commander then attacked Demetrius’s camp, captured him, brought him to Arsaces, and threw him in prison!
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[4] During Simon’s rule, the land enjoyed peace. He dedicated himself to his nation’s well-being, and his leadership and good reputation consistently pleased them.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[5] Among his many achievements: He captured Joppa to serve as [a] harbor, providing access to the islands in the sea.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[6] He expanded his nation’s territory and took control of the land.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[7] He brought back many captives and gained control of Gazara, Beth-Zur, and the citadel [in JeruSalem]. He purified these locations, and no one could resist him.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[8] People farmed their land in peace; the land yielded its crops, and the trees in the plains produced their fruit.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[9] Older people gathered in the public squares, discussing positive matters, while young men wore splendid clothes and military uniforms.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[10] He provisioned the cities with food and strengthened their defenses, so his glorious name became known everywhere.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[11] He established peace throughout the land, and Israel rejoiced immensely.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[12] Everyone... ‘...sat under their own vine and fig tree, with no one to frighten them.’ [Micah 4:4]
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[13] Hostilities against them ceased throughout the land, and [enemy] kings were defeated during that time.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[14] He supported all the humble among his people; he meticulously followed the Law and eliminated every lawless and wicked person.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[15] He honored the holy objects and increased the number of sacred vessels.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[16] News of JoNathan’s death reached Rome and even Sparta, causing them great sorrow.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[17] But when they learned that his brother Simon had replaced him as high priest and was governing the land and its cities,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[18] they wrote to him on bronze tablets to reaffirm the friendship and alliance they had established with his brothers, Judas and JoNathan.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[19] These letters were publicly read to an assembly in JeruSalem. Here is a copy of the letters sent by the Spartans:
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[20] ‘Greetings from the rulers of Sparta and the city of Sparta to Simon, the high priest, and to the elders, the priests, and the rest of our Jewish brothers!
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[21] ‘The ambassadors you sent to us informed us of your glory and honor, and we were pleased by their arrival.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[22] We’ve recorded their statements in the public councils as follows: ‘Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater (son of Jason), ambassadors from the Jews, came to us to renew their friendship with us.’
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[23] ‘The people were pleased to receive these men with honor and to place a copy of their statements in the public records, so the Spartan people would have [a] memorial. A copy of these matters was also sent to Simon the high priest.’
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[24] Following this, Simon sent Numenius to Rome with [a] large golden shield weighing 1,000 minas, to affirm their alliance. When the people heard these words, they said:
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[25] ‘What loving kindness can we bestow upon Simon and his sons?
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[26] Because he, his brothers, and his family have stood firm, fighting Israel’s enemies and securing their freedom!’ So this was inscribed on bronze tablets and erected on [a] pillar on Mount Zion. This is a copy of the inscription:
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[27] ‘On the 18th of Elul, in the 172nd year, which marked Simon’s third year as high priest,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[28] in SaraMel, at [a] large assembly of priests, the people, national rulers, and elders of the land, it was proclaimed to us that:
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[29] ‘Since wars frequently occurred in the land, Simon, son of Mattathias, [a] descendant of Joarib, and his brothers bravely risked their lives and resisted their nation’s enemies, so their holy places and the Law could be preserved. They brought great glory to their nation.’
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[30] ‘JoNathan united their nation, became their high priest, and subsequently died.’
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[31] ‘When their enemies sought to invade their land to destroy it and seize their holy objects,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[32] Simon rose up and fought for his nation! He spent a great deal of his own money, armed his nation’s soldiers, and paid them.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[33] ‘He fortified the cities of Judea, including Beth-Zur on Judea’s borders, where the enemies’ previously stored their weapons, and he stationed [a] garrison of Jewish men there.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[34] He also fortified Joppa by the sea and Gazara on Azotus’s borders, where enemies previously resided. He settled Jews there and provided everything necessary for their rebuilding.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[35] ‘The people recognized Simon’s faithfulness and the great things he planned to do for his nation. So, they appointed him as their leader and high priest because of all these accomplishments, and because of the righteousness and faithfulness he demonstrated to his nation, and because he consistently sought to uplift his people.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[36] ‘During his time, he achieved great prosperity. He successfully expelled foreign nations from their land, including those in David’s City in JeruSalem who had built [a] fortress for themselves. From this fortress, they would attack and defile the areas around the sanctuary, causing significant harm to its purity.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[37] He settled Jewish men in it and strengthened its defenses to secure the land and the city, and he rebuilt JeruSalem’s walls.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[38] ‘King Demetrius also confirmed his high priesthood based on these actions,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[39] and made him one of his friends, bestowing great honor upon him.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[40] ‘It was also known that the Romans called the Jews friends, allies, and brothers, and that they had received Simon’s ambassadors with honor.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[41] ‘And [it’s also known that] the Jews and priests were pleased for Simon to serve as their leader and high priest into the age (until [a] faithful prophet appears)
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[42] and that he should: Serve as their general Be in charge of the holy objects Be able to appoint officials over their tasks, the land, the military, and the fortifications
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[43] Be in charge of the holy objects To be obeyed by everyone [‘Additionally:] All documents in the land should be issued in his name [He should] wear purple and gold
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[44] ‘Furthermore, it’s not lawful for anyone among the people or the priests to disregard any of these rules, or to speak against what he says, or to convene an assembly in the land without his permission, or to wear purple or [a] golden brooch.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[45] ‘Whoever acts contrary to these things or disregards any of these rules will be punished!’
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[46] All the people were pleased to grant Simon the authority to act as stated.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[47] Simon accepted this and was pleased to serve as high priest, general, and ethnarch of the Jews and priests, and to lead everyone.
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[48] They decreed that this inscription should be placed on bronze tablets and erected in the sanctuary’s enclosure in [a] prominent place,
[1 Maccabees] [14]:[49] and that copies of them should be preserved in the treasury for Simon and his sons.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[1] King Antiochus [VII Sidetes], the son of Demetrius [I Soter], sent letters from the islands to Simon, the Judeans’ priest and ethnarch, and to the whole nation.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[2] The message read: ‘King Antiochus [VII Sidetes] to Simon, the great priest and ethnarch, and to the Judeans’ nation, greetings!’
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[3] ‘Since some scoundrels have taken control of our fathers’ kingdom, I plan to take it back for myself, so I can bring it back to its original condition. I’ve hired many foreign troops and prepared warships!
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[4] ‘I want to go into the land to go after those who have corrupted our land and those who have ruined many cities in the kingdom...
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[5] Therefore, I now confirm all the exemptions that the kings before me granted you, along with any others they might have given you:
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[6] ‘You’re allowed to mint your own coins in your land.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[7] ‘JeruSalem and the holy places will be free. ‘All the weapons you’ve prepared and the fortifications you’ve built, which you currently control, will remain yours.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[8] ‘All royal debts, both current and future, are now permanently forgiven for you into the age.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[9] ‘Once we’ve established our kingdom, we’ll greatly honor you, your nation, and the temple, so your glory will be recognized throughout the entire earth.’
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[10] In the 174th year, Antiochus marched into his fathers’ land. All the forces joined him, so only a few remained with Tryphon.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[11] King Antiochus pursued him, and Tryphon fled to Dora, a city on the coast.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[12] Tryphon knew that things had gone badly for him, and his forces had deserted him.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[13] Antiochus then camped outside Dora with 120,000 warriors and 8,000 cavalry.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[14] He encircled the city, and his ships joined the siege from the sea. He attacked the city from both land and sea, allowing no one to enter or leave.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[15] Meanwhile, Numenius and his companions arrived back from Rome, carrying letters addressed to various kings and lands. The letters read as follows:
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[16] ‘Lucius, the Romans’ Consul, to King Ptolemy, greetings!
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[17] ‘The Judeans’ ambassadors, our friends and allies, have come to us, sent by Simon the high priest and Judea’s people, to renew their long-standing friendship and alliance with us.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[18] They brought with them a golden shield weighing 5,000 minas.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[19] ‘Therefore, we’ve decided to write to the kings and lands, telling them not to harm the Judeans, nor to wage war against them, their cities, or their lands, and not to ally with those who wage war against them.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[20] ‘We’ve also decided it was right to accept the shield from them.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[21] Therefore, if any scoundrels have escaped from their land and taken shelter with you, hand them over to Simon the high priest, so he can bring them to justice according to their law.’
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[22] He also wrote these same things to: King Demetrius [II Nicator] Attalus [II Philadelphus] Arathes [II] Arsaces [I of Parthia]
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[23] And [he further wrote] to all the lands, including: [Lampsacus] The Spartans Delos Myndus Sicyon Caria Samos Pamphylia Lycia Halicarnassus Cos Side Aradus Rhodes Phaselis Gortyna Cnidus Cyprus Cyrene
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[24] A copy of these letters was also sent to Simon the high priest.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[25] King Antiochus, for the second time, camped outside Dora. He attacked the city relentlessly, using all available methods and siege engines, trapping Tryphon inside, preventing him from entering or leaving.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[26] [High priest] Simon sent him 2,000 chosen men to help him, along with silver, gold, and plenty of supplies.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[27] However, Antiochus refused to accept them. Instead, he canceled all the agreements he had previously made with Simon and became hostile toward him.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[28] He then sent Athenobius, one of his friends, to deliver a message to Simon, saying: ‘You’re in control of Joppa, Gazara, and the citadel in JeruSalem, which are cities that belong to my kingdom!
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[29] You’ve ruined their territories, caused great damage to the land, and taken control of many places within my kingdom!
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[30] ‘Therefore, hand over the cities you’ve seized, and the tribute from the places you’ve taken control of, especially those on the borders of Judea.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[31] ‘Otherwise, pay 500 talents of silver as compensation, and another 500 talents for the destruction you’ve caused and for the tribute owed by the cities. If you refuse, we’ll come and wage war against you.’
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[32] Athenobius, the king’s friend, came to JeruSalem and was astonished by Simon’s splendor, which included a cup decorated with gold and silver and an impressive display of wealth. He then relayed the king’s demands to Simon and his people.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[33] Simon replied to him: ‘We haven’t taken foreign land, nor have we taken foreign possessions. Instead, we’ve taken control of our fathers’ inheritance, which our enemies unjustly took from us in the past.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[34] ‘Now that we have the opportunity, we’re holding firmly to our and our fathers’ inheritance.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[35] As for Joppa and Gazara, which you demand, these cities caused great harm to our people and our land. For these, we’ll pay 100 talents.’ Athenobius did not respond to his offer.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[36] Athenobius returned to the king in a rage, reporting Simon’s words, describing his splendor, and reporting everything else he’d seen. The king became extremely angry!
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[37] Meanwhile, Tryphon boarded a ship and fled to Orthosia.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[38] The king then appointed Cendebaeus as the general of the coastal region and provided him with infantry and cavalry troops.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[39] He commanded Cendebaeus to camp facing Judea, to rebuild Kedron, to strengthen the cities, and to wage war against the people. The king himself, however, continued to pursue Tryphon.
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[40] Well, Cendebaeus arrived at Jamnia and began to provoke the people. [He was] invading Judea, taking captives, and committing murder!
[1 Maccabees] [15]:[41] He rebuilt Kedron and stationed cavalry and other troops there to patrol the roads of Judea, just as the king had commanded him.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[1] John [Hyrcanus] left Gazara and told his father Simon what Cendebaeus was doing. Simon called his two elder sons, Judas and John, and said to them:
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[2] ‘I, my brothers, and my [whole] family have fought Israel’s battles since we were young, until now. We often succeeded in our efforts to rescue Israel.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[3] ‘But now I’ve grown old. You, however, by [His] mercy, are strong and in your prime. Take over for me and your uncle; go and fight for our nation! ‘May help from heaven be with you!’
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[4] Then he chose 20,000 warriors and cavalry from the land. They marched against Cendebaeus and camped in Modin.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[5] Early the next morning, they moved onto the plain. Suddenly, they saw [a] large force of infantry and cavalry approaching them! [A wadi in a] winter torrent separated the two armies.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[6] John and his men camped facing the enemy. He saw his own troops hesitating to cross the wadi, so he crossed first. When his men saw him, they followed him across.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[7] Then he arranged his troops, positioning the cavalry among the infantry. The enemy’s cavalry, however, was very numerous.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[8] They blew the trumpets, and Cendebaeus’s forces were completely defeated. Many of his men were wounded or killed, while the rest fled to their fortress!
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[9] Meanwhile, Judas, John’s brother, was wounded. John, however, pursued the enemy until they reached Kedron, a place Cendebaeus had built.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[10] They fled to the towers on Azotus’ plain, and John set the fortress ablaze. About 1,000 men died there, and John returned safely to Judea.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[11] Meanwhile, [a man named] Ptolemy (son of Abub) had become the general of the plain of Jericho. He was very wealthy, owning much silver and gold,
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[12] because he was the high priest’s son-in-law.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[13] His head filled with ambition, he wanted to take control of the land [of Judah]. So he started forming treacherous plans against Simon and his sons, with the intention of destroying them.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[14] Simon, meanwhile, was inspecting the cities throughout the land and managing their matters. In the 177th year, in the 11th month (Shebat), he went down to Jericho, accompanied by [his sons] Mattathias and Judas, as well as his other sons.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[15] Ptolemy (son of Abub) welcomed them to the small fortress called Dok, which he himself had built. He welcomed them with [a] great banquet, but he had hidden men there, with treacherous plans...
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[16] When Simon and his sons were drunk, Ptolemy and his men stood up, grabbed their weapons, and stormed into the banquet hall! They killed Simon, his sons, and some of his attendants.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[17] Thus, he committed [a] terrible betrayal, repaying good with evil.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[18] Ptolemy then wrote to the king, reporting these events and requesting the king send him troops for assistance, so he could hand over their land and cities to him.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[19] He also sent other men to Gazara to kill John. He also sent letters to the military commanders (chiliarchs), inviting them to join him and promising them silver, gold, and other gifts.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[20] He also sent others to capture JeruSalem and the Temple Mount.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[21] However, someone raced ahead to inform John in Gazara that his father and brothers had been killed, and that Ptolemy had also dispatched men to kill him.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[22] When John heard this, he was deeply shocked. He immediately arrested the men who had come to kill him and executed them, knowing they intended to kill him.
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[23] The rest of John’s actions, his wars, his brave deeds, the walls he built, and all his other accomplishments,
[1 Maccabees] [16]:[24] these are recorded in the records of his high priesthood, from the time he became high priest after his father.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[1] JosiAh celebrated the Passover in JeruSalem for his Lord. They sacrificed the Passover on the 14th day of the first month,
[1 Esdras] [1]:[2] after he had organized the priests by their divisions, dressed in the Lord’s temple.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[3] He also told the Levites, who served in the temple for Israel, to dedicate themselves to the Lord in the place where the holy Chest of the Lord was, in the house that King Solomon, David’s son, had built. He also told the Levites:
[1 Esdras] [1]:[4] ‘You’re not to carry it on your shoulders. ‘Now, serve your [Jehovah] God and serve his nation Israel! ‘Prepare yourselves according to your ancestral houses and tribes, following the arrangements made by David, Israel’s king, and his son Solomon.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[5] Stand in the sanctuary according to your family divisions as Levites, before your brothers, Israel’s sons.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[6] ‘In proper order, sacrifice the Passover lamb and prepare the sacrifices for your brothers. Perform the Passover according to the Lord’s command given to Moses.’
[1 Esdras] [1]:[7] Well, JosiAh donated 30,000 lambs and young goats, and 3,000 calves to the people who were present. These came from the king’s own possessions, as he had announced, and were given to the people, priests, and Levites.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[8] Helkiah, Zachariah, and Jehiel, who oversaw the temple, gave the priests 2,600 sheep and 300 calves for the Passover.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[9] Jeconiah, Shemaiah, Nathanael his brother, Hashabiah, Jehiel, and Joram, who were commanders of a thousand, gave the Levites 1,000 sheep and 700 calves for the Passover.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[10] So, with these preparations complete, the priests and Levites took their proper places, holding the unleavened bread. They stood before the people, arranged by their tribes and ancestral divisions, to offer to the Lord according to what was written in Moses’ book. This was done in the morning.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[11] They roasted the Passover offerings over fire as was customary. They also boiled the sacrifices in bronze vessels and cauldrons, creating a pleasing aroma. Then they distributed them to all the people.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[12] Afterward, they prepared for themselves and for their brothers, the priests, Aaron’s sons.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[13] The priests were busy offering up the fat portions until late in the evening. So, the Levites prepared for themselves and for their brothers, the priests, Aaron’s sons.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[14] The singers, Asaph’s sons, were in their appointed places, following David’s arrangements. Asaph, Zachariah, and Jeduthun were the ones the king had appointed.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[15] The doorkeepers were at every gate. No one needed to leave their assigned duty, because their brothers, the Levites, had made preparations for them.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[16] So, the service of the Lord’s sacrifice was completed that day. The Passover offerings were brought, and the sacrifices were offered on the Lord’s altar, according to King JosiAh’s command.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[17] The Israelites who were present at that time celebrated the Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[18] No such Passover had been celebrated in Israel since the time of Samuel the prophet.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[19] Yes, none of Israel’s kings had celebrated a Passover like the one JosiAh celebrated, along with the priests, the Levites, the Judeans, and all Israel who were present in JeruSalem!
[1 Esdras] [1]:[20] This Passover was celebrated in the 18th year of JosiAh’s reign.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[21] JosiAh’s deeds were upright before his Lord, performed with a heart full of devotion...
[1 Esdras] [1]:[22] However, what concerned him has been recorded from earlier times: it was about those who had sinned and acted impiously against the Lord, more impiously than any other nation or kingdom, and this grieved him... And the Lord’s words concerning Israel came true.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[23] After all these deeds of JosiAh, Pharaoh, Egypt’s king, came to wage war at Carchemish by the Euphrates. JosiAh went out to meet him.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[24] Egypt’s king sent messengers to him, saying: ‘What concern is this of yours, O Judah’s king?
[1 Esdras] [1]:[25] ‘I haven’t been sent against you by [Jehovah] God, because my war is by the Euphrates. And now [Jehovah] is with me, helping me to hurry. Withdraw, and don’t oppose the Lord.’
[1 Esdras] [1]:[26] But JosiAh didn’t turn his chariot around... Instead, he tried to wage war against [Pharaoh], not paying attention to Jeremiah the prophet’s words, which came from [Jehovah].
[1 Esdras] [1]:[27] Instead, he engaged him in battle in the plain of Megiddo. And the rulers came down to King JosiAh.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[28] The king said to his servants: ‘Take me away from the battle, for I’m severely wounded.’ His servants immediately removed him from the battle line,
[1 Esdras] [1]:[29] and he got into his second chariot. When he was brought back to JeruSalem, he died and was buried in his ancestral tomb.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[30] All Judah mourned JosiAh. Jeremiah the prophet lamented for JosiAh, and the leaders, along with women, mourned him up to this very day. And this practice was established to be observed by all the people of Israel into the age.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[31] Also, these things have been recorded in the Book of Chronicles concerning Judah’s kings: every single deed of JosiAh, his glory, and his understanding of [Jehovah]‘s law. Both his deeds and the present events have been recorded in the book of Israel’s and Judah’s kings.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[32] The people of the land took JeconiAh [also known as JehoAhaz], JosiAh’s son, and made him king in place of his father JosiAh. He was 23 years old.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[33] He reigned in Israel and JeruSalem for three months. Then Egypt’s king restored him to reign in JeruSalem,
[1 Esdras] [1]:[34] and fined the nation 100 talents [~7,000 lb / 3,200 kg] of silver and one talent [~70 lb / 32 kg] of gold.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[35] Egypt’s king then appointed JehoiAkim, his brother, as Judah’s and JeruSalem’s king.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[36] JehoiAkim imprisoned the nobles, but he seized Zarius, his brother, and brought him up from Egypt.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[37] JehoiAkim was 25 years old when he began to reign over Judah and JeruSalem, and he did what was evil in [Jehovah]‘s sight.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[38] After him, NebuChadnezzar, Babylon’s king, came and bound him with bronze chains, leading him away to Babylon.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[39] NebuChadnezzar also took some of the Lord’s sacred vessels, carried them away, and stored them in his temple in Babylon.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[40] The things recorded about him, his uncleanness, and his impiety have been written down in the Book of the Kings’ Chronicles.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[41] His son JehoiAkim [also known as JehoiAchin] reigned in his place. When he was appointed, he was eight[teen] years old.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[42] He reigned in JeruSalem for three months and ten days, and he did what was evil in [Jehovah]‘s sight.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[43] After one year, NebuChadnezzar sent for him and transferred him to Babylon, along with the Lord’s sacred vessels,
[1 Esdras] [1]:[44] and appointed ZedekiAh [to be] king of Judah and JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[45] He did what was evil in [Jehovah]‘s sight, and he wasn’t ashamed by Jeremiah the prophet’s words spoken by the Lord.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[46] Even though he had sworn an oath to King NebuChadnezzar in the Lord’s name, he broke his oath and rebelled. He became stubborn and hardened his heart, breaking the laws of [Jehovah], Israel’s God.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[47] Also, the people’s leaders and the priests committed many impious and lawless acts... Worse than all the nations’ abominations! They also even defiled the Lord’s temple, which was perfected in JeruSalem!
[1 Esdras] [1]:[48] Their fathers’ King, [that is, God,] sent word to them through his messenger, calling them back, because he had compassion on them and on his dwelling place.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[49] But they scoffed at his messengers. On the very day [Jehovah] spoke, they mocked his prophets... This continued until he became so angry with his nation because of their impious deeds that he commanded the Babylonian kings to come against them!
[1 Esdras] [1]:[50] These Babylonians killed their young men with the sword around the Holy Temple. They spared no one — neither young men nor virgins, old men nor young — but delivered everyone into their hands.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[51] They took: all the Lord’s sacred vessels, both great and small the Lord’s Chests the royal treasuries...and carried them away to Babylon!
[1 Esdras] [1]:[52] They burned the Lord’s house, tore down JeruSalem’s walls, and set its towers on fire.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[53] They utterly destroyed all her glorious things. As for those who remained, he led them away with the sword to Babylon.
[1 Esdras] [1]:[54] They became servants to him and his sons until the Persians came to power, fulfilling the Lord’s word spoken by Jeremiah. [Jeremiah 25:11]
[1 Esdras] [1]:[55] Yes, until the land had enjoyed its Sabbaths, the whole time of its desolation, it kept Sabbath — until the 70 years were over.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[1] In the first year of Cyrus, King of Persia, [Jehovah]‘s word spoken by Jeremiah was about to come true.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[2] [Jehovah] stirred up the spirit of Cyrus, Persia’s king. So he issued a proclamation throughout his whole kingdom, both verbally and in writing, saying:
[1 Esdras] [2]:[3] ‘This is what Cyrus, Persia’s king, says: '[Jehovah] of Israel, [Jehovah] the Most High, has made me king over the whole earth,
[1 Esdras] [2]:[4] and he told me to build his house in JeruSalem, which is in Judea.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[5] ‘So, if you are one of his people, may their Lord be with them! They should go up to JeruSalem in Judea and build the house of Israel’s Lord! This is the Lord who lives in JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[6] ‘Therefore, everyone in various places should help those who are returning with: Gold Silver Gifts Horses Cattle ‘Plus other offerings they’ve promised for the Lord’s temple in JeruSalem.’
[1 Esdras] [2]:[7] So, the tribal family heads of Judah and Benjamin, along with the priests and Levites (indeed, everyone whose spirit [Jehovah] had stirred up) got ready to go up and build the Lord’s house in JeruSalem!
[1 Esdras] [2]:[8] Their neighbors helped them in every way, giving silver, gold, horses, cattle, and many other generous offerings, because many people’s minds had been stirred.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[9] King Cyrus also brought out the Lord’s holy vessels, which NebuChadnezzar had taken from JeruSalem and put in his idol temple.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[10] Then, Cyrus, Persia’s king, gave them to his treasurer, Mithridates.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[11] Mithridates then delivered them to Sanabassar, Judea’s governor.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[12] The list of these items was: 1,000 golden libation bowls 1,000 silver libation bowls 29 silver censers 30 golden bowls 210 silver bowls 1,000 other vessels
[1 Esdras] [2]:[13] In total, there were 5,469 vessels, both gold and silver.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[14] Sanabassar took them up to JeruSalem with those who had returned from captivity in Babylon.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[15] During the reign of Artaxerxes (Persia’s king), Belemus, Mithradates, Tabellius, Rathymus, Beeltethmus, Samellius the scribe, and their other associates living in Samaria and other regions, wrote this letter against the people living in Judea and JeruSalem:
[1 Esdras] [2]:[16] ‘To King Artaxerxes, our lord, from your servants Rathymus, the chief administrator, Samellius the scribe, the rest of their council, and those in Coele-Syria and Phoenicia:
[1 Esdras] [2]:[17] ‘We want our lord the king to know that the Jews who came from you to us have arrived in JeruSalem and are living in that rebellious and wicked city. They’re repairing its marketplaces and walls, and laying the foundations for a temple.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[18] ‘So, if this city is rebuilt and its walls are completed, they will certainly refuse to pay taxes and will even rebel against kings. ‘Since the temple’s work is underway, we think it’s wise not to ignore this but to inform our lord the king, so that, if you wish, an investigation can be done into your predecessors’ records.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[19] You’ll find in the records what has been written about these matters, and you’ll learn that this city has always been rebellious, causing trouble for kings and cities. The Jews there have been rebellious and organizing sieges since ancient times, which is why this city was destroyed.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[20] ‘So, we’re informing you, O lord king, that if this city is rebuilt and its walls are put up, you won’t have access to Coele-Syria and Phoenicia anymore.’
[1 Esdras] [2]:[21] The king then sent this reply to Rathymus, the chief administrator, Beeltethmus, Samellius the scribe, and their other associates living in Samaria, Syria, and Phoenicia:
[1 Esdras] [2]:[22] ‘I’ve read the letter you sent me. So I ordered an investigation, and it was found that this city has long been hostile to kings,
[1 Esdras] [2]:[23] and its people have been starting rebellions and wars. Powerful and oppressive kings once ruled in JeruSalem, collecting taxes from Coele-Syria and Phoenicia.
[1 Esdras] [2]:[24] ‘Therefore, I now command that these people be stopped from rebuilding the city, and that care be taken to prevent anything else from happening that might lead to greater wickedness and trouble for kings.’
[1 Esdras] [2]:[25] When King Artaxerxes’s decree was read, Rathymus, Samellius the scribe, and their associates immediately went to JeruSalem with cavalry and a military escort... They began to stop those who were building, and the temple’s construction in JeruSalem stopped until the second year of Persian King Darius’ reign.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[1] King Darius hosted a grand feast for everyone under his rule, including his household staff and all the nobles from Media and Persia.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[2] This also included all the satraps, generals, and local governors who served him, from India to Ethiopia, across 127 regions.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[3] They ate and drank as much as they wanted, then left. King Darius, however, went to his bedroom, slept, and then woke up.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[4] Then the three young bodyguards, who guarded the king, said to each other:
[1 Esdras] [3]:[5] ‘Let’s each suggest [a] statement. Whichever statement is judged wisest, King Darius will give great gifts and wonderful rewards to the person who wrote it!
[1 Esdras] [3]:[6] ‘This includes: A purple robe to wear Golden cups to drink from A gold bed to sleep on A chariot with golden reins A fine linen turban A necklace for his neck.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[7] He’ll also be made second in command to Darius because of his wisdom, and he’ll be called a relative of Darius!’
[1 Esdras] [3]:[8] So each man wrote down his statement, sealed it, and put it under King Darius’s pillow. They said:
[1 Esdras] [3]:[9] ‘When the king wakes up, he’ll be given the writings! The person whose statement the king and the three nobles of Persia decide is the wisest will win, just as we’ve agreed.’
[1 Esdras] [3]:[10] The first wrote: ‘Wine is the strongest.’
[1 Esdras] [3]:[11] The second wrote: ‘The king is the strongest.’
[1 Esdras] [3]:[12] The third wrote: ‘Women are the strongest, but above all else, truth wins.’
[1 Esdras] [3]:[13] When the king woke up, they took the writings and gave them to him, and he read them.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[14] Then he sent for and summoned all the nobles from Persia and Media, along with the satraps, generals, local governors, and officials. He sat down in the council room, and the writings were read aloud to everyone.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[15] Then he said: ‘Call the young men. They need to present their arguments.’ So they were called, and they came in.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[16] The assembly told them: ‘Explain what you’ve written to us.’
[1 Esdras] [3]:[17] ‘Gentlemen, wine is incredibly powerful! It tricks the minds of everyone who drinks it.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[18] ‘It makes everyone’s mind the same, whether they’re a king or an orphan, a servant or a free person, poor or rich.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[19] ‘Also, it turns every mind into a state of celebration and joy, making people forget all their sorrows and debts.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[20] It makes all hearts feel rich, and causes them to forget about kings and satraps. It even makes them talk about everything as if it’s about money.
[1 Esdras] [3]:[21] ‘When people drink, they forget to be friendly to their friends and brothers. Soon, they’re even drawing swords against each other...
[1 Esdras] [3]:[22] ‘And when they wake up from the wine, they don’t remember what they did!
[1 Esdras] [3]:[23] ‘Gentlemen, doesn’t wine truly win, since it forces people to act like this?’ He then fell silent.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[1] The second speaker, who had talked about the king’s power, then began to speak. He began:
[1 Esdras] [4]:[2] ‘Men, don’t people control the earth, the sea, and everything in them?
[1 Esdras] [4]:[3] But the king overpowers, rules, and masters them; they do everything he tells them!
[1 Esdras] [4]:[4] ‘If he tells them to wage war against each other, don’t they do it? If he sends them out against enemies, they march out and conquer mountains, walls, and towers.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[5] They kill and are killed, and they don’t disobey the king’s command, do they? If they conquer, they bring everything to the king. And if they plunder, they bring all the rest as well.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[6] ‘And those who don’t serve in war or fight, but farm the land — when they sow and reap, don’t they bring their produce to the king? They also force each other to bring their taxes to the king.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[7] ‘And even if he’s alone, if he says to kill, they kill. ‘If he says to release, they release.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[8] ‘If he says to strike, they strike. ‘If he says to destroy, they destroy. ‘If he says to build, they build.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[9] ‘If he says to cut down, they cut down. ‘If he says to plant, they plant.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[10] ‘All his people and his forces obey him. ‘What’s more, while he himself relaxes, eats, drinks, and sleeps,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[11] they guard him. No one can leave to do his own work, and they don’t disobey him.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[12] ‘Men, how can the king not be the most powerful, since everyone obeys him like this?’ Thus, he fell silent.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[13] Then the third speaker, [the son of] ZerubbaBel, who had talked about women and truth, began to speak. He said:
[1 Esdras] [4]:[14] ‘Men, isn’t the king great? Aren’t men numerous? And isn’t wine strong? Who then is their master, or who rules over them? ‘Isn’t it women?
[1 Esdras] [4]:[15] ‘Women gave birth to the king and all the people who rule the sea and the earth.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[16] Men came into being from them... And it was women who nourished those who planted the vineyards where wine is made.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[17] They make men’s clothing, and they bring honor to men. ‘Men can’t exist without women!
[1 Esdras] [4]:[18] ‘If men gather gold, silver, and every beautiful thing, and then they see a single woman beautiful in form and beauty,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[19] they abandon all these things and stare at her with open mouths. They all prefer her to gold, silver, and every beautiful thing!
[1 Esdras] [4]:[20] ‘A man leaves his own father who raised him, and his own land, and clings to his own wife.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[21] With his wife, he gives up his very life. He remembers neither father, mother, nor land.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[22] ‘From this, you should know that women rule over you, shouldn’t you? Don’t you toil and labor, and give and bring everything to women?
[1 Esdras] [4]:[23] A man takes his sword and goes out to travel, to plunder, and to steal, even sailing the sea and rivers,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[24] he faces the lion, and doesn’t he walk in darkness? When he steals, snatches, and strips, he brings it back to his beloved!
[1 Esdras] [4]:[25] ‘A man loves his own wife more than his father and mother.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[26] Many have been driven to despair because of women, and haven’t they become slaves because of them?
[1 Esdras] [4]:[27] ‘Many have perished, stumbled, and sinned because of women!
[1 Esdras] [4]:[28] ‘Now, don’t you believe me? Isn’t the king great in his authority? Don’t all lands fear to challenge him?
[1 Esdras] [4]:[29] ‘I saw him and Apame, the king’s concubine and the admirable Bartacus’s daughter, sitting at the king’s right hand,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[30] taking the diadem from the king’s head and putting it on her own, and even slapping the king with her left hand.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[31] What’s more, the king gazed at her with an open mouth! ‘If she laughed at him, he laughed. But if she became angry with him, he flattered her so she might be reconciled to him!
[1 Esdras] [4]:[32] ‘Men, how can women not be powerful, seeing that they act like this?’
[1 Esdras] [4]:[33] Then the king and the magnates looked at each other. He then began to speak about truth. He said:
[1 Esdras] [4]:[34] ‘Men, aren’t women strong? ‘The earth is great, heaven is high, and the sun is swift in its course. It revolves in the circle of the heavens and returns to its place in one day.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[35] Isn’t the one who makes these things great? ‘And truth is great and stronger than all things.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[36] ‘All the earth calls upon truth, and heaven praises it. All works are shaken and tremble, and there is nothing unjust about it.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[37] ‘Wine is unjust, the king is unjust, women are unjust, all men’s sons are unjust, and all their works are unjust — aren’t all such things?! There is no truth in them, and they will perish in their injustice.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[38] ‘But truth remains and is strong into the age... It lives and prevails into the age of the age.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[39] ‘With truth, there’s no partiality or distinction. Doesn’t it do what is just for all the unjust and wicked? And everyone is pleased with its works,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[40] and in its judgment there’s nothing unjust. Truth possesses strength, the kingdom, authority, and majesty for all the ages! Praised be The God of truth!’
[1 Esdras] [4]:[41] Then he stopped speaking. All the people shouted aloud, saying: ‘Great is truth, and it prevails!’
[1 Esdras] [4]:[42] Then the king said to him: ‘Ask for whatever you wish, beyond what is written, and we will give it to you, since you’ve been found to be the wisest. You’ll sit next to me and be called my relative.’
[1 Esdras] [4]:[43] Then he said to the king: ‘Remember the vow you made to rebuild JeruSalem on the day you received your kingdom,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[44] and to send back all the vessels taken from JeruSalem that Cyrus had set aside, when he vowed to destroy Babylon and vowed to send them back there.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[45] ‘You also vowed to rebuild the temple which the Judeans burned, when Judea was laid waste by the Babylonians.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[46] Now, this is what I request, Lord King, and what I ask of you. ‘Isn’t this the great favor from you? Therefore, I beg you to fulfill the vow you made from your own mouth to the King of Heaven.’
[1 Esdras] [4]:[47] Then King Darius stood up and kissed him [on the cheek]. He then wrote letters to all the: Stewards Local rulers Generals Satraps...instructing them to escort him and all those with him who were going up to rebuild JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[48] He also wrote letters to all the local rulers in: Coele-Syria Phoenicia Lebanon...instructing them to transport cedar wood from Lebanon to JeruSalem, so they could build the city with him.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[49] He also wrote to all the Judeans who were returning from the kingdom to Judea about their freedom, stating that no: Powerful person Satrap Local ruler Steward...should enter their homes,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[50] and that all the land they would possess should be exempt from tax for them, and that the Babylonians should release the villages they held from the Judeans.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[51] And for the building of the temple, 20 talents [~1,400 lb / 640 kg] a year were to be given until it was completed;
[1 Esdras] [4]:[52] and for burnt offerings to be consumed daily upon the altar, as they were commanded to offer 17 [talents] [~1,190 lb / 544 kg], and an additional 10 talents [~700 lb / 320 kg] each year.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[53] Also: For all those coming from Babylonia to establish the city, freedom was to be granted to them and their children, and to all the priests who were coming.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[54] He wrote about the provisions and the priestly vestments in which they were to serve there.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[55] He wrote to the Levites to give them provisions until the day the house was completed and JeruSalem was rebuilt.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[56] He wrote to all those guarding the city to give them allotments and wages.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[57] He sent out all the vessels that Cyrus had set apart from Babylon. And everything that Cyrus had commanded to be done, he himself also commanded to be done and sent out to JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[58] Well, when the young man left [the palace], he lifted his face to heaven, facing JeruSalem, and praised the King of Heaven, saying:
[1 Esdras] [4]:[59] ‘Victory comes from You, Wisdom comes from You, And Yours is the glory. I am Your servant.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[60] ‘Praised are You, Who has given me wisdom. And I give thanks to You, Master of our fathers.’
[1 Esdras] [4]:[61] So he took the letters and went out to Babylon, and reported to all his brothers.
[1 Esdras] [4]:[62] They praised The God of their fathers, because he had granted them relief and freedom,
[1 Esdras] [4]:[63] to go up and rebuild JeruSalem and the temple where his name was invoked. They feasted with music and joy for seven days.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[1] After this, leaders of ancestral families were chosen to go up, organized by their tribes, along with their wives, sons, daughters, servants, and livestock.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[2] Darius also sent 1,000 horsemen with them to make sure they returned safely to JeruSalem, bringing musical instruments, drums, and flutes.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[3] He also arranged for all their celebrating brothers to go with them.

[1 Esdras] [5]:[43] When the leaders of the ancestral families arrived at God’s temple in JeruSalem, they vowed to rebuild the temple on its original site, as much as they could afford.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[44] They contributed to the temple’s treasury for the construction work: 1,000 minas of gold 5,000 minas of silver 100 priestly robes
[1 Esdras] [5]:[45] The priests, the Levites, and some of the people settled in JeruSalem and the surrounding land. The temple-singers, doorkeepers, and all the rest of Israel settled in their villages.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[46] When the 7th month arrived, and Israel’s people were in their own towns, they unitedly gathered in the open square in front of the first gate, which faced east.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[47] Jesus, Josedek’s son, and his priestly brothers, along with Zorobabel, Salathiel’s son, and his brothers, stood up and prepared Israel’s God’s altar,
[1 Esdras] [5]:[48] to offer burnt offerings on it, as commanded in the book of Moses, the man of God.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[49] Foreigners [who lived] in the land gathered around them as they set themselves up at the altar in its proper place. Even though the foreigners were hostile to them, and all the nations on the earth had overcome them, they still offered sacrifices at the appointed times, burnt offerings to [Jehovah], both morning and evening.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[50] They also kept the Festival of Temporary Structures as written in the Law, and offered daily sacrifices, as was proper.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[51] Afterward, they offered regular offerings, and sacrifices for Sabbaths, New Moons, and all other special feasts.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[52] Everyone who had made a vow to God began to offer sacrifices to God from the New Moon of the first month, even though God’s temple hadn’t been built yet.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[53] They gave silver to the stonecutters and carpenters, as well as supplies, food, and gifts to the Sidonians and Tyrians. This was so they would bring cedar wood from Lebanon and transport it by rafts to Joppa’s harbor, as decreed for them by Cyrus, the Persians’ king.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[54] In the 2nd year, in the 2nd month, Zorobabel (Salathiel’s son), Jesus (Josedek’s son), and their brothers, the priests (the Levites), and everyone who had returned from captivity to JeruSalem, arrived at God’s temple in JeruSalem and began the work.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[55] They began to lay the foundation of God’s temple on the New Moon of the 2nd month of the 2nd year after their arrival in Judea and JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[56] They appointed the Levites, aged 20 and older, to oversee the Lord’s work: Jesus, with his sons and brothers Damadiel his brother Jesus Hemadaboun’s sons Judah Eiliadoun’s son’s sons Yes, with their sons and brothers, all the Levites stood together as overseers of the work in the Lord’s house. The builders then [began] to build the Lord’s temple.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[57] The priests stood in their robes, with trumpets and other musical instruments. Asaph’s sons, who were Levites, with cymbals, sang praise to [Jehovah] and praised him, according to David, Israel’s king’s custom.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[58] They shouted with hymns, praising [Jehovah], for his goodness and his glory endure into the ages for all Israel...
[1 Esdras] [5]:[59] All the people blew trumpets and shouted loudly, praising [Jehovah] for [Jehovah]‘s house’s rebuilding!
[1 Esdras] [5]:[60] But many of the priests, Levites, and family heads (the elders who had seen the previous temple) wept loudly and bitterly when this temple was being built,
[1 Esdras] [5]:[61] while many others shouted with trumpets and great joy.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[62] As a result, the people couldn’t tell the sound of the trumpets from the sound of the people’s weeping, because the crowd was making such a loud noise with trumpets that it could be heard from a great distance.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[63] Well, when the enemies of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin heard this, they came to find out what the trumpet sound was...
[1 Esdras] [5]:[64] They learned that those who’d returned from captivity were building the temple to [Jehovah], Israel’s God.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[65] So they approached Zorobabel, Jesus, and the family heads, saying to them: ‘Let us build with you,
[1 Esdras] [5]:[66] because we worship your Lord just as you do, and we’ve been sacrificing to him ever since the days of Asbakaphath, the Assyrians’ king, who brought us here.’
[1 Esdras] [5]:[67] But Zorobabel, Jesus, and Israel’s family leaders said to them: ‘It’s not for you to build [a] house for our [Jehovah] God.
[1 Esdras] [5]:[68] We alone will build for the Lord of Israel, just as Cyrus, the Persians’ king, commanded us.’
[1 Esdras] [5]:[69] Yes, the people of the land opposed those in Judea and harassed them, preventing them from building...
[1 Esdras] [5]:[70] They made plans, stirred up the people, and formed conspiracies, preventing the building from being completed throughout King Cyrus’ lifetime. They were prevented from building for two years, until Darius’ reign.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[1] In the second year of Darius’s reign, the prophets Haggai and Zechariah, Iddo’s son, prophesied to the Jews living in Judea and JeruSalem. They spoke to them in [Jehovah]‘s name, Israel’s God.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[2] Then Zerubbabel, Salathiel’s son, and Jeshua, Jozedek’s son, began building the Lord’s house in JeruSalem. The Lord’s prophets were there, helping them.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[3] At that same time, Sisinnes, Syria and Phoenicia’s governor, along with Sathrabouzanes and their associates, came to them
[1 Esdras] [6]:[4] and asked: ‘By whose command are you building this house and finishing this roof and all these other parts? And who are the builders doing this work?’
[1 Esdras] [6]:[5] The Jews’ elders, who had returned from captivity, received loving kindness from the Lord, as he watched over them.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[6] They were not stopped from building until a report could be sent to Darius about them and a reply received.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[7] This is a copy of the letter that Sisinnes, Syria and Phoenicia’s governor, along with Sathrabourzanes and their associates, who were rulers in Syria and Phoenicia, wrote and sent to Darius. It said: ‘To King Darius, greetings.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[8] ‘Our lord the king should know that when we came to Judea’s land and JeruSalem’s city, we found the Jews’ elders who had returned from captivity in JeruSalem’s city building a great, new Lord’s house. They were using expensive cut stones and timbers for the walls.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[9] ‘They were doing this work diligently; the work was succeeding for them, and it was being completed with great honor and care.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[10] ‘So we questioned these elders, asking: ‘By whose command are you building this house and laying the foundations for this construction?’
[1 Esdras] [6]:[11] ‘Therefore, we asked them about the men leading this work, so we could inform you and write to you. We also asked for a list of names of those in charge.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[12] ‘But they replied, saying: ‘We are the Lord’s servants, who created the heavens and the earth.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[13] This house was built many years ago by [a] great and mighty Israel’s king, and he finished it.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[14] But because our ancestors greatly angered and sinned against the Lord, Israel’s God in heaven, he handed them over to NebuChadnezzar, Babylon’s king, the Chaldeans’ king;
[1 Esdras] [6]:[15] who tore down and burned the house down, and took the people captive to Babylon.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[16] ‘However, in Cyrus’s first year of reign, Babylonia’s king, King Cyrus issued an order to rebuild this house,
[1 Esdras] [6]:[17] and the sacred gold and silver vessels, which NebuChadnezzar had taken from the house in JeruSalem and placed in his own temple, King Cyrus brought out of the temple in Babylonia again, and gave them to Zerubbabel and Sabanassar, the governor.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[18] ‘He was commanded to bring all these vessels back and place them in the temple in JeruSalem, and that the Lord’s temple should be built on that very site.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[19] Then Sanabassarus came and laid the foundations for [Jehovah]‘s house in JeruSalem, and from then until now, it has been under construction but isn’t finished.’
[1 Esdras] [6]:[20] ‘So now, O king, please have a search made in our lord the king’s royal archives in Babylon,
[1 Esdras] [6]:[21] and if it is found that the building of the Lord’s house in JeruSalem was indeed authorized by an order from King Cyrus. ‘And if our lord the king thinks it’s right, please send us word about these matters.’
[1 Esdras] [6]:[22] So King Darius ordered a search to be made in the archives kept in Babylon, and it was found in Ecbatana, in the fortress in Media’s province, where these things had been recorded:
[1 Esdras] [6]:[23] ‘In King Cyrus’s first year of reign, King Cyrus ordered that the Lord’s house in JeruSalem be built, where continuous burnt offerings are made.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[24] It should be 60 cubits high [100 feet / 30 m] and 60 cubits wide [100 feet / 30 m], with three layers of cut stones and one layer of new native timber. The costs are to be paid from King Cyrus’s treasury.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[25] ‘And the sacred gold and silver vessels from [Jehovah]‘s house, which NebuChadnezzar had taken from the house in JeruSalem and brought to Babylon, are to be returned to the house in JeruSalem, to their original place, so they can be stored there.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[26] ‘Also, he ordered Sisinnes, the governor of Syria and Phoenicia, along with Sathrabouzanes, their associates, and the appointed rulers in Syria and Phoenicia, to stay away from that place, and to allow [Jehovah]‘s servant Zerubbabel, Judea’s governor, and the Jews’ elders to build the Lord’s house on its site.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[27] ‘I also ordered that the building be finished without any interference, and to supervise closely, so that those who returned from captivity in Judea can work together until the Lord’s house is finished;
[1 Esdras] [6]:[28] and that from the taxes from Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, careful provision be made for these men for sacrifices to the Lord, specifically for Zerubbabel the governor, providing: Bulls Rams Lambs
[1 Esdras] [6]:[29] ‘Also, wheat, salt, wine, and oil are to be provided continuously, year after year, just as the priests in JeruSalem may order for daily use, without any argument,
[1 Esdras] [6]:[30] so that offerings can be made to The God Most High for the king and his servants, and so they can pray for their lives.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[31] ‘It is also ordered that if anyone breaks any of these written orders or cancels them, a beam is to be taken from his own house, and he is to be hanged on it, and his possessions will become royal property.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[32] ‘Also, may the Lord, whose name is honored there, destroy every king and nation who tries to stop or harm [Jehovah]‘s house in JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [6]:[33] ‘I, King Darius, have carefully ordered that these things must be done.’
[1 Esdras] [7]:[1] Sisinnes, the governor of Coele-Syria and Phoenicia, along with Sathrabouzanes and their associates, obeyed the orders from King Darius.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[2] They carefully supervised the sacred work, working with the Judean elders and the temple officials.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[3] The sacred work succeeded because Haggai and Zechariah, the prophets, kept prophesying.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[4] They finished these tasks as commanded by Israel’s God [Jehovah], and with the approval of Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes, Persia’s kings,
[1 Esdras] [7]:[5] the house was completed on Adar 23rd, during the sixth year of King Darius’s reign.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[6] The Israelites, priests, Levites, and the others who had returned from captivity and joined them, followed what was written in Moses’ Book.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[7] To dedicate [Jehovah]‘s temple, they offered: 100 bulls 200 rams 400 lambs
[1 Esdras] [7]:[8] They also offered 12 male goats as [a] sin offering for all Israel, representing Israel’s 12 tribal divisions.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[9] The priests and Levites took their assigned places, organized by their tribal divisions, to manage the work of [Jehovah], Israel’s God, as written in Moses’ Book. The gatekeepers also took their posts at each gate.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[10] The Israelites who had returned from captivity celebrated the Passover on the 14th day of the first month, after the priests and Levites had all purified themselves.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[11] All the exiles were purified as well, because they had purified themselves. In fact, the Levites had all purified themselves together.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[12] They offered the Passover sacrifice for all the exiles, for their brothers the priests, and for themselves.
[1 Esdras] [7]:[13] Then the Israelites who had returned from captivity ate, seeking the Lord (including everyone who had separated themselves from the disgusting practices of the land’s peoples).
[1 Esdras] [7]:[14] They then celebrated the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven days, rejoicing before [Jehovah],
[1 Esdras] [7]:[15] because he had turned the heart of the king of Assyria favorably toward them, strengthening their hands for the work of Israel’s God, [Jehovah].
[1 Esdras] [8]:[1] After these events, during King Artaxerxes of Persia’s reign, Ezra went up [to JeruSalem]. [He was the]: Son of Azariah Son of Zechariah Son of Chelkias Son of Salemos
[1 Esdras] [8]:[2] Son of Saddoulokos Son of Acheitob Son of Amartheios Son of Ozeias Son of Bokkas Son of Abeisai Son of Pheinees Son of Eleazar Son of Aaron, the first priest.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[3] Yes, this Ezra went up [to JeruSalem] from Babylon, for he was [a] very skilled scribe in Moses’ Law, which had been given by The God of Israel.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[4] The king honored him, for Ezra had found loving kindness in his sight regarding all his requests.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[5] And from Israel’s sons, there went up to JeruSalem with him: Priests Levites Temple-singers Doorkeepers Temple-servants
[1 Esdras] [8]:[6] This occurred in King Artaxerxes’ seventh year of reign, in the fifth month. For they had departed from Babylon on the 1st day of the 1st month and arrived in JeruSalem, thanks to the prosperous journey granted to them by The Lord upon him.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[7] Absaras was so knowledgeable that he made sure nothing from [Jehovah]‘s Law and its commandments (its statutes and judgments) would be left out for all Israel.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[8] [A] copy of the letter sent by King Artaxerxes to Ezra, the priest and interpreter of [Jehovah]‘s Law, is provided below. King Artaxerxes to Ezra, the priest and interpreter of [Jehovah]‘s Law:
[1 Esdras] [8]:[9] ‘Greetings.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[10] ‘After considering what is right and humane, I have commanded that all who willingly choose to go, whether from the Jewish nation, or from the priests, or from the Levites, or from others in our kingdom, may accompany you to JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[11] ‘Therefore, let all who are willing depart with you, just as it has been decided by me and my seven counselors.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[12] This is so that they may inquire about Judea and JeruSalem, in accordance with [Jehovah’s] Law as it stands,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[13] and to bring to The Lord the gifts which I and my friends have vowed for JeruSalem. ‘Also, all the gold and silver that may be found in Babylonia’s land, designated for The Lord in JeruSalem, along with what the people have donated for their Lord's temple in JeruSalem,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[14] is to be collected, both the gold and silver, for the purchase of bulls, rams, lambs, and their accompanying offerings,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[15] so that sacrifices may be offered upon their Lord's altar in JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[16] ‘And whatever else you and your brothers wish to do with the gold and silver, carry out according to your God’s will.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[17] Regarding your God’s sacred vessels given for the service of his temple in JeruSalem, and whatever else you may require for the service of your God’s temple,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[18] you shall take from the royal treasury.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[19] ‘Take notice! I, King Artaxerxes, have commanded Syria and Phoenicia’s treasurers to diligently provide Ezra, the priest and interpreter of The God Most High’s Law, with whatever he requests, up to 100 talents [~7,000 lb / 3,200 kg] of silver,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[20] likewise also up to 100 kors [~600 bushels / 22,000 L] of wheat and 100 baths [~600 gal / 2,200 L] of wine.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[21] ‘Let all this be done precisely according to The God Most High’s Law, so that no wrath may come upon the king’s kingdom or his sons.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[22] ‘And it’s also decreed for you that no taxation or other imposition shall be levied upon any of: Priests Levites Temple-singers Doorkeepers Temple-servants Administrators of this temple. ‘No one shall have authority to impose anything upon them.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[23] ‘And you, Ezra, according to The God's wisdom, are to appoint judges and magistrates, so that they may administer justice throughout all Syria and Phoenicia to all who know your God’s Law; and those who don’t know it, you shall teach.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[24] ‘And all who transgress your God’s Law or the royal law shall be diligently punished, whether by death, or by other severe penalties, and not merely by monetary fines or deportation.’
[1 Esdras] [8]:[25] Praised be The Lord alone, who put these things into my king’s [heart], to glorify his house in JeruSalem!
[1 Esdras] [8]:[26] He also honored me before the kings and all his friends and nobles.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[27] So, strengthened by [Jehovah] my God’s help, I gathered men from Israel to go up [to JeruSalem] with me.

[1 Esdras] [8]:[41] I assembled them at the place called the River, and we camped there for three days. While I was inspecting them,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[42] I didn’t find any priests or Levites among them.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[43] So I sent for: Eleazar Iduel Maasmas Ennatan Samaias Ioribos Nathan Ennatan Zacharias Mesolabōn...who were leading and knowledgeable men,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[44] and instructed them to go to Laadaios, the leader of the treasury at that place,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[45] and to tell Lodaios, his brothers, and the treasurers there to send us men who could serve as priests in our Lord’s house.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[46] They sent: Asebebias, [a] knowledgeable man, from Mooli’s sons, of Levi, of Israel Along with ten of his sons and brothers
[1 Esdras] [8]:[47] They also sent: 20 men from Chanounaios’ sons, including their own sons
[1 Esdras] [8]:[48] And from the temple-servants (whom David and the leaders had assigned to assist the Levites) they sent: 220 temple-servants [A] list of all their names was recorded.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[49] There I proclaimed [a] fast for the young men before our Lord,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[50] so that we might seek from him [a] prosperous journey for ourselves, our children, and our livestock.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[51] For I was ashamed to ask the king for an escort of horsemen and footmen to protect us from our enemies along the way.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[52] You see, we had told the king that our Lord’s strength would be with all who seek him for every good purpose.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[53] So we again entreated our Lord concerning all these matters, and he was gracious to us.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[54] Then I set aside twelve men from the priestly families’ chiefs, along with Eserebias and Hassamias, and ten of their brothers...
[1 Esdras] [8]:[55] And I weighed out for them the silver, gold, and our Lord’s sacred vessels for his house, which the king, his counselors, his nobles, and all Israel had donated.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[56] He delivered to them, having weighed it to be: 650 talents [~45,500 lb / 20,800 kg] of silver Silver vessels weighing 100 talents 100 talents [~7,000 lb / 3,200 kg] of gold 20 golden bowls And ten shining vessels of fine bronze And I said to them:
[1 Esdras] [8]:[57] ‘You yourselves are holy to the Lord, and these vessels are holy. The silver and gold are [a] freewill offering to [Jehovah], the Lord of our fathers...
[1 Esdras] [8]:[58] ‘So, be vigilant! Guard them until you [safely] deliver them to the chambers of our Lord’s house in JeruSalem, to the chiefs of the priestly and Levite families, and to Israel’s ancestral houses’ leaders.’
[1 Esdras] [8]:[59] So the priests and Levites received the silver, gold, and vessels, and brought them to the Lord’s temple in JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[60] We set out from Thera on the 12th day of the 1st month. By our Lord’s mighty hand that was upon us, we arrived in JeruSalem... He rescued us from ambushes and from every enemy!
[1 Esdras] [8]:[61] On the 3rd day after our arrival, the silver and gold were weighed and delivered to [Jehovah’s] house to Marmothis, son of Oureias, the priest,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[62] along with Eleazar, son of Pheinees. With them were the Levites Iosabees, son of Ieesous, and Moeth, son of Sabannos. Everything was counted and weighed, and the total weight was recorded at that very hour.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[63] Those who had returned from captivity offered [the following] sacrifices to [Jehovah], The God of Israel: 96 bulls 76 rams 12 goats as peace offerings All of these were [a] sacrifice to the Lord.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[64] They also delivered the king’s decrees to the royal governors and to Syria and Phoenicia’s satraps, who then honored the people and the Lord’s temple.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[65] After these things were completed, the leaders came to me, saying:
[1 Esdras] [8]:[66] ‘The leaders, priests, and Levites haven’t separated themselves from the foreign nations’ uncleanness! [That of the]... Canaanites Hittites Perizzites Jebusites Moabites Egyptians And Idumaeans
[1 Esdras] [8]:[67] ‘They have intermarried with some of their daughters, both they and their sons. So, the holy offspring has become mixed with the land’s foreign nations. Indeed, the leaders and nobles have been foremost in this lawlessness from the very beginning!’
[1 Esdras] [8]:[68] As soon as I heard this, I tore my clothes and my sacred vestment! I pulled out hair from my head and beard, and sat down distraught and deeply distressed...
[1 Esdras] [8]:[69] Everyone who trembled at the word of [Jehovah] of Israel gathered around me as I mourned over this lawlessness... I remained deeply distressed until the evening sacrifice.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[70] Then, rising from my fast, with my clothes and sacred vestment still torn, I knelt down and stretched out my hands to The Lord, saying:
[1 Esdras] [8]:[71] ‘O [Jehovah], ‘I am ashamed and utterly confounded before You!
[1 Esdras] [8]:[72] ‘For our sins have risen above our heads, and our iniquities have reached even to heaven,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[73] from our ancestors’ times until this very day. ‘We are in great sin!
[1 Esdras] [8]:[74] ‘Thanks to our sins and our ancestors’ sins, we, along with our brothers, our kings, and our priests, were delivered into the hands of earth’s kings, to the sword, to captivity, to plunder, and to shame, even to this present day!
[1 Esdras] [8]:[75] ‘And now, for [a] brief moment, mercy has been shown to us by the Lord [Jehovah]. He has left us [a] remnant and [a] name in this holy place,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[76] and has uncovered [a] light for us in our Lord’s house, to give us sustenance during the time of our servitude. ‘Even while we were enslaved, our Lord didn’t abandon us,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[77] but granted us loving kindness in the sight of Persia’s kings, to provide us with sustenance,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[78] and to glorify our temple, to raise up desolate Zion, and to give us [a] firm foothold in Judea and JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[79] ‘So now, what shall we say, O [Jehovah], after all this? ‘For we have disobeyed Your commandments, which You gave through Your servants the prophets, who said:
[1 Esdras] [8]:[80] ‘The land which you are entering to inherit is [a] defiled land, defiled by the uncleanness of the land’s foreign peoples; they’ve filled it with their impurity.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[81] ‘Now, therefore, don’t give your daughters in marriage to their sons, nor take their daughters for your sons!
[1 Esdras] [8]:[82] And you should never seek peace or prosperity with them, so that you’ll be strong, eat the land’s good things, and leave it as an inheritance to your children into the age.’
[1 Esdras] [8]:[83] ‘And all that has happened to us is because of our evil deeds and great sins. ‘For You, O [Jehovah], have lightened our sins,
[1 Esdras] [8]:[84] and given us such [a] remnant. Yet we have again turned back to transgress Your law by mixing with the uncleanness of the land’s nations.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[85] Weren’t You angry enough with us to destroy us completely, leaving no root, no remnant, no name for us?
[1 Esdras] [8]:[86] ‘O [Jehovah] of Israel, You are true! ‘For we are left as [a] remnant this very day.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[87] Look! We are before You in our lawlessness; for we can’t stand before You any longer because of these things.’
[1 Esdras] [8]:[88] While Ezra was praying and confessing, weeping and prostrate before the temple, [a] very large crowd gathered around him from JeruSalem — men, women, and young men. There was great weeping among the crowd.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[89] Then Iechonias (son of Iehelos), one of the sons of Israel, called out and said to Ezra: ‘We’ve sinned against the Lord! We’ve settled with foreign women from the land’s peoples. And now, this guilt rests upon all of Israel.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[90] ‘Therefore, let’s now swear to the Lord to send all our foreign wives and their children away, as you have determined, [and make it a] requirement for everybody who obeys the Lord’s Law.
[1 Esdras] [8]:[91] ‘Get up and act! This matter is your responsibility, but we’ll back you up!’
[1 Esdras] [8]:[92] So Ezra arose and made the priestly and Levite families’ chiefs, and all Israel, swear to do all of this... And they swore to it!
[1 Esdras] [9]:[1] Ezra left the temple court and went into the chamber of Jonan the Naseibos.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[2] While there, he didn’t eat bread or drink water, mourning the people’s many sins.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[3] Then, an announcement was made across all Judea and JeruSalem, telling everyone who had returned from captivity to gather in JeruSalem.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[4] Anyone who didn’t show up within two or three days, as decided by the presiding elders, would have their livestock confiscated, and that person would be excluded from the community of the exiles!
[1 Esdras] [9]:[5] So, those from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin gathered in JeruSalem within three days. This happened on the 20th day of the 9th month.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[6] The entire assembly sat together in the open space in front of the temple, trembling because winter was coming.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[7] Ezra stood up and said to them: ‘You’ve acted unlawfully by marrying foreign women, thus adding to Israel’s sin.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[8] ‘Now, confess and give glory to [Jehovah], our fathers’ God,
[1 Esdras] [9]:[9] and do his will. Separate yourselves from the peoples of the land and from the foreign women!’
[1 Esdras] [9]:[10] The entire assembly shouted loudly, saying: ‘We’ll do as you’ve said!
[1 Esdras] [9]:[11] ‘But the assembly is large, and it’s winter! We can’t stay out in the open. This task isn’t something that can be done in one or two days, for we’ve sinned greatly in these matters.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[12] ‘Therefore, let’s have the leaders of our assembly step forward. Then, at a set time, everyone from our households with foreign wives should come,
[1 Esdras] [9]:[13] accompanied by the local elders and judges. We’ll do this until [Jehovah]‘s anger over this is removed from us.’
[1 Esdras] [9]:[14] Jonathan (son of Azaelos) and Hezekiah (son of Thokanos) accepted these terms, and Mosollamos, Leuis, and Sabbataios served as judges with them.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[15] This is what those who had returned from captivity [from Babylon] did.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[16] Ezra the priest selected men, leaders of their respective clans, all by name. They convened on the 1st day of the 10th month to investigate the matter.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[17] The investigation concerning the men who had married foreign women was completed by the 1st day of the 1st month.

[1 Esdras] [9]:[38] The entire assembly gathered together as one in the open area before the eastern gate of the temple.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[39] They asked Ezra, the priest and the reader of the Law, to bring out Moses’ Law, which The God of Israel had given.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[40] So Ezra the high priest brought Moses’ Law before the entire assembly — men, women, and all the priests — to hear the Law, on the 1st day of the 7th month.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[41] He read from the open area in front of the temple gate from dawn until midday, in the presence of the men and women; and they paid close attention to it!
[1 Esdras] [9]:[42] Ezra, the priest and Law’s reader, stood upon the wooden platform that had been constructed.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[43] Standing beside him on his right were: Mattathias Sammou Ananias Azarias Oureias Hezekiah Baalsamos

[1 Esdras] [9]:[45] Ezra took up the Law’s book for the people, for he was seated in a prominent place before everyone.
