[1 Esdras] [9]:[47] and the entire assembly cried out: ‘May it be so!, may it be so!!’ Then, raising their hands, they bowed down to the ground and bowed down to The God.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[48] [These men] taught [Jehovah’s] law: Jesus Anniouth Sarabeias Jadeinos Jarsouboos Abtaios Autaias Maiannas Kaleitas Azarias Katethzabdos Annias Phalias And the Levites And they read the Lord’s Law to the assembly, explaining it as they read.
[1 Esdras] [9]:[49] Attarates said to Ezra the high priest and reader, and to the Levites who were teaching the multitude, addressing everyone:
[1 Esdras] [9]:[50] ‘This day is holy to the Lord!’ (For all the people wept as they heard the Law.)
[1 Esdras] [9]:[51] ‘Go now, eat rich foods and send portions to those who have nothing,
[1 Esdras] [9]:[52] for the day is holy to the Lord, and do not grieve; for the Lord will bring you honor.’
[1 Esdras] [9]:[53] The Levites also encouraged the people, saying repeatedly: ‘This day is holy; don’t grieve.’
[1 Esdras] [9]:[54] So everyone went to eat, drink, and celebrate, sharing portions with those who had nothing. They were extremely happy,
[1 Esdras] [9]:[55] for they had been enlightened by the teaching, and felt a profound sense of unity.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[1] This psalm is David’s own composition, outside the numbered collection—written after his duel with GoliAth. I was youngest of my brothers, Smallest in my father’s house… So I tended my father’s sheep.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[2] My hands crafted [a] lyre, My fingers shaped [a] harp.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[3] But who could tell [Jehovah]? He himself was listening.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[4] He sent his messenger And from the sheep, took me… Then with his oil, He anointed me.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[5] My brothers? Tall and strong. But [Jehovah] didn’t choose them.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[6] I marched out to face the foreigner— With his idols, he cursed me.
[Psalm 151] [1]:[7] So I grabbed his own sword— Cut off his head! And lifted Israel’s shame.
[Matthew] [1]:[1] This is the scroll of the origins of Jesus the Anointed, the Son of David, the Son of AbraHam:
[Matthew] [1]:[2] AbraHam fathered IsaAc. IsaAc fathered Jacob. Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
[Matthew] [1]:[3] Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez fathered HezRon. HezRon fathered Ram.
[Matthew] [1]:[4] Ram fathered AmiNadab. AmiNadab fathered NaShon. NaShon fathered SalMon.
[Matthew] [1]:[5] SalMon fathered BoAz by RaHab. BoAz fathered Obed by Ruth. Obed fathered JesSe.
[Matthew] [1]:[6] JesSe fathered David, the king. David fathered Solomon by the wife of UriAh.
[Matthew] [1]:[7] Solomon fathered RehoBoam. RehoBoam fathered AbiJah. AbiJah fathered Asa.
[Matthew] [1]:[8] Asa fathered JehoShaphat. JehoShaphat fathered JehoRam. JehoRam fathered UzZiAh.
[Matthew] [1]:[9] UzZiAh fathered JoTham. JoTham fathered Ahaz. Ahaz fathered HezekiAh.
[Matthew] [1]:[10] HezekiAh fathered ManasSeh. ManasSeh fathered Amon. Amon fathered JosiAh.
[Matthew] [1]:[11] JosiAh fathered JeconiAh and his brothers before the deportation to Babylon.
[Matthew] [1]:[12] After the deportation to Babylon: JeconiAh fathered ShalathiEl. ShalathiEl fathered ZerubBabel.
[Matthew] [1]:[13] ZerubBabel fathered AbiUd. AbiUd fathered EliAkim. EliAkim fathered Azor.
[Matthew] [1]:[14] Azor fathered ZaDok. ZaDok fathered Achim. Achim fathered EliUd.
[Matthew] [1]:[15] EliUd fathered EliAzar. EliAzar fathered MatThan. MatThan fathered Jacob.
[Matthew] [1]:[16] Jacob fathered JoSeph [the father of Mary] from whom Jesus (who has called the Anointed One) was born.
[Matthew] [1]:[17] So, there were: 14 generations from AbraHam to David, 14 generations from David until the deportation to Babylon, and 14 generations from the deportation to Babylon until [the coming of] the Anointed One.
[Matthew] [1]:[18] This is the way that Jesus the Anointed One started out: While his mother Mary was promised in marriage to JoSeph, she was found to be pregnant by [God’s] Holy breath before the marriage was consummated.
[Matthew] [1]:[19] However, because JoSeph (her man) was righteous and didn’t want to make [Mary] a public spectacle, he planned to release her secretly.
[Matthew] [1]:[20] But after he decided to do that, {Look!} [Jehovah’s] messenger appeared to him in a dream, saying: ‘JoSeph, son of David, don’t be afraid to take Mary as your wife, because what has been fathered in her is from [God’s] holy breath.
[Matthew] [1]:[21] She’ll give birth to a son and you must call his name Jesus [meaning, Yahweh Saves], because he will save his people from their sins.’
[Matthew] [1]:[22] This whole thing happened so that what was spoken by [Jehovah] through the Prophet would be fulfilled:
[Matthew] [1]:[23] '{Look!} A virgin will get pregnant and then bear a son Whose name you must call, ImManuEl.’ [Meaning, With Us is God.] [Isaiah 7:14]
[Matthew] [1]:[24] Well, after JoSeph woke up, he did what [Jehovah’s] messenger told him to do, and he took the woman.
[Matthew] [1]:[25] However, [JoSeph] didn’t have sexual relations with her until after she’d given birth to a son, whom he called by the name Jesus.
[Matthew] [2]:[1] Then, after Jesus was born (in BethLehem of Judea during the days of King Herod), {Look!} Magi from the east came to JeruSalem,
[Matthew] [2]:[2] asking: ‘Where is this one who was born to be the king of the Jews? We saw his star in the east and we came to bow low before him.’
[Matthew] [2]:[3] Well, when he heard about this, King Herod was very disturbed (as was everyone else in JeruSalem).
[Matthew] [2]:[4] So he gathered all the Chief Priests and the peoples’ Scribes and asked them where this Anointed One was to be born.
[Matthew] [2]:[5] And they replied: ‘In BethLehem of Judea… Because, this is what was written through the Prophet:
[Matthew] [2]:[6] ‘And you, O BethLehem in the land of Judea Will no way be the least among rulers of Judah. For from you, will come forth a leader, Who will shepherd IsraEl, My people.’ [Micah 5:2-4, paraphrased]
[Matthew] [2]:[7] Then Herod secretly called for those Magi and carefully determined from them when the star had appeared.
[Matthew] [2]:[8] And before he sent them on to BethLehem, he said: ‘Search carefully for the young child... And when you find him, report back to me, so I can go and bow before him also.’
[Matthew] [2]:[9] Then, after listening to what the king had to say, they traveled on… For {Look!} the star that they saw in the east went ahead of them until it stood directly over [the place] where the young child was!
[Matthew] [2]:[10] Well, when they saw the star [do this], they were beside themselves with joy!
[Matthew] [2]:[11] And after they entered the house, they saw the little boy with Mary (his mother), and they fell down and bowed before him. Then they opened their treasures and gave the child gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
[Matthew] [2]:[12] However, because they’d been given a divine warning in a dream that they weren’t to return to Herod, they went back home via another route.
[Matthew] [2]:[13] Well, after they left, {Look!} [Jehovah’s] messenger appeared to JoSeph in a dream and said: ‘Get up! Take the boy and his mother, then hurry to Egypt and stay there until I tell you otherwise, because Herod is going to search for the boy to destroy him!’
[Matthew] [2]:[14] So he got up during the night and took the child and his mother, and they left for Egypt,
[Matthew] [2]:[15] where they stayed until after Herod died… So the thing that was said by [Jehovah] through the Prophet would be fulfilled: ‘I called My son out of Egypt.’ [Hosea 11:1, MT; see note]
[Matthew] [2]:[16] Well, when Herod saw that the Magi had outwitted him, he was furious. So he sent [a proclamation] throughout BethLehem and its districts to have all the boys that were two-years-old and younger to be gathered [for destruction], since that was the period he’d determined so carefully from the Magi.
[Matthew] [2]:[17] And that’s also when the thing that was spoken through the Prophet JeremiAh was fulfilled, which said:
[Matthew] [2]:[18] ‘A voice was heard crying from RamAh… The sounds of weeping, wailing, and grief. It was the voice of RachEl, crying for her sons, And she refused to accept any comfort, Because they’re no longer [alive].’ [Jeremiah 31:15]
[Matthew] [2]:[19] Well, after Herod died, {Look!} [Jehovah’s] messenger appeared in a dream to JoSeph while he was in Egypt,
[Matthew] [2]:[20] and he said: ‘Now, get up and take the child and his mother back to the land of IsraEl, because those who wanted to take the child’s life are dead!’
[Matthew] [2]:[21] So [JoSeph] got up and took the child and his mother back to the land of IsraEl.
[Matthew] [2]:[22] However, when he heard that ArcheLaus had become the ruler in Judah in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there, because of a divine warning that he had received in a dream. As a result, he traveled to the territory of Galilee,
[Matthew] [2]:[23] and they went to live in a city named Nazareth. So the thing that was spoken through the prophet was fulfilled, that he would be called a Nazarene, [meaning, contemptible].
[Matthew] [3]:[1] It was back in those days that John the Immerser came preaching in the desert around Judea,
[Matthew] [3]:[2] saying: ‘Repent, for the Kingdom [of God] has drawn near.’
[Matthew] [3]:[3] He’s the one about whom the Prophet IsaiAh spoke, saying: ‘A voice is calling out in the desert: ‘Prepare the way for the Lord… Before him, straighten the roads!’ [Isaiah 40:3]
[Matthew] [3]:[4] John wore clothes made of camel’s hair, he had a thick leather belt around his waist, and what he ate was locusts and wild honey.
[Matthew] [3]:[5] Then, [people from] JeruSalem (as well as from the rest of Judea and the area all around the Jordan) came to him
[Matthew] [3]:[6] to be immersed in the Jordan River, as they openly admitted their sins.
[Matthew] [3]:[7] And when he saw many of the Pharisees and SadDucees coming to be immersed, he said to them: ‘Children of vipers! ‘Who has shown you the need to flee from the coming rage?
[Matthew] [3]:[8] You should first produce the [type of] fruit that proves you’re worthy of repentance!
[Matthew] [3]:[9] ‘And don’t be so bold as to say, Our father is AbraHam; for I tell you that God can make children of AbraHam from these stones!
[Matthew] [3]:[10] ‘Now the ax is already lying at the roots of the trees and every tree that isn’t producing good fruit is going to be cut down and thrown into the fire!
[Matthew] [3]:[11] ‘Indeed, I dip you in water [as a sign of your] repentance. But the one who is coming behind me is greater than me… In fact, I’m unfit to remove his sandals! ‘[When he arrives], he will immerse you in fire and breath…
[Matthew] [3]:[12] Yes, he’ll [take] his shovel into his hands and completely clean up his threshing floor, then he will gather the ‘wheat’ into his storehouse and burn all the ‘chaff’ with a fire that can’t be extinguished!’
[Matthew] [3]:[13] Then sometime later, Jesus came from Galilee to see John at the Jordan River in order to be immersed by him.
[Matthew] [3]:[14] But [John] tried to prevent him, saying: ‘Since I’m the one who should be immersed by you; why are you coming to me?’
[Matthew] [3]:[15] But Jesus told him: ‘Let it be like this for now… This is the right thing for us to do, so we can fulfill all that’s righteous.’ And at that, [John] no longer tried to stop him.
[Matthew] [3]:[16] Well, after Jesus was immersed, immediately after he came up out of the water, {Look!} the heavens opened up before him, and [John] saw God’s breath descending upon him [in the form of] a dove.
[Matthew] [3]:[17] And {Look!} there was also a voice that came out of the sky that said: ‘This is My dearly-loved Son, with whom I’m well pleased.’
[Matthew] [4]:[1] Then [God’s] breath led Jesus into the desert to be tempted by the Slanderer.
[Matthew] [4]:[2] And after he’d fasted for 40 days and 40 nights, he became very hungry.
[Matthew] [4]:[3] So the Tempter came to him and said: ‘If you’re [really] the Son of God, tell these stones to become loaves of bread!’
[Matthew] [4]:[4] And [Jesus] replied: ‘It is written: ‘Man doesn’t live by just bread alone, But by every word that comes from God’s mouth.’ [Deuteronomy 8:3]
[Matthew] [4]:[5] Then the Slanderer took him to the Holy City and put him up on one of the Temple’s high battle towers.
[Matthew] [4]:[6] And he said: ‘If you’re [really] a son of God, jump down! For it is written: ‘He’ll assign [His] messengers around you, And on their hands, they’ll lift you, So you’ll not hit your foot on a stone.’ [Psalm 91:11-12]
[Matthew] [4]:[7] But Jesus told him: ‘Once again, it is written: ‘Don’t put [Jehovah] your God to the test.’ [Deuteronomy 6:16]
[Matthew] [4]:[8] Then the Slanderer took him to an unusually high mountain where he showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
[Matthew] [4]:[9] And he said: ‘I’ll give all of these to you if you’ll just bow before me with your face to the ground.’
[Matthew] [4]:[10] But Jesus replied: ‘Go away Slanderer, because it is written: ‘Indeed; you must worship [Jehovah], your God, And Him alone should you serve.’ [Deuteronomy 6:13]
[Matthew] [4]:[11] Well after that, the Slanderer left him, and {Look!} [God’s] messengers came and started serving [Jesus’ needs].
[Matthew] [4]:[12] Then, it was after he heard that John had been arrested that [Jesus] returned to Galilee…
[Matthew] [4]:[13] He moved out of Nazareth and started living in CapharNaum (which is by the sea in the districts of ZebuLun and NaphTali).

[Matthew] [4]:[18] Then, it was while he was walking along by the Sea of Galilee that he saw two brothers, Simon (the one called Peter) and his brother Andrew… Fishermen who were casting their nets on the sea.

[Matthew] [4]:[25] So huge crowds from Galilee, the DecaPolis, JeruSalem and the rest of Judea, as well as those from the other side of the Jordan, started following him.
[Matthew] [5]:[1] Well, when [Jesus] saw the crowds, he went up a mountain and sat down, and his disciples came to him.
[Matthew] [5]:[2] Then he opened his mouth and started teaching them, saying:
[Matthew] [5]:[3] ‘Blest are the humble; For theirs is the Kingdom of [God].
[Matthew] [5]:[4] ‘Blest are those who are sad; For they’ll be given comfort.
[Matthew] [5]:[5] ‘Blest are also the meek; For they’ll inherit the land.
[Matthew] [5]:[6] ‘Those hungering and thirsting for righteousness are blest; For they’ll find satisfaction.
[Matthew] [5]:[7] ‘Blest are those who show mercy; For mercy is what they’ll receive.
[Matthew] [5]:[8] ‘Blest are those with pure hearts; For they’ll [come to] see God.
[Matthew] [5]:[9] ‘Blest are those who make peace; For they’ll be called Sons of God.
[Matthew] [5]:[10] ‘Blest are those who receive persecution For doing [things that are] righteous, Since theirs is the Kingdom of [God].
[Matthew] [5]:[11] ‘You’re blest when they [shout] insults at you, And when they persecute you, Then say many bad things about you And lie about you for my sake.
[Matthew] [5]:[12] ‘For this, you should [cry out in] joy; Since your reward in the heavens is great, For that’s how they treated the Prophets before you.
[Matthew] [5]:[13] ‘You’re the salt of the earth; But if salt becomes weak, is it still salt? No, when it no longer has strength, It’s thrown outside to be walked on.
[Matthew] [5]:[14] ‘You’re the light of this world… And a city on a hill can’t be hidden!
[Matthew] [5]:[15] ‘You don’t light a lamp And then put it under a basket… You put it on a lampstand instead, Where it can shine throughout the whole house!
[Matthew] [5]:[16] ‘So let your light shine before all, Then they can speak of the good things you’ve done And give glory to your Father in the heavens.
[Matthew] [5]:[17] ‘Don’t think that I came to destroy The Law or the [words of the] Prophets… For I came to fulfill, not to destroy.
[Matthew] [5]:[18] ‘I’m telling you the truth when I say that it’s more likely that the land and skies would pass away, than for an iota or a small point on a letter of the Law to pass away before it’s all fulfilled.
[Matthew] [5]:[19] ‘So, whoever breaks the least of the commands and teaches others to do the same will be called the least in the Kingdom of [God], while those who teach and follow them will be called great in the Kingdom.
[Matthew] [5]:[20] ‘I also say this to you: ‘If you aren’t more righteous than the Scribes and Pharisees, you won’t enter the Kingdom of [God].
[Matthew] [5]:[21] ‘You’ve heard that the ancients were told: ‘You must not commit murder, for those who murder will be judged.’
[Matthew] [5]:[22] ‘However, I tell you this: ‘Anyone who stays angry with his brother will have to be judged, and anyone who calls his brother empty-headed must stand before the religious court. Also, anyone who [calls his brother] a moron will be [condemned] to the garbage-dump fires.
[Matthew] [5]:[23] ‘And if you bring a gift to [God’s] Altar, but while you’re on the way you remember that your brother holds something against you;
[Matthew] [5]:[24] leave your gift at the Altar and go [to him]. ‘First make peace with your brother, and then return to offer your gift.
[Matthew] [5]:[25] ‘Also, while you’re on your way [to a court], you should quickly work out an agreement with your adversary, so you won’t have to leave the matter in the hands of the judge... Who may hand you over to the bailiff... Who’ll then lock you in jail.
[Matthew] [5]:[26] ‘If that happens, I tell you this for a fact: ‘You won’t be released ‘til you’ve paid the last penny!
[Matthew] [5]:[27] ‘You’ve all heard that it’s said: ‘You must not commit adultery.’
[Matthew] [5]:[28] ‘But I tell you that any man who stares at a woman and develops a desire [to have] her, has committed adultery [with her] in his heart.
[Matthew] [5]:[29] ‘So if your right eye becomes a trap to you, pull it out and throw it away! For it’s better to lose a piece of yourself than to lose your whole body in the garbage dump.
[Matthew] [5]:[30] Or if your right hand becomes a trap to you, cut it off and throw it away! For it’s better to lose a piece of yourself than to lose your whole body in the garbage dump.
[Matthew] [5]:[31] ‘It is also said that [any man] who releases his woman should give her a certificate of rejection.
[Matthew] [5]:[32] But I say: ‘[Any man] who releases his woman except on account of sexual immorality, leads her into adultery. And [any man] who marries a woman who has been released is committing adultery.
[Matthew] [5]:[33] ‘Again, you heard it was said long ago: ‘You must not swear a false oath; rather, you must do as you vow to [Jehovah].’ Numbers 30:2]
[Matthew] [5]:[34] ‘However, I tell you this: Swear oaths by nothing at all! ‘Don’t swear by heaven, For that’s God’s throne;

[Matthew] [13]:[4] And some of his seeds fell by the road, Where birds quickly came there and ate them.
[Matthew] [13]:[5] ‘Others fell among rocks where there wasn’t much soil, Yet, they quickly started to sprout.

So they’re unable to see with their eyes, And they can’t hear with their ears, Nor can they understand in their hearts, Then turn back, so that I can heal them.’ [Isaiah 6:9-10]

[Mark] [1]:[23] Well at the time, there was a man in the synagogue that was under the influence of an unclean spirit, which caused him to shout:
[Mark] [1]:[24] ‘What dealings do I have with you, Jesus of Nazareth? Did you come here to destroy me? I know who you are! You’re The Holy One of God!’
[Mark] [1]:[25] But Jesus scolded [the spirit], saying: ‘Put a muzzle on it and come out of him!’
[Mark] [1]:[26] So the unclean spirit (after throwing the man into convulsions and causing him to yell loudly) came out.
[Mark] [1]:[27] This shocked the people, and they started asking each other: ‘What’s this, some new teaching? For he has the power to give orders to unclean spirits and they obey him!’
[Mark] [1]:[28] So after that, the story about him was spread throughout all the country around Galilee.
[Mark] [1]:[29] Well from there, [Jesus] left the synagogue along with James and John, and they went directly to the home of Simon and Andrew,
[Mark] [1]:[30] where they found Simon’s (Peter’s) mother-in-law lying down and burning up with a fever, which they immediately pointed out to [Jesus].
[Mark] [1]:[31] So he took her by the hand to help her up, then the fever left her and she started serving them.
[Mark] [1]:[32] Well that evening, after sunset, people started bringing all those who were ill and the demon-possessed to him…
[Mark] [1]:[33] Virtually the whole city had gathered at their door!
[Mark] [1]:[34] So he cured their various illnesses and expelled many demons. However, he wouldn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew that he was the Anointed One.
[Mark] [1]:[35] Then early the next morning, while it was still dark, he got up and went outside to a remote place where he started praying.
[Mark] [1]:[36] However, Simon (and those who were with him) searched
[Mark] [1]:[37] for him, and when they found him they said: ‘Everyone has been looking for you!’
[Mark] [1]:[38] But he said to them: ‘Let’s go into the nearby villages, so I can preach there too. For, that’s why I came outside.’
[Mark] [1]:[39] And [after that], he traveled throughout all of Galilee, preaching in their synagogues and casting out demons.
[Mark] [1]:[40] It was while he was there that an infected person came to him, who got down on his knees and said: ‘If you just want to, you can make me clean!’
[Mark] [1]:[41] And moved with pity, [Jesus] stuck out his hand and touched him, saying: ‘I want to… Be clean.’
[Mark] [1]:[42] Then the infection immediately left him and he became clean!
[Mark] [1]:[43] But [Jesus] sent him away and gave him strict orders
[Mark] [1]:[44] not to tell anyone what he’d done. He only told him to go and show himself to the Priests and to bring along the offering of cleansing that was specified by Moses, as a witness to them.
[Mark] [1]:[45] However, after the man left, he started telling everyone and spreading the word around, so that Jesus wasn’t able to enter the cities openly, and he had to camp out in lonely places… Yet [the people] still kept coming to him from all directions.
[Mark] [2]:[1] Well after several days, [Jesus] returned to CapharNaum, and when word got out that he was back home,
[Mark] [2]:[2] so many people came to him that there wasn’t any room around the door. Then he started preaching the word to them.
[Mark] [2]:[3] Thereafter, four people came to him carrying a man who was paralyzed.
[Mark] [2]:[4] But because the crowd was so large, they couldn’t get him to [Jesus]. So, they dug an opening through the part of the roof where [Jesus] was standing, and lowered down the cot on which the [man] was lying.
[Mark] [2]:[5] Then when Jesus saw how much faith they’d shown, he said to the paralyzed man: ‘Child, your sins are forgiven.’
[Mark] [2]:[6] Well, when they heard him say that, some of the Scribes that were sitting there started reasoning in their hearts:
[Mark] [2]:[7] ‘Why is he talking in such a way, for this is blasphemy! ‘Who is able to forgive sins other than the one God?’
[Mark] [2]:[8] And through the spirit, Jesus immediately realized that they were reasoning in this way inside themselves, so he asked them: ‘Why are [such bad] thoughts entering your hearts?
[Mark] [2]:[9] Which is easier, to tell the paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven’, or, ‘Get up, pick up your cot, and walk’?
[Mark] [2]:[10] ‘Well, so that you men will know that the Son of Man has been authorized to forgive sins on the earth...’
[Mark] [2]:[11] [He said to the man]: ‘Get up, pick up your cot, and go home!’
[Mark] [2]:[12] And immediately, the man got right up, picked up his cot, and walked out in front of everyone! Well, all those who were there were beside themselves and they started glorifying God, saying: ‘We’ve never seen anything like this!’
[Mark] [2]:[13] Then later, he went outside to the seashore, where huge crowds came to him and he taught them.
[Mark] [2]:[14] It was as he was passing the tax office that he noticed Levi (son of AlphaEus), sitting there. So [he] said to him: ‘Follow me.’ And [Levi] got right up and went with him.
[Mark] [2]:[15] Then later, as Jesus was reclining at the table in [Levi’s] home, several tax collectors and sinners started coming and reclining with him and his disciples (many of whom became Jesus’ followers).
[Mark] [2]:[16] But when the Scribes and Pharisees saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, they asked his disciples: ‘Why is he eating with the tax collectors and sinners?’
[Mark] [2]:[17] And because Jesus overheard this, he said: ‘Those who are well don’t need a doctor, only the ill do. ‘So I didn’t come to call the righteous, just the sinners.’
[Mark] [2]:[18] Well, back then, John’s disciples (who practiced fasting, as did the Pharisees) came to [Jesus] and asked: ‘Why is it that while the disciples of John and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, your disciples don’t fast?’
[Mark] [2]:[19] And Jesus replied: ‘The sons of the bride chamber can’t fast while the bridegroom is among them, because as long as he’s with them, there’s [no reason to] fast.
[Mark] [2]:[20] ‘But the days are coming when the groom will be taken away… And then they’ll fast.
[Mark] [2]:[21] ‘Understand that no one sews patches of new cloth onto old clothes, for if they do, the new [cloth] will shrink and stretch the old cloth, which will make the tear worse.
[Mark] [2]:[22] ‘Also, if you put young wine into old wineskins, the [new] wine will burst the skins and both the wine and the skins will be lost. So it’s best for people to use new wineskins for new wine.’
[Mark] [2]:[23] Then on another day, as [Jesus] was walking through the grain fields on the Sabbath, his disciples started plucking heads of grain [to eat] as they were traveling along.
[Mark] [2]:[24] And the Pharisees asked him: '{Look!} Why are they doing something that’s illegal on the Sabbath?’
[Mark] [2]:[25] But he replied: ‘Haven’t you ever read what David did when he was in need, and he and the men who were with him got hungry (in the account about AbiAthar, the High Priest)…
[Mark] [2]:[26] How he entered the House of God and ate the Presentation Bread, which isn’t legal for anyone to eat other than the Priests, and how he also gave some of it to the men who were with him?’
[Mark] [2]:[27] Then [Jesus] said this: ‘The Sabbath came into existence for the sake of mankind, not mankind for the Sabbath.
[Mark] [2]:[28] ‘But you should also know that the Son of Man is the Lord of the Sabbath.’
[Mark] [3]:[1] On another occasion, he entered a synagogue where there happened to be a man with a withered hand
[Mark] [3]:[2] Well, [the Pharisees] were watching [Jesus] closely to see if he would cure him on the Sabbath, because they were trying to find something that they could accuse him of doing wrong.
[Mark] [3]:[3] However, [Jesus] said to the man with the withered hand: ‘Get up and come into the center [of the room].’
[Mark] [3]:[4] Then he asked everyone there: ‘Is it legal to do something good or bad, or to save a life or destroy it on the Sabbath?’ But no one would answer.
[Mark] [3]:[5] Then, after looking around at them angrily (because he was saddened by the dullness of their hearts), he said to the man: ‘Now, stretch out your hand.’ So he stretched it out... And his hand was restored!
[Mark] [3]:[6] Well, right away the Pharisees went outside and met with the followers of Herod, and they started talking about ways to destroy him.
[Mark] [3]:[7] Meanwhile, Jesus and his disciples got up and walked out to the sea, followed by a huge crowd that had come from all around Galilee and Judea.
[Mark] [3]:[8] For people were coming to him from as far away as JeruSalem, Idumea, the other side of the Jordan, and the area around Tyre and Sidon. Huge numbers came to him when they heard of the things that he was doing.
[Mark] [3]:[9] Well, to keep the crowds at bay, [Jesus] had instructed his disciples to always have a little boat available for him.
[Mark] [3]:[10] For because he cured so many that had terrible diseases, people were literally falling on him just to touch him!
[Mark] [3]:[11] And when unclean spirits saw him, they’d bow low before him and shout: ‘You’re the Son of The God!’
[Mark] [3]:[12] However, he scolded them and warned them not to expose him.
[Mark] [3]:[13] Then [Jesus] walked up a mountain, where he called for those whom he’d chosen,
[Mark] [3]:[14] and he formed a [special] group from these twelve that he started calling Apostles (Sent Ones), that were to stay with him. Thereafter, he also sent them out to preach,
[Mark] [3]:[15] and he gave them the power to cast out demons.
[Mark] [3]:[16] The names of those in the group of twelve that he formed were: Simon (Peter),
[Mark] [3]:[17] James (son of ZebediOu), and his brother John (he called them BoanErges, which means Sons of Thunder),
[Mark] [3]:[18] Andrew, Philip, BarTholomew ([NathaniEl]), Matthew, Thomas, James (son of AlphaEus), ThadDaeus (Judas), Simon the CanaNaean, and
[Mark] [3]:[19] Judas IsCariot (who later betrayed him). Well, whenever he went into a house after that,
[Mark] [3]:[20] so many people would show up, that they couldn’t even eat a meal!
[Mark] [3]:[21] And when [Jesus’] relatives heard what was happening, they tried to take him away, because they said that he’d lost his mind!
[Mark] [3]:[22] There were also some scribes that had come down from JeruSalem who were telling people he was [under the influence of] BeElZebub, and that he was using ‘the ruler of the demons to cast out the demons.’
[Mark] [3]:[23] So he called [the scribes] to him and he reasoned with them using [these] parables: ‘How can the Opposer throw out the Opposer?
[Mark] [3]:[24] For a kingdom divided cannot stand.
[Mark] [3]:[25] Nor can a house that’s divided.
[Mark] [3]:[26] So, if the Opposer is divided, He cannot stand and he’s reaching his end.
[Mark] [3]:[27] ‘Also, no one can enter a mighty man’s house And rob him of all his things Unless he first ties him up… Only then can he loot his house.
[Mark] [3]:[28] ‘So I tell you this as the truth: ‘Sons of men can be forgiven for all, No matter what sins that they might commit Or whatever blasphemies they speak.
[Mark] [3]:[29] But whoever blasphemes [God’s] Holy breath Won’t be forgiven throughout the age, And it remains a sin throughout the ages.’
[Mark] [3]:[30] Of course, [Jesus] was saying this to them because they’d accused him of having an unclean spirit.
[Mark] [3]:[31] Meanwhile, [Jesus’] mother and brothers had arrived and were standing outside, so they asked [someone] to call for him,
[Mark] [3]:[32] because there was a crowd sitting around him at the time. Therefore, someone went up to him and said: ‘Look! Your mother and brothers are outside and they’re looking for you!’
[Mark] [3]:[33] But he said to them all: ‘Just who are my mother and brothers?’
[Mark] [3]:[34] Then he looked at those who were sitting around him in a circle and said: ‘Look… My mother and brothers!
[Mark] [3]:[35] For, all that do the will of our God Are truly my brothers, sisters, and mother.’
[Mark] [4]:[1] Well on another occasion, as he was teaching by the seashore, such a huge crowd came to him there that he had to step into a boat and sit out on the sea, as the crowd stood on the shore.
[Mark] [4]:[2] Then he taught them many things through parables, saying:
[Mark] [4]:[3] ‘Now, pay close attention! '{Look!} A farmer went out to do planting.
[Mark] [4]:[4] And as he was scattering seeds, A few fell alongside the road, Which were thereafter eaten by birds.
[Mark] [4]:[5] ‘Other seeds fell among rocks, And they sprouted where there wasn’t much ground. But because there was too little soil,
[Mark] [4]:[6] When the sun arose, they were scorched… They withered, because they didn’t have roots.
[Mark] [4]:[7] ‘Other seeds fell among briers, Which grew and choked out those seeds, So they couldn’t produce any fruit.
[Mark] [4]:[8] ‘But others fell upon good soil, Where they flourished and grew, producing much fruit, Some 30, some 60, or 100 times more.’
[Mark] [4]:[9] Then he added: ‘Let those who have ears pay attention!’
[Mark] [4]:[10] Well later, the twelve [disciples] (as well as the rest that were around him) asked [Jesus] what the parable meant.
[Mark] [4]:[11] And he told them this: ‘The mystery of the Kingdom of God has just been given to you. For those on the outside only hear the stories
[Mark] [4]:[12] so when they can look, they can’t see, and when they hear, they don’t really listen and understand, so they can ever turn back and be forgiven.
[Mark] [4]:[13] ‘However, if you don’t understand the meanings of these parables, how will you be able to understand all the rest?
[Mark] [4]:[14] ‘The one who is scattering the seeds is planting the word,
[Mark] [4]:[15] and where it falls beside the road, the Opposer immediately comes and snatches away all that was dropped there.
[Mark] [4]:[16] ‘The same is true of those that fall among the rocks. These are the ones who joyfully accept the word as soon as they hear it,
[Mark] [4]:[17] but because they don’t have roots, they only last a little while. For when some difficulty or persecution comes along over the word, they’re stumbled.
[Mark] [4]:[18] ‘Likewise, those who are planted among the thorns are the ones who hear the word,
[Mark] [4]:[19] but let it get choked out by the concerns of this life, the allure of wealth, and desires for other things, so they become unfruitful.
[Mark] [4]:[20] ‘However, those that are planted on the fine soil are the ones who listen to the word and accept it… ‘Then they bear fruit 30, 60, and 100 times more.’
[Mark] [4]:[21] So Jesus went on to tell them this: ‘You don’t put a lamp under a basket, Nor do you put it under a bed… You it put on a table, instead.
[Mark] [4]:[22] So there’s no secret that won’t be made known, Or anything hidden that won’t be shown…
[Mark] [4]:[23] Let those who have ears pay attention!’
[Mark] [4]:[24] He continued: ‘Pay attention to the things that I’m saying! Whatever amount that you measure for others Is the amount that you’ll receive… And more will be added to that.
[Mark] [4]:[25] For those who have will be given more, While all will be taken from those who don’t have.’
[Mark] [4]:[26] Then he went on to say: ‘The Kingdom of God is much like a man Who scatters his seeds on the ground,
[Mark] [4]:[27] And goes to sleep through the night. Then, when he wakes up the next morning, He finds that the seeds have sprouted and grown, And he doesn’t really know how it happened!
[Mark] [4]:[28] ‘For the ground produces fruit by itself… First the blades, then the stalks, And finally, the full heads of grain.
[Mark] [4]:[29] Then as soon as it has all ripened, The man arrives with his sickle… For the time to harvest has arrived.’
[Mark] [4]:[30] And he asked: ‘To what [else] can the Kingdom of God be compared… What parables can we use to describe it?
[Mark] [4]:[31] ‘It’s much like the small mustard seed, Which, before it’s planted under the ground Is one of the smallest seeds on the earth.
[Mark] [4]:[32] Yet, after it’s planted, it grows To be larger than all vegetation… It grows branches that can be so great That birds in the skies can dwell in its shadow.’
[Mark] [4]:[33] Yes, this is the way he taught the word to them, speaking in parables for as long as they were able to pay attention.
[Mark] [4]:[34] It’s a fact that if he wasn’t speaking in parables, he wasn’t talking to them. However, when they were all alone, he thereafter explained everything to his disciples.
[Mark] [4]:[35] Well, later that evening, he said to them: ‘Now, let’s cross over to the other shore.’
[Mark] [4]:[36] So after they dismissed the crowd, they left in the same boat that he had been teaching from (along with some other boats that came with them).
[Mark] [4]:[37] However, a gale-force wind then arose and waves were pouring into the boats... [spurious words]
[Mark] [4]:[38] But meanwhile, [Jesus] was peacefully sleeping on a pillow in the stern. So they woke him up and said: ‘Teacher, aren’t you worried that we’re about to die?’
[Mark] [4]:[39] So he got up and scolded the wind, then he said to the sea: ‘Be quiet! Hush!’ And at that, the wind died down and a great calm set in.
[Mark] [4]:[40] And he asked them: ‘Why are you so cowardly? Don’t you have any faith?’
[Mark] [4]:[41] Well, this really frightened them and they started asking each other: ‘Who really is this? For even the wind and the sea obeys him!’
[Mark] [5]:[1] Then when they got to the other side of the sea to the country of the Garasenes,
[Mark] [5]:[2] [Jesus] got out of the boat and was immediately confronted by a man with an unclean spirit, who had come from the tombs.
[Mark] [5]:[3] For he lived among the tombs and no one had been able to restrain him, even with chains.
[Mark] [5]:[4] In fact, he’d often been bound using leg irons and chains, but he broke the chains and smashed the leg irons. Nothing was strong enough to hold him!
[Mark] [5]:[5] So all day and night long, he’d go around the tombs and the mountains yelling crazily, while hitting himself with rocks.
[Mark] [5]:[6] Then, when he saw Jesus coming in the distance, he ran up to him and bowed low,
[Mark] [5]:[7] screaming: ‘What dealings do I have with you, Jesus, the Son of the Most High God? ‘I put you under oath by God not to torment me!’
[Mark] [5]:[8] [He said this] because [Jesus] had told the unclean spirit to come out of the man.
[Mark] [5]:[9] Then [Jesus] asked [the spirit]: ‘What’s your name?’ And it replied: ‘My name is Legion, because there are many of us!’
[Mark] [5]:[10] And [the spirits] repeatedly begged [Jesus] not to drive them out of those fields.
[Mark] [5]:[11] Well at the time, there was a large group of pigs feeding on the mountain.
[Mark] [5]:[12] So [the demons] begged Jesus to send them into the pigs,
[Mark] [5]:[13] and he gave them permission. So the unclean spirits came out and entered the pigs, then they all ran down a steep drop-off and fell into the sea, drowning about 2,000 of them.
[Mark] [5]:[14] Well thereafter, the herdsmen ran off and reported this to the people in the cities and the fields roundabout, and then all the people went there to see [what had happened].
[Mark] [5]:[15] And when they got to Jesus, they could see that the man who’d once been possessed by the legion [of demons] was just sitting there, wearing clothes, and in his right mind… And this frightened them.
[Mark] [5]:[16] Then after [the herdsmen] who had been there explained everything that had happened to the demon-possessed man and to the pigs,
[Mark] [5]:[17] the people begged [Jesus] to leave their district!
[Mark] [5]:[18] Well, as [Jesus] got back into the boat, the man who was once demonized started begging to let him come with them.
[Mark] [5]:[19] However, [Jesus] wouldn’t allow this, for he said: ‘Go back to your home and family and tell them all the things that [Jehovah] has done for you, and about the great mercy He has shown to you.’
[Mark] [5]:[20] So [the man] went back to the DecaPolis and started telling everyone about what Jesus had done for him, and it amazed everyone.
[Mark] [5]:[21] Well, after they had crossed back to the other side [of the sea] in the boat, a huge crowd started to gather as Jesus arrived.
[Mark] [5]:[22] Then, one of the [local] synagogue’s head people (a man named JaiRus) came and fell at his feet.
[Mark] [5]:[23] And he kept begging [Jesus], saying: ‘My little daughter is [about to breathe her] last. Please come and lay your hands on her so she can recover and live!’
[Mark] [5]:[24] So [Jesus] went off with him, and a huge number followed along, all crowded against him...
[Mark] [5]:[25] Well, among [these people] was a woman who had [endured] a blood flow for about 12 years…
[Mark] [5]:[26] She’d suffered a lot at the hands of the healers, and she’d spent everything she had to no avail (she only got worse).
[Mark] [5]:[27] So when she heard about Jesus, she came up behind [him] in the crowd and touched his clothes;
[Mark] [5]:[28] for she kept saying: ‘If I can just touch his clothes I’ll be saved [from this condition].’
[Mark] [5]:[29] And right away, her fountain of blood dried up, and she knew in her body that she had been healed of this plague!
[Mark] [5]:[30] However Jesus also recognized in himself that some power had left him when this happened. So he turned around in the crowd and asked: ‘Who touched my clothes?’
[Mark] [5]:[31] And his disciples replied: ‘You see all these people crowded around you, and you ask, Who touched me?’
[Mark] [5]:[32] But he kept on looking around to see who did this.
[Mark] [5]:[33] Then the woman (who was frightened and trembling because she knew what had happened to her) came and fell down before him and told him the truth.
[Mark] [5]:[34] And he said to her: ‘Daughter, your faith has saved you! Go in peace… And may this be the last of the plague.’
[Mark] [5]:[35] Meanwhile, as he was still speaking, a messenger came from the home of the synagogue chief, who told him: ‘Your daughter has died, so don’t bother the teacher.’
[Mark] [5]:[36] But when Jesus overheard this, he told the chief of the synagogue: ‘Don’t be afraid, just have faith.’
[Mark] [5]:[37] Well, [when he reached the home], he didn’t allow anyone to go with him other than Peter, James, and John (James’ brother).
[Mark] [5]:[38] And when he got inside the synagogue-chief’s house and saw all the confusion, crying, and wailing,
[Mark] [5]:[39] he asked: ‘Why are you creating such an uproar and crying? The little girl isn’t dead, she’s just sleeping!’
[Mark] [5]:[40] Well at that, they all started laughing at him. But after he ushered them outside, he took the father, mother, and those who were with him into [the room] where the child was.
[Mark] [5]:[41] Then he took [the little girl] by the hand and said: ‘Talitha, cumi!’ (which translates as, ‘Little girl, wake up!’).
[Mark] [5]:[42] And the 12-year-old girl got up right away and started walking around! Well, [the parents] were beside themselves [with joy].
[Mark] [5]:[43] Then he told them to give her something to eat, and he repeatedly ordered them not to tell anyone what had really happened.
[Mark] [6]:[1] Thereafter, he left that place and went with his disciples to the town where he’d grown up.
[Mark] [6]:[2] And when the Sabbath arrived, he entered their synagogue and started teaching. Well, most of those who heard him were shocked, and asked: ‘Where did he get all these things? Why has such wisdom been given to this man, and why are such powerful deeds being performed through his hands?
[Mark] [6]:[3] ‘For isn’t this the carpenter, Mary’s son, and the brother of James, JoSeph, Judas, and Simon? And aren’t his sisters here among us?’ So they were stumbled over him.
[Mark] [6]:[4] And Jesus told them: ‘A Prophet doesn’t go without honor anywhere – other than in his own home, among his relatives, and in the area where he grew up.’
[Mark] [6]:[5] So because of this, he wasn’t able to preform any powerful deeds there, apart from laying his hands on a few [sick ones], whom he cured.
[Mark] [6]:[6] For he was amazed by their lack of faith. Well from there, he traveled around to the local villages in a circuit, teaching.
[Mark] [6]:[7] Then he called the twelve [disciples] and started sending them out by twos, and he gave them power over the unclean spirits.
[Mark] [6]:[8] He ordered them not to carry anything with them other than a walking stick… [yes,] no bread, no food pouch, nor copper money in their sashes.
[Mark] [6]:[9] And he told them not to tie on their sandals or to [carry extra] underclothes.
[Mark] [6]:[10] For he said: ‘Wherever you enter a house, stay in that place until you get ready to leave.
[Mark] [6]:[11] But in those places where they don’t invite you in or listen to you, shake the dirt off your feet as you leave, as a witness against them.’ [spurious words, copied from Matthew 10:15]
[Mark] [6]:[12] So they all went out and preached, calling for people to repent,
[Mark] [6]:[13] as they were casting out many demons and greasing sick people with oil to cure them.
[Mark] [6]:[14] Meanwhile, King Herod had heard about how famous [Jesus] was becoming. For some people were saying: ‘John, the man who did the immersing [in water], has been raised from the dead! And now there are great powers working through him.’
[Mark] [6]:[15] However, others were saying that he was EliJah, and some were saying that he was a Prophet like one of the Prophets [of old].
[Mark] [6]:[16] But after he’d listened to all of this, Herod concluded: ‘The John whom I beheaded has been raised!’
[Mark] [6]:[17] For it was Herod himself that had [ordered] John arrested and locked in prison over the matter of his taking Herodias (his brother’s woman),
[Mark] [6]:[18] since John kept telling Herod that he’d broken the Law by taking her.
[Mark] [6]:[19] That’s why Herodias hated him and wanted him killed… However [until then], she’d been unable to do so.
[Mark] [6]:[20] Herod was actually afraid of John, because he knew that he was a righteous and holy man. As a result, he kept him safely [locked away]. For after he’d listened to him for a while, Herod had no idea what to do with him. So, he gladly just kept on listening to him.
[Mark] [6]:[21] However, there came a day that turned out to be convenient for Herod… It was when he was holding a banquet to celebrate his [own] birthday. He had invited several high-ranking men, military commanders, and the foremost people of Galilee.
[Mark] [6]:[22] There, Herod and Herodias’ daughter entered and danced before them. This pleased Herod and those at the table so much, that the king said to the little girl: ‘Ask for whatever you wish and, I’ll give it to you!’
[Mark] [6]:[23] Yes, he swore to her: ‘Whatever you ask of me I’ll give you, up to half of my kingdom!’
[Mark] [6]:[24] So she went out and asked her mother: ‘What should I ask for?’ And [her mother] replied: ‘Ask for the head of John, the one who does the immersing!’
[Mark] [6]:[25] So she ran back to the king and said: ‘I want you to give me the head of John the Immerser on a platter… Right now.’
[Mark] [6]:[26] And although this deeply disturbed the king, he didn’t want to ignore her because of the oaths, and because of those who were reclining at the table.
[Mark] [6]:[27] So the king immediately sent his bodyguard and commanded him to bring back [John’s] head. And that’s when [the guard] went off and beheaded John in prison,

[Luke] [1]:[1] Since many others have already taken on the job of putting together a statement of the facts regarding the things we believe

[Luke] [1]:[5] In the days of King Herod of Judea, there was a Priest named ZechariAh who was of the division of AbiJah. He had a wife named EliZabeth [meaning, My God has Sworn], who was a descendant of Aaron.

[Luke] [1]:[10] Since it was the scheduled time for offering incense, a large crowd of people had also gathered outside to pray.

[Luke] [7]:[18] Meanwhile, John’s disciples had been reporting back to him about the things that were happening.
[Luke] [7]:[19] So John called two of his disciples and sent them to the Lord to ask: ‘Are you the one who is to come, or should we expect someone else?’
[Luke] [7]:[20] And when they got to [Jesus], the men told him: ‘John the Immerser sent us to ask if you’re the Anointed One, or if we’re to expect someone else?’
[Luke] [7]:[21] Well, during that same hour, Jesus cured many people who were ill or in great pain or had wicked spirits, and he granted many blind people the gift of vision.
[Luke] [7]:[22] And after that, he said this [to John’s disciples]: ‘Now, go back and report what you’ve seen and heard to John. [Tell him that] the blind are seeing, the lame are walking, people with infections are being cleansed, the deaf are hearing, the dead are being raised, and the poor are hearing the good news…
[Luke] [7]:[23] ‘So, the one who isn’t stumbled by me will be blest.’
[Luke] [7]:[24] Well, after John’s messengers left, he asked the crowd this about John: ‘What did you go to the desert to see… Reeds being blown in the wind?
[Luke] [7]:[25] Yes, what did you go out to see… A man who has dressed in soft clothes? Those who dress and live well, Are the ones who are living in mansions.
[Luke] [7]:[26] ‘So, what did you go out to see… A Prophet? Yes, and I say, much more than a Prophet,
[Luke] [7]:[27] For, he’s the one of whom it was written: '{Look!} I will send My messenger before him, To prepare the road that he’ll travel.’ [Malachi 3:1]
[Luke] [7]:[28] ‘So I tell you this: ‘Of all those born of a woman, None have been greater than John. Yet the least in the Kingdom of God Will be greater than him.’
[Luke] [7]:[29] Well, when all the common people and the tax collectors heard this, they praised God’s righteousness, because they’d all been immersed with John’s immersion.
[Luke] [7]:[30] But the Pharisees and those who were trained in the Law disregarded this counsel from God, and they didn’t go out to be immersed by John.
[Luke] [7]:[31] [So, Jesus said this to them]: ‘To what can I compare this people… Yes, what are they really like?
[Luke] [7]:[32] They’re like children that play in the markets And shout at each other and say: We played the flute, but you didn’t dance… We wailed, but you didn’t cry.
[Luke] [7]:[33] ‘For when John the Immerser arrived, He didn’t feast or drink any wine… Yet you said that he had a demon!
[Luke] [7]:[34] ‘But when the Son of Man arrived here, Eating well and drinking the wine, You called him an alcoholic and glutton… A friend to tax collectors and sinners!
[Luke] [7]:[35] ‘But wisdom is proven righteous by its results.’
[Luke] [7]:[36] Thereafter, one of the Pharisees invited [Jesus] to dine with him, so he went to the Pharisee’s house and reclined at his table.
[Luke] [7]:[37] But {Look!} a woman of the city (a known sinner), who had learned that [Jesus] was going to recline for a meal in the house of the Pharisee, brought in an alabaster jar of perfumed ointment...
[Luke] [7]:[38] And she reclined behind him at his feet and started weeping and wetting his feet with her tears, then wiping them dry with her hair, as she tenderly kissed his feet and greased them with the perfumed ointment.
[Luke] [7]:[39] Well, when the Pharisee that invited him saw this, he thought to himself: ‘If this man was truly a Prophet, he’d know who it is and just what kind of woman is touching him… She’s a sinner!’
[Luke] [7]:[40] Then Jesus said to him: ‘Simon, I have something to tell you.’ And [Simon] replied: ‘Go ahead and tell it, Teacher!’ [And Jesus said:]
[Luke] [7]:[41] ‘There were two men who each owed money to a certain lender... One was in debt for 500 silver coins, and the other for 50.
[Luke] [7]:[42] Well, when neither one could pay him back, he freely forgave them both. ‘So, which one will love him more?’
[Luke] [7]:[43] Then Simon answered: ‘I guess it’s the one he forgave the most.’ And [Jesus] said: ‘You judged correctly.’
[Luke] [7]:[44] Then Jesus turned and looked at the woman, and he said to Simon: ‘Do you see this woman? ‘When I entered your house, you didn’t give me any water for my feet… Yet this woman wet my feet with her tears, and she wiped them dry with her hair!
[Luke] [7]:[45] ‘And you didn’t greet me with a kiss… Yet from the time that I entered, this woman has been tenderly kissing my feet.
[Luke] [7]:[46] ‘You didn’t grease my head with oil either… Yet this woman greased my feet with perfumed ointment.
[Luke] [7]:[47] ‘So I tell you: Although she has many sins, they are forgiven because she showed a lot of love. However, those who haven’t been forgiven for much, don’t love as much.’
[Luke] [7]:[48] Then he told her: ‘Your sins are forgiven.’
[Luke] [7]:[49] Well at that, those who were reclining at the table with him started wondering within themselves: ‘Just who is this man who [thinks he can] even forgive sins?’
[Luke] [7]:[50] But he said to the woman: ‘Your faith has saved you. Go your own way in peace.’
[Luke] [8]:[1] Well after that, [Jesus] started traveling from city to city and village to village with the twelve [disciples], preaching and proclaiming the good news of the Kingdom of God.
[Luke] [8]:[2] Also [traveling with him] were some women whom [he’d] cured of wicked spirits and illnesses. There was Mary (whom is called the Magdalean) from whom 7 demons had come out,
[Luke] [8]:[3] Joanna the wife of Chuza (Herod’s top aid), as well as Susanna and many others that were serving his needs from their possessions.
[Luke] [8]:[4] Well when a large crowd had gathered along with those who were traveling with him from city to city, he spoke to them using this parable:
[Luke] [8]:[5] ‘A farmer went out to plant seeds. ‘And as he was planting, some fell by the road, Which were walked on, and birds came to eat them.
[Luke] [8]:[6] ‘Others fell among rocks, Where they dried up after they sprouted, Because there was too little water.
[Luke] [8]:[7] ‘Still others fell among thorns, Which grew and then choked them out.
[Luke] [8]:[8] ‘But some fell on the good soil and grew, Producing fruit 100 times more.’ And after he said this, he shouted: ‘Let those who have ears to hear, listen to me!’
[Luke] [8]:[9] Well, his disciples later asked him what this parable meant.
[Luke] [8]:[10] So he said: ‘While you’ve been allowed to understand the mysteries of the Kingdom of God, the rest of these people just hear the stories. So when they look, they look in vain, and when they hear, they don’t understand.
[Luke] [8]:[11] ‘Now, the illustration means this: ‘The seeds are the word of God.
[Luke] [8]:[12] ‘Those [that fall] by the road are people who listen, but then the Slanderer comes and snatches the word from their hearts, so they don’t believe and come to salvation.
[Luke] [8]:[13] ‘Those which fall on the rocks are the ones who hear and welcome the word with joy... But because they don’t have any roots, they only believe for a season. So, when a time of testing comes along, they fall away.
[Luke] [8]:[14] ‘As for those which fall among the thorns... These are the ones who have heard, but because of their daily concerns such as [seeking] wealth and the pleasures of living, they’re choked out and fail to produce any fruit.
[Luke] [8]:[15] ‘However, [those which fall] on the good soil have good and pure hearts. And after hearing the Word, they remember it and keep on bearing fruit.
[Luke] [8]:[16] ‘Understand that nobody lights a lamp and then covers it with a pot, or hides it under a bed… They put it on a lampstand so that those who step in can see by the light.
[Luke] [8]:[17] ‘So there’s nothing hidden that won’t be shown, Or nothing covered that won’t be known, And then brought out in the light.
[Luke] [8]:[18] ‘So pay attention to the way that you listen... For those who have will be given more. But as for those who have nothing, What they think they have will be taken away from them.’
[Luke] [8]:[19] It was then that [Jesus’] mother and brothers came to see him, but they were unable to reach him because of the crowd.
[Luke] [8]:[20] So someone came up to him and said: ‘Your mother and brothers are waiting outside and [they] want to see you.’
[Luke] [8]:[21] But he replied: ‘My mother and brothers are these that hear the word of God and obey it.’
[Luke] [8]:[22] Well, some days later, [Jesus] and his disciples got into a boat, and he said to them: ‘Let’s cross over to the other side of the lake.’ So they set off...
[Luke] [8]:[23] And as they were sailing along, he fell asleep. But then a violent windstorm came down on the lake, and the boat started taking on water, putting them in a dangerous situation.
[Luke] [8]:[24] So [the disciples] went over and woke Jesus up and said: ‘Lord… Lord… We’re about to drown!’ Then when he awoke, he scolded the wind and the raging water, which made things suddenly become very calm and peaceful.
[Luke] [8]:[25] And then he asked them: ‘Where is your faith?’ Well, they were frightened and awestruck [by what had happened], and they started asking each other: ‘Who really is this? For he even orders the wind and waves and they obey him!’
[Luke] [8]:[26] Then from there, they sailed on to the country of the GeraSenes, which is on the shore directly across from Galilee.
[Luke] [8]:[27] And when he stepped out on land, a demonized man came from the city to meet him. This man hadn’t worn clothing for some time, and he didn’t live in a house, for he stayed among the tombs.
[Luke] [8]:[28] And when he saw Jesus, he screamed and fell down in front of him, shouting: ‘What dealings do I have with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I beg you… Don’t torment me!’
[Luke] [8]:[29] ([He said this, because Jesus] had ordered the unclean spirit to come out of the man). [This man had been] arrested repeatedly, then bound with chains and leg irons and put under guard... But he would break the chains, and the demons forced him to [live in] such isolated places.
[Luke] [8]:[30] So Jesus asked him: ‘What’s your name?’ And they replied: ‘Legion’ (because many demons had entered him).
[Luke] [8]:[31] And they kept begging him not to order them to go away into the abyss.
[Luke] [8]:[32] Well at the time, a large herd of pigs happened to be feeding there on the mountain; so they begged [Jesus] to allow them to go into [the pigs]… And he gave them permission.
[Luke] [8]:[33] Then the demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the whole herd ran down a steep drop-off into the lake and drowned!
[Luke] [8]:[34] Well, when the herders saw this, they ran and reported what had happened throughout the whole city and countryside.
[Luke] [8]:[35] As a result, the people all came to see this. When they got to Jesus, they found the man whom the demons had left now wearing clothes and in his right mind – [sitting] there at Jesus’ feet… And this frightened them.
[Luke] [8]:[36] Then those who had witnessed what had happened explained to the people how the demon-possessed man had been cured.
[Luke] [8]:[37] And the huge number [of people] who had come from the surrounding area started begging [Jesus] to leave them, because they were so frightened! So, he stepped back into the boat to return [to the other side of the lake].
[Luke] [8]:[38] However, the man whom the demons had left started begging [Jesus] to let him go back with him. But he sent the man away, saying:
[Luke] [8]:[39] ‘Just go home and tell everyone about all the things that God has done for you.’ So the man went back and spread the word about what Jesus had done throughout the whole city.
[Luke] [8]:[40] Meanwhile, a crowd was waiting for Jesus when he got back [to the other side], because they were all expecting him.
[Luke] [8]:[41] And {Look!} a man named JaiRus (who was a presiding officer of the [local] synagogue) came to him and fell at Jesus’ feet, begging him to come to his home,
[Luke] [8]:[42] because his only daughter (who was about 12 years old) was dying. Well, as he was on his way [to the man’s house], the people were all crowded closely around him,
[Luke] [8]:[43] and a woman who had [been experiencing] a blood flow for some 12 years (which no one had been able to cure)

[Luke] [8]:[45] So Jesus asked: ‘Who touched me?’ Well, everyone denied it. And Peter said: ‘Master, there’s a whole crowd of people around you [and they’re all] touching you!’
[Luke] [8]:[46] But Jesus said: ‘Someone else touched me, because I felt the power flowing out of me.’
[Luke] [8]:[47] So, seeing that [what she did] didn’t go unnoticed, the woman came up and fell down in front of Jesus trembling, then she told everyone why she touched him and of how she’d been healed instantly.
[Luke] [8]:[48] So [Jesus] said to her: ‘Daughter, your faith has saved you. Go your own way in peace.’
[Luke] [8]:[49] Then as he was still talking, someone came up beside the presiding officer of the synagogue and said: ‘Your daughter has died, so don’t bother the teacher anymore.’
[Luke] [8]:[50] But when he heard this, Jesus said to the man: ‘Don’t be afraid; just have faith and she’ll be saved.’
[Luke] [8]:[51] Well when he got to the man’s house, he wouldn’t let anyone go inside with him other than Peter, John, James, and the girl’s father and mother.
[Luke] [8]:[52] Meanwhile, [outside] the people were all crying and beating themselves in grief over her. So he said to them: ‘Stop crying! The girl isn’t dead, she’s just sleeping.’
[Luke] [8]:[53] Then they all started laughing at him, because they all knew that she’d died.
[Luke] [8]:[54] But thereafter, he went inside and took her by the hand and called her, saying: ‘Child, get up!’
[Luke] [8]:[55] And at that, she started breathing and she stood up! Then he ordered that she be given something to eat.
[Luke] [8]:[56] Well, they were beside themselves [with joy]… But he warned them not to tell anyone what happened.

[Luke] [9]:[4] But, wherever you enter a home, lodge there and go out [to preach].
[Luke] [9]:[5] ‘And wherever people fail to welcome you, just shake the dust off your feet as you’re leaving that city, as a witness against them.’

[Luke] [9]:[7] Meanwhile, Herod (the district ruler) had heard about everything that was happening, and he was bothered by doubts. You see, some people were saying that [Jesus] was actually John raised from the dead,

[Luke] [9]:[28] Well, just as he said, this is what happened about eight days later: He’d taken Peter, John, and James up on a mountain to pray...
[Luke] [9]:[29] And as he was praying, his face changed and his clothes started to glow!
[Luke] [9]:[30] Then {Look!} two men appeared and started talking to him… It was Moses and EliJah!
[Luke] [9]:[31] (They could recognize them.) And these men started talking [with Jesus] about his departure that was about to be fulfilled in JeruSalem.
[Luke] [9]:[32] Until then, Peter and the others had been very sleepy. But when they saw his glory and the two men standing with him, they were suddenly wide-awake!
[Luke] [9]:[33] And through the separation between them, Peter said to Jesus: ‘Master, it’s good for us to be here, so let us erect three temporary structures… One for you, one for Moses, and one for EliJah!’ But he really didn’t know what he was saying.

[Luke] [9]:[37] Then the next day, as they were descending the mountain, they were met by a huge crowd.

[Luke] [9]:[39] ‘Look! A spirit comes over him and he screams... Then it throws him into convulsions and he foams [at the mouth]. And although it stops after that, it leaves him all bruised!
[Luke] [9]:[40] ‘I begged your disciples to throw it out, but they couldn’t do it!’

[Luke] [9]:[42] However, just as [the son] was approaching, the demon threw him to the ground and forced him into a violent convulsion. But Jesus scolded the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father… And everyone was astonished by the majestic power of God.

[Luke] [9]:[46] But then later, [the Apostles] started wondering which of them would be the greatest.

[Luke] [9]:[49] In reply, John said: ‘Master, we saw a man casting out demons by using your name and we tried to stop him, because he isn’t one of us!’

[Luke] [9]:[51] Now, since the number of days before he was going to be lifted up were about to run out, Jesus became firm in his resolve to go up to JeruSalem.

[Luke] [9]:[53] However, [the people there told them] that he wasn’t welcome if he was headed towards JeruSalem!
[Luke] [9]:[54] And when the Disciples James and John [heard about] this, they asked Jesus: ‘Lord, do you want us to call fire down from the sky to wipe them out?’
[Luke] [9]:[55] But he turned and scolded them,
[Luke] [9]:[56] [spurious words] and they traveled on to another village.
[Luke] [9]:[57] Well, as they were traveling along the road, someone said to [Jesus]: ‘Lord, I’ll follow you wherever you go!’
[Luke] [9]:[58] And Jesus told him: ‘Foxes have burrows, and [birds] in the skies have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.’
[Luke] [9]:[59] Well after that, he invited someone else to become his follower. But the man replied: ‘First let me go and bury my father.’
[Luke] [9]:[60] And [Jesus] told him: ‘Let the dead bury their own dead! You should go out and preach about the Kingdom of God!’
[Luke] [9]:[61] Then another one came up and said: ‘I’ll follow you Lord… But first let me say goodbye to those in my home.’
[Luke] [9]:[62] However, Jesus told him: ‘No one who looks back after he puts his hands to a plow is well suited for the Kingdom of God.’
[Luke] [10]:[1] Well after that, the Lord appointed 70 others that he sent out ahead of him in pairs into every city and place that he was going to go.
[Luke] [10]:[2] And he told them: ‘There’s a huge harvest, but there aren’t enough workers. So, beg the Master of the harvest to force more workers to do the harvesting.
[Luke] [10]:[3] ‘Now, get going! ‘Look; I’m sending you out as lambs among wolves.
[Luke] [10]:[4] Therefore, don’t carry a bag of money or a food pouch or sandals, and don’t [stop to] greet people along the road.
[Luke] [10]:[5] ‘Then as you enter each house you should say: ‘May this house have peace.’
[Luke] [10]:[6] ‘And if a son of peace lives there, your peace will rest upon him… But if not, it’ll return to you.
[Luke] [10]:[7] So, stay in that house and eat and drink the things that they provide, because a worker deserves his wages… Don’t keep moving from one house to another.

[Luke] [10]:[19] For I’ve given you the authority to walk on serpents, scorpions, and on the power of the enemy… And nothing will harm you!
[Luke] [10]:[20] ‘However, don’t be joyful because [evil] spirits obeyed you; be joyful that your names have now been written in the heavens!’

[Luke] [10]:[23] Then with that, he turned to his disciples and spoke to them privately, saying: ‘The eyes that are seeing the things that you’re seeing, are blest;

[Luke] [10]:[25] {Look!} Then a man who knew the Law very well stood up [in the crowd], and to test [Jesus], he asked: ‘Teacher, what must I do to inherit age-long life?’
[Luke] [10]:[26] And [Jesus] replied: ‘What’s written in the Law… What have you read there?’
[Luke] [10]:[27] Then the man said: ‘You must love [Jehovah] your God with your whole heart, soul, strength, and mind, and you must love your neighbor as yourself.’ [combination of Deuteronomy 6:4-5 and 34]
[Luke] [10]:[28] And [Jesus] replied: ‘That’s the right answer. Keep on doing that and you’ll live.’
