[Acts] [1]:[22] (starting with his immersion by John until the day that he was taken up from us), and someone who witnessed his resurrection, should become one of us.’
[Acts] [1]:[23] So they asked two men to stand up, JoSeph (who is called BarSabbas and was surnamed Justus) and MatThias.
[Acts] [1]:[24] Then they prayed, saying: ‘O [Jehovah], ‘The One who knows the hearts of all men, ‘Show us which of these two You’ve chosen
[Acts] [1]:[25] to receive the position of Apostleship that Judas abandoned so that he could go his own way.’
[Acts] [1]:[26] And at that, they were both handed lots, and the selected lot fell to MatThias. As a result, he was considered as being among the other 11 Apostles.
[Acts] [2]:[1] Now, towards the end of the day known as Pentecost, while they were all observing that celebration,
[Acts] [2]:[2] a noise suddenly came out of the sky! It sounded like a violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
[Acts] [2]:[3] Then they saw what looked like tongues of fire, which were distributed so that one [tongue] sat over each of them...
[Acts] [2]:[4] And they all became filled with holy breath and started speaking different languages, saying whatever the breath was telling them to say!
[Acts] [2]:[5] Now at the time, there were reverent Jews from every nation under the sky who were staying in JeruSalem.
[Acts] [2]:[6] So when this sound occurred, a huge crowd gathered there and everyone was bewildered, because each person heard one of [the disciples] speaking his own language.
[Acts] [2]:[7] They were astonished and started to wonder and say: ‘These people who are talking are all Galileans, aren’t they?
[Acts] [2]:[8] So how is it that we’re each hearing our own native tongue being spoken?’
[Acts] [2]:[9] [Well, there were] Parthinians, Medes, Elamites, MesoPotamians, Judeans, CappaDokians, [and people from] Pontus, [the province of] Asia,
[Acts] [2]:[10] Phrygia, PamPhylia, Egypt, parts of Libya Cyrene, travelers from Rome (Jews and proselytes),
[Acts] [2]:[11] Cretans, and Arabians. [They said]: ‘We hear them talking about the wonderful things of God in our own language!’
[Acts] [2]:[12] Yes, they were all astonished and confused, and they were asking each other: ‘What’s this all about?’
[Acts] [2]:[13] However, others joked about them saying: ‘They’re full of sweet wine!’
[Acts] [2]:[14] But Peter then stood up beside the 11, and raising his voice, he said this: ‘Men of Judea and all you who live in JeruSalem, ‘I want you to know something… Listen to what I’m saying to you!
[Acts] [2]:[15] ‘These [men] really aren’t drunk as you think, because it’s only the 3rd hour of the day [that is, 9 AM in the Jewish time system, 12 noon in the Roman system]....
[Acts] [2]:[16] What’s happening is the thing that was said through the Prophet JoEl!
[Acts] [2]:[17] ‘For through him, God said: ‘In the last days, says The God, I will pour out my breath on all flesh, And your sons and daughters will then prophesy; Your young men will also have visions, And the old among you will [see things in] dreams.
[Acts] [2]:[18] ‘Yes, even upon My male servants And on those who are My handmaidens, I will pour out my breath in those days, And all will then prophesy.
[Acts] [2]:[19] ‘From the skies above, I’ll send omens and signs With blood, fire, and smoke to the earth down below,
[Acts] [2]:[20] Before the great, shining day of the Lord. ‘For the sun will be changed into darkness And the moon will be changed into blood.
[Acts] [2]:[21] Then, all of those will be saved That have called on the name of the Lord.’ Joel 2:28-32]
[Acts] [2]:[22] ‘Men of IsraEl; listen to these words! ‘Jesus the Nazarene was a man who was shown to you by The God with power, omens, and signs that He performed through him in your midst, as you already know.
[Acts] [2]:[23] Yet you handed this man (who had received his advice and his ability to see the future from God) over to men who don’t have the Law, and who then nailed him up!
[Acts] [2]:[24] ‘But thereafter, God resurrected him, freeing him from the cords of death, because it wasn’t possible for [death] to hold him down.
[Acts] [2]:[25] ‘So, notice that David said this about him: ‘I’ve always put the Lord before me; And since He’s at my right hand, I’ll never be shaken.
[Acts] [2]:[26] ‘Therefore, in my heart, I’m cheerful, And with my tongue, I’ll rejoice; For my body finds rest in the hope
[Acts] [2]:[27] That in the grave, You’ll not leave me, And Your loyal one won’t see decay.
[Acts] [2]:[28] ‘For the ways of life, You’ve shown me, And You’ll fill me with joy from Your face.’ [Psalm 16:8-11]
[Acts] [2]:[29] ‘Men! Brothers! ‘It’s good to speak to you openly about the patriarch David; for he died, was buried, and his tomb is still with us to this day.
[Acts] [2]:[30] For he was a Prophet, and he knew that The God had sworn an oath to him that He’d put someone on his throne who was the fruit of his loins.
[Acts] [2]:[31] ‘So [David] looked into the future and spoke about the resurrection of the Anointed One… That he wouldn’t be abandoned in the grave and that his flesh wouldn’t see decay.
[Acts] [2]:[32] ‘So this [one] Jesus has now been resurrected by The God (we’ve all been witnesses to this fact)
[Acts] [2]:[33] and he’s been elevated to God’s right hand, where he’s received the holy breath that the Father promised. ‘Therefore, he’s the one who poured out everything you’ve been seeing and hearing today!
[Acts] [2]:[34] ‘And although David didn’t go to heaven, he said: ‘[Jehovah] said this to my Lord: ‘Sit here at My right hand,
[Acts] [2]:[35] ‘Til I set your enemies as a stool for your feet.’ [Psalm 110:1]
[Acts] [2]:[36] ‘So let the entire House of IsraEl know for sure that God appointed this Jesus whom you impaled to be the Lord and His Anointed One!’
[Acts] [2]:[37] Well when they heard this, they were all stabbed to the heart! So they asked Peter and the other Apostles: ‘Men, Brothers, what must we do?’
[Acts] [2]:[38] Then Peter told them: ‘Repent! ‘And each of you should get immersed in the name of Jesus the Anointed One, so your sins can be forgiven… And then you’ll receive the gift of the holy breath.
[Acts] [2]:[39] ‘That’s a promise to you, to your children, and to all those who are far away… To all those who’ll be called by our God, [Jehovah]!’
[Acts] [2]:[40] Well thereafter, he went on and testified to them a lot more, giving them this advice: ‘Get saved from this crooked people!’
[Acts] [2]:[41] Then those who welcomed his words were immersed… And about 3,000 people were added that day!
[Acts] [2]:[42] These continued to attend, listening to the Apostles as they were teaching, and everyone participated as they were sharing in meals and in prayers.
[Acts] [2]:[43] For they were all in awe over the many signs and omens that started happening through the Apostles.
[Acts] [2]:[44] And all who became believers started sharing everything that they had;
[Acts] [2]:[45] they even sold their belongings and properties and distributed the proceeds to anyone who was in need.
[Acts] [2]:[46] They also agreed to go to the Temple every day, after which they’d eat their meals in private homes… Eating the food happily and with sincere hearts,
[Acts] [2]:[47] praising The God and finding favor with everyone. And all the while, the Lord kept adding more newly-saved ones to them each day.
[Acts] [3]:[1] Now, Peter and John had gone to the Temple for the scheduled time of prayer (at the 9th hour [that is, 3pm]),
[Acts] [3]:[2] and a man was there who had been lame from birth; [he] had to be carried and placed near the Temple gate (the one called Beautiful) every day, to beg from those entering the Temple.
[Acts] [3]:[3] And when he saw Peter and John about to enter the Temple, he started begging from them.
[Acts] [3]:[4] But Peter and John stared at him and said: ‘Look at us!’
[Acts] [3]:[5] So he looked at them, expecting to get something.
[Acts] [3]:[6] Then Peter said: ‘I don’t have any silver or gold, but I’ll give you what I do have… In the name of Jesus the Nazarene, the Anointed One, walk!’
[Acts] [3]:[7] Then he took him by the right hand and lifted him; and instantly, the soles of his feet and his anklebones were made well!
[Acts] [3]:[8] So he jumped up and stood… And then he started walking! So he entered the Temple with them, walking, jumping, and praising God.
[Acts] [3]:[9] Well, everyone noticed him walking around and praising God,
[Acts] [3]:[10] and they started to realize that this was the man who used to sit and beg at the Temple’s Beautiful Gate. This astonished them and they were all delighted by what had happened to him.
[Acts] [3]:[11] So, as the man was holding onto Peter and John near what was called The Columns of Solomon, all the people came running to them, shocked out of their wits.
[Acts] [3]:[12] And when Peter saw this, he said: ‘Men of IsraEl, ‘Why are you surprised at this? And why are you staring at us as though we made him walk by our own power or by our own devotion?
[Acts] [3]:[13] ‘It was the God of AbraHam, IsaAc, and Jacob – the God of our ancestors – who glorified His servant Jesus, whom you then betrayed and disowned before the face of Pilate after he’d actually decided to release him.
[Acts] [3]:[14] ‘Yes, you disowned that holy and righteous man, and you asked [Pilate] to [instead] release a man who was a murderer!
[Acts] [3]:[15] So you killed the Prince of Life! However, God thereafter raised him from the dead, which we had all witnessed!
[Acts] [3]:[16] ‘It’s because of [our] faith in his name that this man here –whom you see and know– was made well. Yes, it’s because of faith that everything you see here has happened!
[Acts] [3]:[17] ‘And now brothers, I know that what you did was done in ignorance… And this was true of your rulers.
[Acts] [3]:[18] But, just as it was foretold by the mouths of all the Prophets, it was God who caused His Anointed One to endure all these things, so that it could be fulfilled this way.
[Acts] [3]:[19] ‘So now, repent and turn around to get your sins erased, so that you might come to see a period of refreshment from [Jehovah]!
[Acts] [3]:[20] Then He will send this one [who was] proclaimed [or appointed] to you… The Anointed Jesus.
[Acts] [3]:[21] ‘However, he will remain in the heavens until the time when everything that God told us through the mouths of the holy [ones] in His age of the Prophets is restored.
[Acts] [3]:[22] ‘In fact, it was Moses who said: ‘[Jehovah] God will raise a Prophet like me from among your brothers, and you must listen to everything that he tells you.
[Acts] [3]:[23] Then if the people don’t listen to that Prophet, they’ll all be destroyed!’ [Deuteronomy 18:18-19]
[Acts] [3]:[24] ‘Why, all the Prophets from SamuEl onwards – everyone who spoke – clearly talked about these days...
[Acts] [3]:[25] And you are the sons of the Prophets! And [you’re also sons] of the Sacred Agreement that God made with your ancestors, when he told AbraHam: ‘All the families of the earth will be blest by your offspring!’ [Genesis 22:18]
[Acts] [3]:[26] ‘Therefore, God then raised this servant and sent him to you first as a blessing to you, so that each of you might turn away from the bad things that you’re doing.’
[Acts] [4]:[1] Well, as Peter and John were talking to the people, the Chief Priests, the Temple captains, and the SadDucees came up to them,
[Acts] [4]:[2] and were very annoyed by the fact that [Peter and John] were teaching the people and telling them how Jesus had been resurrected from the dead...
[Acts] [4]:[3] So they had them arrested and held until the next day (since it was already evening).
[Acts] [4]:[4] However, many of those who listened to them started believing, and their numbers grew until there were about 5,000 men.
[Acts] [4]:[5] Then the next day, a meeting was held in JeruSalem that included the rulers, elders, and scribes,
[Acts] [4]:[6] along with AnNas the Chief Priest, CaiAphas, John, Alexander, and all the rest of the Chief Priest’s relatives.
[Acts] [4]:[7] They stood [Peter and John] in their midst and asked them: ‘Who authorized you? And who told you that you could do these things?’
[Acts] [4]:[8] Then Peter (who became filled with Holy breath) spoke to them, saying: ‘Rulers of the people and elders,
[Acts] [4]:[9] ‘If we’re being questioned here today because [we] did a good deed for a handicapped person, and if we’re being asked who made him well...
[Acts] [4]:[10] Then you and all the people of IsraEl should know that it was done in the name of Jesus of Nazareth, the Anointed One… Whom you hung on a pole! ‘For God raised him from the dead, and he actually stood next to this man whom you now see here, completely healthy!
[Acts] [4]:[11] ‘Yes, this is ‘the stone that was rejected’ by you builders, but which has now ‘become the foundation cornerstone’! [reference to Psalm 118:22]
[Acts] [4]:[12] ‘So, salvation isn’t going to come from anyone else, because there isn’t another name that’s been given to any other man under the sky who can save us!’
[Acts] [4]:[13] Well, when they saw the confidence of Peter and John and realized that they were uneducated and common, everyone was amazed… And they started to recognize them, remembering that these men used to be with Jesus.
[Acts] [4]:[14] However, as they looked at the man who was standing next to them who’d been cured, nobody could come up with anything to say in rebuttal.
[Acts] [4]:[15] So then they sent them outside of the Jewish High-Court hall as they discussed the matter between themselves.
[Acts] [4]:[16] And they were saying: ‘What will we do with them? For it’s a fact that a sign has come through them! ‘And because everyone in JeruSalem saw it, we can’t deny it!
[Acts] [4]:[17] ‘So, to keep the news about this from being spread among all the people, let’s just threaten them and tell them not to speak to anyone about this name ever again!’
[Acts] [4]:[18] So then they called them back in and warned them not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus anywhere.
[Acts] [4]:[19] However, Peter and John replied: ‘Whether it’s righteous in God’s eyes to listen to you rather than to God, judge for yourselves...
[Acts] [4]:[20] But we can’t stop talking about the things that we’ve actually seen and heard!’
[Acts] [4]:[21] So then, after they threatened them a little more, they let them go, because they couldn’t find any reason to punish them. [Of course, they also chose not to do anything] on account of the people, since they were all praising God over what had happened…
[Acts] [4]:[22] For the man who was healed was more than 40 years old.
[Acts] [4]:[23] Well, after they’d been released, [Peter and John] returned to their [brothers] and reported what the Chief Priests and elders had told them.
[Acts] [4]:[24] And on hearing this, they all raised their voices to God together and said: ‘O our only King… You who made the lands, the skies, the seas, and everything in them...
[Acts] [4]:[25] Through Your breath, You had asked through the mouth of our father David (Your servant): ‘Why do the nations and all of the peoples Think about things that are worthless?
[Acts] [4]:[26] For, the rulers of their lands and their kings Are against [Jehovah] and His anointed.’ [Psalm 2:1-2]
[Acts] [4]:[27] ‘Even Herod and Pontius Pilate (these gentiles) have joined with the IsraElites in this city against Your Holy servant Jesus, whom You chose
[Acts] [4]:[28] to do all the things that Your hands and directions commanded.
[Acts] [4]:[29] ‘So, O [Jehovah], ‘Pay attention to their threats, and allow Your slaves to keep on speaking Your Word in full confidence,
[Acts] [4]:[30] while You stretch out Your hand to do healing and continue to bring signs and omens in the name of Your Holy Servant Jesus.’
[Acts] [4]:[31] Well, as they were asking God for this, the place where they were meeting started to shake! Then everyone was filled with the holy breath and they started speaking the word of God confidently.
[Acts] [4]:[32] As a result, a huge crowd became believers, and they started sharing everything that they had with a single heart and soul. None of them claimed that anything they owned was their own, for they shared everything…
[Acts] [4]:[33] And all the while, the Apostles continued to give a powerful testimony about the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. So a great manifestation of loving-kindness came over all of them.
[Acts] [4]:[34] In fact, nobody could be described as being needy among them, because everyone who owned fields or houses sold them and brought back the money from the things that they sold,
[Acts] [4]:[35] laying it at the feet of the Apostles. Then everything was distributed among them according to each one’s needs.
[Acts] [4]:[36] For example, JoSeph, whom the Apostles called BarNabas (which translates as Son of Comfort), a Levite and a native of Cyprus,
[Acts] [4]:[37] sold a piece of land that he owned and then he brought in the money, laying it at the feet of the Apostles.
[Acts] [5]:[1] However, a man named AnaNias (along with his wife SapPhira) also sold some property that they owned,
[Acts] [5]:[2] but he secretly kept part of the money… And his wife knew about this. Then he brought in part of it and laid it at the feet of the Apostles.
[Acts] [5]:[3] But Peter asked: ‘AnaNias, ‘Why has the Opposer made you so bold as to try to fool the Holy breath and to secretly hold back some of the money for the field?
[Acts] [5]:[4] ‘As long you owned it, it was yours. And after you sold it, wasn’t the money still yours? So, why did you plan to do such a thing in your heart? ‘You should understand that you weren’t lying to men, but to God!’
[Acts] [5]:[5] Well, just as he heard those words, AnaNias fell to the ground and died – which really frightened everyone who heard about it!
[Acts] [5]:[6] Then some of the younger men got up and wrapped him in a cloth, and they carried him outside to be buried.
[Acts] [5]:[7] It was about three hours later that his wife arrived… And she didn’t know what had happened.
[Acts] [5]:[8] So Peter asked her: ‘Tell me, did you sell the field for such-and-such amount?’ And she answered: ‘Yes, for such-and-such.’
[Acts] [5]:[9] Then Peter said: ‘Why did you two agree to test the spirit of [Jehovah]? ‘Look! The feet of those who buried your husband are at the door, and they’ll carry you out also.’
[Acts] [5]:[10] And at that, she instantly dropped dead at his feet! So when the young men returned, they also found her dead and they carried her out to be buried next to her husband.
[Acts] [5]:[11] Well, when the whole gathering (and everyone else) heard about this, they were all frightened by the things that were happening.
[Acts] [5]:[12] Yet thereafter, many signs and omens continued to be performed among the people at the hands of the Apostles, who used to meet among the Columns of Solomon.
[Acts] [5]:[13] It’s true that nobody else had enough courage to join them there, but the people continued to speak well of them,
[Acts] [5]:[14] and large numbers of men and women kept on being added to those who believed in the Lord.
[Acts] [5]:[15] [So after that], people started bringing their sick out into the main streets lying on little beds and cots, so that when Peter passed by, his shadow could fall on some of them.
[Acts] [5]:[16] Also, throngs from the cities around JeruSalem kept coming, carrying sick people and those who were bothered by unclean spirits… And everyone was cured!
[Acts] [5]:[17] However, the High Priest and everyone with him (particularly the members of the SadDucees’ sect) became very jealous of this.
[Acts] [5]:[18] So they attacked the Apostles and arrested them, then they locked them up in a public jail.
[Acts] [5]:[19] But during the night, [Jehovah’s] messenger opened the doors of the jail and brought them out, saying:
[Acts] [5]:[20] ‘Now go! Keep on standing in the Temple and telling the people everything about The Life.’
[Acts] [5]:[21] So after they were told this, they went back to the Temple at daybreak and started teaching again. Then when the High Priest and those who were with him finally arrived, they assembled the Jewish High Court, along with all the elders of the sons of IsraEl, and they sent [officers] to the jail to have [the Apostles] brought in.
[Acts] [5]:[22] But when the officers got there, they couldn’t find them in the lockup! So they reported back,
[Acts] [5]:[23] saying: ‘We found the jail locked and guards posted at the doors. But when we went in, we couldn’t find anyone inside!’
[Acts] [5]:[24] Well when the Temple captain and the Chief Priests were told this, they were confused and they wondered what had really happened.
[Acts] [5]:[25] But then someone came and reported: ‘Look! The men you put in jail are standing in the Temple teaching the people!’
[Acts] [5]:[26] So the captain took his officers and brought them back peacefully (because they were afraid of being stoned by the people).
[Acts] [5]:[27] Then they led them in and stood them in the Jewish High Court hall, where the High Priest questioned them and said:
[Acts] [5]:[28] ‘Although we ordered you not to teach about this name, {Look!} you’ve filled JeruSalem with your teachings, and you’re determined to bring the blood of this man down upon us!’
[Acts] [5]:[29] However, Peter and the rest of the Apostles replied: ‘We must obey God as ruler rather than men!
[Acts] [5]:[30] ‘For it was the God of our fathers who raised this Jesus, whom you arrested and had hung on a tree.
[Acts] [5]:[31] And after that, God raised him to His right hand to serve as the Primary Leader and Savior in order to cause IsraEl to repent so that He could forgive their sins!
[Acts] [5]:[32] ‘We’re witnesses to these things, as is the Holy breath which God gave to those who are obeying Him as their ruler.’
[Acts] [5]:[33] Well, when [the leaders] heard this, they were really cut to heart and they wanted to murder [the Apostles]!
[Acts] [5]:[34] But then a certain man stood up in the Jewish High Court hall (a Pharisee named GamaliEl, who was a highly-regarded teacher of the Law) and he commanded that the men be taken outside for a little while.
[Acts] [5]:[35] Then he said: ‘Men of IsraEl, ‘Be very careful about what you plan to do to these men.
[Acts] [5]:[36] ‘Do you remember when TheuDas came along saying that he was somebody important, and quite a few people (about 400 of them) followed him? But then he was done away with, and all those who listened to him were scattered and came to nothing.
[Acts] [5]:[37] ‘And after him, Judas the Galilean arose during the registration, and he drew people after him. But then he died, and all those who listened to him were scattered.
[Acts] [5]:[38] ‘So in this situation, I tell you not to mess with these men… Leave them alone! Because, if this thing that they’re doing is from men, it’ll be overthrown.
[Acts] [5]:[39] But if it’s from God, you won’t be able to overthrow them and you’ll actually be fighting against God!’
[Acts] [5]:[40] Well [after he said that], they all agreed with him. So then they called the Apostles back in and had them whipped, and they ordered them to stop talking about the name of Jesus… And then they released them.
[Acts] [5]:[41] But as they were leaving the Jewish High Court, [the Apostles] were actually rejoicing because they’d been found worthy of being dishonored for [Jesus’] name!
[Acts] [5]:[42] So they didn’t stop after that… They kept on teaching and announcing the good news about Jesus the Anointed One every day, both in the Temple and in [private] homes.
[Acts] [6]:[1] Now, back in those days when the disciples were increasing, the Greek-speaking Jews started grumbling about the Hebrew-speaking Jews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.
[Acts] [6]:[2] As a result, the 12 called all the disciples to them and said: ‘The thought of our having to abandon the word of God to serve tables is displeasing to us.
[Acts] [6]:[3] ‘So brothers, find seven qualified males among you who are filled with wisdom and the breath [of God], and we’ll appoint them to handle these needs,
[Acts] [6]:[4] so we can continue in our prayers and in serving the word.’
[Acts] [6]:[5] Well, what they suggested sounded good to the whole group, so they selected Stephen (a man who was filled with faith and holy breath), as well as Philip, ProChorus, NiCanor, Timon, ParMenas, and NicoLaus (a proselyte from AntiOch).
[Acts] [6]:[6] Then they took them before the Apostles, who prayed over them and laid their hands on them.
[Acts] [6]:[7] Thereafter, the word of God kept spreading and the number of disciples in JeruSalem kept on multiplying. For even a large number of Priests started obeying the faith!
[Acts] [6]:[8] Stephen was especially filled with joy and power, and he was performing great omens and signs among the people.
[Acts] [6]:[9] But then certain men came from the so-called Synagogue of Freed Men (along with some Cyrenians, Alexandrians, Kilikians, and [people from the province of] Asia) and started arguing with him.
[Acts] [6]:[10] Well, because their arguments couldn’t stand up against the wisdom and breath [of God] that he was speaking with,
[Acts] [6]:[11] they persuaded some men to say that they’d heard him say blasphemous things against Moses and God,
[Acts] [6]:[12] which riled up the people. So, some of the elders and scribes came and arrested him, then they dragged him up before the Jewish High Court,
[Acts] [6]:[13] where they produced some false witnesses who said: ‘This man is speaking against this Holy Place and against the Law!
[Acts] [6]:[14] For we heard him say that Jesus the Nazarene will tear this place down and change the customs that were given to us by Moses!’
[Acts] [6]:[15] Then as everyone who was sitting in the Jewish High Court was looking at him, they saw his face become like that of a messenger [of God].
[Acts] [7]:[1] So the High Priest asked him: ‘Is all of this true?’
[Acts] [7]:[2] And [Stephen] said: ‘Men… Brothers… Fathers… Listen! ‘Our father AbraHam saw the Glorious God while he was in MesoPotamia, before he moved to Haran.
[Acts] [7]:[3] ‘And [God] said to him: ‘Leave your land and your relatives and go to the land that I’m going to show you.’ [Genesis 12:1]
[Acts] [7]:[4] ‘So he went to the land of the Chaldeans and started living in Haran. Then after his father died, [God] caused him to move to the land where you now live.
[Acts] [7]:[5] ‘However, He didn’t give him any land as his inheritance… Not a foot’s width! Yet [God] did promise him a land that he could own and pass on to his descendants, even though at the time when he didn’t have any children.
[Acts] [7]:[6] ‘Moreover, God spoke to him and told him that his descendants would also have to live in a foreign land where they’d be oppressed and serve as slaves for 400 years.
[Acts] [7]:[7] ‘And God said: ‘I will pass judgment on the nation they serve as slaves.’ [Genesis 15:14] ‘And then after that: '...they will come here and serve Me.’ Exodus 3:12]

[Acts] [20]:[28] ‘Therefore, you need to pay close attention to yourselves and to the whole flock over which the holy breath has appointed you overseers… Feed the Lord’s congregation, which he purchased with his own blood.
[Acts] [20]:[29] ‘For I know that after I leave, oppressive wolves will enter among you who won’t spare the flock,
[Acts] [20]:[30] and that men from among you will arise and speak twisted things to attract some of the disciples to following them!
[Acts] [20]:[31] ‘So you must stay awake… And keep those three years in mind during which I didn’t stop counseling each of you tearfully, both night and day.
[Acts] [20]:[32] ‘Now, I’m leaving you the loving care of our Lord who can build you up and give you an inheritance among all the Holy Ones.
[Acts] [20]:[33] ‘[You know that] I haven’t longed for anyone’s silver, gold, or clothing.
[Acts] [20]:[34] For you’re aware of how I’ve used my own hands to take care of my own needs and [for the needs] of those who were with me.
[Acts] [20]:[35] ‘I’ve demonstrated to you how important it is for us to work like this, so we can help those who are weak. Therefore, remember the words that were said by our Lord Jesus: ‘There’s more happiness in giving than there is in receiving.’
[Acts] [20]:[36] And after he said this, he kneeled down with them all and prayed.
[Acts] [20]:[37] Well, many tears flowed as they hugged Paul’s neck and tenderly kissed him.
[Acts] [20]:[38] For when he said that they wouldn’t see his face again, they were deeply saddened. And from there, they all accompanied him out to the ship.
[Acts] [21]:[1] Well, when we finally tore ourselves away from them and put out to sea, we ran straight over to Cos, then to Rhodes the next day, and from there to Patara.
[Acts] [21]:[2] And when we found a boat that was going to Phoenicia, we went aboard and sailed off.
[Acts] [21]:[3] From there we came in sight of the Island of Cyprus, passing it on our left, and we sailed on to Syria, landing at Tyre (because that’s where the boat was to unload its cargo).
[Acts] [21]:[4] And while we were there, we searched for and found the disciples, and we stayed with them for seven days. However, by the breath [of God], they repeatedly warned Paul not to set foot in JeruSalem.
[Acts] [21]:[5] [Then a week later], we got ready to continue our journey, and everyone (including the women and children) followed us outside of the city. And after kneeling down on the beach, we had a prayer
[Acts] [21]:[6] before saying goodbye to each other. Then we boarded the ship, as they returned to their homes.
[Acts] [21]:[7] Well, after we left Tyre, we finally arrived at Ptolemais, where we greeted the brothers and spent the day with them.
[Acts] [21]:[8] Then on the next day, we traveled to Caesarea, where we went to the house of Philip the Evangelizer (one of the seven men), and stayed with him.
[Acts] [21]:[9] This man had four virgin daughters who all prophesied.
[Acts] [21]:[10] But after we’d stayed there for several days, a Prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
[Acts] [21]:[11] He walked right up to us and removed Paul’s sash, then he used it to tie up his own hands and feet, and said: ‘This is what the holy breath has declared: ‘The Judeans will bind the man who owns this sash and then hand him over to the gentiles.’
[Acts] [21]:[12] Well when we heard this, we all (everyone there) started begging [Paul] not to go to JeruSalem.
[Acts] [21]:[13] But Paul replied: ‘Why are you crying and crushing my heart? I’m not only ready to be bound, but also to die in JeruSalem for the name of our Lord Jesus!’
[Acts] [21]:[14] And when we couldn’t change his mind, we gave in, saying: ‘May [God’s] Will be done.’
[Acts] [21]:[15] So after several days, we prepared for the journey and headed towards JeruSalem.
[Acts] [21]:[16] Meanwhile, some of the disciples from Caesarea traveled with us and led us to the home of a man who showed us some hospitality… Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple.
[Acts] [21]:[17] Well, when we arrived in JeruSalem, the brothers were all happy to see us.
[Acts] [21]:[18] And the next [day], we went with Paul to see James and the rest of the elders.
[Acts] [21]:[19] So [Paul] greeted them and started giving a detailed account of the things that God had done among the nations through his ministry.
[Acts] [21]:[20] And after hearing about it, they glorified God. Then they said to him: ‘Our brother, ‘You know how many thousands of believers there are among the Jews, and they all zealously obey the Law.
[Acts] [21]:[21] But they’ve heard the rumor that you’re teaching Jews who live among the nations an apostasy from Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children or to follow our traditions.
[Acts] [21]:[22] ‘So, what do you suppose we can do about this? ‘Since they’re going to hear that you’ve arrived,
[Acts] [21]:[23] this is what we’re telling you to do: ‘We have four men who have taken a sacred vow…
[Acts] [21]:[24] Take them with you, and all of you should cleanse yourselves ceremonially, then pay to have your heads shaved. That way, everyone will know that there’s no truth to the rumors we’ve heard about you, and that you’re personally following the rules and obeying the Law.
[Acts] [21]:[25] ‘As for the gentiles who have become believers... We’ve already sent them our decision to stay free from things that are sacrificed to idols, from blood, from whatever is strangled, and from sexual immorality.’
[Acts] [21]:[26] So the next day, Paul took the [four] men along and they cleansed themselves ceremonially. Then they entered the Temple to give their notice of their ceremonial cleansing (to start counting the days until an offering should be made for each of them).
[Acts] [21]:[27] But when the seven days were about up, some Judeans from [the province of] Asia saw him in the Temple and started a riot among the crowd… They grabbed him,
[Acts] [21]:[28] shouting: ‘Men of IsraEl! Help! ‘This is the man who is teaching against our people, against the Law, and this place... To everyone, everywhere! ‘He’s even defiled this Holy Place by bringing Greeks into the Temple!’
[Acts] [21]:[29] ([They said this], because they’d seen him in the city earlier with Trophimus the Ephesian, and they [mistakenly] thought that Paul had also brought him into the Temple).
[Acts] [21]:[30] Well, the whole city was in an uproar, and many people started running there. So they grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the Temple, then they closed the [Temple] doors
[Acts] [21]:[31] and tried to kill him! But when the commander of the [Roman] garrison heard the uproar there in JeruSalem,
[Acts] [21]:[32] he immediately took a contingent of officers and soldiers, and ran down to them. So when [the mob] saw the commander coming with his soldiers, they stopped beating up Paul.
[Acts] [21]:[33] However, the commander then arrested [Paul] and ordered him to be bound with two chains. Thereafter, he asked [the mob] who he was and what he’d done.
[Acts] [21]:[34] However, some in the crowd started shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. So because he couldn’t be sure of anything (due to all the confusion), he commanded [that Paul] should be taken back to their garrison.
[Acts] [21]:[35] Well, when they reached the [garrison] stairs, the situation got even worse. For the mob became so violent that the soldiers had to literally carry [Paul] along
[Acts] [21]:[36] while the people followed them shouting: ‘Take him away!’
[Acts] [21]:[37] Then, as he was being carried into the garrison, Paul asked the commander: ‘Am I allowed to say something to you?’ And he replied: ‘Can you speak Greek?
[Acts] [21]:[38] ‘Aren’t you the Egyptian who started a rebellion and led 4,000 dagger men into the desert some time ago?’
[Acts] [21]:[39] But Paul said: ‘No... I’m really a Jew from Tarsus in Kilikia – I’m a citizen of a well-known city. So I beg you, allow me to speak to the people!’
[Acts] [21]:[40] Well at that, he gave Paul permission. So [Paul] stood on the stairs and waved his arms [to quiet] the crowd. And when everything quieted down, he spoke to them in Hebrew, saying:
[Acts] [22]:[1] ‘Men, brothers, and fathers! ‘Allow me to say something in my own defense now.’
[Acts] [22]:[2] Well when they heard him addressing them in Hebrew [possibly meaning the common the language of the Hebrews, which was Aramaic], things did get quieter. And he said:
[Acts] [22]:[3] ‘I’m a Jew who was born in Tarsus of Kilikia. I went to school right here in this city, and I received my instruction at the feet of GamaliEl, who taught me to obey the Law of our fathers strictly and to show the same zeal for God that you’re showing today.
[Acts] [22]:[4] ‘I personally persecuted this ‘Way,’ by arresting and delivering their men and women to prisons for execution.
[Acts] [22]:[5] ‘The High Priest and the entire assembly of elders can corroborate this, because I obtained letters from them to our brothers in Damascus, where I went to bring everybody they had in prison back to JeruSalem for punishment.
[Acts] [22]:[6] ‘But as I was on my way and getting close to Damascus, at about noon, a bright light in the sky flashed all around me!
[Acts] [22]:[7] ‘Then I fell to the ground and I heard a voice say to me: ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’
[Acts] [22]:[8] ‘So I asked: ‘Who are you, Lord?’ ‘And he replied: ‘I’m Jesus the Nazarene, the one you’re persecuting!’
[Acts] [22]:[9] ‘Well, the men who were with me also saw the light, but they didn’t hear the voice of the person speaking to me.
[Acts] [22]:[10] ‘Then I asked: ‘What must I do, Lord?’ ‘And the Lord said to me: ‘Get up and go to Damascus. There you’ll be told all about what you’ve been assigned to do.’
[Acts] [22]:[11] ‘However, since I couldn’t see anymore because of the brilliance of that light, those who were [traveling] with me had to lead me into Damascus by the hand.
[Acts] [22]:[12] ‘Now, AnaNias (a man who devoutly obeyed the Law and that was well spoken of by all the Judeans that live there)
[Acts] [22]:[13] came and stood next to me. ‘Then he said: ‘Saul… Brother… See again!’ ‘And I could immediately see him!
[Acts] [22]:[14] ‘Then he said: ‘The God of our fathers has selected you to learn about His Will, to see the Righteous One, and to hear the voice from his mouth,
[Acts] [22]:[15] because you are to be his witness to everything that you’ve seen and heard.
[Acts] [22]:[16] ‘So now, why are you wasting time? Get up, get immersed [in water], and ‘wash your sins away’ by calling on his name!’
[Acts] [22]:[17] ‘Then after I got back to JeruSalem... And while I was praying in the Temple, I fell into a trance where I saw [Jesus]!
[Acts] [22]:[18] ‘And he said to me: ‘Hurry! You must leave JeruSalem right away, because the [people here] don’t want to listen to your testimony about me!’
[Acts] [22]:[19] ‘But I said: ‘Lord, they all know very well that in one synagogue after another I once had everyone who believes in you arrested and whipped!
[Acts] [22]:[20] ‘And when the blood of your witness Stephen was being spilled, I stood there and approved of it… In fact, I guarded the robes of those who killed him!’
[Acts] [22]:[21] ‘Well at that, he just told me: ‘Leave, because I’m sending you to far-away nations.’
[Acts] [22]:[22] Now, they had been listening to him until he said that, but then they started shouting: ‘Kill this man, for he isn’t fit to live!’
[Acts] [22]:[23] And because they were shouting, throwing their clothes around and tossing dirt in the air,
[Acts] [22]:[24] the commander ordered that Paul should be taken inside their garrison. There he gave orders to scourge him with a whip so as to force him to explain why everyone was shouting about him that way.
[Acts] [22]:[25] But when they stretched him out to be whipped, Paul asked the centurion who was standing there: ‘Is it legal for you to whip a man who is a Roman and hasn’t been charged with a crime?’
[Acts] [22]:[26] Well when the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and said: ‘Just look at what you were about to do! This man is a Roman!’
[Acts] [22]:[27] So the commander came to [Paul] and asked: ‘Tell me, are you a Roman?’ And he answered: ‘Yes.’
[Acts] [22]:[28] Then the commander said: ‘I paid a lot to obtain my citizenship.’ And Paul said: ‘Well, I was born [a citizen]!’
[Acts] [22]:[29] Well at that, the men who were about to torture him left immediately. And on learning that he’d arrested a Roman [citizen], the military commander was frightened.
[Acts] [22]:[30] So the next day, because he wanted to know for sure just what the Jews were accusing him of, he [unshackled] him and commanded the Chief Priests and the entire Jewish Court to assemble. Then he brought Paul down and stood him before them.
[Acts] [23]:[1] Well, Paul just glared at the [judges of the] Jewish Court, and said: ‘Men… Brothers… I have a perfectly clear conscience about the way I behave before God down to this day.’
[Acts] [23]:[2] And at that, the High Priest AnaNias ordered those who were standing by him to hit him in the mouth.
[Acts] [23]:[3] So Paul said: ‘God is going to hit you – you whitewashed wall! ‘Do you sit there judging me by the Law, and at the same time break the Law by telling them to hit me?’
[Acts] [23]:[4] Then those who were standing by him asked: ‘Are you speaking against the High Priest of God?’
[Acts] [23]:[5] And Paul answered: ‘Brothers, I didn’t know he was the High Priest. For it’s written: ‘You must not speak badly of the one who rules your people.’ [Exodus 22:28]
[Acts] [23]:[6] Then when Paul noticed that part of the group were SadDucees and the rest were Pharisees, he called out in the High Court: ‘Men… Brothers… It’s because I’m a Pharisee, and the son of a Pharisee, that I’m being judged over my hope in the resurrection of the dead!’
[Acts] [23]:[7] And after he said this, quite an argument broke out between the Pharisees and SadDucees, which divided the crowd,
[Acts] [23]:[8] since the SadDucees say that there’s no such thing as a resurrection, or [divine] messengers, or the breath [of God] – yet the Pharisees publicly preach all such things.
[Acts] [23]:[9] So there was lots of shouting, and some of the Pharisees’ scribes stood up and started heatedly arguing, saying: ‘We don’t find anything wrong with this man! ‘For if the breath [of God] or [one of His] messengers spoke to him, [what of it?]’ [spurious words, copied from Acts 5:39]
[Acts] [23]:[10] Well, the argument became so heated that the commander feared that they’d pull Paul to pieces! So he ordered the soldiers to go down and take him from their midst and bring him back to their garrison.
[Acts] [23]:[11] Then on the following night, the Lord stood next to [Paul] and said: ‘Be strong! ‘So far, you’ve thoroughly testified to things about me in JeruSalem… But now you must also testify about me in Rome!’
[Acts] [23]:[12] Well the next morning, the Judeans formed an alliance – they all swore with a curse that they wouldn’t eat or drink until after they’d killed Paul
[Acts] [23]:[13] (there were more than 40 men who formed this oath-bound conspiracy).
[Acts] [23]:[14] So they went to the Chief Priests and elders and said: ‘We’ve taken a solemn oath with a curse not to take a bite of food until after we’ve killed Paul!
[Acts] [23]:[15] ‘Therefore, we want you and the High Court to explain to the military commander that he should bring [Paul] to you so you can learn more about the charges against him… And we’ll be ready to kill him before he gets there!’
[Acts] [23]:[16] However, Paul’s nephew heard that they’d be waiting for him, so he went to the garrison and reported it to Paul.
[Acts] [23]:[17] Then Paul called one of the centurions and said: ‘Take this young man to the commander, because he’s got something to report.’
[Acts] [23]:[18] So [the soldier] took [Paul’s nephew] to the commander and told him: ‘The prisoner Paul called me and asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.’
[Acts] [23]:[19] Well, the commander took him by the hand and led him in, then he asked him privately: ‘What do you want to report to me?’
[Acts] [23]:[20] And he answered: ‘The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish Court tomorrow, pretending to want to learn more about the charges against him.
[Acts] [23]:[21] ‘But whatever you do, don’t let them convince you to do this, because they have more than 40 men waiting to ambush him. These men have sworn an oath with a curse not to eat or drink anything until after they’ve killed him. And now they’re ready, expecting you to promise [to do this for them].’
[Acts] [23]:[22] So at that, the commander sent the young man away, giving him the order: ‘Don’t tell anyone that you’ve explained this to me.’
[Acts] [23]:[23] Then he called in two of his centurions and said: ‘I want you to get 200 soldiers ready, plus 70 cavalrymen and 200 spearmen… Have them prepared to march all the way to Caesarea at the third hour of the night [3am in the Roman system, 9pm in the Jewish].
[Acts] [23]:[24] Also, provide an animal for Paul to ride, for I want you to carry him safely to Governor Felix.’
[Acts] [23]:[25] Then he wrote a letter [to Felix] that read like this:
[Acts] [23]:[26] ‘Claudius Lysias to the mighty Governor Felix: ‘Rejoice!
[Acts] [23]:[27] ‘This man was seized by the Jews and they were about to kill him. However, I came there quickly with a contingent of soldiers and rescued him, because I learned that he was a Roman.
[Acts] [23]:[28] ‘And because I wanted to know their accusation against him, I had him taken down to their High Court.
[Acts] [23]:[29] There I found that they were just accusing him over questions that have to do with their Law… But he hadn’t been charged with anything that deserves death or being sent to jail.
[Acts] [23]:[30] ‘However, because I learned of a plot against this man, I’m sending him to you right away, and I’m ordering his accusers to speak against him before you.’
[Acts] [23]:[31] So these soldiers followed their orders and they took Paul to AntiPatris that night.
[Acts] [23]:[32] Then the next day, they sent him on with the cavalry (which later returned to the garrison).
[Acts] [23]:[33] And when they got to Caesarea, they delivered the letter to the governor along with Paul.
[Acts] [23]:[34] Well, after he read the letter, [Felix] asked [Paul] which province he was from. And when he heard that he was from Kilikia, he said:
[Acts] [23]:[35] ‘I’ll give you a thorough hearing after your accusers get here.’ So thereafter, he gave orders that [Paul] should be kept under guard in the Praetorian Palace of Herod.
[Acts] [24]:[1] Well five days later, High Priest AnaNias arrived with some elders and an orator named Tertullus, and they explained their accusations against Paul to the governor.
[Acts] [24]:[2] Then when he was called forward, Tertullus said this: ‘You’ve brought about so much peace, and we welcome the well-thought-out reforms that you’ve brought to our nation
[Acts] [24]:[3] in every way and everywhere with the greatest thankfulness, O mighty Felix.
[Acts] [24]:[4] ‘But, so that I don’t waste any of your time, I beg you to hear us briefly, in your kindness...
[Acts] [24]:[5] ‘We found this man –this plague– stirring up rebellions among the Judeans throughout the whole inhabited earth, for he’s the leader of the sect of the Nazarenes.
[Acts] [24]:[6] And when he tried to profane our Temple, we arrested him.
[Acts] [24]:[8] [spurious words] You can examine him yourself to learn more about all these things that we’re saying against him.’
[Acts] [24]:[9] And at that, the Judeans also joined in the attack, affirming that the things [Tertullus] was saying were true.
[Acts] [24]:[10] Thereafter, the governor nodded for Paul to speak. And Paul said: ‘I know very well that you’ve been the judge of our nation for many years. ‘So I’m happy to speak in my own defense about these things that I’ve been accused of,
[Acts] [24]:[11] since you’re in a good position to understand them. ‘It hasn’t been more than 12 days since I went to worship in JeruSalem,
[Acts] [24]:[12] and they didn’t find me in the Temple arguing with anyone, nor did they find me inciting a riot in the synagogues… Or anywhere else in the city for that matter!
[Acts] [24]:[13] ‘So right now, they can’t prove any of the things they’re accusing me of before you.
[Acts] [24]:[14] ‘But I do admit to this: ‘That which they’re calling a sect, is nothing more than the way that I’ve always worshipped the God of my fathers. ‘For I believe everything that’s written in the Law and in the Prophets,
[Acts] [24]:[15] and I have this hope in God – which they also accept – that there’s going to be a resurrection of the righteous and the unrighteous.
[Acts] [24]:[16] ‘This is why I’m constantly on the alert so that I don’t offend my conscience by doing anything against God or men.
[Acts] [24]:[17] And this is also why, after [being gone for] several years, I returned [to JeruSalem]… To bring gifts to the poor in my nation and to present my offerings [before God].
[Acts] [24]:[18] ‘But it was while I was doing this that they found me in the Temple – ceremonially cleansed, by the way – and I wasn’t there with a mob, nor did I start a riot! ‘Actually, some Jews from the [province of] Asia
[Acts] [24]:[19] should be here before you to accuse me… That is, if they could actually find anything against me.
[Acts] [24]:[20] ‘Just ask these who are here to tell you what bad things they found me doing as I stood before their High Court…
[Acts] [24]:[21] There was only what I shouted while I was standing among them, when I said: ‘I’m being judged before you today over the resurrection of the dead!’
[Acts] [24]:[22] Well, although Felix knew a lot about things that have to do with the ‘Way,’ he just put them all off, saying: ‘When Commander Lysias gets here, I’ll make a decision on this matter that you’re so concerned about.’
[Acts] [24]:[23] And thereafter, [Felix] ordered the centurion not to kill [Paul], but to allow him some liberty, and not to prevent his people from serving his needs.
[Acts] [24]:[24] It was several days later that Felix arrived with his woman Drousille. And since she was a Jew, he sent for Paul and they listened to him talk about his belief in the Anointed Jesus.
[Acts] [24]:[25] However, Felix became frightened when Paul started talking about righteousness, self-control, and the coming judgment! So he said: ‘That’s enough for now! ‘Go on back, and when I have more time, I’ll send for you again.’
[Acts] [24]:[26] However, he was actually hoping that Paul would try to bribe him... So, he sent for him and talked to him frequently!
[Acts] [24]:[27] Well after two years, Felix was succeeded by Porcius Festus. And because Felix wanted to be liked by the Jews, he also kept Paul locked up.
[Acts] [25]:[1] It was just three days after Festus had been appointed the provincial governor that he traveled from Caesarea to JeruSalem –
[Acts] [25]:[2] and there the Chief Priests and Judean leaders talked to him about Paul.
[Acts] [25]:[3] They begged him (asking it as a favor) to send [Paul] to JeruSalem… Since they planned to ambush and kill him along the road.
[Acts] [25]:[4] However, Festus replied that he would just keep Paul in Caesarea. But, because he would be leaving [JeruSalem] shortly, he said to them:
[Acts] [25]:[5] ‘Those of you who have been empowered to do so should come back with me, and if he’s committed some crime, you can make your accusations against him there.’
[Acts] [25]:[6] Well, after he’d spent about 8 to 10 days [in JeruSalem], Festus returned to Caesarea. And the next day, he sat on the Judgment Seat and ordered to have Paul brought in.
[Acts] [25]:[7] And when [Paul] arrived, the Jews that had come from JeruSalem stood all around him and charged him with several serious offenses… However, they couldn’t prove anything.
[Acts] [25]:[8] Then Paul stood up and spoke in his own defense, saying: ‘I haven’t committed any sins against the Law of the Jews, against the Temple, or against Caesar!’
[Acts] [25]:[9] However, Festus (in an attempt to gain favor with the Jews) asked Paul: ‘Do you want to go back to JeruSalem and be judged over these things before me there?’
[Acts] [25]:[10] But Paul said: ‘I’m standing before the Judgment Seat of Caesar, and this is where I ought to be judged! ‘I’ve done nothing wrong to the Judeans, as you’re finding out for yourself.
[Acts] [25]:[11] ‘However, if I’m really a criminal and have done something that I should die for, I’m not begging off from dying. ‘On the other hand, if nothing they’re accusing me of is true, then nobody can just hand me over to them as a favor! ‘Therefore, I appeal to Caesar!’
[Acts] [25]:[12] Well after discussing it with his counselors, Festus replied: ‘You have appealed to Caesar, so to Caesar you’ll go!’
[Acts] [25]:[13] Then after several days had passed, Agrippa (the king) and Bernice [the king’s sister] arrived in Caesarea to pay a courtesy visit on Festus.
[Acts] [25]:[14] So, since they were to spend several days there, Festus laid the matter of Paul before the king, saying: ‘There’s a man here who was left as a prisoner by Felix.
[Acts] [25]:[15] ‘When I was in JeruSalem, the Chief Priests and Judean elders brought me some information about him and asked me to condemn him to death.
[Acts] [25]:[16] ‘But I told them that it isn’t the Roman way to just hand a man over as a favor before he meets his accusers face-to-face and gets a chance to speak in his own defense.
[Acts] [25]:[17] ‘So when they got here, I didn’t delay the matter… The next day I sat down on the Judgment Seat and ordered the man to be brought in.
[Acts] [25]:[18] And when they came [before me], his accusers didn’t really produce any serious charges as I thought they would...
[Acts] [25]:[19] They simply complained about some dispute that they had with him over questions about their religion and about some ‘Jesus’ who was dead, but whom Paul kept claiming was alive!
[Acts] [25]:[20] ‘Well, I became so confused over the matter that I finally asked if he’d like to go to JeruSalem to be judged there over these matters.
[Acts] [25]:[21] But then Paul appealed to be bound over for a decision by the August One, so I ordered him to be held until I can send him to Caesar.’
[Acts] [25]:[22] So Agrippa told Festus: ‘I’d also like to hear from this man.’ And he said: ‘You’ll hear him tomorrow!’
[Acts] [25]:[23] Then the next day, Agrippa and Bernice arrived with a lot of pomp and ceremony and went into the hearing room along with some military commanders and prominent men from the city. And when Festus gave the command, Paul was brought in.
[Acts] [25]:[24] So Festus said: ‘O King Agrippa, and all who are here with us, ‘Now you can see this man about whom all the Judeans both here and in JeruSalem are shouting that he shouldn’t be allowed to live any longer.
[Acts] [25]:[25] ‘However, I haven’t found anything that he’s done to deserve death; so when he appealed to the August One, I decided to send him there…
[Acts] [25]:[26] But I really don’t have anything to write to [my] lord about. ‘Therefore, I brought him here before you… And especially before you, King Agrippa, so that you can examine him and judge something that I can write to him about.
[Acts] [25]:[27] ‘For it seems unreasonable to send a prisoner [to Rome] and not be able to specify the charges against him.’
[Acts] [26]:[1] So at that, Agrippa said to Paul: ‘You may now speak on your own behalf.’ Well, Paul stretched his hands out and said this in his defense:
[Acts] [26]:[2] ‘King Agrippa, ‘I’m happy to be here so as to defend myself before you today over all these things that I’ve been accused of by the Jews,

[Acts] [27]:[1] Well, since it had been decided that we had to sail away to Italy, they handed Paul (along with some other prisoners) over to a centurion named Julius, who was [a soldier] of the Augustus Division.
[Acts] [27]:[2] So we boarded a ship along with AristArchus (a Macedonian from ThesSalonica). Now, the ship had come from AdraMyttium, and it was sailing to places along the coast of the [province of] Asia.
[Acts] [27]:[3] So the next day, when we landed at Sidon, Julius treated Paul very kindly by allowing him to visit friends that cared for his needs.
[Acts] [27]:[4] From there we sailed around Cyprus, because the winds were against us.
[Acts] [27]:[5] Then we got into the open sea [south of] Kilikia and PamPhylia, and we put into port at Myra in Lukias.

[Acts] [27]:[7] Then, after sailing slowly (and with a lot of difficulty) for several days, we stopped at Knidos. And because the winds wouldn’t let us go on, we sailed [south of] Salmone, Crete.
[Acts] [27]:[8] Then following the coastline carefully, we came to a place called Fair Havens, near the city of Lasea.
[Acts] [27]:[9] Well, since we’d lost so much time (it was already past [Yom Kippur]) and the sea was hazardous to navigate, Paul made a recommendation.
[Acts] [27]:[10] He said: ‘Men, I see that any further navigation is going to result in damage and huge losses not only to the cargo and ship, but to our lives!’
[Acts] [27]:[11] However, the army officer preferred to listened to the pilot and the ship’s owner, rather than to what Paul was saying.
[Acts] [27]:[12] Now, since this harbor was a poor place to winter, the majority recommended that they set sail and go on, in an attempt to make it to Phoenix, where they could spend the winter (a harbor in Crete that has openings to the northeast and southeast).
[Acts] [27]:[13] Well, when the south wind started blowing gently, they thought that this would meet their needs... So they weighed anchor and coasted along the shore next to Crete.
[Acts] [27]:[14] But after a little while, a typhoon wind they call the Euro Clydon bore down on us!
[Acts] [27]:[15] And because the ship was being tossed so violently that it couldn’t maintain its heading, we just gave up and [allowed ourselves to be] carried along by the wind.
[Acts] [27]:[16] Then when we passed south of a small island called Cauda, we used all our strength to get hold of the rowboat that was tied at the rear of the ship.
[Acts] [27]:[17] And after we hoisted it aboard, they started wrapping the ship with [ropes and chains]. Also, since they were afraid of running aground on the shoals, they lowered the masts and we were just carried along.
[Acts] [27]:[18] Then on the next day (because we were still being violently tossed by the storm), they started to lighten the ship.
[Acts] [27]:[19] And by the third [day], they’d tossed all of the boat’s furnishings overboard with their own hands!
[Acts] [27]:[20] Now, since we hadn’t seen the sun or stars for several days and a storm was still over us, we’d lost any hope of being saved…
[Acts] [27]:[21] And considerable time had elapsed since anyone had been able to eat. But then Paul stood up in the midst of them and said: ‘Men, you certainly should have taken my advice and not put out to sea from Crete, just to suffer this kind of damage and loss.
[Acts] [27]:[22] But now I’m telling you to be happy, because not a single life will be lost… Although the ship will [be lost]...
[Acts] [27]:[23] Because a messenger from the God whom I serve and belong to, came to me this evening and said:
[Acts] [27]:[24] ‘Don’t be afraid, Paul. You’ll stand before Caesar. ‘And {Look!} God has favored you by also giving you [the lives of] those who are sailing with you.’
[Acts] [27]:[25] ‘So be happy, men! Because, I believe that God will do exactly as He told me!
[Acts] [27]:[26] However, we’ll be cast ashore on an island.’
[Acts] [27]:[27] Well thereafter (on the evening starting the 14th day), as we were being carried along in the Adriatic Sea (at about midnight), the sailors thought that we might be getting close to land...
[Acts] [27]:[28] So they did a depth sounding and found it at 120 feet (37m). Then after we’d traveled on a little farther, they took another depth sounding, and this time it was 91 feet (27.8m).
[Acts] [27]:[29] So, because they were afraid that we might soon run aground on the rocks, they threw out four anchors at the stern and we waited for daylight.

[Romans] [3]:[29] [Therefore, do you think that our God is] only the God of the Jews? And that He’s not also [the God of] the gentiles? [Yes, He’s the God] of the gentiles also!

[Romans] [3]:[31] Then, can we say that our faith overrides the Law? Never may that happen! Rather, [our faith] makes the Law stronger!
[Romans] [4]:[1] For example: Consider our fleshly ancestor AbraHam.

[Romans] [4]:[17] Just as it’s written: ‘I’ve appointed you to be the father of many nations.’ [Genesis 17:5] He’s our father, standing before The God in whom he believed… The One who makes the dead alive and calls the things that aren’t and makes them exist.
[Romans] [4]:[18] So although [AbraHam] really didn’t have any reason for hope, he started to believe that he’d become the father of many nations – for he was told: ‘They’ll be your offspring.’ [Genesis 15:5]
[Romans] [4]:[19] Even though his body was almost dead (since he was 100 years old), and the womb of SarAh was dead, this failed to weaken his faith –

[Romans] [4]:[21] For [AbraHam] was completely convinced that [God] could do whatever He promised.

[Romans] [4]:[25] For after he’d been offered up for our errors, he was then raised... All so we can be counted as righteous too!

[2 Corinthians] [13]:[11] Finally, brothers: Keep on rejoicing, growing to perfection, and being courageous. Also, be of the same mind and live peaceably, so that the God of love and peace will always be with you.

[Galatians] [1]:[24] So they ended up glorifying God because of me.

And while I was there, I explained to the prominent ones about how I’d been preaching to the gentiles… However I did this privately, for fear that somehow I’d been doing it all for nothing.
