[Ephesians] [1]:[1] Paul, an Apostle of the Anointed Jesus (by the will of God), to the Holy Ones in Ephesus… Those faithful ones in the Anointed Jesus:
[Ephesians] [1]:[2] May you receive loving care and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus the Anointed!
[Ephesians] [1]:[3] Yes, may the God and Father of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One be praised! For He’s blest us with every blessing of his breath in the heavens through the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [1]:[4] Also, He chose us to be in him – before the foundation of the age, so we could become holy and unblemished before Him in love.
[Ephesians] [1]:[5] For He’s pre-designated us to be adopted sons through Jesus the Anointed One, as it pleases His will,
[Ephesians] [1]:[6] in praise of the glory of the loving care that [is shown by] the one through whom He shows His favor upon us… This one whom He loves[, that is, Jesus].
[Ephesians] [1]:[7] It’s through this one, and his blood, that our ransom has been paid; and it’s through the richness of his loving care that our sins could be forgiven.
[Ephesians] [1]:[8] [Also, we’ve received] such an abundance of wisdom and good sense [through him].
[Ephesians] [1]:[9] For He’s allowed us to understand the mystery of His will, according to His pleasure. He decided [all] this within Himself
[Ephesians] [1]:[10] for [the purpose of arranging] an administration, at the appointed time, to renew everything both in heaven and earth via the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [1]:[11] So, it’s through [Jesus] that we’ve obtained the inheritance that was predetermined by [God’s] purpose for him… Yes, this one, through whom all things are accomplished according to [God’s] council and will!
[Ephesians] [1]:[12] So those who were the first to put faith in the Anointed One might give praise to his glory.
[Ephesians] [1]:[13] [For, he’s the one] through whom you heard the words of truth (the good news about your salvation), [the one] in whom you put faith, and [the one] who has sealed you with the promised holy breath...
[Ephesians] [1]:[14] Which is the guarantee that he inherited us through the ransom that he paid to purchase us for his glory and praise.
[Ephesians] [1]:[15] This is why, when I heard of your faith in the Lord Jesus (and of your love for all the Holy Ones),
[Ephesians] [1]:[16] I haven’t stopped giving thanks for you! Yes, I keep mentioning you in my prayers, and
[Ephesians] [1]:[17] asking the God of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One (the glorious Father) to give you the spirit of wisdom, and to reveal to you an accurate knowledge about Him,
[Ephesians] [1]:[18] so that the eyes of your hearts will be enlightened – and you can know the glorious richness of the hope that He’s called you for, and which He holds as an inheritance for the Holy Ones.
[Ephesians] [1]:[19] O how great His power is towards those of us who are believers – while it operates through the mightiness
[Ephesians] [1]:[20] that He demonstrated in the case of the Anointed One, when He raised him from the dead and seated him at His right hand in the heavens!
[Ephesians] [1]:[21] Yes, far above every government, authority, power, lordship, and above every name that’s been given... Not only in this age, but also in the one that’s coming,
[Ephesians] [1]:[22] when He’ll put everything under his feet, and make him the ‘head’ of everything to the called ones,
[Ephesians] [1]:[23] those who are his ‘body,’ his fullness, and his completeness.
[Ephesians] [2]:[1] For you have ‘died’ to the ways of sin and error –
[Ephesians] [2]:[2] in which you once walked (the ways of this world) when you used to follow the ruler of the power of the air… The spirit that now operates in the sons of disobedience,
[Ephesians] [2]:[3] which is the way we were all once headed as we followed our human desires and did whatever our bodies wanted. Yes, because of the cravings that we once had, we were like everyone else… The natural children of [God’s] wrath!
[Ephesians] [2]:[4] But due to the love that He has for us, God (who is so rich in mercy)
[Ephesians] [2]:[5] made us alive in the Anointed One while we were still ‘dead’ in our failings. So it’s by His loving kindness that we’ve been saved
[Ephesians] [2]:[6] and raised [to life] together, then seated together in the heavens in the Anointed Jesus,
[Ephesians] [2]:[7] so that, in ages to come, [God] can show the tremendous richness of His loving care by the kindness that He’s shown towards us through the Anointed Jesus.
[Ephesians] [2]:[8] Yes, it’s because of [His] loving care that you’ve been saved, through a faith that didn’t come from within yourselves, but as a gift from God!
[Ephesians] [2]:[9] No, it didn’t come from anything that you’ve done, so you could boast.
[Ephesians] [2]:[10] Instead, we’re His workmanship… We were created through the Anointed Jesus to do the good things that God previously prepared as the ways we should walk in.
[Ephesians] [2]:[11] Remember: Although you were once other races in the flesh, and were called ‘the uncircumcised’ by those who were circumcised by hand in the flesh,
[Ephesians] [2]:[12] and you were without the Anointed One (you were aliens to the citizens of IsraEl and strangers to the Sacred Agreement of the promise… Godless and without any hope in this world)... It was
[Ephesians] [2]:[13] through the Anointed Jesus, you who were once far away, have now come to be near to him – via his blood.
[Ephesians] [2]:[14] So he’s our peace [between us]. For he made the two ([Jews and Gentiles]) one by breaking down the wall that fenced them off from each other.
[Ephesians] [2]:[15] Through his flesh, he destroyed the hatred [that was brought about by] the Law of Commandments and rules, so that through himself he could take the two, and create a new man – in order to bring about this peace.
[Ephesians] [2]:[16] Therefore, he brought both [types of] people back to God, [united] as one ‘body’ through the upright [execution stake] – using himself to destroy the hatred between them!
[Ephesians] [2]:[17] For when he came, he proclaimed the good news of peace to you who were far away, and to those who were nearby...
[Ephesians] [2]:[18] So that through him, we can all gain access to the Father in [the same] spirit.
[Ephesians] [2]:[19] As a result, you’re not strangers or aliens anymore! You’re fellow citizens among the Holy Ones, and family members of God’s household!
[Ephesians] [2]:[20] You’re being built upon the foundation of the Apostles and the Prophets, and the cornerstone is the Anointed Jesus himself!
[Ephesians] [2]:[21] And through him, the whole building is being fitted together, growing into a Most Holy Place for [Jehovah].
[Ephesians] [2]:[22] Through the spirit, you’re being built into a place for The God to dwell!
[Ephesians] [3]:[1] I give thanks that I (Paul) am a slave of the Anointed Jesus on your behalf… Yes for you – the people among the other races!
[Ephesians] [3]:[2] Perhaps you’ve heard about the responsibility that I was given (by the loving care of God) concerning you,
[Ephesians] [3]:[3] and of how this mystery, that I wrote to you about briefly in the past, was revealed to me.
[Ephesians] [3]:[4] So as you read on, hopefully you can grasp [how well] I understand the mystery of the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [3]:[5] [Although this mystery] wasn’t revealed to past generations of the sons of men, it’s now been revealed through his holy Apostles and Prophets via [God’s] breath…
[Ephesians] [3]:[6] [The mystery is this:] That other races will also be fellow heirs, fellow members of the ‘body,’ and fellow partakers of the promise (in the Anointed Jesus), through the Good News.
[Ephesians] [3]:[7] And I became a servant of this [Good News] through the gift given to me by the loving care of God, and in harmony with His Power.
[Ephesians] [3]:[8] This loving care was revealed to me (a man who is less than the least of all the Holy Ones) so that I should preach the good news about the unimaginable richness of the Anointed One to the other races,
[Ephesians] [3]:[9] and to shine a light on how this mystery –which was hidden throughout the ages in The God who created all things– shall work out!
[Ephesians] [3]:[10] Yes, so that governments and heavenly powers might now learn about the vast wisdom of The God via His called ones.
[Ephesians] [3]:[11] [This] has been His age-long purpose through the Anointed Jesus our Lord.
[Ephesians] [3]:[12] And it’s through our confidence and faith in him that we’ve been given this direction and this freedom to speak out.
[Ephesians] [3]:[13] It’s also because of this that I’m asking you not to tire of the concern I have for you, because it glorifies you.
[Ephesians] [3]:[14] For it’s over this that I thankfully bend my knees to the Father
[Ephesians] [3]:[15] (out of whom all lines in heaven and on earth get their paternal names)
[Ephesians] [3]:[16] to [ask Him to] grant you (by the richness of His glory) the power to become strong in His spirit, and to make the persons you are on the inside
[Ephesians] [3]:[17] alive in the Anointed One, through the faith in your hearts, along with love... And to give you sufficient roots and foundation
[Ephesians] [3]:[18] to be able to understand (along with the rest of the Holy Ones) the width, the length, the height, and the depth…
[Ephesians] [3]:[19] Yes, to recognize the love of the Anointed One (which is more than you can comprehend), and to fill you with all the fullness that can only come from The God!
[Ephesians] [3]:[20] Now, to the One who, through His power that operates in us, can do far more than anything we can ask or even conceive:
[Ephesians] [3]:[21] May He be glorified by the called ones and by the Anointed Jesus throughout all generations and into ages of ages… May it be so!
[Ephesians] [4]:[1] So as a prisoner in the Lord, I’m urging you to be sure that you’re worthy of the calling you’ve received –
[Ephesians] [4]:[2] in all humility, gentleness, and patience, while you lovingly put up with each other.
[Ephesians] [4]:[3] Try hard to recognize the unifying force of [God’s] breath, and its power to bring you together in peace.
[Ephesians] [4]:[4] For there’s just one ‘body’ and one spirit, according to the one hope you were called towards (when you were called)…
[Ephesians] [4]:[5] There’s just one Lord, one faith, one immersion,
[Ephesians] [4]:[6] and one God and Father of everyone, who is over all, through all, and in all.
[Ephesians] [4]:[7] Now, the amount of loving care that was shown to each of us depends upon how much of the Gift the Anointed One measured out to us.
[Ephesians] [4]:[8] For he says: ‘To the highest places, he’s stepped up, And he led captives into captivity; Then, he gave gifts to the people.’ [Psalm 68:18]
[Ephesians] [4]:[9] So when it says ‘he stepped up,’ this also means that he first had to step down to the lower places… [that is,] to the earth.
[Ephesians] [4]:[10] So the one who stepped down, also stepped back up – high above the skies – so he could bring everything to a completion.
[Ephesians] [4]:[11] Then he assigned some to be Apostles, some to be Prophets, some to be messengers of the Good News, and some to be shepherds and teachers,
[Ephesians] [4]:[12] in order to prepare the Holy Ones for the work of serving and strengthening the body of the Anointed One,
[Ephesians] [4]:[13] until we all become one in the faith and in knowledge of the Son of The God – to the point where we’re a complete man who fully measures up to the stature of the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [4]:[14] Yes, so we won’t be [spiritual] ‘babies’ anymore, being troubled and confused by every breeze of deceitful teachings from people who’ll use any cunning scheme to seduce you.
[Ephesians] [4]:[15] Therefore, while holding onto the truth (and in love), let’s develop in every way into this one who is the ‘head’ [of the ‘body’] – the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [4]:[16] For he brings the whole ‘body’ firmly together at its joints, and supplies enough of the gift to each part according to its needs, so the ‘body’ will grow itself in love.
[Ephesians] [4]:[17] I say and advise this from [Jehovah]: Don’t continue in the same path that the nations are following, because their thoughts are worthless,
[Ephesians] [4]:[18] their minds have been darkened to any understanding, and they’re aliens to a god-fearing life because they’re ignorant [of God] and blind in their hearts!
[Ephesians] [4]:[19] For since they’re cut off from any hope, they’ve surrendered themselves to debauchery, and greedily doing filthy things.
[Ephesians] [4]:[20] However, that isn’t what you’ve learned to be true of the Anointed One
[Ephesians] [4]:[21] (if you for a fact heard and were taught about him), because truth comes through Jesus.
[Ephesians] [4]:[22] Therefore, you must get rid of the former man (who is corrupted by sinful desires)
[Ephesians] [4]:[23] and create a new personality.
[Ephesians] [4]:[24] Then put on this new person… Yes, [someone] created by God in righteousness and true purity.
[Ephesians] [4]:[25] Also, get rid of lying… You must always tell your neighbors the truth, because we’re all fellow ‘body parts’ of each other!
[Ephesians] [4]:[26] [Yes, you can] get irritated, but don’t sin… For the sun will never set on reasons to be irritated!
[Ephesians] [4]:[27] Nor should you allow any room for the Slanderer [to act].
[Ephesians] [4]:[28] So if you’ve been a thief, you shouldn’t steal anymore. Instead, you should work hard and do good things with your hands, so you’ll have something to share with the needy.
[Ephesians] [4]:[29] Nor should you allow any foul words to come out of your mouths. Instead, use good words that are upbuilding (as needed) to show that you care about everyone who listens to you.
[Ephesians] [4]:[30] Don’t impede the holy breath of The God, with which you’re sealed for the day of salvation.
[Ephesians] [4]:[31] Yes, get rid of all the bitterness, anger, wrath, screaming, and slandering, and everything bad,
[Ephesians] [4]:[32] and be kind to each other… Be sympathetic and graciously forgive each other, as God (through the Anointed One) has graciously forgiven you.
[Ephesians] [5]:[1] Become imitators of God as His beloved children,
[Ephesians] [5]:[2] and keep on walking in love – in the same way that the Anointed One loved you and gave himself up for you, as an offering and a sweet-smelling sacrifice to The God.
[Ephesians] [5]:[3] Don’t allow sexual immorality or any type of uncleanness or greediness to be even mentioned among you – as would be expected of holy people.
[Ephesians] [5]:[4] Nor [should you share in] shameful conduct, foolishness, or dirty jokes (which are all unbecoming), but instead, [share] in the giving of thanks.
[Ephesians] [5]:[5] [For it’s easy] to recognize those who are immoral, unclean, and greedy (which really amounts to being idol worshipers); and you know that such ones won’t receive an inheritance in the Kingdom of the Anointed One and of The God.
[Ephesians] [5]:[6] So don’t allow anyone to seduce you with empty words; for the wrath of God is coming upon the disobedient sons [of mankind] because of things like that!
[Ephesians] [5]:[7] Therefore, don’t go along with them...
[Ephesians] [5]:[8] Because, although you were once dark, you’ve now become light in the Lord! So instead, keep on walking as children of the light!
[Ephesians] [5]:[9] For the fruitage of light is every sort of goodness, righteousness, and truth…
[Ephesians] [5]:[10] Things that prove to be pleasing to the Lord.
[Ephesians] [5]:[11] So don’t share in the unproductive deeds of darkness. Rather, speak out against them!
[Ephesians] [5]:[12] It’s shameful to speak about things that are only done in private,
[Ephesians] [5]:[13] because everything that the light speaks against is being exposed, since the light illuminates everything.
[Ephesians] [5]:[14] That’s why it’s said: ‘Wake up, sleepy! Rise from the house of the ‘dead'… Then the Anointed One will shine upon you.’ [possibly a quote from a popular hymn]
[Ephesians] [5]:[15] So you must pay close attention to the ways that you’re walking… That it’s not like foolish ones, but like wise ones.
[Ephesians] [5]:[16] Buy the time [to do this], because these are wicked days.
[Ephesians] [5]:[17] Yes, don’t be foolish, but start learning what the Lord’s will for us is.
[Ephesians] [5]:[18] And don’t be getting drunk on wine, which leads down an unsavory path. Instead, fill yourselves with the breath [of God],
[Ephesians] [5]:[19] and speak to each other in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs… Sing and create music in your hearts to [Jehovah]
[Ephesians] [5]:[20] in the name of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One. Yes, always give thanks to our God and Father for everything!
[Ephesians] [5]:[21] You should also submit to each other in the same way that you show reverential fear for the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [5]:[22] Wives should submit to their husbands like they would to the Lord,
[Ephesians] [5]:[23] because a husband is the head and origin of his wife, just as the Anointed One is the head and origin of the congregation, that is, the savior of that ‘body.’
[Ephesians] [5]:[24] So, just as the congregation submits to the Anointed One, that’s how wives should [submit] to their husbands in everything.
[Ephesians] [5]:[25] Men: Love your wives as the Anointed One loved the congregation and gave himself up to make it holy.
[Ephesians] [5]:[26] He washed it in a bath of water (so to speak),
[Ephesians] [5]:[27] in order to present a glorious gathering to himself that doesn’t have any spots, wrinkles, or any such things, but which is holy and without any blemishes.
[Ephesians] [5]:[28] Yes, that’s how the men should love their wives… As their own bodies. So, the man who loves his wife is really showing love for himself…
[Ephesians] [5]:[29] And nobody ever hates his own flesh. Rather, he feeds it and takes pride in it, just as the Anointed One does the congregation.
[Ephesians] [5]:[30] And we’ve become parts of [Jesus’] ‘body'… Of his very flesh and his bones!
[Ephesians] [5]:[31] [So as the scripture says]: ‘A man will leave his father and mother and stick with his woman, and the two will become one flesh.’ [Genesis 2:24]
[Ephesians] [5]:[32] Now, this is a great mystery, because I’m comparing [the relationship between husbands and wives] to the Anointed One and [his love for] the congregation.
[Ephesians] [5]:[33] But this is how each man should love his wife… As he does himself. And women should have a reverential fear of their husbands.
[Ephesians] [6]:[1] Children: Obey your parents in our Lord, because this is righteous.
[Ephesians] [6]:[2] Honor your father and mother, for this is the first Commandment that came with a promise:
[Ephesians] [6]:[3] ’...that things would go well for you, and that you may live a long time on the land.’ [Exodus 20:12 or Deuteronomy 5:16]
[Ephesians] [6]:[4] Fathers: Don’t frustrate your children, but bring them up in the discipline and council of our Lord.
[Ephesians] [6]:[5] Slaves: Be obedient to those who are your fleshly masters with reverential fear and sincere hearts, like you would to the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [6]:[6] Don’t just put on a good show to please men, but as slaves of the Anointed One, do the will of God whole-souled.
[Ephesians] [6]:[7] Be willing slaves as to the Lord (not of men),
[Ephesians] [6]:[8] because you know that whatever good you do will be rewarded by the Lord, whether you’re a slave or a free man.
[Ephesians] [6]:[9] Masters: Keep on doing the same for [your slaves]… And don’t be threatening them, because you know that there’s a Master who is over both them and you in the heavens, and He doesn’t recognize any difference [between you].
[Ephesians] [6]:[10] [To all:] Finally, become powerful in the mightiness and strength of the Lord.
[Ephesians] [6]:[11] Put on the complete suit of God’s armor, so that you can resist the methods of the Slanderer.
[Ephesians] [6]:[12] For our fight isn’t against flesh and blood, but against the governments, the authorities, the mighty ones of this worldly darkness, and against the unseen wicked powers in the heavens.
[Ephesians] [6]:[13] So because of this, take up the complete suit [that comes from] God, so you can fight in that wicked day and still be found standing.
[Ephesians] [6]:[14] Yes, stand firm with your hips wrapped in the truth and wearing the breastplate of righteousness!
[Ephesians] [6]:[15] Wrap your feet and prepare them with the good news of peace.
[Ephesians] [6]:[16] And above all else, pick up the large shield of faith, with which you can quench all the flaming missiles of the wicked one!
[Ephesians] [6]:[17] Also, accept the helmet of salvation and the sword of the spirit (which are the things that God has said).
[Ephesians] [6]:[18] Keep on praying and begging [God] about everything in spirit throughout each season. Be aware of this, and never stop petitioning [God] on behalf of all the Holy Ones.
[Ephesians] [6]:[19] Also [pray] for me… That the words may be given to me to open my mouth and speak freely so I can make the mystery of the good news known [to others].
[Ephesians] [6]:[20] Indeed, that’s why I’m now an ambassador in chains… So that I can speak boldly about these things and to say the things that I’m supposed to say.
[Ephesians] [6]:[21] Now, so you can know how I’m getting along and what I’m doing, TychiKos (a beloved brother and faithful servant of the Lord) will explain everything to you.
[Ephesians] [6]:[22] This is why I’m sending him to you… To let you know what’s happening to us and to bring comfort to your hearts.
[Ephesians] [6]:[23] Peace to the brothers, and love with faith from God the Father and from the Lord Jesus the Anointed One.
[Ephesians] [6]:[24] May all those who have an uncorrupted love for our Lord Jesus the Anointed One receive [His] loving care. May it be so!
[Philippians] [1]:[1] Paul and Timothy, slaves of the Anointed Jesus, to all the Holy Ones in the Anointed Jesus [who are] in Philippi, along with the overseers and servants:
[Philippians] [1]:[2] May you have kindness and peace from God our Father, and from the Lord Jesus the Anointed!
[Philippians] [1]:[3] I thank my God every time you’re mentioned,
[Philippians] [1]:[4] and I’m constantly begging [God] on your behalf… Yes, begging with joy,
[Philippians] [1]:[5] because of your partnership in [sharing] the good news from the first day until now.
[Philippians] [1]:[6] I’m confident that the one who started this good work among you will continue to perfect it until the Day of Jesus the Anointed One.
[Philippians] [1]:[7] It’s a righteous thing for me to think this way about all of you, and I keep you in my heart – both when I’m in chains, and when I’m defending and confirming the good news, for you’re all sharers in my loving care.
[Philippians] [1]:[8] God is my witness as to how much I long for all of you with the same tender affection that the Anointed Jesus has.
[Philippians] [1]:[9] And this is what I keep praying: That your love will continue to grow more and more, along with your higher knowledge and understanding;
[Philippians] [1]:[10] and that you’ll keep on proving the most excellent things, so that you might be found pure and blameless until the day of the Anointed One…
[Philippians] [1]:[11] Yes, being filled with righteous fruit (through the Anointed Jesus) to God’s glory and praise.
[Philippians] [1]:[12] Now, I want you to know this, brothers: I’m seeing results from what I’m doing for the Good News’s advancement.
[Philippians] [1]:[13] For my imprisonment because of the Anointed One has become public knowledge among the entire Praetorian Guard and everyone else [here].
[Philippians] [1]:[14] Also, because of my chains, most of the brothers in the Lord are now more confident and they’re showing more courage and fearlessness when teaching the word of God.
[Philippians] [1]:[15] Unfortunately, it’s true that some are preaching the Anointed One out of [a spirit of] envy and rivalry. However, many others are doing it for good motives…
[Philippians] [1]:[16] Out of love, because they know that [the reason why] I’m lying here is to defend the good news.
[Philippians] [1]:[17] Yet, none of the rest are doing it for good reasons; for they’re preaching the Anointed One by arguing – and they think that this will create more problems for me while I’m in prison.
[Philippians] [1]:[18] But it doesn’t make any difference, for whether they’re just pretending or they’re being sincere, the Anointed One is being made known... And I rejoice over this. In fact, I’ll keep on rejoicing,
[Philippians] [1]:[19] because I know that through your earnest prayers and a [generous] supply of the spirit of Jesus the Anointed One, I’ll be saved [from this imprisonment].
[Philippians] [1]:[20] Yes, I eagerly hope (and don’t expect to be disappointed) that soon I’ll be able to speak freely about the Anointed One just as before, and even more so, whether my body is dead or alive!
[Philippians] [1]:[21] To me, life is the Anointed One and my reward is death...
[Philippians] [1]:[22] However, if I can keep on living in the flesh, I consider this to be the fruitage of my work. Which do I prefer? I won’t say,
[Philippians] [1]:[23] for I’m obsessed by the two. What I really want is to be released [from this body] and to be with the Anointed One, since that’s surely the best.
[Philippians] [1]:[24] However, for your sakes, it’s better for me to remain in the flesh.
[Philippians] [1]:[25] And because I’m confident of this, I know that I’ll survive and still be with all of you, so I can help you to grow in the joy of the faith…
[Philippians] [1]:[26] And then your reasons for pride in the Anointed Jesus will grow because of me, due to the fact that I’ll be coming to you again.
[Philippians] [1]:[27] Just behave in a way that’s worthy of the good news about the Anointed One, so that regardless of whether I’m coming to visit or I’m far away, I can hear [good] things about you… For example, [I want to hear] that you’re all standing firm with the same motivations, and that you’re serving the faith of the good news side-by-side as a single ‘person,’
[Philippians] [1]:[28] not being frightened by those who oppose you. [This fine conduct on your part] will be evidence of both their [spiritual] ruin, and our salvation.
[Philippians] [1]:[29] God has given you the privilege of not only really believing in the Anointed One, but also of suffering for him,
[Philippians] [1]:[30] and of struggling with the same things you saw me [struggle with], which you’re now hearing are happening to me again.
[Philippians] [2]:[1] Therefore, if there’s any encouragement [to be found] in the Anointed One, any consoling love, any fellowship of the [Holy] breath, any depth of heart or compassion
[Philippians] [2]:[2] – anything that would make my joy in you complete – [it would be to hear that] you’ve been: Of one mind, Of one love, Of one spirit, and Of one will.
[Philippians] [2]:[3] And that you aren’t doing anything out of spite or pride but humbly, believing all the others to be better than you.
[Philippians] [2]:[4] Also that you’re not just watching out for yourselves, but for the best interests of each other!

[1 Timothy] [1]:[20] This includes Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I’ve handed over to the Opposer so they can be taught not to blaspheme.

[1 Timothy] [4]:[4] (for everything that God created is good, and nothing should be thrown away). So if we thank Him for it,
[1 Timothy] [4]:[5] it becomes holy by what we say to God in our prayers.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[6] So if you’ll explain these things to the brothers, you’ll prove yourself a fine servant of the Anointed Jesus, and [you’ll] grow strong on the words of the Faith and the fine teachings that you’ve been following so closely.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[7] You must avoid worldly fables and old-wives’ tales, and train yourself to be a truly reverent person...
[1 Timothy] [4]:[8] For even though physical exercise does some good, learning reverence [for God] is good for all things! It holds the promise of life – both now, and into that which is coming.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[9] Yes, what I’m saying is trustworthy and deserves [your special] attention,
[1 Timothy] [4]:[10] for this is why we’ve been struggling and working so hard as we’ve continued to put faith in a living God who is the Savior of all men – but mostly of the faithful.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[11] So, instruct and teach…
[1 Timothy] [4]:[12] And don’t allow anyone to look down on you because you’re young! Instead, become an example to the faithful in what you say, in what you do, in your love, in your faith, and in your purity!
[1 Timothy] [4]:[13] Until I get there, work at public reading, at giving council, and on your teaching abilities.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[14] Don’t be careless with the gift in you, which was given through a prophecy when the elders laid their hands on you.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[15] Think deeply about these things… Get wrapped up in them, so that everyone can see the progress that you’re making.
[1 Timothy] [4]:[16] Yes, pay close attention to yourself and to your teaching, and stick with it! For if you do that, you’ll save both yourself and those who are listening to you!
[1 Timothy] [5]:[1] Don’t be too harsh with older men… Speak to them as you would to fathers, to younger men as brothers,
[1 Timothy] [5]:[2] to older women as mothers, and to younger women as sisters, with all purity.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[3] Show honor to the widows who are really living as widows.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[4] However, if a widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn the lesson of how to show deep respect inside their own families – by paying what they owe to their parents and grandparents… For in God’s sight, that’s the right thing to do.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[5] Now, a [truly-worthy] widow is one who has been left on her own, and because she puts her hope in God, she keeps begging Him in her prayers both night and day.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[6] However, [a widow] who lives alone for pleasure is already ‘dead’ while she’s still alive.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[7] So you must always teach them this, so they’ll be found blameless:
[1 Timothy] [5]:[8] ‘If you don’t provide for [those who are] your own (especially for those in your own households), you’ve denied the faith and you’re worse than an unbeliever!’
[1 Timothy] [5]:[9] However, put a widow on the list if: She’s more than 60 years old, She’s had just one husband,
[1 Timothy] [5]:[10] She’s done good things that can be attested to, She’s raised children, She’s been hospitable, She’s washed the feet of the Holy Ones, She’s provided for those in difficulty, She’s followed the course of doing all sorts of good deeds.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[11] On the other hand, turn down younger widows... For when they feel the need, they leave the Anointed One because they want to marry!
[1 Timothy] [5]:[12] And they’re judged for doing this, because they set aside the faith that they had at first,
[1 Timothy] [5]:[13] while learning wasteful habits such as going around and doing a lot of visiting. They not only waste time, they also gossip, meddle in other people’s affairs, and talk about things that they shouldn’t.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[14] I prefer to see younger widows marry, have children, and manage a home. That way, the Opposer isn’t given something over which he can gleefully gloat...
[1 Timothy] [5]:[15] Yet, some of them have already turned to following the Slanderer.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[16] So if any believing woman has a widow [in her family], she should take care of this herself, so that the congregation won’t have to handle the burden and can then help those [truly in need].
[1 Timothy] [5]:[17] Also, let the elders who take the lead in a fine way be considered as worthy of a double honor… Especially those who work hard at speaking and teaching!
[1 Timothy] [5]:[18] For the Scriptures tell us: ‘You shouldn’t muzzle a bull when it’s threshing [grain].’ [Deuteronomy 25:4] And that a worker deserves his pay! [Deuteronomy 24:14-15]
[1 Timothy] [5]:[19] [Also, don’t] accept an accusation against an elder unless there are two or three witnesses.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[20] However, you should expose those whom you find guilty of sins before all onlookers, so the rest will be afraid [of doing such things].
[1 Timothy] [5]:[21] Before God, the Anointed Jesus, and the chosen messengers, I solemnly charge you to follow these instructions! However, don’t reach any conclusions before you’ve heard all the evidence, and never decide because you’re biased one way or the other.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[22] Also, don’t be too quick to [appoint] any man [to a responsibility], so you aren’t found to be a sharer in the sins of others. Keep yourself pure!
[1 Timothy] [5]:[23] And don’t just drink water, instead you might take a little wine for the sake of your stomach and for your frequent illnesses.
[1 Timothy] [5]:[24] [Remember that] the sins of some people are done in the open and lead directly to judgment. However, the [sins] of the rest will eventually become known...
[1 Timothy] [5]:[25] For just as many good deeds become widely known, [sins] can’t be kept hidden either.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[1] Now, those who are in bondage as slaves should treat their masters as worthy of all honor, so that the Name of God and our teachings won’t be slandered.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[2] And those who have believing owners shouldn’t think less of them because they are brothers. Rather, they should zealously serve them as slaves, because those who work hard are considered faithful and are loved in return. Keep on teaching these things and giving them this encouragement!
[1 Timothy] [6]:[3] Now, if anyone is teaching something different and doesn’t follow these life-giving words (which are those of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One), or doesn’t teach deep respect for God...
[1 Timothy] [6]:[4] He’s just blowing smoke, he doesn’t understand anything, and he is ill with arguing and debating over words… It results in envy, arguing, slandering, wicked suspicions,
[1 Timothy] [6]:[5] and conflict between men with corrupt minds who have let themselves be robbed of the truth… And they’re the same ones who say that we should earn a profit from this worship! But you, keep yourself away from them!
[1 Timothy] [6]:[6] Of course, we do gain much ‘profit’ from this worship… That is, if we pay our own way.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[7] For none of us brought anything into the world and we can’t carry anything out!
[1 Timothy] [6]:[8] So if we have enough to eat and enough to wear, we should be satisfied with that.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[9] However, those who want to be rich fall into temptation, snares, and many foolish and damaging desires, which drag people down into destruction and ruin…
[1 Timothy] [6]:[10] For the love of money is the root of everything that’s bad. And because some have reached out for it, they’ve been led away from the faith and into error, stabbing themselves all over and causing themselves a lot of pain.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[11] But you, O man of God – flee from these things, and pursue righteousness, reverence, faith, love, endurance, and humility.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[12] Yes, fight this fine contest of the faith. Also, seize this age-long life to which you were called – about which you offered such a fine confession before so many witnesses!
[1 Timothy] [6]:[13] I’m ordering you in the sight of The God (who is saving all), and of the Anointed Jesus (who gave such a fine testimony before Pontius Pilate),
[1 Timothy] [6]:[14] to obey these instructions flawlessly and blamelessly until the appearance of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One
[1 Timothy] [6]:[15] whom God will reveal at his time. Yes, the only praised and only sovereign, The King of kings and Lord of lords.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[16] The only one who can’t perish, And who lives in unapproachable light. The one whom no man has seen or can see, May he have honor, and age-long power. May it be so!
[1 Timothy] [6]:[17] Also, give orders to those who are rich in this age not to think too much of themselves, and not to trust in their wealth (which is fickle), but in God who brings [the type of] wealth to us that we can truly enjoy.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[18] [Yes, teach them to] work at being good, to be rich in good deeds, and to be generous and ready to share...
[1 Timothy] [6]:[19] while they safely store away for themselves the treasures of a fine foundation in that which is coming, so they can put on the real life.
[1 Timothy] [6]:[20] O Timothy, Guard this hope and turn away from all the worldly babbling, as well as everything falsely called ‘knowledge.’
[1 Timothy] [6]:[21] Because it’s through [such things] that some who once showed much promise in the faith have been turned aside. May [God’s] loving care be with you. May it be so!
[2 Timothy] [1]:[1] Paul, an Apostle of the Anointed Jesus by the will of The God and by the promise of life in the Anointed Jesus,
[2 Timothy] [1]:[2] to my loved child Timothy: May you find loving care, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from the Anointed Jesus, our Lord!
[2 Timothy] [1]:[3] I’m thankful to The God whom I’m worshiping with a clean conscience (as did my forefathers) that I never forget you in my prayers, which I offer [on your behalf] night and day.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[4] For I remember you with tears and I long to see you, so that I can be filled with joy.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[5] I fondly remember the unhypocritical faith that your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice had first, and I’m confident that you have this also.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[6] So, this is the reason why I’m reminding you to rekindle the gift of God that you received when I first laid my hands on you.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[7] Since God didn’t give us a spirit of fear (but of power, love, and good sense),
[2 Timothy] [1]:[8] don’t be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord or of me – a prisoner for his sake! So, come and share with us in suffering evil for the good news with the power of God.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[9] For He didn’t save us or call us to holiness because of anything that we’ve done, but because it’s been His will throughout the ages to show us His loving kindness, through Jesus the Anointed One.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[10] And all of this has now appeared via the arrival of our Savior, the Anointed Jesus, who has done away with death – and is shining a light on life and freedom from corruption through this good news
[2 Timothy] [1]:[11] (of which I was appointed a preacher, an Apostle, and a teacher).
[2 Timothy] [1]:[12] Yes, this is the reason why I’ve been suffering these things and why I’m unashamed… Because I really know this one in whom I’ve put my faith, and I’m confident that he’ll guard everything I’ve entrusted to him until that Day.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[13] Likewise, you should be hanging onto the healthy words that you heard from me and which I laid out for you (through the love that’s in the Anointed Jesus).
[2 Timothy] [1]:[14] You should be guarding these things that you’ve been given through [this] Holy breath that dwells within us!
[2 Timothy] [1]:[15] I’m sure that you’re aware of the fact that everyone in the [province of] Asia have turned their backs on me, and especially PhyGelus and HermoGenes...
[2 Timothy] [1]:[16] But may the Lord’s mercy rest upon the household of OnesiPhorus, because he’s often brought me refreshment and he’s never been ashamed of my chains.
[2 Timothy] [1]:[17] For when he came to Rome, he diligently started searching for me and quickly found me!
[2 Timothy] [1]:[18] So, may he find mercy with the Lord on that Day. And you know very well how much he served me in Ephesus, too.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[1] However, as for you my child, Keep growing stronger in the loving care of the Anointed Jesus,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[2] and keep on teaching the things that you heard from so many witnesses while you were with me, to faithful men who are qualified to teach others.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[3] Then, as a fine soldier of the Anointed Jesus, [be prepared to] endure hardships!
[2 Timothy] [2]:[4] For no soldier can just go on living his life as he once did, since he wants to please the one who enlisted him.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[5] And the same is true of an athlete… He can’t win the prize unless he plays by the rules!
[2 Timothy] [2]:[6] Yet, the hardworking field-hand must also be the first one to taste the fruit.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[7] If you’ll visualize what I’m saying, the Lord will truly give you insight into everything.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[8] Remember that the good news I’ve been preaching teaches us that Jesus the Anointed (the offspring of David) was raised from the dead…
[2 Timothy] [2]:[9] And it’s over this that I’m being persecuted and imprisoned like a criminal. However, the word of God hasn’t been locked up with me!
[2 Timothy] [2]:[10] I’m putting up with all of this for the sake of the elected ones… So they can gain the salvation that comes from being in the Anointed Jesus and receiving age-long glory.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[11] For you can believe the saying: ‘If we die together, We’ll also live together;
[2 Timothy] [2]:[12] And if we hang on together, We’ll also rule as kings together!’ However, if we deny this, he’ll also deny us.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[13] Even if we stop believing in him, he’ll still believe, [won’t he?] Because he can [hardly] deny his own existence!
[2 Timothy] [2]:[14] I want you to keep on reminding [the brothers] about these things, and I want you to instruct them –in the sight of God– not to be arguing over words, for this is just a waste of time and it’s a snare to those who listen to it.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[15] As for you: Keep on seeking God’s approval zealously, so you’re accepted by Him as a workman who has got nothing to be ashamed of, and who lays out the truth straightforwardly.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[16] Therefore, you should avoid speaking about worldly and foolish topics, because this leads [people] away from pure worship,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[17] and whatever is said [spreads like] a field of gangrene! That’s what happened to Hymenaeus and PhileTos –
[2 Timothy] [2]:[18] they got away from the truth and started teaching that the resurrection has already happened, which misdirected the faith of some.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[19] However, you have a solid foundation in God, and it has this seal [of approval], that [Jehovah]... ‘...knows who are His.’ [Numbers 16:5 or Nahum 1:7] And: ‘Everyone who calls on the Name of the Lord will be rescued.’ Joel 2:32, see note]
[2 Timothy] [2]:[20] Now, in a large house there aren’t just containers made of gold and silver, but also those [made] of wood and pottery… Because some were made for honorable purposes, while others were made for dishonorable purposes.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[21] So if anyone chooses to be clean, he must remove [everything that’s dishonorable] from himself so that he can become a container for an honorable purpose – holy and useful to his master. And from then on, he must be ready to do every sort of good work.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[22] So, flee from the desires of youth, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, and peace... Along with everyone else who is calling on the Lord with a clean heart.
[2 Timothy] [2]:[23] However, avoid foolish and ignorant questions, because you know that they just create arguments…
[2 Timothy] [2]:[24] and a slave of the Lord shouldn’t be arguing. Instead, we should be gentle with everyone, we should be good teachers, and we should know how to keep our composure in bad [situations]
[2 Timothy] [2]:[25] so we can teach those who disagree calmly. [After all,] perhaps God may lead them to repentance and to an accurate knowledge of the truth,
[2 Timothy] [2]:[26] so that they may escape the Slanderer’s snares and return to their good senses – once they realize how they’ve been lured into his cage!
[2 Timothy] [3]:[1] Understand that hard times will come in the last days,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[2] and people will just love themselves and money... [They’ll be] braggarts, loud blasphemers, argumentative ([even] with their own people), unthankful, wicked.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[3] [They’ll be] false accusers, addicted to lust, fierce, hating what’s good,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[4] betrayers, impetuous, and proud of [themselves] – yes, lovers of many pleasures, away from the love of God.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[5] Even though they might have some form of Godly fear, they’ll be far away from its power [to change them]. You should reject people like this,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[6] because it’s from among such ones that certain men will arise... Ones who’ll work their way into homes and seduce weak women who are loaded down with sins (because they have so many desires),
[2 Timothy] [3]:[7] and who’ll always just be students who can never come to a higher knowledge of the truth.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[8] So, whenever you must deal with men who are resisting the truth and corrupting their own minds (making themselves worthless when it comes to the faith), follow the example of Moses when he opposed JanNes and JamBres,
[2 Timothy] [3]:[9] so they can’t make any more inroads. Then (as happened [to JanNes and JamBres]) their unreasonableness will become clear for everyone [to see]!
[2 Timothy] [3]:[10] Now... You’ve closely followed my teachings, my directions, my purposes, my faith, my patience, my love, and my endurance.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[11] [However, you’ve also had to share in] my persecution and my sufferings (such as the things that happened to me in AntiOch, Iconium, and Lystra), and you’ve endured the same types of opposition that I’ve had to endure (but from which the Lord has delivered me).
[2 Timothy] [3]:[12] For everybody who wants to worship The God through the Anointed Jesus is going to be persecuted...
[2 Timothy] [3]:[13] Because wicked and deceitful men will just get worse and worse, misleading and being misled!
[2 Timothy] [3]:[14] As for you: Stick with the things that you’ve learned and were convinced to believe… And remember from whom you learned them!
[2 Timothy] [3]:[15] For you’ve been familiar with the Holy Writings since you were a child, and they can make you wise for salvation through your faith in the Anointed Jesus.
[2 Timothy] [3]:[16] [Remember that] all the Holy Writings were inspired by God and they’re good for teaching, for correcting, for setting things straight, and for providing righteous discipline…
[2 Timothy] [3]:[17] They qualify a man of God by providing him with whatever he needs to do all sorts of good work.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[1] So I solemnly charge you in the sight of God and the Anointed Jesus (who is going to judge the living and the dead when he manifests himself in his Kingdom)
[2 Timothy] [4]:[2] to keep on preaching the word! Keep on doing it through both good times and bad! Then, as you consider [what you see], you must offer criticism and encouragement. However, you should do this patiently and with all of your teaching skills.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[3] Yet, the time is coming when they won’t put up with life-giving teachings anymore. Rather (because they will prefer to follow their own desires), they will gather teachers for themselves who’ll tell them whatever they want to hear!
[2 Timothy] [4]:[4] They won’t listen to the truth, but they’ll all show up when it comes to listening to fables.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[5] But as for you: Be serious about everything, endure all the bad, preach the good news, and completely carry out your ministry!
[2 Timothy] [4]:[6] As for me: Even though I’ll soon be poured out as a sacrifice, and the time for my undoing is almost here,
[2 Timothy] [4]:[7] I can say that I’ve wrestled the fine match, I’ve finished the race, and I’ve obeyed the faith!
[2 Timothy] [4]:[8] So now he’s keeping a righteous crown for me, which the Lord (the righteous judge) will give me on that day (but not just to me, but to everyone who eagerly looks forward to his appearance).
[2 Timothy] [4]:[9] So hurry… Come to me quickly –
[2 Timothy] [4]:[10] because Demas has let me down and gone to ThesSalonica (since he still loves this age), Kreskes has gone to Galatia, Titus has gone to Dalmatia,
[2 Timothy] [4]:[11] and Luke is the only one who is here with me! So, go find Mark and bring him with you, because his services are very useful to me.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[12] Oh yes, I also sent Tychikus off to Ephesus.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[13] And when you come here, bring along the robe that I left with Carpus in Troas… And the scrolls, especially the parchments.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[14] Alexander the coppersmith has testified and said many bad things against me. But the Lord will repay him for what he’s done.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[15] So watch out for him! Because he really opposes everything that we say.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[16] Unfortunately, nobody stayed with me during my first court hearing… But despite the fact they all left me, I don’t want this to be held against them,
[2 Timothy] [4]:[17] because the Lord stood by me. Yes, he gave me strength so that the preaching might be completed through me, and that all the gentiles might hear it. As a result, I was saved from the lion’s mouth!
[2 Timothy] [4]:[18] And the Lord will continue to save me from every sort of wickedness until he brings me into his heavenly Kingdom. May he be glorified throughout the ages of ages… May it be so!
[2 Timothy] [4]:[19] Give my greetings to Priska and Aquila, and to the household of OnesiPhorus.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[20] Erastus stayed in Corinth, and I left Trophimus at Miletus, because he was sick.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[21] Hurry and get here before the winter arrives! EuBoulos sends you his greetings, as do Poudes, Linos, Klaudia, and all the brothers.
[2 Timothy] [4]:[22] May the Lord bless the spirit you’re showing, and may his loving care be with all of you. May it be so.
[Titus] [1]:[1] From Paul – a slave of God, an Apostle of Jesus the Anointed One and a follower of the faith of God’s elected who have a complete knowledge of truth and whose worship
[Titus] [1]:[2] is based on the hope of age-long life, which The God (who doesn’t lie) promised ages ago
[Titus] [1]:[3] and who, in His own due time, made His Word known through an important message that was entrusted to me by the command of our God and Savior.
[Titus] [1]:[4] To Titus – a true child in the faith that we hold in common. May you have loving care and peace from God the Father, and from the Anointed Jesus our Savior!
[Titus] [1]:[5] The reason why I left you in Crete is so that you could straighten out some of the problems there, and for you to appoint elders in each city, as I instructed you.
[Titus] [1]:[6] [So, choose those who] haven’t been charged with misconduct… One-woman men who have believing children who aren’t rebellious or accused of being beyond hope.
[Titus] [1]:[7] Because, as a manager of the household of God, an overseer must be blameless. [He can’t be] selfish, quick tempered, a heavy drinker, a fighter, or a greedy person.
[Titus] [1]:[8] Rather, [he must be] hospitable, a faithful friend, levelheaded, righteous, devout, self-controlled,
[Titus] [1]:[9] [and a person who] lives by the word of truth, so he can teach and encourage those who are strong as he exposes the wrongs of those who contradict.
[Titus] [1]:[10] For there are lots of rebellious and deceitful windbags (most of whom are circumcised)
[Titus] [1]:[11] and whose mouths need to be sealed. They’re the ones who are dishonestly making money by teaching things that they shouldn’t, and they’re misleading entire households!
[Titus] [1]:[12] It was one of their own prophets who said: ‘Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and lazy gluttons.’ [Epimenides of Crete]
[Titus] [1]:[13] And that’s a fact! This is why you’ll have to be tough when it comes to exposing their wrong ways, so they can become healthy in the faith, and stop
[Titus] [1]:[14] paying attention to Jewish myths and the rules of men, which are turning them away from the truth.
[Titus] [1]:[15] For although everything is clean to those who are clean, nothing is clean for those who are dirty and faithless, because both their minds and their consciences are dirty!
[Titus] [1]:[16] And while they all claim to know God, everything they do disproves it, because they are disgusting, disobedient, and unqualified to do anything worthwhile.
[Titus] [2]:[1] You however, keep on talking about the correct, healthy teachings.
[Titus] [2]:[2] Encourage the older men to be free from excesses and to be serious, levelheaded, and healthy in their faith, love, and endurance.
[Titus] [2]:[3] [Also encourage] the older women to behave as though they’d just entered a holy place… Not to be slanderers or alcoholics, but to become teachers of good things.
[Titus] [2]:[4] Teach the younger women to love their husbands and their children…
[Titus] [2]:[5] To be level headed, pure, homemakers, and good people who are willing to obey their husbands so that God’s Word won’t be spoken of shamefully.
[Titus] [2]:[6] And you must give younger men the same encouragement… To be level-headed.
[Titus] [2]:[7] [Teach them to] become good examples in all sorts of good deeds, to be serious and blameless in their teaching,
[Titus] [2]:[8] and to speak in wholesome ways so that no one can condemn them, and nobody who opposes us will have anything bad to say about us.
[Titus] [2]:[9] Also, teach those who are slaves to obey their masters in everything… To please them well, not to talk back,
[Titus] [2]:[10] and not to steal things! They should prove that they’re faithful in doing whatever is right, so they can adorn the teachings of our God and Savior in everything.
[Titus] [2]:[11] For the reason why God’s loving care is being displayed [through us] is so that we all might be saved!
[Titus] [2]:[12] And once they’ve rejected the godlessness and worldly desires, they must then be taught how to live sensibly, righteously, and devoutly in this age
[Titus] [2]:[13] while they expect the blest hope and the manifestations of the glory of the great God, and our Savior, the Anointed Jesus...
[Titus] [2]:[14] [the one] who handed himself over in order to free us by ransom from lawlessness, and to bring out a clean people for himself who are all zealous in doing whatever is good.
[Titus] [2]:[15] Yes, I’m authorizing you to talk about such things, as well as to encourage and correct… And don’t let anyone ignore you!
[Titus] [3]:[1] Keep on reminding them that they must be obedient and that they must submit to the rulers and the authorities… That they must always be ready and willing to do good things!
[Titus] [3]:[2] They shouldn’t be slanderous to anyone or want to fight with them. [Rather, they should all] be willing to give in to [the wishes of] others and to be humble before everyone.
[Titus] [3]:[3] Realise that we were all once senseless, disobedient sinners... Slaves to our own desires in badness and envy (disgusting [people] who hated each other),
[Titus] [3]:[4] but when God’s kindness and compassion, our Savior, came here
[Titus] [3]:[5] (not because we were righteous, but because of His mercy), He saved us through the cleansing [water] that re-created us – by means of the renewing [power] of holy breath.
[Titus] [3]:[6] Yes, He poured plenty of it over us, through Jesus, our Anointed Savior,
[Titus] [3]:[7] so that afterwards we are counted as righteous (through His loving care), that we might become heirs who have the hope of age-long life.
[Titus] [3]:[8] You can believe these things… And these are the instructions that I want you to keep on giving to them, so that those who have come to believe in The God will stand firm in doing all that is right! Yes, these are good and helpful things that you must teach them.

[Hebrews] [1]:[1] A long time ago, God spoke to our fathers through the Prophets in many places and in many ways.

[Hebrews] [1]:[10] And also: ‘In the beginning, O Lord, you laid the foundations of the earth, And [you] made the heavens with your hands.

[Hebrews] [1]:[14] Aren’t all these others just spirits who serve – sent to serve those who’ll inherit life?
[Hebrews] [2]:[1] This is why it’s so important for us to pay extraordinary attention to the things that we’ve heard, so we don’t drift away!

[Hebrews] [2]:[5] However, He didn’t entrust the home that’s coming (the one I’m talking about) to the hands of [His angelic] messengers!

[Hebrews] [7]:[22] Therefore, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better Sacred Agreement,
[Hebrews] [7]:[23] since there always had to be lots of Priests because they were mortal – their deaths prevented them from continuing [to serve].
[Hebrews] [7]:[24] However, because [Jesus exists] eternally, his Priesthood is permanent!
[Hebrews] [7]:[25] And [this is why] he’s able to save those who approach The God through him, because he will always be alive to plead for them!
[Hebrews] [7]:[26] Yes, he’s truly become a High Priest for us – pure, without evil, without blemish, separate from sins, and exalted higher than the heavens!
[Hebrews] [7]:[27] And unlike the [Levitical] High Priests who have to offer daily sacrifices for their own sins first, and then for the people, he only had to do this once – when he offered himself!
[Hebrews] [7]:[28] Yes – the [Jewish] Law appoints men with weaknesses as High Priests... But the promise that came with a sworn oath (which supersedes the [Jewish] Law) [has appointed] the Son – [someone] who remains perfect eternally!
[Hebrews] [8]:[1] But the main point of everything is this: We have a High Priest who is sitting on the right-hand side of the throne of Majesty in the heavens.
[Hebrews] [8]:[2] He’s become a servant of the Most Holy, but in the real Tent built by God, not man.
[Hebrews] [8]:[3] And since every appointed High Priest must bring gifts and sacrifices, [Jesus] must have something to offer too.
[Hebrews] [8]:[4] However, if he was [still] here upon the Earth, he wouldn’t be a Priest, because there are [already] Priests who are [appointed] by the Law to offer gifts.
[Hebrews] [8]:[5] Now, when they handle these duties, they’re following a pattern that’s a shadow of [how it’s done] in the heavens...
