[James] [1]:[1] [From] James, a slave of God and of the Lord Jesus the Anointed One, to the tweleve tribes that are scattered about: Rejoice!
[James] [1]:[2] Consider it all a joyful experience, my brothers, when you have to endure various types of trials,
[James] [1]:[3] because you know that this proving of your faith helps you to endure.
[James] [1]:[4] So, may your endurance reach its goal of making you perfect and complete in every way, lacking in nothing.
[James] [1]:[5] If any of you are lacking in wisdom, you should continue to ask God, and He will give it to you… He provides it easily and without any scolding!
[James] [1]:[6] However, you must believe [that you’ll receive it] and not have any doubts, for those who doubt are like waves of the sea that are driven and blown about by the wind.
[James] [1]:[7] Such a person shouldn’t expect to receive anything at all from [Jehovah],
[James] [1]:[8] due to his unsureness and lack of faith.
[James] [1]:[9] Therefore, let the lowly brother boast of his high standing,
[James] [1]:[10] and the rich one boast of his lowliness, because he too will pass away like a flower in a field...
[James] [1]:[11] For when the sun comes up and puts out all its heat, the plant withers, the flower drops off, and its beauty fades… And this is how the rich man will fade away in his journey through life!
[James] [1]:[12] However, the man who endures his trials is blest, because after he’s been approved, he’ll receive the garland of life that the Lord promised to all those who love him.
[James] [1]:[13] So may no one who is being tried ever say: ‘I’m being tried by God!’...because God doesn’t send bad things to try us. In fact, He doesn’t try anyone!
[James] [1]:[14] Rather, we’re each being tried by our own desires, which bait us and lead us on.
[James] [1]:[15] Then when our desires become pregnant, they give birth to sin... And once the sin is committed, it ends in death.
[James] [1]:[16] Don’t allow anyone to mislead you, my beloved brothers...
[James] [1]:[17] Every good deed and every perfect gift comes to us from above. It comes down from the Father of all light, who doesn’t change any more than a shadow when it turns.
[James] [1]:[18] And because it was His Will, He gave birth to us through the message of truth, so that we could be some of the first fruitage of His creation.
[James] [1]:[19] Recognize this, my beloved brothers: Every man must be eager to listen... Slow to speak... And slow to get angry!
[James] [1]:[20] For a man’s anger doesn’t make him righteous with God.
[James] [1]:[21] So, once you’ve gotten rid of all the filth and badness, humbly allow the Word to grow within you… Because it can save your lives!
[James] [1]:[22] Yes, become a person who does what the Word [directs him to do]. Don’t [be someone who just] listens to it, [for people like that] are fooling themselves.
[James] [1]:[23] Because if anyone is a hearer but not a doer, he’s like the man who looks into a mirror at the face he was born with
[James] [1]:[24] and carefully considers himself, then leaves and immediately forgets what sort of person he really is.
[James] [1]:[25] However, the one who gazes into the perfect Law that belongs to a free people – and then keeps on looking into it – isn’t someone who listens and forgets, but someone who takes action! This man will be blest in whatever he does!
[James] [1]:[26] Now, if any of you think of yourselves as devout, but you’re misleading your hearts by not putting a bridle on your tongues, your worship is worthless...
[James] [1]:[27] For what our God and Father views as clean, pure worship is this: [Providing aid] to orphans and widows when they’re in need, and keeping ourselves free from the stains of this system of things.
[James] [2]:[1] My brothers, Don’t show favoritism when it comes to the glorious faith of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One!
[James] [2]:[2] Because if a man who is wearing a gold ring and fine clothes enters your synagogue, and then somebody whose clothes are filthy also enters...
[James] [2]:[3] do you favor the one who is wearing the fine clothes and say: ‘Here’s a good place to sit?’ And do you then say to the poor one: ‘Stand [over there]!’ Or: ‘Sit here under my footstool?’
[James] [2]:[4] If so, aren’t you showing favoritism among yourselves and judging from evil thoughts?
[James] [2]:[5] Listen, my beloved brothers! Didn’t God choose the poor of this system of things to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom that He promised to those who love Him?
[James] [2]:[6] Yet, you [tend to] dishonor the poor! Aren’t rich people the ones who are oppressing you and dragging you into courts?
[James] [2]:[7] And aren’t they the ones who speak badly of the good name you’re called by?
[James] [2]:[8] Now, if you’re obeying the royal law of the Scriptures that says, ‘You must love your neighbor as yourself,’ you’re doing well...
[James] [2]:[9] But if you’re showing favoritism, then you’re sinning and the Law convicts you of being its violator!
[James] [2]:[10] Because if someone who is trying to obey the Law fails in just one little part of it, then he’s broken the whole thing.
[James] [2]:[11] Because the One who said: ‘You must not commit adultery,’ [Exodus 20:14]...also said: ‘You must not murder.’ [Exodus 20:13] So if you aren’t committing adultery, but you murder someone, you’ve broken the whole Law.
[James] [2]:[12] Therefore, speak and behave as though you’re about to be judged by the law of a free people…
[James] [2]:[13] And [remember that] the merciless will be judged without mercy, since mercy is an important part of justice.
[James] [2]:[14] So what good does it do, my brothers, if someone says that he has faith, but isn’t moved to do anything about it? Can his faith save him?
[James] [2]:[15] [For example], if a brother or sister doesn’t have clothing or enough food for each day,
[James] [2]:[16] and you tell him: ‘Go in peace; be warm and well fed.’...if you don’t give him what he needs to survive, what good have you done?
[James] [2]:[17] So, faith without good deeds is dead!
[James] [2]:[18] Now, someone can say: ‘Even though you may do good things, I have [more] faith!’ Well, you show me your faith without good deeds, and I’ll show you my faith by the good things that I do.
[James] [2]:[19] And do you say that you believe there’s just one God? That’s good… But the demons believe that too! Yes, they believe and it frightens them!
[James] [2]:[20] I want you to know, O empty man, that faith apart from [good] deeds is dead!
[James] [2]:[21] For wasn’t our father AbraHam called righteous because of the things that he did… Such as when he offered up his son IsaAc on the altar?
[James] [2]:[22] Yes, you can see how his faith worked along with his deeds, and that it was his deeds that perfected his faith.
[James] [2]:[23] So the scripture was fulfilled that says AbraHam... ‘...believed in The God, and for this he was considered to be righteous...’ [Genesis 15:6]...and he was called God’s friend.
[James] [2]:[24] So you see, a man is pronounced righteous by the things that he does, not just by the things he believes!
[James] [2]:[25] The same was true of the prostitute, RaHab. For she was called righteous because she took the messengers in and then sent them out by another way.
[James] [2]:[26] So, just as a body that isn’t breathing is dead, faith without good deeds is dead.
[James] [3]:[1] Brothers, not many of you should become teachers, because you know that [teachers] will be held more accountable…
[James] [3]:[2] and we all make a lot of mistakes! So if there’s any man who doesn’t stumble in his words, he’s perfect and he can lead his whole body as if with a bridle...
[James] [3]:[3] Because if we put a bridle in the mouth of a horse to make it obey us, we can control its whole body.
[James] [3]:[4] {Look!} Even large boats that are driven by strong winds are steered wherever the pilot wishes by very small rudders…
[James] [3]:[5] and that’s just like it is with the tongue! Even though it’s just a little body part, it can boast about big things… And just a little flame can set a whole forest on fire!
[James] [3]:[6] That’s how the tongue is… It’s a flame in a world of unrighteousness. It sits among our body members as the corrupter of the whole body, which sets our very origins on fire… And what sets them ablaze is the garbage dump!
[James] [3]:[7] Even though every sort of wild animal, flying creature, slithering thing, and sea creature can be tamed (and has been tamed) by men,
[James] [3]:[8] no man can tame the tongue… For it won’t stop saying bad things, and it’s full of deadly poison.
[James] [3]:[9] With it we can praise the highest Lord and the Father, or curse men who came into existence in God’s image…
[James] [3]:[10] So out of the same mouth comes both blessings and curses. There’s no need for things like this to keep happening, my brothers!
[James] [3]:[11] Are there any fountains that bubble up both sweet and bitter [water]?
[James] [3]:[12] Fig trees can’t produce olives. Grapevines can’t produce figs. And you can’t get sweet water from salt water, can you my brothers?
[James] [3]:[13] So, who among you is wise and understanding? Let him show that he has the inner strength that comes from wisdom through the ways that he acts and the things that he does.
[James] [3]:[14] But if you’re bitterly jealous, and in your hearts you just want to argue... Don’t be too proud of this and don’t lie about the facts.
[James] [3]:[15] This isn’t wisdom that comes from above! It’s earthly, animalistic, and demonic!
[James] [3]:[16] For where you find jealousy and arguing, you’ll also find disorder and everything that’s foul.
[James] [3]:[17] But the wisdom that comes from above is first of all pure, then peaceable, reasonable, ready to obey, and full of mercy and good fruitage. It isn’t hypocritical or prejudiced,
[James] [3]:[18] because the seeds of the fruit of righteousness are planted in peace by the peacemakers!
[James] [4]:[1] So, where are all these fights and wars among you coming from? Aren’t they the result of battles that are being fought in your body parts over [sensual] pleasures?
[James] [4]:[2] You want, but you can’t have! You’re jealous... And murderous... But that doesn’t get you anything! You’re fighting and waging war, but you haven’t received because you haven’t asked.
[James] [4]:[3] Then when you do ask, you don’t receive, because you’re asking for the wrong reasons, since all that you’re really interested in is pleasure!
[James] [4]:[4] Adulteresses, don’t you know that if you’re a friend of the world you’re an enemy of God? So, whoever wants to be a friend of this world is putting himself down as God’s enemy!
[James] [4]:[5] Does the writing say that the spirit within us... ‘...lusts with envy...’ [perhaps referencing Proverbs 27:4]...for no reason?
[James] [4]:[6] Now, the loving care that He sends to us is greater than of all that, for we were told: ‘[Jehovah] opposes the proud, But shows loving-care to the humble.’ [Proverbs 3:34]
[James] [4]:[7] So, let’s do what God says… Resist the Opposer and he’ll run from you!
[James] [4]:[8] But draw closer to God and He will draw closer to you! So, wash your hands, you sinners! And those of you who are undecided should purify your hearts!
[James] [4]:[9] Otherwise you’ll be crying, groaning, and miserable… Your laughter will be turned into groaning and your joy will be turned into sadness!
[James] [4]:[10] Yes, humble yourselves in the eyes of [Jehovah] and He will lift you higher!
[James] [4]:[11] Brothers, stop complaining about each other, because those who speak against or judge their brothers are speaking against and judging the Law. And if you’re judging the Law, you aren’t someone who is under it, you’re its judge…
[James] [4]:[12] And there’s just one Lawgiver and Judge who can either save or destroy. So, who [do you think] you are to be judging your neighbors?
[James] [4]:[13] And those of you who say: ‘Today or tomorrow I’m going to travel to this city or that, and I’ll spend a year there doing business and making profits...’
[James] [4]:[14] You don’t even know what’s going to happen in your life tomorrow! For you’re just a mist that appears for a little while and then disappears!
[James] [4]:[15] Shouldn’t you rather be saying... ‘If it’s [Jehovah’s] will, I’ll live and do this or that?’
[James] [4]:[16] But now you’re taking pride in things that you just assume to be true, and being proud over such things is wickedness.
[James] [4]:[17] Because, whenever you know what’s right and you don’t do it, that’s a sin to you!
[James] [5]:[1] So go on, you who are rich... Cry and bawl over the miseries that you’ll have to endure!
[James] [5]:[2] For your wealth will rot away. Your clothes will be moth-eaten.
[James] [5]:[3] Your gold and silver will corrode. And whatever remains will testify against you and eat your flesh – just like the fire that you’ve treasured away for yourselves in the last days.
[James] [5]:[4] Look! The wages that you refused to pay the workers that harvested your fields are crying out, and the cries of the reapers have reached the ears of [Jehovah] of Armies!
[James] [5]:[5] For you’ve lived on the earth merrily and have been greedy… Yes, you fattened-up your own bodies to be ready for the day of slaughter!
[James] [5]:[6] You’ve condemned and murdered a righteous one, [even though] he didn’t stand against you.
[James] [5]:[7] Brothers, let’s be patient until the Lord arrives. {Look!} For just as the farmer harvests the precious fruitage of the ground after patiently waiting for both the early and late rains,
[James] [5]:[8] we must also be patient… But with determined hearts; because the appearance of the Lord is drawing near.
[James] [5]:[9] Brothers, stop groaning about each other, so you won’t be judged. For look… The judge is now standing at the door!
[James] [5]:[10] Brothers, you should learn from the examples of the Prophets who spoke in the Name of [Jehovah] about how to suffer bad things and how to be patient,
[James] [5]:[11] for we call those who endured, ‘the blest!’ You’ve all heard of the endurance of Job and you saw how [Jehovah] ended it… And this proves that [Jehovah] is very kind and merciful.
[James] [5]:[12] But above all, my brothers... Stop swearing oaths by heaven, or by the earth, or by anything else. Just let your yes mean yes, and your no mean no, so that you don’t fail when you’re being judged!
[James] [5]:[13] Are there any among you who are being persecuted? Let them keep on praying! Are there any among you who are cheerful? Let them sing psalms!
[James] [5]:[14] Are there any among you who are ill? Let them call the elders and ask them to pray over them, as they rub them with oil in the name of the Lord!
[James] [5]:[15] Then their faithful prayers will rescue the ill and the Lord will lift them and forgive any sins that they’ve committed.
[James] [5]:[16] So, admit your errors to each other and pray that each one of you will be healed, because prayer has a lot of power when it’s working through righteous people.
[James] [5]:[17] Remember that EliJah was just a man with passions like ours; but when he prayed and asked for it not to rain, it didn’t rain in the land for three and a half years!
[James] [5]:[18] Then when he prayed again, the skies poured with rain, causing the ground to produce its fruitage!
[James] [5]:[19] My brothers, Whenever someone is led astray from the truth and someone else leads him back...
[James] [5]:[20] Recognize that the one who turns the sinner from the error of his ways will save his own life from death… And it will cover many of his own sins as well.
[1 Peter] [1]:[1] Peter, an Apostle of Jesus the Anointed One, to the elected ones among the scattered [Jews] living in Pontus, Galatia, CappaDokia, Asia Minor, and Bithynia...
[1 Peter] [1]:[2] who, by the foreknowledge of The God and Father, and by the holiness of the breath, are obedient and sprinkled with the blood of Jesus the Anointed One... May loving care and peace be multiplied among you!
[1 Peter] [1]:[3] Praise the God and Father of our Lord Jesus the Anointed One, who according to His great mercy fathered within us the hope of life by resurrecting Jesus the Anointed One from the dead,
[1 Peter] [1]:[4] so that an undying, incorruptible, and enduring inheritance will be reserved for you in the heavens.
[1 Peter] [1]:[5] Yes, you who are being guarded by faith through the power of God for a salvation that’s ready to be revealed in this final season,
[1 Peter] [1]:[6] and in which you’re rejoicing. So, although you’re currently being grieved by various trials,
[1 Peter] [1]:[7] understand that these things are happening to you in order to prove your faith, which is something that’s much more valuable than gold that’s refined and proven by fire, and so that you’ll be found to be a reason for praise, honor, and glory at the revealing of Jesus the Anointed One.
[1 Peter] [1]:[8] For even though you’ve never seen him, you’ve loved him.. And even though you can’t see him, you’ve believed in him and are rejoicing with an unspeakable and glorified joy.
[1 Peter] [1]:[9] For it’s by this that you’re carrying off for yourselves the reward of the hope that’s bringing salvation to your lives!
[1 Peter] [1]:[10] And when it comes to this salvation, understand that the Prophets (those who prophesied that this loving-kindness would be shown to you) used to seek and search,
[1 Peter] [1]:[11] trying (through the spirit of the anointing that was in them) to determine the exact time and circumstances of the sufferings of the Anointed One, and of his being glorified… Yes, they knew about this even back then!
[1 Peter] [1]:[12] However, it wasn’t revealed to them as it has been to you, for they were just servants of the things that have now been revealed to you by those who proclaimed the good news to you through holy breath sent from heaven. Yes [at that time], even the messengers [of God] wanted to see these things!
[1 Peter] [1]:[13] As a result, prepare your minds to understand, and become perfectly sober when it comes to your hope of the loving kindness that’ll be manifested in you at the revelation of Jesus the Anointed One.
[1 Peter] [1]:[14] And as obedient children, don’t go back to being what you used to be by desiring ignorant things.
[1 Peter] [1]:[15] Rather, like the Holy One who called you, become holy in all of your ways.
[1 Peter] [1]:[16] For it’s written: ‘You must be holy, because I’m holy!’ [Leviticus 11:45, one of many places saying this]
[1 Peter] [1]:[17] So, if you’re calling this One your Father (someone who doesn’t discriminate, but judges each person by the things that they do), you should be living your lives in fear!
[1 Peter] [1]:[18] For you’ve got to recognize that the ransom, which was paid to release you from the worthless way of life that you learned from your fathers, wasn’t paid for with things that waste away like silver or gold.
[1 Peter] [1]:[19] Rather, it was paid for with the precious blood of a spotless and perfect lamb, the Anointed One!
[1 Peter] [1]:[20] And even though he was appointed before the founding of the cosmos, he’s been finally revealed during this period for your sakes...
[1 Peter] [1]:[21] so that, through him, you could come to believe in The God who raised him from the dead and glorified him, and so that you could put all your faith and hope in that God.
[1 Peter] [1]:[22] Then, after you’ve purified your lives by [learning how to] obey the truth, you must also learn to love each other intensely… Yes – develop a sincere brotherly love for each other out of a pure heart!
[1 Peter] [1]:[23] For you weren’t born again as seeds which are planted [in the ground] and will perish, but as something that, through the enduring Word of the living God, is now imperishable!
[1 Peter] [1]:[24] [As it is written]: ‘All flesh is like grass And its glory is like the flowers in a field. But although grass dries up and its flowers will drop,
[1 Peter] [1]:[25] God’s Word lasts throughout the ages.’ [Isaiah 40:8] Yes, these are the words that we’ve preached to you as good news.
[1 Peter] [2]:[1] Therefore, you must now get rid of all of your badness, deceit, hypocrisy, envy, and slandering!
[1 Peter] [2]:[2] Then, like newborn babies, develop a taste for the pure milk of the Word, which will help you to grow to salvation…
[1 Peter] [2]:[3] That is, if you have indeed tasted that the Lord is good.
[1 Peter] [2]:[4] Yes, you must approach him as though he’s a living block of stone that was for a fact rejected by men, but has been chosen as something precious by God.
[1 Peter] [2]:[5] Because, it’s upon him that you’re being built as living blocks into a Spiritual Temple and as a Holy Priesthood to offer spiritual sacrifices that are acceptable to God, through Jesus the Anointed One.
[1 Peter] [2]:[6] For the Scripture says: '{Look!} I am laying in Zion a select and precious cornerstone... And all who put faith in it will never be shamed.’ [Isaiah 28:16]
[1 Peter] [2]:[7] Therefore, you’ve put faith in this precious thing that others don’t believe in… ‘The block that the builders rejected, but which has become the foundation cornerstone.’ [Psalm 118:22]
[1 Peter] [2]:[8] And, ‘A stumbling block... and snare’ [Isaiah 8:14 (MT, DSS) see note]...to those who stumble over the words because of the disobedient ways they’ve been appointed to.
[1 Peter] [2]:[9] And now you’ve become a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, and a people who were specially selected to announce the virtues of the One who called you out of darkness and into His wonderful light.
[1 Peter] [2]:[10] So, although you haven’t always been a nation, you’re now a nation of God! And although you once knew no mercy, you’re the ones who are now being shown mercy!
[1 Peter] [2]:[11] My loved ones, I want to encourage you [Jews] who are [living as] foreigners and exiles not to indulge in the things that your bodies might crave and which fight a battle against the person who you are on the inside.
[1 Peter] [2]:[12] Yes, while you’re [living] among the other races, behave yourselves, so that when they condemn you and say bad things about you, they can see the good things that you’re doing and then glorify The God in the Day that He arrives for His inspection.
[1 Peter] [2]:[13] Also, you must obey every office that men have created through the Lord, regardless of whether the one who is over you is a king,
[1 Peter] [2]:[14] or [just] a governor who has been sent [by the king] to punish criminals and to praise those who are doing good things.
[1 Peter] [2]:[15] Because, it’s God’s Will for you to do good things, so that you can put a muzzle on the ignorant accusations of unreasonable men.
[1 Peter] [2]:[16] And even though you’re a free people, as slaves of God, don’t use your freedom as a cover-up for doing bad things!
[1 Peter] [2]:[17] Rather, be respectful to everyone, love your brothers, fear God, and show special respect for the king.
[1 Peter] [2]:[18] Those of you who are household servants should obey and fear your masters… And not just those who are good and reasonable, but also those who are hard to please.
[1 Peter] [2]:[19] For if a person with a Godly conscience has to put up with the grief of having to suffer for something he didn’t do, it shows a lot of inner strength.
[1 Peter] [2]:[20] So if you’re being slapped for something wrong that you didn’t do, and you [choose to] put up with suffering when you’ve only done good things, this shows your inner strength to God.
[1 Peter] [2]:[21] And for a fact, this is the [course] you were called to... Because, the Anointed One suffered on your behalf as an example, so that you’d follow in his tracks.
[1 Peter] [2]:[22] ‘He wasn’t guilty of any sin, ‘And his mouth didn’t speak any lies.’ [Isaiah 53:9]
[1 Peter] [2]:[23] When they shouted bad things at him, he didn’t shout back. When he was suffering, he didn’t threaten anyone. He just left himself [in the hands of] the One who judges righteously.
[1 Peter] [2]:[24] Then he... ‘carried our sins’ [Isaiah 53:4]...on his body when he was hung on the tree. That’s when the sins died so that we could, thereafter, be counted as righteous. For, ‘by his wounds, you were healed.’ [Isaiah 53:5]
[1 Peter] [2]:[25] Yes, ‘you were like sheep who had strayed’ [Isaiah 53:6]...but you have now returned to the shepherd who is watching over your lives.

[1 Peter] [3]:[2] when they see the fear that you’re showing by being pure.
[1 Peter] [3]:[3] Don’t let your beauty come from fancy hairstyles, gold jewelry, or the way you arrange your clothes,
[1 Peter] [3]:[4] but from what’s hidden in your hearts… Let it be the type of clean, quiet, and mild personality that’s valuable in the eyes of God!
[1 Peter] [3]:[5] Indeed, this is how holy women in the past who put their hope in God have been beautifying themselves… By obeying their husbands.
[1 Peter] [3]:[6] So, just as SarAh used to obey AbraHam, calling him ‘Lord;’ you should become her children in doing good things, so you’ll have nothing to fear.

[1 Peter] [3]:[11] ‘Turn away from what’s bad and do what’s good, As you search for and chase after peace!
[1 Peter] [3]:[12] ‘[Jehovah] watches out for the righteous, And He listens when they’re crying to Him… But [Jehovah] opposes those who are doing what’s bad.’ [Psalm 34:12-16a]
[1 Peter] [3]:[13] Therefore, who’ll treat you badly if you’re zealously doing what’s righteous?
[1 Peter] [3]:[14] And even if you should have to suffer for doing something righteous, you’ll be blest! So, don’t be afraid or even be bothered by such things!
[1 Peter] [3]:[15] Rather, make the Lord Anointed One holy in your hearts, and always be ready to make a defense before anyone who demands to know why you’ve got this hope. However, do it calmly... And with [Godly] fear.
[1 Peter] [3]:[16] Yes, keep a clean conscience so that anyone who may accuse you and speak out against you will be shamed by your fine conduct.
[1 Peter] [3]:[17] And remember that it’s better for you to suffer for doing something good (if that’s God’s will) than for doing something that’s bad.
[1 Peter] [3]:[18] For even the Anointed One died (once and for all time) over sins as someone who is righteous on behalf of those who are unrighteous, so as to lead you to God. He was dead in the flesh, but alive in spirit,

[1 Enoch] [100]:[12] So, give gifts to the rain, dew, cloud, and mist, So they won’t be stopped from coming down to you. Pay out gold so they’ll come down!
[1 Enoch] [100]:[13] Because, if snow, frost, and its cold are cast upon you, Along with the winds, their ice, and all their punishments, You won’t be able to stand against the cold and their punishments.
[1 Enoch] [101]:[1] So, everyone, understand the Most High’s actions and be afraid to do wrong in his presence.
[1 Enoch] [101]:[2] If he closes the sky’s windows and stops the dew and rain from falling because of you, what will you do?
[1 Enoch] [101]:[3] If he unleashes his anger on you and your actions, won’t you plead with him? Why do you speak so arrogantly and harshly against his greatness?
[1 Enoch] [101]:[4] Look at the ship captains who sail the sea, whose ships are thrown around by the waves and storms...
[1 Enoch] [101]:[5] When the storm batters them, they all become afraid. Also, they throw all their valuable goods and belongings overboard into the sea, fearing in their hearts that the sea will swallow them and they’ll die in it.
[1 Enoch] [101]:[6] Well, isn’t the entire sea and all its waters the Most High’s creation? And didn’t he himself set its boundaries, control it, and surround it with sand?
[1 Enoch] [101]:[7] And when he roars, they tremble and dry up, and the fish...
[1 Enoch] [101]:[8] ...earth and everything in it? And who gave understanding to all the creatures moving in the sea? [Yes, and] the ship captains fear the sea.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[1] When he unleashes the raging fire that consumes you, Where will you flee for safety? And when he speaks,
[1 Enoch] [102]:[2] you’ll be shaken, And filled with fear by [a] mighty sound! The entire earth will be shaken, Trembling, and deeply disturbed.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[3] The messengers will carry out their commands, And the heavens and celestial bodies will be shaken and tremble. All the earth’s inhabitants, Especially you sinners, Will be accursed into the age; You’ll have no reason for joy.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[4] So, take courage, you righteous And pious souls who have died.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[5] Don’t grieve that your souls Went down into the place of the dead [literally, Hades] in sorrow. Nor that your physical bodies didn’t receive What your holiness deserved during your lifetime. That’s because the days you lived Were days of sinners and the accursed on earth.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[6] When you die, the sinners will claim that the pious Simply died by chance. And they’ll ask: ‘What good did their actions bring them?’
[1 Enoch] [102]:[7] For they died just like us!’ Well, then, see how they die in sorrow and darkness, And what extra benefit did they get?
[1 Enoch] [102]:[8] From now on, the righteous will rise and be saved. And the sinners will see us eating and drinking into the age.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[9] So, [they thought they could] seize, sin, rob, and acquire......and see good days.
[1 Enoch] [102]:[10] So, you who justify yourselves, See what kind of destruction happened to them; Because no righteousness was found in them Until they died and perished...
[1 Enoch] [102]:[11] They became as if they had never existed, And their souls went down into the place of the dead [literally, Hades] with pain.
[1 Enoch] [103]:[1] I swear to you...
[1 Enoch] [103]:[2] I understand this mystery because I’ve read the heavenly tablets, seen the essential writing, and learned what was written and engraved in them about you,
[1 Enoch] [103]:[3] that good things, joy, and honor have been prepared and inscribed for the pious souls who have died.
[1 Enoch] [103]:[4] They will rejoice; their spirits certainly won’t perish, nor will their memory vanish from the Great One’s presence throughout all generations of the ages. So, don’t fear their criticism. As for you, the sinful dead, when you die, it will be said of you:
[1 Enoch] [103]:[5] ‘Blest are the sinners, for they lived out all their days...’ and they died gloriously,
[1 Enoch] [103]:[6] ‘and no judgment happened in their lifetime!’
[1 Enoch] [103]:[7] You know that your souls will be led down into the Place of the Dead,
[1 Enoch] [103]:[8] and there they’ll be in great distress, in darkness, trapped, and in a burning flame. Your souls will face great judgment in all the generations of the age. Woe to you! You have no reason to be joyful. But for you, righteous ones, who were holy in life, don’t say:
[1 Enoch] [103]:[9] ‘We suffered through days of hardship; we were worn out and reduced, and we found no helper.
[1 Enoch] [103]:[10] We were crushed and died; we despaired, no longer seeing any hope of salvation day after day.
[1 Enoch] [103]:[11] ‘We hoped to become the head, but we became the tail. We toiled, yet we didn’t become masters of our own earnings. We became prey for sinners; the lawless ones burdened us with their oppression
[1 Enoch] [103]:[12] ‘Our rulers, our enemies, attack us and surround us. We looked for [a] place to flee from them, so we could find relief.
[1 Enoch] [103]:[14] ‘We cried out to those who brought us down and oppressed us, but they didn’t accept our pleas, nor would they listen to us.
[1 Enoch] [103]:[15] ‘They didn’t help us, nor did they find [a] way to stand against those who oppressed and destroyed us; instead, they strengthened our enemies against us. They killed us and reduced our numbers. And they don’t acknowledge our murdered ones, nor do they remember the sins of their own sinners.’
[1 Enoch] [104]:[1] I swear to you that the messengers in heaven remember you favorably before the glory of the Great One.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[2] Therefore, be confident now, because you’ve been worn out by troubles and hardships. You’ll shine brightly, appearing like the stars in heaven, and heaven’s ‘windows’ will be opened for you,
[1 Enoch] [104]:[3] and your cry will be heard. The judgment you’ve called for will be revealed
[1 Enoch] [104]:[4] concerning all the issues brought up on your behalf about your suffering, and against everyone who acted violently and harmed you.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[5] Don’t fear the troubles on the day of the great judgment, because you certainly won’t be found among the sinners. But as for you, sinners, you’ll be stripped of everything, and eternal judgment will come upon you into all the generations of the ages.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[6] Don’t be afraid, righteous ones, when you see sinners succeeding and doing well. Don’t become partners with them, but stay far away from all their wicked actions.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[7] Don’t say, sinners, that your sins certainly won’t be uncovered, even after a long time.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[8] Now, I reveal to you that light and darkness, day and night, oversee all your sins.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[9] Don’t let your mind mislead you. Don’t lie, don’t change the words of truth, and don’t speak falsely against the words of the Holy One. And don’t bow down to your idols, because all falsehoods and all error don’t lead to righteousness...
[1 Enoch] [104]:[10] Sinners change and copy the words of truth, and they mislead many people. They lie and make up big stories, and they write their own versions in their names.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[11] I wish they would write all my words truthfully in their names, and neither take away from nor change these words, but write everything truthfully, just as I’ve testified to them.
[1 Enoch] [104]:[12] Also, I know [a] second mystery: My books will be given to the righteous, the holy, and the wise, for truth’s joy,
[1 Enoch] [104]:[13] and they’ll believe them and rejoice in them. All the righteous will greatly rejoice to learn all truth’s ways from them.
[1 Enoch] [106]:[1] [Enoch says:] ‘Some time later, Methuselah, my son, married [a] woman, and she gave birth to [a] son, whom he named Lamech. People had become less righteous until that day. When Lamech grew up, he also married [a] woman, and she gave birth to [a] child.
[1 Enoch] [106]:[2] ‘When the child was born, its skin was whiter than snow and redder than [a] rose; its hair was completely white, like white wool, and it was curly and glorious! When it opened its eyes, the house shone as brightly as the sun.
[1 Enoch] [106]:[3] It rose from the midwife’s hands, opened its mouth, and blessed the Lord.
[1 Enoch] [106]:[4] ‘Now, Lamech was afraid of the child and fled to his father Methuselah, and said:
[1 Enoch] [106]:[5] ‘I’ve had [a] strange child born to me. It’s not like humans, but like the children of heaven’s messengers! Its appearance is stranger, not like ours; its eyes are like sunbeams, and its face is glorious.
[1 Enoch] [106]:[6] ‘I suspect it’s not my child, but from [an] messenger, and I’m worried that something terrible might happen on earth during its lifetime.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[7] ‘Father, please, I beg you, go to our father Enoch and ask...
[1 Enoch] [106]:[8] ‘So he came to me at the earth’s ends, where he found me, and said: ‘My father, listen to me and come.’ ‘I heard his voice, went to him, and said: ‘Look! I’m here, my child; why have you come to me?’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[9] ‘He replied: ‘Father, I came here because of [a] great need.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[10] ‘Now, my son Lamech has had [a] child born to him. His form and appearance are not like humans, and his skin color is whiter than snow and redder than [a] rose! The hair on his head is whiter than white wool, and his eyes are unlike sunbeams!
[1 Enoch] [106]:[11] ‘He rose from the midwife’s hands, opened his mouth, and blessed the Lord of the Age.
[1 Enoch] [106]:[12] My son Lamech was afraid and fled to me. He doesn’t believe the child is his son, but that it’s from messengers... '...the exact knowledge you possess, and the truth.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[13] Then I replied: ‘The Lord will issue [a] new decree upon the earth, and in the same way, my child, I’ve seen and revealed this to you; because in the generation of my father Jared, they disobeyed [Jehovah’s] word, breaking heaven’s agreement.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[14] ‘Look, they’re sinning and breaking the custom; they associate with women, sin with them, and have married from among them, and they bear children who are not like breaths, but are physical beings.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[15] ‘There will be great wrath upon the earth, and [a] Downpour, and there will be great destruction for one year.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[16] ‘This child who has been born will be spared, and three of his children will be saved from those who die on the earth;
[1 Enoch] [106]:[17] and he will bring peace to the earth from the corruption within it.’
[1 Enoch] [106]:[18] ‘Now, tell Lamech that this child is truly and rightfully his, and name him Noah. He will be your remnant, and through him, you and his sons will find relief from the earth’s corruption, from all sinners, and from all the earth’s destructions...
[1 Enoch] [106]:[19] ’...he showed and revealed them to me, and I read them in heaven’s tablets.’
[1 Enoch] [107]:[1] ‘Then I saw what was written there: that [a] generation would be worse than the next, and I saw this continue until [a] generation of righteousness would appear. Evil would disappear, sin would leave the earth, and good things would come to the earth for them.
[1 Enoch] [107]:[2] ‘Now, go, my child, and tell your son Lamech that this child who was born is truly his son, not someone else’s.’
[1 Enoch] [107]:[3] ‘Well, when Methuselah heard his grandfather Enoch’s words — Enoch had told him this in a mysterious way — he [went back and told Lamech]. The child was named Noah, bringing joy to the earth and saving it from destruction.’
